title: A covenant timing trap
prompt: A loan is payable in 18 months. At the reporting date, a covenant breach makes it repayable on demand. The lender grants a waiver only after year end. No grace period existed at year end. Classify the loan.
explanation: The right to defer settlement must exist at the reporting date. A later waiver does not create that right retrospectively.

title: The hidden production loss
prompt: A factory incurs abnormal wasted materials of LKR 240,000. Management proposes adding them to inventory to smooth its gross margin. What should the controller do?
options: Spread it over the next three years
explanation: Abnormal amounts of wasted materials, labour and other production costs are excluded from inventory cost.

title: Non-cash expansion
prompt: A company acquires equipment by entering a lease; no cash changes hands at inception. How does this acquisition enter the cash flow statement?
options: Exclude it from cash flows and disclose the non-cash transaction separately
Show equal investing outflow and financing inflow
explanation: Investing and financing transactions without cash flows are excluded from the statement and disclosed elsewhere.

title: Estimate or error?
prompt: New engineering evidence shortens a machine’s remaining useful life. The original estimate used all reliable information then available. How is the change applied?
options: Prospectively in current and future periods
explanation: New information changes an estimate; it is not a prior-period error. Depreciation changes prospectively.

title: Material prior-year omission
prompt: A material invoice was omitted last year despite reliable information being available before authorisation. Comparatives can be restated. What is the correction?
options: Retrospective restatement of comparatives and relevant opening balances
explanation: Material prior-period errors are corrected retrospectively unless impracticable.

title: Evidence arriving late
prompt: A customer becomes bankrupt after year end, confirming severe financial difficulty that already existed at year end. The statements are not yet authorised. What follows?
options: Recognise a new-year reserve in OCI
explanation: The bankruptcy supplies evidence about a condition existing at the reporting date.

title: Dividend pressure
prompt: Directors declare a dividend after year end but before authorisation. No obligation existed at year end. What is the year-end treatment?
options: No year-end liability; disclose as required
Recognise dividend payable at year end
explanation: A dividend declared after the reporting period is not a liability at the reporting date.

title: Tax loss optimism
prompt: An entity has unused tax losses and a recent history of losses. Forecasts lack convincing evidence of future taxable profit. Should it recognise the entire deferred tax asset?
options: No; recognise only to the extent supported by probable taxable profit
Yes, because the losses legally exist
Yes, at the undiscounted loss amount
explanation: Unused tax losses require probable future taxable profit; recent losses demand convincing supporting evidence.

title: Replacement accounting
prompt: A major inspection component is replaced and the new inspection meets recognition criteria. The old inspection’s carrying amount can be identified. What is required?
options: Capitalise the new inspection and derecognise the old component
Expense the new inspection and retain the old one
Recognise a revaluation reserve for the replacement
explanation: Major inspection costs can qualify for recognition; the remaining carrying amount of the previous inspection is derecognised.

title: Actuarial shock
prompt: Under defined benefit accounting, an actuarial loss arises from a change in demographic assumptions. Where is the remeasurement recognised?
options: A deferred asset amortised through profit
explanation: Remeasurements of the net defined benefit liability or asset are recognised in OCI and are not subsequently reclassified to profit or loss.

title: Cash is not enough
prompt: A grant has been received, but reasonable assurance that its attached conditions will be met does not exist. Is immediate grant income justified?
options: No; receipt alone is not conclusive evidence that conditions will be met
Yes, cash receipt determines grant income
Yes, all grants go directly to equity
Only if management wants higher profit
explanation: Recognition requires reasonable assurance both of compliance with conditions and receipt of the grant.

title: Historical-cost foreign asset
prompt: Inventory purchased in foreign currency is carried at historical cost. Which rate translates its cost at year end?
options: The settlement-date rate regardless of timing
explanation: Non-monetary items measured at historical cost use the exchange rate at the transaction date. NRV testing may require separate translation.

title: Construction stops
prompt: A qualifying construction project is inactive for an extended period because of a discretionary work stoppage. No necessary technical or administrative work continues. What happens to borrowing cost capitalisation?
options: Continue automatically until the loan is repaid
explanation: Capitalisation is suspended during extended periods when active development is interrupted, subject to the standard’s exceptions.

title: Zero-price related party deal
prompt: A parent provides services to its subsidiary at no charge. Can the subsidiary omit related party consideration solely because no price was charged?
options: No; transfer of services can be a related party transaction even without a price
Yes; all intragroup transactions are exempt in separate accounts
Only the parent needs to consider disclosure
explanation: A related party transaction includes a transfer of resources, services or obligations regardless of whether a price is charged.

title: Whose accounts?
prompt: A retirement benefit plan prepares its own financial report. Which distinction correctly identifies LKAS 26’s role?
options: It governs plan reporting; employer benefit accounting is addressed by LKAS 19
It replaces LKAS 19 in employer accounts
It applies only to payroll tax
explanation: LKAS 26 addresses accounting and reporting by retirement benefit plans, distinct from employers’ accounting.

title: Separate does not mean consolidate
prompt: In separate financial statements, which set of measurement bases is permitted for investments in subsidiaries, joint ventures and associates, applied consistently within each category?
options: Cost, SLFRS 9, or the equity method
explanation: LKAS 27 permits cost, SLFRS 9 measurement, or the equity method in separate financial statements.

title: Influence without control
prompt: An investor owns 25% of voting rights, participates in financial policy decisions, and does not control or jointly control the investee. What normally applies in consolidated reporting?
explanation: Significant influence is presumed at 20% or more voting power unless clearly demonstrated otherwise; associates generally use the equity method.

title: The 100% shortcut
prompt: An analyst says cumulative inflation of 100% over three years is an automatic legal trigger and the only factor to assess. Is that correct?
options: No; it is an indicator among characteristics requiring judgment
Yes; there are no other indicators
Yes; only listed companies apply it
explanation: The standard does not establish an absolute inflation rate. Cumulative inflation approaching or exceeding 100% over three years is one indicator.

title: The label is misleading
prompt: A preference share requires mandatory cash redemption on a fixed date. No exception applies. What determines its classification?
options: Its contractual cash obligation makes it a financial liability
The word share makes it equity
Its voting rights alone make it equity
Management’s intention to refinance makes it equity
explanation: Classification follows contractual substance and the obligation to deliver cash, rather than the instrument’s legal label.

title: Anti-dilution discipline
prompt: Including a potential ordinary share would increase EPS from continuing operations. How should it be treated in diluted EPS?
options: Include it because every option must dilute EPS
Deduct it from the basic EPS denominator
explanation: Potential ordinary shares are included only when dilutive; anti-dilutive instruments are excluded.

title: Interim smoothing
prompt: A retailer earns most revenue in December. In June it proposes accruing expected December sales to smooth half-year profit. What is appropriate?
options: Do not anticipate seasonal revenue that would not be recognised at year end
Accrue half of the expected December revenue
Recognise revenue based on annual budget
Recognise it if cash flow is seasonal
explanation: Seasonal revenue is not anticipated or deferred at interim dates if such treatment would be inappropriate at year end.

title: Goodwill comeback
prompt: Goodwill was impaired last year. This year the acquired business recovers strongly. Can that goodwill impairment be reversed?
options: No; impairment of goodwill is not reversed
Yes, only if the CEO approves
explanation: A subsequent recovery may reflect internally generated goodwill; the standard prohibits reversing goodwill impairment.

title: Boardroom restructuring
prompt: A board approves a detailed restructuring plan before year end but has neither started implementation nor announced its main features to those affected. Is approval alone sufficient for a constructive obligation?
options: No; a valid expectation must have been raised in those affected
Yes; any board decision creates a provision
Yes; future losses are always provided
No provisions are ever allowed for restructuring
explanation: A restructuring provision requires a detailed formal plan and a valid expectation created by implementation or announcement.

title: Future operating losses
prompt: A budget forecasts operating losses next year. There is no present obligation to a third party. What is the correct response?
options: Do not provide for future operating losses; consider impairment indicators
Recognise the full budgeted loss as a provision
Recognise a deferred tax liability for the loss
explanation: Future operating losses do not meet the definition of a liability or the provision recognition criteria.

title: Research becomes development
prompt: A project enters development but management cannot demonstrate probable future economic benefits or adequate resources to complete it. What follows?
options: Expense costs until all development recognition criteria are met
Capitalise from the day research began
Recognise the project at the CEO’s valuation
explanation: Development costs are capitalised only when all specified criteria are demonstrated. Research expenditure is expensed.

title: Legacy model
prompt: In a case explicitly requiring the historical LKAS 39 incurred-loss impairment model, what is the key distinction from the SLFRS 9 expected credit loss model?
options: Objective evidence of a loss event is required under the incurred-loss model
Lifetime expected losses always arise on day one for every asset
No financial asset can ever be impaired
All losses are recorded in share capital
explanation: This is a legacy-model comparison. LKAS 39 incurred-loss recognition requires objective evidence of impairment; do not silently substitute it for SLFRS 9 ECL.

title: Owner moves in
prompt: A property held for rentals becomes occupied by the owner for its administration. Which fact supports a transfer out of investment property?
options: Commencement of owner occupation evidences a change in use
A change in the tenant’s accountant
explanation: Transfers occur when there is a change in use supported by evidence, including commencement of owner occupation.

title: Harvest boundary
prompt: Tea leaves are harvested from bearer plants. Under the general measurement rule, what becomes their cost for subsequent LKAS 2 accounting?
options: Fair value less costs to sell at harvest
Zero because the leaves grew naturally
explanation: Agricultural produce is measured at fair value less costs to sell at harvest; that amount becomes cost under LKAS 2. Bearer plants themselves fall under LKAS 16.

title: Opening balance sheet
prompt: A first-time adopter prepares its opening SLFRS statement of financial position. Which approach is generally correct, subject to specified exemptions and exceptions?
options: Recognise required assets and liabilities, remove prohibited items, reclassify and measure under SLFRSs
Carry forward every previous GAAP balance unchanged
Recognise all transition adjustments as current revenue
explanation: The opening SLFRS statement is the starting point; the recognition, derecognition, classification and measurement requirements apply subject to the standard’s reliefs.

title: Equity option grant
prompt: Employee equity-settled options vest over three years of service. Which value anchors the measurement of the services, assuming grant-date fair value can be estimated?
options: Grant-date fair value of the equity instruments, recognised over the vesting period
Year-end share price remeasurement of the equity award every year
The par value of the shares only
explanation: Employee equity-settled awards use grant-date fair value; service recognition follows the vesting period, with applicable vesting-condition rules.

title: Acquisition adviser invoice
prompt: An acquirer pays a consultant to evaluate and negotiate a business combination. The fee is not a debt or equity issuance cost. How is it treated?
options: Expense as the service is received
explanation: Acquisition-related advisory costs are expensed, except costs to issue debt or equity that follow the relevant standards.

title: Legacy insurance boundary
prompt: For a case expressly using the SLFRS 4 edition, which proposition is correct?
options: It contains insurance-contract requirements and specified reliefs; it is not the SLFRS 17 measurement model
It applies to every ordinary retail sale
explanation: The archive includes both SLFRS 4 and SLFRS 17. This question tests the legacy framework rather than asserting current applicability.

title: Sale is ready
prompt: An asset meets held-for-sale classification criteria and is within SLFRS 5 measurement scope. What follows?
options: Measure at the lower of carrying amount and fair value less costs to sell; cease depreciation
Continue depreciation and revalue to replacement cost
Always measure at selling price before selling costs
Recognise the expected sale gain immediately
explanation: Classification changes measurement and ends depreciation for the asset; a sale gain is not anticipated.

title: Before the right exists
prompt: A mining entity incurs expenditure before obtaining legal rights to explore a specific area. Is that expenditure within SLFRS 6’s exploration and evaluation scope?
options: No; expenditure before legal exploration rights is outside this scope
Yes; all mining expenditure is in scope
Yes; only if paid in foreign currency
No; the standard covers only mineral sales
explanation: SLFRS 6 excludes expenditures before exploration rights are obtained and after technical feasibility and commercial viability are demonstrable.

title: Risk disclosure gap
prompt: A bank discloses financial instrument balances but nothing about liquidity risk exposure or how it manages that risk. Is balance disclosure alone sufficient?
options: No; disclosures must also explain relevant risks and their management
Yes; carrying amounts satisfy every disclosure
Yes; risk information belongs only in advertising
explanation: The objective covers significance of financial instruments and the nature and extent of related risks, including liquidity risk.

title: Who sees the segment?
prompt: A component earns revenue, has discrete financial information, and its results are regularly reviewed by the chief operating decision maker to allocate resources and assess performance. What does this indicate?
explanation: The management approach identifies operating segments through business activity, CODM review and discrete financial information. Reportability is a further assessment.

title: Collect the cash flows
prompt: A debt asset is held solely to collect contractual cash flows. The cash flows are solely principal and interest. No fair value option is elected. What category ordinarily applies?
options: Mandatory fair value through profit or loss
explanation: Both the hold-to-collect business model and SPPI condition are met, supporting amortised cost absent a relevant designation.

title: Credit deterioration
prompt: A debt asset under the general ECL model has a significant increase in credit risk since initial recognition but is not credit-impaired. What loss allowance is required?
explanation: Significant increases in credit risk move the asset to lifetime ECL under the general approach.

title: Control below 50%
prompt: An investor has power over relevant activities, exposure to variable returns, and the ability to use power to affect those returns, despite owning 45% of votes. What is the central conclusion?
options: Control can exist; consolidate if the control assessment confirms these facts
explanation: Control requires power, variable returns and the link between them; ownership percentage alone is not decisive.

title: Joint rights
prompt: Two parties have joint control and rights to the assets and obligations for the liabilities of an arrangement. What type is it?
options: Joint venture solely because two parties exist
explanation: A joint operation gives rights to assets and obligations for liabilities; a joint venture gives rights to net assets.

title: Judgment transparency
prompt: A group concludes that an investee is controlled despite holding less than half of its voting rights. What disclosure theme is especially relevant?
options: Significant judgments and assumptions used in determining control
No disclosure because management made a judgment
explanation: SLFRS 12 requires significant judgments and assumptions about control, joint control, significant influence and arrangement type.

title: Entity plan versus market
prompt: Management plans never to sell a machine. Does that intention determine fair value?
options: No; fair value uses market participant assumptions in an orderly exit transaction
Yes; fair value equals management’s budget
Yes; only original cost can be used
explanation: Fair value is a market-based measurement, not an entity-specific measure; an intention to hold does not override that basis.

title: Regulatory scope gate
prompt: An entity already reporting under SLFRSs has never recognised regulatory deferral balances. Can it freely begin applying SLFRS 14?
options: No; the standard’s eligibility is limited to qualifying first-time adopters with prior-GAAP balances
Yes; any regulated entity may elect it at any time
Yes; it is mandatory for every utility
explanation: SLFRS 14 has a narrow scope tied to first-time adoption and regulatory deferral account balances recognised under previous GAAP.

title: A deposit is not a sale
prompt: A retailer receives a customer deposit but has not transferred the promised goods. What does receipt ordinarily create?
options: A contract liability rather than revenue
explanation: Revenue depicts satisfaction of a performance obligation. Payment before transfer generally creates a contract liability.

title: Uncertain bonus
prompt: A service contract includes a performance bonus. Including all of it could cause a significant revenue reversal when uncertainty resolves. What should the entity do?
options: Constrain variable consideration to the amount meeting the highly probable no-significant-reversal test
explanation: Variable consideration is included only to the extent that a significant reversal is highly probable not to occur when uncertainty resolves.

title: Not every service is a lease
prompt: A supplier has a substantive right to substitute the asset throughout the period of use. Which conclusion is most appropriate?
options: There is no identified asset for a lease on these facts
Every contract naming equipment is a lease
The customer must recognise the supplier’s entire factory
explanation: A substantive substitution right prevents the asset from being an identified asset for lease accounting.

title: Onerous insurance group
prompt: Under the SLFRS 17 model, an insurance group is onerous at initial recognition. How is the loss generally treated?
options: Recognise the loss immediately in profit or loss
Hide the loss in a positive contractual service margin
Defer the loss until the last claim is paid
explanation: An onerous group generates an immediate loss; the contractual service margin does not shelter a day-one loss. Applicability is assessed separately.

title: New presentation architecture
prompt: In a case explicitly applying the SLFRS 18, which list gives its five profit-or-loss categories?
options: Operating, investing, financing, income taxes, discontinued operations
explanation: SLFRS 18 specifies these five categories. Classification still requires the detailed rules, including specified main business activities. The standard states a 1 January 2027 effective date.

title: Reduced disclosure is not reduced measurement
prompt: An eligible subsidiary elects the SLFRS 19. What does it change?
options: Disclosure requirements; other applicable SLFRS recognition and measurement requirements remain
All assets are measured at cost
Consolidation becomes optional for every group
Every accounting standard is replaced by cash accounting
explanation: SLFRS 19 permits eligible subsidiaries to apply reduced disclosures while applying the recognition, measurement and presentation requirements of other SLFRSs. The standard states 1 January 2027.

title: Small but publicly accountable
prompt: A bank holds assets in a fiduciary capacity for a broad group of outsiders as a primary business. Can small size alone make it eligible for the SME framework?
options: No; public accountability is a separate eligibility barrier
Yes; headcount is the only criterion
Yes; all unlisted entities automatically qualify
explanation: The SME framework is intended for entities without public accountability that publish general purpose financial statements. Size alone is insufficient.

title: Choose the framework first
prompt: A finance team plans to mix convenient rules from full SLFRSs and the Smaller Entities standard without establishing eligibility or a consistent reporting basis. What should be resolved first?
options: The applicable framework and eligibility, then consistent policies under that framework
Whichever rule gives the highest profit each month
Only the colour of the financial statements
Use full SLFRS disclosures with arbitrary cash-basis measurements
explanation: The Smaller Entities document is a separate reporting framework. Establish the reporting basis and eligibility before selecting policies; it is not a menu of exemptions from full SLFRSs.

title: A faithful but irrelevant number
prompt: A valuation is perfectly documented but cannot affect users’ decisions about the entity. Which fundamental quality is missing?
explanation: Useful financial information must be both relevant and faithfully represented. Enhancing qualities cannot make irrelevant information useful.

title: Framework versus a Standard
prompt: A preparer finds a conflict between a specific SLFRS requirement and its reading of the Conceptual Framework. Which normally prevails?
options: The specific Standard; the Framework does not override it
The Framework automatically overrides every Standard
Management may select the more profitable result
Neither applies when there is judgment
explanation: The Framework is not a Standard and does not override a Standard or its requirements.

title: Inventory rescue • 1
prompt: Inventory cost is LKR 110,000; expected selling price is 109,000, completion costs 2,000, and costs necessary to sell 1,000. What carrying amount is appropriate?
explanation: NRV = 109,000 − 2,000 − 1,000 = 106,000. Carry at the lower of cost and NRV.

title: Recoverable amount • 1
prompt: An asset has carrying amount 910,000, value in use 705,000, and fair value less costs of disposal 755,000. All figures are LKR. What impairment loss is required?

title: Deferred tax bridge • 1
prompt: Equipment carrying amount is 820,000; tax base is 710,000. The enacted rate on reversal is 30%. Assume no recognition exception. What deferred tax liability arises?
explanation: Taxable temporary difference = 820,000 − 710,000. DTL = difference × 30% = 33,000.00. Rate is an exercise assumption.

title: Component depreciation • 1
prompt: A machine costs 1,100,000, has residual value 100,000, and a five-year useful life. It is available for use throughout the full year. Straight-line method; no impairment. Find annual depreciation.
explanation: Depreciable amount = cost − residual value. Divide 1,000,000 by five = 200,000.00.

title: Currency close • 1
prompt: A USD 11,000 trade payable was recognised at LKR 300/USD and remains unpaid. Closing rate is LKR 311/USD. What exchange LOSS arises? No hedging applies.
explanation: Monetary payable is retranslated at closing rate. Loss = USD 11,000 × (311 − 300) = LKR 121,000.

title: Associate roll-forward • 1
prompt: Opening associate investment is 2,100,000. Holding is 30%; associate earns 410,000 and pays total dividends 100,000. No fair value adjustments, OCI, unrealised profits or impairment. Closing carrying amount?
explanation: Opening + 30% of profit − 30% of dividends = 2,193,000.00. Dividends reduce the investment.

title: Weighted earnings • 1
prompt: Profit attributable to parent is LKR 1,100,000, including the amount available for equity preference dividends of LKR 100,000. Weighted average ordinary shares are 100,000. No other adjustments. Basic EPS?
explanation: Ordinary earnings = 1,100,000 − 100,000. Divide by 100,000 weighted shares = LKR 10.00.

title: Bundle allocation • 1
prompt: A contract price of LKR 990,000 covers a delivered device and distinct future support. Stand-alone prices are device 600,000 and support 400,000. No allocation exception applies. How much is allocated to the delivered device?
explanation: Allocate by relative stand-alone prices: 990,000 × 600,000 / 1,000,000 = 594,000.00. Support revenue waits for its performance.

title: Acquisition bridge • 1
prompt: Consideration is 2,100,000; NCI measured at fair value is 500,000; identifiable net assets at acquisition are 1,800,000. No previous holding or other adjustments. Find goodwill.
explanation: Goodwill = consideration + NCI − identifiable net assets = 800,000.

title: Lease inception • 1
prompt: Two annual payments of LKR 110,000 fall due at each year end. Discount rate 10%. Initial direct costs are 20,000, incentives received at commencement 5,000. No prepayments or restoration costs. Initial right-of-use asset? Round to cents.

title: ECL desk • 1
prompt: In a simplified single-scenario exercise, exposure is LKR 1,100,000, probability of default is 2% and loss given default is 40%. Assume timing and discounting effects are immaterial. Compute expected loss.
explanation: For this simplified exercise: exposure × PD × LGD = 1,100,000 × 2% × 40% = 8,800.00. Full SLFRS 9 measurement also considers scenarios, time value and reasonable supportable information.

title: Disposal decision • 1
prompt: An asset meets held-for-sale criteria. Carrying amount is 1,050,000; fair value 950,000; costs to sell 20,000. It is within SLFRS 5 measurement scope. What write-down is required?
explanation: Fair value less costs to sell = 930,000. Write-down = 1,050,000 − 930,000 = 120,000.

title: Inventory rescue • 2
prompt: Inventory cost is LKR 120,000; expected selling price is 118,000, completion costs 4,000, and costs necessary to sell 2,000. What carrying amount is appropriate?
explanation: NRV = 118,000 − 4,000 − 2,000 = 112,000. Carry at the lower of cost and NRV.

title: Recoverable amount • 2
prompt: An asset has carrying amount 920,000, value in use 710,000, and fair value less costs of disposal 760,000. All figures are LKR. What impairment loss is required?

title: Deferred tax bridge • 2
prompt: Equipment carrying amount is 840,000; tax base is 720,000. The enacted rate on reversal is 30%. Assume no recognition exception. What deferred tax liability arises?
explanation: Taxable temporary difference = 840,000 − 720,000. DTL = difference × 30% = 36,000.00. Rate is an exercise assumption.

title: Component depreciation • 2
prompt: A machine costs 1,200,000, has residual value 100,000, and a five-year useful life. It is available for use throughout the full year. Straight-line method; no impairment. Find annual depreciation.
explanation: Depreciable amount = cost − residual value. Divide 1,100,000 by five = 220,000.00.

title: Currency close • 2
prompt: A USD 12,000 trade payable was recognised at LKR 300/USD and remains unpaid. Closing rate is LKR 312/USD. What exchange LOSS arises? No hedging applies.
explanation: Monetary payable is retranslated at closing rate. Loss = USD 12,000 × (312 − 300) = LKR 144,000.

title: Associate roll-forward • 2
prompt: Opening associate investment is 2,200,000. Holding is 30%; associate earns 420,000 and pays total dividends 100,000. No fair value adjustments, OCI, unrealised profits or impairment. Closing carrying amount?
explanation: Opening + 30% of profit − 30% of dividends = 2,296,000.00. Dividends reduce the investment.

title: Weighted earnings • 2
prompt: Profit attributable to parent is LKR 1,200,000, including the amount available for equity preference dividends of LKR 100,000. Weighted average ordinary shares are 100,000. No other adjustments. Basic EPS?
explanation: Ordinary earnings = 1,200,000 − 100,000. Divide by 100,000 weighted shares = LKR 11.00.

title: Bundle allocation • 2
prompt: A contract price of LKR 1,080,000 covers a delivered device and distinct future support. Stand-alone prices are device 600,000 and support 400,000. No allocation exception applies. How much is allocated to the delivered device?
explanation: Allocate by relative stand-alone prices: 1,080,000 × 600,000 / 1,000,000 = 648,000.00. Support revenue waits for its performance.

title: Acquisition bridge • 2
prompt: Consideration is 2,200,000; NCI measured at fair value is 500,000; identifiable net assets at acquisition are 1,800,000. No previous holding or other adjustments. Find goodwill.
explanation: Goodwill = consideration + NCI − identifiable net assets = 900,000.

title: Lease inception • 2
prompt: Two annual payments of LKR 120,000 fall due at each year end. Discount rate 10%. Initial direct costs are 20,000, incentives received at commencement 5,000. No prepayments or restoration costs. Initial right-of-use asset? Round to cents.

title: ECL desk • 2
prompt: In a simplified single-scenario exercise, exposure is LKR 1,200,000, probability of default is 2% and loss given default is 40%. Assume timing and discounting effects are immaterial. Compute expected loss.
explanation: For this simplified exercise: exposure × PD × LGD = 1,200,000 × 2% × 40% = 9,600.00. Full SLFRS 9 measurement also considers scenarios, time value and reasonable supportable information.

title: Disposal decision • 2
prompt: An asset meets held-for-sale criteria. Carrying amount is 1,100,000; fair value 1,000,000; costs to sell 20,000. It is within SLFRS 5 measurement scope. What write-down is required?
explanation: Fair value less costs to sell = 980,000. Write-down = 1,100,000 − 980,000 = 120,000.

title: Inventory rescue • 3
prompt: Inventory cost is LKR 130,000; expected selling price is 127,000, completion costs 6,000, and costs necessary to sell 3,000. What carrying amount is appropriate?
explanation: NRV = 127,000 − 6,000 − 3,000 = 118,000. Carry at the lower of cost and NRV.

title: Recoverable amount • 3
prompt: An asset has carrying amount 930,000, value in use 715,000, and fair value less costs of disposal 765,000. All figures are LKR. What impairment loss is required?

title: Deferred tax bridge • 3
prompt: Equipment carrying amount is 860,000; tax base is 730,000. The enacted rate on reversal is 30%. Assume no recognition exception. What deferred tax liability arises?
explanation: Taxable temporary difference = 860,000 − 730,000. DTL = difference × 30% = 39,000.00. Rate is an exercise assumption.

title: Component depreciation • 3
prompt: A machine costs 1,300,000, has residual value 100,000, and a five-year useful life. It is available for use throughout the full year. Straight-line method; no impairment. Find annual depreciation.
explanation: Depreciable amount = cost − residual value. Divide 1,200,000 by five = 240,000.00.

title: Currency close • 3
prompt: A USD 13,000 trade payable was recognised at LKR 300/USD and remains unpaid. Closing rate is LKR 313/USD. What exchange LOSS arises? No hedging applies.
explanation: Monetary payable is retranslated at closing rate. Loss = USD 13,000 × (313 − 300) = LKR 169,000.

title: Associate roll-forward • 3
prompt: Opening associate investment is 2,300,000. Holding is 30%; associate earns 430,000 and pays total dividends 100,000. No fair value adjustments, OCI, unrealised profits or impairment. Closing carrying amount?
explanation: Opening + 30% of profit − 30% of dividends = 2,399,000.00. Dividends reduce the investment.

title: Weighted earnings • 3
prompt: Profit attributable to parent is LKR 1,300,000, including the amount available for equity preference dividends of LKR 100,000. Weighted average ordinary shares are 100,000. No other adjustments. Basic EPS?
explanation: Ordinary earnings = 1,300,000 − 100,000. Divide by 100,000 weighted shares = LKR 12.00.

title: Bundle allocation • 3
prompt: A contract price of LKR 1,170,000 covers a delivered device and distinct future support. Stand-alone prices are device 600,000 and support 400,000. No allocation exception applies. How much is allocated to the delivered device?
explanation: Allocate by relative stand-alone prices: 1,170,000 × 600,000 / 1,000,000 = 702,000.00. Support revenue waits for its performance.

title: Acquisition bridge • 3
prompt: Consideration is 2,300,000; NCI measured at fair value is 500,000; identifiable net assets at acquisition are 1,800,000. No previous holding or other adjustments. Find goodwill.
explanation: Goodwill = consideration + NCI − identifiable net assets = 1,000,000.

title: Lease inception • 3
prompt: Two annual payments of LKR 130,000 fall due at each year end. Discount rate 10%. Initial direct costs are 20,000, incentives received at commencement 5,000. No prepayments or restoration costs. Initial right-of-use asset? Round to cents.

title: ECL desk • 3
prompt: In a simplified single-scenario exercise, exposure is LKR 1,300,000, probability of default is 2% and loss given default is 40%. Assume timing and discounting effects are immaterial. Compute expected loss.
explanation: For this simplified exercise: exposure × PD × LGD = 1,300,000 × 2% × 40% = 10,400.00. Full SLFRS 9 measurement also considers scenarios, time value and reasonable supportable information.

title: Disposal decision • 3
prompt: An asset meets held-for-sale criteria. Carrying amount is 1,150,000; fair value 1,050,000; costs to sell 20,000. It is within SLFRS 5 measurement scope. What write-down is required?

title: Group close: unrealised margin
prompt: P owns 80% of S. P sold inventory costing LKR 600,000 to S for 900,000. Half remains in S’s inventory at year end. P’s separate profit is 2,000,000 and S’s is 800,000. No other adjustments, tax or OCI. What consolidated profit is attributable to P’s owners?
explanation: Downstream unrealised profit = (900,000 − 600,000) × 50% = 150,000, entirely attributable to the parent. Owners’ profit = 2,000,000 − 150,000 + 80% × 800,000 = 2,490,000.

title: Step acquisition: two bridges
prompt: P previously held 30% of S with carrying amount LKR 600,000 and fair value 850,000. P pays 1,700,000 for another 50%, obtaining control.
