explanation: Remeasure the previous holding to 850,000 (a separate 250,000 gain). Goodwill = 1,700,000 + 850,000 + 500,000 − 2,400,000 = 650,000. Do not include the old carrying amount instead of fair value.

title: Effective interest: transaction costs
prompt: A hold-to-collect SPPI bond is acquired for LKR 950,000 plus directly attributable transaction costs of 20,000. Its effective annual rate, incorporating those costs, is 8%. A coupon of 60,000 is received at year end. There are no other cash flows, credit losses or fair value designations. What is gross amortised cost after the coupon?
explanation: Initial gross carrying amount = 970,000. Effective interest = 970,000 × 8% = 77,600. Closing gross amortised cost = 970,000 + 77,600 − 60,000 = 987,600.

title: Construction: cumulative catch-up
prompt: A contract satisfies the over-time recognition criteria. Transaction price is LKR 12,000,000. Cumulative costs incurred are 4,500,000; revised total expected costs are 9,000,000. All costs faithfully depict progress and the cost-to-cost method is appropriate. Revenue already recognised in previous periods is 3,000,000. What revenue is recognised this period?
explanation: Revised completion = 4.5m / 9m = 50%. Cumulative revenue = 12m × 50% = 6m. Current-period revenue = 6m − prior revenue of 3m = 3m.

title: Lease liability after payment
prompt: A lease liability at commencement is LKR 1,000,000. Annual interest is 10%; a payment of 300,000 is made at the end of year one. Immediately after payment, a qualifying modification changes future payments and produces a revised present value of 900,000. What increase in the liability is recognised on remeasurement? Assume it is not a separate lease and there is no scope reduction.
explanation: Before remeasurement: 1,000,000 + 100,000 interest − 300,000 cash = 800,000. Revised liability is 900,000. Increase of 100,000 generally adjusts the right-of-use asset in these facts.

title: CGU: protect the floor
prompt: A CGU contains goodwill of LKR 100,000, plant of 600,000 and a building of 300,000. Recoverable amount of the CGU is 820,000. Plant has a separately determinable fair value less disposal costs of 570,000 and no higher determinable value in use. The building has no binding individual floor. How much impairment is allocated to the building?
explanation: Total loss = 1,000,000 − 820,000 = 180,000. First eliminate goodwill of 100,000. Pro rata remaining loss would assign 53,333.33 to plant, but its 570,000 floor limits plant loss to 30,000. Allocate the remaining 50,000 to the building.

title: Warranty portfolio: expected value
prompt: For 1,000 products, each has a 70% chance of no defect, a 25% chance of a minor defect costing LKR 400, and a 5% chance of a major defect costing 2,000. A present warranty obligation exists; outflow for the portfolio is probable and discounting is immaterial. Calculate the provision.
explanation: For a large population, use probability-weighted outcomes. Per product = 70% × 0 + 25% × 400 + 5% × 2,000 = 200. Portfolio provision = 1,000 × 200 = 200,000.

title: Specific borrowing: net eligible cost
prompt: A specific loan of LKR 6,000,000 at 12% is outstanding all year for a qualifying asset. Capitalisation conditions are met from 1 April to 31 December. During those nine months temporary investment income on the borrowing is 45,000. There are no interruptions or other borrowings. Calculate capitalisable borrowing costs.
explanation: Eligible interest = 6,000,000 × 12% × 9/12 = 540,000. Deduct investment income of 45,000 during the eligible period. Capitalise 495,000; pre-commencement interest is expensed.

title: Revaluation: tax in OCI
prompt: Immediately before revaluation, an asset’s carrying amount and tax base both equal LKR 1,000,000. It is revalued to 1,500,000; tax base is unchanged. The enacted tax rate on reversal is 30%, with no recognition exception. What net revaluation increase remains in OCI after its associated deferred tax?
explanation: Gross revaluation increase = 500,000. Associated deferred tax liability = 500,000 × 30% = 150,000, recognised in OCI consistently with the revaluation. Net increase = 350,000.

title: Associate: eliminate downstream profit
prompt: Opening equity-method investment is LKR 1,000,000. Investor owns 30%. Associate’s profit is 500,000 and dividends total 100,000. Investor sells goods costing 300,000 to the associate for 450,000; one third remains unsold. No tax, OCI, basis differences or impairment. What is the closing investment carrying amount?
explanation: Normal closing amount = 1,000,000 + 30% × 500,000 − 30% × 100,000 = 1,120,000. Downstream unrealised profit = 150,000 × 1/3 = 50,000. Eliminate investor’s 30% share, 15,000, against investment: 1,105,000.

title: Revision after two years
prompt: An asset costs LKR 1,200,000 with residual value 200,000 and useful life five years. After two full years of straight-line depreciation, new information changes remaining useful life to four years and residual value to 80,000. No impairment or revaluation. Calculate year-three depreciation.
explanation: Original depreciation = (1,200,000 − 200,000) / 5 = 200,000 per year. Carrying amount after two years = 800,000. Revised depreciation prospectively = (800,000 − 80,000) / 4 = 180,000.

title: Vesting: revised staff estimate
prompt: On 1 January year one, 100 employees each receive 100 equity options with grant-date fair value LKR 30 per option, conditional on three years’ service. At year-one end, 90 employees are expected to vest; at year-two end this estimate rises to 96. No market or other performance conditions apply. Calculate year-two expense alone.
explanation: Total expected award value at year two = 96 × 100 × 30 = 288,000. Cumulative expense for 2/3 service = 192,000. Year-one expense = 90 × 100 × 30 / 3 = 90,000. Year-two expense = 102,000.

title: Material does not mean large only
prompt: A small related-party payment would reveal a director’s undisclosed conflict. Management calls it immaterial solely because it is below a numerical threshold. Which assessment is strongest?
options: Consider nature and context as well as magnitude
Exclude it whenever it is below 5% of profit
Assess only its effect on cash
Apply the auditor’s threshold without considering users
explanation: Materiality depends on whether information could influence users’ decisions; nature or magnitude, or both, can matter.

title: The idle factory denominator
prompt: Production is abnormally low, leaving fixed overhead unallocated when normal capacity is used. How is that unallocated overhead treated?
options: Expense it in the period incurred
Increase unit inventory cost to absorb every fixed cost
Defer it as an intangible asset
Include it only in inventory sold next year
explanation: Fixed production overhead allocation uses normal capacity. Low production does not justify inflating inventory; unallocated overhead is expensed.

title: Overdraft integration
prompt: A bank overdraft is repayable on demand and forms an integral part of daily cash management, with balances fluctuating between positive and overdrawn. What treatment can apply for cash-flow purposes?
options: Include it as a component of cash and cash equivalents
Always classify its movements solely as investing
Always exclude it from cash equivalents regardless of facts
Net it against every long-term borrowing
explanation: The cash-equivalent definition can include such overdrafts under the specific cash-management exception; ordinary bank borrowings are generally financing.

title: Voluntary policy change
prompt: Management proposes a voluntary accounting policy change because it gives reliable and more relevant information. No transition provision or impracticability exception applies. How is it normally applied?
options: Retrospectively as though the policy had always applied
Prospectively because every voluntary change is an estimate
Only to transactions after the next year end
Through a current-period exceptional gain without comparatives
explanation: A qualifying voluntary policy change is normally applied retrospectively, adjusting affected comparatives and opening equity.

title: Fire after year end
prompt: A fire destroys a warehouse after the reporting date. No related condition existed at year end, but the loss is material. What follows, assuming going concern remains appropriate?
options: Do not adjust year-end asset values for the fire; disclose the event and estimated effect
Write down the asset at the reporting date
Recognise a year-end provision for the future fire
Disclose nothing until the insurer settles
explanation: A material non-adjusting event is disclosed with its nature and an estimate of financial effect, or a statement that estimation is not possible.

title: Offsetting is conditional
prompt: A group has deferred tax assets in one jurisdiction and deferred tax liabilities in another, without the requisite legal right or same-tax-authority conditions. May it net them merely because the consolidated group is the same?
options: No; the deferred-tax offset criteria must be satisfied
Yes; all consolidated tax balances must be netted
Yes; whenever the same accounting team prepares them
Yes; if the tax rates are identical
explanation: Offsetting is conditional, including an enforceable right and specified conditions relating to the tax authority and taxable entities. Consolidation alone is insufficient.

title: Ready but not yet used
prompt: A machine is in the location and condition necessary to operate as intended, but remains idle while management waits for a customer order. When does depreciation begin?
options: When it is available for use
Only when the first sale is invoiced
Only when production reaches normal capacity
Only when the loan is repaid
explanation: Depreciation begins when an asset is available for use, rather than when management chooses to start using it.

title: Past service cost timing
prompt: A plan amendment increases benefits for service already provided. Recognition is not accelerated by an earlier related restructuring. When is the resulting past service cost recognised?
options: Over the remaining service life of the workforce
Directly in OCI as an actuarial remeasurement
explanation: Past service cost is recognised at the earlier of the plan amendment or curtailment and the recognition of related restructuring costs or termination benefits.

title: Grant compensation pattern
prompt: A grant compensates specific payroll costs over two years and its recognition conditions are met. Which pattern is appropriate?
options: Recognise grant income systematically in the periods of the related payroll expense
Recognise the whole grant only when the last employee leaves
Always recognise the whole grant as equity
Recognise income only when the cash is spent, regardless of expense recognition
explanation: Grants are recognised in profit or loss on a systematic basis over periods in which the related costs are recognised.

title: Functional currency evidence
prompt: A company invoices mostly in currency A, which mainly influences selling prices and labour costs. Its owners prefer currency B. What should drive functional-currency determination?
options: The primary economic environment and the standard’s indicators
The currency with the most stable exchange rate
The presentation currency selected for investors automatically
explanation: Functional currency reflects the primary economic environment. Presentation currency is a separate choice.

title: Ready in parts
prompt: A qualifying development consists of independently usable buildings. One building is substantially ready while work continues elsewhere. What happens to capitalisation for that completed building?
options: Cease capitalisation for that part when substantially all necessary activities are complete
Continue until every building in the project is complete
Continue until the building is sold
Reverse all borrowing costs on the completed building
explanation: When parts can be used while construction continues on other parts, capitalisation ceases for each usable completed part.

title: Ordinary customer concentration
prompt: A distributor derives 70% of sales from one customer. There is no control, joint control, significant influence or other related-party relationship. Is economic dependence alone sufficient to make the customer related?
options: No; economic dependence alone does not create a related party
Yes; every customer above 50% of sales is related
Yes; every major customer is key management
Yes; any commercial contract creates joint control
explanation: A major customer or supplier is not related merely because of resulting economic dependence. Other disclosure requirements may still apply.

title: Plan investment measurement
prompt: A retirement benefit plan holds traded investments for which market value is available. Under LKAS 26, what measurement is generally required?
options: Fair value, with market value used for marketable securities
Historical purchase cost with no subsequent adjustment
The employer’s carrying amount of the plan deficit
Nominal value regardless of market information
explanation: Retirement benefit plan investments are carried at fair value, with market value for marketable securities; specific exceptions are addressed in the standard.

title: Dividend or investment reduction?
prompt: An investment in a subsidiary is measured at cost in separate statements. The investor’s right to receive a dividend is established. What normally happens, subject to impairment consideration?
options: Recognise the dividend in profit or loss
Always deduct it from the cost investment
Recognise it only when consolidated cash increases
explanation: Dividends are recognised when the right to receive payment is established. Under the equity method they reduce the investment, but this case uses cost.

title: Associate losses exceed interest
prompt: An investor’s share of associate losses reduces its interest, including relevant long-term interests, to zero. It has no legal or constructive obligation and has made no payments on the associate’s behalf. What follows?
options: Discontinue recognition of further losses under the specified conditions
Charge all further losses to share capital
explanation: Further losses are recognised only to the extent of obligations or payments on behalf of the associate once the interest is reduced to zero.

title: Cash in a changing measuring unit
prompt: In hyperinflationary reporting, a fixed nominal cash balance already expressed in year-end monetary units is treated how in the restated statement of financial position?
options: Do not index the monetary balance itself
Multiply the balance by the full annual index ratio
Restate it only if it is held abroad
Reclassify it as a non-monetary asset
explanation: Monetary items are not restated because they are already expressed in the measuring unit current at reporting date. Purchasing-power effects contribute to the monetary gain or loss.

title: Treasury share resale
prompt: An entity buys back its own equity instruments and later resells them at a higher price. What is the general accounting for the difference?
options: Recognise it within equity, with no profit-or-loss gain
Recognise a trading gain in revenue
explanation: An entity’s own equity instruments are deducted from equity; no gain or loss is recognised in profit or loss on purchase, sale, issue or cancellation.

title: Bonus issue after reporting date
prompt: A bonus issue occurs after reporting date but before authorisation. How does it affect basic and diluted EPS for presented periods?
options: Adjust share numbers retrospectively for the bonus issue
Ignore it until next year’s EPS only
Restate earnings but leave the share denominator unchanged
Treat bonus shares as debt instruments
explanation: A bonus issue changes shares without a corresponding change in resources, so share numbers are adjusted retrospectively, including if the event occurs before authorisation.

title: Annual tax rate estimate
prompt: For an ordinary interim period with no unusual discrete tax item, which approach generally determines interim income tax expense?
options: Use the best estimate of the weighted average annual effective income tax rate
Use the statutory rate without considering the annual effective rate
Recognise no tax until annual statements
Recognise the whole annual tax charge in the first quarter
explanation: Interim income tax expense is recognised using the best estimate of the weighted average annual effective income tax rate expected for the full financial year.

title: A reversal has a ceiling
prompt: An asset other than goodwill recovers after impairment. What limits its increased carrying amount when reversing impairment?
options: The carrying amount that would have arisen, net of depreciation, without the previous impairment
Its original purchase cost before all depreciation in every case
No limit if recoverable amount has risen
explanation: A reversal cannot raise carrying amount above the amount that would have been determined had no impairment been recognised.

title: Reimbursement certainty
prompt: An entity recognises a provision and expects an insurer to reimburse some expenditure. When is a separate reimbursement asset recognised?
options: When reimbursement is virtually certain if the entity settles the obligation
Always net the expected recovery against the liability
explanation: A reimbursement asset is recognised only when virtually certain on settlement and cannot exceed the provision. The provision remains a separate liability.

title: Training for a new system
prompt: A company incurs staff training costs for a new software platform. The training creates no separately controlled resource. What is the normal treatment?
options: Add it automatically to the software asset
Capitalise it as indefinite-life staff knowledge
explanation: Training expenditure is normally expensed; spending expected to benefit the future does not automatically create an identifiable controlled intangible asset.

title: Legacy hedge accounting boundary
prompt: A case expressly applies LKAS 39 hedge-accounting requirements. A derivative economically offsets risk, but required hedge designation and documentation were absent at inception. Is economic offset alone sufficient for hedge accounting?
options: No; formal designation, documentation and other qualifying conditions matter
Yes; every economic offset automatically qualifies
Yes; derivatives are never measured at fair value
Only the derivative’s legal name matters
explanation: This is a legacy LKAS 39 case. Qualifying hedge accounting requires the specified designation, documentation and effectiveness conditions; economic intent alone is insufficient.

title: Fair value model and depreciation
prompt: A property properly classified as investment property is measured using the fair value model. What is the normal subsequent treatment?
options: Recognise fair-value changes in profit or loss and do not depreciate under that model
Depreciate and recognise every fair-value change in OCI
Recognise fair-value gains only on sale
Use the PPE revaluation reserve automatically
explanation: The investment-property fair value model recognises period changes in profit or loss; it differs from the PPE revaluation model.

title: Growing produce on bearer plants
prompt: An entity owns bearer tea plants and growing tea leaves. Which division of accounting is appropriate?
options: Bearer plants follow LKAS 16; produce growing on them follows LKAS 41
Both always follow LKAS 16 at historical cost
Both always follow LKAS 2 before harvest
explanation: Bearer plants are outside the biological-asset accounting of LKAS 41, but produce growing on bearer plants remains within its scope.

title: First adoption is explicit
prompt: An entity publishes its first annual financial statements containing an explicit and unreserved statement of compliance with SLFRSs. Which description generally fits those statements?
options: Its first SLFRS financial statements under SLFRS 1
An interim report under LKAS 34 only
A regulatory return outside any reporting framework
explanation: First SLFRS financial statements are the first annual statements in which the entity adopts SLFRSs by an explicit and unreserved compliance statement.

title: Cash-settled award remeasurement
prompt: A cash-settled share-based payment liability remains unsettled at year end. What measurement is generally required?
options: Remeasure its fair value at each reporting date and settlement, with changes in profit or loss
Measure solely at the nominal value of shares
explanation: Cash-settled share-based payment liabilities are remeasured to fair value until settlement; changes are recognised in profit or loss.

title: Bargain purchase discipline
prompt: The preliminary acquisition calculation suggests a bargain purchase gain. What must happen before recognition of that gain?
options: Reassess the identification and measurement of acquired net assets and the other calculation components
Recognise negative goodwill as a permanent liability without reassessment
Add an arbitrary amount to goodwill to eliminate the gain
Recognise the gain directly as share capital
explanation: The acquirer reassesses the calculation and measurements before recognising a bargain purchase gain in profit or loss.

title: Legacy catastrophe reserve
prompt: A case expressly uses the SLFRS 4. Management proposes a provision for possible future catastrophe claims under contracts that do not exist at the reporting date. What does the standard require?
options: Do not recognise such provisions for possible claims under non-existent contracts
Recognise all statistically possible future claims
Capitalise the provision as a reinsurance asset
Recognise the provision only in OCI
explanation: The legacy framework prohibits provisions for possible future claims under insurance contracts that are not in existence at the reporting date, such as catastrophe or equalisation provisions.

title: Plan abandoned
prompt: An asset ceases to satisfy held-for-sale criteria. Which measurement basis applies on reclassification, subject to the detailed rules?
options: The lower of adjusted pre-classification carrying amount and recoverable amount at the decision date
Always fair value with no limit
Always its last held-for-sale amount with no adjustment
explanation: The adjusted pre-classification amount reflects depreciation or revaluation that would have occurred. It is compared with recoverable amount when the decision not to sell is made.

title: Exploration right expires
prompt: An exploration licence has expired, is not expected to be renewed and there is no other basis supporting recovery. What is the immediate accounting assessment?
options: Assess exploration and evaluation assets for impairment
Always continue capitalisation until commercial production
Transfer the whole balance into goodwill
Ignore the expiry if management once expected success
explanation: Expiry or expected expiry of the right to explore, without expected renewal, is an impairment indicator under the exploration standard.

title: Liquidity table basis
prompt: An entity prepares the contractual maturity analysis for non-derivative financial liabilities. Which general cash-flow basis applies?
explanation: The maturity analysis is based on remaining contractual maturities using contractual undiscounted cash flows, including relevant contractual payments.

title: External revenue coverage
prompt: Segments passing the 10% tests account for only 68% of entity external revenue. What additional requirement applies?
options: Identify further reportable segments until at least 75% of external revenue is included
Stop because the 10% tests override the coverage test
Add corporate income tax to segment revenue
Consolidate the smallest segment into goodwill
explanation: The 75% external-revenue coverage requirement may require additional reportable segments even when they do not meet the 10% tests.

title: Debt FVOCI recycling
prompt: A qualifying debt asset measured at FVOCI is derecognised on sale. What normally happens to its cumulative OCI gain or loss?
options: Reclassify it from equity to profit or loss
Never reclassify it, as for the equity FVOCI election
Transfer it directly to share capital
Add it permanently to the buyer’s asset balance
explanation: Debt FVOCI gains and losses accumulated in OCI are reclassified on derecognition. The irrevocable equity FVOCI election has different recycling rules.

title: Protective veto
prompt: A lender can veto extraordinary actions solely to protect its credit interest but cannot direct the borrower’s relevant activities. Are those rights alone sufficient to give it power?
options: No; protective rights alone do not confer power
Yes; lending always creates a subsidiary
Only if the borrower has a profit
explanation: Protective rights safeguard the holder’s interests without giving power over the investee; the full control assessment remains necessary.

title: Joint control is contractual
prompt: Three investors share an arrangement. The governing agreement requires unanimous consent of the two parties that collectively control it for relevant-activity decisions. What defines joint control?
options: Contractually agreed sharing of control with the required unanimous consent
Any situation with at least two shareholders
Equal economic returns without a decision agreement
explanation: Joint control is the contractually agreed sharing of control and exists only when relevant-activity decisions require unanimous consent of the parties sharing control.

title: Unconsolidated structured exposure
prompt: An entity sponsors an unconsolidated structured entity and retains exposure to variable returns. What disclosure objective is particularly relevant?
options: Explain the nature and risks of interests in unconsolidated structured entities
Disclose only legal ownership percentages in every case
Omit the interest because it is unconsolidated
Treat sponsorship automatically as an exemption from all disclosure
explanation: SLFRS 12 includes disclosures enabling users to understand interests in, and risks associated with, unconsolidated structured entities.

title: Principal versus most advantageous
prompt: An accessible principal market exists. Another accessible market would give higher net proceeds after transaction costs. Which market anchors fair value?
options: The principal market, even if another market appears more advantageous
Always the market with highest net proceeds
An inaccessible market with the highest quoted price
The entity’s preferred customer’s purchase budget
explanation: The principal market is used when it exists. The most advantageous market is used in the absence of a principal market.

title: Eligibility does not create a balance
prompt: A qualifying first-time adopter applies SLFRS 14. Does this permit it to recognise any new type of regulatory deferral account balance merely to improve profit?
options: No; continuing previous-GAAP policies is subject to the standard’s limited changes and requirements
Yes; every future tariff shortfall becomes an asset
Yes; management may invent balances without an accounting policy
Only if the new balance is credited to revenue
explanation: SLFRS 14 permits specified continuation of previous-GAAP regulatory accounting with restrictions; it is not an unrestricted right to create deferral balances.

title: Principal or agent
prompt: An intermediary arranges for another supplier to provide a service and does not control that specified service before transfer to the customer. What revenue presentation generally follows if it is an agent?
options: Recognise the fee or commission to which it expects to be entitled
Recognise gross customer billings as revenue in every case
Recognise the supplier’s total assets as its own
Recognise revenue only when the supplier earns a profit
explanation: An agent arranges provision by another party and recognises its fee or commission; control of the specified good or service distinguishes a principal.

title: Short-term election boundary
prompt: A lessee has a 12-month lease containing a purchase option. Can it qualify as a short-term lease solely because the term is 12 months?
options: No; a lease containing a purchase option is not a short-term lease
Yes; purchase options are ignored for all leases
explanation: The short-term lease definition excludes a lease containing a purchase option. The definition and any election must be assessed before applying the exemption.

title: No day-one profit release
prompt: Under the general insurance measurement model, a profitable group’s contractual service margin represents what at initial recognition?
options: Unearned profit recognised as insurance contract services are provided
An immediate operating revenue gain in full
An equity capital injection by policyholders
The fair value of every future premium with no deductions
explanation: The CSM represents unearned profit and is recognised over the provision of insurance contract services, subject to the model’s requirements.

title: Management measure transparency
prompt: In a case explicitly applying the SLFRS 18, a qualifying management-defined performance measure is used in public communications. What is the central disclosure requirement?
options: Explain it in the required single note, including reconciliation to the most directly comparable specified subtotal or total
Replace all required subtotals with it
Exclude it automatically because it is non-GAAP
Recognise the measure as an asset
explanation: The new-standard framework requires a single note with the specified explanations and reconciliations for management-defined performance measures. This case assumes the definition is met.

title: The eligible subsidiary gate
prompt: A subsidiary has no public accountability. Its ultimate parent produces consolidated SLFRS financial statements available for public use. Under the SLFRS 19, which eligibility conclusion is supported?
options: It can meet the stated subsidiary eligibility conditions for the reduced-disclosure election
It is ineligible merely because it has a parent
Every subsidiary is automatically eligible regardless of public accountability
It must switch recognition and measurement to cash basis
explanation: Eligibility requires a subsidiary without public accountability and an ultimate or intermediate parent producing qualifying consolidated statements available for public use. The edition’s application date remains relevant.

title: SME borrowing cost contrast
prompt: A case expressly applies Section 25 of the SME framework. How are borrowing costs generally treated there?
options: Recognise all borrowing costs as an expense when incurred
Capitalise every borrowing cost under LKAS 23 automatically
Recognise them directly in share capital
Defer them until the borrowing is repaid
explanation: The SME framework has its own requirements. Section 25 requires borrowing costs to be expensed, unlike qualifying-asset capitalisation under full LKAS 23.

title: A framework-specific policy question
prompt: A learner finds a recognition issue in statements prepared under the Smaller Entities framework. Which research approach is appropriate?
options: Read that framework’s applicable section and policy hierarchy before deciding treatment
Import the most favourable rule from any standard without a hierarchy
Assume all full-SLFRS exemptions apply automatically
Apply a different framework to each transaction based on profit impact
explanation: A separate reporting framework has its own applicable requirements and policy guidance. Cross-framework assumptions cannot replace reading those requirements.
reference: accounting policies and relevant transaction sections

title: Prudence and neutrality
prompt: Management deliberately understates assets whenever uncertainty exists, claiming this is prudence. Which interpretation is appropriate?
options: Prudence supports neutral caution under uncertainty rather than deliberate bias
Prudence requires maximum possible understatement in every case
explanation: Prudence is caution when making judgments under uncertainty and supports neutrality. It does not justify deliberate understatement or overstatement.

title: Deferred grant release • case 1
prompt: A depreciable asset has a five-year life and no residual value. An asset-related grant of LKR 420,000 is recognised as deferred income on 1 January, when the asset becomes available for use. All conditions are met. Straight-line depreciation is appropriate. How much grant income is recognised for the full year?
explanation: Release the deferred grant systematically over the five-year life: 420,000 / 5 = 84,000.00. Receipt is not the income pattern.

title: Grant deducted from asset • case 1
prompt: A company elects to deduct an asset grant from the asset carrying amount. Cost is LKR 2,100,000, grant 510,000, estimated residual value 100,000, and life five years. The asset is available for the full year. Find annual straight-line depreciation under this presentation.
explanation: Net depreciable amount = 2,100,000 − 510,000 − 100,000 = 1,490,000. Divide by five = 298,000.00. The grant affects expense through reduced depreciation.

title: Defined benefit net interest • case 1
prompt: Opening defined benefit obligation is LKR 5,100,000; opening plan assets are 4,050,000. Discount rate is 8%. There are no contributions, benefit payments or other timing adjustments during the year, and no asset-ceiling effect. Calculate net interest expense.
explanation: Opening net liability = 1,050,000. Apply the 8% discount rate: net interest expense = 84,000.00. Do not use gross obligation interest alone.

title: Pension liability roll-forward • case 1
prompt: Opening net defined benefit liability is LKR 1,050,000. Current service cost is 200,000; net interest expense is 84,000.00; employer contributions are 150,000; net remeasurement LOSS is 81,000. No other movements or asset ceiling apply. What is closing net liability?
explanation: Closing net liability = opening + service cost + net interest + remeasurement loss − employer contributions = 1,265,000.00. Remeasurement goes to OCI but still changes the liability.

title: Plan net assets for benefits • case 1
prompt: A retirement plan has assets of LKR 8,200,000, operating liabilities of 310,000, and actuarial present value of promised benefits of 9,000,000. Calculate net assets AVAILABLE for benefits, rather than the funding deficit.
explanation: Net assets available for benefits = plan assets − liabilities other than the actuarial present value of promised benefits: 8,200,000 − 310,000 = 7,890,000.00. The benefit obligation is compared separately.

title: Indirect operating bridge • case 1
prompt: Profit before tax is LKR 1,100,000. It includes depreciation of 200,000 and a disposal gain of 50,000. Trade receivables increase 81,000; inventory increases 60,000; trade payables increase 40,000. No other adjustments. Find cash generated from operations BEFORE tax and interest cash-flow deductions.
explanation: Profit + depreciation − disposal gain − receivable increase − inventory increase + payable increase = 1,149,000.00. This is before tax and interest cash deductions.

title: Indexed land carrying amount • case 1
prompt: An entity with a hyperinflationary functional currency bought non-depreciable land for LKR 1,050,000 when the general price index was 120. Reporting-date index is 180. The land remains at historical cost before restatement; no impairment applies. Calculate its restated amount.
explanation: Restate historical non-monetary cost by closing index / acquisition index: 1,050,000 × 180 / 120 = 1,575,000.00. Monetary balances are treated differently.

title: Convertible debt equity residual • case 1
prompt: A compound convertible bond is issued for LKR 2,100,000. The liability component, valued using the market rate for similar debt without conversion, is 1,640,000. No transaction costs or tax effects apply. Find the equity component at initial recognition.
explanation: Allocate the liability first; equity is the residual: 2,100,000 − 1,640,000 = 460,000.00. Subsequent changes in the market value of conversion rights do not remeasure this equity component.

title: Midyear share issue EPS • case 1
prompt: Profit attributable to parent is LKR 1,900,000. Deductible equity preference dividends are 100,000. There are 200,000 ordinary shares from 1 January, and 100,000 new shares are issued for full market value on 1 July. Year ends 31 December. Use six months for each half. Find basic EPS in LKR per share.
explanation: Weighted shares = 200,000 + 100,000 × 6/12 = 250,000. Ordinary earnings = 1,800,000. EPS = 7.20 per share.

title: Treasury-share dilution • case 1
prompt: Ordinary earnings are LKR 2,100,000; weighted ordinary shares are 1,000,000. There are 200,000 options outstanding all year, exercise price LKR 20, average market price LKR 40. All conditions for inclusion are met; no earnings adjustment or other dilution applies. Find diluted EPS in LKR per share.
explanation: Assumed proceeds repurchase 200,000 × 20/40 = 100,000 shares. Incremental shares = 100,000. Diluted denominator = 1,100,000; EPS = 1.91 per share.

title: Interim tax catch-up • case 1
prompt: At the half-year, year-to-date pretax profit is LKR 3,100,000. The best estimate of the weighted annual effective tax rate is 28%. First-quarter income tax expense was 350,000. No discrete items, losses or jurisdiction complications apply. What tax expense is recognised in the second quarter alone?
explanation: Cumulative half-year tax expense = 3,100,000 × 28% = 868,000.00. Deduct the 350,000 already recognised; quarter-two charge = 518,000.00. Rate is a case assumption.

title: Impairment reversal cap • case 1
prompt: A depreciable asset other than goodwill now carries at LKR 610,000. Without past impairment it would carry at 815,000 after normal depreciation. Revised recoverable amount is 920,000. No revaluation model applies. Calculate the impairment reversal permitted.
explanation: Restored amount is capped at the no-impairment carrying amount 815,000, which is below recoverable amount. Reversal = 815,000 − 610,000 = 205,000.00.

title: Discounted restoration obligation • case 1
prompt: A present restoration obligation requires a single payment of LKR 1,050,000 exactly two years from the reporting date. The appropriate pre-tax discount rate is 10%, with risks not double-counted in cash flows. Time value is material. Find the provision at the reporting date.
explanation: Provision = expected payment / (1 + discount rate)² = 1,050,000 / 1.10² = 867,768.60. Unwinding is recognised over time.

title: Unwinding a discounted provision • case 1
prompt: A restoration provision opens at LKR 520,000. Its discount rate is 8%; one full year passes. There are no payments or changes in timing, cash estimates or discount rate. What finance cost arises solely from unwinding the discount?
explanation: The passage-of-time increase is opening provision × 8% = 41,600.00. This unwinding is recognised as a borrowing cost rather than a fresh asset expenditure in this case.

title: Development recognition boundary • case 1
prompt: A project incurs research costs of LKR 155,000, then development costs of 100,000 BEFORE all recognition criteria are met. After meeting every criterion, directly attributable development costs are 310,000 and later 210,000. The asset is not yet available for use. What cost is recognised as the intangible asset?
explanation: Capitalise only costs from the date all recognition criteria are first met: 310,000 + 210,000 = 520,000.00. Previously expensed expenditure is not reinstated.

title: Investment property value bridge • case 1
prompt: Investment property uses the fair value model. Opening fair value is LKR 5,100,000; closing fair value is 5,410,000. No acquisitions, disposals, transfers, rental accrual effects or capital expenditure occur. What fair-value gain is recognised in profit or loss?
explanation: Fair-value gain = closing value − opening value = 310,000.00. No depreciation is separately charged under this model.

title: Harvest measurement into inventory • case 1
prompt: At harvest, 1,100 kg of produce has a market price of LKR 500 per kg and costs to sell of LKR 20 per kg. Assume no other valuation adjustments. What is its total initial cost for subsequent inventory accounting?
explanation: At harvest, fair value less costs to sell = 1,100 × (500 − 20) = 528,000.00. This becomes cost when applying LKAS 2 afterwards.

title: First-year equity award accrual • case 1
prompt: A four-year service-vesting equity option grant has 100 options per employee and grant-date fair value LKR 40 per option. At year-one end, 52 employees are expected to satisfy the service condition. No market or other performance conditions apply. Find cumulative employee expense after one full year.
explanation: Expected total grant value = 52 × 100 × 40 = 208,000. Recognise one quarter for the first year of service: 52,000.00.

title: Partial goodwill method • case 1
prompt: An acquirer purchases 80% of a business for LKR 2,600,000. Identifiable net assets at acquisition have fair value 2,450,000. NCI is measured at its proportionate share of identifiable net assets. No previous holding or other adjustments exist. Find goodwill.
explanation: Proportionate NCI = 20% × 2,450,000 = 490,000.00. Goodwill = consideration + NCI − net assets = 640,000.00. This differs from the full-goodwill fair-value-NCI approach.

title: Withdrawn sale measurement • case 1
prompt: An asset ceases to meet held-for-sale criteria. Its carrying amount immediately before initial held-for-sale classification was LKR 1,550,000. Depreciation that would have been recognised since then is 150,000; no revaluation applies. Recoverable amount at the decision not to sell is 1,610,000. Find its carrying amount on reclassification.
explanation: Adjusted pre-classification amount = 1,550,000 − 150,000 = 1,400,000. Compare with recoverable amount 1,610,000; take the lower = 1,400,000.00.

title: Segment profit threshold • case 1
prompt: Profitable operating segments have combined profits of LKR 4,100,000. Loss-making segments have combined losses of 2,050,000 in absolute value. Calculate the absolute profit-or-loss threshold for the 10% quantitative test. Do not offset profits against losses.
explanation: Use 10% of the greater of combined profitable-segment profits and absolute loss-making-segment losses: 10% × 4,100,000 = 410,000.00.

title: Reportable external revenue gap • case 1
prompt: Total entity external revenue is LKR 11,000,000. Currently identified reportable segments cover 62% of it. What minimum additional external revenue must be included by identifying further reportable segments to reach the 75% coverage requirement?
explanation: Required coverage = 75% of total. Current coverage = 62%. Minimum gap = 13% × 11,000,000 = 1,430,000.00. Actual added segments may exceed this minimum.

title: Discount bond year-one bridge • case 1
prompt: A qualifying amortised-cost debt asset has face value LKR 1,050,000. Its initial gross carrying amount, including costs, is 97% of face. Its effective rate is 7%, while a 5%-of-face coupon is received at year end. Ignore impairment and other cash flows. Find closing gross carrying amount.
explanation: Opening = 1,018,500.00. EIR interest = opening × 7% = 71,295.00; coupon = 52,500.00. Closing = opening + EIR interest − coupon = 1,037,295.00.

title: Probability-weighted ECL scenarios • case 1
prompt: A two-scenario ECL model has exposure LKR 2,100,000. In a base scenario (70% probability), expected discounted cash shortfall is 2% of exposure; in a downside scenario (30%), it is 12%. These rates already include loss severity, default risk and discounting. Find probability-weighted ECL.
explanation: Weight the scenario losses: 2,100,000 × (70% × 2% + 30% × 12%) = 2,100,000 × 5% = 105,000.00. Do not apply PD or LGD again because the scenario rates already include them.

title: Upstream profit and NCI • case 1
prompt: Parent owns 75% of S. S reports profit LKR 730,000. Consolidation requires extra depreciation of 100,000 on acquisition-date fair-value adjustments. An upstream inventory sale by S contains unrealised profit of 81,000 remaining in the group. No tax or other adjustments apply. Find profit attributable to NCI.
explanation: Adjusted subsidiary profit = 730,000 − 100,000 − 81,000 = 549,000. Upstream profit elimination affects S’s adjusted result. NCI = 25% × adjusted profit = 137,250.00.

title: Joint operation result • case 1
prompt: A joint operator has a 40% direct share of a joint operation’s revenue and expenses. Total third-party revenue is LKR 4,100,000, related expenses are 2,650,000. There are no sales between operators, other rights, tax or adjustments. Find the net contribution to the operator’s profit.
explanation: Recognise the share of revenue and expenses according to rights and obligations: 40% × (4,100,000 − 2,650,000) = 580,000.00. This is joint-operation accounting, not a net investment under the equity method.

title: Transport versus transaction costs • case 1
prompt: A commodity quantity of 1,050 units is located away from its accessible principal market. Quoted market price is LKR 600 per unit. Transport to that market costs 30 per unit; transaction costs are 10 per unit. Location is an asset characteristic. Find total fair value under SLFRS 13.
explanation: Adjust for transport because location is an asset characteristic, but do not deduct transaction costs from fair value: 1,050 × (600 − 30) = 598,500.00.

title: Financing component in a sale • case 1
prompt: Control of goods transfers today. A fixed payment of LKR 1,050,000 is due exactly two years later. A significant financing component exists; the appropriate annual discount rate is 10%. No other performance obligations or adjustments apply. Find revenue at transfer, excluding later financing income.
explanation: Revenue reflects the cash selling price: 1,050,000 / 1.10² = 867,768.60. The remaining amount is recognised as financing income over time under the relevant requirements.

title: Billings ahead of performance • case 1
prompt: For one contract, cumulative unconditional billings are LKR 2,100,000, cumulative revenue recognised is 1,470,000.00, and cash collected is 1,050,000.00. The uncollected invoice remains a separate receivable. There are no other contract balances or taxes. What is the contract liability?
explanation: Billings ahead of recognised performance = 2,100,000 − 1,470,000.00 = 630,000.00. The receivable equals billings less collections and is separately presented; it is not deducted again from this contract liability.

title: ROU depreciation period • case 1
prompt: Initial right-of-use asset is LKR 1,050,000. Lease term is four years; the underlying asset’s useful life is six years. Ownership does not transfer and purchase is not reasonably certain. Straight-line depreciation starts on 1 January; no residual value, impairment or remeasurement applies. Find full-year depreciation.

title: Initial CSM without day-one profit • case 1

explanation: Adjust for transport because location is an asset characteristic, but do not deduct transaction costs from fair value: 1,450 × (600 − 30) = 826,500.00.

title: Financing component in a sale • case 9
prompt: Control of goods transfers today. A fixed payment of LKR 1,450,000 is due exactly two years later. A significant financing component exists; the appropriate annual discount rate is 10%. No other performance obligations or adjustments apply. Find revenue at transfer, excluding later financing income.
explanation: Revenue reflects the cash selling price: 1,450,000 / 1.10² = 1,198,347.11. The remaining amount is recognised as financing income over time under the relevant requirements.

title: Billings ahead of performance • case 9
prompt: For one contract, cumulative unconditional billings are LKR 2,900,000, cumulative revenue recognised is 2,030,000.00, and cash collected is 1,450,000.00. The uncollected invoice remains a separate receivable. There are no other contract balances or taxes. What is the contract liability?
explanation: Billings ahead of recognised performance = 2,900,000 − 2,030,000.00 = 870,000.00. The receivable equals billings less collections and is separately presented; it is not deducted again from this contract liability.

title: ROU depreciation period • case 9
prompt: Initial right-of-use asset is LKR 1,450,000. Lease term is four years; the underlying asset’s useful life is six years. Ownership does not transfer and purchase is not reasonably certain. Straight-line depreciation starts on 1 January; no residual value, impairment or remeasurement applies. Find full-year depreciation.
explanation: Without ownership transfer or a reasonably certain purchase, depreciate to the earlier of ROU useful life and lease term. Here four years: 1,450,000 / 4 = 362,500.00.

title: Initial CSM without day-one profit • case 9
prompt: Apply the SLFRS 17 general model. At initial recognition, a group has present value of future premium inflows LKR 1,950,000, present value of future outflows 1,380,000, and risk adjustment 109,000. No cash flows occur on recognition, no previously recognised balances exist, and the group is not onerous. Find the initial contractual service margin.
explanation: Net fulfilment cash inflow before CSM = inflows − outflows − risk adjustment = 461,000.00. The CSM offsets that net inflow so no day-one profit is recognised under these assumptions.

title: General borrowing capitalisation • case 9
prompt: Weighted-average qualifying-asset expenditure during the eligible period is LKR 1,725,000. The appropriate capitalisation rate on general borrowings is 8%. Actual borrowing costs incurred are 12% of a borrowing balance of 2,900,000. There are no specific borrowings, interruptions or other limits. Find eligible capitalised borrowing costs.
explanation: Apply the general capitalisation rate to weighted expenditure: 1,725,000 × 8% = 138,000.00. This is below actual borrowing costs of 348,000.00, so capitalise 138,000.00. The actual-cost ceiling is not binding.

title: Deferred grant release • case 10
prompt: A depreciable asset has a five-year life and no residual value. An asset-related grant of LKR 600,000 is recognised as deferred income on 1 January, when the asset becomes available for use. All conditions are met. Straight-line depreciation is appropriate. How much grant income is recognised for the full year?
explanation: Release the deferred grant systematically over the five-year life: 600,000 / 5 = 120,000.00. Receipt is not the income pattern.

title: Grant deducted from asset • case 10
prompt: A company elects to deduct an asset grant from the asset carrying amount. Cost is LKR 3,000,000, grant 600,000, estimated residual value 100,000, and life five years. The asset is available for the full year. Find annual straight-line depreciation under this presentation.
explanation: Net depreciable amount = 3,000,000 − 600,000 − 100,000 = 2,300,000. Divide by five = 460,000.00. The grant affects expense through reduced depreciation.

title: Defined benefit net interest • case 10
prompt: Opening defined benefit obligation is LKR 6,000,000; opening plan assets are 4,500,000. Discount rate is 8%. There are no contributions, benefit payments or other timing adjustments during the year, and no asset-ceiling effect. Calculate net interest expense.
explanation: Opening net liability = 1,500,000. Apply the 8% discount rate: net interest expense = 120,000.00. Do not use gross obligation interest alone.

title: Pension liability roll-forward • case 10
prompt: Opening net defined benefit liability is LKR 1,500,000. Current service cost is 200,000; net interest expense is 120,000.00; employer contributions are 150,000; net remeasurement LOSS is 90,000. No other movements or asset ceiling apply. What is closing net liability?
explanation: Closing net liability = opening + service cost + net interest + remeasurement loss − employer contributions = 1,760,000.00. Remeasurement goes to OCI but still changes the liability.

title: Plan net assets for benefits • case 10
prompt: A retirement plan has assets of LKR 10,000,000, operating liabilities of 400,000, and actuarial present value of promised benefits of 9,000,000. Calculate net assets AVAILABLE for benefits, rather than the funding deficit.
explanation: Net assets available for benefits = plan assets − liabilities other than the actuarial present value of promised benefits: 10,000,000 − 400,000 = 9,600,000.00. The benefit obligation is compared separately.

title: Indirect operating bridge • case 10
prompt: Profit before tax is LKR 2,000,000. It includes depreciation of 200,000 and a disposal gain of 50,000. Trade receivables increase 90,000; inventory increases 60,000; trade payables increase 40,000. No other adjustments. Find cash generated from operations BEFORE tax and interest cash-flow deductions.
explanation: Profit + depreciation − disposal gain − receivable increase − inventory increase + payable increase = 2,040,000.00. This is before tax and interest cash deductions.

title: Indexed land carrying amount • case 10
prompt: An entity with a hyperinflationary functional currency bought non-depreciable land for LKR 1,500,000 when the general price index was 120. Reporting-date index is 180. The land remains at historical cost before restatement; no impairment applies. Calculate its restated amount.
explanation: Restate historical non-monetary cost by closing index / acquisition index: 1,500,000 × 180 / 120 = 2,250,000.00. Monetary balances are treated differently.

title: Convertible debt equity residual • case 10
prompt: A compound convertible bond is issued for LKR 3,000,000. The liability component, valued using the market rate for similar debt without conversion, is 2,000,000. No transaction costs or tax effects apply. Find the equity component at initial recognition.
explanation: Allocate the liability first; equity is the residual: 3,000,000 − 2,000,000 = 1,000,000.00. Subsequent changes in the market value of conversion rights do not remeasure this equity component.

title: Midyear share issue EPS • case 10
prompt: Profit attributable to parent is LKR 2,800,000. Deductible equity preference dividends are 100,000. There are 200,000 ordinary shares from 1 January, and 100,000 new shares are issued for full market value on 1 July. Year ends 31 December. Use six months for each half. Find basic EPS in LKR per share.
explanation: Weighted shares = 200,000 + 100,000 × 6/12 = 250,000. Ordinary earnings = 2,700,000. EPS = 10.80 per share.

title: Treasury-share dilution • case 10
prompt: Ordinary earnings are LKR 3,000,000; weighted ordinary shares are 1,000,000. There are 200,000 options outstanding all year, exercise price LKR 20, average market price LKR 40. All conditions for inclusion are met; no earnings adjustment or other dilution applies. Find diluted EPS in LKR per share.
explanation: Assumed proceeds repurchase 200,000 × 20/40 = 100,000 shares. Incremental shares = 100,000. Diluted denominator = 1,100,000; EPS = 2.73 per share.

title: Interim tax catch-up • case 10
prompt: At the half-year, year-to-date pretax profit is LKR 4,000,000. The best estimate of the weighted annual effective tax rate is 28%. First-quarter income tax expense was 350,000. No discrete items, losses or jurisdiction complications apply. What tax expense is recognised in the second quarter alone?
explanation: Cumulative half-year tax expense = 4,000,000 × 28% = 1,120,000.00. Deduct the 350,000 already recognised; quarter-two charge = 770,000.00. Rate is a case assumption.

title: Impairment reversal cap • case 10
prompt: A depreciable asset other than goodwill now carries at LKR 700,000. Without past impairment it would carry at 950,000 after normal depreciation. Revised recoverable amount is 1,100,000. No revaluation model applies. Calculate the impairment reversal permitted.
explanation: Restored amount is capped at the no-impairment carrying amount 950,000, which is below recoverable amount. Reversal = 950,000 − 700,000 = 250,000.00.

title: Discounted restoration obligation • case 10
prompt: A present restoration obligation requires a single payment of LKR 1,500,000 exactly two years from the reporting date. The appropriate pre-tax discount rate is 10%, with risks not double-counted in cash flows. Time value is material. Find the provision at the reporting date.
explanation: Provision = expected payment / (1 + discount rate)² = 1,500,000 / 1.10² = 1,239,669.42. Unwinding is recognised over time.

title: Unwinding a discounted provision • case 10
prompt: A restoration provision opens at LKR 700,000. Its discount rate is 8%; one full year passes. There are no payments or changes in timing, cash estimates or discount rate. What finance cost arises solely from unwinding the discount?
explanation: The passage-of-time increase is opening provision × 8% = 56,000.00. This unwinding is recognised as a borrowing cost rather than a fresh asset expenditure in this case.

title: Development recognition boundary • case 10
prompt: A project incurs research costs of LKR 200,000, then development costs of 100,000 BEFORE all recognition criteria are met. After meeting every criterion, directly attributable development costs are 400,000 and later 300,000. The asset is not yet available for use. What cost is recognised as the intangible asset?
explanation: Capitalise only costs from the date all recognition criteria are first met: 400,000 + 300,000 = 700,000.00. Previously expensed expenditure is not reinstated.

title: Investment property value bridge • case 10
prompt: Investment property uses the fair value model. Opening fair value is LKR 6,000,000; closing fair value is 6,400,000. No acquisitions, disposals, transfers, rental accrual effects or capital expenditure occur. What fair-value gain is recognised in profit or loss?
explanation: Fair-value gain = closing value − opening value = 400,000.00. No depreciation is separately charged under this model.

title: Harvest measurement into inventory • case 10
prompt: At harvest, 2,000 kg of produce has a market price of LKR 500 per kg and costs to sell of LKR 20 per kg. Assume no other valuation adjustments. What is its total initial cost for subsequent inventory accounting?
explanation: At harvest, fair value less costs to sell = 2,000 × (500 − 20) = 960,000.00. This becomes cost when applying LKAS 2 afterwards.

title: First-year equity award accrual • case 10
prompt: A four-year service-vesting equity option grant has 100 options per employee and grant-date fair value LKR 40 per option. At year-one end, 70 employees are expected to satisfy the service condition. No market or other performance conditions apply. Find cumulative employee expense after one full year.
explanation: Expected total grant value = 70 × 100 × 40 = 280,000. Recognise one quarter for the first year of service: 70,000.00.

title: Partial goodwill method • case 10
prompt: An acquirer purchases 80% of a business for LKR 3,500,000. Identifiable net assets at acquisition have fair value 2,900,000. NCI is measured at its proportionate share of identifiable net assets. No previous holding or other adjustments exist. Find goodwill.
explanation: Proportionate NCI = 20% × 2,900,000 = 580,000.00. Goodwill = consideration + NCI − net assets = 1,180,000.00. This differs from the full-goodwill fair-value-NCI approach.

title: Withdrawn sale measurement • case 10
prompt: An asset ceases to meet held-for-sale criteria. Its carrying amount immediately before initial held-for-sale classification was LKR 2,000,000. Depreciation that would have been recognised since then is 150,000; no revaluation applies. Recoverable amount at the decision not to sell is 1,700,000. Find its carrying amount on reclassification.
explanation: Adjusted pre-classification amount = 2,000,000 − 150,000 = 1,850,000. Compare with recoverable amount 1,700,000; take the lower = 1,700,000.00.

title: Segment profit threshold • case 10
prompt: Profitable operating segments have combined profits of LKR 5,000,000. Loss-making segments have combined losses of 2,500,000 in absolute value. Calculate the absolute profit-or-loss threshold for the 10% quantitative test. Do not offset profits against losses.
explanation: Use 10% of the greater of combined profitable-segment profits and absolute loss-making-segment losses: 10% × 5,000,000 = 500,000.00.

title: Reportable external revenue gap • case 10
prompt: Total entity external revenue is LKR 20,000,000. Currently identified reportable segments cover 62% of it. What minimum additional external revenue must be included by identifying further reportable segments to reach the 75% coverage requirement?
explanation: Required coverage = 75% of total. Current coverage = 62%. Minimum gap = 13% × 20,000,000 = 2,600,000.00. Actual added segments may exceed this minimum.

title: Discount bond year-one bridge • case 10
prompt: A qualifying amortised-cost debt asset has face value LKR 1,500,000. Its initial gross carrying amount, including costs, is 97% of face. Its effective rate is 7%, while a 5%-of-face coupon is received at year end. Ignore impairment and other cash flows. Find closing gross carrying amount.
explanation: Opening = 1,455,000.00. EIR interest = opening × 7% = 101,850.00; coupon = 75,000.00. Closing = opening + EIR interest − coupon = 1,481,850.00.

title: Probability-weighted ECL scenarios • case 10
prompt: A two-scenario ECL model has exposure LKR 3,000,000. In a base scenario (70% probability), expected discounted cash shortfall is 2% of exposure; in a downside scenario (30%), it is 12%. These rates already include loss severity, default risk and discounting. Find probability-weighted ECL.
explanation: Weight the scenario losses: 3,000,000 × (70% × 2% + 30% × 12%) = 3,000,000 × 5% = 150,000.00. Do not apply PD or LGD again because the scenario rates already include them.

title: Upstream profit and NCI • case 10
prompt: Parent owns 75% of S. S reports profit LKR 1,000,000. Consolidation requires extra depreciation of 100,000 on acquisition-date fair-value adjustments. An upstream inventory sale by S contains unrealised profit of 90,000 remaining in the group. No tax or other adjustments apply. Find profit attributable to NCI.
explanation: Adjusted subsidiary profit = 1,000,000 − 100,000 − 90,000 = 810,000. Upstream profit elimination affects S’s adjusted result. NCI = 25% × adjusted profit = 202,500.00.

title: Joint operation result • case 10
prompt: A joint operator has a 40% direct share of a joint operation’s revenue and expenses. Total third-party revenue is LKR 5,000,000, related expenses are 3,100,000. There are no sales between operators, other rights, tax or adjustments. Find the net contribution to the operator’s profit.
explanation: Recognise the share of revenue and expenses according to rights and obligations: 40% × (5,000,000 − 3,100,000) = 760,000.00. This is joint-operation accounting, not a net investment under the equity method.

title: Transport versus transaction costs • case 10
prompt: A commodity quantity of 1,500 units is located away from its accessible principal market. Quoted market price is LKR 600 per unit. Transport to that market costs 30 per unit; transaction costs are 10 per unit. Location is an asset characteristic. Find total fair value under SLFRS 13.
explanation: Adjust for transport because location is an asset characteristic, but do not deduct transaction costs from fair value: 1,500 × (600 − 30) = 855,000.00.

title: Financing component in a sale • case 10
prompt: Control of goods transfers today. A fixed payment of LKR 1,500,000 is due exactly two years later. A significant financing component exists; the appropriate annual discount rate is 10%. No other performance obligations or adjustments apply. Find revenue at transfer, excluding later financing income.
explanation: Revenue reflects the cash selling price: 1,500,000 / 1.10² = 1,239,669.42. The remaining amount is recognised as financing income over time under the relevant requirements.

title: Billings ahead of performance • case 10
prompt: For one contract, cumulative unconditional billings are LKR 3,000,000, cumulative revenue recognised is 2,100,000.00, and cash collected is 1,500,000.00. The uncollected invoice remains a separate receivable. There are no other contract balances or taxes. What is the contract liability?
explanation: Billings ahead of recognised performance = 3,000,000 − 2,100,000.00 = 900,000.00. The receivable equals billings less collections and is separately presented; it is not deducted again from this contract liability.

title: ROU depreciation period • case 10
prompt: Initial right-of-use asset is LKR 1,500,000. Lease term is four years; the underlying asset’s useful life is six years. Ownership does not transfer and purchase is not reasonably certain. Straight-line depreciation starts on 1 January; no residual value, impairment or remeasurement applies. Find full-year depreciation.
explanation: Without ownership transfer or a reasonably certain purchase, depreciate to the earlier of ROU useful life and lease term. Here four years: 1,500,000 / 4 = 375,000.00.

title: Initial CSM without day-one profit • case 10
prompt: Apply the SLFRS 17 general model. At initial recognition, a group has present value of future premium inflows LKR 2,000,000, present value of future outflows 1,400,000, and risk adjustment 110,000. No cash flows occur on recognition, no previously recognised balances exist, and the group is not onerous. Find the initial contractual service margin.
explanation: Net fulfilment cash inflow before CSM = inflows − outflows − risk adjustment = 490,000.00. The CSM offsets that net inflow so no day-one profit is recognised under these assumptions.

title: General borrowing capitalisation • case 10
prompt: Weighted-average qualifying-asset expenditure during the eligible period is LKR 1,750,000. The appropriate capitalisation rate on general borrowings is 8%. Actual borrowing costs incurred are 12% of a borrowing balance of 3,000,000. There are no specific borrowings, interruptions or other limits. Find eligible capitalised borrowing costs.
explanation: Apply the general capitalisation rate to weighted expenditure: 1,750,000 × 8% = 140,000.00. This is below actual borrowing costs of 360,000.00, so capitalise 140,000.00. The actual-cost ceiling is not binding.

title: A series is one obligation
prompt: A cleaning contract promises the same distinct daily service for a year. Each day meets over-time recognition criteria and the same progress method would apply to each. How are the promises identified?
options: A single performance obligation comprising the qualifying series
One goods obligation recognised on day one
No performance obligation until year end
explanation: A series of distinct goods or services is one performance obligation when they are substantially the same and meet the specified transfer-pattern criteria.

title: A renewal discount earned today
prompt: Buying the current service gives a customer an exclusive renewal discount beyond discounts available to similar customers without the current contract. The option provides a material right. What follows?
options: Account for that material right as a separate performance obligation
Ignore it because renewal is optional
Recognise all allocated option revenue immediately
Record only a provision for next year’s marketing costs
explanation: A customer option providing a material right is a separate performance obligation, with consideration allocated to it and revenue recognised when exercised or expired.

title: Performance before an unconditional right
prompt: An entity recognises revenue for completed work, but payment remains conditional on a further performance milestone beyond the passage of time. What describes its right to consideration?
options: A contract asset, subject to the relevant conditions
An unconditional trade receivable solely because revenue exists
An equity investment in the customer
explanation: A receivable is unconditional except for the passage of time. A conditional right arising from performance is presented as a contract asset.

title: A genuine bill-and-hold request
prompt: A customer requests a substantive delay in physical delivery. Goods are separately identified, ready for transfer, and cannot be used or redirected by the seller. All other control-transfer conditions are met. Is physical possession always necessary for revenue?
options: No; the qualifying bill-and-hold arrangement can transfer control before delivery
Yes; physical delivery is the sole possible control criterion
No; invoicing alone always transfers control
Yes; revenue must wait until the customer resells the goods
explanation: Bill-and-hold revenue requires the general control assessment and specific criteria, including a substantive reason, separate identification, readiness and inability to redirect the goods.

title: Consignment is not a sale
prompt: A supplier delivers goods to a dealer but can require their return or transfer elsewhere. The dealer has no unconditional obligation to pay before selling them to end customers. What should the supplier assess?
options: A consignment arrangement in which delivery need not transfer control
A completed sale merely because the goods moved physically
A lease liability for the dealer’s entire premises
Automatic revenue equal to the dealer’s list price
explanation: Indicators of consignment include continued supplier control, an ability to require return or transfer, and no unconditional dealer payment obligation.

title: Repurchase promise changes the substance
prompt: A seller has an enforceable forward obligation to repurchase an asset for an amount equal to or above its original selling price. The specified financing-arrangement rules apply. How is the transaction treated?
options: As a financing arrangement, retaining the asset and recognising a financial liability
As an ordinary sale with all profit recognised immediately
As an equity issuance by the customer
As a contract asset equal to the future repurchase price
explanation: A forward or call repurchase arrangement at or above the original selling price is generally a financing arrangement under the specified rules; the asset remains recognised.

title: Leveraged returns are not basic lending
prompt: A debt contract multiplies changes in an equity index to determine the lender’s return. The cash flows fail the solely-principal-and-interest condition. It is not a designated hedge. Can a hold-to-collect intention alone justify amortised cost?
options: No; the asset generally falls into FVTPL when the SPPI condition fails
Yes; business-model intent overrides all contractual terms
Yes; any instrument legally called debt is amortised cost
No; the equity method is mandatory
explanation: Amortised cost requires both the relevant business model and qualifying contractual cash flows. Exposure to leveraged equity returns does not represent basic principal and interest.

title: Equity FVOCI on disposal
prompt: An eligible non-trading equity investment has an irrevocable FVOCI election. It is sold at a gain. What happens to the cumulative fair-value gain in OCI?
options: It is not recycled to profit or loss; a transfer within equity is permitted
It is always recycled exactly like debt FVOCI
It becomes operating revenue on disposal
It reverses every dividend previously recognised
explanation: For the equity FVOCI election, amounts presented in OCI are not subsequently transferred to profit or loss, although they may be transferred within equity.

title: Purchased credit-impaired assets
prompt: A purchased financial asset is credit-impaired at initial recognition. Which interest approach applies to its amortised-cost measurement?
options: Use a credit-adjusted effective interest rate incorporating initial expected credit losses
Use the risk-free rate and ignore expected losses
Always calculate interest on contractual face value regardless of purchase price
Treat the initial discount entirely as day-one interest revenue
explanation: Purchased or originated credit-impaired assets use a credit-adjusted EIR; only cumulative changes in lifetime ECL since initial recognition are recognised as the loss allowance.

title: Simplified trade receivable impairment
prompt: A trade receivable under SLFRS 15 has no significant financing component. Which expected-credit-loss approach is required?
options: Lifetime ECL under the simplified approach
Zero ECL until a customer misses a payment
The LKAS 39 incurred-loss model by default
explanation: For the specified trade receivables, the loss allowance is always measured at lifetime expected credit losses without tracking a significant increase in credit risk.

title: A substantial debt modification
prompt: A borrower exchanges debt with the same lender. The contractual terms are substantially different under the relevant qualitative and quantitative assessment. What is the general accounting consequence?
options: Derecognise the original financial liability and recognise the new liability
Always carry forward the old liability unchanged
Recognise a revaluation reserve instead of a new liability
Treat every lender payment as a dividend
explanation: An exchange or modification with substantially different terms is an extinguishment of the original liability and recognition of a new one. The assessment includes the specified discounted-cash-flow test and other relevant terms.

title: One sale is not a new business model
prompt: A treasury team sells one hold-to-collect bond for liquidity reasons. Management says this automatically requires reclassifying every remaining asset. Which principle applies?
options: Reclassification occurs only when the business model for managing financial assets changes
Every individual sale automatically reclassifies all assets
Reclassification is allowed whenever it improves profit
A change in fair value alone determines the business model
explanation: Business-model changes must be significant to the entity’s operations and demonstrable; changes in intention for particular assets do not by themselves qualify.

title: Decision maker or agent?
prompt: An investment manager makes investment decisions but its delegated rights, remuneration and other exposures establish that it acts as an agent. Does exercising those delegated rights give it control by itself?
options: No; an agent does not control the investee through those delegated decision rights
Yes; every investment manager consolidates every managed fund
Yes; receiving a fee alone establishes control
No; only legal ownership can ever establish control
explanation: The principal-agent assessment considers the scope of authority, other parties’ rights, remuneration and exposure to variable returns. Delegated decision-making power held as an agent does not confer control.

title: Investment entity exception
prompt: A parent meets the definition of an investment entity. A subsidiary is held as an investment and is not a service subsidiary required to be consolidated. What exception generally applies?
options: Measure the investment subsidiary at FVTPL rather than consolidate it
Always consolidate without assessing the exception
explanation: An investment entity generally measures qualifying subsidiaries at FVTPL. A subsidiary providing investment-related services may be subject to a separate consolidation requirement.

title: Potential votes must be substantive
prompt: An investor holds potential voting rights. What matters when assessing whether those rights contribute to power?
options: Whether the rights are substantive, considering practical ability to exercise when relevant decisions must be made
Their existence on paper always gives control
Only their nominal number, with no timing assessment
Whether management expects the investee to report a profit
explanation: The assessment considers substantive rights, practical barriers and when relevant-activity decisions need to be made. Potential rights are not automatically power.

title: Uniform group policies
prompt: A subsidiary uses an accounting policy different from the group’s for like transactions in similar circumstances. What is generally needed in preparing consolidated statements?
options: Make appropriate adjustments to apply uniform accounting policies
Retain the policy solely because the subsidiary is overseas
Offset the difference against all dividends
Ignore it whenever the subsidiary has minority shareholders
explanation: Consolidated statements use uniform accounting policies for like transactions and events in similar circumstances; appropriate adjustments are made when required.

title: Acquiring assets without a business
prompt: An acquired set does not meet the definition of a business. How does that affect the acquisition method?
options: It is an asset acquisition outside business-combination accounting, and does not generate goodwill
Every purchase of several assets must generate goodwill
The whole price is expensed immediately
The buyer must recognise a bargain purchase gain in every case
explanation: An acquisition of an asset or a group of assets that is not a business is outside SLFRS 3’s business-combination scope; the cost is allocated under the applicable asset-acquisition requirements.

title: Contingent consideration after acquisition
prompt: Liability-classified contingent consideration changes in fair value due to events arising after the acquisition date. It is not a measurement-period adjustment. What generally follows?
options: Remeasure through profit or loss under the applicable requirements
Adjust goodwill for every subsequent change
Freeze the liability permanently at its acquisition-date amount
Reclassify the change as a dividend
explanation: Subsequent fair-value changes in liability-classified contingent consideration that are not measurement-period adjustments are generally recognised in profit or loss. Equity-classified consideration has different requirements.

title: The measurement-period clock
prompt: An acquirer obtains information nine months after acquisition. The information concerns a new post-acquisition event rather than facts existing at acquisition. Is it a measurement-period adjustment just because it arrived within one year?
options: No; the nature of the information must relate to acquisition-date facts and circumstances
Yes; every change within twelve months adjusts goodwill
Yes; the timing alone determines the accounting
No; measurement-period adjustments are never permitted
explanation: The measurement period permits provisional acquisition accounting to reflect new information about acquisition-date conditions, and cannot exceed one year. It is not a general twelve-month goodwill-adjustment window.

title: Pure sales-based rent
prompt: A lessee pays additional rent equal to a percentage of actual sales. The amount is neither in-substance fixed nor dependent on an index or rate. What is the general treatment of that variable payment?
options: Exclude it from initial lease liability and recognise it when the triggering event occurs, unless another standard requires inclusion in an asset
Include an unlimited sales forecast in initial liability
Recognise all possible variable rent as goodwill
Always ignore it even after sales occur
