explanation: Variable lease payments outside the liability measurement are recognised when the event or condition triggering payment occurs, subject to relevant asset-cost requirements.

title: Restoration belongs in two balances
prompt: A lessee has an initial obligation to restore the leased premises that meets LKAS 37 recognition requirements. The related costs do not arise from producing inventory. Which general treatment applies?
options: Include the estimate in ROU asset cost and recognise a separate restoration provision
Include it only in the lease liability as rent
Recognise no amount until the final cash payment
Recognise it only as a reduction in revenue
explanation: The ROU asset includes the estimated restoration costs, with the obligation recognised and measured under LKAS 37 rather than treated as a lease payment liability.

title: Operating lessor initial direct costs
prompt: A lessor incurs qualifying initial direct costs to obtain an operating lease. What is the general treatment?
options: Add them to the carrying amount of the underlying asset and recognise as expense over the lease term on the same basis as lease income
Always expense them on day one without considering the standard
Recognise them as a financial asset equal to total future rentals
Credit them to a revaluation reserve
explanation: Qualifying initial direct costs of an operating lease are added to the underlying asset and expensed over the lease term on the same basis as lease income.

title: Sale-and-leaseback that is not a sale
prompt: A transfer of an asset in a purported sale-and-leaseback fails the SLFRS 15 sale requirements. How does the seller-lessee generally account for the transfer?
options: Continue recognising the asset and recognise a financial liability equal to the proceeds
Derecognise the asset and recognise the full sale gain
Recognise only a new intangible asset
Recognise proceeds directly in share capital
explanation: When the transfer is not a sale, the seller-lessee continues recognising the asset and accounts for the transfer proceeds as a financial liability.

title: A proposed tax rate is not enacted
prompt: A new tax rate has merely been proposed before year end and is not enacted or substantively enacted. The existing rate remains enacted. Which rate basis applies to deferred tax?
options: Rates enacted or substantively enacted by the reporting date and expected on reversal
The highest rate ever used by the entity
explanation: Deferred tax uses rates expected when the asset is realised or liability settled, based on rates and laws enacted or substantively enacted at reporting date.

title: Revisit an unrecognised DTA
prompt: A deferred tax asset was not recognised last year because recovery was not probable. New reliable evidence this year supports sufficient future taxable profit. What must the entity do?
options: Reassess the unrecognised DTA and recognise it to the extent recovery is now probable
Never revisit a prior non-recognition decision
Recognise the whole legal tax loss regardless of evidence
Recognise it directly as sales revenue
explanation: The carrying amount of a DTA is reviewed and unrecognised DTAs are reassessed at each reporting date, reflecting changes in recovery probability.

title: Goodwill initial recognition exception
prompt: The initial recognition of goodwill produces a taxable temporary difference within the specific goodwill exception. What does LKAS 12 require?
options: Do not recognise the deferred tax liability arising from that initial goodwill recognition
Recognise the DTL and increase goodwill repeatedly
Recognise all goodwill as an immediate tax expense
Always recognise a deferred tax asset equal to goodwill
explanation: The standard has a specific exception for deferred tax liabilities arising from the initial recognition of goodwill. This is distinct from DTLs on identifiable acquired assets.

title: Corporate assets in a CGU test
prompt: A headquarters asset cannot generate independent cash inflows. A reasonable and consistent allocation to relevant CGUs is possible. How is it incorporated in impairment testing?
options: Allocate its carrying amount on a reasonable and consistent basis to the relevant CGUs
Exclude it from all impairment tests permanently
Test it using nonexistent independent cash receipts
Assign its full amount to every CGU simultaneously
explanation: Corporate assets are considered in testing the relevant CGUs, using reasonable and consistent allocation where possible; otherwise the larger-group procedures apply.

title: Annual test despite no warning
prompt: An intangible asset has an indefinite useful life and no obvious impairment indicators this year. Is an impairment test still required?
options: Yes; test annually as well as when indicators arise
No; only finite-life assets are tested
No; indefinite means the asset cannot lose value
Only if the entity reports an operating loss
explanation: Intangibles with indefinite useful lives, intangibles not yet available for use and goodwill have annual impairment-testing requirements in addition to indicator-based testing.

title: Do not value an uncommitted rescue
prompt: Value-in-use forecasts include savings from a future restructuring to which the entity is not yet committed. What is appropriate?
options: Exclude those future restructuring benefits and related cash flows under the specified rules
Include every proposed efficiency saving automatically
Add the restructuring budget directly to recoverable amount
Recognise a provision solely to make the valuation possible
explanation: Value in use reflects the asset’s current condition and excludes cash flows from a future restructuring not yet committed to and from future improvements or enhancements.

title: Probable inflow versus virtual certainty
prompt: A lawsuit pursued by an entity will probably produce an economic inflow but the inflow is not virtually certain. What is the general treatment?
options: Do not recognise the contingent asset; disclose it when inflow is probable
Recognise an asset whenever inflow exceeds 50% probability
Recognise the full claim as revenue and reverse it if necessary
explanation: Contingent assets are not recognised. Probable inflows are disclosed; recognition becomes appropriate when the inflow is virtually certain and the asset is no longer contingent.

title: Directly related fulfilment costs
prompt: An onerous-contract assessment requires the costs of fulfilling a contract. Under the amended guidance, which costs are included?
options: Incremental costs and an allocation of other costs directly related to fulfilling contracts
Only incremental materials, never directly related depreciation
Every corporate expense regardless of relationship
Only cash paid during the current month
explanation: Fulfilment costs include incremental costs and an allocation of other costs directly related to fulfilling contracts, such as relevant depreciation.

title: Do not price risk twice
prompt: An estimated provision cash flow already reflects a particular risk. Management also increases the discount rate to reflect that same risk, without consistency. What should be corrected?
options: Avoid double counting risk in both the cash flows and discount rate
Always maximise both adjustments to create prudence
Use an arbitrary rate to achieve the desired provision
Omit time value even when it is material
explanation: The discount rate is pre-tax and reflects time value and liability-specific risks only to the extent those risks have not already adjusted estimated cash flows.

title: Revalue the class
prompt: An entity revalues one building but leaves similar buildings in the same class at outdated amounts merely to show a favourable result. Which requirement is relevant?
options: Revalue the entire class of assets, subject to permitted rolling timing that keeps values current
Revalue only assets with increases in value
Use a different model every year for each individual building without restriction
Offset the increase against unrelated inventories
explanation: When an item is revalued, the entire class to which it belongs is revalued to avoid selective revaluation and mixed-date amounts.

title: Daily servicing versus replacement
prompt: Routine repairs maintain a machine’s existing operating condition and do not create a separately qualifying replacement component or inspection asset. What is the general treatment?
options: Capitalise every payment connected with the machine
Recognise the repair as a revaluation surplus
Delay the expense until the machine is sold
explanation: Day-to-day servicing costs are not recognised in the carrying amount of PPE. Qualifying replacements and major inspections are assessed separately.

title: Inventory reversal has a boundary
prompt: Inventory previously written down to NRV recovers because circumstances change. How is a reversal limited?
options: The reversal cannot exceed the original write-down, leaving the lower of cost and revised NRV
The inventory can always be written up to any current selling price
The original cost ceases to be relevant forever
The reversal is always credited directly to equity
explanation: A reversal is limited to the original write-down so the new carrying amount is the lower of cost and revised NRV. The reversal reduces inventory expense.

title: Interchangeable units and LIFO
prompt: A retailer wants to use LIFO for ordinarily interchangeable inventory solely because it produces a preferred profit. Which cost formulas does LKAS 2 specify for these inventories?
options: LIFO or any formula management prefers
Only specific identification for every retail item
The current selling price without considering cost
explanation: The standard specifies FIFO or weighted average for ordinarily interchangeable inventories, with consistent formulas for inventories of similar nature and use.

title: Identify the cash tax flow
prompt: Income tax paid can be specifically identified with an investing transaction. How is that cash flow classified under the applicable requirement?
options: As investing when specifically identified with that transaction; otherwise tax is usually operating
Always financing because governments fund public spending
Exclude it from all cash flows
explanation: Tax cash flows are separately disclosed and generally operating unless specifically identified with financing or investing activities.

title: Unrealised FX is not a receipt
prompt: The reporting-currency value of cash held in foreign currency rises solely because exchange rates change. How is this dealt with in the cash flow statement reconciliation?
options: Present the exchange-rate effect separately to reconcile opening and closing cash; it is not an operating, investing or financing cash flow
Record an operating cash receipt equal to the unrealised gain
Ignore the effect and leave closing cash unreconciled
explanation: Unrealised exchange changes are not cash flows; the effect on cash and cash equivalents is presented separately from operating, investing and financing flows.

title: Indefinite does not mean infinite
prompt: An intangible has no foreseeable limit to the period of expected net cash inflows and is classified as having an indefinite useful life. What ongoing obligation remains?
options: Review the useful-life assessment each period and perform required impairment testing
Never reassess useful life because indefinite means infinite
Recognise an automatic annual revaluation gain
explanation: Indefinite means no foreseeable limit, not infinite life. The assessment is reviewed each period; a change to finite life is accounted for as an estimate change and indicates possible impairment.

title: Twenty percent is a presumption
prompt: An investor owns 22% of voting rights, but clear evidence demonstrates it has no significant influence. Is the percentage alone conclusive?
options: No; the significant-influence presumption can be rebutted by clear evidence
Yes; the investment must always be consolidated
No; only a holding above 50% can ever create significant influence
explanation: Holding 20% or more creates a rebuttable presumption of significant influence. The assessment considers the relevant evidence and is distinct from control.

title: Returns-adjusted sales revenue • case 1
prompt: A retailer transfers 1,020 products at LKR 1,500 each and receives payment in full. Its supported estimate is that 4.1% will be returned for a full refund. The variable-consideration constraint permits this estimate; no other obligations or taxes apply. What sales revenue is recognised at transfer, excluding the separately accounted return asset?
explanation: Exclude consideration expected to be refunded: 1,530,000.00 × (1 − 4.1%) = 1,467,270.00 revenue. The expected refund is a separate liability; the recovery asset affects cost of sales separately.

title: Loyalty material-right allocation • case 1
prompt: Cash consideration of LKR 1,025,000 covers delivered goods and loyalty points that are a separate material right. Stand-alone selling price of the goods is 1,000,000; the points’ estimated stand-alone price is 105,000, ALREADY adjusted for redemption probability. No points are redeemed yet. What contract liability is allocated to the points?
explanation: Allocate by relative stand-alone prices: 1,025,000 × 105,000 / 1,105,000 = 97,398.19. Do not apply redemption probability again; it is already included in the points’ stand-alone price.

title: Contract-cost asset impairment • case 1
prompt: A qualifying sales commission asset initially cost LKR 186,000 and is amortised evenly over three years. After one year of amortisation, expected remaining consideration for the related services is 910,000; directly related future fulfilment costs not yet expensed are 879,000. Other assets have already been tested and no further adjustment is required. Find the impairment loss on this contract-cost asset.
explanation: Post-amortisation carrying amount = 124,000.00. Recoverable benchmark = remaining consideration − related future costs = 31,000. Impairment = 124,000.00 − 31,000 = 93,000.00.

title: Non-distinct contract modification • case 1
prompt: A single over-time construction obligation had original price LKR 10,100,000. Revenue of 4,040,000.00 was recognised before modification. Approved added work is NOT distinct and adds 2,050,000 to the price. Under the appropriate input method the modified combined obligation is now 50% complete. No variable-price constraint or other issue applies. Find the cumulative catch-up revenue adjustment at modification.
explanation: Because added work is not distinct, update the existing combined obligation. Revised cumulative revenue = (10,100,000 + 2,050,000) × 50% = 6,075,000.00. Less previously recognised 4,040,000.00 gives an adjustment of 2,035,000.00.

title: Advance financing and revenue • case 1
prompt: A customer prepays LKR 1,025,000 exactly two years before goods transfer. The arrangement contains a significant financing component benefiting the supplier; the appropriate annual rate is 8%. No exemption applies. No other consideration or obligations exist. What revenue is recognised when control of the goods transfers?
explanation: Accrete the contract liability for two years: 1,025,000 × 1.08² = 1,195,560.00. The financing cost is recognised separately over the two years; the increased liability is released as revenue on transfer.

title: Upfront fee over the service term • case 1
prompt: A two-year service contract has a non-refundable joining fee of LKR 126,000 plus fixed monthly fees of 10,000 for 24 months. The joining activity transfers no separate service, all consideration relates to one evenly provided service obligation, and no renewal material right exists. Find revenue for the first six months of service.
explanation: Total transaction price = 126,000 + 24 × 10,000 = 366,000. The upfront activity is not a separate obligation. Recognise 6/24 of the total = 91,500.00.
family: Upfront fee over the service term

title: Credit-impaired net interest basis • case 1
prompt: A loan originated unimpaired subsequently became credit-impaired in the prior reporting period and remains so throughout the current year. Opening gross amortised cost is LKR 1,550,000; loss allowance is 310,000. Original effective rate is 9%. No cash flows or other opening adjustments occur. Find current-year interest revenue.
explanation: For this subsequently credit-impaired asset, apply the original EIR to amortised cost NET of allowance: (1,550,000 − 310,000) × 9% = 111,600.00. This is not the purchased/originated credit-impaired model.

title: Loan modification without derecognition • case 1
prompt: A financial asset is modified WITHOUT derecognition. Immediately before modification its gross carrying amount is LKR 1,020,000. Revised contractual receipts are 455,000 in one year and 508,000 in two years. Original EIR is 10%. Ignore fees and ECL changes. Find the modification LOSS recognised now.
explanation: Recompute gross carrying amount using the ORIGINAL EIR: 455,000/1.10 + 508,000/1.10² = 833,471.07. Modification loss = old gross amount 1,020,000 − 833,471.07 = 186,528.93.

title: Debt FVOCI residual movement • case 1
prompt: A debt investment at FVOCI opens with equal fair value and gross amortised cost of LKR 1,025,000, and no accumulated OCI. Current EIR interest is 82,000.00, coupon received is 61,000, and closing fair value is 1,179,000. No impairment, foreign exchange, purchases or disposals apply. Find the fair-value gain recognised in OCI for this year.
explanation: Closing amortised-cost benchmark = 1,025,000 + 82,000.00 − 61,000 = 1,046,000.00. OCI is fair value minus that benchmark = 1,179,000 − 1,046,000.00 = 133,000.00. EIR interest is profit or loss.

title: Debt extinguishment after settlement fees • case 1
prompt: A financial liability with carrying amount LKR 1,230,000 is fully extinguished by a cash settlement of 1,070,000 plus a fee of 20,500 paid to the lender as part of the settlement consideration. No replacement debt, other costs or equity component exists. Find the extinguishment GAIN.
explanation: Total consideration paid = 1,070,000 + lender settlement fee 20,500.00 = 1,090,500.00. Gain = liability carrying amount − total settlement consideration = 139,500.00.

title: Own-credit split on an FVTPL liability • case 1
prompt: A liability is designated at FVTPL under the eligible fair-value option. Its fair value increases by LKR 105,000, producing a total loss. Of this, 21,000 is attributable to improved own credit and qualifies for OCI presentation. The split does not create or enlarge an accounting mismatch. Find the loss recognised in PROFIT OR LOSS.
explanation: The eligible own-credit component of 21,000 goes to OCI. The remaining fair-value loss goes to profit or loss: 105,000 − 21,000 = 84,000.00. This presentation is for designated liabilities under the stated conditions.
family: Own-credit split on an FVTPL liability

title: Midyear acquisition and parent earnings • case 1
prompt: P acquires 80% of S on 1 October and reports to 31 December. P’s own annual profit is LKR 2,050,000, excluding any S dividend. S’s annual profit of 1,260,000 accrues evenly. Additional depreciation on acquisition-date fair-value adjustments for the POST-acquisition quarter is 41,000. No tax, intragroup trading, goodwill impairment or other adjustment exists. Find consolidated profit attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Only post-acquisition profit enters: S’s quarter = 315,000.00; less FV depreciation 41,000 gives 274,000.00. Owners’ profit = 2,050,000 + 80% of adjusted quarter profit = 2,269,200.00.

title: Intragroup PPE transfer at year end • case 1
prompt: On 1 January P sells equipment to S for LKR 918,000; carrying amount in P was 612,000. Remaining useful life is three years with no residual value. S depreciates the transfer price straight-line for the full year. No tax or impairment applies. By how much must S’s closing PPE amount be REDUCED on consolidation to restore the group basis?
explanation: Eliminate transfer gain of 306,000, but reverse excess depreciation of 306,000/3 = 102,000.00. Net reduction in closing group PPE = 204,000.00. The intragroup sale does not create a group gain.
family: Intragroup PPE transfer at year end

title: Loss of control and retained interest • case 1
prompt: P loses control of S. Sale proceeds are LKR 2,050,000; fair value of the retained interest is 610,000; carrying NCI derecognised is 405,000. S’s consolidated net assets INCLUDING goodwill carry at 2,530,000. No accumulated OCI, transaction costs or other adjustment exists. Calculate the gain on loss of control.
explanation: Gain = proceeds + fair value retained + carrying NCI − subsidiary net assets including goodwill = 2,050,000 + 610,000 + 405,000 − 2,530,000 = 535,000.00.
family: Loss of control and retained interest

title: Buy more without losing control • case 1
prompt: P increases ownership of S from 80% to 90% and retains control. Carrying amount of the entire 20% NCI before purchase is LKR 410,000. P pays 310,000 for the additional 10% interest. No OCI or other changes exist. What amount is DEBITED to parent owners’ equity for the difference between consideration and NCI carrying amount acquired?
explanation: The purchased 10 percentage points are half of the previous 20% NCI. Derecognise NCI of 205,000.00. Debit parent equity for excess consideration: 310,000 − 205,000.00 = 105,000.00. There is no new goodwill or profit-or-loss charge.

title: Acquisition consideration at present value • case 1
prompt: An acquirer pays cash LKR 2,050,000 now, owes fixed consideration of 1,111,000 in one year, and has acquisition-date fair value of contingent consideration of 205,000. Discount fixed deferred consideration at 10%. NCI fair value is 500,000; identifiable net assets are 3,020,000. No previous holding or other adjustment applies. Find goodwill.
explanation: Deferred consideration PV = 1,111,000/1.10 = 1,010,000.00. Goodwill = upfront + discounted fixed consideration + contingent FV + NCI − identifiable net assets = 745,000.00. Later financing unwinding is separate.

title: Acquisition uplift and deferred tax • case 1
prompt: Consideration is LKR 3,050,000; NCI is measured at fair value of 600,000. Identifiable net assets before an equipment uplift are 2,820,000. Acquisition-date equipment uplift is 410,000, with no tax-base uplift. Tax rate on reversal is 30%; no DTL exception applies. No other adjustment exists. Find goodwill after recognising the uplift and related DTL.
explanation: DTL on uplift = 410,000 × 30% = 123,000.00. Net identifiable assets = 2,820,000 + 410,000 − DTL = 3,107,000.00. Goodwill = consideration + NCI − net identifiable assets = 543,000.00.

title: Measurement-period goodwill adjustment • case 1
prompt: Provisional goodwill was LKR 1,020,000. During the measurement period, new information about acquisition-date facts establishes an additional identifiable equipment fair-value uplift of 205,000. The tax base is unchanged and a 30% DTL must be recognised. NCI was measured at fair value and that value is unchanged. All other acquisition amounts are final. Find revised acquisition-date goodwill.
explanation: Additional net identifiable assets = uplift − 30% DTL = 143,500.00. Retrospectively reduce goodwill by that net amount: 1,020,000 − 143,500.00 = 876,500.00. Subsequent equipment depreciation is considered separately.

title: Advance rent and initial ROU cost • case 1
prompt: A three-year lease has three equal annual payments of LKR 155,000 each: one at commencement, one in a year and one in two years. Discount rate is 10%. Initial direct costs are 20,000 and incentives received at commencement are 5,000. No restoration obligation exists. Find initial ROU asset cost.
explanation: Initial liability excludes the payment already made: 155,000/1.10 + 155,000/1.10² = 269,008.26. ROU = liability + commencement payment + direct costs − incentive = 439,008.26.
family: Advance rent and initial ROU cost

title: Index-linked payment remeasurement • case 1
prompt: A CPI change triggers a lessee remeasurement. Immediately before it, lease liability is LKR 201,000. The revised remaining payments are 122,210 in one year and the same amount in two years. The original 10% discount rate remains appropriate; no floating-interest-rate change or modification applies. Find the INCREASE in liability, normally adjusting the ROU asset.
explanation: Revised liability = 122,210/1.10 + 122,210/1.10² = 212,100.00. For this index change retain the original discount rate. Increase = revised liability − 201,000 = 11,100.00.

title: Partial termination and remaining ROU • case 1
prompt: A lease modification reduces scope by 40%, with a proportionate reduction in the ROU asset and liability. Immediately before modification, ROU carrying amount is LKR 920,000 and liability 1,020,000. After accounting for termination, remeasuring the remaining payments at the revised appropriate rate gives a liability of 635,000. No impairment applies. Find the FINAL ROU carrying amount after both steps.
explanation: First retain 60% of the ROU (552,000.00) and liability (612,000.00), recognising the termination difference in profit or loss. Then adjust ROU by revised liability minus remaining liability: 23,000.00. Final ROU = 575,000.00.

title: Finance lessor effective interest • case 1
prompt: A finance lessor’s net investment comprises four year-end rentals of LKR 310,000 and an unguaranteed residual of 105,000 recovered at the end of year four. The interest rate implicit in the lease is 8%. No initial direct costs outside those reflected in this rate, credit losses or other adjustments exist. Find finance income for the first year, BEFORE the first rental is received.
explanation: Initial net investment = PV of the four rentals plus PV of residual = 1,103,937.45. First-year finance income = opening net investment × 8% = 88,315.00, giving a constant periodic return.

title: Warranty deductible temporary difference • case 1
prompt: A recognised warranty provision carries at LKR 315,000. The entire amount will be deductible only when paid, so its tax base is zero. Sufficient future taxable profit is probable and no recognition exception applies. The enacted rate on reversal is 30%. Find the deferred tax asset.
explanation: Liability tax base = carrying amount − future deduction = zero. Deductible temporary difference = 315,000; DTA = 315,000 × 30% = 94,500.00. Tax expense recognition and cash deduction occur in different periods.

title: Deferred tax expense bridge • case 1
prompt: Opening DTL is LKR 100,000 and closing DTL is 152,000. Opening DTA is 80,000 and closing DTA is 61,000. All changes belong in profit or loss, with no acquisitions, OCI, equity or foreign-exchange effects. Find deferred tax EXPENSE for the year.
explanation: Expense = increase in DTL + decrease in DTA = (152,000 − 100,000) + (80,000 − 61,000) = 71,000.00. Do not confuse the closing net balance with the period expense.

title: Tax loss recognition ceiling • case 1
prompt: Unused tax losses are LKR 820,000. Convincing evidence supports probable FUTURE taxable profit of only 510,000 before those losses expire. There are no other recovery sources or taxable temporary differences. Tax rate is 30%. Find the DTA that can be recognised on the losses.
explanation: Recognise only the losses supported by probable taxable profit: min(820,000, 510,000) × 30% = 153,000.00. The legal loss balance alone does not justify a larger asset.

title: Discounted VIU versus disposal value • case 1
prompt: An asset carries at LKR 1,220,000. Its appropriate value-in-use forecast is 310,000 received at each of the next three year ends, plus net disposal proceeds of 200,000 at year three. Appropriate discount rate is 10%. Fair value less costs of disposal is 850,000. No other cash flows or valuation adjustments apply. Find the impairment loss.
explanation: VIU = PV of three operating receipts plus PV of terminal disposal = 921,187.08. Recoverable amount is the HIGHER of VIU and 850,000: 921,187.08. Impairment = 1,220,000 − 921,187.08 = 298,812.92.

title: CGU residual pro-rata allocation • case 1
prompt: A CGU contains goodwill of LKR 150,000, asset A of 610,000, and asset B of 405,000. Recoverable amount is 805,000. No individual-asset floor restricts allocation and there are no other assets. Find asset B’s carrying amount AFTER allocating the CGU impairment.
explanation: Total impairment = 1,165,000 − 805,000 = 360,000. First eliminate goodwill of 150,000. Allocate remaining 210,000 pro rata to A and B. B loss = 83,793.10; closing B = 321,206.90.

title: CGU reversal without restoring goodwill • case 1
prompt: After past impairment, a CGU has assets A at LKR 600,000 and B at 400,000. All previously impaired goodwill is zero. Recoverable amount now rises to 1,205,000. A’s maximum permitted amount under its no-impairment ceiling is 651,000, and B’s is 502,000; no lower individual recoverable-amount limit applies. What is the maximum total CGU carrying amount after reversal?
explanation: Goodwill impairment is never reversed. The other assets cannot exceed their permitted ceilings: 651,000 + 502,000 = 1,153,000.00, below CGU recoverable amount 1,205,000. Allocate reversals subject to those ceilings.

title: Onerous contract least net exit cost • case 1
prompt: A contract has a present onerous obligation. Directly related costs to fulfil are LKR 1,520,000, while expected contract benefits are 1,005,000. The alternative is to terminate now for a penalty of 310,000. No dedicated asset impairment is required and discounting is immaterial. Find the provision for the least net unavoidable cost.
explanation: Net cost of fulfilling = 1,520,000 − 1,005,000 = 515,000. Compare with termination penalty 310,000; the least net cost of exit is 310,000.00. Do not provide for gross fulfilment costs without expected benefits.
family: Onerous contract least net exit cost

title: Restructuring cost boundary • case 1
prompt: A qualifying restructuring has created the required present obligations. Direct supplier-contract cancellation penalties are LKR 205,000; legally required closure clean-up costs are 102,000. Planned staff retraining is 150,000, marketing is 80,000, and investment in new systems is 50,000 for continuing operations. No leases, employee termination benefits, other assets or discounting complications apply. What amount is included in the restructuring provision?
explanation: Include direct expenditures necessarily entailed by the restructuring and unrelated to ongoing activities: 205,000 + 102,000 = 307,000.00. Retraining, marketing and new-system investment for continuing business are excluded.

title: Inspection replacement and depreciation • case 1
prompt: On 1 January an asset’s carrying amount is LKR 920,000, including an old inspection component of 100,000. A new qualifying major inspection costs 186,000 that day and the old component is derecognised. The remaining main asset has four years’ life; the new inspection has three. Both use straight-line depreciation with zero residual value. Find total carrying amount at year end.
explanation: Derecognise old inspection: main asset = 820,000. Depreciate main asset by 205,000.00 and new inspection by 62,000.00. Closing = 615,000.00 + 124,000.00 = 739,000.00.

title: Commercial exchange gain • case 1
prompt: An equipment exchange has commercial substance. The entity gives equipment with carrying amount LKR 810,000 and reliably measurable fair value 1,020,000, plus 200,000 cash. Fair value of the received equipment is not more clearly evident. No other costs or taxes apply. What GAIN is recognised on derecognising the equipment given?
explanation: Cost of received equipment = fair value given + cash = 1,220,000. The gain on the equipment surrendered is only its fair value minus carrying amount: 1,020,000 − 810,000 = 210,000.00. The cash paid is not a gain.

title: Periodic weighted average with discount • case 1
prompt: Opening inventory is 1,000 units at LKR 100 each. A purchase of 520 units is invoiced at 120 each with a 10% trade discount; inward freight is 2,000. Closing quantity is 510 units. Use periodic weighted average. NRV exceeds cost; there are no other movements or costs. Find closing inventory carrying amount.
explanation: Net purchase price per unit = 120 × 90% = 108. Total available cost = 100,000 + 520 × 108 + 2,000 = 158,160. Average = cost / 1,520 units. Closing value = average × 510 = 53,066.84.

title: Net acquisition cash flow • case 1
prompt: A subsidiary acquisition involves cash consideration PAID this year of LKR 1,050,000, plus deferred consideration of 200,000 not yet paid. Cash and cash equivalents acquired with the subsidiary are 105,000; acquired borrowings are 300,000. No fees or other cash payments occur. Find the net INVESTING cash outflow from obtaining control.
explanation: Cash flow from obtaining control is investing, reported net of cash and cash equivalents acquired: 1,050,000 − 105,000 = 945,000.00 outflow. Unpaid deferred consideration and assumed debt are not cash payments in this case.

title: Research expense and midyear amortisation • case 1
prompt: In the current year a project incurs research costs LKR 81,000, development spending of 50,000 before recognition criteria are met, then qualifying development cost of 620,000. The completed asset becomes available for use on 1 July, has a five-year finite life and zero residual value. Use six months of straight-line amortisation. Find TOTAL current-year expense from these items; no impairment applies.
explanation: Expense research and pre-recognition development: 81,000 + 50,000. Capitalise 620,000, then amortise for six months: 620,000/5 × 6/12 = 62,000.00. Total expense = 193,000.00.

title: Associate upstream adjusted earnings • case 1
prompt: An investor owns 30% of an associate. Associate profit is LKR 520,000. The investor’s equity-method adjustments include extra depreciation of 102,000 on acquisition-date fair values, and an upstream inventory sale leaves unrealised profit of 61,000 in the investor’s inventory. No tax, basis differences beyond those stated, impairment or other adjustments apply. Find the equity-accounted share of profit after both adjustments.
explanation: Adjust associate result before taking the share: 520,000 − 102,000 − 61,000 = 357,000. Investor’s share = 30% × adjusted result = 107,100.00. The investor’s share of upstream unrealised profit is eliminated.

title: Returns-adjusted sales revenue • case 2
prompt: A retailer transfers 1,040 products at LKR 1,500 each and receives payment in full. Its supported estimate is that 4.2% will be returned for a full refund. The variable-consideration constraint permits this estimate; no other obligations or taxes apply. What sales revenue is recognised at transfer, excluding the separately accounted return asset?
explanation: Exclude consideration expected to be refunded: 1,560,000.00 × (1 − 4.2%) = 1,494,480.00 revenue. The expected refund is a separate liability; the recovery asset affects cost of sales separately.

title: Loyalty material-right allocation • case 2
prompt: Cash consideration of LKR 1,050,000 covers delivered goods and loyalty points that are a separate material right. Stand-alone selling price of the goods is 1,000,000; the points’ estimated stand-alone price is 110,000, ALREADY adjusted for redemption probability. No points are redeemed yet. What contract liability is allocated to the points?
explanation: Allocate by relative stand-alone prices: 1,050,000 × 110,000 / 1,110,000 = 104,054.05. Do not apply redemption probability again; it is already included in the points’ stand-alone price.

title: Contract-cost asset impairment • case 2
prompt: A qualifying sales commission asset initially cost LKR 192,000 and is amortised evenly over three years. After one year of amortisation, expected remaining consideration for the related services is 920,000; directly related future fulfilment costs not yet expensed are 888,000. Other assets have already been tested and no further adjustment is required. Find the impairment loss on this contract-cost asset.
explanation: Post-amortisation carrying amount = 128,000.00. Recoverable benchmark = remaining consideration − related future costs = 32,000. Impairment = 128,000.00 − 32,000 = 96,000.00.

title: Non-distinct contract modification • case 2
prompt: A single over-time construction obligation had original price LKR 10,200,000. Revenue of 4,080,000.00 was recognised before modification. Approved added work is NOT distinct and adds 2,100,000 to the price. Under the appropriate input method the modified combined obligation is now 50% complete. No variable-price constraint or other issue applies. Find the cumulative catch-up revenue adjustment at modification.
explanation: Because added work is not distinct, update the existing combined obligation. Revised cumulative revenue = (10,200,000 + 2,100,000) × 50% = 6,150,000.00. Less previously recognised 4,080,000.00 gives an adjustment of 2,070,000.00.

title: Advance financing and revenue • case 2
prompt: A customer prepays LKR 1,050,000 exactly two years before goods transfer. The arrangement contains a significant financing component benefiting the supplier; the appropriate annual rate is 8%. No exemption applies. No other consideration or obligations exist. What revenue is recognised when control of the goods transfers?
explanation: Accrete the contract liability for two years: 1,050,000 × 1.08² = 1,224,720.00. The financing cost is recognised separately over the two years; the increased liability is released as revenue on transfer.

title: Upfront fee over the service term • case 2
prompt: A two-year service contract has a non-refundable joining fee of LKR 132,000 plus fixed monthly fees of 10,000 for 24 months. The joining activity transfers no separate service, all consideration relates to one evenly provided service obligation, and no renewal material right exists. Find revenue for the first six months of service.
explanation: Total transaction price = 132,000 + 24 × 10,000 = 372,000. The upfront activity is not a separate obligation. Recognise 6/24 of the total = 93,000.00.
family: Upfront fee over the service term

title: Credit-impaired net interest basis • case 2
prompt: A loan originated unimpaired subsequently became credit-impaired in the prior reporting period and remains so throughout the current year. Opening gross amortised cost is LKR 1,600,000; loss allowance is 320,000. Original effective rate is 9%. No cash flows or other opening adjustments occur. Find current-year interest revenue.
explanation: For this subsequently credit-impaired asset, apply the original EIR to amortised cost NET of allowance: (1,600,000 − 320,000) × 9% = 115,200.00. This is not the purchased/originated credit-impaired model.

title: Loan modification without derecognition • case 2
prompt: A financial asset is modified WITHOUT derecognition. Immediately before modification its gross carrying amount is LKR 1,040,000. Revised contractual receipts are 460,000 in one year and 516,000 in two years. Original EIR is 10%. Ignore fees and ECL changes. Find the modification LOSS recognised now.
explanation: Recompute gross carrying amount using the ORIGINAL EIR: 460,000/1.10 + 516,000/1.10² = 844,628.10. Modification loss = old gross amount 1,040,000 − 844,628.10 = 195,371.90.

title: Debt FVOCI residual movement • case 2
prompt: A debt investment at FVOCI opens with equal fair value and gross amortised cost of LKR 1,050,000, and no accumulated OCI. Current EIR interest is 84,000.00, coupon received is 62,000, and closing fair value is 1,208,000. No impairment, foreign exchange, purchases or disposals apply. Find the fair-value gain recognised in OCI for this year.
explanation: Closing amortised-cost benchmark = 1,050,000 + 84,000.00 − 62,000 = 1,072,000.00. OCI is fair value minus that benchmark = 1,208,000 − 1,072,000.00 = 136,000.00. EIR interest is profit or loss.

title: Debt extinguishment after settlement fees • case 2
prompt: A financial liability with carrying amount LKR 1,260,000 is fully extinguished by a cash settlement of 1,090,000 plus a fee of 21,000 paid to the lender as part of the settlement consideration. No replacement debt, other costs or equity component exists. Find the extinguishment GAIN.
explanation: Total consideration paid = 1,090,000 + lender settlement fee 21,000.00 = 1,111,000.00. Gain = liability carrying amount − total settlement consideration = 149,000.00.

title: Own-credit split on an FVTPL liability • case 2
prompt: A liability is designated at FVTPL under the eligible fair-value option. Its fair value increases by LKR 110,000, producing a total loss. Of this, 22,000 is attributable to improved own credit and qualifies for OCI presentation. The split does not create or enlarge an accounting mismatch. Find the loss recognised in PROFIT OR LOSS.
explanation: The eligible own-credit component of 22,000 goes to OCI. The remaining fair-value loss goes to profit or loss: 110,000 − 22,000 = 88,000.00. This presentation is for designated liabilities under the stated conditions.
family: Own-credit split on an FVTPL liability

title: Midyear acquisition and parent earnings • case 2
prompt: P acquires 80% of S on 1 October and reports to 31 December. P’s own annual profit is LKR 2,100,000, excluding any S dividend. S’s annual profit of 1,320,000 accrues evenly. Additional depreciation on acquisition-date fair-value adjustments for the POST-acquisition quarter is 42,000. No tax, intragroup trading, goodwill impairment or other adjustment exists. Find consolidated profit attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Only post-acquisition profit enters: S’s quarter = 330,000.00; less FV depreciation 42,000 gives 288,000.00. Owners’ profit = 2,100,000 + 80% of adjusted quarter profit = 2,330,400.00.

title: Intragroup PPE transfer at year end • case 2
prompt: On 1 January P sells equipment to S for LKR 936,000; carrying amount in P was 624,000. Remaining useful life is three years with no residual value. S depreciates the transfer price straight-line for the full year. No tax or impairment applies. By how much must S’s closing PPE amount be REDUCED on consolidation to restore the group basis?
explanation: Eliminate transfer gain of 312,000, but reverse excess depreciation of 312,000/3 = 104,000.00. Net reduction in closing group PPE = 208,000.00. The intragroup sale does not create a group gain.
family: Intragroup PPE transfer at year end

title: Loss of control and retained interest • case 2
prompt: P loses control of S. Sale proceeds are LKR 2,100,000; fair value of the retained interest is 620,000; carrying NCI derecognised is 410,000. S’s consolidated net assets INCLUDING goodwill carry at 2,560,000. No accumulated OCI, transaction costs or other adjustment exists. Calculate the gain on loss of control.
explanation: Gain = proceeds + fair value retained + carrying NCI − subsidiary net assets including goodwill = 2,100,000 + 620,000 + 410,000 − 2,560,000 = 570,000.00.
family: Loss of control and retained interest

title: Buy more without losing control • case 2
prompt: P increases ownership of S from 80% to 90% and retains control. Carrying amount of the entire 20% NCI before purchase is LKR 420,000. P pays 320,000 for the additional 10% interest. No OCI or other changes exist. What amount is DEBITED to parent owners’ equity for the difference between consideration and NCI carrying amount acquired?
explanation: The purchased 10 percentage points are half of the previous 20% NCI. Derecognise NCI of 210,000.00. Debit parent equity for excess consideration: 320,000 − 210,000.00 = 110,000.00. There is no new goodwill or profit-or-loss charge.

title: Acquisition consideration at present value • case 2
prompt: An acquirer pays cash LKR 2,100,000 now, owes fixed consideration of 1,122,000 in one year, and has acquisition-date fair value of contingent consideration of 210,000. Discount fixed deferred consideration at 10%. NCI fair value is 500,000; identifiable net assets are 3,040,000. No previous holding or other adjustment applies. Find goodwill.
explanation: Deferred consideration PV = 1,122,000/1.10 = 1,020,000.00. Goodwill = upfront + discounted fixed consideration + contingent FV + NCI − identifiable net assets = 790,000.00. Later financing unwinding is separate.

title: Acquisition uplift and deferred tax • case 2
prompt: Consideration is LKR 3,100,000; NCI is measured at fair value of 600,000. Identifiable net assets before an equipment uplift are 2,840,000. Acquisition-date equipment uplift is 420,000, with no tax-base uplift. Tax rate on reversal is 30%; no DTL exception applies. No other adjustment exists. Find goodwill after recognising the uplift and related DTL.
explanation: DTL on uplift = 420,000 × 30% = 126,000.00. Net identifiable assets = 2,840,000 + 420,000 − DTL = 3,134,000.00. Goodwill = consideration + NCI − net identifiable assets = 566,000.00.

title: Measurement-period goodwill adjustment • case 2
prompt: Provisional goodwill was LKR 1,040,000. During the measurement period, new information about acquisition-date facts establishes an additional identifiable equipment fair-value uplift of 210,000. The tax base is unchanged and a 30% DTL must be recognised. NCI was measured at fair value and that value is unchanged. All other acquisition amounts are final. Find revised acquisition-date goodwill.
explanation: Additional net identifiable assets = uplift − 30% DTL = 147,000.00. Retrospectively reduce goodwill by that net amount: 1,040,000 − 147,000.00 = 893,000.00. Subsequent equipment depreciation is considered separately.

title: Advance rent and initial ROU cost • case 2
prompt: A three-year lease has three equal annual payments of LKR 160,000 each: one at commencement, one in a year and one in two years. Discount rate is 10%. Initial direct costs are 20,000 and incentives received at commencement are 5,000. No restoration obligation exists. Find initial ROU asset cost.
explanation: Initial liability excludes the payment already made: 160,000/1.10 + 160,000/1.10² = 277,685.95. ROU = liability + commencement payment + direct costs − incentive = 452,685.95.
family: Advance rent and initial ROU cost

title: Index-linked payment remeasurement • case 2
prompt: A CPI change triggers a lessee remeasurement. Immediately before it, lease liability is LKR 202,000. The revised remaining payments are 123,420 in one year and the same amount in two years. The original 10% discount rate remains appropriate; no floating-interest-rate change or modification applies. Find the INCREASE in liability, normally adjusting the ROU asset.
explanation: Revised liability = 123,420/1.10 + 123,420/1.10² = 214,200.00. For this index change retain the original discount rate. Increase = revised liability − 202,000 = 12,200.00.

title: Partial termination and remaining ROU • case 2
prompt: A lease modification reduces scope by 40%, with a proportionate reduction in the ROU asset and liability. Immediately before modification, ROU carrying amount is LKR 940,000 and liability 1,040,000. After accounting for termination, remeasuring the remaining payments at the revised appropriate rate gives a liability of 650,000. No impairment applies. Find the FINAL ROU carrying amount after both steps.
explanation: First retain 60% of the ROU (564,000.00) and liability (624,000.00), recognising the termination difference in profit or loss. Then adjust ROU by revised liability minus remaining liability: 26,000.00. Final ROU = 590,000.00.

title: Finance lessor effective interest • case 2
prompt: A finance lessor’s net investment comprises four year-end rentals of LKR 320,000 and an unguaranteed residual of 110,000 recovered at the end of year four. The interest rate implicit in the lease is 8%. No initial direct costs outside those reflected in this rate, credit losses or other adjustments exist. Find finance income for the first year, BEFORE the first rental is received.
explanation: Initial net investment = PV of the four rentals plus PV of residual = 1,140,733.87. First-year finance income = opening net investment × 8% = 91,258.71, giving a constant periodic return.

title: Warranty deductible temporary difference • case 2
prompt: A recognised warranty provision carries at LKR 330,000. The entire amount will be deductible only when paid, so its tax base is zero. Sufficient future taxable profit is probable and no recognition exception applies. The enacted rate on reversal is 30%. Find the deferred tax asset.
explanation: Liability tax base = carrying amount − future deduction = zero. Deductible temporary difference = 330,000; DTA = 330,000 × 30% = 99,000.00. Tax expense recognition and cash deduction occur in different periods.

title: Deferred tax expense bridge • case 2
prompt: Opening DTL is LKR 100,000 and closing DTL is 154,000. Opening DTA is 80,000 and closing DTA is 62,000. All changes belong in profit or loss, with no acquisitions, OCI, equity or foreign-exchange effects. Find deferred tax EXPENSE for the year.
explanation: Expense = increase in DTL + decrease in DTA = (154,000 − 100,000) + (80,000 − 62,000) = 72,000.00. Do not confuse the closing net balance with the period expense.

title: Tax loss recognition ceiling • case 2
prompt: Unused tax losses are LKR 840,000. Convincing evidence supports probable FUTURE taxable profit of only 520,000 before those losses expire. There are no other recovery sources or taxable temporary differences. Tax rate is 30%. Find the DTA that can be recognised on the losses.
explanation: Recognise only the losses supported by probable taxable profit: min(840,000, 520,000) × 30% = 156,000.00. The legal loss balance alone does not justify a larger asset.

title: Discounted VIU versus disposal value • case 2
prompt: An asset carries at LKR 1,240,000. Its appropriate value-in-use forecast is 320,000 received at each of the next three year ends, plus net disposal proceeds of 200,000 at year three. Appropriate discount rate is 10%. Fair value less costs of disposal is 850,000. No other cash flows or valuation adjustments apply. Find the impairment loss.
explanation: VIU = PV of three operating receipts plus PV of terminal disposal = 946,055.60. Recoverable amount is the HIGHER of VIU and 850,000: 946,055.60. Impairment = 1,240,000 − 946,055.60 = 293,944.40.

title: CGU residual pro-rata allocation • case 2
prompt: A CGU contains goodwill of LKR 150,000, asset A of 620,000, and asset B of 410,000. Recoverable amount is 810,000. No individual-asset floor restricts allocation and there are no other assets. Find asset B’s carrying amount AFTER allocating the CGU impairment.
explanation: Total impairment = 1,180,000 − 810,000 = 370,000. First eliminate goodwill of 150,000. Allocate remaining 220,000 pro rata to A and B. B loss = 87,572.82; closing B = 322,427.18.

title: CGU reversal without restoring goodwill • case 2
prompt: After past impairment, a CGU has assets A at LKR 600,000 and B at 400,000. All previously impaired goodwill is zero. Recoverable amount now rises to 1,210,000. A’s maximum permitted amount under its no-impairment ceiling is 652,000, and B’s is 504,000; no lower individual recoverable-amount limit applies. What is the maximum total CGU carrying amount after reversal?
explanation: Goodwill impairment is never reversed. The other assets cannot exceed their permitted ceilings: 652,000 + 504,000 = 1,156,000.00, below CGU recoverable amount 1,210,000. Allocate reversals subject to those ceilings.

title: Onerous contract least net exit cost • case 2

The alternative is to terminate now for a penalty of 320,000. No dedicated asset impairment is required and discounting is immaterial. Find the provision for the least net unavoidable cost.
explanation: Net cost of fulfilling = 1,540,000 − 1,010,000 = 530,000. Compare with termination penalty 320,000; the least net cost of exit is 320,000.00. Do not provide for gross fulfilment costs without expected benefits.
family: Onerous contract least net exit cost

title: Restructuring cost boundary • case 2
prompt: A qualifying restructuring has created the required present obligations. Direct supplier-contract cancellation penalties are LKR 210,000; legally required closure clean-up costs are 104,000. Planned staff retraining is 150,000, marketing is 80,000, and investment in new systems is 50,000 for continuing operations. No leases, employee termination benefits, other assets or discounting complications apply. What amount is included in the restructuring provision?
explanation: Include direct expenditures necessarily entailed by the restructuring and unrelated to ongoing activities: 210,000 + 104,000 = 314,000.00. Retraining, marketing and new-system investment for continuing business are excluded.

title: Inspection replacement and depreciation • case 2
prompt: On 1 January an asset’s carrying amount is LKR 940,000, including an old inspection component of 100,000. A new qualifying major inspection costs 192,000 that day and the old component is derecognised. The remaining main asset has four years’ life; the new inspection has three. Both use straight-line depreciation with zero residual value. Find total carrying amount at year end.
explanation: Derecognise old inspection: main asset = 840,000. Depreciate main asset by 210,000.00 and new inspection by 64,000.00. Closing = 630,000.00 + 128,000.00 = 758,000.00.

title: Commercial exchange gain • case 2
prompt: An equipment exchange has commercial substance. The entity gives equipment with carrying amount LKR 820,000 and reliably measurable fair value 1,040,000, plus 200,000 cash. Fair value of the received equipment is not more clearly evident. No other costs or taxes apply. What GAIN is recognised on derecognising the equipment given?
explanation: Cost of received equipment = fair value given + cash = 1,240,000. The gain on the equipment surrendered is only its fair value minus carrying amount: 1,040,000 − 820,000 = 220,000.00. The cash paid is not a gain.

title: Periodic weighted average with discount • case 2
prompt: Opening inventory is 1,000 units at LKR 100 each. A purchase of 540 units is invoiced at 120 each with a 10% trade discount; inward freight is 2,000. Closing quantity is 520 units. Use periodic weighted average. NRV exceeds cost; there are no other movements or costs. Find closing inventory carrying amount.
explanation: Net purchase price per unit = 120 × 90% = 108. Total available cost = 100,000 + 540 × 108 + 2,000 = 160,320. Average = cost / 1,540 units. Closing value = average × 520 = 54,134.03.

title: Net acquisition cash flow • case 2
prompt: A subsidiary acquisition involves cash consideration PAID this year of LKR 1,100,000, plus deferred consideration of 200,000 not yet paid. Cash and cash equivalents acquired with the subsidiary are 110,000; acquired borrowings are 300,000. No fees or other cash payments occur. Find the net INVESTING cash outflow from obtaining control.
explanation: Cash flow from obtaining control is investing, reported net of cash and cash equivalents acquired: 1,100,000 − 110,000 = 990,000.00 outflow. Unpaid deferred consideration and assumed debt are not cash payments in this case.

title: Research expense and midyear amortisation • case 2
prompt: In the current year a project incurs research costs LKR 82,000, development spending of 50,000 before recognition criteria are met, then qualifying development cost of 640,000. The completed asset becomes available for use on 1 July, has a five-year finite life and zero residual value. Use six months of straight-line amortisation. Find TOTAL current-year expense from these items; no impairment applies.
explanation: Expense research and pre-recognition development: 82,000 + 50,000. Capitalise 640,000, then amortise for six months: 640,000/5 × 6/12 = 64,000.00. Total expense = 196,000.00.

title: Associate upstream adjusted earnings • case 2
prompt: An investor owns 30% of an associate. Associate profit is LKR 540,000. The investor’s equity-method adjustments include extra depreciation of 104,000 on acquisition-date fair values, and an upstream inventory sale leaves unrealised profit of 62,000 in the investor’s inventory. No tax, basis differences beyond those stated, impairment or other adjustments apply. Find the equity-accounted share of profit after both adjustments.
explanation: Adjust associate result before taking the share: 540,000 − 104,000 − 62,000 = 374,000. Investor’s share = 30% × adjusted result = 112,200.00. The investor’s share of upstream unrealised profit is eliminated.

title: Returns-adjusted sales revenue • case 3
prompt: A retailer transfers 1,060 products at LKR 1,500 each and receives payment in full. Its supported estimate is that 4.3% will be returned for a full refund. The variable-consideration constraint permits this estimate; no other obligations or taxes apply. What sales revenue is recognised at transfer, excluding the separately accounted return asset?
explanation: Exclude consideration expected to be refunded: 1,590,000.00 × (1 − 4.3%) = 1,521,630.00 revenue. The expected refund is a separate liability; the recovery asset affects cost of sales separately.

title: Loyalty material-right allocation • case 3
prompt: Cash consideration of LKR 1,075,000 covers delivered goods and loyalty points that are a separate material right. Stand-alone selling price of the goods is 1,000,000; the points’ estimated stand-alone price is 115,000, ALREADY adjusted for redemption probability. No points are redeemed yet. What contract liability is allocated to the points?
explanation: Allocate by relative stand-alone prices: 1,075,000 × 115,000 / 1,115,000 = 110,874.44. Do not apply redemption probability again; it is already included in the points’ stand-alone price.

title: Contract-cost asset impairment • case 3
prompt: A qualifying sales commission asset initially cost LKR 198,000 and is amortised evenly over three years. After one year of amortisation, expected remaining consideration for the related services is 930,000; directly related future fulfilment costs not yet expensed are 897,000. Other assets have already been tested and no further adjustment is required. Find the impairment loss on this contract-cost asset.
explanation: Post-amortisation carrying amount = 132,000.00. Recoverable benchmark = remaining consideration − related future costs = 33,000. Impairment = 132,000.00 − 33,000 = 99,000.00.

title: Non-distinct contract modification • case 3
prompt: A single over-time construction obligation had original price LKR 10,300,000. Revenue of 4,120,000.00 was recognised before modification. prompt: A financial asset is modified WITHOUT derecognition. Immediately before modification its gross carrying amount is LKR 1,060,000. title: Debt FVOCI residual movement • case 3
prompt: A debt investment at FVOCI opens with equal fair value and gross amortised cost of LKR 1,075,000, and no accumulated OCI. explanation: Closing amortised-cost benchmark = 1,075,000 + 86,000.00 − 63,000 = 1,098,000.00. OCI is fair value minus that benchmark = 1,237,000 − 1,098,000.00 = 139,000.00. EIR interest is profit or loss.

title: Debt extinguishment after settlement fees • case 3
prompt: A financial liability with carrying amount LKR 1,290,000 is fully extinguished by a cash settlement of 1,110,000 plus a fee of 21,500 paid to the lender as part of the settlement consideration. No replacement debt, other costs or equity component exists. Find the extinguishment GAIN.
explanation: Total consideration paid = 1,110,000 + lender settlement fee 21,500.00 = 1,131,500.00. Gain = liability carrying amount − total settlement consideration = 158,500.00.

family: Own-credit split on an FVTPL liability

prompt: A three-year lease has three equal annual payments of LKR 165,000 each: one at commencement, one in a year and one in two years. Discount rate is 10%. Initial direct costs are 20,000 and incentives received at commencement are 5,000. No restoration obligation exists. Find initial ROU asset cost.
explanation: Initial liability excludes the payment already made: 165,000/1.10 + 165,000/1.10² = 286,363.64. ROU = liability + commencement payment + direct costs − incentive = 466,363.64.
family: Advance rent and initial ROU cost

title: Index-linked payment remeasurement • case 3
prompt: A CPI change triggers a lessee remeasurement. Immediately before it, lease liability is LKR 203,000. The revised remaining payments are 124,630 in one year and the same amount in two years. The original 10% discount rate remains appropriate; no floating-interest-rate change or modification applies. Find the INCREASE in liability, normally adjusting the ROU asset.
explanation: Revised liability = 124,630/1.10 + 124,630/1.10² = 216,300.00. For this index change retain the original discount rate. Increase = revised liability − 203,000 = 13,300.00.

title: Partial termination and remaining ROU • case 3
prompt: A lease modification reduces scope by 40%, with a proportionate reduction in the ROU asset and liability. Immediately before modification, ROU carrying amount is LKR 960,000 and liability 1,060,000. After accounting for termination, remeasuring the remaining payments at the revised appropriate rate gives a liability of 665,000. No impairment applies. Find the FINAL ROU carrying amount after both steps.
explanation: First retain 60% of the ROU (576,000.00) and liability (636,000.00), recognising the termination difference in profit or loss. Then adjust ROU by revised liability minus remaining liability: 29,000.00. Final ROU = 605,000.00.

title: Finance lessor effective interest • case 3
prompt: A finance lessor’s net investment comprises four year-end rentals of LKR 330,000 and an unguaranteed residual of 115,000 recovered at the end of year four. The interest rate implicit in the lease is 8%. No initial direct costs outside those reflected in this rate, credit losses or other adjustments exist. Find finance income for the first year, BEFORE the first rental is received.
explanation: Initial net investment = PV of the four rentals plus PV of residual = 1,177,530.29. First-year finance income = opening net investment × 8% = 94,202.42, giving a constant periodic return.

title: Warranty deductible temporary difference • case 3
prompt: A recognised warranty provision carries at LKR 345,000. The entire amount will be deductible only when paid, so its tax base is zero. Sufficient future taxable profit is probable and no recognition exception applies. The enacted rate on reversal is 30%. Find the deferred tax asset.
explanation: Liability tax base = carrying amount − future deduction = zero. Deductible temporary difference = 345,000; DTA = 345,000 × 30% = 103,500.00. Tax expense recognition and cash deduction occur in different periods.

title: Deferred tax expense bridge • case 3
prompt: Opening DTL is LKR 100,000 and closing DTL is 156,000. Opening DTA is 80,000 and closing DTA is 63,000. All changes belong in profit or loss, with no acquisitions, OCI, equity or foreign-exchange effects. Find deferred tax EXPENSE for the year.
explanation: Expense = increase in DTL + decrease in DTA = (156,000 − 100,000) + (80,000 − 63,000) = 73,000.00. Do not confuse the closing net balance with the period expense.

title: Tax loss recognition ceiling • case 3
prompt: Unused tax losses are LKR 860,000. Convincing evidence supports probable FUTURE taxable profit of only 530,000 before those losses expire. There are no other recovery sources or taxable temporary differences. Tax rate is 30%. Find the DTA that can be recognised on the losses.
explanation: Recognise only the losses supported by probable taxable profit: min(860,000, 530,000) × 30% = 159,000.00. The legal loss balance alone does not justify a larger asset.

title: Discounted VIU versus disposal value • case 3
prompt: An asset carries at LKR 1,260,000. Its appropriate value-in-use forecast is 330,000 received at each of the next three year ends, plus net disposal proceeds of 200,000 at year three. Appropriate discount rate is 10%. Fair value less costs of disposal is 850,000. No other cash flows or valuation adjustments apply. Find the impairment loss.
explanation: VIU = PV of three operating receipts plus PV of terminal disposal = 970,924.12. Recoverable amount is the HIGHER of VIU and 850,000: 970,924.12. Impairment = 1,260,000 − 970,924.12 = 289,075.88.

title: CGU residual pro-rata allocation • case 3
prompt: A CGU contains goodwill of LKR 150,000, asset A of 630,000, and asset B of 415,000. Recoverable amount is 815,000. No individual-asset floor restricts allocation and there are no other assets. Find asset B’s carrying amount AFTER allocating the CGU impairment.
explanation: Total impairment = 1,195,000 − 815,000 = 380,000. First eliminate goodwill of 150,000. Allocate remaining 230,000 pro rata to A and B. B loss = 91,339.71; closing B = 323,660.29.

title: CGU reversal without restoring goodwill • case 3
prompt: After past impairment, a CGU has assets A at LKR 600,000 and B at 400,000. All previously impaired goodwill is zero. Recoverable amount now rises to 1,215,000. A’s maximum permitted amount under its no-impairment ceiling is 653,000, and B’s is 506,000; no lower individual recoverable-amount limit applies. What is the maximum total CGU carrying amount after reversal?
explanation: Goodwill impairment is never reversed. The other assets cannot exceed their permitted ceilings: 653,000 + 506,000 = 1,159,000.00, below CGU recoverable amount 1,215,000. Allocate reversals subject to those ceilings.

title: Onerous contract least net exit cost • case 3
prompt: A contract has a present onerous obligation. Directly related costs to fulfil are LKR 1,560,000, while expected contract benefits are 1,015,000. The alternative is to terminate now for a penalty of 330,000. No dedicated asset impairment is required and discounting is immaterial. Find the provision for the least net unavoidable cost.
explanation: Net cost of fulfilling = 1,560,000 − 1,015,000 = 545,000. Compare with termination penalty 330,000; the least net cost of exit is 330,000.00. Do not provide for gross fulfilment costs without expected benefits.
family: Onerous contract least net exit cost

title: Restructuring cost boundary • case 3
prompt: A qualifying restructuring has created the required present obligations. Direct supplier-contract cancellation penalties are LKR 215,000; legally required closure clean-up costs are 106,000. Planned staff retraining is 150,000, marketing is 80,000, and investment in new systems is 50,000 for continuing operations. No leases, employee termination benefits, other assets or discounting complications apply. What amount is included in the restructuring provision?
explanation: Include direct expenditures necessarily entailed by the restructuring and unrelated to ongoing activities: 215,000 + 106,000 = 321,000.00. Retraining, marketing and new-system investment for continuing business are excluded.

title: Inspection replacement and depreciation • case 3
prompt: On 1 January an asset’s carrying amount is LKR 960,000, including an old inspection component of 100,000. A new qualifying major inspection costs 198,000 that day and the old component is derecognised. The remaining main asset has four years’ life; the new inspection has three. Both use straight-line depreciation with zero residual value. Find total carrying amount at year end.

title: Commercial exchange gain • case 3

Fair value of the received equipment is not more clearly evident. No other costs or taxes apply. What GAIN is recognised on derecognising the equipment given?
explanation: Cost of received equipment = fair value given + cash = 1,260,000. The gain on the equipment surrendered is only its fair value minus carrying amount: 1,060,000 − 830,000 = 230,000.00. The cash paid is not a gain.

title: Periodic weighted average with discount • case 3
prompt: Opening inventory is 1,000 units at LKR 100 each. A purchase of 560 units is invoiced at 120 each with a 10% trade discount; inward freight is 2,000. Closing quantity is 530 units. Use periodic weighted average. NRV exceeds cost; there are no other movements or costs. Find closing inventory carrying amount.
explanation: Net purchase price per unit = 120 × 90% = 108. Total available cost = 100,000 + 560 × 108 + 2,000 = 162,480. Average = cost / 1,560 units. Closing value = average × 530 = 55,201.54.

title: Net acquisition cash flow • case 3
prompt: A subsidiary acquisition involves cash consideration PAID this year of LKR 1,150,000, plus deferred consideration of 200,000 not yet paid. Cash and cash equivalents acquired with the subsidiary are 115,000; acquired borrowings are 300,000. No fees or other cash payments occur. Find the net INVESTING cash outflow from obtaining control.
explanation: Cash flow from obtaining control is investing, reported net of cash and cash equivalents acquired: 1,150,000 − 115,000 = 1,035,000.00 outflow. Unpaid deferred consideration and assumed debt are not cash payments in this case.

title: Research expense and midyear amortisation • case 3
prompt: In the current year a project incurs research costs LKR 83,000, development spending of 50,000 before recognition criteria are met, then qualifying development cost of 660,000. The completed asset becomes available for use on 1 July, has a five-year finite life and zero residual value. Use six months of straight-line amortisation. Find TOTAL current-year expense from these items; no impairment applies.
explanation: Expense research and pre-recognition development: 83,000 + 50,000. Capitalise 660,000, then amortise for six months: 660,000/5 × 6/12 = 66,000.00. Total expense = 199,000.00.

title: Associate upstream adjusted earnings • case 3
prompt: An investor owns 30% of an associate. Associate profit is LKR 560,000. The investor’s equity-method adjustments include extra depreciation of 106,000 on acquisition-date fair values, and an upstream inventory sale leaves unrealised profit of 63,000 in the investor’s inventory. No tax, basis differences beyond those stated, impairment or other adjustments apply. Find the equity-accounted share of profit after both adjustments.
explanation: Adjust associate result before taking the share: 560,000 − 106,000 − 63,000 = 391,000. Investor’s share = 30% × adjusted result = 117,300.00. The investor’s share of upstream unrealised profit is eliminated.

title: Returns-adjusted sales revenue • case 4

The variable-consideration constraint permits this estimate; no other obligations or taxes apply. What sales revenue is recognised at transfer, excluding the separately accounted return asset?
explanation: Exclude consideration expected to be refunded: 1,620,000.00 × (1 − 4.4%) = 1,548,720.00 revenue. The expected refund is a separate liability; the recovery asset affects cost of sales separately.

title: Loyalty material-right allocation • case 4
prompt: Cash consideration of LKR 1,100,000 covers delivered goods and loyalty points that are a separate material right. Stand-alone selling price of the goods is 1,000,000; the points’ estimated stand-alone price is 120,000, ALREADY adjusted for redemption probability. No points are redeemed yet. What contract liability is allocated to the points?

title: Contract-cost asset impairment • case 4

After one year of amortisation, expected remaining consideration for the related services is 940,000; directly related future fulfilment costs not yet expensed are 906,000. Other assets have already been tested and no further adjustment is required. Find the impairment loss on this contract-cost asset.
explanation: Post-amortisation carrying amount = 136,000.00. Recoverable benchmark = remaining consideration − related future costs = 34,000. Impairment = 136,000.00 − 34,000 = 102,000.00.

title: Non-distinct contract modification • case 4
prompt: A single over-time construction obligation had original price LKR 10,400,000. Revenue of 4,160,000.00 was recognised before modification. Approved added work is NOT distinct and adds 2,200,000 to the price. Under the appropriate input method the modified combined obligation is now 50% complete. No variable-price constraint or other issue applies. Find the cumulative catch-up revenue adjustment at modification.
explanation: Because added work is not distinct, update the existing combined obligation. Revised cumulative revenue = (10,400,000 + 2,200,000) × 50% = 6,300,000.00. Less previously recognised 4,160,000.00 gives an adjustment of 2,140,000.00.

title: Advance financing and revenue • case 4

The arrangement contains a significant financing component benefiting the supplier; the appropriate annual rate is 8%. No exemption applies. No other consideration or obligations exist. What revenue is recognised when control of the goods transfers?
explanation: Accrete the contract liability for two years: 1,100,000 × 1.08² = 1,283,040.00. The financing cost is recognised separately over the two years; the increased liability is released as revenue on transfer.

title: Upfront fee over the service term • case 4

The joining activity transfers no separate service, all consideration relates to one evenly provided service obligation, and no renewal material right exists. Find revenue for the first six months of service.
explanation: Total transaction price = 144,000 + 24 × 10,000 = 384,000. The upfront activity is not a separate obligation. Recognise 6/24 of the total = 96,000.00.
family: Upfront fee over the service term

title: Credit-impaired net interest basis • case 4

title: Loan modification without derecognition • case 4
prompt: A financial asset is modified WITHOUT derecognition. Immediately before modification its gross carrying amount is LKR 1,080,000. Revised contractual receipts are 470,000 in one year and 532,000 in two years. Original EIR is 10%. Ignore fees and ECL changes. Find the modification LOSS recognised now.
explanation: Recompute gross carrying amount using the ORIGINAL EIR: 470,000/1.10 + 532,000/1.10² = 866,942.15. Modification loss = old gross amount 1,080,000 − 866,942.15 = 213,057.85.

title: Debt FVOCI residual movement • case 4
prompt: A debt investment at FVOCI opens with equal fair value and gross amortised cost of LKR 1,100,000, and no accumulated OCI. Current EIR interest is 88,000.00, coupon received is 64,000, and closing fair value is 1,266,000. No impairment, foreign exchange, purchases or disposals apply. Find the fair-value gain recognised in OCI for this year.
explanation: Closing amortised-cost benchmark = 1,100,000 + 88,000.00 − 64,000 = 1,124,000.00. OCI is fair value minus that benchmark = 1,266,000 − 1,124,000.00 = 142,000.00. EIR interest is profit or loss.

title: Debt extinguishment after settlement fees • case 4
prompt: A financial liability with carrying amount LKR 1,320,000 is fully extinguished by a cash settlement of 1,130,000 plus a fee of 22,000 paid to the lender as part of the settlement consideration. No replacement debt, other costs or equity component exists. Find the extinguishment GAIN.
explanation: Total consideration paid = 1,130,000 + lender settlement fee 22,000.00 = 1,152,000.00. Gain = liability carrying amount − total settlement consideration = 168,000.00.

title: Own-credit split on an FVTPL liability • case 4
prompt: A liability is designated at FVTPL under the eligible fair-value option. Its fair value increases by LKR 120,000, producing a total loss. Of this, 24,000 is attributable to improved own credit and qualifies for OCI presentation. The split does not create or enlarge an accounting mismatch. Find the loss recognised in PROFIT OR LOSS.
explanation: The eligible own-credit component of 24,000 goes to OCI. The remaining fair-value loss goes to profit or loss: 120,000 − 24,000 = 96,000.00. This presentation is for designated liabilities under the stated conditions.
family: Own-credit split on an FVTPL liability

title: Midyear acquisition and parent earnings • case 4
prompt: P acquires 80% of S on 1 October and reports to 31 December. P’s own annual profit is LKR 2,200,000, excluding any S dividend. S’s annual profit of 1,440,000 accrues evenly. Additional depreciation on acquisition-date fair-value adjustments for the POST-acquisition quarter is 44,000. No tax, intragroup trading, goodwill impairment or other adjustment exists. Find consolidated profit attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Only post-acquisition profit enters: S’s quarter = 360,000.00; less FV depreciation 44,000 gives 316,000.00. Owners’ profit = 2,200,000 + 80% of adjusted quarter profit = 2,452,800.00.

title: Intragroup PPE transfer at year end • case 4
prompt: On 1 January P sells equipment to S for LKR 972,000; carrying amount in P was 648,000. Remaining useful life is three years with no residual value. S depreciates the transfer price straight-line for the full year. No tax or impairment applies. By how much must S’s closing PPE amount be REDUCED on consolidation to restore the group basis?
explanation: Eliminate transfer gain of 324,000, but reverse excess depreciation of 324,000/3 = 108,000.00. Net reduction in closing group PPE = 216,000.00. The intragroup sale does not create a group gain.
family: Intragroup PPE transfer at year end

title: Loss of control and retained interest • case 4
prompt: P loses control of S. Sale proceeds are LKR 2,200,000; fair value of the retained interest is 640,000; carrying NCI derecognised is 420,000. S’s consolidated net assets INCLUDING goodwill carry at 2,620,000. No accumulated OCI, transaction costs or other adjustment exists. Calculate the gain on loss of control.
explanation: Gain = proceeds + fair value retained + carrying NCI − subsidiary net assets including goodwill = 2,200,000 + 640,000 + 420,000 − 2,620,000 = 640,000.00.
