title: Buy more without losing control • case 4
prompt: P increases ownership of S from 80% to 90% and retains control. Carrying amount of the entire 20% NCI before purchase is LKR 440,000. P pays 340,000 for the additional 10% interest. No OCI or other changes exist. What amount is DEBITED to parent owners’ equity for the difference between consideration and NCI carrying amount acquired?
explanation: The purchased 10 percentage points are half of the previous 20% NCI. Derecognise NCI of 220,000.00. Debit parent equity for excess consideration: 340,000 − 220,000.00 = 120,000.00. There is no new goodwill or profit-or-loss charge.

title: Acquisition consideration at present value • case 4
prompt: An acquirer pays cash LKR 2,200,000 now, owes fixed consideration of 1,144,000 in one year, and has acquisition-date fair value of contingent consideration of 220,000. Discount fixed deferred consideration at 10%. NCI fair value is 500,000; identifiable net assets are 3,080,000. No previous holding or other adjustment applies. Find goodwill.
explanation: Deferred consideration PV = 1,144,000/1.10 = 1,040,000.00. Goodwill = upfront + discounted fixed consideration + contingent FV + NCI − identifiable net assets = 880,000.00. Later financing unwinding is separate.

title: Acquisition uplift and deferred tax • case 4
prompt: Consideration is LKR 3,200,000; NCI is measured at fair value of 600,000. Identifiable net assets before an equipment uplift are 2,880,000. Acquisition-date equipment uplift is 440,000, with no tax-base uplift. Tax rate on reversal is 30%; no DTL exception applies. No other adjustment exists. Find goodwill after recognising the uplift and related DTL.
explanation: DTL on uplift = 440,000 × 30% = 132,000.00. Net identifiable assets = 2,880,000 + 440,000 − DTL = 3,188,000.00. Goodwill = consideration + NCI − net identifiable assets = 612,000.00.

title: Measurement-period goodwill adjustment • case 4
prompt: Provisional goodwill was LKR 1,080,000. During the measurement period, new information about acquisition-date facts establishes an additional identifiable equipment fair-value uplift of 220,000. The tax base is unchanged and a 30% DTL must be recognised. NCI was measured at fair value and that value is unchanged. All other acquisition amounts are final. Find revised acquisition-date goodwill.
explanation: Additional net identifiable assets = uplift − 30% DTL = 154,000.00. Retrospectively reduce goodwill by that net amount: 1,080,000 − 154,000.00 = 926,000.00. Subsequent equipment depreciation is considered separately.

explanation: Total impairment = 1,210,000 − 820,000 = 390,000. First eliminate goodwill of 150,000. Allocate remaining 240,000 pro rata to A and B. B loss = 95,094.34; closing B = 324,905.66.

explanation: Cash flow from obtaining control is investing, reported net of cash and cash equivalents acquired: 1,200,000 − 120,000 = 1,080,000.00 outflow. Unpaid deferred consideration and assumed debt are not cash payments in this case.

title: Research expense and midyear amortisation • case 4
prompt: In the current year a project incurs research costs LKR 84,000, development spending of 50,000 before recognition criteria are met, then qualifying development cost of 680,000. The completed asset becomes available for use on 1 July, has a five-year finite life and zero residual value. Use six months of straight-line amortisation. Find TOTAL current-year expense from these items; no impairment applies.
explanation: Expense research and pre-recognition development: 84,000 + 50,000. Capitalise 680,000, then amortise for six months: 680,000/5 × 6/12 = 68,000.00. Total expense = 202,000.00.

title: Associate upstream adjusted earnings • case 4
prompt: An investor owns 30% of an associate. Associate profit is LKR 580,000. The investor’s equity-method adjustments include extra depreciation of 108,000 on acquisition-date fair values, and an upstream inventory sale leaves unrealised profit of 64,000 in the investor’s inventory. No tax, basis differences beyond those stated, impairment or other adjustments apply. Find the equity-accounted share of profit after both adjustments.
explanation: Adjust associate result before taking the share: 580,000 − 108,000 − 64,000 = 408,000. Investor’s share = 30% × adjusted result = 122,400.00. The investor’s share of upstream unrealised profit is eliminated.

title: Returns-adjusted sales revenue • case 5
prompt: A retailer transfers 1,100 products at LKR 1,500 each and receives payment in full. Its supported estimate is that 4.5% will be returned for a full refund. The variable-consideration constraint permits this estimate; no other obligations or taxes apply. What sales revenue is recognised at transfer, excluding the separately accounted return asset?
explanation: Exclude consideration expected to be refunded: 1,650,000.00 × (1 − 4.5%) = 1,575,750.00 revenue. The expected refund is a separate liability; the recovery asset affects cost of sales separately.

title: Loyalty material-right allocation • case 5
prompt: Cash consideration of LKR 1,125,000 covers delivered goods and loyalty points that are a separate material right. Stand-alone selling price of the goods is 1,000,000; the points’ estimated stand-alone price is 125,000, ALREADY adjusted for redemption probability. No points are redeemed yet. What contract liability is allocated to the points?
explanation: Allocate by relative stand-alone prices: 1,125,000 × 125,000 / 1,125,000 = 125,000.00. Do not apply redemption probability again; it is already included in the points’ stand-alone price.

title: Contract-cost asset impairment • case 5
prompt: A qualifying sales commission asset initially cost LKR 210,000 and is amortised evenly over three years. After one year of amortisation, expected remaining consideration for the related services is 950,000; directly related future fulfilment costs not yet expensed are 915,000. Other assets have already been tested and no further adjustment is required. Find the impairment loss on this contract-cost asset.
explanation: Post-amortisation carrying amount = 140,000.00. Recoverable benchmark = remaining consideration − related future costs = 35,000. Impairment = 140,000.00 − 35,000 = 105,000.00.

title: Non-distinct contract modification • case 5
prompt: A single over-time construction obligation had original price LKR 10,500,000. Revenue of 4,200,000.00 was recognised before modification. Approved added work is NOT distinct and adds 2,250,000 to the price. Under the appropriate input method the modified combined obligation is now 50% complete. No variable-price constraint or other issue applies. Find the cumulative catch-up revenue adjustment at modification.
explanation: Because added work is not distinct, update the existing combined obligation. Revised cumulative revenue = (10,500,000 + 2,250,000) × 50% = 6,375,000.00. Less previously recognised 4,200,000.00 gives an adjustment of 2,175,000.00.

title: Advance financing and revenue • case 5
prompt: A customer prepays LKR 1,125,000 exactly two years before goods transfer. The arrangement contains a significant financing component benefiting the supplier; the appropriate annual rate is 8%. No exemption applies. No other consideration or obligations exist. What revenue is recognised when control of the goods transfers?
explanation: Accrete the contract liability for two years: 1,125,000 × 1.08² = 1,312,200.00. The financing cost is recognised separately over the two years; the increased liability is released as revenue on transfer.

title: Upfront fee over the service term • case 5
prompt: A two-year service contract has a non-refundable joining fee of LKR 150,000 plus fixed monthly fees of 10,000 for 24 months. The joining activity transfers no separate service, all consideration relates to one evenly provided service obligation, and no renewal material right exists. Find revenue for the first six months of service.
explanation: Total transaction price = 150,000 + 24 × 10,000 = 390,000. The upfront activity is not a separate obligation. Recognise 6/24 of the total = 97,500.00.
family: Upfront fee over the service term

title: Credit-impaired net interest basis • case 5
prompt: A loan originated unimpaired subsequently became credit-impaired in the prior reporting period and remains so throughout the current year. Opening gross amortised cost is LKR 1,750,000; loss allowance is 350,000. Original effective rate is 9%. No cash flows or other opening adjustments occur. Find current-year interest revenue.
explanation: For this subsequently credit-impaired asset, apply the original EIR to amortised cost NET of allowance: (1,750,000 − 350,000) × 9% = 126,000.00. This is not the purchased/originated credit-impaired model.

title: Loan modification without derecognition • case 5
prompt: A financial asset is modified WITHOUT derecognition. Immediately before modification its gross carrying amount is LKR 1,100,000. Revised contractual receipts are 475,000 in one year and 540,000 in two years. Original EIR is 10%. Ignore fees and ECL changes. Find the modification LOSS recognised now.
explanation: Recompute gross carrying amount using the ORIGINAL EIR: 475,000/1.10 + 540,000/1.10² = 878,099.17. Modification loss = old gross amount 1,100,000 − 878,099.17 = 221,900.83.

title: Debt FVOCI residual movement • case 5
prompt: A debt investment at FVOCI opens with equal fair value and gross amortised cost of LKR 1,125,000, and no accumulated OCI. Current EIR interest is 90,000.00, coupon received is 65,000, and closing fair value is 1,295,000. No impairment, foreign exchange, purchases or disposals apply. Find the fair-value gain recognised in OCI for this year.
explanation: Closing amortised-cost benchmark = 1,125,000 + 90,000.00 − 65,000 = 1,150,000.00. OCI is fair value minus that benchmark = 1,295,000 − 1,150,000.00 = 145,000.00. EIR interest is profit or loss.

title: Debt extinguishment after settlement fees • case 5
prompt: A financial liability with carrying amount LKR 1,350,000 is fully extinguished by a cash settlement of 1,150,000 plus a fee of 22,500 paid to the lender as part of the settlement consideration. No replacement debt, other costs or equity component exists. Find the extinguishment GAIN.
explanation: Total consideration paid = 1,150,000 + lender settlement fee 22,500.00 = 1,172,500.00. Gain = liability carrying amount − total settlement consideration = 177,500.00.

title: Own-credit split on an FVTPL liability • case 5
prompt: A liability is designated at FVTPL under the eligible fair-value option. Its fair value increases by LKR 125,000, producing a total loss. Of this, 25,000 is attributable to improved own credit and qualifies for OCI presentation. The split does not create or enlarge an accounting mismatch. Find the loss recognised in PROFIT OR LOSS.
explanation: The eligible own-credit component of 25,000 goes to OCI. The remaining fair-value loss goes to profit or loss: 125,000 − 25,000 = 100,000.00. This presentation is for designated liabilities under the stated conditions.
family: Own-credit split on an FVTPL liability

title: Midyear acquisition and parent earnings • case 5
prompt: P acquires 80% of S on 1 October and reports to 31 December. P’s own annual profit is LKR 2,250,000, excluding any S dividend. S’s annual profit of 1,500,000 accrues evenly. Additional depreciation on acquisition-date fair-value adjustments for the POST-acquisition quarter is 45,000. No tax, intragroup trading, goodwill impairment or other adjustment exists. Find consolidated profit attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Only post-acquisition profit enters: S’s quarter = 375,000.00; less FV depreciation 45,000 gives 330,000.00. Owners’ profit = 2,250,000 + 80% of adjusted quarter profit = 2,514,000.00.

title: Intragroup PPE transfer at year end • case 5
prompt: On 1 January P sells equipment to S for LKR 990,000; carrying amount in P was 660,000. Remaining useful life is three years with no residual value. S depreciates the transfer price straight-line for the full year. No tax or impairment applies. By how much must S’s closing PPE amount be REDUCED on consolidation to restore the group basis?
explanation: Eliminate transfer gain of 330,000, but reverse excess depreciation of 330,000/3 = 110,000.00. Net reduction in closing group PPE = 220,000.00. The intragroup sale does not create a group gain.
family: Intragroup PPE transfer at year end

title: Loss of control and retained interest • case 5
prompt: P loses control of S. Sale proceeds are LKR 2,250,000; fair value of the retained interest is 650,000; carrying NCI derecognised is 425,000. S’s consolidated net assets INCLUDING goodwill carry at 2,650,000. No accumulated OCI, transaction costs or other adjustment exists. Calculate the gain on loss of control.
explanation: Gain = proceeds + fair value retained + carrying NCI − subsidiary net assets including goodwill = 2,250,000 + 650,000 + 425,000 − 2,650,000 = 675,000.00.

title: Buy more without losing control • case 5

No OCI or other changes exist. What amount is DEBITED to parent owners’ equity for the difference between consideration and NCI carrying amount acquired?
explanation: The purchased 10 percentage points are half of the previous 20% NCI. Derecognise NCI of 225,000.00. Debit parent equity for excess consideration: 350,000 − 225,000.00 = 125,000.00. There is no new goodwill or profit-or-loss charge.

title: Acquisition consideration at present value • case 5
prompt: An acquirer pays cash LKR 2,250,000 now, owes fixed consideration of 1,155,000 in one year, and has acquisition-date fair value of contingent consideration of 225,000. Discount fixed deferred consideration at 10%. NCI fair value is 500,000; identifiable net assets are 3,100,000. No previous holding or other adjustment applies. Find goodwill.
explanation: Deferred consideration PV = 1,155,000/1.10 = 1,050,000.00. Goodwill = upfront + discounted fixed consideration + contingent FV + NCI − identifiable net assets = 925,000.00. Later financing unwinding is separate.

title: Acquisition uplift and deferred tax • case 5
prompt: Consideration is LKR 3,250,000; NCI is measured at fair value of 600,000. Identifiable net assets before an equipment uplift are 2,900,000. Acquisition-date equipment uplift is 450,000, with no tax-base uplift. Tax rate on reversal is 30%; no DTL exception applies. No other adjustment exists. Find goodwill after recognising the uplift and related DTL.
explanation: DTL on uplift = 450,000 × 30% = 135,000.00. Net identifiable assets = 2,900,000 + 450,000 − DTL = 3,215,000.00. Goodwill = consideration + NCI − net identifiable assets = 635,000.00.

title: Measurement-period goodwill adjustment • case 5
prompt: Provisional goodwill was LKR 1,100,000. During the measurement period, new information about acquisition-date facts establishes an additional identifiable equipment fair-value uplift of 225,000. The tax base is unchanged and a 30% DTL must be recognised. NCI was measured at fair value and that value is unchanged. All other acquisition amounts are final. Find revised acquisition-date goodwill.
explanation: Additional net identifiable assets = uplift − 30% DTL = 157,500.00. Retrospectively reduce goodwill by that net amount: 1,100,000 − 157,500.00 = 942,500.00. Subsequent equipment depreciation is considered separately.

title: Advance rent and initial ROU cost • case 5
prompt: A three-year lease has three equal annual payments of LKR 175,000 each: one at commencement, one in a year and one in two years. Discount rate is 10%. Initial direct costs are 20,000 and incentives received at commencement are 5,000. No restoration obligation exists. Find initial ROU asset cost.
explanation: Initial liability excludes the payment already made: 175,000/1.10 + 175,000/1.10² = 303,719.01. ROU = liability + commencement payment + direct costs − incentive = 493,719.01.
family: Advance rent and initial ROU cost

title: Index-linked payment remeasurement • case 5
prompt: A CPI change triggers a lessee remeasurement. Immediately before it, lease liability is LKR 205,000. The revised remaining payments are 127,050 in one year and the same amount in two years. The original 10% discount rate remains appropriate; no floating-interest-rate change or modification applies. Find the INCREASE in liability, normally adjusting the ROU asset.
explanation: Revised liability = 127,050/1.10 + 127,050/1.10² = 220,500.00. For this index change retain the original discount rate. Increase = revised liability − 205,000 = 15,500.00.

title: Partial termination and remaining ROU • case 5
prompt: A lease modification reduces scope by 40%, with a proportionate reduction in the ROU asset and liability. Immediately before modification, ROU carrying amount is LKR 1,000,000 and liability 1,100,000. After accounting for termination, remeasuring the remaining payments at the revised appropriate rate gives a liability of 695,000. No impairment applies. Find the FINAL ROU carrying amount after both steps.
explanation: First retain 60% of the ROU (600,000.00) and liability (660,000.00), recognising the termination difference in profit or loss. Then adjust ROU by revised liability minus remaining liability: 35,000.00. Final ROU = 635,000.00.

title: Finance lessor effective interest • case 5
prompt: A finance lessor’s net investment comprises four year-end rentals of LKR 350,000 and an unguaranteed residual of 125,000 recovered at the end of year four. The interest rate implicit in the lease is 8%. No initial direct costs outside those reflected in this rate, credit losses or other adjustments exist. Find finance income for the first year, BEFORE the first rental is received.
explanation: Initial net investment = PV of the four rentals plus PV of residual = 1,251,123.13. First-year finance income = opening net investment × 8% = 100,089.85, giving a constant periodic return.

title: Warranty deductible temporary difference • case 5
prompt: A recognised warranty provision carries at LKR 375,000. The entire amount will be deductible only when paid, so its tax base is zero. Sufficient future taxable profit is probable and no recognition exception applies. The enacted rate on reversal is 30%. Find the deferred tax asset.
explanation: Liability tax base = carrying amount − future deduction = zero. Deductible temporary difference = 375,000; DTA = 375,000 × 30% = 112,500.00. Tax expense recognition and cash deduction occur in different periods.

title: Deferred tax expense bridge • case 5
prompt: Opening DTL is LKR 100,000 and closing DTL is 160,000. Opening DTA is 80,000 and closing DTA is 65,000. All changes belong in profit or loss, with no acquisitions, OCI, equity or foreign-exchange effects. Find deferred tax EXPENSE for the year.
explanation: Expense = increase in DTL + decrease in DTA = (160,000 − 100,000) + (80,000 − 65,000) = 75,000.00. Do not confuse the closing net balance with the period expense.

title: Tax loss recognition ceiling • case 5
prompt: Unused tax losses are LKR 900,000. Convincing evidence supports probable FUTURE taxable profit of only 550,000 before those losses expire. There are no other recovery sources or taxable temporary differences. Tax rate is 30%. Find the DTA that can be recognised on the losses.
explanation: Recognise only the losses supported by probable taxable profit: min(900,000, 550,000) × 30% = 165,000.00. The legal loss balance alone does not justify a larger asset.

title: Discounted VIU versus disposal value • case 5
prompt: An asset carries at LKR 1,300,000. Its appropriate value-in-use forecast is 350,000 received at each of the next three year ends, plus net disposal proceeds of 200,000 at year three. Appropriate discount rate is 10%. Fair value less costs of disposal is 850,000. No other cash flows or valuation adjustments apply. Find the impairment loss.
explanation: VIU = PV of three operating receipts plus PV of terminal disposal = 1,020,661.16. Recoverable amount is the HIGHER of VIU and 850,000: 1,020,661.16. Impairment = 1,300,000 − 1,020,661.16 = 279,338.84.

title: CGU residual pro-rata allocation • case 5
prompt: A CGU contains goodwill of LKR 150,000, asset A of 650,000, and asset B of 425,000. Recoverable amount is 825,000. No individual-asset floor restricts allocation and there are no other assets. Find asset B’s carrying amount AFTER allocating the CGU impairment.
explanation: Total impairment = 1,225,000 − 825,000 = 400,000. First eliminate goodwill of 150,000. Allocate remaining 250,000 pro rata to A and B. B loss = 98,837.21; closing B = 326,162.79.

title: CGU reversal without restoring goodwill • case 5
prompt: After past impairment, a CGU has assets A at LKR 600,000 and B at 400,000. All previously impaired goodwill is zero. Recoverable amount now rises to 1,225,000. A’s maximum permitted amount under its no-impairment ceiling is 655,000, and B’s is 510,000; no lower individual recoverable-amount limit applies. What is the maximum total CGU carrying amount after reversal?
explanation: Goodwill impairment is never reversed. The other assets cannot exceed their permitted ceilings: 655,000 + 510,000 = 1,165,000.00, below CGU recoverable amount 1,225,000. Allocate reversals subject to those ceilings.

title: Onerous contract least net exit cost • case 5

The alternative is to terminate now for a penalty of 350,000. No dedicated asset impairment is required and discounting is immaterial. Find the provision for the least net unavoidable cost.
explanation: Net cost of fulfilling = 1,600,000 − 1,025,000 = 575,000. Compare with termination penalty 350,000; the least net cost of exit is 350,000.00. Do not provide for gross fulfilment costs without expected benefits.
family: Onerous contract least net exit cost

title: Restructuring cost boundary • case 5
prompt: A qualifying restructuring has created the required present obligations. Direct supplier-contract cancellation penalties are LKR 225,000; legally required closure clean-up costs are 110,000. Planned staff retraining is 150,000, marketing is 80,000, and investment in new systems is 50,000 for continuing operations. No leases, employee termination benefits, other assets or discounting complications apply. What amount is included in the restructuring provision?
explanation: Include direct expenditures necessarily entailed by the restructuring and unrelated to ongoing activities: 225,000 + 110,000 = 335,000.00. Retraining, marketing and new-system investment for continuing business are excluded.

title: Inspection replacement and depreciation • case 5

A new qualifying major inspection costs 210,000 that day and the old component is derecognised. The remaining main asset has four years’ life; the new inspection has three. Both use straight-line depreciation with zero residual value. Find total carrying amount at year end.
explanation: Derecognise old inspection: main asset = 900,000. Depreciate main asset by 225,000.00 and new inspection by 70,000.00. Closing = 675,000.00 + 140,000.00 = 815,000.00.

title: Commercial exchange gain • case 5
prompt: An equipment exchange has commercial substance. The entity gives equipment with carrying amount LKR 850,000 and reliably measurable fair value 1,100,000, plus 200,000 cash. Fair value of the received equipment is not more clearly evident. No other costs or taxes apply. What GAIN is recognised on derecognising the equipment given?
explanation: Cost of received equipment = fair value given + cash = 1,300,000. The gain on the equipment surrendered is only its fair value minus carrying amount: 1,100,000 − 850,000 = 250,000.00. The cash paid is not a gain.

title: Periodic weighted average with discount • case 5
prompt: Opening inventory is 1,000 units at LKR 100 each. A purchase of 600 units is invoiced at 120 each with a 10% trade discount; inward freight is 2,000. Closing quantity is 550 units. Use periodic weighted average. NRV exceeds cost; there are no other movements or costs. Find closing inventory carrying amount.
explanation: Net purchase price per unit = 120 × 90% = 108. Total available cost = 100,000 + 600 × 108 + 2,000 = 166,800. Average = cost / 1,600 units. Closing value = average × 550 = 57,337.50.

title: Net acquisition cash flow • case 5
prompt: A subsidiary acquisition involves cash consideration PAID this year of LKR 1,250,000, plus deferred consideration of 200,000 not yet paid. Cash and cash equivalents acquired with the subsidiary are 125,000; acquired borrowings are 300,000. No fees or other cash payments occur. Find the net INVESTING cash outflow from obtaining control.
explanation: Cash flow from obtaining control is investing, reported net of cash and cash equivalents acquired: 1,250,000 − 125,000 = 1,125,000.00 outflow. Unpaid deferred consideration and assumed debt are not cash payments in this case.

title: Loss of control and retained interest • case 6
prompt: P loses control of S. Sale proceeds are LKR 2,300,000; fair value of the retained interest is 660,000; carrying NCI derecognised is 430,000. S’s consolidated net assets INCLUDING goodwill carry at 2,680,000. No accumulated OCI, transaction costs or other adjustment exists. Calculate the gain on loss of control.
explanation: Gain = proceeds + fair value retained + carrying NCI − subsidiary net assets including goodwill = 2,300,000 + 660,000 + 430,000 − 2,680,000 = 710,000.00.
family: Loss of control and retained interest

title: Buy more without losing control • case 6
prompt: P increases ownership of S from 80% to 90% and retains control. Carrying amount of the entire 20% NCI before purchase is LKR 460,000. P pays 360,000 for the additional 10% interest. No OCI or other changes exist. What amount is DEBITED to parent owners’ equity for the difference between consideration and NCI carrying amount acquired?
explanation: The purchased 10 percentage points are half of the previous 20% NCI. Derecognise NCI of 230,000.00. Debit parent equity for excess consideration: 360,000 − 230,000.00 = 130,000.00. There is no new goodwill or profit-or-loss charge.

title: Acquisition consideration at present value • case 6
prompt: An acquirer pays cash LKR 2,300,000 now, owes fixed consideration of 1,166,000 in one year, and has acquisition-date fair value of contingent consideration of 230,000. Discount fixed deferred consideration at 10%. NCI fair value is 500,000; identifiable net assets are 3,120,000. No previous holding or other adjustment applies. Find goodwill.
explanation: Deferred consideration PV = 1,166,000/1.10 = 1,060,000.00. Goodwill = upfront + discounted fixed consideration + contingent FV + NCI − identifiable net assets = 970,000.00. Later financing unwinding is separate.

title: Acquisition uplift and deferred tax • case 6
prompt: Consideration is LKR 3,300,000; NCI is measured at fair value of 600,000. Identifiable net assets before an equipment uplift are 2,920,000. Acquisition-date equipment uplift is 460,000, with no tax-base uplift. Tax rate on reversal is 30%; no DTL exception applies. No other adjustment exists. Find goodwill after recognising the uplift and related DTL.
explanation: DTL on uplift = 460,000 × 30% = 138,000.00. Net identifiable assets = 2,920,000 + 460,000 − DTL = 3,242,000.00. Goodwill = consideration + NCI − net identifiable assets = 658,000.00.

title: Measurement-period goodwill adjustment • case 6
prompt: Provisional goodwill was LKR 1,120,000. During the measurement period, new information about acquisition-date facts establishes an additional identifiable equipment fair-value uplift of 230,000. The tax base is unchanged and a 30% DTL must be recognised. NCI was measured at fair value and that value is unchanged. All other acquisition amounts are final. Find revised acquisition-date goodwill.
explanation: Additional net identifiable assets = uplift − 30% DTL = 161,000.00. Retrospectively reduce goodwill by that net amount: 1,120,000 − 161,000.00 = 959,000.00. Subsequent equipment depreciation is considered separately.

title: Advance rent and initial ROU cost • case 6
prompt: A three-year lease has three equal annual payments of LKR 180,000 each: one at commencement, one in a year and one in two years. Discount rate is 10%. Initial direct costs are 20,000 and incentives received at commencement are 5,000. No restoration obligation exists. Find initial ROU asset cost.
explanation: Initial liability excludes the payment already made: 180,000/1.10 + 180,000/1.10² = 312,396.69. ROU = liability + commencement payment + direct costs − incentive = 507,396.69.
family: Advance rent and initial ROU cost

title: Index-linked payment remeasurement • case 6
prompt: A CPI change triggers a lessee remeasurement. Immediately before it, lease liability is LKR 206,000. The revised remaining payments are 128,260 in one year and the same amount in two years. The original 10% discount rate remains appropriate; no floating-interest-rate change or modification applies. Find the INCREASE in liability, normally adjusting the ROU asset.
explanation: Revised liability = 128,260/1.10 + 128,260/1.10² = 222,600.00. For this index change retain the original discount rate. Increase = revised liability − 206,000 = 16,600.00.

title: Partial termination and remaining ROU • case 6
prompt: A lease modification reduces scope by 40%, with a proportionate reduction in the ROU asset and liability. Immediately before modification, ROU carrying amount is LKR 1,020,000 and liability 1,120,000. After accounting for termination, remeasuring the remaining payments at the revised appropriate rate gives a liability of 710,000. No impairment applies. Find the FINAL ROU carrying amount after both steps.
explanation: First retain 60% of the ROU (612,000.00) and liability (672,000.00), recognising the termination difference in profit or loss. Then adjust ROU by revised liability minus remaining liability: 38,000.00. Final ROU = 650,000.00.

title: Finance lessor effective interest • case 6
prompt: A finance lessor’s net investment comprises four year-end rentals of LKR 360,000 and an unguaranteed residual of 130,000 recovered at the end of year four. The interest rate implicit in the lease is 8%. No initial direct costs outside those reflected in this rate, credit losses or other adjustments exist. Find finance income for the first year, BEFORE the first rental is received.
explanation: Initial net investment = PV of the four rentals plus PV of residual = 1,287,919.54. First-year finance income = opening net investment × 8% = 103,033.56, giving a constant periodic return.

title: Warranty deductible temporary difference • case 6
prompt: A recognised warranty provision carries at LKR 390,000. The entire amount will be deductible only when paid, so its tax base is zero. Sufficient future taxable profit is probable and no recognition exception applies. The enacted rate on reversal is 30%. Find the deferred tax asset.
explanation: Liability tax base = carrying amount − future deduction = zero. Deductible temporary difference = 390,000; DTA = 390,000 × 30% = 117,000.00. Tax expense recognition and cash deduction occur in different periods.

title: Deferred tax expense bridge • case 6
prompt: Opening DTL is LKR 100,000 and closing DTL is 162,000. Opening DTA is 80,000 and closing DTA is 66,000. All changes belong in profit or loss, with no acquisitions, OCI, equity or foreign-exchange effects. Find deferred tax EXPENSE for the year.
explanation: Expense = increase in DTL + decrease in DTA = (162,000 − 100,000) + (80,000 − 66,000) = 76,000.00. Do not confuse the closing net balance with the period expense.

title: Tax loss recognition ceiling • case 6

title: Discounted VIU versus disposal value • case 6

explanation: VIU = PV of three operating receipts plus PV of terminal disposal = 1,045,529.68. Recoverable amount is the HIGHER of VIU and 850,000: 1,045,529.68. Impairment = 1,320,000 − 1,045,529.68 = 274,470.32.

title: CGU residual pro-rata allocation • case 6

title: CGU reversal without restoring goodwill • case 6

title: Restructuring cost boundary • case 6

title: Inspection replacement and depreciation • case 6

title: Periodic weighted average with discount • case 6

title: Research expense and midyear amortisation • case 6

title: Non-distinct contract modification • case 7

title: Onerous contract least net exit cost • case 7
prompt: A contract has a present onerous obligation. Directly related costs to fulfil are LKR 1,640,000, while expected contract benefits are 1,035,000. The alternative is to terminate now for a penalty of 370,000. No dedicated asset impairment is required and discounting is immaterial. Find the provision for the least net unavoidable cost.
explanation: Net cost of fulfilling = 1,640,000 − 1,035,000 = 605,000. Compare with termination penalty 370,000; the least net cost of exit is 370,000.00. Do not provide for gross fulfilment costs without expected benefits.
family: Onerous contract least net exit cost

title: Restructuring cost boundary • case 7
prompt: A qualifying restructuring has created the required present obligations. Direct supplier-contract cancellation penalties are LKR 235,000; legally required closure clean-up costs are 114,000. Planned staff retraining is 150,000, marketing is 80,000, and investment in new systems is 50,000 for continuing operations. No leases, employee termination benefits, other assets or discounting complications apply. What amount is included in the restructuring provision?
explanation: Include direct expenditures necessarily entailed by the restructuring and unrelated to ongoing activities: 235,000 + 114,000 = 349,000.00. Retraining, marketing and new-system investment for continuing business are excluded.

title: Inspection replacement and depreciation • case 7
prompt: On 1 January an asset’s carrying amount is LKR 1,040,000, including an old inspection component of 100,000. A new qualifying major inspection costs 222,000 that day and the old component is derecognised. The remaining main asset has four years’ life; the new inspection has three. Both use straight-line depreciation with zero residual value. Find total carrying amount at year end.
explanation: Derecognise old inspection: main asset = 940,000. Depreciate main asset by 235,000.00 and new inspection by 74,000.00. Closing = 705,000.00 + 148,000.00 = 853,000.00.

title: Commercial exchange gain • case 7
prompt: An equipment exchange has commercial substance. The entity gives equipment with carrying amount LKR 870,000 and reliably measurable fair value 1,140,000, plus 200,000 cash. Fair value of the received equipment is not more clearly evident. No other costs or taxes apply. What GAIN is recognised on derecognising the equipment given?
explanation: Cost of received equipment = fair value given + cash = 1,340,000. The gain on the equipment surrendered is only its fair value minus carrying amount: 1,140,000 − 870,000 = 270,000.00. The cash paid is not a gain.

title: Periodic weighted average with discount • case 7
prompt: Opening inventory is 1,000 units at LKR 100 each. A purchase of 640 units is invoiced at 120 each with a 10% trade discount; inward freight is 2,000. Closing quantity is 570 units. Use periodic weighted average. NRV exceeds cost; there are no other movements or costs. Find closing inventory carrying amount.
explanation: Net purchase price per unit = 120 × 90% = 108. Total available cost = 100,000 + 640 × 108 + 2,000 = 171,120. Average = cost / 1,640 units. Closing value = average × 570 = 59,474.63.

title: Net acquisition cash flow • case 7
prompt: A subsidiary acquisition involves cash consideration PAID this year of LKR 1,350,000, plus deferred consideration of 200,000 not yet paid. Cash and cash equivalents acquired with the subsidiary are 135,000; acquired borrowings are 300,000. No fees or other cash payments occur. Find the net INVESTING cash outflow from obtaining control.
explanation: Cash flow from obtaining control is investing, reported net of cash and cash equivalents acquired: 1,350,000 − 135,000 = 1,215,000.00 outflow. Unpaid deferred consideration and assumed debt are not cash payments in this case.

title: Research expense and midyear amortisation • case 7
prompt: In the current year a project incurs research costs LKR 87,000, development spending of 50,000 before recognition criteria are met, then qualifying development cost of 740,000. The completed asset becomes available for use on 1 July, has a five-year finite life and zero residual value. Use six months of straight-line amortisation. Find TOTAL current-year expense from these items; no impairment applies.
explanation: Expense research and pre-recognition development: 87,000 + 50,000. Capitalise 740,000, then amortise for six months: 740,000/5 × 6/12 = 74,000.00. Total expense = 211,000.00.

title: Associate upstream adjusted earnings • case 7
prompt: An investor owns 30% of an associate. Associate profit is LKR 640,000. The investor’s equity-method adjustments include extra depreciation of 114,000 on acquisition-date fair values, and an upstream inventory sale leaves unrealised profit of 67,000 in the investor’s inventory. No tax, basis differences beyond those stated, impairment or other adjustments apply. Find the equity-accounted share of profit after both adjustments.
explanation: Adjust associate result before taking the share: 640,000 − 114,000 − 67,000 = 459,000. Investor’s share = 30% × adjusted result = 137,700.00. The investor’s share of upstream unrealised profit is eliminated.

title: Returns-adjusted sales revenue • case 8
prompt: A retailer transfers 1,160 products at LKR 1,500 each and receives payment in full. Its supported estimate is that 4.8% will be returned for a full refund. The variable-consideration constraint permits this estimate; no other obligations or taxes apply. What sales revenue is recognised at transfer, excluding the separately accounted return asset?
explanation: Exclude consideration expected to be refunded: 1,740,000.00 × (1 − 4.8%) = 1,656,480.00 revenue. The expected refund is a separate liability; the recovery asset affects cost of sales separately.

title: Loyalty material-right allocation • case 8
prompt: Cash consideration of LKR 1,200,000 covers delivered goods and loyalty points that are a separate material right. Stand-alone selling price of the goods is 1,000,000; the points’ estimated stand-alone price is 140,000, ALREADY adjusted for redemption probability. No points are redeemed yet. What contract liability is allocated to the points?
explanation: Allocate by relative stand-alone prices: 1,200,000 × 140,000 / 1,140,000 = 147,368.42. Do not apply redemption probability again; it is already included in the points’ stand-alone price.

title: Contract-cost asset impairment • case 8
prompt: A qualifying sales commission asset initially cost LKR 228,000 and is amortised evenly over three years. After one year of amortisation, expected remaining consideration for the related services is 980,000; directly related future fulfilment costs not yet expensed are 942,000. Other assets have already been tested and no further adjustment is required. Find the impairment loss on this contract-cost asset.
explanation: Post-amortisation carrying amount = 152,000.00. Recoverable benchmark = remaining consideration − related future costs = 38,000. Impairment = 152,000.00 − 38,000 = 114,000.00.

title: Non-distinct contract modification • case 8
prompt: A single over-time construction obligation had original price LKR 10,800,000. Revenue of 4,320,000.00 was recognised before modification. Approved added work is NOT distinct and adds 2,400,000 to the price. Under the appropriate input method the modified combined obligation is now 50% complete. No variable-price constraint or other issue applies. Find the cumulative catch-up revenue adjustment at modification.
explanation: Because added work is not distinct, update the existing combined obligation. Revised cumulative revenue = (10,800,000 + 2,400,000) × 50% = 6,600,000.00. Less previously recognised 4,320,000.00 gives an adjustment of 2,280,000.00.

title: Advance financing and revenue • case 8
prompt: A customer prepays LKR 1,200,000 exactly two years before goods transfer. The arrangement contains a significant financing component benefiting the supplier; the appropriate annual rate is 8%. No exemption applies. No other consideration or obligations exist. What revenue is recognised when control of the goods transfers?
explanation: Accrete the contract liability for two years: 1,200,000 × 1.08² = 1,399,680.00. The financing cost is recognised separately over the two years; the increased liability is released as revenue on transfer.

title: Upfront fee over the service term • case 8
prompt: A two-year service contract has a non-refundable joining fee of LKR 168,000 plus fixed monthly fees of 10,000 for 24 months. The joining activity transfers no separate service, all consideration relates to one evenly provided service obligation, and no renewal material right exists. Find revenue for the first six months of service.
explanation: Total transaction price = 168,000 + 24 × 10,000 = 408,000. The upfront activity is not a separate obligation. Recognise 6/24 of the total = 102,000.00.
family: Upfront fee over the service term

title: Credit-impaired net interest basis • case 8
prompt: A loan originated unimpaired subsequently became credit-impaired in the prior reporting period and remains so throughout the current year. Opening gross amortised cost is LKR 1,900,000; loss allowance is 380,000. Original effective rate is 9%. No cash flows or other opening adjustments occur. Find current-year interest revenue.
explanation: For this subsequently credit-impaired asset, apply the original EIR to amortised cost NET of allowance: (1,900,000 − 380,000) × 9% = 136,800.00. This is not the purchased/originated credit-impaired model.

title: Loan modification without derecognition • case 8
prompt: A financial asset is modified WITHOUT derecognition. Immediately before modification its gross carrying amount is LKR 1,160,000. Revised contractual receipts are 490,000 in one year and 564,000 in two years. Original EIR is 10%. Ignore fees and ECL changes. Find the modification LOSS recognised now.
explanation: Recompute gross carrying amount using the ORIGINAL EIR: 490,000/1.10 + 564,000/1.10² = 911,570.25. Modification loss = old gross amount 1,160,000 − 911,570.25 = 248,429.75.

title: Debt FVOCI residual movement • case 8
prompt: A debt investment at FVOCI opens with equal fair value and gross amortised cost of LKR 1,200,000, and no accumulated OCI. Current EIR interest is 96,000.00, coupon received is 68,000, and closing fair value is 1,382,000. No impairment, foreign exchange, purchases or disposals apply. Find the fair-value gain recognised in OCI for this year.
explanation: Closing amortised-cost benchmark = 1,200,000 + 96,000.00 − 68,000 = 1,228,000.00. OCI is fair value minus that benchmark = 1,382,000 − 1,228,000.00 = 154,000.00. EIR interest is profit or loss.

title: Debt extinguishment after settlement fees • case 8
prompt: A financial liability with carrying amount LKR 1,440,000 is fully extinguished by a cash settlement of 1,210,000 plus a fee of 24,000 paid to the lender as part of the settlement consideration. No replacement debt, other costs or equity component exists. Find the extinguishment GAIN.
explanation: Total consideration paid = 1,210,000 + lender settlement fee 24,000.00 = 1,234,000.00. Gain = liability carrying amount − total settlement consideration = 206,000.00.

title: Own-credit split on an FVTPL liability • case 8
prompt: A liability is designated at FVTPL under the eligible fair-value option. Its fair value increases by LKR 140,000, producing a total loss. Of this, 28,000 is attributable to improved own credit and qualifies for OCI presentation. The split does not create or enlarge an accounting mismatch. Find the loss recognised in PROFIT OR LOSS.
explanation: The eligible own-credit component of 28,000 goes to OCI. The remaining fair-value loss goes to profit or loss: 140,000 − 28,000 = 112,000.00. This presentation is for designated liabilities under the stated conditions.
family: Own-credit split on an FVTPL liability

title: Midyear acquisition and parent earnings • case 8
prompt: P acquires 80% of S on 1 October and reports to 31 December. P’s own annual profit is LKR 2,400,000, excluding any S dividend. S’s annual profit of 1,680,000 accrues evenly. Additional depreciation on acquisition-date fair-value adjustments for the POST-acquisition quarter is 48,000. No tax, intragroup trading, goodwill impairment or other adjustment exists. Find consolidated profit attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Only post-acquisition profit enters: S’s quarter = 420,000.00; less FV depreciation 48,000 gives 372,000.00. Owners’ profit = 2,400,000 + 80% of adjusted quarter profit = 2,697,600.00.

title: Intragroup PPE transfer at year end • case 8
prompt: On 1 January P sells equipment to S for LKR 1,044,000; carrying amount in P was 696,000. Remaining useful life is three years with no residual value. S depreciates the transfer price straight-line for the full year. No tax or impairment applies. By how much must S’s closing PPE amount be REDUCED on consolidation to restore the group basis?
explanation: Eliminate transfer gain of 348,000, but reverse excess depreciation of 348,000/3 = 116,000.00. Net reduction in closing group PPE = 232,000.00. The intragroup sale does not create a group gain.
family: Intragroup PPE transfer at year end

title: Loss of control and retained interest • case 8
prompt: P loses control of S. Sale proceeds are LKR 2,400,000; fair value of the retained interest is 680,000; carrying NCI derecognised is 440,000. S’s consolidated net assets INCLUDING goodwill carry at 2,740,000. No accumulated OCI, transaction costs or other adjustment exists. Calculate the gain on loss of control.
explanation: Gain = proceeds + fair value retained + carrying NCI − subsidiary net assets including goodwill = 2,400,000 + 680,000 + 440,000 − 2,740,000 = 780,000.00.
family: Loss of control and retained interest

title: Buy more without losing control • case 8
prompt: P increases ownership of S from 80% to 90% and retains control. Carrying amount of the entire 20% NCI before purchase is LKR 480,000. P pays 380,000 for the additional 10% interest. No OCI or other changes exist. What amount is DEBITED to parent owners’ equity for the difference between consideration and NCI carrying amount acquired?
explanation: The purchased 10 percentage points are half of the previous 20% NCI. Derecognise NCI of 240,000.00. Debit parent equity for excess consideration: 380,000 − 240,000.00 = 140,000.00. There is no new goodwill or profit-or-loss charge.

title: Acquisition consideration at present value • case 8
prompt: An acquirer pays cash LKR 2,400,000 now, owes fixed consideration of 1,188,000 in one year, and has acquisition-date fair value of contingent consideration of 240,000. Discount fixed deferred consideration at 10%. NCI fair value is 500,000; identifiable net assets are 3,160,000. No previous holding or other adjustment applies. Find goodwill.
explanation: Deferred consideration PV = 1,188,000/1.10 = 1,080,000.00. Goodwill = upfront + discounted fixed consideration + contingent FV + NCI − identifiable net assets = 1,060,000.00. Later financing unwinding is separate.

title: Acquisition uplift and deferred tax • case 8
prompt: Consideration is LKR 3,400,000; NCI is measured at fair value of 600,000. Identifiable net assets before an equipment uplift are 2,960,000. Acquisition-date equipment uplift is 480,000, with no tax-base uplift. Tax rate on reversal is 30%; no DTL exception applies. No other adjustment exists. Find goodwill after recognising the uplift and related DTL.
explanation: DTL on uplift = 480,000 × 30% = 144,000.00. Net identifiable assets = 2,960,000 + 480,000 − DTL = 3,296,000.00. Goodwill = consideration + NCI − net identifiable assets = 704,000.00.

title: Measurement-period goodwill adjustment • case 8
prompt: Provisional goodwill was LKR 1,160,000. During the measurement period, new information about acquisition-date facts establishes an additional identifiable equipment fair-value uplift of 240,000. The tax base is unchanged and a 30% DTL must be recognised. NCI was measured at fair value and that value is unchanged. All other acquisition amounts are final. Find revised acquisition-date goodwill.
explanation: Additional net identifiable assets = uplift − 30% DTL = 168,000.00. Retrospectively reduce goodwill by that net amount: 1,160,000 − 168,000.00 = 992,000.00. Subsequent equipment depreciation is considered separately.

title: Advance rent and initial ROU cost • case 8
prompt: A three-year lease has three equal annual payments of LKR 190,000 each: one at commencement, one in a year and one in two years. Discount rate is 10%. Initial direct costs are 20,000 and incentives received at commencement are 5,000. No restoration obligation exists. Find initial ROU asset cost.
explanation: Initial liability excludes the payment already made: 190,000/1.10 + 190,000/1.10² = 329,752.07. ROU = liability + commencement payment + direct costs − incentive = 534,752.07.
family: Advance rent and initial ROU cost

title: Index-linked payment remeasurement • case 8
prompt: A CPI change triggers a lessee remeasurement. Immediately before it, lease liability is LKR 208,000. The revised remaining payments are 130,680 in one year and the same amount in two years. The original 10% discount rate remains appropriate; no floating-interest-rate change or modification applies. Find the INCREASE in liability, normally adjusting the ROU asset.
explanation: Revised liability = 130,680/1.10 + 130,680/1.10² = 226,800.00. For this index change retain the original discount rate. Increase = revised liability − 208,000 = 18,800.00.

title: Partial termination and remaining ROU • case 8
prompt: A lease modification reduces scope by 40%, with a proportionate reduction in the ROU asset and liability. Immediately before modification, ROU carrying amount is LKR 1,060,000 and liability 1,160,000. After accounting for termination, remeasuring the remaining payments at the revised appropriate rate gives a liability of 740,000. No impairment applies. Find the FINAL ROU carrying amount after both steps.
explanation: First retain 60% of the ROU (636,000.00) and liability (696,000.00), recognising the termination difference in profit or loss. Then adjust ROU by revised liability minus remaining liability: 44,000.00. Final ROU = 680,000.00.

title: Finance lessor effective interest • case 8
prompt: A finance lessor’s net investment comprises four year-end rentals of LKR 380,000 and an unguaranteed residual of 140,000 recovered at the end of year four. The interest rate implicit in the lease is 8%. No initial direct costs outside those reflected in this rate, credit losses or other adjustments exist. Find finance income for the first year, BEFORE the first rental is received.
explanation: Initial net investment = PV of the four rentals plus PV of residual = 1,361,512.38. First-year finance income = opening net investment × 8% = 108,920.99, giving a constant periodic return.

title: Warranty deductible temporary difference • case 8
prompt: A recognised warranty provision carries at LKR 420,000. The entire amount will be deductible only when paid, so its tax base is zero. Sufficient future taxable profit is probable and no recognition exception applies. The enacted rate on reversal is 30%. Find the deferred tax asset.
explanation: Liability tax base = carrying amount − future deduction = zero. Deductible temporary difference = 420,000; DTA = 420,000 × 30% = 126,000.00. Tax expense recognition and cash deduction occur in different periods.

title: Deferred tax expense bridge • case 8
prompt: Opening DTL is LKR 100,000 and closing DTL is 166,000. Opening DTA is 80,000 and closing DTA is 68,000. All changes belong in profit or loss, with no acquisitions, OCI, equity or foreign-exchange effects. Find deferred tax EXPENSE for the year.
explanation: Expense = increase in DTL + decrease in DTA = (166,000 − 100,000) + (80,000 − 68,000) = 78,000.00. Do not confuse the closing net balance with the period expense.

title: Tax loss recognition ceiling • case 8
prompt: Unused tax losses are LKR 960,000. Convincing evidence supports probable FUTURE taxable profit of only 580,000 before those losses expire. There are no other recovery sources or taxable temporary differences. Tax rate is 30%. Find the DTA that can be recognised on the losses.
explanation: Recognise only the losses supported by probable taxable profit: min(960,000, 580,000) × 30% = 174,000.00. The legal loss balance alone does not justify a larger asset.

title: Discounted VIU versus disposal value • case 8
prompt: An asset carries at LKR 1,360,000. Its appropriate value-in-use forecast is 380,000 received at each of the next three year ends, plus net disposal proceeds of 200,000 at year three. Appropriate discount rate is 10%. Fair value less costs of disposal is 850,000. No other cash flows or valuation adjustments apply. Find the impairment loss.
explanation: VIU = PV of three operating receipts plus PV of terminal disposal = 1,095,266.72. Recoverable amount is the HIGHER of VIU and 850,000: 1,095,266.72. Impairment = 1,360,000 − 1,095,266.72 = 264,733.28.

title: CGU residual pro-rata allocation • case 8
prompt: A CGU contains goodwill of LKR 150,000, asset A of 680,000, and asset B of 440,000. Recoverable amount is 840,000. No individual-asset floor restricts allocation and there are no other assets. Find asset B’s carrying amount AFTER allocating the CGU impairment.
explanation: Total impairment = 1,270,000 − 840,000 = 430,000. First eliminate goodwill of 150,000. Allocate remaining 280,000 pro rata to A and B. B loss = 110,000.00; closing B = 330,000.00.

title: CGU reversal without restoring goodwill • case 8
prompt: After past impairment, a CGU has assets A at LKR 600,000 and B at 400,000. All previously impaired goodwill is zero. Recoverable amount now rises to 1,240,000. A’s maximum permitted amount under its no-impairment ceiling is 658,000, and B’s is 516,000; no lower individual recoverable-amount limit applies. What is the maximum total CGU carrying amount after reversal?
explanation: Goodwill impairment is never reversed. The other assets cannot exceed their permitted ceilings: 658,000 + 516,000 = 1,174,000.00, below CGU recoverable amount 1,240,000. Allocate reversals subject to those ceilings.

explanation: Recompute gross carrying amount using the ORIGINAL EIR: 495,000/1.10 + 572,000/1.10² = 922,727.27. Modification loss = old gross amount 1,180,000 − 922,727.27 = 257,272.73.

title: Debt FVOCI residual movement • case 9
prompt: A debt investment at FVOCI opens with equal fair value and gross amortised cost of LKR 1,225,000, and no accumulated OCI. Current EIR interest is 98,000.00, coupon received is 69,000, and closing fair value is 1,411,000. No impairment, foreign exchange, purchases or disposals apply. Find the fair-value gain recognised in OCI for this year.
explanation: Closing amortised-cost benchmark = 1,225,000 + 98,000.00 − 69,000 = 1,254,000.00. OCI is fair value minus that benchmark = 1,411,000 − 1,254,000.00 = 157,000.00. EIR interest is profit or loss.

title: Debt extinguishment after settlement fees • case 9
prompt: A financial liability with carrying amount LKR 1,470,000 is fully extinguished by a cash settlement of 1,230,000 plus a fee of 24,500 paid to the lender as part of the settlement consideration. No replacement debt, other costs or equity component exists. Find the extinguishment GAIN.
explanation: Total consideration paid = 1,230,000 + lender settlement fee 24,500.00 = 1,254,500.00. Gain = liability carrying amount − total settlement consideration = 215,500.00.

title: Own-credit split on an FVTPL liability • case 9
prompt: A liability is designated at FVTPL under the eligible fair-value option. Its fair value increases by LKR 145,000, producing a total loss. Of this, 29,000 is attributable to improved own credit and qualifies for OCI presentation. The split does not create or enlarge an accounting mismatch. Find the loss recognised in PROFIT OR LOSS.
explanation: The eligible own-credit component of 29,000 goes to OCI. The remaining fair-value loss goes to profit or loss: 145,000 − 29,000 = 116,000.00. This presentation is for designated liabilities under the stated conditions.
family: Own-credit split on an FVTPL liability

title: Midyear acquisition and parent earnings • case 9
prompt: P acquires 80% of S on 1 October and reports to 31 December. P’s own annual profit is LKR 2,450,000, excluding any S dividend. S’s annual profit of 1,740,000 accrues evenly. Additional depreciation on acquisition-date fair-value adjustments for the POST-acquisition quarter is 49,000. No tax, intragroup trading, goodwill impairment or other adjustment exists. Find consolidated profit attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Only post-acquisition profit enters: S’s quarter = 435,000.00; less FV depreciation 49,000 gives 386,000.00. Owners’ profit = 2,450,000 + 80% of adjusted quarter profit = 2,758,800.00.

title: Intragroup PPE transfer at year end • case 9
prompt: On 1 January P sells equipment to S for LKR 1,062,000; carrying amount in P was 708,000. Remaining useful life is three years with no residual value. S depreciates the transfer price straight-line for the full year. No tax or impairment applies. By how much must S’s closing PPE amount be REDUCED on consolidation to restore the group basis?
explanation: Eliminate transfer gain of 354,000, but reverse excess depreciation of 354,000/3 = 118,000.00. Net reduction in closing group PPE = 236,000.00. The intragroup sale does not create a group gain.
family: Intragroup PPE transfer at year end

title: Loss of control and retained interest • case 9
prompt: P loses control of S. Sale proceeds are LKR 2,450,000; fair value of the retained interest is 690,000; carrying NCI derecognised is 445,000. S’s consolidated net assets INCLUDING goodwill carry at 2,770,000. No accumulated OCI, transaction costs or other adjustment exists. Calculate the gain on loss of control.
explanation: Gain = proceeds + fair value retained + carrying NCI − subsidiary net assets including goodwill = 2,450,000 + 690,000 + 445,000 − 2,770,000 = 815,000.00.
family: Loss of control and retained interest

title: Buy more without losing control • case 9
prompt: P increases ownership of S from 80% to 90% and retains control. Carrying amount of the entire 20% NCI before purchase is LKR 490,000. P pays 390,000 for the additional 10% interest. No OCI or other changes exist. What amount is DEBITED to parent owners’ equity for the difference between consideration and NCI carrying amount acquired?
explanation: The purchased 10 percentage points are half of the previous 20% NCI. Derecognise NCI of 245,000.00. Debit parent equity for excess consideration: 390,000 − 245,000.00 = 145,000.00. There is no new goodwill or profit-or-loss charge.

title: Acquisition consideration at present value • case 9
prompt: An acquirer pays cash LKR 2,450,000 now, owes fixed consideration of 1,199,000 in one year, and has acquisition-date fair value of contingent consideration of 245,000. Discount fixed deferred consideration at 10%. NCI fair value is 500,000; identifiable net assets are 3,180,000. No previous holding or other adjustment applies. Find goodwill.
explanation: Deferred consideration PV = 1,199,000/1.10 = 1,090,000.00. Goodwill = upfront + discounted fixed consideration + contingent FV + NCI − identifiable net assets = 1,105,000.00. Later financing unwinding is separate.

title: Acquisition uplift and deferred tax • case 9
prompt: Consideration is LKR 3,450,000; NCI is measured at fair value of 600,000. Identifiable net assets before an equipment uplift are 2,980,000. Acquisition-date equipment uplift is 490,000, with no tax-base uplift. Tax rate on reversal is 30%; no DTL exception applies. No other adjustment exists. Find goodwill after recognising the uplift and related DTL.
explanation: DTL on uplift = 490,000 × 30% = 147,000.00. Net identifiable assets = 2,980,000 + 490,000 − DTL = 3,323,000.00. Goodwill = consideration + NCI − net identifiable assets = 727,000.00.

title: Measurement-period goodwill adjustment • case 9
prompt: Provisional goodwill was LKR 1,180,000. During the measurement period, new information about acquisition-date facts establishes an additional identifiable equipment fair-value uplift of 245,000. The tax base is unchanged and a 30% DTL must be recognised. NCI was measured at fair value and that value is unchanged. All other acquisition amounts are final. Find revised acquisition-date goodwill.
explanation: Additional net identifiable assets = uplift − 30% DTL = 171,500.00. Retrospectively reduce goodwill by that net amount: 1,180,000 − 171,500.00 = 1,008,500.00. Subsequent equipment depreciation is considered separately.

title: Advance rent and initial ROU cost • case 9
prompt: A three-year lease has three equal annual payments of LKR 195,000 each: one at commencement, one in a year and one in two years. Discount rate is 10%. Initial direct costs are 20,000 and incentives received at commencement are 5,000. No restoration obligation exists. Find initial ROU asset cost.
explanation: Initial liability excludes the payment already made: 195,000/1.10 + 195,000/1.10² = 338,429.75. ROU = liability + commencement payment + direct costs − incentive = 548,429.75.
family: Advance rent and initial ROU cost

title: Index-linked payment remeasurement • case 9
prompt: A CPI change triggers a lessee remeasurement. Immediately before it, lease liability is LKR 209,000. The revised remaining payments are 131,890 in one year and the same amount in two years. The original 10% discount rate remains appropriate; no floating-interest-rate change or modification applies. Find the INCREASE in liability, normally adjusting the ROU asset.
explanation: Revised liability = 131,890/1.10 + 131,890/1.10² = 228,900.00. For this index change retain the original discount rate. Increase = revised liability − 209,000 = 19,900.00.

title: Partial termination and remaining ROU • case 9
prompt: A lease modification reduces scope by 40%, with a proportionate reduction in the ROU asset and liability. Immediately before modification, ROU carrying amount is LKR 1,080,000 and liability 1,180,000. After accounting for termination, remeasuring the remaining payments at the revised appropriate rate gives a liability of 755,000. No impairment applies. Find the FINAL ROU carrying amount after both steps.
explanation: First retain 60% of the ROU (648,000.00) and liability (708,000.00), recognising the termination difference in profit or loss. Then adjust ROU by revised liability minus remaining liability: 47,000.00. Final ROU = 695,000.00.

title: Finance lessor effective interest • case 9
prompt: A finance lessor’s net investment comprises four year-end rentals of LKR 390,000 and an unguaranteed residual of 145,000 recovered at the end of year four. The interest rate implicit in the lease is 8%. No initial direct costs outside those reflected in this rate, credit losses or other adjustments exist. Find finance income for the first year, BEFORE the first rental is received.
explanation: Initial net investment = PV of the four rentals plus PV of residual = 1,398,308.80. First-year finance income = opening net investment × 8% = 111,864.70, giving a constant periodic return.

title: Warranty deductible temporary difference • case 9
prompt: A recognised warranty provision carries at LKR 435,000. The entire amount will be deductible only when paid, so its tax base is zero. Sufficient future taxable profit is probable and no recognition exception applies. The enacted rate on reversal is 30%. Find the deferred tax asset.
explanation: Liability tax base = carrying amount − future deduction = zero. Deductible temporary difference = 435,000; DTA = 435,000 × 30% = 130,500.00. Tax expense recognition and cash deduction occur in different periods.

title: Deferred tax expense bridge • case 9
prompt: Opening DTL is LKR 100,000 and closing DTL is 168,000. Opening DTA is 80,000 and closing DTA is 69,000. All changes belong in profit or loss, with no acquisitions, OCI, equity or foreign-exchange effects. Find deferred tax EXPENSE for the year.
explanation: Expense = increase in DTL + decrease in DTA = (168,000 − 100,000) + (80,000 − 69,000) = 79,000.00. Do not confuse the closing net balance with the period expense.

title: Tax loss recognition ceiling • case 9
prompt: Unused tax losses are LKR 980,000. Convincing evidence supports probable FUTURE taxable profit of only 590,000 before those losses expire. There are no other recovery sources or taxable temporary differences. Tax rate is 30%. Find the DTA that can be recognised on the losses.
explanation: Recognise only the losses supported by probable taxable profit: min(980,000, 590,000) × 30% = 177,000.00. The legal loss balance alone does not justify a larger asset.

title: Discounted VIU versus disposal value • case 9
prompt: An asset carries at LKR 1,380,000. Its appropriate value-in-use forecast is 390,000 received at each of the next three year ends, plus net disposal proceeds of 200,000 at year three. Appropriate discount rate is 10%. Fair value less costs of disposal is 850,000. No other cash flows or valuation adjustments apply. Find the impairment loss.
explanation: VIU = PV of three operating receipts plus PV of terminal disposal = 1,120,135.24. Recoverable amount is the HIGHER of VIU and 850,000: 1,120,135.24. Impairment = 1,380,000 − 1,120,135.24 = 259,864.76.

title: CGU residual pro-rata allocation • case 9
prompt: A CGU contains goodwill of LKR 150,000, asset A of 690,000, and asset B of 445,000. Recoverable amount is 845,000. No individual-asset floor restricts allocation and there are no other assets. Find asset B’s carrying amount AFTER allocating the CGU impairment.
explanation: Total impairment = 1,285,000 − 845,000 = 440,000. First eliminate goodwill of 150,000. Allocate remaining 290,000 pro rata to A and B. B loss = 113,700.44; closing B = 331,299.56.

title: CGU reversal without restoring goodwill • case 9
prompt: After past impairment, a CGU has assets A at LKR 600,000 and B at 400,000. All previously impaired goodwill is zero. Recoverable amount now rises to 1,245,000. A’s maximum permitted amount under its no-impairment ceiling is 659,000, and B’s is 518,000; no lower individual recoverable-amount limit applies. What is the maximum total CGU carrying amount after reversal?
explanation: Goodwill impairment is never reversed. The other assets cannot exceed their permitted ceilings: 659,000 + 518,000 = 1,177,000.00, below CGU recoverable amount 1,245,000. Allocate reversals subject to those ceilings.

title: Onerous contract least net exit cost • case 9
prompt: A contract has a present onerous obligation. Directly related costs to fulfil are LKR 1,680,000, while expected contract benefits are 1,045,000. The alternative is to terminate now for a penalty of 390,000. No dedicated asset impairment is required and discounting is immaterial. Find the provision for the least net unavoidable cost.
explanation: Net cost of fulfilling = 1,680,000 − 1,045,000 = 635,000. Compare with termination penalty 390,000; the least net cost of exit is 390,000.00. Do not provide for gross fulfilment costs without expected benefits.
family: Onerous contract least net exit cost

title: Restructuring cost boundary • case 9
prompt: A qualifying restructuring has created the required present obligations. Direct supplier-contract cancellation penalties are LKR 245,000; legally required closure clean-up costs are 118,000. Planned staff retraining is 150,000, marketing is 80,000, and investment in new systems is 50,000 for continuing operations. No leases, employee termination benefits, other assets or discounting complications apply. What amount is included in the restructuring provision?
explanation: Include direct expenditures necessarily entailed by the restructuring and unrelated to ongoing activities: 245,000 + 118,000 = 363,000.00. Retraining, marketing and new-system investment for continuing business are excluded.

title: Inspection replacement and depreciation • case 9
prompt: On 1 January an asset’s carrying amount is LKR 1,080,000, including an old inspection component of 100,000. A new qualifying major inspection costs 234,000 that day and the old component is derecognised. The remaining main asset has four years’ life; the new inspection has three. Both use straight-line depreciation with zero residual value. Find total carrying amount at year end.

title: Commercial exchange gain • case 9
prompt: An equipment exchange has commercial substance. The entity gives equipment with carrying amount LKR 890,000 and reliably measurable fair value 1,180,000, plus 200,000 cash. Fair value of the received equipment is not more clearly evident. No other costs or taxes apply. What GAIN is recognised on derecognising the equipment given?
explanation: Cost of received equipment = fair value given + cash = 1,380,000. The gain on the equipment surrendered is only its fair value minus carrying amount: 1,180,000 − 890,000 = 290,000.00. The cash paid is not a gain.

title: Periodic weighted average with discount • case 9
prompt: Opening inventory is 1,000 units at LKR 100 each. A purchase of 680 units is invoiced at 120 each with a 10% trade discount; inward freight is 2,000. Closing quantity is 590 units. Use periodic weighted average. NRV exceeds cost; there are no other movements or costs. Find closing inventory carrying amount.
explanation: Net purchase price per unit = 120 × 90% = 108. Total available cost = 100,000 + 680 × 108 + 2,000 = 175,440. Average = cost / 1,680 units. Closing value = average × 590 = 61,612.86.

title: Net acquisition cash flow • case 9
prompt: A subsidiary acquisition involves cash consideration PAID this year of LKR 1,450,000, plus deferred consideration of 200,000 not yet paid. Cash and cash equivalents acquired with the subsidiary are 145,000; acquired borrowings are 300,000. No fees or other cash payments occur. Find the net INVESTING cash outflow from obtaining control.
explanation: Cash flow from obtaining control is investing, reported net of cash and cash equivalents acquired: 1,450,000 − 145,000 = 1,305,000.00 outflow. Unpaid deferred consideration and assumed debt are not cash payments in this case.

title: Research expense and midyear amortisation • case 9
prompt: In the current year a project incurs research costs LKR 89,000, development spending of 50,000 before recognition criteria are met, then qualifying development cost of 780,000. The completed asset becomes available for use on 1 July, has a five-year finite life and zero residual value. Use six months of straight-line amortisation. Find TOTAL current-year expense from these items; no impairment applies.
explanation: Expense research and pre-recognition development: 89,000 + 50,000. Capitalise 780,000, then amortise for six months: 780,000/5 × 6/12 = 78,000.00. Total expense = 217,000.00.

title: Associate upstream adjusted earnings • case 9
prompt: An investor owns 30% of an associate. Associate profit is LKR 680,000. The investor’s equity-method adjustments include extra depreciation of 118,000 on acquisition-date fair values, and an upstream inventory sale leaves unrealised profit of 69,000 in the investor’s inventory. No tax, basis differences beyond those stated, impairment or other adjustments apply. Find the equity-accounted share of profit after both adjustments.
explanation: Adjust associate result before taking the share: 680,000 − 118,000 − 69,000 = 493,000. Investor’s share = 30% × adjusted result = 147,900.00. The investor’s share of upstream unrealised profit is eliminated.

title: Returns-adjusted sales revenue • case 10
prompt: A retailer transfers 1,200 products at LKR 1,500 each and receives payment in full. Its supported estimate is that 5.0% will be returned for a full refund. The variable-consideration constraint permits this estimate; no other obligations or taxes apply. What sales revenue is recognised at transfer, excluding the separately accounted return asset?
explanation: Exclude consideration expected to be refunded: 1,800,000.00 × (1 − 5.0%) = 1,710,000.00 revenue. The expected refund is a separate liability; the recovery asset affects cost of sales separately.

title: Loyalty material-right allocation • case 10
prompt: Cash consideration of LKR 1,250,000 covers delivered goods and loyalty points that are a separate material right. Stand-alone selling price of the goods is 1,000,000; the points’ estimated stand-alone price is 150,000, ALREADY adjusted for redemption probability. No points are redeemed yet. What contract liability is allocated to the points?
explanation: Allocate by relative stand-alone prices: 1,250,000 × 150,000 / 1,150,000 = 163,043.48. Do not apply redemption probability again; it is already included in the points’ stand-alone price.

title: Contract-cost asset impairment • case 10
prompt: A qualifying sales commission asset initially cost LKR 240,000 and is amortised evenly over three years. After one year of amortisation, expected remaining consideration for the related services is 1,000,000; directly related future fulfilment costs not yet expensed are 960,000. Other assets have already been tested and no further adjustment is required. Find the impairment loss on this contract-cost asset.
explanation: Post-amortisation carrying amount = 160,000.00. Recoverable benchmark = remaining consideration − related future costs = 40,000. Impairment = 160,000.00 − 40,000 = 120,000.00.

title: Non-distinct contract modification • case 10
prompt: A single over-time construction obligation had original price LKR 11,000,000. Revenue of 4,400,000.00 was recognised before modification. Approved added work is NOT distinct and adds 2,500,000 to the price. Under the appropriate input method the modified combined obligation is now 50% complete. No variable-price constraint or other issue applies. Find the cumulative catch-up revenue adjustment at modification.
explanation: Because added work is not distinct, update the existing combined obligation. Revised cumulative revenue = (11,000,000 + 2,500,000) × 50% = 6,750,000.00. Less previously recognised 4,400,000.00 gives an adjustment of 2,350,000.00.

title: Advance financing and revenue • case 10
prompt: A customer prepays LKR 1,250,000 exactly two years before goods transfer. The arrangement contains a significant financing component benefiting the supplier; the appropriate annual rate is 8%. No exemption applies. No other consideration or obligations exist. What revenue is recognised when control of the goods transfers?
explanation: Accrete the contract liability for two years: 1,250,000 × 1.08² = 1,458,000.00. The financing cost is recognised separately over the two years; the increased liability is released as revenue on transfer.

title: Upfront fee over the service term • case 10
prompt: A two-year service contract has a non-refundable joining fee of LKR 180,000 plus fixed monthly fees of 10,000 for 24 months. The joining activity transfers no separate service, all consideration relates to one evenly provided service obligation, and no renewal material right exists. Find revenue for the first six months of service.
explanation: Total transaction price = 180,000 + 24 × 10,000 = 420,000. The upfront activity is not a separate obligation. Recognise 6/24 of the total = 105,000.00.
family: Upfront fee over the service term

title: Credit-impaired net interest basis • case 10
prompt: A loan originated unimpaired subsequently became credit-impaired in the prior reporting period and remains so throughout the current year. Opening gross amortised cost is LKR 2,000,000; loss allowance is 400,000. Original effective rate is 9%. No cash flows or other opening adjustments occur. Find current-year interest revenue.
explanation: For this subsequently credit-impaired asset, apply the original EIR to amortised cost NET of allowance: (2,000,000 − 400,000) × 9% = 144,000.00. This is not the purchased/originated credit-impaired model.

title: Debt FVOCI residual movement • case 10

explanation: Total consideration paid = 1,250,000 + lender settlement fee 25,000.00 = 1,275,000.00. Gain = liability carrying amount − total settlement consideration = 225,000.00.
