explanation: Recognise allocation to A plus half of support: 1,590,000 × (600,000 + 150,000) / 1,200,000 = 993,750.00. B’s allocation remains unrecognised as revenue.

title: Progress excluding abnormal waste • case 13
prompt: An over-time contract has transaction price LKR 11,300,000. Costs incurred are 4,520,000, including abnormal waste of 226,000 that does not depict progress. Expected TOTAL productive costs excluding that waste are 9,040,000. Cost-to-cost is appropriate after excluding the waste; no other adjustment applies. Find cumulative revenue, not profit.
explanation: Exclude abnormal waste from the progress numerator. Productive progress = (4,520,000 − 226,000) / 9,040,000. Revenue = transaction price × that progress = 5,367,500.00. The wasted cost is not a revenue-producing input.

title: Uninstalled materials without margin • case 13
prompt: A single over-time construction obligation has price LKR 12,600,000. All B19(b) conditions justify recognising revenue equal to cost for significant uninstalled materials of 2,520,000 already controlled by the customer. Other productive costs incurred are 1,890,000; expected total OTHER costs are 7,560,000. No revenue was previously recognised. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise material revenue without margin: 2,520,000. Recognise the remaining price using other-cost progress: (12,600,000 − 2,520,000) × 1,890,000/7,560,000. Total revenue = 5,040,000.00.

title: Agent commission after collection • case 13
prompt: An intermediary is an AGENT and collects customer cash of LKR 1,650,000 for a completed supplier service. It must remit 88% to the supplier and is entitled to the remaining 12% commission. It controls neither the underlying service nor any distinct extra service, and there is no tax. Find its revenue.
explanation: An agent recognises its fee or commission, not the supplier’s gross billings: 1,650,000 × 12% = 198,000.00. The amount due to the supplier is separately accounted for.

title: Distinct remaining goods blended prospectively • case 13
prompt: At modification, 100 distinct goods remain under an existing contract at LKR 1,130 each. Another 50 distinct goods are added at 904 each. The modification is NOT a separate contract, but remaining goods are distinct from those already transferred, so paragraph 21(a) applies prospectively. Thirty of the remaining goods are then transferred. Find revenue for those thirty.
explanation: Prospective remaining consideration = 100 × 1,130 + 50 × 904. Divide by 150 remaining goods, then multiply by 30 = 31,640.00. Do not retrospectively revise revenue on goods already transferred.

title: FVTPL acquisition expense • case 13
prompt: A financial asset is acquired at fair value LKR 1,060,000 and is classified at FVTPL. Directly attributable broker costs are 26,500, paid separately. No fair-value change occurs immediately after purchase. Find the immediate profit-or-loss expense from acquiring this asset.
explanation: Transaction costs on an FVTPL asset are expensed. Initial asset carrying amount is fair value 1,060,000; immediate acquisition expense is 26,500.00.

title: Collateral cash-shortfall discounting • case 13
prompt: A credit loss scenario has a contractual receipt of LKR 1,325,000 due in one year. The ONLY expected recovery at that same date is collateral sale proceeds of 895,000, less sale costs of 63,000. Scenario probability is 100% and original EIR is 10%. Collateral is an integral contractual credit enhancement and not separately recognised. Find discounted ECL.
explanation: One-year shortfall = contractual receipt − net collateral recovery = 1,325,000 − (895,000 − 63,000). Discount that shortfall at 10%: 448,181.82. Do not ignore recovery costs or discount only one side of same-date cash flows.

title: Three-band provision matrix • case 13
prompt: Under the simplified lifetime-ECL approach, supported adjusted loss rates are 1% on current receivables of LKR 1,260,000, 5% on past-due balances of 365,000, and 30% on severely overdue balances of 126,000. Rates already include all required forward-looking and discounting effects. Find total loss allowance.
explanation: Apply each appropriate band rate and add: 1,260,000×1% + 365,000×5% + 126,000×30% = 68,650.00. Do not apply one blended band mechanically to all balances.

title: Equity FVOCI profit-or-loss dividend • case 13
prompt: An eligible equity investment has the irrevocable FVOCI election. During the year it gains LKR 146,000 in fair value and earns a dividend of 73,000. Dividend recognition criteria are met and the dividend clearly represents a return on investment, not recovery of cost. There are no other effects. Find income recognised in PROFIT OR LOSS.
explanation: The qualifying dividend of 73,000.00 is profit-or-loss income. The fair-value movement of 146,000 is OCI under this election and is not added to the profit-or-loss amount.

title: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset • case 13
prompt: A loan is sold with full derecognition. Immediately before sale, gross carrying amount is LKR 1,260,000, loss allowance 126,000, and cash proceeds 1,197,000. No accumulated OCI, sale fees or other adjustments exist. Find the derecognition GAIN relative to net carrying amount.
explanation: Net carrying amount = 1,260,000 − 126,000 = 1,134,000. Compare proceeds with that net amount: 1,197,000 − 1,134,000 = 63,000.00 gain. Derecognise both the gross asset and related allowance.
family: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset

title: Non-substantial liability modification gain • case 13
prompt: An amortised-cost liability is modified WITHOUT extinguishment, with no fees. Its carrying amount is LKR 1,130,000. The sole revised payment is 1,299,500 in two years. Original EIR is 10%; the modification is assessed as non-substantial. Find the immediate modification GAIN from recalculating amortised cost at the original EIR.
explanation: Revised amortised cost = 1,299,500/1.10² = 1,073,966.94. Gain = old liability 1,130,000 − revised PV = 56,033.06. The original EIR is retained for this non-extinguishing modification.

title: Credit-risk improvement allowance release • case 13
prompt: A debt asset under the GENERAL ECL model previously had significant credit-risk deterioration and lifetime allowance LKR 126,000. At reporting date the criteria for lifetime ECL are no longer met; required 12-month ECL is 16,500. No write-offs, new assets or other allowance movements occur. Find the impairment reversal in profit or loss.
explanation: When lifetime measurement is no longer required, the general model returns to 12-month ECL. Release the excess allowance: 126,000 − 16,500 = 109,500.00. This is not a receivable under mandatory simplified lifetime ECL.

title: Upstream inventory elimination with tax • case 13
prompt: P and S report profits AFTER their own tax of LKR 2,520,000 and 1,060,000. An upstream inventory sale leaves unrealised profit of 252,000 in group closing inventory. A recoverable DTA is recognised on the full elimination at 30%, with the tax effect in profit or loss. No other consolidation adjustments exist. Find TOTAL consolidated profit, before attribution to owners and NCI.
explanation: Combine separate after-tax profits, eliminate unrealised profit and recognise the recoverable tax benefit: 2,520,000 + 1,060,000 − 252,000 + 75,600.00 = 3,403,600.00. This question asks total group profit, not its attribution.

title: Full-goodwill impairment and owner profit • case 13
prompt: P owns 80% of S all year. Separate after-tax profits are P LKR 2,190,000 and S 830,000. Goodwill is recognised on the FULL-goodwill basis and an impairment of 265,000 is attributable to S’s CGU and allocated 80:20 between owners and NCI. No other adjustments or tax effects apply. Find consolidated profit attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Owners receive 80% of S’s profit and bear 80% of the full-goodwill loss: 2,190,000 + 80% × (830,000 − 265,000) = 2,642,000.00. Do not charge the owners with 100% of this full-goodwill loss.

title: Partial goodwill CGU gross-up • case 13
prompt: P owns 80% of S. Recognised PARTIAL goodwill is LKR 1,008,000; S’s other net assets in the tested CGU carry at 5,040,000. Recoverable amount of the WHOLE CGU is 5,670,000. Gross up goodwill for unrecognised NCI goodwill when testing; the whole impairment falls within grossed-up goodwill. No tax or other adjustments apply. Find impairment actually recognised on group goodwill.
explanation: Grossed-up goodwill = 1,008,000/80% = 1,260,000.00. Whole-CGU impairment = grossed goodwill + other net assets − recoverable amount = 630,000.00. Only the parent’s 80% goodwill portion is recognised, so recorded loss = 504,000.00.
reference: LKAS 36 Appendix C paras C4–C8; SLFRS 10 para B86

title: Consolidated retained earnings bridge • case 13
prompt: P owns 75% of S. At year end P retained earnings are LKR 3,650,000, and S retained earnings 2,390,000. S retained earnings at acquisition were 1,000,000. Cumulative post-acquisition extra FV depreciation is 126,000. A downstream sale by P leaves unrealised profit of 93,000. No tax, goodwill impairment, dividends recognised by P, OCI or other adjustments apply. Find consolidated retained earnings attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Group owners’ retained earnings = parent RE + 75% of adjusted post-acquisition S reserves − the parent’s downstream unrealised profit: 4,505,000.00. Pre-acquisition reserves do not enter post-acquisition group retained earnings.

title: Loss of control and translation reserve • case 13
prompt: P loses control of a foreign subsidiary. Proceeds are LKR 2,720,000; retained interest FV 630,000; NCI carrying amount 365,000; consolidated net assets INCLUDING goodwill 2,990,000. A cumulative translation GAIN of 126,000, entirely attributable to P, must be reclassified to profit or loss on loss of control. No other effects apply. Find total disposal gain including that reclassification.
explanation: Base gain = proceeds + retained FV + NCI − net assets = 725,000.00. Add the parent’s translation gain recycled on disposal: 126,000. Total = 851,000.00.
family: Loss of control and translation reserve

title: Residual guarantee expected payment • case 13
prompt: A lessee owes three year-end rentals of LKR 265,000. It guarantees residual value up to 100,000, but the amount EXPECTED to be payable under that guarantee is 43,000 at year three. Discount rate is 10%. No other liability payments exist. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the amount expected to be payable, not automatically the maximum guarantee. Liability = PV of three rentals + 43,000/1.10³ = 691,322.31.

title: Reasonably certain purchase option PV • case 13
prompt: A lease requires three year-end rentals of LKR 215,000, plus a purchase option price of 630,000 payable at year three. Exercise is reasonably certain. Discount rate is 10%. No incentives, other payments or initial prepayments apply. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the reasonably certain purchase price in the liability: PV of rentals + purchase price discounted for three years = 1,008,001.50. Do not omit or leave the future option payment undiscounted.

title: Lease and service component allocation • case 13
prompt: A two-year contract requires bundled payments of LKR 315,000 at each year end. Relative stand-alone prices are equipment lease 200,000 and distinct maintenance 50,000 per year. The lessee does NOT elect to combine components. Lease discount rate is 10%; no other payments exist. Find initial lease liability for the LEASE component only.
explanation: Allocate 200,000/250,000 = 80% of each bundled payment to the lease: 252,000.00. Discount those two lease payments, excluding maintenance, to obtain 437,355.37.

title: Exempt short-term lease rent-free start • case 13
prompt: A twelve-month lease with no purchase option qualifies for the elected short-term exemption. The first three months are rent free, then nine monthly payments of LKR 26,500 are due. The asset is available throughout and straight-line expense is appropriate. Find lease expense for the FIRST six months, ignoring accrual settlement timing.
explanation: Total fixed payments are nine rents. Spread evenly over all twelve months: 26,500 × 9/12 × 6 = 119,250.00. Rent-free months still receive an expense allocation.

title: Sale-and-leaseback rights transferred • case 13
prompt: A transfer qualifies as a sale under SLFRS 15 at fair value LKR 12,600,000; asset carrying amount is 7,300,000. Market-rate leaseback payments have PV 5,040,000. There are no off-market adjustments or variable-payment complications. At inception, what sale gain is recognised for rights TRANSFERRED to the buyer-lessor?
explanation: Total gain = 12,600,000 − 7,300,000 = 5,300,000. Retained-use proportion = lease PV / fair value = 40%. Recognise only the transferred-rights proportion of the gain: 3,180,000.00.

title: Reassessed bargain purchase gain • case 13
prompt: After the required reassessment, final acquisition-date consideration is LKR 2,520,000, NCI fair value is 400,000 and identifiable net assets are 3,780,000. There is no prior holding or other adjustment. Find the bargain purchase gain recognised in profit or loss.
explanation: Net identifiable assets exceed consideration plus NCI: 3,780,000 − 2,520,000 − 400,000 = 860,000.00. Reassessment has been completed before recognising the gain.

title: Acquired contingent liability in goodwill • case 13
prompt: Consideration is LKR 4,150,000; NCI FV is 500,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired contingent liability are 3,390,000. The acquired item is a present obligation with reliably measurable FV 265,000 and qualifies for recognition despite non-probable outflow. No tax or other adjustment applies. Find goodwill after recognising it.
explanation: Recognise the qualifying acquired liability: net identifiable assets become 3,390,000 − 265,000. Goodwill = consideration + NCI − adjusted net assets = 1,525,000.00.

title: Separate acquired brand from goodwill • case 13
prompt: Consideration is LKR 3,650,000; NCI FV 600,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired separable brand are 3,120,000. Brand FV is 530,000; tax base is zero and 30% DTL must be recognised. No other adjustments apply. Find goodwill after separate brand and tax recognition.
explanation: An identifiable acquired brand is separate from goodwill. Net addition to identifiable assets = brand FV − 30% DTL = 371,000.00. Goodwill = 3,650,000 + 600,000 − (3,120,000 + 371,000.00) = 759,000.00.

title: Acquisition costs versus issue costs • case 13
prompt: A business acquisition has consideration LKR 2,390,000. Additional costs are acquisition advisory 126,000, qualifying equity-issue costs 70,000 and qualifying debt-issue costs 40,000. The issue costs follow their relevant standards, and no immediate debt-cost amortisation or other expense arises this period. Find the immediate acquisition-related PROFIT-OR-LOSS expense from these costs.
explanation: Expense advisory acquisition costs of 126,000.00. Qualifying equity and debt issuance costs follow their respective standards and are not added to this immediate acquisition-service expense or goodwill.

title: Temporary difference and enacted rate change • case 13
prompt: A taxable temporary difference opens at LKR 200,000 with a DTL measured at 25%. At year end the difference is 365,000 and the enacted rate expected on reversal is 30%. Both the underlying movements and rate change belong in profit or loss. No other tax movements exist. Find deferred tax expense for the year.
explanation: Opening DTL = 200,000×25% = 50,000. Closing DTL = 365,000×30% = 109,500.00. Expense is the full increase, including rate remeasurement: 59,500.00. Rates are exercise assumptions.
family: Temporary difference and enacted rate change

title: Revalued non-depreciable land tax basis • case 13
prompt: Non-depreciable land is revalued from cost LKR 1,260,000 to fair value 1,890,000; tax base remains cost. The enacted rate for recovery through SALE is 20%, while a 30% use rate would otherwise apply. The revaluation and associated tax go to OCI. No other effects exist. Find the net OCI revaluation increase after deferred tax.
explanation: For this non-depreciable revalued asset, measure tax consequences on recovery through sale: DTL = (1,890,000 − 1,260,000)×20%. Net OCI increase = gross uplift less that DTL = 504,000.00.

title: Current tax reconciliation and prepayment • case 13
prompt: Accounting pretax profit is LKR 2,650,000. It includes a permanently non-deductible fine of 126,000, exempt income of 50,000, and warranty expense of 265,000 deductible only on payment. Current-year warranty payments of 80,000 are deductible and were charged against the provision, not current profit. Tax rate is 30%; tax prepayments are 300,000. No other tax adjustments exist. Find closing CURRENT tax payable, not total tax expense.
explanation: Taxable profit = 2,650,000 + fine 126,000 − exempt income 50,000 + provision expense 265,000 − deductible payments 80,000 = 2,911,000. Current tax less prepaid 300,000 = 573,300.00. Deferred tax is separate.

title: Consolidated inventory tax difference • case 13
prompt: After eliminating an intragroup profit, inventory carries in consolidated statements at LKR 756,000. Its tax base in the buyer’s tax jurisdiction is 1,134,000. The buyer’s enacted rate is 30%; sufficient taxable profit is probable. No offsetting, exception or other tax effects apply. Find the consolidated DTA on this inventory.
explanation: The consolidated carrying amount is below tax base, creating a deductible temporary difference of 378,000. Use the buyer’s relevant tax rate: difference ×30% = 113,400.00.

title: Depreciation after recognised impairment • case 13
prompt: Immediately before an impairment, equipment carries at LKR 1,260,000. Recoverable amount is 830,000 and impairment is recognised. After that date it has four years’ remaining useful life and residual value 100,000. Straight-line depreciation is appropriate; no further revaluation or impairment applies. Find depreciation for the next FULL year.
explanation: First reduce the asset to recoverable amount 830,000. Thereafter allocate revised depreciable amount over remaining life: (830,000 − 100,000)/4 = 182,500.00.

title: Allocated headquarters in CGU impairment • case 13
prompt: CGU A carries operating assets of LKR 730,000; CGU B carries 400,000. A headquarters asset of 200,000 can be allocated reasonably and consistently in proportion to those operating-asset amounts. A’s recoverable amount INCLUDING its headquarters share is 715,000. No goodwill or other assets exist. Find the impairment loss for A including its allocation.
explanation: Allocate headquarters to A: 200,000 × 730,000/(730,000+400,000) = 129,203.54. Tested A carrying amount is 859,203.54. Impairment versus recoverable amount 715,000 = 144,203.54.

title: Break-even value-in-use cash flow • case 13
prompt: An asset carries at LKR 1,260,000. Its fair value less costs of disposal is lower. A valid VIU model uses THREE equal year-end operating cash inflows, plus 100,000 net disposal proceeds at year three, discounted at 10%. What minimum equal ANNUAL operating cash inflow makes VIU exactly equal carrying amount? Ignore tax and other adjustments.
explanation: Let annual flow be X. X×(1/1.10 + 1/1.10² + 1/1.10³) + 100,000/1.10³ = 1,260,000. Solve for X = 476,453.17. This sensitivity calculation identifies the VIU break-even point.

title: Discounted warranty expected-value portfolio • case 13
prompt: A present warranty obligation covers 1,260 products. Per product, probabilities are 70% no defect, 25% a minor repair costing LKR 400, and 5% a major repair costing 2,000. All expected payments occur exactly in TWO years. Outflow for the portfolio is probable; appropriate discount rate is 10% with no risk double counting. Find the provision.
explanation: Expected cash payment = 1,260×(25%×400 + 5%×2,000) = 252,000.0. Discount two years at 10%: 252,000.0/1.10² = 208,264.46. The probability assessment applies to the portfolio.

title: Provision movement with revised estimate • case 13
prompt: A discounted provision opens at LKR 630,000. Unwinding for a full year is at 8%. A 100,000 settlement occurs at the year END, after unwinding. At that same reporting date, a new estimate increases the remaining provision by 76,000. No other changes occur. Find closing provision.
explanation: Closing = opening + 8% unwinding − year-end settlement + estimate increase: 630,000×1.08 −100,000 +76,000 = 656,400.00. Classification of the estimate change’s counterpart is assessed separately.

title: Revaluation increase after earlier loss • case 13
prompt: PPE carries at LKR 730,000 before revaluation and is revalued to 1,260,000. A prior revaluation decrease on THIS asset of 176,000 was recognised in profit or loss and has not been reversed. No tax effects apply. Find the current increase recognised in OCI after reversing the eligible prior loss in profit or loss.
explanation: Gross increase = 1,260,000 − 730,000 = 530,000. First recognise 176,000 in profit or loss to reverse the prior decrease. Remaining 354,000.00 is OCI revaluation surplus.

title: Nine-month depreciation and disposal gain • case 13
prompt: Equipment cost LKR 1,460,000, residual value 200,000 and useful life five years, straight-line. Two FULL years’ depreciation were recognised before this year. It is sold after nine months of the current year for 1,045,000. It was not previously held for sale and no impairment or revaluation applies. Find disposal GAIN after the required nine-month depreciation.
explanation: Annual depreciation = (1,460,000−200,000)/5. Deduct two full years and another 9/12 year from cost to obtain disposal-date carrying amount 767,000.00. Gain = proceeds − that amount = 278,000.00.

title: Customer collections with a write-off • case 13
prompt: All sales are on credit. Revenue is LKR 3,650,000; opening GROSS trade receivables are 600,000; closing GROSS receivables are 930,000. Receivables of 113,000 were written off during the year. There are no taxes, returns, contract balances, acquisitions or exchange changes. Find cash collected from customers.
explanation: Gross receivable roll-forward: opening + credit sales − cash receipts − write-offs = closing. Thus receipts = 3,650,000+600,000−930,000−113,000 = 3,207,000.00. Write-offs are not cash receipts.

title: Loan funding net cash effect • case 13
prompt: A company receives cash loan proceeds of LKR 1,260,000 and immediately pays a directly attributable lender issue fee of 26,500. Both payments are classified as financing cash flows in this case. No other cash movement occurs. Find the NET financing cash inflow from these two cash movements; this question does not require net line-item presentation.
explanation: Net financing cash effect = proceeds − cash fee = 1,260,000 − 26,500.00 = 1,233,500.00. Effective-interest amortisation later is not another inception cash payment.

title: Item-by-item NRV without offsetting headroom • case 13
prompt: Two unrelated inventory lines require separate NRV tests. A has 165 units, cost LKR 1,000 and NRV 900 each. B has 126 units, cost 1,000 and NRV 1,200 each. There is no basis to group them for the write-down test. Find TOTAL closing inventory carrying amount.
explanation: Carry A at 900 per unit and B at its lower cost of 1,000. Total = 165×900 + 126×1,000 = 274,500.00. B’s NRV headroom cannot offset A’s write-down.

title: Units-of-production intangible amortisation • case 13
prompt: A finite-life production licence costs LKR 1,160,000, has zero residual value, and is expected to support 150,000 units in total. Actual output this year is 36,500 units. A units-of-production method reliably reflects consumption and the asset was available throughout. No impairment or estimate change applies. Find annual amortisation.
explanation: Apply the supported consumption pattern: amortisation = 1,160,000 × 36,500/150,000 = 282,266.67. It is the share of expected lifetime production consumed, not an automatic straight-line charge.

prompt: An equity-method investment and relevant long-term interests were previously reduced to zero. Unrecognised share of prior losses totals LKR 106,000; the investor has no obligation and made no support payments. In the current year its share of associate profit is 159,000. No other adjustments or changes in interest apply. Find the share of profit that can now be RECOGNISED.
explanation: First absorb unrecognised prior losses before resuming recognised profit. Recognised amount = current profit share 159,000 − prior unrecognised losses 106,000 = 53,000.00.

prompt: A retailer has transferred 1,350 products. It expects 54 to be returned. Find the separate asset for the right to recover returned products, excluding the refund liability.
explanation: Recovery asset = original carrying amount of expected returns less recovery costs and potential value decrease: 54 × (600 − 20 − 30) = 29,700.00. It is assessed separately from the customer refund liability.
family: Return recovery asset net of costs

prompt: A customer’s annual purchases reach 11,400 units at list price LKR 200. Crossing the threshold entitles it to a 5% retrospective rebate on ALL units. Cumulative revenue before this new supported estimate equals full list price; no rebate was previously accrued. The constraint permits the estimate. explanation: The revised transaction price reflects the retrospective rebate on all units. Revenue reduction = 11,400 × 200 × 5% = 114,000.00. Recognise the corresponding refund obligation as appropriate.

explanation: The specified discount-allocation exception applies. Allocate all 64,000 discount to A: 270,000 − 64,000 = 206,000.00. Do not default to relative allocation when the exception’s criteria are met.

prompt: A contract price of LKR 1,620,000 covers goods A, goods B and twelve months of distinct support. Stand-alone prices are 600,000, 300,000 and 300,000 respectively. title: Uninstalled materials without margin • case 14
prompt: A single over-time construction obligation has price LKR 12,800,000. All B19(b) conditions justify recognising revenue equal to cost for significant uninstalled materials of 2,560,000 already controlled by the customer. Other productive costs incurred are 1,920,000; expected total OTHER costs are 7,680,000. No revenue was previously recognised. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise material revenue without margin: 2,560,000. Recognise the remaining price using other-cost progress: (12,800,000 − 2,560,000) × 1,920,000/7,680,000. Total revenue = 5,120,000.00.

title: Agent commission after collection • case 14
prompt: An intermediary is an AGENT and collects customer cash of LKR 1,700,000 for a completed supplier service. It must remit 88% to the supplier and is entitled to the remaining 12% commission. It controls neither the underlying service nor any distinct extra service, and there is no tax. Find its revenue.
explanation: An agent recognises its fee or commission, not the supplier’s gross billings: 1,700,000 × 12% = 204,000.00. The amount due to the supplier is separately accounted for.

title: Distinct remaining goods blended prospectively • case 14
prompt: At modification, 100 distinct goods remain under an existing contract at LKR 1,140 each. Another 50 distinct goods are added at 912 each. The modification is NOT a separate contract, but remaining goods are distinct from those already transferred, so paragraph 21(a) applies prospectively. Thirty of the remaining goods are then transferred. Find revenue for those thirty.
explanation: Prospective remaining consideration = 100 × 1,140 + 50 × 912. Divide by 150 remaining goods, then multiply by 30 = 31,920.00. Do not retrospectively revise revenue on goods already transferred.

title: FVTPL acquisition expense • case 14
prompt: A financial asset is acquired at fair value LKR 1,080,000 and is classified at FVTPL. Directly attributable broker costs are 27,000, paid separately. No fair-value change occurs immediately after purchase. Find the immediate profit-or-loss expense from acquiring this asset.
explanation: Transaction costs on an FVTPL asset are expensed. Initial asset carrying amount is fair value 1,080,000; immediate acquisition expense is 27,000.00.

title: Collateral cash-shortfall discounting • case 14
prompt: A credit loss scenario has a contractual receipt of LKR 1,350,000 due in one year. The ONLY expected recovery at that same date is collateral sale proceeds of 910,000, less sale costs of 64,000. Scenario probability is 100% and original EIR is 10%. Collateral is an integral contractual credit enhancement and not separately recognised. Find discounted ECL.
explanation: One-year shortfall = contractual receipt − net collateral recovery = 1,350,000 − (910,000 − 64,000). Discount that shortfall at 10%: 458,181.82. Do not ignore recovery costs or discount only one side of same-date cash flows.

title: Three-band provision matrix • case 14
prompt: Under the simplified lifetime-ECL approach, supported adjusted loss rates are 1% on current receivables of LKR 1,280,000, 5% on past-due balances of 370,000, and 30% on severely overdue balances of 128,000. Rates already include all required forward-looking and discounting effects. Find total loss allowance.
explanation: Apply each appropriate band rate and add: 1,280,000×1% + 370,000×5% + 128,000×30% = 69,700.00. Do not apply one blended band mechanically to all balances.

title: Equity FVOCI profit-or-loss dividend • case 14
prompt: An eligible equity investment has the irrevocable FVOCI election. During the year it gains LKR 148,000 in fair value and earns a dividend of 74,000. Dividend recognition criteria are met and the dividend clearly represents a return on investment, not recovery of cost. There are no other effects. Find income recognised in PROFIT OR LOSS.
explanation: The qualifying dividend of 74,000.00 is profit-or-loss income. The fair-value movement of 148,000 is OCI under this election and is not added to the profit-or-loss amount.

title: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset • case 14
prompt: A loan is sold with full derecognition. Immediately before sale, gross carrying amount is LKR 1,280,000, loss allowance 128,000, and cash proceeds 1,216,000. No accumulated OCI, sale fees or other adjustments exist. Find the derecognition GAIN relative to net carrying amount.
explanation: Net carrying amount = 1,280,000 − 128,000 = 1,152,000. Compare proceeds with that net amount: 1,216,000 − 1,152,000 = 64,000.00 gain. Derecognise both the gross asset and related allowance.
family: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset

title: Non-substantial liability modification gain • case 14
prompt: An amortised-cost liability is modified WITHOUT extinguishment, with no fees. Its carrying amount is LKR 1,140,000. The sole revised payment is 1,311,000 in two years. Original EIR is 10%; the modification is assessed as non-substantial. Find the immediate modification GAIN from recalculating amortised cost at the original EIR.
explanation: Revised amortised cost = 1,311,000/1.10² = 1,083,471.07. Gain = old liability 1,140,000 − revised PV = 56,528.93. The original EIR is retained for this non-extinguishing modification.

title: Credit-risk improvement allowance release • case 14
prompt: A debt asset under the GENERAL ECL model previously had significant credit-risk deterioration and lifetime allowance LKR 128,000. At reporting date the criteria for lifetime ECL are no longer met; required 12-month ECL is 17,000. No write-offs, new assets or other allowance movements occur. Find the impairment reversal in profit or loss.
explanation: When lifetime measurement is no longer required, the general model returns to 12-month ECL. Release the excess allowance: 128,000 − 17,000 = 111,000.00. This is not a receivable under mandatory simplified lifetime ECL.

title: Upstream inventory elimination with tax • case 14
prompt: P and S report profits AFTER their own tax of LKR 2,560,000 and 1,080,000. An upstream inventory sale leaves unrealised profit of 256,000 in group closing inventory. A recoverable DTA is recognised on the full elimination at 30%, with the tax effect in profit or loss. No other consolidation adjustments exist. Find TOTAL consolidated profit, before attribution to owners and NCI.
explanation: Combine separate after-tax profits, eliminate unrealised profit and recognise the recoverable tax benefit: 2,560,000 + 1,080,000 − 256,000 + 76,800.00 = 3,460,800.00. This question asks total group profit, not its attribution.

title: Full-goodwill impairment and owner profit • case 14
prompt: P owns 80% of S all year. Separate after-tax profits are P LKR 2,220,000 and S 840,000. Goodwill is recognised on the FULL-goodwill basis and an impairment of 270,000 is attributable to S’s CGU and allocated 80:20 between owners and NCI. No other adjustments or tax effects apply. Find consolidated profit attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Owners receive 80% of S’s profit and bear 80% of the full-goodwill loss: 2,220,000 + 80% × (840,000 − 270,000) = 2,676,000.00. Do not charge the owners with 100% of this full-goodwill loss.

title: Partial goodwill CGU gross-up • case 14
prompt: P owns 80% of S. Recognised PARTIAL goodwill is LKR 1,024,000; S’s other net assets in the tested CGU carry at 5,120,000. Recoverable amount of the WHOLE CGU is 5,760,000. Gross up goodwill for unrecognised NCI goodwill when testing; the whole impairment falls within grossed-up goodwill. No tax or other adjustments apply. Find impairment actually recognised on group goodwill.
explanation: Grossed-up goodwill = 1,024,000/80% = 1,280,000.00. Whole-CGU impairment = grossed goodwill + other net assets − recoverable amount = 640,000.00. Only the parent’s 80% goodwill portion is recognised, so recorded loss = 512,000.00.
reference: LKAS 36 Appendix C paras C4–C8; SLFRS 10 para B86

title: Consolidated retained earnings bridge • case 14
prompt: P owns 75% of S. At year end P retained earnings are LKR 3,700,000, and S retained earnings 2,420,000. S retained earnings at acquisition were 1,000,000. Cumulative post-acquisition extra FV depreciation is 128,000. A downstream sale by P leaves unrealised profit of 94,000. No tax, goodwill impairment, dividends recognised by P, OCI or other adjustments apply. Find consolidated retained earnings attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Group owners’ retained earnings = parent RE + 75% of adjusted post-acquisition S reserves − the parent’s downstream unrealised profit: 4,575,000.00. Pre-acquisition reserves do not enter post-acquisition group retained earnings.

title: Loss of control and translation reserve • case 14
prompt: P loses control of a foreign subsidiary. Proceeds are LKR 2,760,000; retained interest FV 640,000; NCI carrying amount 370,000; consolidated net assets INCLUDING goodwill 3,020,000. A cumulative translation GAIN of 128,000, entirely attributable to P, must be reclassified to profit or loss on loss of control. No other effects apply. Find total disposal gain including that reclassification.
explanation: Base gain = proceeds + retained FV + NCI − net assets = 750,000.00. Add the parent’s translation gain recycled on disposal: 128,000. Total = 878,000.00.
family: Loss of control and translation reserve

title: Residual guarantee expected payment • case 14
prompt: A lessee owes three year-end rentals of LKR 270,000. It guarantees residual value up to 100,000, but the amount EXPECTED to be payable under that guarantee is 44,000 at year three. Discount rate is 10%. No other liability payments exist. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the amount expected to be payable, not automatically the maximum guarantee. Liability = PV of three rentals + 44,000/1.10³ = 704,507.89.

title: Reasonably certain purchase option PV • case 14
prompt: A lease requires three year-end rentals of LKR 220,000, plus a purchase option price of 640,000 payable at year three. Exercise is reasonably certain. Discount rate is 10%. No incentives, other payments or initial prepayments apply. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the reasonably certain purchase price in the liability: PV of rentals + purchase price discounted for three years = 1,027,948.91. Do not omit or leave the future option payment undiscounted.

title: Lease and service component allocation • case 14
prompt: A two-year contract requires bundled payments of LKR 320,000 at each year end. Relative stand-alone prices are equipment lease 200,000 and distinct maintenance 50,000 per year. The lessee does NOT elect to combine components. Lease discount rate is 10%; no other payments exist. Find initial lease liability for the LEASE component only.
explanation: Allocate 200,000/250,000 = 80% of each bundled payment to the lease: 256,000.00. Discount those two lease payments, excluding maintenance, to obtain 444,297.52.

title: Exempt short-term lease rent-free start • case 14
prompt: A twelve-month lease with no purchase option qualifies for the elected short-term exemption. The first three months are rent free, then nine monthly payments of LKR 27,000 are due. The asset is available throughout and straight-line expense is appropriate. Find lease expense for the FIRST six months, ignoring accrual settlement timing.
explanation: Total fixed payments are nine rents. Spread evenly over all twelve months: 27,000 × 9/12 × 6 = 121,500.00. Rent-free months still receive an expense allocation.

title: Sale-and-leaseback rights transferred • case 14
prompt: A transfer qualifies as a sale under SLFRS 15 at fair value LKR 12,800,000; asset carrying amount is 7,400,000. Market-rate leaseback payments have PV 5,120,000. There are no off-market adjustments or variable-payment complications. At inception, what sale gain is recognised for rights TRANSFERRED to the buyer-lessor?
explanation: Total gain = 12,800,000 − 7,400,000 = 5,400,000. Retained-use proportion = lease PV / fair value = 40%. Recognise only the transferred-rights proportion of the gain: 3,240,000.00.

title: Reassessed bargain purchase gain • case 14
prompt: After the required reassessment, final acquisition-date consideration is LKR 2,560,000, NCI fair value is 400,000 and identifiable net assets are 3,840,000. There is no prior holding or other adjustment. Find the bargain purchase gain recognised in profit or loss.
explanation: Net identifiable assets exceed consideration plus NCI: 3,840,000 − 2,560,000 − 400,000 = 880,000.00. Reassessment has been completed before recognising the gain.

title: Acquired contingent liability in goodwill • case 14
prompt: Consideration is LKR 4,200,000; NCI FV is 500,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired contingent liability are 3,420,000. The acquired item is a present obligation with reliably measurable FV 270,000 and qualifies for recognition despite non-probable outflow. No tax or other adjustment applies. Find goodwill after recognising it.
explanation: Recognise the qualifying acquired liability: net identifiable assets become 3,420,000 − 270,000. Goodwill = consideration + NCI − adjusted net assets = 1,550,000.00.

title: Separate acquired brand from goodwill • case 14
prompt: Consideration is LKR 3,700,000; NCI FV 600,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired separable brand are 3,160,000. Brand FV is 540,000; tax base is zero and 30% DTL must be recognised. No other adjustments apply. Find goodwill after separate brand and tax recognition.
explanation: An identifiable acquired brand is separate from goodwill. Net addition to identifiable assets = brand FV − 30% DTL = 378,000.00. Goodwill = 3,700,000 + 600,000 − (3,160,000 + 378,000.00) = 762,000.00.

title: Acquisition costs versus issue costs • case 14
prompt: A business acquisition has consideration LKR 2,420,000. Additional costs are acquisition advisory 128,000, qualifying equity-issue costs 70,000 and qualifying debt-issue costs 40,000. The issue costs follow their relevant standards, and no immediate debt-cost amortisation or other expense arises this period. Find the immediate acquisition-related PROFIT-OR-LOSS expense from these costs.
explanation: Expense advisory acquisition costs of 128,000.00. Qualifying equity and debt issuance costs follow their respective standards and are not added to this immediate acquisition-service expense or goodwill.

title: Temporary difference and enacted rate change • case 14
prompt: A taxable temporary difference opens at LKR 200,000 with a DTL measured at 25%. At year end the difference is 370,000 and the enacted rate expected on reversal is 30%. Both the underlying movements and rate change belong in profit or loss. No other tax movements exist. Find deferred tax expense for the year.
explanation: Opening DTL = 200,000×25% = 50,000. Closing DTL = 370,000×30% = 111,000.00. Expense is the full increase, including rate remeasurement: 61,000.00. Rates are exercise assumptions.
family: Temporary difference and enacted rate change

title: Revalued non-depreciable land tax basis • case 14
prompt: Non-depreciable land is revalued from cost LKR 1,280,000 to fair value 1,920,000; tax base remains cost. The enacted rate for recovery through SALE is 20%, while a 30% use rate would otherwise apply. The revaluation and associated tax go to OCI. No other effects exist. Find the net OCI revaluation increase after deferred tax.
explanation: For this non-depreciable revalued asset, measure tax consequences on recovery through sale: DTL = (1,920,000 − 1,280,000)×20%. Net OCI increase = gross uplift less that DTL = 512,000.00.

title: Current tax reconciliation and prepayment • case 14
prompt: Accounting pretax profit is LKR 2,700,000. It includes a permanently non-deductible fine of 128,000, exempt income of 50,000, and warranty expense of 270,000 deductible only on payment. Current-year warranty payments of 80,000 are deductible and were charged against the provision, not current profit. Tax rate is 30%; tax prepayments are 300,000. No other tax adjustments exist. Find closing CURRENT tax payable, not total tax expense.
explanation: Taxable profit = 2,700,000 + fine 128,000 − exempt income 50,000 + provision expense 270,000 − deductible payments 80,000 = 2,968,000. Current tax less prepaid 300,000 = 590,400.00. Deferred tax is separate.

title: Consolidated inventory tax difference • case 14
prompt: After eliminating an intragroup profit, inventory carries in consolidated statements at LKR 768,000. Its tax base in the buyer’s tax jurisdiction is 1,152,000. The buyer’s enacted rate is 30%; sufficient taxable profit is probable. No offsetting, exception or other tax effects apply. Find the consolidated DTA on this inventory.
explanation: The consolidated carrying amount is below tax base, creating a deductible temporary difference of 384,000. Use the buyer’s relevant tax rate: difference ×30% = 115,200.00.

title: Depreciation after recognised impairment • case 14
prompt: Immediately before an impairment, equipment carries at LKR 1,280,000. Recoverable amount is 840,000 and impairment is recognised. After that date it has four years’ remaining useful life and residual value 100,000. Straight-line depreciation is appropriate; no further revaluation or impairment applies. Find depreciation for the next FULL year.
explanation: First reduce the asset to recoverable amount 840,000. Thereafter allocate revised depreciable amount over remaining life: (840,000 − 100,000)/4 = 185,000.00.

title: Allocated headquarters in CGU impairment • case 14
prompt: CGU A carries operating assets of LKR 740,000; CGU B carries 400,000. A headquarters asset of 200,000 can be allocated reasonably and consistently in proportion to those operating-asset amounts. A’s recoverable amount INCLUDING its headquarters share is 720,000. No goodwill or other assets exist. Find the impairment loss for A including its allocation.
explanation: Allocate headquarters to A: 200,000 × 740,000/(740,000+400,000) = 129,824.56. Tested A carrying amount is 869,824.56. Impairment versus recoverable amount 720,000 = 149,824.56.

title: Break-even value-in-use cash flow • case 14
prompt: An asset carries at LKR 1,280,000. Its fair value less costs of disposal is lower. A valid VIU model uses THREE equal year-end operating cash inflows, plus 100,000 net disposal proceeds at year three, discounted at 10%. What minimum equal ANNUAL operating cash inflow makes VIU exactly equal carrying amount? Ignore tax and other adjustments.
explanation: Let annual flow be X. X×(1/1.10 + 1/1.10² + 1/1.10³) + 100,000/1.10³ = 1,280,000. Solve for X = 484,495.47. This sensitivity calculation identifies the VIU break-even point.

title: Discounted warranty expected-value portfolio • case 14
prompt: A present warranty obligation covers 1,280 products. Per product, probabilities are 70% no defect, 25% a minor repair costing LKR 400, and 5% a major repair costing 2,000. All expected payments occur exactly in TWO years. Outflow for the portfolio is probable; appropriate discount rate is 10% with no risk double counting. Find the provision.
explanation: Expected cash payment = 1,280×(25%×400 + 5%×2,000) = 256,000.0. Discount two years at 10%: 256,000.0/1.10² = 211,570.25. The probability assessment applies to the portfolio.

title: Provision movement with revised estimate • case 14
prompt: A discounted provision opens at LKR 640,000. Unwinding for a full year is at 8%. A 100,000 settlement occurs at the year END, after unwinding. At that same reporting date, a new estimate increases the remaining provision by 78,000. No other changes occur. Find closing provision.
explanation: Closing = opening + 8% unwinding − year-end settlement + estimate increase: 640,000×1.08 −100,000 +78,000 = 669,200.00. Classification of the estimate change’s counterpart is assessed separately.

title: Revaluation increase after earlier loss • case 14
prompt: PPE carries at LKR 740,000 before revaluation and is revalued to 1,280,000. A prior revaluation decrease on THIS asset of 178,000 was recognised in profit or loss and has not been reversed. No tax effects apply. Find the current increase recognised in OCI after reversing the eligible prior loss in profit or loss.
explanation: Gross increase = 1,280,000 − 740,000 = 540,000. First recognise 178,000 in profit or loss to reverse the prior decrease. Remaining 362,000.00 is OCI revaluation surplus.

title: Nine-month depreciation and disposal gain • case 14
prompt: Equipment cost LKR 1,480,000, residual value 200,000 and useful life five years, straight-line. Two FULL years’ depreciation were recognised before this year. It is sold after nine months of the current year for 1,060,000. It was not previously held for sale and no impairment or revaluation applies. Find disposal GAIN after the required nine-month depreciation.
explanation: Annual depreciation = (1,480,000−200,000)/5. Deduct two full years and another 9/12 year from cost to obtain disposal-date carrying amount 776,000.00. Gain = proceeds − that amount = 284,000.00.

title: Customer collections with a write-off • case 14
prompt: All sales are on credit. Revenue is LKR 3,700,000; opening GROSS trade receivables are 600,000; closing GROSS receivables are 940,000. Receivables of 114,000 were written off during the year. There are no taxes, returns, contract balances, acquisitions or exchange changes. Find cash collected from customers.
explanation: Gross receivable roll-forward: opening + credit sales − cash receipts − write-offs = closing. Thus receipts = 3,700,000+600,000−940,000−114,000 = 3,246,000.00. Write-offs are not cash receipts.

title: Loan funding net cash effect • case 14
prompt: A company receives cash loan proceeds of LKR 1,280,000 and immediately pays a directly attributable lender issue fee of 27,000. Both payments are classified as financing cash flows in this case. No other cash movement occurs. Find the NET financing cash inflow from these two cash movements; this question does not require net line-item presentation.
explanation: Net financing cash effect = proceeds − cash fee = 1,280,000 − 27,000.00 = 1,253,000.00. Effective-interest amortisation later is not another inception cash payment.

title: Item-by-item NRV without offsetting headroom • case 14
prompt: Two unrelated inventory lines require separate NRV tests. A has 170 units, cost LKR 1,000 and NRV 900 each. B has 128 units, cost 1,000 and NRV 1,200 each. There is no basis to group them for the write-down test. Find TOTAL closing inventory carrying amount.
explanation: Carry A at 900 per unit and B at its lower cost of 1,000. Total = 170×900 + 128×1,000 = 281,000.00. B’s NRV headroom cannot offset A’s write-down.

title: Units-of-production intangible amortisation • case 14
prompt: A finite-life production licence costs LKR 1,180,000, has zero residual value, and is expected to support 150,000 units in total. Actual output this year is 37,000 units. A units-of-production method reliably reflects consumption and the asset was available throughout. No impairment or estimate change applies. Find annual amortisation.
explanation: Apply the supported consumption pattern: amortisation = 1,180,000 × 37,000/150,000 = 291,066.67. It is the share of expected lifetime production consumed, not an automatic straight-line charge.

title: Profit after suspended associate losses • case 14
prompt: An equity-method investment and relevant long-term interests were previously reduced to zero. Unrecognised share of prior losses totals LKR 108,000; the investor has no obligation and made no support payments. In the current year its share of associate profit is 162,000. No other adjustments or changes in interest apply. Find the share of profit that can now be RECOGNISED.
explanation: First absorb unrecognised prior losses before resuming recognised profit. Recognised amount = current profit share 162,000 − prior unrecognised losses 108,000 = 54,000.00.

title: Return recovery asset net of costs • case 15
prompt: A retailer has transferred 1,375 products. It expects 55 to be returned. Each returned product originally cost LKR 600; expected recovery handling is 20 per item and expected value deterioration is 30 per item. Estimates meet the relevant requirements. Find the separate asset for the right to recover returned products, excluding the refund liability.
explanation: Recovery asset = original carrying amount of expected returns less recovery costs and potential value decrease: 55 × (600 − 20 − 30) = 30,250.00. It is assessed separately from the customer refund liability.
family: Return recovery asset net of costs

title: Retrospective volume rebate true-up • case 15
prompt: A customer’s annual purchases reach 11,500 units at list price LKR 200. Crossing the threshold entitles it to a 5% retrospective rebate on ALL units. Cumulative revenue before this new supported estimate equals full list price; no rebate was previously accrued. The constraint permits the estimate. Find the reduction in cumulative revenue required now.
explanation: The revised transaction price reflects the retrospective rebate on all units. Revenue reduction = 11,500 × 200 × 5% = 115,000.00. Recognise the corresponding refund obligation as appropriate.

title: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation • case 15
prompt: A bundle has distinct goods A and B with stand-alone prices LKR 275,000 and 450,000. Total transaction price is 660,000. ALL paragraph 82 criteria demonstrate that the whole 65,000 discount relates only to A. A transfers now; B is not yet delivered. Find revenue recognised for A.
explanation: The specified discount-allocation exception applies. Allocate all 65,000 discount to A: 275,000 − 65,000 = 210,000.00. Do not default to relative allocation when the exception’s criteria are met.
family: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation

title: Three obligations and partial service • case 15
prompt: A contract price of LKR 1,650,000 covers goods A, goods B and twelve months of distinct support. Stand-alone prices are 600,000, 300,000 and 300,000 respectively. A is delivered, B is not, and six months of evenly provided support are complete. No allocation exception applies. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise allocation to A plus half of support: 1,650,000 × (600,000 + 150,000) / 1,200,000 = 1,031,250.00. B’s allocation remains unrecognised as revenue.

title: Progress excluding abnormal waste • case 15
prompt: An over-time contract has transaction price LKR 11,500,000. Costs incurred are 4,600,000, including abnormal waste of 230,000 that does not depict progress. Expected TOTAL productive costs excluding that waste are 9,200,000. Cost-to-cost is appropriate after excluding the waste; no other adjustment applies. Find cumulative revenue, not profit.
explanation: Exclude abnormal waste from the progress numerator. Productive progress = (4,600,000 − 230,000) / 9,200,000. Revenue = transaction price × that progress = 5,462,500.00. The wasted cost is not a revenue-producing input.

title: Uninstalled materials without margin • case 15
prompt: A single over-time construction obligation has price LKR 13,000,000. All B19(b) conditions justify recognising revenue equal to cost for significant uninstalled materials of 2,600,000 already controlled by the customer. Other productive costs incurred are 1,950,000; expected total OTHER costs are 7,800,000. No revenue was previously recognised. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise material revenue without margin: 2,600,000. Recognise the remaining price using other-cost progress: (13,000,000 − 2,600,000) × 1,950,000/7,800,000. Total revenue = 5,200,000.00.

title: Agent commission after collection • case 15
prompt: An intermediary is an AGENT and collects customer cash of LKR 1,750,000 for a completed supplier service. It must remit 88% to the supplier and is entitled to the remaining 12% commission. It controls neither the underlying service nor any distinct extra service, and there is no tax. Find its revenue.
explanation: An agent recognises its fee or commission, not the supplier’s gross billings: 1,750,000 × 12% = 210,000.00. The amount due to the supplier is separately accounted for.

title: Distinct remaining goods blended prospectively • case 15
prompt: At modification, 100 distinct goods remain under an existing contract at LKR 1,150 each. Another 50 distinct goods are added at 920 each. The modification is NOT a separate contract, but remaining goods are distinct from those already transferred, so paragraph 21(a) applies prospectively. Thirty of the remaining goods are then transferred. Find revenue for those thirty.
explanation: Prospective remaining consideration = 100 × 1,150 + 50 × 920. Divide by 150 remaining goods, then multiply by 30 = 32,200.00. Do not retrospectively revise revenue on goods already transferred.

title: FVTPL acquisition expense • case 15
prompt: A financial asset is acquired at fair value LKR 1,100,000 and is classified at FVTPL. Directly attributable broker costs are 27,500, paid separately. No fair-value change occurs immediately after purchase. Find the immediate profit-or-loss expense from acquiring this asset.
explanation: Transaction costs on an FVTPL asset are expensed. Initial asset carrying amount is fair value 1,100,000; immediate acquisition expense is 27,500.00.

title: Collateral cash-shortfall discounting • case 15
prompt: A credit loss scenario has a contractual receipt of LKR 1,375,000 due in one year. The ONLY expected recovery at that same date is collateral sale proceeds of 925,000, less sale costs of 65,000. Scenario probability is 100% and original EIR is 10%. Collateral is an integral contractual credit enhancement and not separately recognised. Find discounted ECL.
explanation: One-year shortfall = contractual receipt − net collateral recovery = 1,375,000 − (925,000 − 65,000). Discount that shortfall at 10%: 468,181.82. Do not ignore recovery costs or discount only one side of same-date cash flows.

title: Three-band provision matrix • case 15
prompt: Under the simplified lifetime-ECL approach, supported adjusted loss rates are 1% on current receivables of LKR 1,300,000, 5% on past-due balances of 375,000, and 30% on severely overdue balances of 130,000. Rates already include all required forward-looking and discounting effects. Find total loss allowance.
explanation: Apply each appropriate band rate and add: 1,300,000×1% + 375,000×5% + 130,000×30% = 70,750.00. Do not apply one blended band mechanically to all balances.

title: Equity FVOCI profit-or-loss dividend • case 15
prompt: An eligible equity investment has the irrevocable FVOCI election. During the year it gains LKR 150,000 in fair value and earns a dividend of 75,000. Dividend recognition criteria are met and the dividend clearly represents a return on investment, not recovery of cost. There are no other effects. Find income recognised in PROFIT OR LOSS.
explanation: The qualifying dividend of 75,000.00 is profit-or-loss income. The fair-value movement of 150,000 is OCI under this election and is not added to the profit-or-loss amount.

title: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset • case 15
prompt: A loan is sold with full derecognition. Immediately before sale, gross carrying amount is LKR 1,300,000, loss allowance 130,000, and cash proceeds 1,235,000. No accumulated OCI, sale fees or other adjustments exist. Find the derecognition GAIN relative to net carrying amount.
explanation: Net carrying amount = 1,300,000 − 130,000 = 1,170,000. Compare proceeds with that net amount: 1,235,000 − 1,170,000 = 65,000.00 gain. Derecognise both the gross asset and related allowance.
family: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset

title: Non-substantial liability modification gain • case 15
prompt: An amortised-cost liability is modified WITHOUT extinguishment, with no fees. Its carrying amount is LKR 1,150,000. The sole revised payment is 1,322,500 in two years. Original EIR is 10%; the modification is assessed as non-substantial. Find the immediate modification GAIN from recalculating amortised cost at the original EIR.
explanation: Revised amortised cost = 1,322,500/1.10² = 1,092,975.21. Gain = old liability 1,150,000 − revised PV = 57,024.79. The original EIR is retained for this non-extinguishing modification.

title: Credit-risk improvement allowance release • case 15
prompt: A debt asset under the GENERAL ECL model previously had significant credit-risk deterioration and lifetime allowance LKR 130,000. At reporting date the criteria for lifetime ECL are no longer met; required 12-month ECL is 17,500. No write-offs, new assets or other allowance movements occur. Find the impairment reversal in profit or loss.
explanation: When lifetime measurement is no longer required, the general model returns to 12-month ECL. Release the excess allowance: 130,000 − 17,500 = 112,500.00. This is not a receivable under mandatory simplified lifetime ECL.

title: Upstream inventory elimination with tax • case 15
prompt: P and S report profits AFTER their own tax of LKR 2,600,000 and 1,100,000. An upstream inventory sale leaves unrealised profit of 260,000 in group closing inventory. A recoverable DTA is recognised on the full elimination at 30%, with the tax effect in profit or loss. No other consolidation adjustments exist. Find TOTAL consolidated profit, before attribution to owners and NCI.
explanation: Combine separate after-tax profits, eliminate unrealised profit and recognise the recoverable tax benefit: 2,600,000 + 1,100,000 − 260,000 + 78,000.00 = 3,518,000.00. This question asks total group profit, not its attribution.

title: Full-goodwill impairment and owner profit • case 15
prompt: P owns 80% of S all year. Separate after-tax profits are P LKR 2,250,000 and S 850,000. Goodwill is recognised on the FULL-goodwill basis and an impairment of 275,000 is attributable to S’s CGU and allocated 80:20 between owners and NCI. No other adjustments or tax effects apply. Find consolidated profit attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Owners receive 80% of S’s profit and bear 80% of the full-goodwill loss: 2,250,000 + 80% × (850,000 − 275,000) = 2,710,000.00. Do not charge the owners with 100% of this full-goodwill loss.

title: Partial goodwill CGU gross-up • case 15
prompt: P owns 80% of S. Recognised PARTIAL goodwill is LKR 1,040,000; S’s other net assets in the tested CGU carry at 5,200,000. Recoverable amount of the WHOLE CGU is 5,850,000. Gross up goodwill for unrecognised NCI goodwill when testing; the whole impairment falls within grossed-up goodwill. No tax or other adjustments apply. Find impairment actually recognised on group goodwill.
explanation: Grossed-up goodwill = 1,040,000/80% = 1,300,000.00. Whole-CGU impairment = grossed goodwill + other net assets − recoverable amount = 650,000.00. Only the parent’s 80% goodwill portion is recognised, so recorded loss = 520,000.00.
reference: LKAS 36 Appendix C paras C4–C8; SLFRS 10 para B86

title: Consolidated retained earnings bridge • case 15
prompt: P owns 75% of S. At year end P retained earnings are LKR 3,750,000, and S retained earnings 2,450,000. S retained earnings at acquisition were 1,000,000. Cumulative post-acquisition extra FV depreciation is 130,000. A downstream sale by P leaves unrealised profit of 95,000. No tax, goodwill impairment, dividends recognised by P, OCI or other adjustments apply. Find consolidated retained earnings attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Group owners’ retained earnings = parent RE + 75% of adjusted post-acquisition S reserves − the parent’s downstream unrealised profit: 4,645,000.00. Pre-acquisition reserves do not enter post-acquisition group retained earnings.

title: Loss of control and translation reserve • case 15
prompt: P loses control of a foreign subsidiary. Proceeds are LKR 2,800,000; retained interest FV 650,000; NCI carrying amount 375,000; consolidated net assets INCLUDING goodwill 3,050,000. A cumulative translation GAIN of 130,000, entirely attributable to P, must be reclassified to profit or loss on loss of control. No other effects apply. Find total disposal gain including that reclassification.
explanation: Base gain = proceeds + retained FV + NCI − net assets = 775,000.00. Add the parent’s translation gain recycled on disposal: 130,000. Total = 905,000.00.
family: Loss of control and translation reserve

title: Residual guarantee expected payment • case 15
prompt: A lessee owes three year-end rentals of LKR 275,000. It guarantees residual value up to 100,000, but the amount EXPECTED to be payable under that guarantee is 45,000 at year three. Discount rate is 10%. No other liability payments exist. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the amount expected to be payable, not automatically the maximum guarantee. Liability = PV of three rentals + 45,000/1.10³ = 717,693.46.

title: Reasonably certain purchase option PV • case 15
prompt: A lease requires three year-end rentals of LKR 225,000, plus a purchase option price of 650,000 payable at year three. Exercise is reasonably certain. Discount rate is 10%. No incentives, other payments or initial prepayments apply. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the reasonably certain purchase price in the liability: PV of rentals + purchase price discounted for three years = 1,047,896.32. Do not omit or leave the future option payment undiscounted.

title: Lease and service component allocation • case 15
prompt: A two-year contract requires bundled payments of LKR 325,000 at each year end. Relative stand-alone prices are equipment lease 200,000 and distinct maintenance 50,000 per year. The lessee does NOT elect to combine components. Lease discount rate is 10%; no other payments exist. Find initial lease liability for the LEASE component only.
explanation: Allocate 200,000/250,000 = 80% of each bundled payment to the lease: 260,000.00. Discount those two lease payments, excluding maintenance, to obtain 451,239.67.

title: Exempt short-term lease rent-free start • case 15
prompt: A twelve-month lease with no purchase option qualifies for the elected short-term exemption. The first three months are rent free, then nine monthly payments of LKR 27,500 are due. The asset is available throughout and straight-line expense is appropriate. Find lease expense for the FIRST six months, ignoring accrual settlement timing.
explanation: Total fixed payments are nine rents. Spread evenly over all twelve months: 27,500 × 9/12 × 6 = 123,750.00. Rent-free months still receive an expense allocation.

title: Sale-and-leaseback rights transferred • case 15
prompt: A transfer qualifies as a sale under SLFRS 15 at fair value LKR 13,000,000; asset carrying amount is 7,500,000. Market-rate leaseback payments have PV 5,200,000. There are no off-market adjustments or variable-payment complications. At inception, what sale gain is recognised for rights TRANSFERRED to the buyer-lessor?
explanation: Total gain = 13,000,000 − 7,500,000 = 5,500,000. Retained-use proportion = lease PV / fair value = 40%. Recognise only the transferred-rights proportion of the gain: 3,300,000.00.

title: Reassessed bargain purchase gain • case 15
prompt: After the required reassessment, final acquisition-date consideration is LKR 2,600,000, NCI fair value is 400,000 and identifiable net assets are 3,900,000. There is no prior holding or other adjustment. Find the bargain purchase gain recognised in profit or loss.
explanation: Net identifiable assets exceed consideration plus NCI: 3,900,000 − 2,600,000 − 400,000 = 900,000.00. Reassessment has been completed before recognising the gain.

title: Acquired contingent liability in goodwill • case 15
prompt: Consideration is LKR 4,250,000; NCI FV is 500,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired contingent liability are 3,450,000. The acquired item is a present obligation with reliably measurable FV 275,000 and qualifies for recognition despite non-probable outflow. No tax or other adjustment applies. Find goodwill after recognising it.
explanation: Recognise the qualifying acquired liability: net identifiable assets become 3,450,000 − 275,000. Goodwill = consideration + NCI − adjusted net assets = 1,575,000.00.

title: Separate acquired brand from goodwill • case 15
prompt: Consideration is LKR 3,750,000; NCI FV 600,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired separable brand are 3,200,000. Brand FV is 550,000; tax base is zero and 30% DTL must be recognised. No other adjustments apply. Find goodwill after separate brand and tax recognition.
explanation: An identifiable acquired brand is separate from goodwill. Net addition to identifiable assets = brand FV − 30% DTL = 385,000.00. Goodwill = 3,750,000 + 600,000 − (3,200,000 + 385,000.00) = 765,000.00.

title: Acquisition costs versus issue costs • case 15
prompt: A business acquisition has consideration LKR 2,450,000. Additional costs are acquisition advisory 130,000, qualifying equity-issue costs 70,000 and qualifying debt-issue costs 40,000. The issue costs follow their relevant standards, and no immediate debt-cost amortisation or other expense arises this period. Find the immediate acquisition-related PROFIT-OR-LOSS expense from these costs.
explanation: Expense advisory acquisition costs of 130,000.00. Qualifying equity and debt issuance costs follow their respective standards and are not added to this immediate acquisition-service expense or goodwill.

title: Temporary difference and enacted rate change • case 15
prompt: A taxable temporary difference opens at LKR 200,000 with a DTL measured at 25%. At year end the difference is 375,000 and the enacted rate expected on reversal is 30%. Both the underlying movements and rate change belong in profit or loss. No other tax movements exist. Find deferred tax expense for the year.
explanation: Opening DTL = 200,000×25% = 50,000. Closing DTL = 375,000×30% = 112,500.00. Expense is the full increase, including rate remeasurement: 62,500.00. Rates are exercise assumptions.
family: Temporary difference and enacted rate change

title: Revalued non-depreciable land tax basis • case 15
prompt: Non-depreciable land is revalued from cost LKR 1,300,000 to fair value 1,950,000; tax base remains cost. The enacted rate for recovery through SALE is 20%, while a 30% use rate would otherwise apply. The revaluation and associated tax go to OCI. No other effects exist. Find the net OCI revaluation increase after deferred tax.
explanation: For this non-depreciable revalued asset, measure tax consequences on recovery through sale: DTL = (1,950,000 − 1,300,000)×20%. Net OCI increase = gross uplift less that DTL = 520,000.00.

title: Current tax reconciliation and prepayment • case 15
prompt: Accounting pretax profit is LKR 2,750,000. It includes a permanently non-deductible fine of 130,000, exempt income of 50,000, and warranty expense of 275,000 deductible only on payment. Current-year warranty payments of 80,000 are deductible and were charged against the provision, not current profit. Tax rate is 30%; tax prepayments are 300,000. No other tax adjustments exist. Find closing CURRENT tax payable, not total tax expense.
explanation: Taxable profit = 2,750,000 + fine 130,000 − exempt income 50,000 + provision expense 275,000 − deductible payments 80,000 = 3,025,000. Current tax less prepaid 300,000 = 607,500.00. Deferred tax is separate.

title: Consolidated inventory tax difference • case 15
prompt: After eliminating an intragroup profit, inventory carries in consolidated statements at LKR 780,000. Its tax base in the buyer’s tax jurisdiction is 1,170,000. The buyer’s enacted rate is 30%; sufficient taxable profit is probable. No offsetting, exception or other tax effects apply. Find the consolidated DTA on this inventory.
explanation: The consolidated carrying amount is below tax base, creating a deductible temporary difference of 390,000. Use the buyer’s relevant tax rate: difference ×30% = 117,000.00.

title: Depreciation after recognised impairment • case 15
prompt: Immediately before an impairment, equipment carries at LKR 1,300,000. Recoverable amount is 850,000 and impairment is recognised. After that date it has four years’ remaining useful life and residual value 100,000. Straight-line depreciation is appropriate; no further revaluation or impairment applies. Find depreciation for the next FULL year.
explanation: First reduce the asset to recoverable amount 850,000. Thereafter allocate revised depreciable amount over remaining life: (850,000 − 100,000)/4 = 187,500.00.

title: Allocated headquarters in CGU impairment • case 15
prompt: CGU A carries operating assets of LKR 750,000; CGU B carries 400,000. A headquarters asset of 200,000 can be allocated reasonably and consistently in proportion to those operating-asset amounts. A’s recoverable amount INCLUDING its headquarters share is 725,000. No goodwill or other assets exist. Find the impairment loss for A including its allocation.
explanation: Allocate headquarters to A: 200,000 × 750,000/(750,000+400,000) = 130,434.78. Tested A carrying amount is 880,434.78. Impairment versus recoverable amount 725,000 = 155,434.78.

title: Break-even value-in-use cash flow • case 15
prompt: An asset carries at LKR 1,300,000. Its fair value less costs of disposal is lower. A valid VIU model uses THREE equal year-end operating cash inflows, plus 100,000 net disposal proceeds at year three, discounted at 10%. What minimum equal ANNUAL operating cash inflow makes VIU exactly equal carrying amount? Ignore tax and other adjustments.
explanation: Let annual flow be X. X×(1/1.10 + 1/1.10² + 1/1.10³) + 100,000/1.10³ = 1,300,000. Solve for X = 492,537.76. This sensitivity calculation identifies the VIU break-even point.

title: Discounted warranty expected-value portfolio • case 15
prompt: A present warranty obligation covers 1,300 products. Per product, probabilities are 70% no defect, 25% a minor repair costing LKR 400, and 5% a major repair costing 2,000. All expected payments occur exactly in TWO years. Outflow for the portfolio is probable; appropriate discount rate is 10% with no risk double counting. Find the provision.
explanation: Expected cash payment = 1,300×(25%×400 + 5%×2,000) = 260,000.0. Discount two years at 10%: 260,000.0/1.10² = 214,876.03. The probability assessment applies to the portfolio.

title: Provision movement with revised estimate • case 15
prompt: A discounted provision opens at LKR 650,000. Unwinding for a full year is at 8%. A 100,000 settlement occurs at the year END, after unwinding. At that same reporting date, a new estimate increases the remaining provision by 80,000. No other changes occur. Find closing provision.
explanation: Closing = opening + 8% unwinding − year-end settlement + estimate increase: 650,000×1.08 −100,000 +80,000 = 682,000.00. Classification of the estimate change’s counterpart is assessed separately.

title: Revaluation increase after earlier loss • case 15
prompt: PPE carries at LKR 750,000 before revaluation and is revalued to 1,300,000. A prior revaluation decrease on THIS asset of 180,000 was recognised in profit or loss and has not been reversed. No tax effects apply. Find the current increase recognised in OCI after reversing the eligible prior loss in profit or loss.
explanation: Gross increase = 1,300,000 − 750,000 = 550,000. First recognise 180,000 in profit or loss to reverse the prior decrease. Remaining 370,000.00 is OCI revaluation surplus.

title: Nine-month depreciation and disposal gain • case 15
prompt: Equipment cost LKR 1,500,000, residual value 200,000 and useful life five years, straight-line. Two FULL years’ depreciation were recognised before this year. It is sold after nine months of the current year for 1,075,000. It was not previously held for sale and no impairment or revaluation applies. Find disposal GAIN after the required nine-month depreciation.
explanation: Annual depreciation = (1,500,000−200,000)/5. Deduct two full years and another 9/12 year from cost to obtain disposal-date carrying amount 785,000.00. Gain = proceeds − that amount = 290,000.00.

title: Customer collections with a write-off • case 15
prompt: All sales are on credit. Revenue is LKR 3,750,000; opening GROSS trade receivables are 600,000; closing GROSS receivables are 950,000. Receivables of 115,000 were written off during the year. There are no taxes, returns, contract balances, acquisitions or exchange changes. Find cash collected from customers.
explanation: Gross receivable roll-forward: opening + credit sales − cash receipts − write-offs = closing. Thus receipts = 3,750,000+600,000−950,000−115,000 = 3,285,000.00. Write-offs are not cash receipts.

title: Loan funding net cash effect • case 15
prompt: A company receives cash loan proceeds of LKR 1,300,000 and immediately pays a directly attributable lender issue fee of 27,500. Both payments are classified as financing cash flows in this case. No other cash movement occurs. Find the NET financing cash inflow from these two cash movements; this question does not require net line-item presentation.
explanation: Net financing cash effect = proceeds − cash fee = 1,300,000 − 27,500.00 = 1,272,500.00. Effective-interest amortisation later is not another inception cash payment.

title: Item-by-item NRV without offsetting headroom • case 15
prompt: Two unrelated inventory lines require separate NRV tests. A has 175 units, cost LKR 1,000 and NRV 900 each. B has 130 units, cost 1,000 and NRV 1,200 each. There is no basis to group them for the write-down test. Find TOTAL closing inventory carrying amount.
explanation: Carry A at 900 per unit and B at its lower cost of 1,000. Total = 175×900 + 130×1,000 = 287,500.00. B’s NRV headroom cannot offset A’s write-down.

title: Units-of-production intangible amortisation • case 15
prompt: A finite-life production licence costs LKR 1,200,000, has zero residual value, and is expected to support 150,000 units in total. Actual output this year is 37,500 units. A units-of-production method reliably reflects consumption and the asset was available throughout. No impairment or estimate change applies. Find annual amortisation.
explanation: Apply the supported consumption pattern: amortisation = 1,200,000 × 37,500/150,000 = 300,000.00. It is the share of expected lifetime production consumed, not an automatic straight-line charge.

title: Profit after suspended associate losses • case 15
prompt: An equity-method investment and relevant long-term interests were previously reduced to zero. Unrecognised share of prior losses totals LKR 110,000; the investor has no obligation and made no support payments. In the current year its share of associate profit is 165,000. No other adjustments or changes in interest apply. Find the share of profit that can now be RECOGNISED.
explanation: First absorb unrecognised prior losses before resuming recognised profit. Recognised amount = current profit share 165,000 − prior unrecognised losses 110,000 = 55,000.00.

title: Return recovery asset net of costs • case 16
prompt: A retailer has transferred 1,400 products. It expects 56 to be returned. Each returned product originally cost LKR 600; expected recovery handling is 20 per item and expected value deterioration is 30 per item. Estimates meet the relevant requirements. Find the separate asset for the right to recover returned products, excluding the refund liability.
explanation: Recovery asset = original carrying amount of expected returns less recovery costs and potential value decrease: 56 × (600 − 20 − 30) = 30,800.00. It is assessed separately from the customer refund liability.
family: Return recovery asset net of costs

title: Retrospective volume rebate true-up • case 16
prompt: A customer’s annual purchases reach 11,600 units at list price LKR 200. Crossing the threshold entitles it to a 5% retrospective rebate on ALL units. Cumulative revenue before this new supported estimate equals full list price; no rebate was previously accrued. The constraint permits the estimate. Find the reduction in cumulative revenue required now.
explanation: The revised transaction price reflects the retrospective rebate on all units. Revenue reduction = 11,600 × 200 × 5% = 116,000.00. Recognise the corresponding refund obligation as appropriate.

title: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation • case 16
prompt: A bundle has distinct goods A and B with stand-alone prices LKR 280,000 and 460,000. Total transaction price is 674,000. ALL paragraph 82 criteria demonstrate that the whole 66,000 discount relates only to A. A transfers now; B is not yet delivered. Find revenue recognised for A.
explanation: The specified discount-allocation exception applies. Allocate all 66,000 discount to A: 280,000 − 66,000 = 214,000.00. Do not default to relative allocation when the exception’s criteria are met.
family: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation

title: Three obligations and partial service • case 16
prompt: A contract price of LKR 1,680,000 covers goods A, goods B and twelve months of distinct support. Stand-alone prices are 600,000, 300,000 and 300,000 respectively. A is delivered, B is not, and six months of evenly provided support are complete. No allocation exception applies. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise allocation to A plus half of support: 1,680,000 × (600,000 + 150,000) / 1,200,000 = 1,050,000.00. B’s allocation remains unrecognised as revenue.

title: Progress excluding abnormal waste • case 16
prompt: An over-time contract has transaction price LKR 11,600,000. Costs incurred are 4,640,000, including abnormal waste of 232,000 that does not depict progress.
