title: Separate acquired brand from goodwill • case 21
prompt: Consideration is LKR 4,050,000; NCI FV 600,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired separable brand are 3,440,000. Brand FV is 610,000; tax base is zero and 30% DTL must be recognised. No other adjustments apply. Find goodwill after separate brand and tax recognition.
explanation: An identifiable acquired brand is separate from goodwill. Net addition to identifiable assets = brand FV − 30% DTL = 427,000.00. Goodwill = 4,050,000 + 600,000 − (3,440,000 + 427,000.00) = 783,000.00.

title: Acquisition costs versus issue costs • case 21
prompt: A business acquisition has consideration LKR 2,630,000. Additional costs are acquisition advisory 142,000, qualifying equity-issue costs 70,000 and qualifying debt-issue costs 40,000. The issue costs follow their relevant standards, and no immediate debt-cost amortisation or other expense arises this period. Find the immediate acquisition-related PROFIT-OR-LOSS expense from these costs.
explanation: Expense advisory acquisition costs of 142,000.00. Qualifying equity and debt issuance costs follow their respective standards and are not added to this immediate acquisition-service expense or goodwill.

title: Temporary difference and enacted rate change • case 21
prompt: A taxable temporary difference opens at LKR 200,000 with a DTL measured at 25%. At year end the difference is 405,000 and the enacted rate expected on reversal is 30%. Both the underlying movements and rate change belong in profit or loss. No other tax movements exist. Find deferred tax expense for the year.
explanation: Opening DTL = 200,000×25% = 50,000. Closing DTL = 405,000×30% = 121,500.00. Expense is the full increase, including rate remeasurement: 71,500.00. Rates are exercise assumptions.
family: Temporary difference and enacted rate change

title: Revalued non-depreciable land tax basis • case 21
prompt: Non-depreciable land is revalued from cost LKR 1,420,000 to fair value 2,130,000; tax base remains cost. The enacted rate for recovery through SALE is 20%, while a 30% use rate would otherwise apply. The revaluation and associated tax go to OCI. No other effects exist. Find the net OCI revaluation increase after deferred tax.
explanation: For this non-depreciable revalued asset, measure tax consequences on recovery through sale: DTL = (2,130,000 − 1,420,000)×20%. Net OCI increase = gross uplift less that DTL = 568,000.00.

title: Current tax reconciliation and prepayment • case 21
prompt: Accounting pretax profit is LKR 3,050,000. It includes a permanently non-deductible fine of 142,000, exempt income of 50,000, and warranty expense of 305,000 deductible only on payment. Current-year warranty payments of 80,000 are deductible and were charged against the provision, not current profit. Tax rate is 30%; tax prepayments are 300,000. No other tax adjustments exist. Find closing CURRENT tax payable, not total tax expense.
explanation: Taxable profit = 3,050,000 + fine 142,000 − exempt income 50,000 + provision expense 305,000 − deductible payments 80,000 = 3,367,000. Current tax less prepaid 300,000 = 710,100.00. Deferred tax is separate.

title: Consolidated inventory tax difference • case 21
prompt: After eliminating an intragroup profit, inventory carries in consolidated statements at LKR 852,000. Its tax base in the buyer’s tax jurisdiction is 1,278,000. The buyer’s enacted rate is 30%; sufficient taxable profit is probable. No offsetting, exception or other tax effects apply. Find the consolidated DTA on this inventory.
explanation: The consolidated carrying amount is below tax base, creating a deductible temporary difference of 426,000. Use the buyer’s relevant tax rate: difference ×30% = 127,800.00.

title: Depreciation after recognised impairment • case 21
prompt: Immediately before an impairment, equipment carries at LKR 1,420,000. Recoverable amount is 910,000 and impairment is recognised. After that date it has four years’ remaining useful life and residual value 100,000. Straight-line depreciation is appropriate; no further revaluation or impairment applies. Find depreciation for the next FULL year.
explanation: First reduce the asset to recoverable amount 910,000. Thereafter allocate revised depreciable amount over remaining life: (910,000 − 100,000)/4 = 202,500.00.

title: Allocated headquarters in CGU impairment • case 21
prompt: CGU A carries operating assets of LKR 810,000; CGU B carries 400,000. A headquarters asset of 200,000 can be allocated reasonably and consistently in proportion to those operating-asset amounts. A’s recoverable amount INCLUDING its headquarters share is 755,000. No goodwill or other assets exist. Find the impairment loss for A including its allocation.
explanation: Allocate headquarters to A: 200,000 × 810,000/(810,000+400,000) = 133,884.30. Tested A carrying amount is 943,884.30. Impairment versus recoverable amount 755,000 = 188,884.30.

title: Break-even value-in-use cash flow • case 21
prompt: An asset carries at LKR 1,420,000. Its fair value less costs of disposal is lower. A valid VIU model uses THREE equal year-end operating cash inflows, plus 100,000 net disposal proceeds at year three, discounted at 10%. What minimum equal ANNUAL operating cash inflow makes VIU exactly equal carrying amount? Ignore tax and other adjustments.
explanation: Let annual flow be X. X×(1/1.10 + 1/1.10² + 1/1.10³) + 100,000/1.10³ = 1,420,000. Solve for X = 540,791.54. This sensitivity calculation identifies the VIU break-even point.

title: Discounted warranty expected-value portfolio • case 21
prompt: A present warranty obligation covers 1,420 products. Per product, probabilities are 70% no defect, 25% a minor repair costing LKR 400, and 5% a major repair costing 2,000. All expected payments occur exactly in TWO years. Outflow for the portfolio is probable; appropriate discount rate is 10% with no risk double counting. Find the provision.
explanation: Expected cash payment = 1,420×(25%×400 + 5%×2,000) = 284,000.0. Discount two years at 10%: 284,000.0/1.10² = 234,710.74. The probability assessment applies to the portfolio.

title: Provision movement with revised estimate • case 21
prompt: A discounted provision opens at LKR 710,000. Unwinding for a full year is at 8%. A 100,000 settlement occurs at the year END, after unwinding. At that same reporting date, a new estimate increases the remaining provision by 92,000. No other changes occur. Find closing provision.
explanation: Closing = opening + 8% unwinding − year-end settlement + estimate increase: 710,000×1.08 −100,000 +92,000 = 758,800.00. Classification of the estimate change’s counterpart is assessed separately.

title: Revaluation increase after earlier loss • case 21
prompt: PPE carries at LKR 810,000 before revaluation and is revalued to 1,420,000. A prior revaluation decrease on THIS asset of 192,000 was recognised in profit or loss and has not been reversed. No tax effects apply. Find the current increase recognised in OCI after reversing the eligible prior loss in profit or loss.
explanation: Gross increase = 1,420,000 − 810,000 = 610,000. First recognise 192,000 in profit or loss to reverse the prior decrease. Remaining 418,000.00 is OCI revaluation surplus.

title: Nine-month depreciation and disposal gain • case 21
prompt: Equipment cost LKR 1,620,000, residual value 200,000 and useful life five years, straight-line. Two FULL years’ depreciation were recognised before this year. It is sold after nine months of the current year for 1,165,000. It was not previously held for sale and no impairment or revaluation applies. Find disposal GAIN after the required nine-month depreciation.
explanation: Annual depreciation = (1,620,000−200,000)/5. Deduct two full years and another 9/12 year from cost to obtain disposal-date carrying amount 839,000.00. Gain = proceeds − that amount = 326,000.00.

title: Customer collections with a write-off • case 21
prompt: All sales are on credit. Revenue is LKR 4,050,000; opening GROSS trade receivables are 600,000; closing GROSS receivables are 1,010,000. Receivables of 121,000 were written off during the year. There are no taxes, returns, contract balances, acquisitions or exchange changes. Find cash collected from customers.
explanation: Gross receivable roll-forward: opening + credit sales − cash receipts − write-offs = closing. Thus receipts = 4,050,000+600,000−1,010,000−121,000 = 3,519,000.00. Write-offs are not cash receipts.

title: Loan funding net cash effect • case 21
prompt: A company receives cash loan proceeds of LKR 1,420,000 and immediately pays a directly attributable lender issue fee of 30,500. Both payments are classified as financing cash flows in this case. No other cash movement occurs. Find the NET financing cash inflow from these two cash movements; this question does not require net line-item presentation.
explanation: Net financing cash effect = proceeds − cash fee = 1,420,000 − 30,500.00 = 1,389,500.00. Effective-interest amortisation later is not another inception cash payment.

title: Item-by-item NRV without offsetting headroom • case 21
prompt: Two unrelated inventory lines require separate NRV tests. A has 205 units, cost LKR 1,000 and NRV 900 each. B has 142 units, cost 1,000 and NRV 1,200 each. There is no basis to group them for the write-down test. Find TOTAL closing inventory carrying amount.
explanation: Carry A at 900 per unit and B at its lower cost of 1,000. Total = 205×900 + 142×1,000 = 326,500.00. B’s NRV headroom cannot offset A’s write-down.

title: Units-of-production intangible amortisation • case 21
prompt: A finite-life production licence costs LKR 1,320,000, has zero residual value, and is expected to support 150,000 units in total. Actual output this year is 40,500 units. A units-of-production method reliably reflects consumption and the asset was available throughout. No impairment or estimate change applies. Find annual amortisation.
explanation: Apply the supported consumption pattern: amortisation = 1,320,000 × 40,500/150,000 = 356,400.00. It is the share of expected lifetime production consumed, not an automatic straight-line charge.

title: Profit after suspended associate losses • case 21
prompt: An equity-method investment and relevant long-term interests were previously reduced to zero. Unrecognised share of prior losses totals LKR 122,000; the investor has no obligation and made no support payments. In the current year its share of associate profit is 183,000. No other adjustments or changes in interest apply. Find the share of profit that can now be RECOGNISED.
explanation: First absorb unrecognised prior losses before resuming recognised profit. Recognised amount = current profit share 183,000 − prior unrecognised losses 122,000 = 61,000.00.

title: Return recovery asset net of costs • case 22
prompt: A retailer has transferred 1,550 products. It expects 62 to be returned. Each returned product originally cost LKR 600; expected recovery handling is 20 per item and expected value deterioration is 30 per item. Estimates meet the relevant requirements. Find the separate asset for the right to recover returned products, excluding the refund liability.
explanation: Recovery asset = original carrying amount of expected returns less recovery costs and potential value decrease: 62 × (600 − 20 − 30) = 34,100.00. It is assessed separately from the customer refund liability.
family: Return recovery asset net of costs

title: Retrospective volume rebate true-up • case 22
prompt: A customer’s annual purchases reach 12,200 units at list price LKR 200. Crossing the threshold entitles it to a 5% retrospective rebate on ALL units. Cumulative revenue before this new supported estimate equals full list price; no rebate was previously accrued. The constraint permits the estimate. Find the reduction in cumulative revenue required now.
explanation: The revised transaction price reflects the retrospective rebate on all units. Revenue reduction = 12,200 × 200 × 5% = 122,000.00. Recognise the corresponding refund obligation as appropriate.

title: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation • case 22
prompt: A bundle has distinct goods A and B with stand-alone prices LKR 310,000 and 520,000. Total transaction price is 758,000. ALL paragraph 82 criteria demonstrate that the whole 72,000 discount relates only to A. A transfers now; B is not yet delivered. Find revenue recognised for A.
explanation: The specified discount-allocation exception applies. Allocate all 72,000 discount to A: 310,000 − 72,000 = 238,000.00. Do not default to relative allocation when the exception’s criteria are met.
family: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation

title: Three obligations and partial service • case 22
prompt: A contract price of LKR 1,860,000 covers goods A, goods B and twelve months of distinct support. Stand-alone prices are 600,000, 300,000 and 300,000 respectively. A is delivered, B is not, and six months of evenly provided support are complete. No allocation exception applies. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise allocation to A plus half of support: 1,860,000 × (600,000 + 150,000) / 1,200,000 = 1,162,500.00. B’s allocation remains unrecognised as revenue.

title: Progress excluding abnormal waste • case 22
prompt: An over-time contract has transaction price LKR 12,200,000. Costs incurred are 4,880,000, including abnormal waste of 244,000 that does not depict progress. Expected TOTAL productive costs excluding that waste are 9,760,000. Cost-to-cost is appropriate after excluding the waste; no other adjustment applies. Find cumulative revenue, not profit.
explanation: Exclude abnormal waste from the progress numerator. Productive progress = (4,880,000 − 244,000) / 9,760,000. Revenue = transaction price × that progress = 5,795,000.00. The wasted cost is not a revenue-producing input.

title: Uninstalled materials without margin • case 22
prompt: A single over-time construction obligation has price LKR 14,400,000. All B19(b) conditions justify recognising revenue equal to cost for significant uninstalled materials of 2,880,000 already controlled by the customer. Other productive costs incurred are 2,160,000; expected total OTHER costs are 8,640,000. No revenue was previously recognised. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise material revenue without margin: 2,880,000. Recognise the remaining price using other-cost progress: (14,400,000 − 2,880,000) × 2,160,000/8,640,000. Total revenue = 5,760,000.00.

title: Agent commission after collection • case 22
prompt: An intermediary is an AGENT and collects customer cash of LKR 2,100,000 for a completed supplier service. It must remit 88% to the supplier and is entitled to the remaining 12% commission. It controls neither the underlying service nor any distinct extra service, and there is no tax. Find its revenue.
explanation: An agent recognises its fee or commission, not the supplier’s gross billings: 2,100,000 × 12% = 252,000.00. The amount due to the supplier is separately accounted for.

title: Distinct remaining goods blended prospectively • case 22
prompt: At modification, 100 distinct goods remain under an existing contract at LKR 1,220 each. Another 50 distinct goods are added at 976 each. The modification is NOT a separate contract, but remaining goods are distinct from those already transferred, so paragraph 21(a) applies prospectively. Thirty of the remaining goods are then transferred. Find revenue for those thirty.
explanation: Prospective remaining consideration = 100 × 1,220 + 50 × 976. Divide by 150 remaining goods, then multiply by 30 = 34,160.00. Do not retrospectively revise revenue on goods already transferred.

title: FVTPL acquisition expense • case 22
prompt: A financial asset is acquired at fair value LKR 1,240,000 and is classified at FVTPL. Directly attributable broker costs are 31,000, paid separately. No fair-value change occurs immediately after purchase. Find the immediate profit-or-loss expense from acquiring this asset.
explanation: Transaction costs on an FVTPL asset are expensed. Initial asset carrying amount is fair value 1,240,000; immediate acquisition expense is 31,000.00.

title: Collateral cash-shortfall discounting • case 22
prompt: A credit loss scenario has a contractual receipt of LKR 1,550,000 due in one year. The ONLY expected recovery at that same date is collateral sale proceeds of 1,030,000, less sale costs of 72,000. Scenario probability is 100% and original EIR is 10%. Collateral is an integral contractual credit enhancement and not separately recognised. Find discounted ECL.
explanation: One-year shortfall = contractual receipt − net collateral recovery = 1,550,000 − (1,030,000 − 72,000). Discount that shortfall at 10%: 538,181.82. Do not ignore recovery costs or discount only one side of same-date cash flows.

title: Three-band provision matrix • case 22
prompt: Under the simplified lifetime-ECL approach, supported adjusted loss rates are 1% on current receivables of LKR 1,440,000, 5% on past-due balances of 410,000, and 30% on severely overdue balances of 144,000. Rates already include all required forward-looking and discounting effects. Find total loss allowance.
explanation: Apply each appropriate band rate and add: 1,440,000×1% + 410,000×5% + 144,000×30% = 78,100.00. Do not apply one blended band mechanically to all balances.

title: Equity FVOCI profit-or-loss dividend • case 22
prompt: An eligible equity investment has the irrevocable FVOCI election. During the year it gains LKR 164,000 in fair value and earns a dividend of 82,000. Dividend recognition criteria are met and the dividend clearly represents a return on investment, not recovery of cost. There are no other effects. Find income recognised in PROFIT OR LOSS.
explanation: The qualifying dividend of 82,000.00 is profit-or-loss income. The fair-value movement of 164,000 is OCI under this election and is not added to the profit-or-loss amount.

title: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset • case 22
prompt: A loan is sold with full derecognition. Immediately before sale, gross carrying amount is LKR 1,440,000, loss allowance 144,000, and cash proceeds 1,368,000. No accumulated OCI, sale fees or other adjustments exist. Find the derecognition GAIN relative to net carrying amount.
explanation: Net carrying amount = 1,440,000 − 144,000 = 1,296,000. Compare proceeds with that net amount: 1,368,000 − 1,296,000 = 72,000.00 gain. Derecognise both the gross asset and related allowance.
family: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset

title: Non-substantial liability modification gain • case 22
prompt: An amortised-cost liability is modified WITHOUT extinguishment, with no fees. Its carrying amount is LKR 1,220,000. The sole revised payment is 1,403,000 in two years. Original EIR is 10%; the modification is assessed as non-substantial. Find the immediate modification GAIN from recalculating amortised cost at the original EIR.
explanation: Revised amortised cost = 1,403,000/1.10² = 1,159,504.13. Gain = old liability 1,220,000 − revised PV = 60,495.87. The original EIR is retained for this non-extinguishing modification.

title: Credit-risk improvement allowance release • case 22
prompt: A debt asset under the GENERAL ECL model previously had significant credit-risk deterioration and lifetime allowance LKR 144,000. At reporting date the criteria for lifetime ECL are no longer met; required 12-month ECL is 21,000. No write-offs, new assets or other allowance movements occur. Find the impairment reversal in profit or loss.
explanation: When lifetime measurement is no longer required, the general model returns to 12-month ECL. Release the excess allowance: 144,000 − 21,000 = 123,000.00. This is not a receivable under mandatory simplified lifetime ECL.

title: Upstream inventory elimination with tax • case 22
prompt: P and S report profits AFTER their own tax of LKR 2,880,000 and 1,240,000. An upstream inventory sale leaves unrealised profit of 288,000 in group closing inventory. A recoverable DTA is recognised on the full elimination at 30%, with the tax effect in profit or loss. No other consolidation adjustments exist. Find TOTAL consolidated profit, before attribution to owners and NCI.
explanation: Combine separate after-tax profits, eliminate unrealised profit and recognise the recoverable tax benefit: 2,880,000 + 1,240,000 − 288,000 + 86,400.00 = 3,918,400.00. This question asks total group profit, not its attribution.

title: Full-goodwill impairment and owner profit • case 22
prompt: P owns 80% of S all year. Separate after-tax profits are P LKR 2,460,000 and S 920,000. Goodwill is recognised on the FULL-goodwill basis and an impairment of 310,000 is attributable to S’s CGU and allocated 80:20 between owners and NCI. No other adjustments or tax effects apply. Find consolidated profit attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Owners receive 80% of S’s profit and bear 80% of the full-goodwill loss: 2,460,000 + 80% × (920,000 − 310,000) = 2,948,000.00. Do not charge the owners with 100% of this full-goodwill loss.

title: Partial goodwill CGU gross-up • case 22
prompt: P owns 80% of S. Recognised PARTIAL goodwill is LKR 1,152,000; S’s other net assets in the tested CGU carry at 5,760,000. Recoverable amount of the WHOLE CGU is 6,480,000. Gross up goodwill for unrecognised NCI goodwill when testing; the whole impairment falls within grossed-up goodwill. No tax or other adjustments apply. Find impairment actually recognised on group goodwill.
explanation: Grossed-up goodwill = 1,152,000/80% = 1,440,000.00. Whole-CGU impairment = grossed goodwill + other net assets − recoverable amount = 720,000.00. Only the parent’s 80% goodwill portion is recognised, so recorded loss = 576,000.00.
reference: LKAS 36 Appendix C paras C4–C8; SLFRS 10 para B86

title: Consolidated retained earnings bridge • case 22
prompt: P owns 75% of S. At year end P retained earnings are LKR 4,100,000, and S retained earnings 2,660,000. S retained earnings at acquisition were 1,000,000. Cumulative post-acquisition extra FV depreciation is 144,000. A downstream sale by P leaves unrealised profit of 102,000. No tax, goodwill impairment, dividends recognised by P, OCI or other adjustments apply. Find consolidated retained earnings attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Group owners’ retained earnings = parent RE + 75% of adjusted post-acquisition S reserves − the parent’s downstream unrealised profit: 5,135,000.00. Pre-acquisition reserves do not enter post-acquisition group retained earnings.

title: Loss of control and translation reserve • case 22
prompt: P loses control of a foreign subsidiary. Proceeds are LKR 3,080,000; retained interest FV 720,000; NCI carrying amount 410,000; consolidated net assets INCLUDING goodwill 3,260,000. A cumulative translation GAIN of 144,000, entirely attributable to P, must be reclassified to profit or loss on loss of control. No other effects apply. Find total disposal gain including that reclassification.
explanation: Base gain = proceeds + retained FV + NCI − net assets = 950,000.00. Add the parent’s translation gain recycled on disposal: 144,000. Total = 1,094,000.00.
family: Loss of control and translation reserve

title: Residual guarantee expected payment • case 22
prompt: A lessee owes three year-end rentals of LKR 310,000. It guarantees residual value up to 200,000, but the amount EXPECTED to be payable under that guarantee is 52,000 at year three. Discount rate is 10%. No other liability payments exist. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the amount expected to be payable, not automatically the maximum guarantee. Liability = PV of three rentals + 52,000/1.10³ = 809,992.49.

title: Reasonably certain purchase option PV • case 22
prompt: A lease requires three year-end rentals of LKR 260,000, plus a purchase option price of 720,000 payable at year three. Exercise is reasonably certain. Discount rate is 10%. No incentives, other payments or initial prepayments apply. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the reasonably certain purchase price in the liability: PV of rentals + purchase price discounted for three years = 1,187,528.17. Do not omit or leave the future option payment undiscounted.

title: Lease and service component allocation • case 22
prompt: A two-year contract requires bundled payments of LKR 360,000 at each year end. Relative stand-alone prices are equipment lease 200,000 and distinct maintenance 50,000 per year. The lessee does NOT elect to combine components. Lease discount rate is 10%; no other payments exist. Find initial lease liability for the LEASE component only.
explanation: Allocate 200,000/250,000 = 80% of each bundled payment to the lease: 288,000.00. Discount those two lease payments, excluding maintenance, to obtain 499,834.71.

title: Exempt short-term lease rent-free start • case 22
prompt: A twelve-month lease with no purchase option qualifies for the elected short-term exemption. The first three months are rent free, then nine monthly payments of LKR 31,000 are due. The asset is available throughout and straight-line expense is appropriate. Find lease expense for the FIRST six months, ignoring accrual settlement timing.
explanation: Total fixed payments are nine rents. Spread evenly over all twelve months: 31,000 × 9/12 × 6 = 139,500.00. Rent-free months still receive an expense allocation.

title: Sale-and-leaseback rights transferred • case 22
prompt: A transfer qualifies as a sale under SLFRS 15 at fair value LKR 14,400,000; asset carrying amount is 8,200,000. Market-rate leaseback payments have PV 5,760,000. There are no off-market adjustments or variable-payment complications. At inception, what sale gain is recognised for rights TRANSFERRED to the buyer-lessor?
explanation: Total gain = 14,400,000 − 8,200,000 = 6,200,000. Retained-use proportion = lease PV / fair value = 40%. Recognise only the transferred-rights proportion of the gain: 3,720,000.00.

title: Reassessed bargain purchase gain • case 22
prompt: After the required reassessment, final acquisition-date consideration is LKR 2,880,000, NCI fair value is 400,000 and identifiable net assets are 4,320,000. There is no prior holding or other adjustment. Find the bargain purchase gain recognised in profit or loss.
explanation: Net identifiable assets exceed consideration plus NCI: 4,320,000 − 2,880,000 − 400,000 = 1,040,000.00. Reassessment has been completed before recognising the gain.

title: Acquired contingent liability in goodwill • case 22
prompt: Consideration is LKR 4,600,000; NCI FV is 500,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired contingent liability are 3,660,000. The acquired item is a present obligation with reliably measurable FV 310,000 and qualifies for recognition despite non-probable outflow. No tax or other adjustment applies. Find goodwill after recognising it.
explanation: Recognise the qualifying acquired liability: net identifiable assets become 3,660,000 − 310,000. Goodwill = consideration + NCI − adjusted net assets = 1,750,000.00.

title: Separate acquired brand from goodwill • case 22
prompt: Consideration is LKR 4,100,000; NCI FV 600,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired separable brand are 3,480,000. Brand FV is 620,000; tax base is zero and 30% DTL must be recognised. No other adjustments apply. Find goodwill after separate brand and tax recognition.
explanation: An identifiable acquired brand is separate from goodwill. Net addition to identifiable assets = brand FV − 30% DTL = 434,000.00. Goodwill = 4,100,000 + 600,000 − (3,480,000 + 434,000.00) = 786,000.00.

title: Acquisition costs versus issue costs • case 22
prompt: A business acquisition has consideration LKR 2,660,000. Additional costs are acquisition advisory 144,000, qualifying equity-issue costs 70,000 and qualifying debt-issue costs 40,000. The issue costs follow their relevant standards, and no immediate debt-cost amortisation or other expense arises this period. Find the immediate acquisition-related PROFIT-OR-LOSS expense from these costs.
explanation: Expense advisory acquisition costs of 144,000.00. Qualifying equity and debt issuance costs follow their respective standards and are not added to this immediate acquisition-service expense or goodwill.

title: Temporary difference and enacted rate change • case 22
prompt: A taxable temporary difference opens at LKR 200,000 with a DTL measured at 25%. At year end the difference is 410,000 and the enacted rate expected on reversal is 30%. Both the underlying movements and rate change belong in profit or loss. No other tax movements exist. Find deferred tax expense for the year.
explanation: Opening DTL = 200,000×25% = 50,000. Closing DTL = 410,000×30% = 123,000.00. Expense is the full increase, including rate remeasurement: 73,000.00. Rates are exercise assumptions.
family: Temporary difference and enacted rate change

title: Revalued non-depreciable land tax basis • case 22
prompt: Non-depreciable land is revalued from cost LKR 1,440,000 to fair value 2,160,000; tax base remains cost. The enacted rate for recovery through SALE is 20%, while a 30% use rate would otherwise apply. The revaluation and associated tax go to OCI. No other effects exist. Find the net OCI revaluation increase after deferred tax.
explanation: For this non-depreciable revalued asset, measure tax consequences on recovery through sale: DTL = (2,160,000 − 1,440,000)×20%. Net OCI increase = gross uplift less that DTL = 576,000.00.

title: Current tax reconciliation and prepayment • case 22
prompt: Accounting pretax profit is LKR 3,100,000. It includes a permanently non-deductible fine of 144,000, exempt income of 50,000, and warranty expense of 310,000 deductible only on payment. Current-year warranty payments of 80,000 are deductible and were charged against the provision, not current profit. Tax rate is 30%; tax prepayments are 300,000. No other tax adjustments exist. Find closing CURRENT tax payable, not total tax expense.
explanation: Taxable profit = 3,100,000 + fine 144,000 − exempt income 50,000 + provision expense 310,000 − deductible payments 80,000 = 3,424,000. Current tax less prepaid 300,000 = 727,200.00. Deferred tax is separate.

title: Consolidated inventory tax difference • case 22
prompt: After eliminating an intragroup profit, inventory carries in consolidated statements at LKR 864,000. Its tax base in the buyer’s tax jurisdiction is 1,296,000. The buyer’s enacted rate is 30%; sufficient taxable profit is probable. No offsetting, exception or other tax effects apply. Find the consolidated DTA on this inventory.
explanation: The consolidated carrying amount is below tax base, creating a deductible temporary difference of 432,000. Use the buyer’s relevant tax rate: difference ×30% = 129,600.00.

title: Depreciation after recognised impairment • case 22
prompt: Immediately before an impairment, equipment carries at LKR 1,440,000. Recoverable amount is 920,000 and impairment is recognised. After that date it has four years’ remaining useful life and residual value 100,000. Straight-line depreciation is appropriate; no further revaluation or impairment applies. Find depreciation for the next FULL year.
explanation: First reduce the asset to recoverable amount 920,000. Thereafter allocate revised depreciable amount over remaining life: (920,000 − 100,000)/4 = 205,000.00.

title: Allocated headquarters in CGU impairment • case 22
prompt: CGU A carries operating assets of LKR 820,000; CGU B carries 400,000. A headquarters asset of 200,000 can be allocated reasonably and consistently in proportion to those operating-asset amounts. A’s recoverable amount INCLUDING its headquarters share is 760,000. No goodwill or other assets exist. Find the impairment loss for A including its allocation.
explanation: Allocate headquarters to A: 200,000 × 820,000/(820,000+400,000) = 134,426.23. Tested A carrying amount is 954,426.23. Impairment versus recoverable amount 760,000 = 194,426.23.

title: Break-even value-in-use cash flow • case 22
prompt: An asset carries at LKR 1,440,000. Its fair value less costs of disposal is lower. A valid VIU model uses THREE equal year-end operating cash inflows, plus 100,000 net disposal proceeds at year three, discounted at 10%. What minimum equal ANNUAL operating cash inflow makes VIU exactly equal carrying amount? Ignore tax and other adjustments.
explanation: Let annual flow be X. X×(1/1.10 + 1/1.10² + 1/1.10³) + 100,000/1.10³ = 1,440,000. Solve for X = 548,833.84. This sensitivity calculation identifies the VIU break-even point.

title: Discounted warranty expected-value portfolio • case 22
prompt: A present warranty obligation covers 1,440 products. Per product, probabilities are 70% no defect, 25% a minor repair costing LKR 400, and 5% a major repair costing 2,000. All expected payments occur exactly in TWO years. Outflow for the portfolio is probable; appropriate discount rate is 10% with no risk double counting. Find the provision.
explanation: Expected cash payment = 1,440×(25%×400 + 5%×2,000) = 288,000.0. Discount two years at 10%: 288,000.0/1.10² = 238,016.53. The probability assessment applies to the portfolio.

title: Provision movement with revised estimate • case 22
prompt: A discounted provision opens at LKR 720,000. Unwinding for a full year is at 8%. A 100,000 settlement occurs at the year END, after unwinding. At that same reporting date, a new estimate increases the remaining provision by 94,000. No other changes occur. Find closing provision.
explanation: Closing = opening + 8% unwinding − year-end settlement + estimate increase: 720,000×1.08 −100,000 +94,000 = 771,600.00. Classification of the estimate change’s counterpart is assessed separately.

title: Revaluation increase after earlier loss • case 22
prompt: PPE carries at LKR 820,000 before revaluation and is revalued to 1,440,000. A prior revaluation decrease on THIS asset of 194,000 was recognised in profit or loss and has not been reversed. No tax effects apply. Find the current increase recognised in OCI after reversing the eligible prior loss in profit or loss.
explanation: Gross increase = 1,440,000 − 820,000 = 620,000. First recognise 194,000 in profit or loss to reverse the prior decrease. Remaining 426,000.00 is OCI revaluation surplus.

title: Nine-month depreciation and disposal gain • case 22
prompt: Equipment cost LKR 1,640,000, residual value 200,000 and useful life five years, straight-line. Two FULL years’ depreciation were recognised before this year. It is sold after nine months of the current year for 1,180,000. It was not previously held for sale and no impairment or revaluation applies. Find disposal GAIN after the required nine-month depreciation.
explanation: Annual depreciation = (1,640,000−200,000)/5. Deduct two full years and another 9/12 year from cost to obtain disposal-date carrying amount 848,000.00. Gain = proceeds − that amount = 332,000.00.

title: Customer collections with a write-off • case 22
prompt: All sales are on credit. Revenue is LKR 4,100,000; opening GROSS trade receivables are 600,000; closing GROSS receivables are 1,020,000. Receivables of 122,000 were written off during the year. There are no taxes, returns, contract balances, acquisitions or exchange changes. Find cash collected from customers.
explanation: Gross receivable roll-forward: opening + credit sales − cash receipts − write-offs = closing. Thus receipts = 4,100,000+600,000−1,020,000−122,000 = 3,558,000.00. Write-offs are not cash receipts.

title: Loan funding net cash effect • case 22
prompt: A company receives cash loan proceeds of LKR 1,440,000 and immediately pays a directly attributable lender issue fee of 31,000. Both payments are classified as financing cash flows in this case. No other cash movement occurs. Find the NET financing cash inflow from these two cash movements; this question does not require net line-item presentation.
explanation: Net financing cash effect = proceeds − cash fee = 1,440,000 − 31,000.00 = 1,409,000.00. Effective-interest amortisation later is not another inception cash payment.

title: Item-by-item NRV without offsetting headroom • case 22
prompt: Two unrelated inventory lines require separate NRV tests. A has 210 units, cost LKR 1,000 and NRV 900 each. B has 144 units, cost 1,000 and NRV 1,200 each. There is no basis to group them for the write-down test. Find TOTAL closing inventory carrying amount.
explanation: Carry A at 900 per unit and B at its lower cost of 1,000. Total = 210×900 + 144×1,000 = 333,000.00. B’s NRV headroom cannot offset A’s write-down.

title: Units-of-production intangible amortisation • case 22
prompt: A finite-life production licence costs LKR 1,340,000, has zero residual value, and is expected to support 150,000 units in total. Actual output this year is 41,000 units. A units-of-production method reliably reflects consumption and the asset was available throughout. No impairment or estimate change applies. Find annual amortisation.
explanation: Apply the supported consumption pattern: amortisation = 1,340,000 × 41,000/150,000 = 366,266.67. It is the share of expected lifetime production consumed, not an automatic straight-line charge.

title: Profit after suspended associate losses • case 22
prompt: An equity-method investment and relevant long-term interests were previously reduced to zero. Unrecognised share of prior losses totals LKR 124,000; the investor has no obligation and made no support payments. In the current year its share of associate profit is 186,000. No other adjustments or changes in interest apply. Find the share of profit that can now be RECOGNISED.
explanation: First absorb unrecognised prior losses before resuming recognised profit. Recognised amount = current profit share 186,000 − prior unrecognised losses 124,000 = 62,000.00.

title: Return recovery asset net of costs • case 23
prompt: A retailer has transferred 1,575 products. It expects 63 to be returned. Each returned product originally cost LKR 600; expected recovery handling is 20 per item and expected value deterioration is 30 per item. Estimates meet the relevant requirements. Find the separate asset for the right to recover returned products, excluding the refund liability.
explanation: Recovery asset = original carrying amount of expected returns less recovery costs and potential value decrease: 63 × (600 − 20 − 30) = 34,650.00. It is assessed separately from the customer refund liability.
family: Return recovery asset net of costs

title: Retrospective volume rebate true-up • case 23
prompt: A customer’s annual purchases reach 12,300 units at list price LKR 200. Crossing the threshold entitles it to a 5% retrospective rebate on ALL units. Cumulative revenue before this new supported estimate equals full list price; no rebate was previously accrued. The constraint permits the estimate. Find the reduction in cumulative revenue required now.
explanation: The revised transaction price reflects the retrospective rebate on all units. Revenue reduction = 12,300 × 200 × 5% = 123,000.00. Recognise the corresponding refund obligation as appropriate.

title: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation • case 23
prompt: A bundle has distinct goods A and B with stand-alone prices LKR 315,000 and 530,000. Total transaction price is 772,000. ALL paragraph 82 criteria demonstrate that the whole 73,000 discount relates only to A. A transfers now; B is not yet delivered. Find revenue recognised for A.
explanation: The specified discount-allocation exception applies. Allocate all 73,000 discount to A: 315,000 − 73,000 = 242,000.00. Do not default to relative allocation when the exception’s criteria are met.
family: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation

title: Three obligations and partial service • case 23
prompt: A contract price of LKR 1,890,000 covers goods A, goods B and twelve months of distinct support. Stand-alone prices are 600,000, 300,000 and 300,000 respectively. A is delivered, B is not, and six months of evenly provided support are complete. No allocation exception applies. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise allocation to A plus half of support: 1,890,000 × (600,000 + 150,000) / 1,200,000 = 1,181,250.00. B’s allocation remains unrecognised as revenue.

title: Progress excluding abnormal waste • case 23
prompt: An over-time contract has transaction price LKR 12,300,000. Costs incurred are 4,920,000, including abnormal waste of 246,000 that does not depict progress. Expected TOTAL productive costs excluding that waste are 9,840,000. Cost-to-cost is appropriate after excluding the waste; no other adjustment applies. Find cumulative revenue, not profit.
explanation: Exclude abnormal waste from the progress numerator. Productive progress = (4,920,000 − 246,000) / 9,840,000. Revenue = transaction price × that progress = 5,842,500.00. The wasted cost is not a revenue-producing input.

title: Uninstalled materials without margin • case 23
prompt: A single over-time construction obligation has price LKR 14,600,000. All B19(b) conditions justify recognising revenue equal to cost for significant uninstalled materials of 2,920,000 already controlled by the customer. Other productive costs incurred are 2,190,000; expected total OTHER costs are 8,760,000. No revenue was previously recognised. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise material revenue without margin: 2,920,000. Recognise the remaining price using other-cost progress: (14,600,000 − 2,920,000) × 2,190,000/8,760,000. Total revenue = 5,840,000.00.

title: Agent commission after collection • case 23
prompt: An intermediary is an AGENT and collects customer cash of LKR 2,150,000 for a completed supplier service. It must remit 88% to the supplier and is entitled to the remaining 12% commission. It controls neither the underlying service nor any distinct extra service, and there is no tax. Find its revenue.
explanation: An agent recognises its fee or commission, not the supplier’s gross billings: 2,150,000 × 12% = 258,000.00. The amount due to the supplier is separately accounted for.

title: Distinct remaining goods blended prospectively • case 23
prompt: At modification, 100 distinct goods remain under an existing contract at LKR 1,230 each. Another 50 distinct goods are added at 984 each. The modification is NOT a separate contract, but remaining goods are distinct from those already transferred, so paragraph 21(a) applies prospectively. Thirty of the remaining goods are then transferred. Find revenue for those thirty.
explanation: Prospective remaining consideration = 100 × 1,230 + 50 × 984. Divide by 150 remaining goods, then multiply by 30 = 34,440.00. Do not retrospectively revise revenue on goods already transferred.

title: FVTPL acquisition expense • case 23
prompt: A financial asset is acquired at fair value LKR 1,260,000 and is classified at FVTPL. Directly attributable broker costs are 31,500, paid separately. No fair-value change occurs immediately after purchase. Find the immediate profit-or-loss expense from acquiring this asset.
explanation: Transaction costs on an FVTPL asset are expensed. Initial asset carrying amount is fair value 1,260,000; immediate acquisition expense is 31,500.00.

title: Collateral cash-shortfall discounting • case 23
prompt: A credit loss scenario has a contractual receipt of LKR 1,575,000 due in one year. The ONLY expected recovery at that same date is collateral sale proceeds of 1,045,000, less sale costs of 73,000. Scenario probability is 100% and original EIR is 10%. Collateral is an integral contractual credit enhancement and not separately recognised. Find discounted ECL.
explanation: One-year shortfall = contractual receipt − net collateral recovery = 1,575,000 − (1,045,000 − 73,000). Discount that shortfall at 10%: 548,181.82. Do not ignore recovery costs or discount only one side of same-date cash flows.

title: Three-band provision matrix • case 23
prompt: Under the simplified lifetime-ECL approach, supported adjusted loss rates are 1% on current receivables of LKR 1,460,000, 5% on past-due balances of 415,000, and 30% on severely overdue balances of 146,000. Rates already include all required forward-looking and discounting effects. Find total loss allowance.
explanation: Apply each appropriate band rate and add: 1,460,000×1% + 415,000×5% + 146,000×30% = 79,150.00. Do not apply one blended band mechanically to all balances.

title: Equity FVOCI profit-or-loss dividend • case 23
prompt: An eligible equity investment has the irrevocable FVOCI election. During the year it gains LKR 166,000 in fair value and earns a dividend of 83,000. Dividend recognition criteria are met and the dividend clearly represents a return on investment, not recovery of cost. There are no other effects. Find income recognised in PROFIT OR LOSS.
explanation: The qualifying dividend of 83,000.00 is profit-or-loss income. The fair-value movement of 166,000 is OCI under this election and is not added to the profit-or-loss amount.

title: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset • case 23
prompt: A loan is sold with full derecognition. Immediately before sale, gross carrying amount is LKR 1,460,000, loss allowance 146,000, and cash proceeds 1,387,000. No accumulated OCI, sale fees or other adjustments exist. Find the derecognition GAIN relative to net carrying amount.
explanation: Net carrying amount = 1,460,000 − 146,000 = 1,314,000. Compare proceeds with that net amount: 1,387,000 − 1,314,000 = 73,000.00 gain. Derecognise both the gross asset and related allowance.
family: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset

title: Non-substantial liability modification gain • case 23
prompt: An amortised-cost liability is modified WITHOUT extinguishment, with no fees. Its carrying amount is LKR 1,230,000. The sole revised payment is 1,414,500 in two years. Original EIR is 10%; the modification is assessed as non-substantial. Find the immediate modification GAIN from recalculating amortised cost at the original EIR.
explanation: Revised amortised cost = 1,414,500/1.10² = 1,169,008.26. Gain = old liability 1,230,000 − revised PV = 60,991.74. The original EIR is retained for this non-extinguishing modification.

title: Credit-risk improvement allowance release • case 23
prompt: A debt asset under the GENERAL ECL model previously had significant credit-risk deterioration and lifetime allowance LKR 146,000. At reporting date the criteria for lifetime ECL are no longer met; required 12-month ECL is 21,500. No write-offs, new assets or other allowance movements occur. Find the impairment reversal in profit or loss.
explanation: When lifetime measurement is no longer required, the general model returns to 12-month ECL. Release the excess allowance: 146,000 − 21,500 = 124,500.00. This is not a receivable under mandatory simplified lifetime ECL.

title: Upstream inventory elimination with tax • case 23
prompt: P and S report profits AFTER their own tax of LKR 2,920,000 and 1,260,000. An upstream inventory sale leaves unrealised profit of 292,000 in group closing inventory. A recoverable DTA is recognised on the full elimination at 30%, with the tax effect in profit or loss. No other consolidation adjustments exist. Find TOTAL consolidated profit, before attribution to owners and NCI.
explanation: Combine separate after-tax profits, eliminate unrealised profit and recognise the recoverable tax benefit: 2,920,000 + 1,260,000 − 292,000 + 87,600.00 = 3,975,600.00. This question asks total group profit, not its attribution.

title: Full-goodwill impairment and owner profit • case 23
prompt: P owns 80% of S all year. Separate after-tax profits are P LKR 2,490,000 and S 930,000. Goodwill is recognised on the FULL-goodwill basis and an impairment of 315,000 is attributable to S’s CGU and allocated 80:20 between owners and NCI. No other adjustments or tax effects apply. Find consolidated profit attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Owners receive 80% of S’s profit and bear 80% of the full-goodwill loss: 2,490,000 + 80% × (930,000 − 315,000) = 2,982,000.00. Do not charge the owners with 100% of this full-goodwill loss.

title: Partial goodwill CGU gross-up • case 23
prompt: P owns 80% of S. Recognised PARTIAL goodwill is LKR 1,168,000; S’s other net assets in the tested CGU carry at 5,840,000. Recoverable amount of the WHOLE CGU is 6,570,000. Gross up goodwill for unrecognised NCI goodwill when testing; the whole impairment falls within grossed-up goodwill. No tax or other adjustments apply. Find impairment actually recognised on group goodwill.
explanation: Grossed-up goodwill = 1,168,000/80% = 1,460,000.00. Whole-CGU impairment = grossed goodwill + other net assets − recoverable amount = 730,000.00. Only the parent’s 80% goodwill portion is recognised, so recorded loss = 584,000.00.
reference: LKAS 36 Appendix C paras C4–C8; SLFRS 10 para B86

title: Consolidated retained earnings bridge • case 23
prompt: P owns 75% of S. At year end P retained earnings are LKR 4,150,000, and S retained earnings 2,690,000. S retained earnings at acquisition were 1,000,000. Cumulative post-acquisition extra FV depreciation is 146,000. A downstream sale by P leaves unrealised profit of 103,000. No tax, goodwill impairment, dividends recognised by P, OCI or other adjustments apply. Find consolidated retained earnings attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Group owners’ retained earnings = parent RE + 75% of adjusted post-acquisition S reserves − the parent’s downstream unrealised profit: 5,205,000.00. Pre-acquisition reserves do not enter post-acquisition group retained earnings.

title: Loss of control and translation reserve • case 23
prompt: P loses control of a foreign subsidiary. Proceeds are LKR 3,120,000; retained interest FV 730,000; NCI carrying amount 415,000; consolidated net assets INCLUDING goodwill 3,290,000. A cumulative translation GAIN of 146,000, entirely attributable to P, must be reclassified to profit or loss on loss of control. No other effects apply. Find total disposal gain including that reclassification.
explanation: Base gain = proceeds + retained FV + NCI − net assets = 975,000.00. Add the parent’s translation gain recycled on disposal: 146,000. Total = 1,121,000.00.
family: Loss of control and translation reserve

title: Residual guarantee expected payment • case 23
prompt: A lessee owes three year-end rentals of LKR 315,000. It guarantees residual value up to 200,000, but the amount EXPECTED to be payable under that guarantee is 53,000 at year three. Discount rate is 10%. No other liability payments exist. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the amount expected to be payable, not automatically the maximum guarantee. Liability = PV of three rentals + 53,000/1.10³ = 823,178.06.

title: Reasonably certain purchase option PV • case 23
prompt: A lease requires three year-end rentals of LKR 265,000, plus a purchase option price of 730,000 payable at year three. Exercise is reasonably certain. Discount rate is 10%. No incentives, other payments or initial prepayments apply. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the reasonably certain purchase price in the liability: PV of rentals + purchase price discounted for three years = 1,207,475.58. Do not omit or leave the future option payment undiscounted.

title: Lease and service component allocation • case 23
prompt: A two-year contract requires bundled payments of LKR 365,000 at each year end. Relative stand-alone prices are equipment lease 200,000 and distinct maintenance 50,000 per year. The lessee does NOT elect to combine components. Lease discount rate is 10%; no other payments exist. Find initial lease liability for the LEASE component only.
explanation: Allocate 200,000/250,000 = 80% of each bundled payment to the lease: 292,000.00. Discount those two lease payments, excluding maintenance, to obtain 506,776.86.

title: Exempt short-term lease rent-free start • case 23
prompt: A twelve-month lease with no purchase option qualifies for the elected short-term exemption. The first three months are rent free, then nine monthly payments of LKR 31,500 are due. The asset is available throughout and straight-line expense is appropriate. Find lease expense for the FIRST six months, ignoring accrual settlement timing.
explanation: Total fixed payments are nine rents. Spread evenly over all twelve months: 31,500 × 9/12 × 6 = 141,750.00. Rent-free months still receive an expense allocation.

title: Sale-and-leaseback rights transferred • case 23
prompt: A transfer qualifies as a sale under SLFRS 15 at fair value LKR 14,600,000; asset carrying amount is 8,300,000. Market-rate leaseback payments have PV 5,840,000. There are no off-market adjustments or variable-payment complications. At inception, what sale gain is recognised for rights TRANSFERRED to the buyer-lessor?
explanation: Total gain = 14,600,000 − 8,300,000 = 6,300,000. Retained-use proportion = lease PV / fair value = 40%. Recognise only the transferred-rights proportion of the gain: 3,780,000.00.

title: Reassessed bargain purchase gain • case 23
prompt: After the required reassessment, final acquisition-date consideration is LKR 2,920,000, NCI fair value is 400,000 and identifiable net assets are 4,380,000. There is no prior holding or other adjustment. Find the bargain purchase gain recognised in profit or loss.
explanation: Net identifiable assets exceed consideration plus NCI: 4,380,000 − 2,920,000 − 400,000 = 1,060,000.00. Reassessment has been completed before recognising the gain.

title: Acquired contingent liability in goodwill • case 23
prompt: Consideration is LKR 4,650,000; NCI FV is 500,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired contingent liability are 3,690,000. The acquired item is a present obligation with reliably measurable FV 315,000 and qualifies for recognition despite non-probable outflow. No tax or other adjustment applies. Find goodwill after recognising it.
explanation: Recognise the qualifying acquired liability: net identifiable assets become 3,690,000 − 315,000. Goodwill = consideration + NCI − adjusted net assets = 1,775,000.00.

title: Separate acquired brand from goodwill • case 23
prompt: Consideration is LKR 4,150,000; NCI FV 600,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired separable brand are 3,520,000. Brand FV is 630,000; tax base is zero and 30% DTL must be recognised. No other adjustments apply. Find goodwill after separate brand and tax recognition.
explanation: An identifiable acquired brand is separate from goodwill. Net addition to identifiable assets = brand FV − 30% DTL = 441,000.00. Goodwill = 4,150,000 + 600,000 − (3,520,000 + 441,000.00) = 789,000.00.

title: Acquisition costs versus issue costs • case 23
prompt: A business acquisition has consideration LKR 2,690,000. Additional costs are acquisition advisory 146,000, qualifying equity-issue costs 70,000 and qualifying debt-issue costs 40,000. The issue costs follow their relevant standards, and no immediate debt-cost amortisation or other expense arises this period. Find the immediate acquisition-related PROFIT-OR-LOSS expense from these costs.
explanation: Expense advisory acquisition costs of 146,000.00. Qualifying equity and debt issuance costs follow their respective standards and are not added to this immediate acquisition-service expense or goodwill.

title: Temporary difference and enacted rate change • case 23
prompt: A taxable temporary difference opens at LKR 200,000 with a DTL measured at 25%. At year end the difference is 415,000 and the enacted rate expected on reversal is 30%. Both the underlying movements and rate change belong in profit or loss. No other tax movements exist. Find deferred tax expense for the year.
explanation: Opening DTL = 200,000×25% = 50,000. Closing DTL = 415,000×30% = 124,500.00. Expense is the full increase, including rate remeasurement: 74,500.00. Rates are exercise assumptions.
family: Temporary difference and enacted rate change

title: Revalued non-depreciable land tax basis • case 23
prompt: Non-depreciable land is revalued from cost LKR 1,460,000 to fair value 2,190,000; tax base remains cost. The enacted rate for recovery through SALE is 20%, while a 30% use rate would otherwise apply. The revaluation and associated tax go to OCI. No other effects exist. Find the net OCI revaluation increase after deferred tax.
explanation: For this non-depreciable revalued asset, measure tax consequences on recovery through sale: DTL = (2,190,000 − 1,460,000)×20%. Net OCI increase = gross uplift less that DTL = 584,000.00.

title: Current tax reconciliation and prepayment • case 23
prompt: Accounting pretax profit is LKR 3,150,000. It includes a permanently non-deductible fine of 146,000, exempt income of 50,000, and warranty expense of 315,000 deductible only on payment. Current-year warranty payments of 80,000 are deductible and were charged against the provision, not current profit. Tax rate is 30%; tax prepayments are 300,000. No other tax adjustments exist. Find closing CURRENT tax payable, not total tax expense.
explanation: Taxable profit = 3,150,000 + fine 146,000 − exempt income 50,000 + provision expense 315,000 − deductible payments 80,000 = 3,481,000. Current tax less prepaid 300,000 = 744,300.00. Deferred tax is separate.

title: Consolidated inventory tax difference • case 23
prompt: After eliminating an intragroup profit, inventory carries in consolidated statements at LKR 876,000. Its tax base in the buyer’s tax jurisdiction is 1,314,000. The buyer’s enacted rate is 30%; sufficient taxable profit is probable. No offsetting, exception or other tax effects apply. Find the consolidated DTA on this inventory.
explanation: The consolidated carrying amount is below tax base, creating a deductible temporary difference of 438,000. Use the buyer’s relevant tax rate: difference ×30% = 131,400.00.

title: Depreciation after recognised impairment • case 23
prompt: Immediately before an impairment, equipment carries at LKR 1,460,000. Recoverable amount is 930,000 and impairment is recognised. After that date it has four years’ remaining useful life and residual value 100,000. Straight-line depreciation is appropriate; no further revaluation or impairment applies. Find depreciation for the next FULL year.
explanation: First reduce the asset to recoverable amount 930,000. Thereafter allocate revised depreciable amount over remaining life: (930,000 − 100,000)/4 = 207,500.00.

title: Allocated headquarters in CGU impairment • case 23
prompt: CGU A carries operating assets of LKR 830,000; CGU B carries 400,000. A headquarters asset of 200,000 can be allocated reasonably and consistently in proportion to those operating-asset amounts. A’s recoverable amount INCLUDING its headquarters share is 765,000. No goodwill or other assets exist. Find the impairment loss for A including its allocation.
explanation: Allocate headquarters to A: 200,000 × 830,000/(830,000+400,000) = 134,959.35. Tested A carrying amount is 964,959.35. Impairment versus recoverable amount 765,000 = 199,959.35.

title: Break-even value-in-use cash flow • case 23
prompt: An asset carries at LKR 1,460,000. Its fair value less costs of disposal is lower. A valid VIU model uses THREE equal year-end operating cash inflows, plus 100,000 net disposal proceeds at year three, discounted at 10%. What minimum equal ANNUAL operating cash inflow makes VIU exactly equal carrying amount? Ignore tax and other adjustments.
explanation: Let annual flow be X. X×(1/1.10 + 1/1.10² + 1/1.10³) + 100,000/1.10³ = 1,460,000. Solve for X = 556,876.13. This sensitivity calculation identifies the VIU break-even point.

title: Discounted warranty expected-value portfolio • case 23
prompt: A present warranty obligation covers 1,460 products. Per product, probabilities are 70% no defect, 25% a minor repair costing LKR 400, and 5% a major repair costing 2,000. All expected payments occur exactly in TWO years. Outflow for the portfolio is probable; appropriate discount rate is 10% with no risk double counting. Find the provision.
explanation: Expected cash payment = 1,460×(25%×400 + 5%×2,000) = 292,000.0. Discount two years at 10%: 292,000.0/1.10² = 241,322.31. The probability assessment applies to the portfolio.

title: Provision movement with revised estimate • case 23
prompt: A discounted provision opens at LKR 730,000. Unwinding for a full year is at 8%. A 100,000 settlement occurs at the year END, after unwinding. At that same reporting date, a new estimate increases the remaining provision by 96,000. No other changes occur. Find closing provision.
explanation: Closing = opening + 8% unwinding − year-end settlement + estimate increase: 730,000×1.08 −100,000 +96,000 = 784,400.00. Classification of the estimate change’s counterpart is assessed separately.

title: Revaluation increase after earlier loss • case 23
prompt: PPE carries at LKR 830,000 before revaluation and is revalued to 1,460,000. A prior revaluation decrease on THIS asset of 196,000 was recognised in profit or loss and has not been reversed. No tax effects apply. Find the current increase recognised in OCI after reversing the eligible prior loss in profit or loss.
explanation: Gross increase = 1,460,000 − 830,000 = 630,000. First recognise 196,000 in profit or loss to reverse the prior decrease. Remaining 434,000.00 is OCI revaluation surplus.

title: Nine-month depreciation and disposal gain • case 23
prompt: Equipment cost LKR 1,660,000, residual value 200,000 and useful life five years, straight-line. Two FULL years’ depreciation were recognised before this year. It is sold after nine months of the current year for 1,195,000. It was not previously held for sale and no impairment or revaluation applies. Find disposal GAIN after the required nine-month depreciation.
explanation: Annual depreciation = (1,660,000−200,000)/5. Deduct two full years and another 9/12 year from cost to obtain disposal-date carrying amount 857,000.00. Gain = proceeds − that amount = 338,000.00.

title: Customer collections with a write-off • case 23
prompt: All sales are on credit. Revenue is LKR 4,150,000; opening GROSS trade receivables are 600,000; closing GROSS receivables are 1,030,000. Receivables of 123,000 were written off during the year. There are no taxes, returns, contract balances, acquisitions or exchange changes. Find cash collected from customers.
explanation: Gross receivable roll-forward: opening + credit sales − cash receipts − write-offs = closing. Thus receipts = 4,150,000+600,000−1,030,000−123,000 = 3,597,000.00. Write-offs are not cash receipts.

title: Loan funding net cash effect • case 23
prompt: A company receives cash loan proceeds of LKR 1,460,000 and immediately pays a directly attributable lender issue fee of 31,500. Both payments are classified as financing cash flows in this case. No other cash movement occurs. Find the NET financing cash inflow from these two cash movements; this question does not require net line-item presentation.
explanation: Net financing cash effect = proceeds − cash fee = 1,460,000 − 31,500.00 = 1,428,500.00. Effective-interest amortisation later is not another inception cash payment.

title: Item-by-item NRV without offsetting headroom • case 23
prompt: Two unrelated inventory lines require separate NRV tests. A has 215 units, cost LKR 1,000 and NRV 900 each. B has 146 units, cost 1,000 and NRV 1,200 each. There is no basis to group them for the write-down test. Find TOTAL closing inventory carrying amount.
explanation: Carry A at 900 per unit and B at its lower cost of 1,000. Total = 215×900 + 146×1,000 = 339,500.00. B’s NRV headroom cannot offset A’s write-down.

title: Units-of-production intangible amortisation • case 23
prompt: A finite-life production licence costs LKR 1,360,000, has zero residual value, and is expected to support 150,000 units in total. Actual output this year is 41,500 units. A units-of-production method reliably reflects consumption and the asset was available throughout. No impairment or estimate change applies. Find annual amortisation.
explanation: Apply the supported consumption pattern: amortisation = 1,360,000 × 41,500/150,000 = 376,266.67. It is the share of expected lifetime production consumed, not an automatic straight-line charge.

title: Profit after suspended associate losses • case 23
prompt: An equity-method investment and relevant long-term interests were previously reduced to zero. Unrecognised share of prior losses totals LKR 126,000; the investor has no obligation and made no support payments. In the current year its share of associate profit is 189,000. No other adjustments or changes in interest apply. Find the share of profit that can now be RECOGNISED.
explanation: First absorb unrecognised prior losses before resuming recognised profit. Recognised amount = current profit share 189,000 − prior unrecognised losses 126,000 = 63,000.00.

title: Return recovery asset net of costs • case 24
prompt: A retailer has transferred 1,600 products. It expects 64 to be returned. Each returned product originally cost LKR 600; expected recovery handling is 20 per item and expected value deterioration is 30 per item. Estimates meet the relevant requirements. Find the separate asset for the right to recover returned products, excluding the refund liability.
explanation: Recovery asset = original carrying amount of expected returns less recovery costs and potential value decrease: 64 × (600 − 20 − 30) = 35,200.00. It is assessed separately from the customer refund liability.
family: Return recovery asset net of costs

title: Retrospective volume rebate true-up • case 24
prompt: A customer’s annual purchases reach 12,400 units at list price LKR 200. Crossing the threshold entitles it to a 5% retrospective rebate on ALL units. Cumulative revenue before this new supported estimate equals full list price; no rebate was previously accrued. The constraint permits the estimate. Find the reduction in cumulative revenue required now.
explanation: The revised transaction price reflects the retrospective rebate on all units. Revenue reduction = 12,400 × 200 × 5% = 124,000.00. Recognise the corresponding refund obligation as appropriate.

title: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation • case 24
prompt: A bundle has distinct goods A and B with stand-alone prices LKR 320,000 and 540,000. Total transaction price is 786,000. ALL paragraph 82 criteria demonstrate that the whole 74,000 discount relates only to A. A transfers now; B is not yet delivered. Find revenue recognised for A.
explanation: The specified discount-allocation exception applies. Allocate all 74,000 discount to A: 320,000 − 74,000 = 246,000.00. Do not default to relative allocation when the exception’s criteria are met.
family: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation

title: Three obligations and partial service • case 24
prompt: A contract price of LKR 1,920,000 covers goods A, goods B and twelve months of distinct support. Stand-alone prices are 600,000, 300,000 and 300,000 respectively. A is delivered, B is not, and six months of evenly provided support are complete. No allocation exception applies. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise allocation to A plus half of support: 1,920,000 × (600,000 + 150,000) / 1,200,000 = 1,200,000.00. B’s allocation remains unrecognised as revenue.

title: Progress excluding abnormal waste • case 24
prompt: An over-time contract has transaction price LKR 12,400,000. Costs incurred are 4,960,000, including abnormal waste of 248,000 that does not depict progress. Expected TOTAL productive costs excluding that waste are 9,920,000. Cost-to-cost is appropriate after excluding the waste; no other adjustment applies. Find cumulative revenue, not profit.
explanation: Exclude abnormal waste from the progress numerator. Productive progress = (4,960,000 − 248,000) / 9,920,000. Revenue = transaction price × that progress = 5,890,000.00. The wasted cost is not a revenue-producing input.

title: Uninstalled materials without margin • case 24
prompt: A single over-time construction obligation has price LKR 14,800,000. All B19(b) conditions justify recognising revenue equal to cost for significant uninstalled materials of 2,960,000 already controlled by the customer. Other productive costs incurred are 2,220,000; expected total OTHER costs are 8,880,000. No revenue was previously recognised. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise material revenue without margin: 2,960,000. Recognise the remaining price using other-cost progress: (14,800,000 − 2,960,000) × 2,220,000/8,880,000. Total revenue = 5,920,000.00.

title: Agent commission after collection • case 24
prompt: An intermediary is an AGENT and collects customer cash of LKR 2,200,000 for a completed supplier service. It must remit 88% to the supplier and is entitled to the remaining 12% commission. It controls neither the underlying service nor any distinct extra service, and there is no tax. Find its revenue.
explanation: An agent recognises its fee or commission, not the supplier’s gross billings: 2,200,000 × 12% = 264,000.00. The amount due to the supplier is separately accounted for.

title: Distinct remaining goods blended prospectively • case 24
prompt: At modification, 100 distinct goods remain under an existing contract at LKR 1,240 each. Another 50 distinct goods are added at 992 each. The modification is NOT a separate contract, but remaining goods are distinct from those already transferred, so paragraph 21(a) applies prospectively. Thirty of the remaining goods are then transferred. Find revenue for those thirty.
explanation: Prospective remaining consideration = 100 × 1,240 + 50 × 992. Divide by 150 remaining goods, then multiply by 30 = 34,720.00. Do not retrospectively revise revenue on goods already transferred.

title: FVTPL acquisition expense • case 24
prompt: A financial asset is acquired at fair value LKR 1,280,000 and is classified at FVTPL. Directly attributable broker costs are 32,000, paid separately. No fair-value change occurs immediately after purchase. Find the immediate profit-or-loss expense from acquiring this asset.
explanation: Transaction costs on an FVTPL asset are expensed. Initial asset carrying amount is fair value 1,280,000; immediate acquisition expense is 32,000.00.

title: Collateral cash-shortfall discounting • case 24
prompt: A credit loss scenario has a contractual receipt of LKR 1,600,000 due in one year. The ONLY expected recovery at that same date is collateral sale proceeds of 1,060,000, less sale costs of 74,000. Scenario probability is 100% and original EIR is 10%. Collateral is an integral contractual credit enhancement and not separately recognised. Find discounted ECL.
explanation: One-year shortfall = contractual receipt − net collateral recovery = 1,600,000 − (1,060,000 − 74,000). Discount that shortfall at 10%: 558,181.82. Do not ignore recovery costs or discount only one side of same-date cash flows.

title: Three-band provision matrix • case 24
prompt: Under the simplified lifetime-ECL approach, supported adjusted loss rates are 1% on current receivables of LKR 1,480,000, 5% on past-due balances of 420,000, and 30% on severely overdue balances of 148,000. Rates already include all required forward-looking and discounting effects. Find total loss allowance.
explanation: Apply each appropriate band rate and add: 1,480,000×1% + 420,000×5% + 148,000×30% = 80,200.00. Do not apply one blended band mechanically to all balances.

title: Equity FVOCI profit-or-loss dividend • case 24
prompt: An eligible equity investment has the irrevocable FVOCI election. During the year it gains LKR 168,000 in fair value and earns a dividend of 84,000. Dividend recognition criteria are met and the dividend clearly represents a return on investment, not recovery of cost. There are no other effects. Find income recognised in PROFIT OR LOSS.
explanation: The qualifying dividend of 84,000.00 is profit-or-loss income. The fair-value movement of 168,000 is OCI under this election and is not added to the profit-or-loss amount.

title: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset • case 24
prompt: A loan is sold with full derecognition. Immediately before sale, gross carrying amount is LKR 1,480,000, loss allowance 148,000, and cash proceeds 1,406,000. No accumulated OCI, sale fees or other adjustments exist. Find the derecognition GAIN relative to net carrying amount.
explanation: Net carrying amount = 1,480,000 − 148,000 = 1,332,000. Compare proceeds with that net amount: 1,406,000 − 1,332,000 = 74,000.00 gain. Derecognise both the gross asset and related allowance.
family: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset

title: Non-substantial liability modification gain • case 24
prompt: An amortised-cost liability is modified WITHOUT extinguishment, with no fees. Its carrying amount is LKR 1,240,000. The sole revised payment is 1,426,000 in two years. Original EIR is 10%; the modification is assessed as non-substantial. Find the immediate modification GAIN from recalculating amortised cost at the original EIR.
explanation: Revised amortised cost = 1,426,000/1.10² = 1,178,512.40. Gain = old liability 1,240,000 − revised PV = 61,487.60. The original EIR is retained for this non-extinguishing modification.

title: Credit-risk improvement allowance release • case 24
prompt: A debt asset under the GENERAL ECL model previously had significant credit-risk deterioration and lifetime allowance LKR 148,000. At reporting date the criteria for lifetime ECL are no longer met; required 12-month ECL is 22,000. No write-offs, new assets or other allowance movements occur. Find the impairment reversal in profit or loss.
explanation: When lifetime measurement is no longer required, the general model returns to 12-month ECL. Release the excess allowance: 148,000 − 22,000 = 126,000.00. This is not a receivable under mandatory simplified lifetime ECL.

title: Upstream inventory elimination with tax • case 24
prompt: P and S report profits AFTER their own tax of LKR 2,960,000 and 1,280,000. An upstream inventory sale leaves unrealised profit of 296,000 in group closing inventory. A recoverable DTA is recognised on the full elimination at 30%, with the tax effect in profit or loss. No other consolidation adjustments exist. Find TOTAL consolidated profit, before attribution to owners and NCI.
explanation: Combine separate after-tax profits, eliminate unrealised profit and recognise the recoverable tax benefit: 2,960,000 + 1,280,000 − 296,000 + 88,800.00 = 4,032,800.00. This question asks total group profit, not its attribution.

title: Full-goodwill impairment and owner profit • case 24
prompt: P owns 80% of S all year. Separate after-tax profits are P LKR 2,520,000 and S 940,000. Goodwill is recognised on the FULL-goodwill basis and an impairment of 320,000 is attributable to S’s CGU and allocated 80:20 between owners and NCI. No other adjustments or tax effects apply. Find consolidated profit attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Owners receive 80% of S’s profit and bear 80% of the full-goodwill loss: 2,520,000 + 80% × (940,000 − 320,000) = 3,016,000.00. Do not charge the owners with 100% of this full-goodwill loss.

title: Partial goodwill CGU gross-up • case 24
prompt: P owns 80% of S. Recognised PARTIAL goodwill is LKR 1,184,000; S’s other net assets in the tested CGU carry at 5,920,000. Recoverable amount of the WHOLE CGU is 6,660,000. Gross up goodwill for unrecognised NCI goodwill when testing; the whole impairment falls within grossed-up goodwill. No tax or other adjustments apply. Find impairment actually recognised on group goodwill.
explanation: Grossed-up goodwill = 1,184,000/80% = 1,480,000.00. Whole-CGU impairment = grossed goodwill + other net assets − recoverable amount = 740,000.00. Only the parent’s 80% goodwill portion is recognised, so recorded loss = 592,000.00.
reference: LKAS 36 Appendix C paras C4–C8; SLFRS 10 para B86

title: Consolidated retained earnings bridge • case 24
prompt: P owns 75% of S. At year end P retained earnings are LKR 4,200,000, and S retained earnings 2,720,000. S retained earnings at acquisition were 1,000,000. Cumulative post-acquisition extra FV depreciation is 148,000. A downstream sale by P leaves unrealised profit of 104,000. No tax, goodwill impairment, dividends recognised by P, OCI or other adjustments apply. Find consolidated retained earnings attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Group owners’ retained earnings = parent RE + 75% of adjusted post-acquisition S reserves − the parent’s downstream unrealised profit: 5,275,000.00. Pre-acquisition reserves do not enter post-acquisition group retained earnings.

title: Loss of control and translation reserve • case 24
prompt: P loses control of a foreign subsidiary. Proceeds are LKR 3,160,000; retained interest FV 740,000; NCI carrying amount 420,000; consolidated net assets INCLUDING goodwill 3,320,000. A cumulative translation GAIN of 148,000, entirely attributable to P, must be reclassified to profit or loss on loss of control. No other effects apply. Find total disposal gain including that reclassification.
explanation: Base gain = proceeds + retained FV + NCI − net assets = 1,000,000.00. Add the parent’s translation gain recycled on disposal: 148,000. Total = 1,148,000.00.
family: Loss of control and translation reserve

title: Residual guarantee expected payment • case 24
prompt: A lessee owes three year-end rentals of LKR 320,000. It guarantees residual value up to 200,000, but the amount EXPECTED to be payable under that guarantee is 54,000 at year three. Discount rate is 10%. No other liability payments exist. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the amount expected to be payable, not automatically the maximum guarantee. Liability = PV of three rentals + 54,000/1.10³ = 836,363.64.

title: Reasonably certain purchase option PV • case 24
prompt: A lease requires three year-end rentals of LKR 270,000, plus a purchase option price of 740,000 payable at year three. Exercise is reasonably certain. Discount rate is 10%. No incentives, other payments or initial prepayments apply. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the reasonably certain purchase price in the liability: PV of rentals + purchase price discounted for three years = 1,227,422.99. Do not omit or leave the future option payment undiscounted.

title: Lease and service component allocation • case 24
prompt: A two-year contract requires bundled payments of LKR 370,000 at each year end. Relative stand-alone prices are equipment lease 200,000 and distinct maintenance 50,000 per year. The lessee does NOT elect to combine components. Lease discount rate is 10%; no other payments exist. Find initial lease liability for the LEASE component only.
explanation: Allocate 200,000/250,000 = 80% of each bundled payment to the lease: 296,000.00. Discount those two lease payments, excluding maintenance, to obtain 513,719.01.

title: Exempt short-term lease rent-free start • case 24
prompt: A twelve-month lease with no purchase option qualifies for the elected short-term exemption. The first three months are rent free, then nine monthly payments of LKR 32,000 are due. The asset is available throughout and straight-line expense is appropriate. Find lease expense for the FIRST six months, ignoring accrual settlement timing.
explanation: Total fixed payments are nine rents. Spread evenly over all twelve months: 32,000 × 9/12 × 6 = 144,000.00. Rent-free months still receive an expense allocation.

title: Sale-and-leaseback rights transferred • case 24
prompt: A transfer qualifies as a sale under SLFRS 15 at fair value LKR 14,800,000; asset carrying amount is 8,400,000. Market-rate leaseback payments have PV 5,920,000.
