There are no off-market adjustments or variable-payment complications. At inception, what sale gain is recognised for rights TRANSFERRED to the buyer-lessor?
explanation: Total gain = 14,800,000 − 8,400,000 = 6,400,000. Retained-use proportion = lease PV / fair value = 40%. Recognise only the transferred-rights proportion of the gain: 3,840,000.00.

title: Reassessed bargain purchase gain • case 24
prompt: After the required reassessment, final acquisition-date consideration is LKR 2,960,000, NCI fair value is 400,000 and identifiable net assets are 4,440,000. There is no prior holding or other adjustment. Find the bargain purchase gain recognised in profit or loss.
explanation: Net identifiable assets exceed consideration plus NCI: 4,440,000 − 2,960,000 − 400,000 = 1,080,000.00. Reassessment has been completed before recognising the gain.

title: Acquired contingent liability in goodwill • case 24
prompt: Consideration is LKR 4,700,000; NCI FV is 500,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired contingent liability are 3,720,000. The acquired item is a present obligation with reliably measurable FV 320,000 and qualifies for recognition despite non-probable outflow. No tax or other adjustment applies. Find goodwill after recognising it.
explanation: Recognise the qualifying acquired liability: net identifiable assets become 3,720,000 − 320,000. Goodwill = consideration + NCI − adjusted net assets = 1,800,000.00.

title: Separate acquired brand from goodwill • case 24
prompt: Consideration is LKR 4,200,000; NCI FV 600,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired separable brand are 3,560,000. Brand FV is 640,000; tax base is zero and 30% DTL must be recognised. No other adjustments apply. Find goodwill after separate brand and tax recognition.
explanation: An identifiable acquired brand is separate from goodwill. Net addition to identifiable assets = brand FV − 30% DTL = 448,000.00. Goodwill = 4,200,000 + 600,000 − (3,560,000 + 448,000.00) = 792,000.00.

title: Acquisition costs versus issue costs • case 24
prompt: A business acquisition has consideration LKR 2,720,000. Additional costs are acquisition advisory 148,000, qualifying equity-issue costs 70,000 and qualifying debt-issue costs 40,000. The issue costs follow their relevant standards, and no immediate debt-cost amortisation or other expense arises this period. Find the immediate acquisition-related PROFIT-OR-LOSS expense from these costs.
explanation: Expense advisory acquisition costs of 148,000.00. Qualifying equity and debt issuance costs follow their respective standards and are not added to this immediate acquisition-service expense or goodwill.

title: Temporary difference and enacted rate change • case 24
prompt: A taxable temporary difference opens at LKR 200,000 with a DTL measured at 25%. At year end the difference is 420,000 and the enacted rate expected on reversal is 30%. Both the underlying movements and rate change belong in profit or loss. No other tax movements exist. Find deferred tax expense for the year.
explanation: Opening DTL = 200,000×25% = 50,000. Closing DTL = 420,000×30% = 126,000.00. Expense is the full increase, including rate remeasurement: 76,000.00. Rates are exercise assumptions.
family: Temporary difference and enacted rate change

title: Revalued non-depreciable land tax basis • case 24
prompt: Non-depreciable land is revalued from cost LKR 1,480,000 to fair value 2,220,000; tax base remains cost. The enacted rate for recovery through SALE is 20%, while a 30% use rate would otherwise apply. The revaluation and associated tax go to OCI. No other effects exist. Find the net OCI revaluation increase after deferred tax.
explanation: For this non-depreciable revalued asset, measure tax consequences on recovery through sale: DTL = (2,220,000 − 1,480,000)×20%. Net OCI increase = gross uplift less that DTL = 592,000.00.

title: Current tax reconciliation and prepayment • case 24
prompt: Accounting pretax profit is LKR 3,200,000. It includes a permanently non-deductible fine of 148,000, exempt income of 50,000, and warranty expense of 320,000 deductible only on payment. Current-year warranty payments of 80,000 are deductible and were charged against the provision, not current profit. Tax rate is 30%; tax prepayments are 300,000. No other tax adjustments exist. Find closing CURRENT tax payable, not total tax expense.
explanation: Taxable profit = 3,200,000 + fine 148,000 − exempt income 50,000 + provision expense 320,000 − deductible payments 80,000 = 3,538,000. Current tax less prepaid 300,000 = 761,400.00. Deferred tax is separate.

title: Consolidated inventory tax difference • case 24
prompt: After eliminating an intragroup profit, inventory carries in consolidated statements at LKR 888,000. Its tax base in the buyer’s tax jurisdiction is 1,332,000. The buyer’s enacted rate is 30%; sufficient taxable profit is probable. No offsetting, exception or other tax effects apply. Find the consolidated DTA on this inventory.
explanation: The consolidated carrying amount is below tax base, creating a deductible temporary difference of 444,000. Use the buyer’s relevant tax rate: difference ×30% = 133,200.00.

title: Depreciation after recognised impairment • case 24
prompt: Immediately before an impairment, equipment carries at LKR 1,480,000. Recoverable amount is 940,000 and impairment is recognised. After that date it has four years’ remaining useful life and residual value 100,000. Straight-line depreciation is appropriate; no further revaluation or impairment applies. Find depreciation for the next FULL year.
explanation: First reduce the asset to recoverable amount 940,000. Thereafter allocate revised depreciable amount over remaining life: (940,000 − 100,000)/4 = 210,000.00.

title: Allocated headquarters in CGU impairment • case 24
prompt: CGU A carries operating assets of LKR 840,000; CGU B carries 400,000. A headquarters asset of 200,000 can be allocated reasonably and consistently in proportion to those operating-asset amounts. A’s recoverable amount INCLUDING its headquarters share is 770,000. No goodwill or other assets exist. Find the impairment loss for A including its allocation.
explanation: Allocate headquarters to A: 200,000 × 840,000/(840,000+400,000) = 135,483.87. Tested A carrying amount is 975,483.87. Impairment versus recoverable amount 770,000 = 205,483.87.

title: Break-even value-in-use cash flow • case 24
prompt: An asset carries at LKR 1,480,000. Its fair value less costs of disposal is lower. A valid VIU model uses THREE equal year-end operating cash inflows, plus 100,000 net disposal proceeds at year three, discounted at 10%. What minimum equal ANNUAL operating cash inflow makes VIU exactly equal carrying amount? Ignore tax and other adjustments.
explanation: Let annual flow be X. X×(1/1.10 + 1/1.10² + 1/1.10³) + 100,000/1.10³ = 1,480,000. Solve for X = 564,918.43. This sensitivity calculation identifies the VIU break-even point.

title: Discounted warranty expected-value portfolio • case 24
prompt: A present warranty obligation covers 1,480 products. Per product, probabilities are 70% no defect, 25% a minor repair costing LKR 400, and 5% a major repair costing 2,000. All expected payments occur exactly in TWO years. Outflow for the portfolio is probable; appropriate discount rate is 10% with no risk double counting. Find the provision.
explanation: Expected cash payment = 1,480×(25%×400 + 5%×2,000) = 296,000.0. Discount two years at 10%: 296,000.0/1.10² = 244,628.10. The probability assessment applies to the portfolio.

title: Provision movement with revised estimate • case 24
prompt: A discounted provision opens at LKR 740,000. Unwinding for a full year is at 8%. A 100,000 settlement occurs at the year END, after unwinding. At that same reporting date, a new estimate increases the remaining provision by 98,000. No other changes occur. Find closing provision.
explanation: Closing = opening + 8% unwinding − year-end settlement + estimate increase: 740,000×1.08 −100,000 +98,000 = 797,200.00. Classification of the estimate change’s counterpart is assessed separately.

title: Revaluation increase after earlier loss • case 24
prompt: PPE carries at LKR 840,000 before revaluation and is revalued to 1,480,000. A prior revaluation decrease on THIS asset of 198,000 was recognised in profit or loss and has not been reversed. No tax effects apply. Find the current increase recognised in OCI after reversing the eligible prior loss in profit or loss.
explanation: Gross increase = 1,480,000 − 840,000 = 640,000. First recognise 198,000 in profit or loss to reverse the prior decrease. Remaining 442,000.00 is OCI revaluation surplus.

title: Nine-month depreciation and disposal gain • case 24
prompt: Equipment cost LKR 1,680,000, residual value 200,000 and useful life five years, straight-line. Two FULL years’ depreciation were recognised before this year. It is sold after nine months of the current year for 1,210,000. It was not previously held for sale and no impairment or revaluation applies. Find disposal GAIN after the required nine-month depreciation.
explanation: Annual depreciation = (1,680,000−200,000)/5. Deduct two full years and another 9/12 year from cost to obtain disposal-date carrying amount 866,000.00. Gain = proceeds − that amount = 344,000.00.

title: Customer collections with a write-off • case 24
prompt: All sales are on credit. Revenue is LKR 4,200,000; opening GROSS trade receivables are 600,000; closing GROSS receivables are 1,040,000. Receivables of 124,000 were written off during the year. There are no taxes, returns, contract balances, acquisitions or exchange changes. Find cash collected from customers.
explanation: Gross receivable roll-forward: opening + credit sales − cash receipts − write-offs = closing. Thus receipts = 4,200,000+600,000−1,040,000−124,000 = 3,636,000.00. Write-offs are not cash receipts.

title: Loan funding net cash effect • case 24
prompt: A company receives cash loan proceeds of LKR 1,480,000 and immediately pays a directly attributable lender issue fee of 32,000. Both payments are classified as financing cash flows in this case. No other cash movement occurs. Find the NET financing cash inflow from these two cash movements; this question does not require net line-item presentation.
explanation: Net financing cash effect = proceeds − cash fee = 1,480,000 − 32,000.00 = 1,448,000.00. Effective-interest amortisation later is not another inception cash payment.

title: Item-by-item NRV without offsetting headroom • case 24
prompt: Two unrelated inventory lines require separate NRV tests. A has 220 units, cost LKR 1,000 and NRV 900 each. B has 148 units, cost 1,000 and NRV 1,200 each. There is no basis to group them for the write-down test. Find TOTAL closing inventory carrying amount.
explanation: Carry A at 900 per unit and B at its lower cost of 1,000. Total = 220×900 + 148×1,000 = 346,000.00. B’s NRV headroom cannot offset A’s write-down.

title: Units-of-production intangible amortisation • case 24
prompt: A finite-life production licence costs LKR 1,380,000, has zero residual value, and is expected to support 150,000 units in total. Actual output this year is 42,000 units. A units-of-production method reliably reflects consumption and the asset was available throughout. No impairment or estimate change applies. Find annual amortisation.
explanation: Apply the supported consumption pattern: amortisation = 1,380,000 × 42,000/150,000 = 386,400.00. It is the share of expected lifetime production consumed, not an automatic straight-line charge.

title: Profit after suspended associate losses • case 24
prompt: An equity-method investment and relevant long-term interests were previously reduced to zero. Unrecognised share of prior losses totals LKR 128,000; the investor has no obligation and made no support payments. In the current year its share of associate profit is 192,000. No other adjustments or changes in interest apply. Find the share of profit that can now be RECOGNISED.
explanation: First absorb unrecognised prior losses before resuming recognised profit. Recognised amount = current profit share 192,000 − prior unrecognised losses 128,000 = 64,000.00.

title: Return recovery asset net of costs • case 25
prompt: A retailer has transferred 1,625 products. It expects 65 to be returned. Each returned product originally cost LKR 600; expected recovery handling is 20 per item and expected value deterioration is 30 per item. Estimates meet the relevant requirements. Find the separate asset for the right to recover returned products, excluding the refund liability.
explanation: Recovery asset = original carrying amount of expected returns less recovery costs and potential value decrease: 65 × (600 − 20 − 30) = 35,750.00. It is assessed separately from the customer refund liability.
family: Return recovery asset net of costs

title: Retrospective volume rebate true-up • case 25
prompt: A customer’s annual purchases reach 12,500 units at list price LKR 200. Crossing the threshold entitles it to a 5% retrospective rebate on ALL units. Cumulative revenue before this new supported estimate equals full list price; no rebate was previously accrued. The constraint permits the estimate. Find the reduction in cumulative revenue required now.
explanation: The revised transaction price reflects the retrospective rebate on all units. Revenue reduction = 12,500 × 200 × 5% = 125,000.00. Recognise the corresponding refund obligation as appropriate.

title: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation • case 25
prompt: A bundle has distinct goods A and B with stand-alone prices LKR 325,000 and 550,000. Total transaction price is 800,000. ALL paragraph 82 criteria demonstrate that the whole 75,000 discount relates only to A. A transfers now; B is not yet delivered. Find revenue recognised for A.
explanation: The specified discount-allocation exception applies. Allocate all 75,000 discount to A: 325,000 − 75,000 = 250,000.00. Do not default to relative allocation when the exception’s criteria are met.
family: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation

title: Three obligations and partial service • case 25
prompt: A contract price of LKR 1,950,000 covers goods A, goods B and twelve months of distinct support. Stand-alone prices are 600,000, 300,000 and 300,000 respectively. A is delivered, B is not, and six months of evenly provided support are complete. No allocation exception applies. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise allocation to A plus half of support: 1,950,000 × (600,000 + 150,000) / 1,200,000 = 1,218,750.00. B’s allocation remains unrecognised as revenue.

title: Progress excluding abnormal waste • case 25
prompt: An over-time contract has transaction price LKR 12,500,000. Costs incurred are 5,000,000, including abnormal waste of 250,000 that does not depict progress. Expected TOTAL productive costs excluding that waste are 10,000,000. Cost-to-cost is appropriate after excluding the waste; no other adjustment applies. Find cumulative revenue, not profit.
explanation: Exclude abnormal waste from the progress numerator. Productive progress = (5,000,000 − 250,000) / 10,000,000. Revenue = transaction price × that progress = 5,937,500.00. The wasted cost is not a revenue-producing input.

title: Uninstalled materials without margin • case 25
prompt: A single over-time construction obligation has price LKR 15,000,000. All B19(b) conditions justify recognising revenue equal to cost for significant uninstalled materials of 3,000,000 already controlled by the customer. Other productive costs incurred are 2,250,000; expected total OTHER costs are 9,000,000. No revenue was previously recognised. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise material revenue without margin: 3,000,000. Recognise the remaining price using other-cost progress: (15,000,000 − 3,000,000) × 2,250,000/9,000,000. Total revenue = 6,000,000.00.

title: Agent commission after collection • case 25
prompt: An intermediary is an AGENT and collects customer cash of LKR 2,250,000 for a completed supplier service. It must remit 88% to the supplier and is entitled to the remaining 12% commission. It controls neither the underlying service nor any distinct extra service, and there is no tax. Find its revenue.
explanation: An agent recognises its fee or commission, not the supplier’s gross billings: 2,250,000 × 12% = 270,000.00. The amount due to the supplier is separately accounted for.

title: Distinct remaining goods blended prospectively • case 25
prompt: At modification, 100 distinct goods remain under an existing contract at LKR 1,250 each. Another 50 distinct goods are added at 1,000 each. The modification is NOT a separate contract, but remaining goods are distinct from those already transferred, so paragraph 21(a) applies prospectively. Thirty of the remaining goods are then transferred. Find revenue for those thirty.
explanation: Prospective remaining consideration = 100 × 1,250 + 50 × 1,000. Divide by 150 remaining goods, then multiply by 30 = 35,000.00. Do not retrospectively revise revenue on goods already transferred.

title: FVTPL acquisition expense • case 25
prompt: A financial asset is acquired at fair value LKR 1,300,000 and is classified at FVTPL. Directly attributable broker costs are 32,500, paid separately. No fair-value change occurs immediately after purchase. Find the immediate profit-or-loss expense from acquiring this asset.
explanation: Transaction costs on an FVTPL asset are expensed. Initial asset carrying amount is fair value 1,300,000; immediate acquisition expense is 32,500.00.

title: Collateral cash-shortfall discounting • case 25
prompt: A credit loss scenario has a contractual receipt of LKR 1,625,000 due in one year. The ONLY expected recovery at that same date is collateral sale proceeds of 1,075,000, less sale costs of 75,000. Scenario probability is 100% and original EIR is 10%. Collateral is an integral contractual credit enhancement and not separately recognised. Find discounted ECL.
explanation: One-year shortfall = contractual receipt − net collateral recovery = 1,625,000 − (1,075,000 − 75,000). Discount that shortfall at 10%: 568,181.82. Do not ignore recovery costs or discount only one side of same-date cash flows.

title: Three-band provision matrix • case 25
prompt: Under the simplified lifetime-ECL approach, supported adjusted loss rates are 1% on current receivables of LKR 1,500,000, 5% on past-due balances of 425,000, and 30% on severely overdue balances of 150,000. Rates already include all required forward-looking and discounting effects. Find total loss allowance.
explanation: Apply each appropriate band rate and add: 1,500,000×1% + 425,000×5% + 150,000×30% = 81,250.00. Do not apply one blended band mechanically to all balances.

title: Equity FVOCI profit-or-loss dividend • case 25
prompt: An eligible equity investment has the irrevocable FVOCI election. During the year it gains LKR 170,000 in fair value and earns a dividend of 85,000. Dividend recognition criteria are met and the dividend clearly represents a return on investment, not recovery of cost. There are no other effects. Find income recognised in PROFIT OR LOSS.
explanation: The qualifying dividend of 85,000.00 is profit-or-loss income. The fair-value movement of 170,000 is OCI under this election and is not added to the profit-or-loss amount.

title: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset • case 25
prompt: A loan is sold with full derecognition. Immediately before sale, gross carrying amount is LKR 1,500,000, loss allowance 150,000, and cash proceeds 1,425,000. No accumulated OCI, sale fees or other adjustments exist. Find the derecognition GAIN relative to net carrying amount.
explanation: Net carrying amount = 1,500,000 − 150,000 = 1,350,000. Compare proceeds with that net amount: 1,425,000 − 1,350,000 = 75,000.00 gain. Derecognise both the gross asset and related allowance.
family: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset

title: Non-substantial liability modification gain • case 25
prompt: An amortised-cost liability is modified WITHOUT extinguishment, with no fees. Its carrying amount is LKR 1,250,000. The sole revised payment is 1,437,500 in two years. Original EIR is 10%; the modification is assessed as non-substantial. Find the immediate modification GAIN from recalculating amortised cost at the original EIR.
explanation: Revised amortised cost = 1,437,500/1.10² = 1,188,016.53. Gain = old liability 1,250,000 − revised PV = 61,983.47. The original EIR is retained for this non-extinguishing modification.

title: Credit-risk improvement allowance release • case 25
prompt: A debt asset under the GENERAL ECL model previously had significant credit-risk deterioration and lifetime allowance LKR 150,000. At reporting date the criteria for lifetime ECL are no longer met; required 12-month ECL is 22,500. No write-offs, new assets or other allowance movements occur. Find the impairment reversal in profit or loss.
explanation: When lifetime measurement is no longer required, the general model returns to 12-month ECL. Release the excess allowance: 150,000 − 22,500 = 127,500.00. This is not a receivable under mandatory simplified lifetime ECL.

title: Upstream inventory elimination with tax • case 25
prompt: P and S report profits AFTER their own tax of LKR 3,000,000 and 1,300,000. An upstream inventory sale leaves unrealised profit of 300,000 in group closing inventory. A recoverable DTA is recognised on the full elimination at 30%, with the tax effect in profit or loss. No other consolidation adjustments exist. Find TOTAL consolidated profit, before attribution to owners and NCI.
explanation: Combine separate after-tax profits, eliminate unrealised profit and recognise the recoverable tax benefit: 3,000,000 + 1,300,000 − 300,000 + 90,000.00 = 4,090,000.00. This question asks total group profit, not its attribution.

title: Full-goodwill impairment and owner profit • case 25
prompt: P owns 80% of S all year. Separate after-tax profits are P LKR 2,550,000 and S 950,000. Goodwill is recognised on the FULL-goodwill basis and an impairment of 325,000 is attributable to S’s CGU and allocated 80:20 between owners and NCI. No other adjustments or tax effects apply. Find consolidated profit attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Owners receive 80% of S’s profit and bear 80% of the full-goodwill loss: 2,550,000 + 80% × (950,000 − 325,000) = 3,050,000.00. Do not charge the owners with 100% of this full-goodwill loss.

title: Partial goodwill CGU gross-up • case 25
prompt: P owns 80% of S. Recognised PARTIAL goodwill is LKR 1,200,000; S’s other net assets in the tested CGU carry at 6,000,000. Recoverable amount of the WHOLE CGU is 6,750,000. Gross up goodwill for unrecognised NCI goodwill when testing; the whole impairment falls within grossed-up goodwill. No tax or other adjustments apply. Find impairment actually recognised on group goodwill.
explanation: Grossed-up goodwill = 1,200,000/80% = 1,500,000.00. Whole-CGU impairment = grossed goodwill + other net assets − recoverable amount = 750,000.00. Only the parent’s 80% goodwill portion is recognised, so recorded loss = 600,000.00.
reference: LKAS 36 Appendix C paras C4–C8; SLFRS 10 para B86

title: Consolidated retained earnings bridge • case 25
prompt: P owns 75% of S. At year end P retained earnings are LKR 4,250,000, and S retained earnings 2,750,000. S retained earnings at acquisition were 1,000,000. Cumulative post-acquisition extra FV depreciation is 150,000. A downstream sale by P leaves unrealised profit of 105,000. No tax, goodwill impairment, dividends recognised by P, OCI or other adjustments apply. Find consolidated retained earnings attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Group owners’ retained earnings = parent RE + 75% of adjusted post-acquisition S reserves − the parent’s downstream unrealised profit: 5,345,000.00. Pre-acquisition reserves do not enter post-acquisition group retained earnings.

title: Loss of control and translation reserve • case 25
prompt: P loses control of a foreign subsidiary. Proceeds are LKR 3,200,000; retained interest FV 750,000; NCI carrying amount 425,000; consolidated net assets INCLUDING goodwill 3,350,000. A cumulative translation GAIN of 150,000, entirely attributable to P, must be reclassified to profit or loss on loss of control. No other effects apply. Find total disposal gain including that reclassification.
explanation: Base gain = proceeds + retained FV + NCI − net assets = 1,025,000.00. Add the parent’s translation gain recycled on disposal: 150,000. Total = 1,175,000.00.
family: Loss of control and translation reserve

title: Residual guarantee expected payment • case 25
prompt: A lessee owes three year-end rentals of LKR 325,000. It guarantees residual value up to 200,000, but the amount EXPECTED to be payable under that guarantee is 55,000 at year three. Discount rate is 10%. No other liability payments exist. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the amount expected to be payable, not automatically the maximum guarantee. Liability = PV of three rentals + 55,000/1.10³ = 849,549.21.

title: Reasonably certain purchase option PV • case 25
prompt: A lease requires three year-end rentals of LKR 275,000, plus a purchase option price of 750,000 payable at year three. Exercise is reasonably certain. Discount rate is 10%. No incentives, other payments or initial prepayments apply. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the reasonably certain purchase price in the liability: PV of rentals + purchase price discounted for three years = 1,247,370.40. Do not omit or leave the future option payment undiscounted.

title: Lease and service component allocation • case 25
prompt: A two-year contract requires bundled payments of LKR 375,000 at each year end. Relative stand-alone prices are equipment lease 200,000 and distinct maintenance 50,000 per year. The lessee does NOT elect to combine components. Lease discount rate is 10%; no other payments exist. Find initial lease liability for the LEASE component only.
explanation: Allocate 200,000/250,000 = 80% of each bundled payment to the lease: 300,000.00. Discount those two lease payments, excluding maintenance, to obtain 520,661.16.

title: Exempt short-term lease rent-free start • case 25
prompt: A twelve-month lease with no purchase option qualifies for the elected short-term exemption. The first three months are rent free, then nine monthly payments of LKR 32,500 are due. The asset is available throughout and straight-line expense is appropriate. Find lease expense for the FIRST six months, ignoring accrual settlement timing.
explanation: Total fixed payments are nine rents. Spread evenly over all twelve months: 32,500 × 9/12 × 6 = 146,250.00. Rent-free months still receive an expense allocation.

title: Sale-and-leaseback rights transferred • case 25
prompt: A transfer qualifies as a sale under SLFRS 15 at fair value LKR 15,000,000; asset carrying amount is 8,500,000. Market-rate leaseback payments have PV 6,000,000. There are no off-market adjustments or variable-payment complications. At inception, what sale gain is recognised for rights TRANSFERRED to the buyer-lessor?
explanation: Total gain = 15,000,000 − 8,500,000 = 6,500,000. Retained-use proportion = lease PV / fair value = 40%. Recognise only the transferred-rights proportion of the gain: 3,900,000.00.

title: Reassessed bargain purchase gain • case 25
prompt: After the required reassessment, final acquisition-date consideration is LKR 3,000,000, NCI fair value is 400,000 and identifiable net assets are 4,500,000. There is no prior holding or other adjustment. Find the bargain purchase gain recognised in profit or loss.
explanation: Net identifiable assets exceed consideration plus NCI: 4,500,000 − 3,000,000 − 400,000 = 1,100,000.00. Reassessment has been completed before recognising the gain.

title: Acquired contingent liability in goodwill • case 25
prompt: Consideration is LKR 4,750,000; NCI FV is 500,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired contingent liability are 3,750,000. The acquired item is a present obligation with reliably measurable FV 325,000 and qualifies for recognition despite non-probable outflow. No tax or other adjustment applies. Find goodwill after recognising it.
explanation: Recognise the qualifying acquired liability: net identifiable assets become 3,750,000 − 325,000. Goodwill = consideration + NCI − adjusted net assets = 1,825,000.00.

title: Separate acquired brand from goodwill • case 25
prompt: Consideration is LKR 4,250,000; NCI FV 600,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired separable brand are 3,600,000. Brand FV is 650,000; tax base is zero and 30% DTL must be recognised. No other adjustments apply. Find goodwill after separate brand and tax recognition.
explanation: An identifiable acquired brand is separate from goodwill. Net addition to identifiable assets = brand FV − 30% DTL = 455,000.00. Goodwill = 4,250,000 + 600,000 − (3,600,000 + 455,000.00) = 795,000.00.

title: Acquisition costs versus issue costs • case 25
prompt: A business acquisition has consideration LKR 2,750,000. Additional costs are acquisition advisory 150,000, qualifying equity-issue costs 70,000 and qualifying debt-issue costs 40,000. The issue costs follow their relevant standards, and no immediate debt-cost amortisation or other expense arises this period. Find the immediate acquisition-related PROFIT-OR-LOSS expense from these costs.
explanation: Expense advisory acquisition costs of 150,000.00. Qualifying equity and debt issuance costs follow their respective standards and are not added to this immediate acquisition-service expense or goodwill.

title: Temporary difference and enacted rate change • case 25
prompt: A taxable temporary difference opens at LKR 200,000 with a DTL measured at 25%. At year end the difference is 425,000 and the enacted rate expected on reversal is 30%. Both the underlying movements and rate change belong in profit or loss. No other tax movements exist. Find deferred tax expense for the year.
explanation: Opening DTL = 200,000×25% = 50,000. Closing DTL = 425,000×30% = 127,500.00. Expense is the full increase, including rate remeasurement: 77,500.00. Rates are exercise assumptions.
family: Temporary difference and enacted rate change

title: Revalued non-depreciable land tax basis • case 25
prompt: Non-depreciable land is revalued from cost LKR 1,500,000 to fair value 2,250,000; tax base remains cost. The enacted rate for recovery through SALE is 20%, while a 30% use rate would otherwise apply. The revaluation and associated tax go to OCI. No other effects exist. Find the net OCI revaluation increase after deferred tax.
explanation: For this non-depreciable revalued asset, measure tax consequences on recovery through sale: DTL = (2,250,000 − 1,500,000)×20%. Net OCI increase = gross uplift less that DTL = 600,000.00.

title: Current tax reconciliation and prepayment • case 25
prompt: Accounting pretax profit is LKR 3,250,000. It includes a permanently non-deductible fine of 150,000, exempt income of 50,000, and warranty expense of 325,000 deductible only on payment. Current-year warranty payments of 80,000 are deductible and were charged against the provision, not current profit. Tax rate is 30%; tax prepayments are 300,000. No other tax adjustments exist. Find closing CURRENT tax payable, not total tax expense.
explanation: Taxable profit = 3,250,000 + fine 150,000 − exempt income 50,000 + provision expense 325,000 − deductible payments 80,000 = 3,595,000. Current tax less prepaid 300,000 = 778,500.00. Deferred tax is separate.

title: Consolidated inventory tax difference • case 25
prompt: After eliminating an intragroup profit, inventory carries in consolidated statements at LKR 900,000. Its tax base in the buyer’s tax jurisdiction is 1,350,000. The buyer’s enacted rate is 30%; sufficient taxable profit is probable. No offsetting, exception or other tax effects apply. Find the consolidated DTA on this inventory.
explanation: The consolidated carrying amount is below tax base, creating a deductible temporary difference of 450,000. Use the buyer’s relevant tax rate: difference ×30% = 135,000.00.

title: Depreciation after recognised impairment • case 25
prompt: Immediately before an impairment, equipment carries at LKR 1,500,000. Recoverable amount is 950,000 and impairment is recognised. After that date it has four years’ remaining useful life and residual value 100,000. Straight-line depreciation is appropriate; no further revaluation or impairment applies. Find depreciation for the next FULL year.
explanation: First reduce the asset to recoverable amount 950,000. Thereafter allocate revised depreciable amount over remaining life: (950,000 − 100,000)/4 = 212,500.00.

title: Allocated headquarters in CGU impairment • case 25
prompt: CGU A carries operating assets of LKR 850,000; CGU B carries 400,000. A headquarters asset of 200,000 can be allocated reasonably and consistently in proportion to those operating-asset amounts. A’s recoverable amount INCLUDING its headquarters share is 775,000. No goodwill or other assets exist. Find the impairment loss for A including its allocation.
explanation: Allocate headquarters to A: 200,000 × 850,000/(850,000+400,000) = 136,000.00. Tested A carrying amount is 986,000.00. Impairment versus recoverable amount 775,000 = 211,000.00.

title: Break-even value-in-use cash flow • case 25
prompt: An asset carries at LKR 1,500,000. Its fair value less costs of disposal is lower. A valid VIU model uses THREE equal year-end operating cash inflows, plus 100,000 net disposal proceeds at year three, discounted at 10%. What minimum equal ANNUAL operating cash inflow makes VIU exactly equal carrying amount? Ignore tax and other adjustments.
explanation: Let annual flow be X. X×(1/1.10 + 1/1.10² + 1/1.10³) + 100,000/1.10³ = 1,500,000. Solve for X = 572,960.73. This sensitivity calculation identifies the VIU break-even point.

title: Discounted warranty expected-value portfolio • case 25
prompt: A present warranty obligation covers 1,500 products. Per product, probabilities are 70% no defect, 25% a minor repair costing LKR 400, and 5% a major repair costing 2,000. All expected payments occur exactly in TWO years. Outflow for the portfolio is probable; appropriate discount rate is 10% with no risk double counting. Find the provision.
explanation: Expected cash payment = 1,500×(25%×400 + 5%×2,000) = 300,000.0. Discount two years at 10%: 300,000.0/1.10² = 247,933.88. The probability assessment applies to the portfolio.

title: Provision movement with revised estimate • case 25
prompt: A discounted provision opens at LKR 750,000. Unwinding for a full year is at 8%. A 100,000 settlement occurs at the year END, after unwinding. At that same reporting date, a new estimate increases the remaining provision by 100,000. No other changes occur. Find closing provision.
explanation: Closing = opening + 8% unwinding − year-end settlement + estimate increase: 750,000×1.08 −100,000 +100,000 = 810,000.00. Classification of the estimate change’s counterpart is assessed separately.

title: Revaluation increase after earlier loss • case 25
prompt: PPE carries at LKR 850,000 before revaluation and is revalued to 1,500,000. A prior revaluation decrease on THIS asset of 200,000 was recognised in profit or loss and has not been reversed. No tax effects apply. Find the current increase recognised in OCI after reversing the eligible prior loss in profit or loss.
explanation: Gross increase = 1,500,000 − 850,000 = 650,000. First recognise 200,000 in profit or loss to reverse the prior decrease. Remaining 450,000.00 is OCI revaluation surplus.

title: Nine-month depreciation and disposal gain • case 25
prompt: Equipment cost LKR 1,700,000, residual value 200,000 and useful life five years, straight-line. Two FULL years’ depreciation were recognised before this year. It is sold after nine months of the current year for 1,225,000. It was not previously held for sale and no impairment or revaluation applies. Find disposal GAIN after the required nine-month depreciation.
explanation: Annual depreciation = (1,700,000−200,000)/5. Deduct two full years and another 9/12 year from cost to obtain disposal-date carrying amount 875,000.00. Gain = proceeds − that amount = 350,000.00.

title: Customer collections with a write-off • case 25
prompt: All sales are on credit. Revenue is LKR 4,250,000; opening GROSS trade receivables are 600,000; closing GROSS receivables are 1,050,000. Receivables of 125,000 were written off during the year. There are no taxes, returns, contract balances, acquisitions or exchange changes. Find cash collected from customers.
explanation: Gross receivable roll-forward: opening + credit sales − cash receipts − write-offs = closing. Thus receipts = 4,250,000+600,000−1,050,000−125,000 = 3,675,000.00. Write-offs are not cash receipts.

title: Loan funding net cash effect • case 25
prompt: A company receives cash loan proceeds of LKR 1,500,000 and immediately pays a directly attributable lender issue fee of 32,500. Both payments are classified as financing cash flows in this case. No other cash movement occurs. Find the NET financing cash inflow from these two cash movements; this question does not require net line-item presentation.
explanation: Net financing cash effect = proceeds − cash fee = 1,500,000 − 32,500.00 = 1,467,500.00. Effective-interest amortisation later is not another inception cash payment.

title: Item-by-item NRV without offsetting headroom • case 25
prompt: Two unrelated inventory lines require separate NRV tests. A has 225 units, cost LKR 1,000 and NRV 900 each. B has 150 units, cost 1,000 and NRV 1,200 each. There is no basis to group them for the write-down test. Find TOTAL closing inventory carrying amount.
explanation: Carry A at 900 per unit and B at its lower cost of 1,000. Total = 225×900 + 150×1,000 = 352,500.00. B’s NRV headroom cannot offset A’s write-down.

title: Units-of-production intangible amortisation • case 25
prompt: A finite-life production licence costs LKR 1,400,000, has zero residual value, and is expected to support 150,000 units in total. Actual output this year is 42,500 units. A units-of-production method reliably reflects consumption and the asset was available throughout. No impairment or estimate change applies. Find annual amortisation.
explanation: Apply the supported consumption pattern: amortisation = 1,400,000 × 42,500/150,000 = 396,666.67. It is the share of expected lifetime production consumed, not an automatic straight-line charge.

title: Profit after suspended associate losses • case 25
prompt: An equity-method investment and relevant long-term interests were previously reduced to zero. Unrecognised share of prior losses totals LKR 130,000; the investor has no obligation and made no support payments. In the current year its share of associate profit is 195,000. No other adjustments or changes in interest apply. Find the share of profit that can now be RECOGNISED.
explanation: First absorb unrecognised prior losses before resuming recognised profit. Recognised amount = current profit share 195,000 − prior unrecognised losses 130,000 = 65,000.00.

title: Return recovery asset net of costs • case 26
prompt: A retailer has transferred 1,650 products. It expects 66 to be returned. Each returned product originally cost LKR 600; expected recovery handling is 20 per item and expected value deterioration is 30 per item. Estimates meet the relevant requirements. Find the separate asset for the right to recover returned products, excluding the refund liability.
explanation: Recovery asset = original carrying amount of expected returns less recovery costs and potential value decrease: 66 × (600 − 20 − 30) = 36,300.00. It is assessed separately from the customer refund liability.
family: Return recovery asset net of costs

title: Retrospective volume rebate true-up • case 26
prompt: A customer’s annual purchases reach 12,600 units at list price LKR 200. Crossing the threshold entitles it to a 5% retrospective rebate on ALL units. Cumulative revenue before this new supported estimate equals full list price; no rebate was previously accrued. The constraint permits the estimate. Find the reduction in cumulative revenue required now.
explanation: The revised transaction price reflects the retrospective rebate on all units. Revenue reduction = 12,600 × 200 × 5% = 126,000.00. Recognise the corresponding refund obligation as appropriate.

title: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation • case 26
prompt: A bundle has distinct goods A and B with stand-alone prices LKR 330,000 and 560,000. Total transaction price is 814,000. ALL paragraph 82 criteria demonstrate that the whole 76,000 discount relates only to A. A transfers now; B is not yet delivered. Find revenue recognised for A.
explanation: The specified discount-allocation exception applies. Allocate all 76,000 discount to A: 330,000 − 76,000 = 254,000.00. Do not default to relative allocation when the exception’s criteria are met.
family: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation

title: Three obligations and partial service • case 26
prompt: A contract price of LKR 1,980,000 covers goods A, goods B and twelve months of distinct support. Stand-alone prices are 600,000, 300,000 and 300,000 respectively. A is delivered, B is not, and six months of evenly provided support are complete. No allocation exception applies. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise allocation to A plus half of support: 1,980,000 × (600,000 + 150,000) / 1,200,000 = 1,237,500.00. B’s allocation remains unrecognised as revenue.

title: Progress excluding abnormal waste • case 26
prompt: An over-time contract has transaction price LKR 12,600,000. Costs incurred are 5,040,000, including abnormal waste of 252,000 that does not depict progress. Expected TOTAL productive costs excluding that waste are 10,080,000. Cost-to-cost is appropriate after excluding the waste; no other adjustment applies. Find cumulative revenue, not profit.
explanation: Exclude abnormal waste from the progress numerator. Productive progress = (5,040,000 − 252,000) / 10,080,000. Revenue = transaction price × that progress = 5,985,000.00. The wasted cost is not a revenue-producing input.

title: Uninstalled materials without margin • case 26
prompt: A single over-time construction obligation has price LKR 15,200,000. All B19(b) conditions justify recognising revenue equal to cost for significant uninstalled materials of 3,040,000 already controlled by the customer. Other productive costs incurred are 2,280,000; expected total OTHER costs are 9,120,000. No revenue was previously recognised. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise material revenue without margin: 3,040,000. Recognise the remaining price using other-cost progress: (15,200,000 − 3,040,000) × 2,280,000/9,120,000. Total revenue = 6,080,000.00.

title: Agent commission after collection • case 26
prompt: An intermediary is an AGENT and collects customer cash of LKR 2,300,000 for a completed supplier service. It must remit 88% to the supplier and is entitled to the remaining 12% commission. It controls neither the underlying service nor any distinct extra service, and there is no tax. Find its revenue.
explanation: An agent recognises its fee or commission, not the supplier’s gross billings: 2,300,000 × 12% = 276,000.00. The amount due to the supplier is separately accounted for.

title: Distinct remaining goods blended prospectively • case 26
prompt: At modification, 100 distinct goods remain under an existing contract at LKR 1,260 each. Another 50 distinct goods are added at 1,008 each. The modification is NOT a separate contract, but remaining goods are distinct from those already transferred, so paragraph 21(a) applies prospectively. Thirty of the remaining goods are then transferred. Find revenue for those thirty.
explanation: Prospective remaining consideration = 100 × 1,260 + 50 × 1,008. Divide by 150 remaining goods, then multiply by 30 = 35,280.00. Do not retrospectively revise revenue on goods already transferred.

title: FVTPL acquisition expense • case 26
prompt: A financial asset is acquired at fair value LKR 1,320,000 and is classified at FVTPL. Directly attributable broker costs are 33,000, paid separately. No fair-value change occurs immediately after purchase. Find the immediate profit-or-loss expense from acquiring this asset.
explanation: Transaction costs on an FVTPL asset are expensed. Initial asset carrying amount is fair value 1,320,000; immediate acquisition expense is 33,000.00.

title: Collateral cash-shortfall discounting • case 26
prompt: A credit loss scenario has a contractual receipt of LKR 1,650,000 due in one year. The ONLY expected recovery at that same date is collateral sale proceeds of 1,090,000, less sale costs of 76,000. Scenario probability is 100% and original EIR is 10%. Collateral is an integral contractual credit enhancement and not separately recognised. Find discounted ECL.
explanation: One-year shortfall = contractual receipt − net collateral recovery = 1,650,000 − (1,090,000 − 76,000). Discount that shortfall at 10%: 578,181.82. Do not ignore recovery costs or discount only one side of same-date cash flows.

title: Three-band provision matrix • case 26
prompt: Under the simplified lifetime-ECL approach, supported adjusted loss rates are 1% on current receivables of LKR 1,520,000, 5% on past-due balances of 430,000, and 30% on severely overdue balances of 152,000. Rates already include all required forward-looking and discounting effects. Find total loss allowance.
explanation: Apply each appropriate band rate and add: 1,520,000×1% + 430,000×5% + 152,000×30% = 82,300.00. Do not apply one blended band mechanically to all balances.

title: Equity FVOCI profit-or-loss dividend • case 26
prompt: An eligible equity investment has the irrevocable FVOCI election. During the year it gains LKR 172,000 in fair value and earns a dividend of 86,000. Dividend recognition criteria are met and the dividend clearly represents a return on investment, not recovery of cost. There are no other effects. Find income recognised in PROFIT OR LOSS.
explanation: The qualifying dividend of 86,000.00 is profit-or-loss income. The fair-value movement of 172,000 is OCI under this election and is not added to the profit-or-loss amount.

title: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset • case 26
prompt: A loan is sold with full derecognition. Immediately before sale, gross carrying amount is LKR 1,520,000, loss allowance 152,000, and cash proceeds 1,444,000. No accumulated OCI, sale fees or other adjustments exist. Find the derecognition GAIN relative to net carrying amount.
explanation: Net carrying amount = 1,520,000 − 152,000 = 1,368,000. Compare proceeds with that net amount: 1,444,000 − 1,368,000 = 76,000.00 gain. Derecognise both the gross asset and related allowance.
family: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset

title: Non-substantial liability modification gain • case 26
prompt: An amortised-cost liability is modified WITHOUT extinguishment, with no fees. Its carrying amount is LKR 1,260,000. The sole revised payment is 1,449,000 in two years. Original EIR is 10%; the modification is assessed as non-substantial. Find the immediate modification GAIN from recalculating amortised cost at the original EIR.
explanation: Revised amortised cost = 1,449,000/1.10² = 1,197,520.66. Gain = old liability 1,260,000 − revised PV = 62,479.34. The original EIR is retained for this non-extinguishing modification.

title: Credit-risk improvement allowance release • case 26
prompt: A debt asset under the GENERAL ECL model previously had significant credit-risk deterioration and lifetime allowance LKR 152,000. At reporting date the criteria for lifetime ECL are no longer met; required 12-month ECL is 23,000. No write-offs, new assets or other allowance movements occur. Find the impairment reversal in profit or loss.
explanation: When lifetime measurement is no longer required, the general model returns to 12-month ECL. Release the excess allowance: 152,000 − 23,000 = 129,000.00. This is not a receivable under mandatory simplified lifetime ECL.

title: Upstream inventory elimination with tax • case 26
prompt: P and S report profits AFTER their own tax of LKR 3,040,000 and 1,320,000. An upstream inventory sale leaves unrealised profit of 304,000 in group closing inventory. A recoverable DTA is recognised on the full elimination at 30%, with the tax effect in profit or loss. No other consolidation adjustments exist. Find TOTAL consolidated profit, before attribution to owners and NCI.
explanation: Combine separate after-tax profits, eliminate unrealised profit and recognise the recoverable tax benefit: 3,040,000 + 1,320,000 − 304,000 + 91,200.00 = 4,147,200.00. This question asks total group profit, not its attribution.

title: Full-goodwill impairment and owner profit • case 26
prompt: P owns 80% of S all year. Separate after-tax profits are P LKR 2,580,000 and S 960,000. Goodwill is recognised on the FULL-goodwill basis and an impairment of 330,000 is attributable to S’s CGU and allocated 80:20 between owners and NCI. No other adjustments or tax effects apply. Find consolidated profit attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Owners receive 80% of S’s profit and bear 80% of the full-goodwill loss: 2,580,000 + 80% × (960,000 − 330,000) = 3,084,000.00. Do not charge the owners with 100% of this full-goodwill loss.

title: Partial goodwill CGU gross-up • case 26
prompt: P owns 80% of S. Recognised PARTIAL goodwill is LKR 1,216,000; S’s other net assets in the tested CGU carry at 6,080,000. Recoverable amount of the WHOLE CGU is 6,840,000. Gross up goodwill for unrecognised NCI goodwill when testing; the whole impairment falls within grossed-up goodwill. No tax or other adjustments apply. Find impairment actually recognised on group goodwill.
explanation: Grossed-up goodwill = 1,216,000/80% = 1,520,000.00. Whole-CGU impairment = grossed goodwill + other net assets − recoverable amount = 760,000.00. Only the parent’s 80% goodwill portion is recognised, so recorded loss = 608,000.00.
reference: LKAS 36 Appendix C paras C4–C8; SLFRS 10 para B86

title: Consolidated retained earnings bridge • case 26
prompt: P owns 75% of S. At year end P retained earnings are LKR 4,300,000, and S retained earnings 2,780,000. S retained earnings at acquisition were 1,000,000. Cumulative post-acquisition extra FV depreciation is 152,000. A downstream sale by P leaves unrealised profit of 106,000. No tax, goodwill impairment, dividends recognised by P, OCI or other adjustments apply. Find consolidated retained earnings attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Group owners’ retained earnings = parent RE + 75% of adjusted post-acquisition S reserves − the parent’s downstream unrealised profit: 5,415,000.00. Pre-acquisition reserves do not enter post-acquisition group retained earnings.

title: Loss of control and translation reserve • case 26
prompt: P loses control of a foreign subsidiary. Proceeds are LKR 3,240,000; retained interest FV 760,000; NCI carrying amount 430,000; consolidated net assets INCLUDING goodwill 3,380,000. A cumulative translation GAIN of 152,000, entirely attributable to P, must be reclassified to profit or loss on loss of control. No other effects apply. Find total disposal gain including that reclassification.
explanation: Base gain = proceeds + retained FV + NCI − net assets = 1,050,000.00. Add the parent’s translation gain recycled on disposal: 152,000. Total = 1,202,000.00.
family: Loss of control and translation reserve

title: Residual guarantee expected payment • case 26
prompt: A lessee owes three year-end rentals of LKR 330,000. It guarantees residual value up to 200,000, but the amount EXPECTED to be payable under that guarantee is 56,000 at year three. Discount rate is 10%. No other liability payments exist. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the amount expected to be payable, not automatically the maximum guarantee. Liability = PV of three rentals + 56,000/1.10³ = 862,734.79.

title: Reasonably certain purchase option PV • case 26
prompt: A lease requires three year-end rentals of LKR 280,000, plus a purchase option price of 760,000 payable at year three. Exercise is reasonably certain. Discount rate is 10%. No incentives, other payments or initial prepayments apply. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the reasonably certain purchase price in the liability: PV of rentals + purchase price discounted for three years = 1,267,317.81. Do not omit or leave the future option payment undiscounted.

title: Lease and service component allocation • case 26
prompt: A two-year contract requires bundled payments of LKR 380,000 at each year end. Relative stand-alone prices are equipment lease 200,000 and distinct maintenance 50,000 per year. The lessee does NOT elect to combine components. Lease discount rate is 10%; no other payments exist. Find initial lease liability for the LEASE component only.
explanation: Allocate 200,000/250,000 = 80% of each bundled payment to the lease: 304,000.00. Discount those two lease payments, excluding maintenance, to obtain 527,603.31.

title: Exempt short-term lease rent-free start • case 26
prompt: A twelve-month lease with no purchase option qualifies for the elected short-term exemption. The first three months are rent free, then nine monthly payments of LKR 33,000 are due. The asset is available throughout and straight-line expense is appropriate. Find lease expense for the FIRST six months, ignoring accrual settlement timing.
explanation: Total fixed payments are nine rents. Spread evenly over all twelve months: 33,000 × 9/12 × 6 = 148,500.00. Rent-free months still receive an expense allocation.

title: Sale-and-leaseback rights transferred • case 26
prompt: A transfer qualifies as a sale under SLFRS 15 at fair value LKR 15,200,000; asset carrying amount is 8,600,000. Market-rate leaseback payments have PV 6,080,000. There are no off-market adjustments or variable-payment complications. At inception, what sale gain is recognised for rights TRANSFERRED to the buyer-lessor?
explanation: Total gain = 15,200,000 − 8,600,000 = 6,600,000. Retained-use proportion = lease PV / fair value = 40%. Recognise only the transferred-rights proportion of the gain: 3,960,000.00.

title: Reassessed bargain purchase gain • case 26
prompt: After the required reassessment, final acquisition-date consideration is LKR 3,040,000, NCI fair value is 400,000 and identifiable net assets are 4,560,000. There is no prior holding or other adjustment. Find the bargain purchase gain recognised in profit or loss.
explanation: Net identifiable assets exceed consideration plus NCI: 4,560,000 − 3,040,000 − 400,000 = 1,120,000.00. Reassessment has been completed before recognising the gain.

title: Acquired contingent liability in goodwill • case 26
prompt: Consideration is LKR 4,800,000; NCI FV is 500,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired contingent liability are 3,780,000. The acquired item is a present obligation with reliably measurable FV 330,000 and qualifies for recognition despite non-probable outflow. No tax or other adjustment applies. Find goodwill after recognising it.
explanation: Recognise the qualifying acquired liability: net identifiable assets become 3,780,000 − 330,000. Goodwill = consideration + NCI − adjusted net assets = 1,850,000.00.

title: Separate acquired brand from goodwill • case 26
prompt: Consideration is LKR 4,300,000; NCI FV 600,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired separable brand are 3,640,000. Brand FV is 660,000; tax base is zero and 30% DTL must be recognised. No other adjustments apply. Find goodwill after separate brand and tax recognition.
explanation: An identifiable acquired brand is separate from goodwill. Net addition to identifiable assets = brand FV − 30% DTL = 462,000.00. Goodwill = 4,300,000 + 600,000 − (3,640,000 + 462,000.00) = 798,000.00.

title: Acquisition costs versus issue costs • case 26
prompt: A business acquisition has consideration LKR 2,780,000. Additional costs are acquisition advisory 152,000, qualifying equity-issue costs 70,000 and qualifying debt-issue costs 40,000. The issue costs follow their relevant standards, and no immediate debt-cost amortisation or other expense arises this period. Find the immediate acquisition-related PROFIT-OR-LOSS expense from these costs.
explanation: Expense advisory acquisition costs of 152,000.00. Qualifying equity and debt issuance costs follow their respective standards and are not added to this immediate acquisition-service expense or goodwill.

title: Temporary difference and enacted rate change • case 26
prompt: A taxable temporary difference opens at LKR 200,000 with a DTL measured at 25%. At year end the difference is 430,000 and the enacted rate expected on reversal is 30%. Both the underlying movements and rate change belong in profit or loss. No other tax movements exist. Find deferred tax expense for the year.
explanation: Opening DTL = 200,000×25% = 50,000. Closing DTL = 430,000×30% = 129,000.00. Expense is the full increase, including rate remeasurement: 79,000.00. Rates are exercise assumptions.
family: Temporary difference and enacted rate change

title: Revalued non-depreciable land tax basis • case 26
prompt: Non-depreciable land is revalued from cost LKR 1,520,000 to fair value 2,280,000; tax base remains cost. The enacted rate for recovery through SALE is 20%, while a 30% use rate would otherwise apply. The revaluation and associated tax go to OCI. No other effects exist. Find the net OCI revaluation increase after deferred tax.
explanation: For this non-depreciable revalued asset, measure tax consequences on recovery through sale: DTL = (2,280,000 − 1,520,000)×20%. Net OCI increase = gross uplift less that DTL = 608,000.00.

title: Current tax reconciliation and prepayment • case 26
prompt: Accounting pretax profit is LKR 3,300,000. It includes a permanently non-deductible fine of 152,000, exempt income of 50,000, and warranty expense of 330,000 deductible only on payment. Current-year warranty payments of 80,000 are deductible and were charged against the provision, not current profit. Tax rate is 30%; tax prepayments are 300,000. No other tax adjustments exist. Find closing CURRENT tax payable, not total tax expense.
explanation: Taxable profit = 3,300,000 + fine 152,000 − exempt income 50,000 + provision expense 330,000 − deductible payments 80,000 = 3,652,000. Current tax less prepaid 300,000 = 795,600.00. Deferred tax is separate.

title: Consolidated inventory tax difference • case 26
prompt: After eliminating an intragroup profit, inventory carries in consolidated statements at LKR 912,000. Its tax base in the buyer’s tax jurisdiction is 1,368,000. The buyer’s enacted rate is 30%; sufficient taxable profit is probable. No offsetting, exception or other tax effects apply. Find the consolidated DTA on this inventory.
explanation: The consolidated carrying amount is below tax base, creating a deductible temporary difference of 456,000. Use the buyer’s relevant tax rate: difference ×30% = 136,800.00.

title: Depreciation after recognised impairment • case 26
prompt: Immediately before an impairment, equipment carries at LKR 1,520,000. Recoverable amount is 960,000 and impairment is recognised. After that date it has four years’ remaining useful life and residual value 100,000. Straight-line depreciation is appropriate; no further revaluation or impairment applies. Find depreciation for the next FULL year.
explanation: First reduce the asset to recoverable amount 960,000. Thereafter allocate revised depreciable amount over remaining life: (960,000 − 100,000)/4 = 215,000.00.

title: Allocated headquarters in CGU impairment • case 26
prompt: CGU A carries operating assets of LKR 860,000; CGU B carries 400,000. A headquarters asset of 200,000 can be allocated reasonably and consistently in proportion to those operating-asset amounts. A’s recoverable amount INCLUDING its headquarters share is 780,000. No goodwill or other assets exist. Find the impairment loss for A including its allocation.
explanation: Allocate headquarters to A: 200,000 × 860,000/(860,000+400,000) = 136,507.94. Tested A carrying amount is 996,507.94. Impairment versus recoverable amount 780,000 = 216,507.94.

title: Break-even value-in-use cash flow • case 26
prompt: An asset carries at LKR 1,520,000. Its fair value less costs of disposal is lower. A valid VIU model uses THREE equal year-end operating cash inflows, plus 100,000 net disposal proceeds at year three, discounted at 10%. What minimum equal ANNUAL operating cash inflow makes VIU exactly equal carrying amount? Ignore tax and other adjustments.
explanation: Let annual flow be X. X×(1/1.10 + 1/1.10² + 1/1.10³) + 100,000/1.10³ = 1,520,000. Solve for X = 581,003.02. This sensitivity calculation identifies the VIU break-even point.

title: Discounted warranty expected-value portfolio • case 26
prompt: A present warranty obligation covers 1,520 products. Per product, probabilities are 70% no defect, 25% a minor repair costing LKR 400, and 5% a major repair costing 2,000. All expected payments occur exactly in TWO years. Outflow for the portfolio is probable; appropriate discount rate is 10% with no risk double counting. Find the provision.
explanation: Expected cash payment = 1,520×(25%×400 + 5%×2,000) = 304,000.0. Discount two years at 10%: 304,000.0/1.10² = 251,239.67. The probability assessment applies to the portfolio.

title: Provision movement with revised estimate • case 26
prompt: A discounted provision opens at LKR 760,000. Unwinding for a full year is at 8%. A 100,000 settlement occurs at the year END, after unwinding. At that same reporting date, a new estimate increases the remaining provision by 102,000. No other changes occur. Find closing provision.
explanation: Closing = opening + 8% unwinding − year-end settlement + estimate increase: 760,000×1.08 −100,000 +102,000 = 822,800.00. Classification of the estimate change’s counterpart is assessed separately.

title: Revaluation increase after earlier loss • case 26
prompt: PPE carries at LKR 860,000 before revaluation and is revalued to 1,520,000. A prior revaluation decrease on THIS asset of 202,000 was recognised in profit or loss and has not been reversed. No tax effects apply. Find the current increase recognised in OCI after reversing the eligible prior loss in profit or loss.
explanation: Gross increase = 1,520,000 − 860,000 = 660,000. First recognise 202,000 in profit or loss to reverse the prior decrease. Remaining 458,000.00 is OCI revaluation surplus.

title: Nine-month depreciation and disposal gain • case 26
prompt: Equipment cost LKR 1,720,000, residual value 200,000 and useful life five years, straight-line. Two FULL years’ depreciation were recognised before this year. It is sold after nine months of the current year for 1,240,000. It was not previously held for sale and no impairment or revaluation applies. Find disposal GAIN after the required nine-month depreciation.
explanation: Annual depreciation = (1,720,000−200,000)/5. Deduct two full years and another 9/12 year from cost to obtain disposal-date carrying amount 884,000.00. Gain = proceeds − that amount = 356,000.00.

title: Customer collections with a write-off • case 26
prompt: All sales are on credit. Revenue is LKR 4,300,000; opening GROSS trade receivables are 600,000; closing GROSS receivables are 1,060,000. Receivables of 126,000 were written off during the year. There are no taxes, returns, contract balances, acquisitions or exchange changes. Find cash collected from customers.
explanation: Gross receivable roll-forward: opening + credit sales − cash receipts − write-offs = closing. Thus receipts = 4,300,000+600,000−1,060,000−126,000 = 3,714,000.00. Write-offs are not cash receipts.

title: Loan funding net cash effect • case 26
prompt: A company receives cash loan proceeds of LKR 1,520,000 and immediately pays a directly attributable lender issue fee of 33,000. Both payments are classified as financing cash flows in this case. No other cash movement occurs. Find the NET financing cash inflow from these two cash movements; this question does not require net line-item presentation.
explanation: Net financing cash effect = proceeds − cash fee = 1,520,000 − 33,000.00 = 1,487,000.00. Effective-interest amortisation later is not another inception cash payment.

title: Item-by-item NRV without offsetting headroom • case 26
prompt: Two unrelated inventory lines require separate NRV tests. A has 230 units, cost LKR 1,000 and NRV 900 each. B has 152 units, cost 1,000 and NRV 1,200 each. There is no basis to group them for the write-down test. Find TOTAL closing inventory carrying amount.
explanation: Carry A at 900 per unit and B at its lower cost of 1,000. Total = 230×900 + 152×1,000 = 359,000.00. B’s NRV headroom cannot offset A’s write-down.

title: Units-of-production intangible amortisation • case 26
prompt: A finite-life production licence costs LKR 1,420,000, has zero residual value, and is expected to support 150,000 units in total. Actual output this year is 43,000 units. A units-of-production method reliably reflects consumption and the asset was available throughout. No impairment or estimate change applies. Find annual amortisation.
explanation: Apply the supported consumption pattern: amortisation = 1,420,000 × 43,000/150,000 = 407,066.67. It is the share of expected lifetime production consumed, not an automatic straight-line charge.

title: Profit after suspended associate losses • case 26
prompt: An equity-method investment and relevant long-term interests were previously reduced to zero. Unrecognised share of prior losses totals LKR 132,000; the investor has no obligation and made no support payments. In the current year its share of associate profit is 198,000. No other adjustments or changes in interest apply. Find the share of profit that can now be RECOGNISED.
explanation: First absorb unrecognised prior losses before resuming recognised profit. Recognised amount = current profit share 198,000 − prior unrecognised losses 132,000 = 66,000.00.

title: Return recovery asset net of costs • case 27
prompt: A retailer has transferred 1,675 products. It expects 67 to be returned. Each returned product originally cost LKR 600; expected recovery handling is 20 per item and expected value deterioration is 30 per item. Estimates meet the relevant requirements. Find the separate asset for the right to recover returned products, excluding the refund liability.
explanation: Recovery asset = original carrying amount of expected returns less recovery costs and potential value decrease: 67 × (600 − 20 − 30) = 36,850.00. It is assessed separately from the customer refund liability.
family: Return recovery asset net of costs

title: Retrospective volume rebate true-up • case 27
prompt: A customer’s annual purchases reach 12,700 units at list price LKR 200. Crossing the threshold entitles it to a 5% retrospective rebate on ALL units. Cumulative revenue before this new supported estimate equals full list price; no rebate was previously accrued. The constraint permits the estimate. Find the reduction in cumulative revenue required now.
explanation: The revised transaction price reflects the retrospective rebate on all units. Revenue reduction = 12,700 × 200 × 5% = 127,000.00. Recognise the corresponding refund obligation as appropriate.

title: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation • case 27
prompt: A bundle has distinct goods A and B with stand-alone prices LKR 335,000 and 570,000. Total transaction price is 828,000. ALL paragraph 82 criteria demonstrate that the whole 77,000 discount relates only to A. A transfers now; B is not yet delivered. Find revenue recognised for A.
explanation: The specified discount-allocation exception applies. Allocate all 77,000 discount to A: 335,000 − 77,000 = 258,000.00. Do not default to relative allocation when the exception’s criteria are met.
family: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation

title: Three obligations and partial service • case 27
prompt: A contract price of LKR 2,010,000 covers goods A, goods B and twelve months of distinct support. Stand-alone prices are 600,000, 300,000 and 300,000 respectively. A is delivered, B is not, and six months of evenly provided support are complete. No allocation exception applies. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise allocation to A plus half of support: 2,010,000 × (600,000 + 150,000) / 1,200,000 = 1,256,250.00. B’s allocation remains unrecognised as revenue.

title: Progress excluding abnormal waste • case 27
prompt: An over-time contract has transaction price LKR 12,700,000. Costs incurred are 5,080,000, including abnormal waste of 254,000 that does not depict progress. Expected TOTAL productive costs excluding that waste are 10,160,000. Cost-to-cost is appropriate after excluding the waste; no other adjustment applies. Find cumulative revenue, not profit.
explanation: Exclude abnormal waste from the progress numerator. Productive progress = (5,080,000 − 254,000) / 10,160,000. Revenue = transaction price × that progress = 6,032,500.00. The wasted cost is not a revenue-producing input.

title: Uninstalled materials without margin • case 27
prompt: A single over-time construction obligation has price LKR 15,400,000. All B19(b) conditions justify recognising revenue equal to cost for significant uninstalled materials of 3,080,000 already controlled by the customer. Other productive costs incurred are 2,310,000; expected total OTHER costs are 9,240,000. No revenue was previously recognised. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise material revenue without margin: 3,080,000. Recognise the remaining price using other-cost progress: (15,400,000 − 3,080,000) × 2,310,000/9,240,000. Total revenue = 6,160,000.00.

title: Agent commission after collection • case 27
prompt: An intermediary is an AGENT and collects customer cash of LKR 2,350,000 for a completed supplier service. It must remit 88% to the supplier and is entitled to the remaining 12% commission. It controls neither the underlying service nor any distinct extra service, and there is no tax. Find its revenue.
explanation: An agent recognises its fee or commission, not the supplier’s gross billings: 2,350,000 × 12% = 282,000.00. The amount due to the supplier is separately accounted for.

title: Distinct remaining goods blended prospectively • case 27
prompt: At modification, 100 distinct goods remain under an existing contract at LKR 1,270 each. Another 50 distinct goods are added at 1,016 each. The modification is NOT a separate contract, but remaining goods are distinct from those already transferred, so paragraph 21(a) applies prospectively. Thirty of the remaining goods are then transferred. Find revenue for those thirty.
explanation: Prospective remaining consideration = 100 × 1,270 + 50 × 1,016. Divide by 150 remaining goods, then multiply by 30 = 35,560.00. Do not retrospectively revise revenue on goods already transferred.

title: FVTPL acquisition expense • case 27
prompt: A financial asset is acquired at fair value LKR 1,340,000 and is classified at FVTPL. Directly attributable broker costs are 33,500, paid separately. No fair-value change occurs immediately after purchase. Find the immediate profit-or-loss expense from acquiring this asset.
explanation: Transaction costs on an FVTPL asset are expensed. Initial asset carrying amount is fair value 1,340,000; immediate acquisition expense is 33,500.00.

title: Collateral cash-shortfall discounting • case 27
prompt: A credit loss scenario has a contractual receipt of LKR 1,675,000 due in one year. The ONLY expected recovery at that same date is collateral sale proceeds of 1,105,000, less sale costs of 77,000. Scenario probability is 100% and original EIR is 10%. Collateral is an integral contractual credit enhancement and not separately recognised. Find discounted ECL.
explanation: One-year shortfall = contractual receipt − net collateral recovery = 1,675,000 − (1,105,000 − 77,000). Discount that shortfall at 10%: 588,181.82. Do not ignore recovery costs or discount only one side of same-date cash flows.

title: Three-band provision matrix • case 27
prompt: Under the simplified lifetime-ECL approach, supported adjusted loss rates are 1% on current receivables of LKR 1,540,000, 5% on past-due balances of 435,000, and 30% on severely overdue balances of 154,000. Rates already include all required forward-looking and discounting effects. Find total loss allowance.
explanation: Apply each appropriate band rate and add: 1,540,000×1% + 435,000×5% + 154,000×30% = 83,350.00. Do not apply one blended band mechanically to all balances.

title: Equity FVOCI profit-or-loss dividend • case 27
prompt: An eligible equity investment has the irrevocable FVOCI election. During the year it gains LKR 174,000 in fair value and earns a dividend of 87,000. Dividend recognition criteria are met and the dividend clearly represents a return on investment, not recovery of cost. There are no other effects. Find income recognised in PROFIT OR LOSS.
explanation: The qualifying dividend of 87,000.00 is profit-or-loss income. The fair-value movement of 174,000 is OCI under this election and is not added to the profit-or-loss amount.

title: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset • case 27
prompt: A loan is sold with full derecognition. Immediately before sale, gross carrying amount is LKR 1,540,000, loss allowance 154,000, and cash proceeds 1,463,000. No accumulated OCI, sale fees or other adjustments exist. Find the derecognition GAIN relative to net carrying amount.
explanation: Net carrying amount = 1,540,000 − 154,000 = 1,386,000. Compare proceeds with that net amount: 1,463,000 − 1,386,000 = 77,000.00 gain. Derecognise both the gross asset and related allowance.
family: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset

title: Non-substantial liability modification gain • case 27
prompt: An amortised-cost liability is modified WITHOUT extinguishment, with no fees. Its carrying amount is LKR 1,270,000. The sole revised payment is 1,460,500 in two years. Original EIR is 10%; the modification is assessed as non-substantial. Find the immediate modification GAIN from recalculating amortised cost at the original EIR.
explanation: Revised amortised cost = 1,460,500/1.10² = 1,207,024.79. Gain = old liability 1,270,000 − revised PV = 62,975.21. The original EIR is retained for this non-extinguishing modification.

title: Credit-risk improvement allowance release • case 27
prompt: A debt asset under the GENERAL ECL model previously had significant credit-risk deterioration and lifetime allowance LKR 154,000. At reporting date the criteria for lifetime ECL are no longer met; required 12-month ECL is 23,500. No write-offs, new assets or other allowance movements occur. Find the impairment reversal in profit or loss.
explanation: When lifetime measurement is no longer required, the general model returns to 12-month ECL. Release the excess allowance: 154,000 − 23,500 = 130,500.00. This is not a receivable under mandatory simplified lifetime ECL.

title: Upstream inventory elimination with tax • case 27
prompt: P and S report profits AFTER their own tax of LKR 3,080,000 and 1,340,000. An upstream inventory sale leaves unrealised profit of 308,000 in group closing inventory. A recoverable DTA is recognised on the full elimination at 30%, with the tax effect in profit or loss. No other consolidation adjustments exist. Find TOTAL consolidated profit, before attribution to owners and NCI.
explanation: Combine separate after-tax profits, eliminate unrealised profit and recognise the recoverable tax benefit: 3,080,000 + 1,340,000 − 308,000 + 92,400.00 = 4,204,400.00. This question asks total group profit, not its attribution.

title: Full-goodwill impairment and owner profit • case 27
prompt: P owns 80% of S all year. Separate after-tax profits are P LKR 2,610,000 and S 970,000. Goodwill is recognised on the FULL-goodwill basis and an impairment of 335,000 is attributable to S’s CGU and allocated 80:20 between owners and NCI. No other adjustments or tax effects apply. Find consolidated profit attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Owners receive 80% of S’s profit and bear 80% of the full-goodwill loss: 2,610,000 + 80% × (970,000 − 335,000) = 3,118,000.00. Do not charge the owners with 100% of this full-goodwill loss.

title: Partial goodwill CGU gross-up • case 27
prompt: P owns 80% of S. Recognised PARTIAL goodwill is LKR 1,232,000; S’s other net assets in the tested CGU carry at 6,160,000. Recoverable amount of the WHOLE CGU is 6,930,000. Gross up goodwill for unrecognised NCI goodwill when testing; the whole impairment falls within grossed-up goodwill. No tax or other adjustments apply. Find impairment actually recognised on group goodwill.
explanation: Grossed-up goodwill = 1,232,000/80% = 1,540,000.00. Whole-CGU impairment = grossed goodwill + other net assets − recoverable amount = 770,000.00. Only the parent’s 80% goodwill portion is recognised, so recorded loss = 616,000.00.
reference: LKAS 36 Appendix C paras C4–C8; SLFRS 10 para B86

title: Consolidated retained earnings bridge • case 27
prompt: P owns 75% of S. At year end P retained earnings are LKR 4,350,000, and S retained earnings 2,810,000. S retained earnings at acquisition were 1,000,000. Cumulative post-acquisition extra FV depreciation is 154,000. A downstream sale by P leaves unrealised profit of 107,000. No tax, goodwill impairment, dividends recognised by P, OCI or other adjustments apply. Find consolidated retained earnings attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Group owners’ retained earnings = parent RE + 75% of adjusted post-acquisition S reserves − the parent’s downstream unrealised profit: 5,485,000.00. Pre-acquisition reserves do not enter post-acquisition group retained earnings.

title: Loss of control and translation reserve • case 27
prompt: P loses control of a foreign subsidiary. Proceeds are LKR 3,280,000; retained interest FV 770,000; NCI carrying amount 435,000; consolidated net assets INCLUDING goodwill 3,410,000. A cumulative translation GAIN of 154,000, entirely attributable to P, must be reclassified to profit or loss on loss of control. No other effects apply. Find total disposal gain including that reclassification.
explanation: Base gain = proceeds + retained FV + NCI − net assets = 1,075,000.00. Add the parent’s translation gain recycled on disposal: 154,000. Total = 1,229,000.00.
family: Loss of control and translation reserve

title: Residual guarantee expected payment • case 27
prompt: A lessee owes three year-end rentals of LKR 335,000. It guarantees residual value up to 200,000, but the amount EXPECTED to be payable under that guarantee is 57,000 at year three. Discount rate is 10%. No other liability payments exist. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the amount expected to be payable, not automatically the maximum guarantee. Liability = PV of three rentals + 57,000/1.10³ = 875,920.36.

title: Reasonably certain purchase option PV • case 27
prompt: A lease requires three year-end rentals of LKR 285,000, plus a purchase option price of 770,000 payable at year three. Exercise is reasonably certain. Discount rate is 10%. No incentives, other payments or initial prepayments apply. Find initial lease liability.
