prompt: P loses control of a foreign subsidiary. Proceeds are LKR 3,400,000; retained interest FV 800,000; NCI carrying amount 450,000; consolidated net assets INCLUDING goodwill 3,500,000. A cumulative translation GAIN of 160,000, entirely attributable to P, must be reclassified to profit or loss on loss of control. No other effects apply. Find total disposal gain including that reclassification.
explanation: Base gain = proceeds + retained FV + NCI − net assets = 1,150,000.00. Add the parent’s translation gain recycled on disposal: 160,000. Total = 1,310,000.00.
family: Loss of control and translation reserve

title: Residual guarantee expected payment • case 30
prompt: A lessee owes three year-end rentals of LKR 350,000. It guarantees residual value up to 200,000, but the amount EXPECTED to be payable under that guarantee is 60,000 at year three. Discount rate is 10%. No other liability payments exist. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the amount expected to be payable, not automatically the maximum guarantee. Liability = PV of three rentals + 60,000/1.10³ = 915,477.08.

title: Reasonably certain purchase option PV • case 30
prompt: A lease requires three year-end rentals of LKR 300,000, plus a purchase option price of 800,000 payable at year three. Exercise is reasonably certain. Discount rate is 10%. No incentives, other payments or initial prepayments apply. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the reasonably certain purchase price in the liability: PV of rentals + purchase price discounted for three years = 1,347,107.44. Do not omit or leave the future option payment undiscounted.

title: Lease and service component allocation • case 30
prompt: A two-year contract requires bundled payments of LKR 400,000 at each year end. Relative stand-alone prices are equipment lease 200,000 and distinct maintenance 50,000 per year. The lessee does NOT elect to combine components. Lease discount rate is 10%; no other payments exist. Find initial lease liability for the LEASE component only.
explanation: Allocate 200,000/250,000 = 80% of each bundled payment to the lease: 320,000.00. Discount those two lease payments, excluding maintenance, to obtain 555,371.90.

title: Exempt short-term lease rent-free start • case 30
prompt: A twelve-month lease with no purchase option qualifies for the elected short-term exemption. The first three months are rent free, then nine monthly payments of LKR 35,000 are due. The asset is available throughout and straight-line expense is appropriate. Find lease expense for the FIRST six months, ignoring accrual settlement timing.
explanation: Total fixed payments are nine rents. Spread evenly over all twelve months: 35,000 × 9/12 × 6 = 157,500.00. Rent-free months still receive an expense allocation.

title: Sale-and-leaseback rights transferred • case 30
prompt: A transfer qualifies as a sale under SLFRS 15 at fair value LKR 16,000,000; asset carrying amount is 9,000,000. Market-rate leaseback payments have PV 6,400,000. There are no off-market adjustments or variable-payment complications. At inception, what sale gain is recognised for rights TRANSFERRED to the buyer-lessor?
explanation: Total gain = 16,000,000 − 9,000,000 = 7,000,000. Retained-use proportion = lease PV / fair value = 40%. Recognise only the transferred-rights proportion of the gain: 4,200,000.00.

title: Reassessed bargain purchase gain • case 30
prompt: After the required reassessment, final acquisition-date consideration is LKR 3,200,000, NCI fair value is 400,000 and identifiable net assets are 4,800,000. There is no prior holding or other adjustment. Find the bargain purchase gain recognised in profit or loss.
explanation: Net identifiable assets exceed consideration plus NCI: 4,800,000 − 3,200,000 − 400,000 = 1,200,000.00. Reassessment has been completed before recognising the gain.

title: Acquired contingent liability in goodwill • case 30
prompt: Consideration is LKR 5,000,000; NCI FV is 500,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired contingent liability are 3,900,000. The acquired item is a present obligation with reliably measurable FV 350,000 and qualifies for recognition despite non-probable outflow. No tax or other adjustment applies. Find goodwill after recognising it.
explanation: Recognise the qualifying acquired liability: net identifiable assets become 3,900,000 − 350,000. Goodwill = consideration + NCI − adjusted net assets = 1,950,000.00.

title: Separate acquired brand from goodwill • case 30
prompt: Consideration is LKR 4,500,000; NCI FV 600,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired separable brand are 3,800,000. Brand FV is 700,000; tax base is zero and 30% DTL must be recognised. No other adjustments apply. Find goodwill after separate brand and tax recognition.
explanation: An identifiable acquired brand is separate from goodwill. Net addition to identifiable assets = brand FV − 30% DTL = 490,000.00. Goodwill = 4,500,000 + 600,000 − (3,800,000 + 490,000.00) = 810,000.00.

title: Acquisition costs versus issue costs • case 30
prompt: A business acquisition has consideration LKR 2,900,000. Additional costs are acquisition advisory 160,000, qualifying equity-issue costs 70,000 and qualifying debt-issue costs 40,000. The issue costs follow their relevant standards, and no immediate debt-cost amortisation or other expense arises this period. Find the immediate acquisition-related PROFIT-OR-LOSS expense from these costs.
explanation: Expense advisory acquisition costs of 160,000.00. Qualifying equity and debt issuance costs follow their respective standards and are not added to this immediate acquisition-service expense or goodwill.

title: Temporary difference and enacted rate change • case 30
prompt: A taxable temporary difference opens at LKR 200,000 with a DTL measured at 25%. At year end the difference is 450,000 and the enacted rate expected on reversal is 30%. Both the underlying movements and rate change belong in profit or loss. No other tax movements exist. Find deferred tax expense for the year.
explanation: Opening DTL = 200,000×25% = 50,000. Closing DTL = 450,000×30% = 135,000.00. Expense is the full increase, including rate remeasurement: 85,000.00. Rates are exercise assumptions.
family: Temporary difference and enacted rate change

title: Revalued non-depreciable land tax basis • case 30
prompt: Non-depreciable land is revalued from cost LKR 1,600,000 to fair value 2,400,000; tax base remains cost. The enacted rate for recovery through SALE is 20%, while a 30% use rate would otherwise apply. The revaluation and associated tax go to OCI. No other effects exist. Find the net OCI revaluation increase after deferred tax.
explanation: For this non-depreciable revalued asset, measure tax consequences on recovery through sale: DTL = (2,400,000 − 1,600,000)×20%. Net OCI increase = gross uplift less that DTL = 640,000.00.

title: Current tax reconciliation and prepayment • case 30
prompt: Accounting pretax profit is LKR 3,500,000. It includes a permanently non-deductible fine of 160,000, exempt income of 50,000, and warranty expense of 350,000 deductible only on payment. Current-year warranty payments of 80,000 are deductible and were charged against the provision, not current profit. Tax rate is 30%; tax prepayments are 300,000. No other tax adjustments exist. Find closing CURRENT tax payable, not total tax expense.
explanation: Taxable profit = 3,500,000 + fine 160,000 − exempt income 50,000 + provision expense 350,000 − deductible payments 80,000 = 3,880,000. Current tax less prepaid 300,000 = 864,000.00. Deferred tax is separate.

title: Consolidated inventory tax difference • case 30
prompt: After eliminating an intragroup profit, inventory carries in consolidated statements at LKR 960,000. Its tax base in the buyer’s tax jurisdiction is 1,440,000. The buyer’s enacted rate is 30%; sufficient taxable profit is probable. No offsetting, exception or other tax effects apply. Find the consolidated DTA on this inventory.
explanation: The consolidated carrying amount is below tax base, creating a deductible temporary difference of 480,000. Use the buyer’s relevant tax rate: difference ×30% = 144,000.00.

title: Depreciation after recognised impairment • case 30
prompt: Immediately before an impairment, equipment carries at LKR 1,600,000. Recoverable amount is 1,000,000 and impairment is recognised. After that date it has four years’ remaining useful life and residual value 100,000. Straight-line depreciation is appropriate; no further revaluation or impairment applies. Find depreciation for the next FULL year.
explanation: First reduce the asset to recoverable amount 1,000,000. Thereafter allocate revised depreciable amount over remaining life: (1,000,000 − 100,000)/4 = 225,000.00.

title: Allocated headquarters in CGU impairment • case 30
prompt: CGU A carries operating assets of LKR 900,000; CGU B carries 400,000. A headquarters asset of 200,000 can be allocated reasonably and consistently in proportion to those operating-asset amounts. A’s recoverable amount INCLUDING its headquarters share is 800,000. No goodwill or other assets exist. Find the impairment loss for A including its allocation.
explanation: Allocate headquarters to A: 200,000 × 900,000/(900,000+400,000) = 138,461.54. Tested A carrying amount is 1,038,461.54. Impairment versus recoverable amount 800,000 = 238,461.54.

title: Break-even value-in-use cash flow • case 30
prompt: An asset carries at LKR 1,600,000. Its fair value less costs of disposal is lower. A valid VIU model uses THREE equal year-end operating cash inflows, plus 100,000 net disposal proceeds at year three, discounted at 10%. What minimum equal ANNUAL operating cash inflow makes VIU exactly equal carrying amount? Ignore tax and other adjustments.
explanation: Let annual flow be X. X×(1/1.10 + 1/1.10² + 1/1.10³) + 100,000/1.10³ = 1,600,000. Solve for X = 613,172.21. This sensitivity calculation identifies the VIU break-even point.

title: Discounted warranty expected-value portfolio • case 30
prompt: A present warranty obligation covers 1,600 products. Per product, probabilities are 70% no defect, 25% a minor repair costing LKR 400, and 5% a major repair costing 2,000. All expected payments occur exactly in TWO years. Outflow for the portfolio is probable; appropriate discount rate is 10% with no risk double counting. Find the provision.
explanation: Expected cash payment = 1,600×(25%×400 + 5%×2,000) = 320,000.0. Discount two years at 10%: 320,000.0/1.10² = 264,462.81. The probability assessment applies to the portfolio.

title: Provision movement with revised estimate • case 30
prompt: A discounted provision opens at LKR 800,000. Unwinding for a full year is at 8%. A 100,000 settlement occurs at the year END, after unwinding. At that same reporting date, a new estimate increases the remaining provision by 110,000. No other changes occur. Find closing provision.
explanation: Closing = opening + 8% unwinding − year-end settlement + estimate increase: 800,000×1.08 −100,000 +110,000 = 874,000.00. Classification of the estimate change’s counterpart is assessed separately.

title: Revaluation increase after earlier loss • case 30
prompt: PPE carries at LKR 900,000 before revaluation and is revalued to 1,600,000. A prior revaluation decrease on THIS asset of 210,000 was recognised in profit or loss and has not been reversed. No tax effects apply. Find the current increase recognised in OCI after reversing the eligible prior loss in profit or loss.
explanation: Gross increase = 1,600,000 − 900,000 = 700,000. First recognise 210,000 in profit or loss to reverse the prior decrease. Remaining 490,000.00 is OCI revaluation surplus.

title: Nine-month depreciation and disposal gain • case 30
prompt: Equipment cost LKR 1,800,000, residual value 200,000 and useful life five years, straight-line. Two FULL years’ depreciation were recognised before this year. It is sold after nine months of the current year for 1,300,000. It was not previously held for sale and no impairment or revaluation applies. Find disposal GAIN after the required nine-month depreciation.
explanation: Annual depreciation = (1,800,000−200,000)/5. Deduct two full years and another 9/12 year from cost to obtain disposal-date carrying amount 920,000.00. Gain = proceeds − that amount = 380,000.00.

title: Customer collections with a write-off • case 30
prompt: All sales are on credit. Revenue is LKR 4,500,000; opening GROSS trade receivables are 600,000; closing GROSS receivables are 1,100,000. Receivables of 130,000 were written off during the year. There are no taxes, returns, contract balances, acquisitions or exchange changes. Find cash collected from customers.
explanation: Gross receivable roll-forward: opening + credit sales − cash receipts − write-offs = closing. Thus receipts = 4,500,000+600,000−1,100,000−130,000 = 3,870,000.00. Write-offs are not cash receipts.

title: Loan funding net cash effect • case 30
prompt: A company receives cash loan proceeds of LKR 1,600,000 and immediately pays a directly attributable lender issue fee of 35,000. Both payments are classified as financing cash flows in this case. No other cash movement occurs. Find the NET financing cash inflow from these two cash movements; this question does not require net line-item presentation.
explanation: Net financing cash effect = proceeds − cash fee = 1,600,000 − 35,000.00 = 1,565,000.00. Effective-interest amortisation later is not another inception cash payment.

title: Item-by-item NRV without offsetting headroom • case 30
prompt: Two unrelated inventory lines require separate NRV tests. A has 250 units, cost LKR 1,000 and NRV 900 each. B has 160 units, cost 1,000 and NRV 1,200 each. There is no basis to group them for the write-down test. Find TOTAL closing inventory carrying amount.
explanation: Carry A at 900 per unit and B at its lower cost of 1,000. Total = 250×900 + 160×1,000 = 385,000.00. B’s NRV headroom cannot offset A’s write-down.

title: Units-of-production intangible amortisation • case 30
prompt: A finite-life production licence costs LKR 1,500,000, has zero residual value, and is expected to support 150,000 units in total. Actual output this year is 45,000 units. A units-of-production method reliably reflects consumption and the asset was available throughout. No impairment or estimate change applies. Find annual amortisation.
explanation: Apply the supported consumption pattern: amortisation = 1,500,000 × 45,000/150,000 = 450,000.00. It is the share of expected lifetime production consumed, not an automatic straight-line charge.

title: Profit after suspended associate losses • case 30
prompt: An equity-method investment and relevant long-term interests were previously reduced to zero. Unrecognised share of prior losses totals LKR 140,000; the investor has no obligation and made no support payments. In the current year its share of associate profit is 210,000. No other adjustments or changes in interest apply. Find the share of profit that can now be RECOGNISED.
explanation: First absorb unrecognised prior losses before resuming recognised profit. Recognised amount = current profit share 210,000 − prior unrecognised losses 140,000 = 70,000.00.

title: Return recovery asset net of costs • case 31
prompt: A retailer has transferred 1,775 products. It expects 71 to be returned. Each returned product originally cost LKR 600; expected recovery handling is 20 per item and expected value deterioration is 30 per item. Estimates meet the relevant requirements. Find the separate asset for the right to recover returned products, excluding the refund liability.
explanation: Recovery asset = original carrying amount of expected returns less recovery costs and potential value decrease: 71 × (600 − 20 − 30) = 39,050.00. It is assessed separately from the customer refund liability.
family: Return recovery asset net of costs

title: Retrospective volume rebate true-up • case 31
prompt: A customer’s annual purchases reach 13,100 units at list price LKR 200. Crossing the threshold entitles it to a 5% retrospective rebate on ALL units. Cumulative revenue before this new supported estimate equals full list price; no rebate was previously accrued. The constraint permits the estimate. Find the reduction in cumulative revenue required now.
explanation: The revised transaction price reflects the retrospective rebate on all units. Revenue reduction = 13,100 × 200 × 5% = 131,000.00. Recognise the corresponding refund obligation as appropriate.

title: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation • case 31
prompt: A bundle has distinct goods A and B with stand-alone prices LKR 355,000 and 610,000. Total transaction price is 884,000. ALL paragraph 82 criteria demonstrate that the whole 81,000 discount relates only to A. A transfers now; B is not yet delivered. Find revenue recognised for A.
explanation: The specified discount-allocation exception applies. Allocate all 81,000 discount to A: 355,000 − 81,000 = 274,000.00. Do not default to relative allocation when the exception’s criteria are met.
family: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation

title: Three obligations and partial service • case 31
prompt: A contract price of LKR 2,130,000 covers goods A, goods B and twelve months of distinct support. Stand-alone prices are 600,000, 300,000 and 300,000 respectively. A is delivered, B is not, and six months of evenly provided support are complete. No allocation exception applies. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise allocation to A plus half of support: 2,130,000 × (600,000 + 150,000) / 1,200,000 = 1,331,250.00. B’s allocation remains unrecognised as revenue.

title: Progress excluding abnormal waste • case 31
prompt: An over-time contract has transaction price LKR 13,100,000. Costs incurred are 5,240,000, including abnormal waste of 262,000 that does not depict progress. Expected TOTAL productive costs excluding that waste are 10,480,000. Cost-to-cost is appropriate after excluding the waste; no other adjustment applies. Find cumulative revenue, not profit.
explanation: Exclude abnormal waste from the progress numerator. Productive progress = (5,240,000 − 262,000) / 10,480,000. Revenue = transaction price × that progress = 6,222,500.00. The wasted cost is not a revenue-producing input.

title: Uninstalled materials without margin • case 31
prompt: A single over-time construction obligation has price LKR 16,200,000. All B19(b) conditions justify recognising revenue equal to cost for significant uninstalled materials of 3,240,000 already controlled by the customer. Other productive costs incurred are 2,430,000; expected total OTHER costs are 9,720,000. No revenue was previously recognised. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise material revenue without margin: 3,240,000. Recognise the remaining price using other-cost progress: (16,200,000 − 3,240,000) × 2,430,000/9,720,000. Total revenue = 6,480,000.00.

title: Agent commission after collection • case 31
prompt: An intermediary is an AGENT and collects customer cash of LKR 2,550,000 for a completed supplier service. It must remit 88% to the supplier and is entitled to the remaining 12% commission. It controls neither the underlying service nor any distinct extra service, and there is no tax. Find its revenue.
explanation: An agent recognises its fee or commission, not the supplier’s gross billings: 2,550,000 × 12% = 306,000.00. The amount due to the supplier is separately accounted for.

title: Distinct remaining goods blended prospectively • case 31
prompt: At modification, 100 distinct goods remain under an existing contract at LKR 1,310 each. Another 50 distinct goods are added at 1,048 each. The modification is NOT a separate contract, but remaining goods are distinct from those already transferred, so paragraph 21(a) applies prospectively. Thirty of the remaining goods are then transferred. Find revenue for those thirty.
explanation: Prospective remaining consideration = 100 × 1,310 + 50 × 1,048. Divide by 150 remaining goods, then multiply by 30 = 36,680.00. Do not retrospectively revise revenue on goods already transferred.

title: FVTPL acquisition expense • case 31
prompt: A financial asset is acquired at fair value LKR 1,420,000 and is classified at FVTPL. Directly attributable broker costs are 35,500, paid separately. No fair-value change occurs immediately after purchase. Find the immediate profit-or-loss expense from acquiring this asset.
explanation: Transaction costs on an FVTPL asset are expensed. Initial asset carrying amount is fair value 1,420,000; immediate acquisition expense is 35,500.00.

title: Collateral cash-shortfall discounting • case 31
prompt: A credit loss scenario has a contractual receipt of LKR 1,775,000 due in one year. The ONLY expected recovery at that same date is collateral sale proceeds of 1,165,000, less sale costs of 81,000. Scenario probability is 100% and original EIR is 10%. Collateral is an integral contractual credit enhancement and not separately recognised. Find discounted ECL.
explanation: One-year shortfall = contractual receipt − net collateral recovery = 1,775,000 − (1,165,000 − 81,000). Discount that shortfall at 10%: 628,181.82. Do not ignore recovery costs or discount only one side of same-date cash flows.

title: Three-band provision matrix • case 31
prompt: Under the simplified lifetime-ECL approach, supported adjusted loss rates are 1% on current receivables of LKR 1,620,000, 5% on past-due balances of 455,000, and 30% on severely overdue balances of 162,000. Rates already include all required forward-looking and discounting effects. Find total loss allowance.
explanation: Apply each appropriate band rate and add: 1,620,000×1% + 455,000×5% + 162,000×30% = 87,550.00. Do not apply one blended band mechanically to all balances.

title: Equity FVOCI profit-or-loss dividend • case 31
prompt: An eligible equity investment has the irrevocable FVOCI election. During the year it gains LKR 182,000 in fair value and earns a dividend of 91,000. Dividend recognition criteria are met and the dividend clearly represents a return on investment, not recovery of cost. There are no other effects. Find income recognised in PROFIT OR LOSS.
explanation: The qualifying dividend of 91,000.00 is profit-or-loss income. The fair-value movement of 182,000 is OCI under this election and is not added to the profit-or-loss amount.

title: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset • case 31
prompt: A loan is sold with full derecognition. Immediately before sale, gross carrying amount is LKR 1,620,000, loss allowance 162,000, and cash proceeds 1,539,000. No accumulated OCI, sale fees or other adjustments exist. Find the derecognition GAIN relative to net carrying amount.
explanation: Net carrying amount = 1,620,000 − 162,000 = 1,458,000. Compare proceeds with that net amount: 1,539,000 − 1,458,000 = 81,000.00 gain. Derecognise both the gross asset and related allowance.
family: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset

title: Non-substantial liability modification gain • case 31
prompt: An amortised-cost liability is modified WITHOUT extinguishment, with no fees. Its carrying amount is LKR 1,310,000. The sole revised payment is 1,506,500 in two years. Original EIR is 10%; the modification is assessed as non-substantial. Find the immediate modification GAIN from recalculating amortised cost at the original EIR.
explanation: Revised amortised cost = 1,506,500/1.10² = 1,245,041.32. Gain = old liability 1,310,000 − revised PV = 64,958.68. The original EIR is retained for this non-extinguishing modification.

title: Credit-risk improvement allowance release • case 31
prompt: A debt asset under the GENERAL ECL model previously had significant credit-risk deterioration and lifetime allowance LKR 162,000. At reporting date the criteria for lifetime ECL are no longer met; required 12-month ECL is 25,500. No write-offs, new assets or other allowance movements occur. Find the impairment reversal in profit or loss.
explanation: When lifetime measurement is no longer required, the general model returns to 12-month ECL. Release the excess allowance: 162,000 − 25,500 = 136,500.00. This is not a receivable under mandatory simplified lifetime ECL.

title: Upstream inventory elimination with tax • case 31
prompt: P and S report profits AFTER their own tax of LKR 3,240,000 and 1,420,000. An upstream inventory sale leaves unrealised profit of 324,000 in group closing inventory. A recoverable DTA is recognised on the full elimination at 30%, with the tax effect in profit or loss. No other consolidation adjustments exist. Find TOTAL consolidated profit, before attribution to owners and NCI.
explanation: Combine separate after-tax profits, eliminate unrealised profit and recognise the recoverable tax benefit: 3,240,000 + 1,420,000 − 324,000 + 97,200.00 = 4,433,200.00. This question asks total group profit, not its attribution.

title: Full-goodwill impairment and owner profit • case 31
prompt: P owns 80% of S all year. Separate after-tax profits are P LKR 2,730,000 and S 1,010,000. Goodwill is recognised on the FULL-goodwill basis and an impairment of 355,000 is attributable to S’s CGU and allocated 80:20 between owners and NCI. No other adjustments or tax effects apply. Find consolidated profit attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Owners receive 80% of S’s profit and bear 80% of the full-goodwill loss: 2,730,000 + 80% × (1,010,000 − 355,000) = 3,254,000.00. Do not charge the owners with 100% of this full-goodwill loss.

title: Partial goodwill CGU gross-up • case 31
prompt: P owns 80% of S. Recognised PARTIAL goodwill is LKR 1,296,000; S’s other net assets in the tested CGU carry at 6,480,000. Recoverable amount of the WHOLE CGU is 7,290,000. Gross up goodwill for unrecognised NCI goodwill when testing; the whole impairment falls within grossed-up goodwill. No tax or other adjustments apply. Find impairment actually recognised on group goodwill.
explanation: Grossed-up goodwill = 1,296,000/80% = 1,620,000.00. Whole-CGU impairment = grossed goodwill + other net assets − recoverable amount = 810,000.00. Only the parent’s 80% goodwill portion is recognised, so recorded loss = 648,000.00.
reference: LKAS 36 Appendix C paras C4–C8; SLFRS 10 para B86

title: Consolidated retained earnings bridge • case 31
prompt: P owns 75% of S. At year end P retained earnings are LKR 4,550,000, and S retained earnings 2,930,000. S retained earnings at acquisition were 1,000,000. Cumulative post-acquisition extra FV depreciation is 162,000. A downstream sale by P leaves unrealised profit of 111,000. No tax, goodwill impairment, dividends recognised by P, OCI or other adjustments apply. Find consolidated retained earnings attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Group owners’ retained earnings = parent RE + 75% of adjusted post-acquisition S reserves − the parent’s downstream unrealised profit: 5,765,000.00. Pre-acquisition reserves do not enter post-acquisition group retained earnings.

title: Loss of control and translation reserve • case 31
prompt: P loses control of a foreign subsidiary. Proceeds are LKR 3,440,000; retained interest FV 810,000; NCI carrying amount 455,000; consolidated net assets INCLUDING goodwill 3,530,000. A cumulative translation GAIN of 162,000, entirely attributable to P, must be reclassified to profit or loss on loss of control. No other effects apply. Find total disposal gain including that reclassification.
explanation: Base gain = proceeds + retained FV + NCI − net assets = 1,175,000.00. Add the parent’s translation gain recycled on disposal: 162,000. Total = 1,337,000.00.
family: Loss of control and translation reserve

title: Residual guarantee expected payment • case 31
prompt: A lessee owes three year-end rentals of LKR 355,000. It guarantees residual value up to 200,000, but the amount EXPECTED to be payable under that guarantee is 61,000 at year three. Discount rate is 10%. No other liability payments exist. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the amount expected to be payable, not automatically the maximum guarantee. Liability = PV of three rentals + 61,000/1.10³ = 928,662.66.

title: Reasonably certain purchase option PV • case 31
prompt: A lease requires three year-end rentals of LKR 305,000, plus a purchase option price of 810,000 payable at year three. Exercise is reasonably certain. Discount rate is 10%. No incentives, other payments or initial prepayments apply. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the reasonably certain purchase price in the liability: PV of rentals + purchase price discounted for three years = 1,367,054.85. Do not omit or leave the future option payment undiscounted.

title: Lease and service component allocation • case 31
prompt: A two-year contract requires bundled payments of LKR 405,000 at each year end. Relative stand-alone prices are equipment lease 200,000 and distinct maintenance 50,000 per year. The lessee does NOT elect to combine components. Lease discount rate is 10%; no other payments exist. Find initial lease liability for the LEASE component only.
explanation: Allocate 200,000/250,000 = 80% of each bundled payment to the lease: 324,000.00. Discount those two lease payments, excluding maintenance, to obtain 562,314.05.

title: Exempt short-term lease rent-free start • case 31
prompt: A twelve-month lease with no purchase option qualifies for the elected short-term exemption. The first three months are rent free, then nine monthly payments of LKR 35,500 are due. The asset is available throughout and straight-line expense is appropriate. Find lease expense for the FIRST six months, ignoring accrual settlement timing.
explanation: Total fixed payments are nine rents. Spread evenly over all twelve months: 35,500 × 9/12 × 6 = 159,750.00. Rent-free months still receive an expense allocation.

title: Sale-and-leaseback rights transferred • case 31
prompt: A transfer qualifies as a sale under SLFRS 15 at fair value LKR 16,200,000; asset carrying amount is 9,100,000. Market-rate leaseback payments have PV 6,480,000. There are no off-market adjustments or variable-payment complications. At inception, what sale gain is recognised for rights TRANSFERRED to the buyer-lessor?
explanation: Total gain = 16,200,000 − 9,100,000 = 7,100,000. Retained-use proportion = lease PV / fair value = 40%. Recognise only the transferred-rights proportion of the gain: 4,260,000.00.

title: Reassessed bargain purchase gain • case 31
prompt: After the required reassessment, final acquisition-date consideration is LKR 3,240,000, NCI fair value is 400,000 and identifiable net assets are 4,860,000. There is no prior holding or other adjustment. Find the bargain purchase gain recognised in profit or loss.
explanation: Net identifiable assets exceed consideration plus NCI: 4,860,000 − 3,240,000 − 400,000 = 1,220,000.00. Reassessment has been completed before recognising the gain.

title: Acquired contingent liability in goodwill • case 31
prompt: Consideration is LKR 5,050,000; NCI FV is 500,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired contingent liability are 3,930,000. The acquired item is a present obligation with reliably measurable FV 355,000 and qualifies for recognition despite non-probable outflow. No tax or other adjustment applies. Find goodwill after recognising it.
explanation: Recognise the qualifying acquired liability: net identifiable assets become 3,930,000 − 355,000. Goodwill = consideration + NCI − adjusted net assets = 1,975,000.00.

title: Separate acquired brand from goodwill • case 31
prompt: Consideration is LKR 4,550,000; NCI FV 600,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired separable brand are 3,840,000. Brand FV is 710,000; tax base is zero and 30% DTL must be recognised. No other adjustments apply. Find goodwill after separate brand and tax recognition.
explanation: An identifiable acquired brand is separate from goodwill. Net addition to identifiable assets = brand FV − 30% DTL = 497,000.00. Goodwill = 4,550,000 + 600,000 − (3,840,000 + 497,000.00) = 813,000.00.

title: Acquisition costs versus issue costs • case 31
prompt: A business acquisition has consideration LKR 2,930,000. Additional costs are acquisition advisory 162,000, qualifying equity-issue costs 70,000 and qualifying debt-issue costs 40,000. The issue costs follow their relevant standards, and no immediate debt-cost amortisation or other expense arises this period. Find the immediate acquisition-related PROFIT-OR-LOSS expense from these costs.
explanation: Expense advisory acquisition costs of 162,000.00. Qualifying equity and debt issuance costs follow their respective standards and are not added to this immediate acquisition-service expense or goodwill.

title: Temporary difference and enacted rate change • case 31
prompt: A taxable temporary difference opens at LKR 200,000 with a DTL measured at 25%. At year end the difference is 455,000 and the enacted rate expected on reversal is 30%. Both the underlying movements and rate change belong in profit or loss. No other tax movements exist. Find deferred tax expense for the year.
explanation: Opening DTL = 200,000×25% = 50,000. Closing DTL = 455,000×30% = 136,500.00. Expense is the full increase, including rate remeasurement: 86,500.00. Rates are exercise assumptions.
family: Temporary difference and enacted rate change

title: Revalued non-depreciable land tax basis • case 31
prompt: Non-depreciable land is revalued from cost LKR 1,620,000 to fair value 2,430,000; tax base remains cost. The enacted rate for recovery through SALE is 20%, while a 30% use rate would otherwise apply. The revaluation and associated tax go to OCI. No other effects exist. Find the net OCI revaluation increase after deferred tax.
explanation: For this non-depreciable revalued asset, measure tax consequences on recovery through sale: DTL = (2,430,000 − 1,620,000)×20%. Net OCI increase = gross uplift less that DTL = 648,000.00.

title: Current tax reconciliation and prepayment • case 31
prompt: Accounting pretax profit is LKR 3,550,000. It includes a permanently non-deductible fine of 162,000, exempt income of 50,000, and warranty expense of 355,000 deductible only on payment. Current-year warranty payments of 80,000 are deductible and were charged against the provision, not current profit. Tax rate is 30%; tax prepayments are 300,000. No other tax adjustments exist. Find closing CURRENT tax payable, not total tax expense.
explanation: Taxable profit = 3,550,000 + fine 162,000 − exempt income 50,000 + provision expense 355,000 − deductible payments 80,000 = 3,937,000. Current tax less prepaid 300,000 = 881,100.00. Deferred tax is separate.

title: Consolidated inventory tax difference • case 31
prompt: After eliminating an intragroup profit, inventory carries in consolidated statements at LKR 972,000. Its tax base in the buyer’s tax jurisdiction is 1,458,000. The buyer’s enacted rate is 30%; sufficient taxable profit is probable. No offsetting, exception or other tax effects apply. Find the consolidated DTA on this inventory.
explanation: The consolidated carrying amount is below tax base, creating a deductible temporary difference of 486,000. Use the buyer’s relevant tax rate: difference ×30% = 145,800.00.

title: Depreciation after recognised impairment • case 31
prompt: Immediately before an impairment, equipment carries at LKR 1,620,000. Recoverable amount is 1,010,000 and impairment is recognised. After that date it has four years’ remaining useful life and residual value 100,000. Straight-line depreciation is appropriate; no further revaluation or impairment applies. Find depreciation for the next FULL year.
explanation: First reduce the asset to recoverable amount 1,010,000. Thereafter allocate revised depreciable amount over remaining life: (1,010,000 − 100,000)/4 = 227,500.00.

title: Allocated headquarters in CGU impairment • case 31
prompt: CGU A carries operating assets of LKR 910,000; CGU B carries 400,000. A headquarters asset of 200,000 can be allocated reasonably and consistently in proportion to those operating-asset amounts. A’s recoverable amount INCLUDING its headquarters share is 805,000. No goodwill or other assets exist. Find the impairment loss for A including its allocation.
explanation: Allocate headquarters to A: 200,000 × 910,000/(910,000+400,000) = 138,931.30. Tested A carrying amount is 1,048,931.30. Impairment versus recoverable amount 805,000 = 243,931.30.

title: Break-even value-in-use cash flow • case 31
prompt: An asset carries at LKR 1,620,000. Its fair value less costs of disposal is lower. A valid VIU model uses THREE equal year-end operating cash inflows, plus 100,000 net disposal proceeds at year three, discounted at 10%. What minimum equal ANNUAL operating cash inflow makes VIU exactly equal carrying amount? Ignore tax and other adjustments.
explanation: Let annual flow be X. X×(1/1.10 + 1/1.10² + 1/1.10³) + 100,000/1.10³ = 1,620,000. Solve for X = 621,214.50. This sensitivity calculation identifies the VIU break-even point.

title: Discounted warranty expected-value portfolio • case 31
prompt: A present warranty obligation covers 1,620 products. Per product, probabilities are 70% no defect, 25% a minor repair costing LKR 400, and 5% a major repair costing 2,000. All expected payments occur exactly in TWO years. Outflow for the portfolio is probable; appropriate discount rate is 10% with no risk double counting. Find the provision.
explanation: Expected cash payment = 1,620×(25%×400 + 5%×2,000) = 324,000.0. Discount two years at 10%: 324,000.0/1.10² = 267,768.60. The probability assessment applies to the portfolio.

title: Provision movement with revised estimate • case 31
prompt: A discounted provision opens at LKR 810,000. Unwinding for a full year is at 8%. A 100,000 settlement occurs at the year END, after unwinding. At that same reporting date, a new estimate increases the remaining provision by 112,000. No other changes occur. Find closing provision.
explanation: Closing = opening + 8% unwinding − year-end settlement + estimate increase: 810,000×1.08 −100,000 +112,000 = 886,800.00. Classification of the estimate change’s counterpart is assessed separately.

title: Revaluation increase after earlier loss • case 31
prompt: PPE carries at LKR 910,000 before revaluation and is revalued to 1,620,000. A prior revaluation decrease on THIS asset of 212,000 was recognised in profit or loss and has not been reversed. No tax effects apply. Find the current increase recognised in OCI after reversing the eligible prior loss in profit or loss.
explanation: Gross increase = 1,620,000 − 910,000 = 710,000. First recognise 212,000 in profit or loss to reverse the prior decrease. Remaining 498,000.00 is OCI revaluation surplus.

title: Nine-month depreciation and disposal gain • case 31
prompt: Equipment cost LKR 1,820,000, residual value 200,000 and useful life five years, straight-line. Two FULL years’ depreciation were recognised before this year. It is sold after nine months of the current year for 1,315,000. It was not previously held for sale and no impairment or revaluation applies. Find disposal GAIN after the required nine-month depreciation.
explanation: Annual depreciation = (1,820,000−200,000)/5. Deduct two full years and another 9/12 year from cost to obtain disposal-date carrying amount 929,000.00. Gain = proceeds − that amount = 386,000.00.

title: Customer collections with a write-off • case 31
prompt: All sales are on credit. Revenue is LKR 4,550,000; opening GROSS trade receivables are 600,000; closing GROSS receivables are 1,110,000. Receivables of 131,000 were written off during the year. There are no taxes, returns, contract balances, acquisitions or exchange changes. Find cash collected from customers.
explanation: Gross receivable roll-forward: opening + credit sales − cash receipts − write-offs = closing. Thus receipts = 4,550,000+600,000−1,110,000−131,000 = 3,909,000.00. Write-offs are not cash receipts.

title: Loan funding net cash effect • case 31
prompt: A company receives cash loan proceeds of LKR 1,620,000 and immediately pays a directly attributable lender issue fee of 35,500. Both payments are classified as financing cash flows in this case. No other cash movement occurs. Find the NET financing cash inflow from these two cash movements; this question does not require net line-item presentation.
explanation: Net financing cash effect = proceeds − cash fee = 1,620,000 − 35,500.00 = 1,584,500.00. Effective-interest amortisation later is not another inception cash payment.

title: Item-by-item NRV without offsetting headroom • case 31
prompt: Two unrelated inventory lines require separate NRV tests. A has 255 units, cost LKR 1,000 and NRV 900 each. B has 162 units, cost 1,000 and NRV 1,200 each. There is no basis to group them for the write-down test. Find TOTAL closing inventory carrying amount.
explanation: Carry A at 900 per unit and B at its lower cost of 1,000. Total = 255×900 + 162×1,000 = 391,500.00. B’s NRV headroom cannot offset A’s write-down.

title: Units-of-production intangible amortisation • case 31
prompt: A finite-life production licence costs LKR 1,520,000, has zero residual value, and is expected to support 150,000 units in total. Actual output this year is 45,500 units. A units-of-production method reliably reflects consumption and the asset was available throughout. No impairment or estimate change applies. Find annual amortisation.
explanation: Apply the supported consumption pattern: amortisation = 1,520,000 × 45,500/150,000 = 461,066.67. It is the share of expected lifetime production consumed, not an automatic straight-line charge.

title: Profit after suspended associate losses • case 31
prompt: An equity-method investment and relevant long-term interests were previously reduced to zero. Unrecognised share of prior losses totals LKR 142,000; the investor has no obligation and made no support payments. In the current year its share of associate profit is 213,000. No other adjustments or changes in interest apply. Find the share of profit that can now be RECOGNISED.
explanation: First absorb unrecognised prior losses before resuming recognised profit. Recognised amount = current profit share 213,000 − prior unrecognised losses 142,000 = 71,000.00.

title: Return recovery asset net of costs • case 32
prompt: A retailer has transferred 1,800 products. It expects 72 to be returned. Each returned product originally cost LKR 600; expected recovery handling is 20 per item and expected value deterioration is 30 per item. Estimates meet the relevant requirements. Find the separate asset for the right to recover returned products, excluding the refund liability.
explanation: Recovery asset = original carrying amount of expected returns less recovery costs and potential value decrease: 72 × (600 − 20 − 30) = 39,600.00. It is assessed separately from the customer refund liability.
family: Return recovery asset net of costs

title: Retrospective volume rebate true-up • case 32
prompt: A customer’s annual purchases reach 13,200 units at list price LKR 200. Crossing the threshold entitles it to a 5% retrospective rebate on ALL units. Cumulative revenue before this new supported estimate equals full list price; no rebate was previously accrued. The constraint permits the estimate. Find the reduction in cumulative revenue required now.
explanation: The revised transaction price reflects the retrospective rebate on all units. Revenue reduction = 13,200 × 200 × 5% = 132,000.00. Recognise the corresponding refund obligation as appropriate.

title: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation • case 32
prompt: A bundle has distinct goods A and B with stand-alone prices LKR 360,000 and 620,000. Total transaction price is 898,000. ALL paragraph 82 criteria demonstrate that the whole 82,000 discount relates only to A. A transfers now; B is not yet delivered. Find revenue recognised for A.
explanation: The specified discount-allocation exception applies. Allocate all 82,000 discount to A: 360,000 − 82,000 = 278,000.00. Do not default to relative allocation when the exception’s criteria are met.
family: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation

title: Three obligations and partial service • case 32
prompt: A contract price of LKR 2,160,000 covers goods A, goods B and twelve months of distinct support. Stand-alone prices are 600,000, 300,000 and 300,000 respectively. A is delivered, B is not, and six months of evenly provided support are complete. No allocation exception applies. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise allocation to A plus half of support: 2,160,000 × (600,000 + 150,000) / 1,200,000 = 1,350,000.00. B’s allocation remains unrecognised as revenue.

title: Progress excluding abnormal waste • case 32
prompt: An over-time contract has transaction price LKR 13,200,000. Costs incurred are 5,280,000, including abnormal waste of 264,000 that does not depict progress. Expected TOTAL productive costs excluding that waste are 10,560,000. Cost-to-cost is appropriate after excluding the waste; no other adjustment applies. Find cumulative revenue, not profit.
explanation: Exclude abnormal waste from the progress numerator. Productive progress = (5,280,000 − 264,000) / 10,560,000. Revenue = transaction price × that progress = 6,270,000.00. The wasted cost is not a revenue-producing input.

title: Uninstalled materials without margin • case 32
prompt: A single over-time construction obligation has price LKR 16,400,000. All B19(b) conditions justify recognising revenue equal to cost for significant uninstalled materials of 3,280,000 already controlled by the customer. Other productive costs incurred are 2,460,000; expected total OTHER costs are 9,840,000. No revenue was previously recognised. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise material revenue without margin: 3,280,000. Recognise the remaining price using other-cost progress: (16,400,000 − 3,280,000) × 2,460,000/9,840,000. Total revenue = 6,560,000.00.

title: Agent commission after collection • case 32
prompt: An intermediary is an AGENT and collects customer cash of LKR 2,600,000 for a completed supplier service. It must remit 88% to the supplier and is entitled to the remaining 12% commission. It controls neither the underlying service nor any distinct extra service, and there is no tax. Find its revenue.
explanation: An agent recognises its fee or commission, not the supplier’s gross billings: 2,600,000 × 12% = 312,000.00. The amount due to the supplier is separately accounted for.

title: Distinct remaining goods blended prospectively • case 32
prompt: At modification, 100 distinct goods remain under an existing contract at LKR 1,320 each. Another 50 distinct goods are added at 1,056 each. The modification is NOT a separate contract, but remaining goods are distinct from those already transferred, so paragraph 21(a) applies prospectively. Thirty of the remaining goods are then transferred. Find revenue for those thirty.
explanation: Prospective remaining consideration = 100 × 1,320 + 50 × 1,056. Divide by 150 remaining goods, then multiply by 30 = 36,960.00. Do not retrospectively revise revenue on goods already transferred.

title: FVTPL acquisition expense • case 32
prompt: A financial asset is acquired at fair value LKR 1,440,000 and is classified at FVTPL. Directly attributable broker costs are 36,000, paid separately. No fair-value change occurs immediately after purchase. Find the immediate profit-or-loss expense from acquiring this asset.
explanation: Transaction costs on an FVTPL asset are expensed. Initial asset carrying amount is fair value 1,440,000; immediate acquisition expense is 36,000.00.

title: Collateral cash-shortfall discounting • case 32
prompt: A credit loss scenario has a contractual receipt of LKR 1,800,000 due in one year. The ONLY expected recovery at that same date is collateral sale proceeds of 1,180,000, less sale costs of 82,000. Scenario probability is 100% and original EIR is 10%. Collateral is an integral contractual credit enhancement and not separately recognised. Find discounted ECL.
explanation: One-year shortfall = contractual receipt − net collateral recovery = 1,800,000 − (1,180,000 − 82,000). Discount that shortfall at 10%: 638,181.82. Do not ignore recovery costs or discount only one side of same-date cash flows.

title: Three-band provision matrix • case 32
prompt: Under the simplified lifetime-ECL approach, supported adjusted loss rates are 1% on current receivables of LKR 1,640,000, 5% on past-due balances of 460,000, and 30% on severely overdue balances of 164,000. Rates already include all required forward-looking and discounting effects. Find total loss allowance.
explanation: Apply each appropriate band rate and add: 1,640,000×1% + 460,000×5% + 164,000×30% = 88,600.00. Do not apply one blended band mechanically to all balances.

title: Equity FVOCI profit-or-loss dividend • case 32
prompt: An eligible equity investment has the irrevocable FVOCI election. During the year it gains LKR 184,000 in fair value and earns a dividend of 92,000. Dividend recognition criteria are met and the dividend clearly represents a return on investment, not recovery of cost. There are no other effects. Find income recognised in PROFIT OR LOSS.
explanation: The qualifying dividend of 92,000.00 is profit-or-loss income. The fair-value movement of 184,000 is OCI under this election and is not added to the profit-or-loss amount.

title: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset • case 32
prompt: A loan is sold with full derecognition. Immediately before sale, gross carrying amount is LKR 1,640,000, loss allowance 164,000, and cash proceeds 1,558,000. No accumulated OCI, sale fees or other adjustments exist. Find the derecognition GAIN relative to net carrying amount.
explanation: Net carrying amount = 1,640,000 − 164,000 = 1,476,000. Compare proceeds with that net amount: 1,558,000 − 1,476,000 = 82,000.00 gain. Derecognise both the gross asset and related allowance.
family: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset

title: Non-substantial liability modification gain • case 32
prompt: An amortised-cost liability is modified WITHOUT extinguishment, with no fees. Its carrying amount is LKR 1,320,000. The sole revised payment is 1,518,000 in two years. Original EIR is 10%; the modification is assessed as non-substantial. Find the immediate modification GAIN from recalculating amortised cost at the original EIR.
explanation: Revised amortised cost = 1,518,000/1.10² = 1,254,545.45. Gain = old liability 1,320,000 − revised PV = 65,454.55. The original EIR is retained for this non-extinguishing modification.

title: Credit-risk improvement allowance release • case 32
prompt: A debt asset under the GENERAL ECL model previously had significant credit-risk deterioration and lifetime allowance LKR 164,000. At reporting date the criteria for lifetime ECL are no longer met; required 12-month ECL is 26,000. No write-offs, new assets or other allowance movements occur. Find the impairment reversal in profit or loss.
explanation: When lifetime measurement is no longer required, the general model returns to 12-month ECL. Release the excess allowance: 164,000 − 26,000 = 138,000.00. This is not a receivable under mandatory simplified lifetime ECL.

title: Upstream inventory elimination with tax • case 32
prompt: P and S report profits AFTER their own tax of LKR 3,280,000 and 1,440,000. An upstream inventory sale leaves unrealised profit of 328,000 in group closing inventory. A recoverable DTA is recognised on the full elimination at 30%, with the tax effect in profit or loss. No other consolidation adjustments exist. Find TOTAL consolidated profit, before attribution to owners and NCI.
explanation: Combine separate after-tax profits, eliminate unrealised profit and recognise the recoverable tax benefit: 3,280,000 + 1,440,000 − 328,000 + 98,400.00 = 4,490,400.00. This question asks total group profit, not its attribution.

title: Full-goodwill impairment and owner profit • case 32
prompt: P owns 80% of S all year. Separate after-tax profits are P LKR 2,760,000 and S 1,020,000. Goodwill is recognised on the FULL-goodwill basis and an impairment of 360,000 is attributable to S’s CGU and allocated 80:20 between owners and NCI. No other adjustments or tax effects apply. Find consolidated profit attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Owners receive 80% of S’s profit and bear 80% of the full-goodwill loss: 2,760,000 + 80% × (1,020,000 − 360,000) = 3,288,000.00. Do not charge the owners with 100% of this full-goodwill loss.

title: Partial goodwill CGU gross-up • case 32
prompt: P owns 80% of S. Recognised PARTIAL goodwill is LKR 1,312,000; S’s other net assets in the tested CGU carry at 6,560,000. Recoverable amount of the WHOLE CGU is 7,380,000. Gross up goodwill for unrecognised NCI goodwill when testing; the whole impairment falls within grossed-up goodwill. No tax or other adjustments apply. Find impairment actually recognised on group goodwill.
explanation: Grossed-up goodwill = 1,312,000/80% = 1,640,000.00. Whole-CGU impairment = grossed goodwill + other net assets − recoverable amount = 820,000.00. Only the parent’s 80% goodwill portion is recognised, so recorded loss = 656,000.00.
reference: LKAS 36 Appendix C paras C4–C8; SLFRS 10 para B86

title: Consolidated retained earnings bridge • case 32
prompt: P owns 75% of S. At year end P retained earnings are LKR 4,600,000, and S retained earnings 2,960,000. S retained earnings at acquisition were 1,000,000. Cumulative post-acquisition extra FV depreciation is 164,000. A downstream sale by P leaves unrealised profit of 112,000. No tax, goodwill impairment, dividends recognised by P, OCI or other adjustments apply. Find consolidated retained earnings attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Group owners’ retained earnings = parent RE + 75% of adjusted post-acquisition S reserves − the parent’s downstream unrealised profit: 5,835,000.00. Pre-acquisition reserves do not enter post-acquisition group retained earnings.

title: Loss of control and translation reserve • case 32
prompt: P loses control of a foreign subsidiary. Proceeds are LKR 3,480,000; retained interest FV 820,000; NCI carrying amount 460,000; consolidated net assets INCLUDING goodwill 3,560,000. A cumulative translation GAIN of 164,000, entirely attributable to P, must be reclassified to profit or loss on loss of control. No other effects apply. Find total disposal gain including that reclassification.
explanation: Base gain = proceeds + retained FV + NCI − net assets = 1,200,000.00. Add the parent’s translation gain recycled on disposal: 164,000. Total = 1,364,000.00.
family: Loss of control and translation reserve

title: Residual guarantee expected payment • case 32
prompt: A lessee owes three year-end rentals of LKR 360,000. It guarantees residual value up to 200,000, but the amount EXPECTED to be payable under that guarantee is 62,000 at year three. Discount rate is 10%. No other liability payments exist. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the amount expected to be payable, not automatically the maximum guarantee. Liability = PV of three rentals + 62,000/1.10³ = 941,848.23.

title: Reasonably certain purchase option PV • case 32
prompt: A lease requires three year-end rentals of LKR 310,000, plus a purchase option price of 820,000 payable at year three. Exercise is reasonably certain. Discount rate is 10%. No incentives, other payments or initial prepayments apply. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the reasonably certain purchase price in the liability: PV of rentals + purchase price discounted for three years = 1,387,002.25. Do not omit or leave the future option payment undiscounted.

title: Lease and service component allocation • case 32
prompt: A two-year contract requires bundled payments of LKR 410,000 at each year end. Relative stand-alone prices are equipment lease 200,000 and distinct maintenance 50,000 per year. The lessee does NOT elect to combine components. Lease discount rate is 10%; no other payments exist. Find initial lease liability for the LEASE component only.
explanation: Allocate 200,000/250,000 = 80% of each bundled payment to the lease: 328,000.00. Discount those two lease payments, excluding maintenance, to obtain 569,256.20.

title: Exempt short-term lease rent-free start • case 32
prompt: A twelve-month lease with no purchase option qualifies for the elected short-term exemption. The first three months are rent free, then nine monthly payments of LKR 36,000 are due. The asset is available throughout and straight-line expense is appropriate. Find lease expense for the FIRST six months, ignoring accrual settlement timing.
explanation: Total fixed payments are nine rents. Spread evenly over all twelve months: 36,000 × 9/12 × 6 = 162,000.00. Rent-free months still receive an expense allocation.

title: Sale-and-leaseback rights transferred • case 32
prompt: A transfer qualifies as a sale under SLFRS 15 at fair value LKR 16,400,000; asset carrying amount is 9,200,000. Market-rate leaseback payments have PV 6,560,000. There are no off-market adjustments or variable-payment complications. At inception, what sale gain is recognised for rights TRANSFERRED to the buyer-lessor?
explanation: Total gain = 16,400,000 − 9,200,000 = 7,200,000. Retained-use proportion = lease PV / fair value = 40%. Recognise only the transferred-rights proportion of the gain: 4,320,000.00.

title: Reassessed bargain purchase gain • case 32
prompt: After the required reassessment, final acquisition-date consideration is LKR 3,280,000, NCI fair value is 400,000 and identifiable net assets are 4,920,000. There is no prior holding or other adjustment. Find the bargain purchase gain recognised in profit or loss.
explanation: Net identifiable assets exceed consideration plus NCI: 4,920,000 − 3,280,000 − 400,000 = 1,240,000.00. Reassessment has been completed before recognising the gain.

title: Acquired contingent liability in goodwill • case 32
prompt: Consideration is LKR 5,100,000; NCI FV is 500,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired contingent liability are 3,960,000. The acquired item is a present obligation with reliably measurable FV 360,000 and qualifies for recognition despite non-probable outflow. No tax or other adjustment applies. Find goodwill after recognising it.
explanation: Recognise the qualifying acquired liability: net identifiable assets become 3,960,000 − 360,000. Goodwill = consideration + NCI − adjusted net assets = 2,000,000.00.

title: Separate acquired brand from goodwill • case 32
prompt: Consideration is LKR 4,600,000; NCI FV 600,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired separable brand are 3,880,000. Brand FV is 720,000; tax base is zero and 30% DTL must be recognised. No other adjustments apply. Find goodwill after separate brand and tax recognition.
explanation: An identifiable acquired brand is separate from goodwill. Net addition to identifiable assets = brand FV − 30% DTL = 504,000.00. Goodwill = 4,600,000 + 600,000 − (3,880,000 + 504,000.00) = 816,000.00.

title: Acquisition costs versus issue costs • case 32
prompt: A business acquisition has consideration LKR 2,960,000. Additional costs are acquisition advisory 164,000, qualifying equity-issue costs 70,000 and qualifying debt-issue costs 40,000. The issue costs follow their relevant standards, and no immediate debt-cost amortisation or other expense arises this period. Find the immediate acquisition-related PROFIT-OR-LOSS expense from these costs.
explanation: Expense advisory acquisition costs of 164,000.00. Qualifying equity and debt issuance costs follow their respective standards and are not added to this immediate acquisition-service expense or goodwill.

title: Temporary difference and enacted rate change • case 32
prompt: A taxable temporary difference opens at LKR 200,000 with a DTL measured at 25%. At year end the difference is 460,000 and the enacted rate expected on reversal is 30%. Both the underlying movements and rate change belong in profit or loss. No other tax movements exist. Find deferred tax expense for the year.
explanation: Opening DTL = 200,000×25% = 50,000. Closing DTL = 460,000×30% = 138,000.00. Expense is the full increase, including rate remeasurement: 88,000.00. Rates are exercise assumptions.
family: Temporary difference and enacted rate change

title: Revalued non-depreciable land tax basis • case 32
prompt: Non-depreciable land is revalued from cost LKR 1,640,000 to fair value 2,460,000; tax base remains cost. The enacted rate for recovery through SALE is 20%, while a 30% use rate would otherwise apply. The revaluation and associated tax go to OCI. No other effects exist. Find the net OCI revaluation increase after deferred tax.
explanation: For this non-depreciable revalued asset, measure tax consequences on recovery through sale: DTL = (2,460,000 − 1,640,000)×20%. Net OCI increase = gross uplift less that DTL = 656,000.00.

title: Current tax reconciliation and prepayment • case 32
prompt: Accounting pretax profit is LKR 3,600,000. It includes a permanently non-deductible fine of 164,000, exempt income of 50,000, and warranty expense of 360,000 deductible only on payment. Current-year warranty payments of 80,000 are deductible and were charged against the provision, not current profit. Tax rate is 30%; tax prepayments are 300,000. No other tax adjustments exist. Find closing CURRENT tax payable, not total tax expense.
explanation: Taxable profit = 3,600,000 + fine 164,000 − exempt income 50,000 + provision expense 360,000 − deductible payments 80,000 = 3,994,000. Current tax less prepaid 300,000 = 898,200.00. Deferred tax is separate.

title: Consolidated inventory tax difference • case 32
prompt: After eliminating an intragroup profit, inventory carries in consolidated statements at LKR 984,000. Its tax base in the buyer’s tax jurisdiction is 1,476,000. The buyer’s enacted rate is 30%; sufficient taxable profit is probable. No offsetting, exception or other tax effects apply. Find the consolidated DTA on this inventory.
explanation: The consolidated carrying amount is below tax base, creating a deductible temporary difference of 492,000. Use the buyer’s relevant tax rate: difference ×30% = 147,600.00.

title: Depreciation after recognised impairment • case 32
prompt: Immediately before an impairment, equipment carries at LKR 1,640,000. Recoverable amount is 1,020,000 and impairment is recognised. After that date it has four years’ remaining useful life and residual value 100,000. Straight-line depreciation is appropriate; no further revaluation or impairment applies. Find depreciation for the next FULL year.
explanation: First reduce the asset to recoverable amount 1,020,000. Thereafter allocate revised depreciable amount over remaining life: (1,020,000 − 100,000)/4 = 230,000.00.

title: Allocated headquarters in CGU impairment • case 32
prompt: CGU A carries operating assets of LKR 920,000; CGU B carries 400,000. A headquarters asset of 200,000 can be allocated reasonably and consistently in proportion to those operating-asset amounts. A’s recoverable amount INCLUDING its headquarters share is 810,000. No goodwill or other assets exist. Find the impairment loss for A including its allocation.
explanation: Allocate headquarters to A: 200,000 × 920,000/(920,000+400,000) = 139,393.94. Tested A carrying amount is 1,059,393.94. Impairment versus recoverable amount 810,000 = 249,393.94.

title: Break-even value-in-use cash flow • case 32
prompt: An asset carries at LKR 1,640,000. Its fair value less costs of disposal is lower. A valid VIU model uses THREE equal year-end operating cash inflows, plus 100,000 net disposal proceeds at year three, discounted at 10%. What minimum equal ANNUAL operating cash inflow makes VIU exactly equal carrying amount? Ignore tax and other adjustments.
explanation: Let annual flow be X. X×(1/1.10 + 1/1.10² + 1/1.10³) + 100,000/1.10³ = 1,640,000. Solve for X = 629,256.80. This sensitivity calculation identifies the VIU break-even point.

title: Discounted warranty expected-value portfolio • case 32
prompt: A present warranty obligation covers 1,640 products. Per product, probabilities are 70% no defect, 25% a minor repair costing LKR 400, and 5% a major repair costing 2,000. All expected payments occur exactly in TWO years. Outflow for the portfolio is probable; appropriate discount rate is 10% with no risk double counting. Find the provision.
explanation: Expected cash payment = 1,640×(25%×400 + 5%×2,000) = 328,000.0. Discount two years at 10%: 328,000.0/1.10² = 271,074.38. The probability assessment applies to the portfolio.

title: Provision movement with revised estimate • case 32
prompt: A discounted provision opens at LKR 820,000. Unwinding for a full year is at 8%. A 100,000 settlement occurs at the year END, after unwinding. At that same reporting date, a new estimate increases the remaining provision by 114,000. No other changes occur. Find closing provision.
explanation: Closing = opening + 8% unwinding − year-end settlement + estimate increase: 820,000×1.08 −100,000 +114,000 = 899,600.00. Classification of the estimate change’s counterpart is assessed separately.

title: Revaluation increase after earlier loss • case 32
prompt: PPE carries at LKR 920,000 before revaluation and is revalued to 1,640,000. A prior revaluation decrease on THIS asset of 214,000 was recognised in profit or loss and has not been reversed. No tax effects apply. Find the current increase recognised in OCI after reversing the eligible prior loss in profit or loss.
explanation: Gross increase = 1,640,000 − 920,000 = 720,000. First recognise 214,000 in profit or loss to reverse the prior decrease. Remaining 506,000.00 is OCI revaluation surplus.

title: Nine-month depreciation and disposal gain • case 32
prompt: Equipment cost LKR 1,840,000, residual value 200,000 and useful life five years, straight-line. Two FULL years’ depreciation were recognised before this year. It is sold after nine months of the current year for 1,330,000. It was not previously held for sale and no impairment or revaluation applies. Find disposal GAIN after the required nine-month depreciation.
explanation: Annual depreciation = (1,840,000−200,000)/5. Deduct two full years and another 9/12 year from cost to obtain disposal-date carrying amount 938,000.00. Gain = proceeds − that amount = 392,000.00.

title: Customer collections with a write-off • case 32
prompt: All sales are on credit. Revenue is LKR 4,600,000; opening GROSS trade receivables are 600,000; closing GROSS receivables are 1,120,000. Receivables of 132,000 were written off during the year. There are no taxes, returns, contract balances, acquisitions or exchange changes. Find cash collected from customers.
explanation: Gross receivable roll-forward: opening + credit sales − cash receipts − write-offs = closing. Thus receipts = 4,600,000+600,000−1,120,000−132,000 = 3,948,000.00. Write-offs are not cash receipts.

title: Loan funding net cash effect • case 32
prompt: A company receives cash loan proceeds of LKR 1,640,000 and immediately pays a directly attributable lender issue fee of 36,000. Both payments are classified as financing cash flows in this case. No other cash movement occurs. Find the NET financing cash inflow from these two cash movements; this question does not require net line-item presentation.
explanation: Net financing cash effect = proceeds − cash fee = 1,640,000 − 36,000.00 = 1,604,000.00. Effective-interest amortisation later is not another inception cash payment.

title: Item-by-item NRV without offsetting headroom • case 32
prompt: Two unrelated inventory lines require separate NRV tests. A has 260 units, cost LKR 1,000 and NRV 900 each. B has 164 units, cost 1,000 and NRV 1,200 each. There is no basis to group them for the write-down test. Find TOTAL closing inventory carrying amount.
explanation: Carry A at 900 per unit and B at its lower cost of 1,000. Total = 260×900 + 164×1,000 = 398,000.00. B’s NRV headroom cannot offset A’s write-down.

title: Units-of-production intangible amortisation • case 32
prompt: A finite-life production licence costs LKR 1,540,000, has zero residual value, and is expected to support 150,000 units in total. Actual output this year is 46,000 units. A units-of-production method reliably reflects consumption and the asset was available throughout. No impairment or estimate change applies. Find annual amortisation.
explanation: Apply the supported consumption pattern: amortisation = 1,540,000 × 46,000/150,000 = 472,266.67. It is the share of expected lifetime production consumed, not an automatic straight-line charge.

title: Profit after suspended associate losses • case 32
prompt: An equity-method investment and relevant long-term interests were previously reduced to zero. Unrecognised share of prior losses totals LKR 144,000; the investor has no obligation and made no support payments. In the current year its share of associate profit is 216,000. No other adjustments or changes in interest apply. Find the share of profit that can now be RECOGNISED.
explanation: First absorb unrecognised prior losses before resuming recognised profit. Recognised amount = current profit share 216,000 − prior unrecognised losses 144,000 = 72,000.00.

title: Return recovery asset net of costs • case 33
prompt: A retailer has transferred 1,825 products. It expects 73 to be returned. Each returned product originally cost LKR 600; expected recovery handling is 20 per item and expected value deterioration is 30 per item. Estimates meet the relevant requirements. Find the separate asset for the right to recover returned products, excluding the refund liability.
explanation: Recovery asset = original carrying amount of expected returns less recovery costs and potential value decrease: 73 × (600 − 20 − 30) = 40,150.00. It is assessed separately from the customer refund liability.
family: Return recovery asset net of costs

title: Retrospective volume rebate true-up • case 33
prompt: A customer’s annual purchases reach 13,300 units at list price LKR 200. Crossing the threshold entitles it to a 5% retrospective rebate on ALL units. Cumulative revenue before this new supported estimate equals full list price; no rebate was previously accrued. The constraint permits the estimate. Find the reduction in cumulative revenue required now.
explanation: The revised transaction price reflects the retrospective rebate on all units. Revenue reduction = 13,300 × 200 × 5% = 133,000.00. Recognise the corresponding refund obligation as appropriate.

title: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation • case 33
prompt: A bundle has distinct goods A and B with stand-alone prices LKR 365,000 and 630,000. Total transaction price is 912,000. ALL paragraph 82 criteria demonstrate that the whole 83,000 discount relates only to A. A transfers now; B is not yet delivered. Find revenue recognised for A.
explanation: The specified discount-allocation exception applies. Allocate all 83,000 discount to A: 365,000 − 83,000 = 282,000.00. Do not default to relative allocation when the exception’s criteria are met.
family: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation

title: Three obligations and partial service • case 33
prompt: A contract price of LKR 2,190,000 covers goods A, goods B and twelve months of distinct support. Stand-alone prices are 600,000, 300,000 and 300,000 respectively. A is delivered, B is not, and six months of evenly provided support are complete. No allocation exception applies. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise allocation to A plus half of support: 2,190,000 × (600,000 + 150,000) / 1,200,000 = 1,368,750.00. B’s allocation remains unrecognised as revenue.

title: Progress excluding abnormal waste • case 33
prompt: An over-time contract has transaction price LKR 13,300,000. Costs incurred are 5,320,000, including abnormal waste of 266,000 that does not depict progress. Expected TOTAL productive costs excluding that waste are 10,640,000. Cost-to-cost is appropriate after excluding the waste; no other adjustment applies. Find cumulative revenue, not profit.
explanation: Exclude abnormal waste from the progress numerator. Productive progress = (5,320,000 − 266,000) / 10,640,000. Revenue = transaction price × that progress = 6,317,500.00. The wasted cost is not a revenue-producing input.

title: Uninstalled materials without margin • case 33
prompt: A single over-time construction obligation has price LKR 16,600,000. All B19(b) conditions justify recognising revenue equal to cost for significant uninstalled materials of 3,320,000 already controlled by the customer. Other productive costs incurred are 2,490,000; expected total OTHER costs are 9,960,000. No revenue was previously recognised. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise material revenue without margin: 3,320,000. Recognise the remaining price using other-cost progress: (16,600,000 − 3,320,000) × 2,490,000/9,960,000. Total revenue = 6,640,000.00.

title: Agent commission after collection • case 33
prompt: An intermediary is an AGENT and collects customer cash of LKR 2,650,000 for a completed supplier service. It must remit 88% to the supplier and is entitled to the remaining 12% commission. It controls neither the underlying service nor any distinct extra service, and there is no tax. Find its revenue.
explanation: An agent recognises its fee or commission, not the supplier’s gross billings: 2,650,000 × 12% = 318,000.00. The amount due to the supplier is separately accounted for.

title: Distinct remaining goods blended prospectively • case 33
prompt: At modification, 100 distinct goods remain under an existing contract at LKR 1,330 each. Another 50 distinct goods are added at 1,064 each. The modification is NOT a separate contract, but remaining goods are distinct from those already transferred, so paragraph 21(a) applies prospectively. Thirty of the remaining goods are then transferred. Find revenue for those thirty.
explanation: Prospective remaining consideration = 100 × 1,330 + 50 × 1,064. Divide by 150 remaining goods, then multiply by 30 = 37,240.00. Do not retrospectively revise revenue on goods already transferred.

title: FVTPL acquisition expense • case 33
prompt: A financial asset is acquired at fair value LKR 1,460,000 and is classified at FVTPL. Directly attributable broker costs are 36,500, paid separately. No fair-value change occurs immediately after purchase. Find the immediate profit-or-loss expense from acquiring this asset.
explanation: Transaction costs on an FVTPL asset are expensed. Initial asset carrying amount is fair value 1,460,000; immediate acquisition expense is 36,500.00.

title: Collateral cash-shortfall discounting • case 33
prompt: A credit loss scenario has a contractual receipt of LKR 1,825,000 due in one year. The ONLY expected recovery at that same date is collateral sale proceeds of 1,195,000, less sale costs of 83,000. Scenario probability is 100% and original EIR is 10%. Collateral is an integral contractual credit enhancement and not separately recognised. Find discounted ECL.
explanation: One-year shortfall = contractual receipt − net collateral recovery = 1,825,000 − (1,195,000 − 83,000). Discount that shortfall at 10%: 648,181.82. Do not ignore recovery costs or discount only one side of same-date cash flows.

title: Three-band provision matrix • case 33
prompt: Under the simplified lifetime-ECL approach, supported adjusted loss rates are 1% on current receivables of LKR 1,660,000, 5% on past-due balances of 465,000, and 30% on severely overdue balances of 166,000. Rates already include all required forward-looking and discounting effects. Find total loss allowance.
explanation: Apply each appropriate band rate and add: 1,660,000×1% + 465,000×5% + 166,000×30% = 89,650.00. Do not apply one blended band mechanically to all balances.

title: Equity FVOCI profit-or-loss dividend • case 33
prompt: An eligible equity investment has the irrevocable FVOCI election. During the year it gains LKR 186,000 in fair value and earns a dividend of 93,000. Dividend recognition criteria are met and the dividend clearly represents a return on investment, not recovery of cost. There are no other effects. Find income recognised in PROFIT OR LOSS.
explanation: The qualifying dividend of 93,000.00 is profit-or-loss income. The fair-value movement of 186,000 is OCI under this election and is not added to the profit-or-loss amount.

title: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset • case 33
prompt: A loan is sold with full derecognition. Immediately before sale, gross carrying amount is LKR 1,660,000, loss allowance 166,000, and cash proceeds 1,577,000. No accumulated OCI, sale fees or other adjustments exist. Find the derecognition GAIN relative to net carrying amount.
explanation: Net carrying amount = 1,660,000 − 166,000 = 1,494,000. Compare proceeds with that net amount: 1,577,000 − 1,494,000 = 83,000.00 gain. Derecognise both the gross asset and related allowance.
family: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset

title: Non-substantial liability modification gain • case 33
prompt: An amortised-cost liability is modified WITHOUT extinguishment, with no fees. Its carrying amount is LKR 1,330,000. The sole revised payment is 1,529,500 in two years. Original EIR is 10%; the modification is assessed as non-substantial. Find the immediate modification GAIN from recalculating amortised cost at the original EIR.
explanation: Revised amortised cost = 1,529,500/1.10² = 1,264,049.59. Gain = old liability 1,330,000 − revised PV = 65,950.41. The original EIR is retained for this non-extinguishing modification.

title: Credit-risk improvement allowance release • case 33
prompt: A debt asset under the GENERAL ECL model previously had significant credit-risk deterioration and lifetime allowance LKR 166,000. At reporting date the criteria for lifetime ECL are no longer met; required 12-month ECL is 26,500. No write-offs, new assets or other allowance movements occur. Find the impairment reversal in profit or loss.
explanation: When lifetime measurement is no longer required, the general model returns to 12-month ECL. Release the excess allowance: 166,000 − 26,500 = 139,500.00. This is not a receivable under mandatory simplified lifetime ECL.

title: Upstream inventory elimination with tax • case 33
prompt: P and S report profits AFTER their own tax of LKR 3,320,000 and 1,460,000. An upstream inventory sale leaves unrealised profit of 332,000 in group closing inventory. A recoverable DTA is recognised on the full elimination at 30%, with the tax effect in profit or loss. No other consolidation adjustments exist. Find TOTAL consolidated profit, before attribution to owners and NCI.
explanation: Combine separate after-tax profits, eliminate unrealised profit and recognise the recoverable tax benefit: 3,320,000 + 1,460,000 − 332,000 + 99,600.00 = 4,547,600.00. This question asks total group profit, not its attribution.

title: Full-goodwill impairment and owner profit • case 33
prompt: P owns 80% of S all year. Separate after-tax profits are P LKR 2,790,000 and S 1,030,000. Goodwill is recognised on the FULL-goodwill basis and an impairment of 365,000 is attributable to S’s CGU and allocated 80:20 between owners and NCI. No other adjustments or tax effects apply. Find consolidated profit attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Owners receive 80% of S’s profit and bear 80% of the full-goodwill loss: 2,790,000 + 80% × (1,030,000 − 365,000) = 3,322,000.00. Do not charge the owners with 100% of this full-goodwill loss.

title: Partial goodwill CGU gross-up • case 33
