prompt: P owns 80% of S. Recognised PARTIAL goodwill is LKR 1,328,000; S’s other net assets in the tested CGU carry at 6,640,000. Recoverable amount of the WHOLE CGU is 7,470,000. Gross up goodwill for unrecognised NCI goodwill when testing; the whole impairment falls within grossed-up goodwill. No tax or other adjustments apply. Find impairment actually recognised on group goodwill.
explanation: Grossed-up goodwill = 1,328,000/80% = 1,660,000.00. Whole-CGU impairment = grossed goodwill + other net assets − recoverable amount = 830,000.00. Only the parent’s 80% goodwill portion is recognised, so recorded loss = 664,000.00.
reference: LKAS 36 Appendix C paras C4–C8; SLFRS 10 para B86

title: Consolidated retained earnings bridge • case 33
prompt: P owns 75% of S. At year end P retained earnings are LKR 4,650,000, and S retained earnings 2,990,000. S retained earnings at acquisition were 1,000,000. Cumulative post-acquisition extra FV depreciation is 166,000. A downstream sale by P leaves unrealised profit of 113,000. No tax, goodwill impairment, dividends recognised by P, OCI or other adjustments apply. Find consolidated retained earnings attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Group owners’ retained earnings = parent RE + 75% of adjusted post-acquisition S reserves − the parent’s downstream unrealised profit: 5,905,000.00. Pre-acquisition reserves do not enter post-acquisition group retained earnings.

title: Loss of control and translation reserve • case 33
prompt: P loses control of a foreign subsidiary. Proceeds are LKR 3,520,000; retained interest FV 830,000; NCI carrying amount 465,000; consolidated net assets INCLUDING goodwill 3,590,000. A cumulative translation GAIN of 166,000, entirely attributable to P, must be reclassified to profit or loss on loss of control. No other effects apply. Find total disposal gain including that reclassification.
explanation: Base gain = proceeds + retained FV + NCI − net assets = 1,225,000.00. Add the parent’s translation gain recycled on disposal: 166,000. Total = 1,391,000.00.
family: Loss of control and translation reserve

title: Residual guarantee expected payment • case 33
prompt: A lessee owes three year-end rentals of LKR 365,000. It guarantees residual value up to 200,000, but the amount EXPECTED to be payable under that guarantee is 63,000 at year three. Discount rate is 10%. No other liability payments exist. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the amount expected to be payable, not automatically the maximum guarantee. Liability = PV of three rentals + 63,000/1.10³ = 955,033.81.

title: Reasonably certain purchase option PV • case 33
prompt: A lease requires three year-end rentals of LKR 315,000, plus a purchase option price of 830,000 payable at year three. Exercise is reasonably certain. Discount rate is 10%. No incentives, other payments or initial prepayments apply. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the reasonably certain purchase price in the liability: PV of rentals + purchase price discounted for three years = 1,406,949.66. Do not omit or leave the future option payment undiscounted.

title: Lease and service component allocation • case 33
prompt: A two-year contract requires bundled payments of LKR 415,000 at each year end. Relative stand-alone prices are equipment lease 200,000 and distinct maintenance 50,000 per year. The lessee does NOT elect to combine components. Lease discount rate is 10%; no other payments exist. Find initial lease liability for the LEASE component only.
explanation: Allocate 200,000/250,000 = 80% of each bundled payment to the lease: 332,000.00. Discount those two lease payments, excluding maintenance, to obtain 576,198.35.

title: Exempt short-term lease rent-free start • case 33
prompt: A twelve-month lease with no purchase option qualifies for the elected short-term exemption. The first three months are rent free, then nine monthly payments of LKR 36,500 are due. The asset is available throughout and straight-line expense is appropriate. Find lease expense for the FIRST six months, ignoring accrual settlement timing.
explanation: Total fixed payments are nine rents. Spread evenly over all twelve months: 36,500 × 9/12 × 6 = 164,250.00. Rent-free months still receive an expense allocation.

title: Sale-and-leaseback rights transferred • case 33
prompt: A transfer qualifies as a sale under SLFRS 15 at fair value LKR 16,600,000; asset carrying amount is 9,300,000. Market-rate leaseback payments have PV 6,640,000. There are no off-market adjustments or variable-payment complications. At inception, what sale gain is recognised for rights TRANSFERRED to the buyer-lessor?
explanation: Total gain = 16,600,000 − 9,300,000 = 7,300,000. Retained-use proportion = lease PV / fair value = 40%. Recognise only the transferred-rights proportion of the gain: 4,380,000.00.

title: Reassessed bargain purchase gain • case 33
prompt: After the required reassessment, final acquisition-date consideration is LKR 3,320,000, NCI fair value is 400,000 and identifiable net assets are 4,980,000. There is no prior holding or other adjustment. Find the bargain purchase gain recognised in profit or loss.
explanation: Net identifiable assets exceed consideration plus NCI: 4,980,000 − 3,320,000 − 400,000 = 1,260,000.00. Reassessment has been completed before recognising the gain.

title: Acquired contingent liability in goodwill • case 33
prompt: Consideration is LKR 5,150,000; NCI FV is 500,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired contingent liability are 3,990,000. The acquired item is a present obligation with reliably measurable FV 365,000 and qualifies for recognition despite non-probable outflow. No tax or other adjustment applies. Find goodwill after recognising it.
explanation: Recognise the qualifying acquired liability: net identifiable assets become 3,990,000 − 365,000. Goodwill = consideration + NCI − adjusted net assets = 2,025,000.00.

title: Separate acquired brand from goodwill • case 33
prompt: Consideration is LKR 4,650,000; NCI FV 600,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired separable brand are 3,920,000. Brand FV is 730,000; tax base is zero and 30% DTL must be recognised. No other adjustments apply. Find goodwill after separate brand and tax recognition.
explanation: An identifiable acquired brand is separate from goodwill. Net addition to identifiable assets = brand FV − 30% DTL = 511,000.00. Goodwill = 4,650,000 + 600,000 − (3,920,000 + 511,000.00) = 819,000.00.

title: Acquisition costs versus issue costs • case 33
prompt: A business acquisition has consideration LKR 2,990,000. Additional costs are acquisition advisory 166,000, qualifying equity-issue costs 70,000 and qualifying debt-issue costs 40,000. The issue costs follow their relevant standards, and no immediate debt-cost amortisation or other expense arises this period. Find the immediate acquisition-related PROFIT-OR-LOSS expense from these costs.
explanation: Expense advisory acquisition costs of 166,000.00. Qualifying equity and debt issuance costs follow their respective standards and are not added to this immediate acquisition-service expense or goodwill.

title: Temporary difference and enacted rate change • case 33
prompt: A taxable temporary difference opens at LKR 200,000 with a DTL measured at 25%. At year end the difference is 465,000 and the enacted rate expected on reversal is 30%. Both the underlying movements and rate change belong in profit or loss. No other tax movements exist. Find deferred tax expense for the year.
explanation: Opening DTL = 200,000×25% = 50,000. Closing DTL = 465,000×30% = 139,500.00. Expense is the full increase, including rate remeasurement: 89,500.00. Rates are exercise assumptions.
family: Temporary difference and enacted rate change

title: Revalued non-depreciable land tax basis • case 33
prompt: Non-depreciable land is revalued from cost LKR 1,660,000 to fair value 2,490,000; tax base remains cost. The enacted rate for recovery through SALE is 20%, while a 30% use rate would otherwise apply. The revaluation and associated tax go to OCI. No other effects exist. Find the net OCI revaluation increase after deferred tax.
explanation: For this non-depreciable revalued asset, measure tax consequences on recovery through sale: DTL = (2,490,000 − 1,660,000)×20%. Net OCI increase = gross uplift less that DTL = 664,000.00.

title: Current tax reconciliation and prepayment • case 33
prompt: Accounting pretax profit is LKR 3,650,000. It includes a permanently non-deductible fine of 166,000, exempt income of 50,000, and warranty expense of 365,000 deductible only on payment. Current-year warranty payments of 80,000 are deductible and were charged against the provision, not current profit. Tax rate is 30%; tax prepayments are 300,000. No other tax adjustments exist. Find closing CURRENT tax payable, not total tax expense.
explanation: Taxable profit = 3,650,000 + fine 166,000 − exempt income 50,000 + provision expense 365,000 − deductible payments 80,000 = 4,051,000. Current tax less prepaid 300,000 = 915,300.00. Deferred tax is separate.

title: Consolidated inventory tax difference • case 33
prompt: After eliminating an intragroup profit, inventory carries in consolidated statements at LKR 996,000. Its tax base in the buyer’s tax jurisdiction is 1,494,000. The buyer’s enacted rate is 30%; sufficient taxable profit is probable. No offsetting, exception or other tax effects apply. Find the consolidated DTA on this inventory.
explanation: The consolidated carrying amount is below tax base, creating a deductible temporary difference of 498,000. Use the buyer’s relevant tax rate: difference ×30% = 149,400.00.

title: Depreciation after recognised impairment • case 33
prompt: Immediately before an impairment, equipment carries at LKR 1,660,000. Recoverable amount is 1,030,000 and impairment is recognised. After that date it has four years’ remaining useful life and residual value 100,000. Straight-line depreciation is appropriate; no further revaluation or impairment applies. Find depreciation for the next FULL year.
explanation: First reduce the asset to recoverable amount 1,030,000. Thereafter allocate revised depreciable amount over remaining life: (1,030,000 − 100,000)/4 = 232,500.00.

title: Allocated headquarters in CGU impairment • case 33
prompt: CGU A carries operating assets of LKR 930,000; CGU B carries 400,000. A headquarters asset of 200,000 can be allocated reasonably and consistently in proportion to those operating-asset amounts. A’s recoverable amount INCLUDING its headquarters share is 815,000. No goodwill or other assets exist. Find the impairment loss for A including its allocation.
explanation: Allocate headquarters to A: 200,000 × 930,000/(930,000+400,000) = 139,849.62. Tested A carrying amount is 1,069,849.62. Impairment versus recoverable amount 815,000 = 254,849.62.

title: Break-even value-in-use cash flow • case 33
prompt: An asset carries at LKR 1,660,000. Its fair value less costs of disposal is lower. A valid VIU model uses THREE equal year-end operating cash inflows, plus 100,000 net disposal proceeds at year three, discounted at 10%. What minimum equal ANNUAL operating cash inflow makes VIU exactly equal carrying amount? Ignore tax and other adjustments.
explanation: Let annual flow be X. X×(1/1.10 + 1/1.10² + 1/1.10³) + 100,000/1.10³ = 1,660,000. Solve for X = 637,299.09. This sensitivity calculation identifies the VIU break-even point.

title: Discounted warranty expected-value portfolio • case 33
prompt: A present warranty obligation covers 1,660 products. Per product, probabilities are 70% no defect, 25% a minor repair costing LKR 400, and 5% a major repair costing 2,000. All expected payments occur exactly in TWO years. Outflow for the portfolio is probable; appropriate discount rate is 10% with no risk double counting. Find the provision.
explanation: Expected cash payment = 1,660×(25%×400 + 5%×2,000) = 332,000.0. Discount two years at 10%: 332,000.0/1.10² = 274,380.17. The probability assessment applies to the portfolio.

title: Provision movement with revised estimate • case 33
prompt: A discounted provision opens at LKR 830,000. Unwinding for a full year is at 8%. A 100,000 settlement occurs at the year END, after unwinding. At that same reporting date, a new estimate increases the remaining provision by 116,000. No other changes occur. Find closing provision.
explanation: Closing = opening + 8% unwinding − year-end settlement + estimate increase: 830,000×1.08 −100,000 +116,000 = 912,400.00. Classification of the estimate change’s counterpart is assessed separately.

title: Revaluation increase after earlier loss • case 33
prompt: PPE carries at LKR 930,000 before revaluation and is revalued to 1,660,000. A prior revaluation decrease on THIS asset of 216,000 was recognised in profit or loss and has not been reversed. No tax effects apply. Find the current increase recognised in OCI after reversing the eligible prior loss in profit or loss.
explanation: Gross increase = 1,660,000 − 930,000 = 730,000. First recognise 216,000 in profit or loss to reverse the prior decrease. Remaining 514,000.00 is OCI revaluation surplus.

title: Nine-month depreciation and disposal gain • case 33
prompt: Equipment cost LKR 1,860,000, residual value 200,000 and useful life five years, straight-line. Two FULL years’ depreciation were recognised before this year. It is sold after nine months of the current year for 1,345,000. It was not previously held for sale and no impairment or revaluation applies. Find disposal GAIN after the required nine-month depreciation.
explanation: Annual depreciation = (1,860,000−200,000)/5. Deduct two full years and another 9/12 year from cost to obtain disposal-date carrying amount 947,000.00. Gain = proceeds − that amount = 398,000.00.

title: Customer collections with a write-off • case 33
prompt: All sales are on credit. Revenue is LKR 4,650,000; opening GROSS trade receivables are 600,000; closing GROSS receivables are 1,130,000. Receivables of 133,000 were written off during the year. There are no taxes, returns, contract balances, acquisitions or exchange changes. Find cash collected from customers.
explanation: Gross receivable roll-forward: opening + credit sales − cash receipts − write-offs = closing. Thus receipts = 4,650,000+600,000−1,130,000−133,000 = 3,987,000.00. Write-offs are not cash receipts.

title: Loan funding net cash effect • case 33
prompt: A company receives cash loan proceeds of LKR 1,660,000 and immediately pays a directly attributable lender issue fee of 36,500. Both payments are classified as financing cash flows in this case. No other cash movement occurs. Find the NET financing cash inflow from these two cash movements; this question does not require net line-item presentation.
explanation: Net financing cash effect = proceeds − cash fee = 1,660,000 − 36,500.00 = 1,623,500.00. Effective-interest amortisation later is not another inception cash payment.

title: Item-by-item NRV without offsetting headroom • case 33
prompt: Two unrelated inventory lines require separate NRV tests. A has 265 units, cost LKR 1,000 and NRV 900 each. B has 166 units, cost 1,000 and NRV 1,200 each. There is no basis to group them for the write-down test. Find TOTAL closing inventory carrying amount.
explanation: Carry A at 900 per unit and B at its lower cost of 1,000. Total = 265×900 + 166×1,000 = 404,500.00. B’s NRV headroom cannot offset A’s write-down.

title: Units-of-production intangible amortisation • case 33
prompt: A finite-life production licence costs LKR 1,560,000, has zero residual value, and is expected to support 150,000 units in total. Actual output this year is 46,500 units. A units-of-production method reliably reflects consumption and the asset was available throughout. No impairment or estimate change applies. Find annual amortisation.
explanation: Apply the supported consumption pattern: amortisation = 1,560,000 × 46,500/150,000 = 483,600.00. It is the share of expected lifetime production consumed, not an automatic straight-line charge.

title: Profit after suspended associate losses • case 33
prompt: An equity-method investment and relevant long-term interests were previously reduced to zero. Unrecognised share of prior losses totals LKR 146,000; the investor has no obligation and made no support payments. In the current year its share of associate profit is 219,000. No other adjustments or changes in interest apply. Find the share of profit that can now be RECOGNISED.
explanation: First absorb unrecognised prior losses before resuming recognised profit. Recognised amount = current profit share 219,000 − prior unrecognised losses 146,000 = 73,000.00.

title: Return recovery asset net of costs • case 34
prompt: A retailer has transferred 1,850 products. It expects 74 to be returned. Each returned product originally cost LKR 600; expected recovery handling is 20 per item and expected value deterioration is 30 per item. Estimates meet the relevant requirements. Find the separate asset for the right to recover returned products, excluding the refund liability.
explanation: Recovery asset = original carrying amount of expected returns less recovery costs and potential value decrease: 74 × (600 − 20 − 30) = 40,700.00. It is assessed separately from the customer refund liability.
family: Return recovery asset net of costs

title: Retrospective volume rebate true-up • case 34
prompt: A customer’s annual purchases reach 13,400 units at list price LKR 200. Crossing the threshold entitles it to a 5% retrospective rebate on ALL units. Cumulative revenue before this new supported estimate equals full list price; no rebate was previously accrued. The constraint permits the estimate. Find the reduction in cumulative revenue required now.
explanation: The revised transaction price reflects the retrospective rebate on all units. Revenue reduction = 13,400 × 200 × 5% = 134,000.00. Recognise the corresponding refund obligation as appropriate.

title: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation • case 34
prompt: A bundle has distinct goods A and B with stand-alone prices LKR 370,000 and 640,000. Total transaction price is 926,000. ALL paragraph 82 criteria demonstrate that the whole 84,000 discount relates only to A. A transfers now; B is not yet delivered. Find revenue recognised for A.
explanation: The specified discount-allocation exception applies. Allocate all 84,000 discount to A: 370,000 − 84,000 = 286,000.00. Do not default to relative allocation when the exception’s criteria are met.
family: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation

title: Three obligations and partial service • case 34
prompt: A contract price of LKR 2,220,000 covers goods A, goods B and twelve months of distinct support. Stand-alone prices are 600,000, 300,000 and 300,000 respectively. A is delivered, B is not, and six months of evenly provided support are complete. No allocation exception applies. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise allocation to A plus half of support: 2,220,000 × (600,000 + 150,000) / 1,200,000 = 1,387,500.00. B’s allocation remains unrecognised as revenue.

title: Progress excluding abnormal waste • case 34
prompt: An over-time contract has transaction price LKR 13,400,000. Costs incurred are 5,360,000, including abnormal waste of 268,000 that does not depict progress. Expected TOTAL productive costs excluding that waste are 10,720,000. Cost-to-cost is appropriate after excluding the waste; no other adjustment applies. Find cumulative revenue, not profit.
explanation: Exclude abnormal waste from the progress numerator. Productive progress = (5,360,000 − 268,000) / 10,720,000. Revenue = transaction price × that progress = 6,365,000.00. The wasted cost is not a revenue-producing input.

title: Uninstalled materials without margin • case 34
prompt: A single over-time construction obligation has price LKR 16,800,000. All B19(b) conditions justify recognising revenue equal to cost for significant uninstalled materials of 3,360,000 already controlled by the customer. Other productive costs incurred are 2,520,000; expected total OTHER costs are 10,080,000. No revenue was previously recognised. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise material revenue without margin: 3,360,000. Recognise the remaining price using other-cost progress: (16,800,000 − 3,360,000) × 2,520,000/10,080,000. Total revenue = 6,720,000.00.

title: Agent commission after collection • case 34
prompt: An intermediary is an AGENT and collects customer cash of LKR 2,700,000 for a completed supplier service. It must remit 88% to the supplier and is entitled to the remaining 12% commission. It controls neither the underlying service nor any distinct extra service, and there is no tax. Find its revenue.
explanation: An agent recognises its fee or commission, not the supplier’s gross billings: 2,700,000 × 12% = 324,000.00. The amount due to the supplier is separately accounted for.

title: Distinct remaining goods blended prospectively • case 34
prompt: At modification, 100 distinct goods remain under an existing contract at LKR 1,340 each. Another 50 distinct goods are added at 1,072 each. The modification is NOT a separate contract, but remaining goods are distinct from those already transferred, so paragraph 21(a) applies prospectively. Thirty of the remaining goods are then transferred. Find revenue for those thirty.
explanation: Prospective remaining consideration = 100 × 1,340 + 50 × 1,072. Divide by 150 remaining goods, then multiply by 30 = 37,520.00. Do not retrospectively revise revenue on goods already transferred.

title: FVTPL acquisition expense • case 34
prompt: A financial asset is acquired at fair value LKR 1,480,000 and is classified at FVTPL. Directly attributable broker costs are 37,000, paid separately. No fair-value change occurs immediately after purchase. Find the immediate profit-or-loss expense from acquiring this asset.
explanation: Transaction costs on an FVTPL asset are expensed. Initial asset carrying amount is fair value 1,480,000; immediate acquisition expense is 37,000.00.

title: Collateral cash-shortfall discounting • case 34
prompt: A credit loss scenario has a contractual receipt of LKR 1,850,000 due in one year. The ONLY expected recovery at that same date is collateral sale proceeds of 1,210,000, less sale costs of 84,000. Scenario probability is 100% and original EIR is 10%. Collateral is an integral contractual credit enhancement and not separately recognised. Find discounted ECL.
explanation: One-year shortfall = contractual receipt − net collateral recovery = 1,850,000 − (1,210,000 − 84,000). Discount that shortfall at 10%: 658,181.82. Do not ignore recovery costs or discount only one side of same-date cash flows.

title: Three-band provision matrix • case 34
prompt: Under the simplified lifetime-ECL approach, supported adjusted loss rates are 1% on current receivables of LKR 1,680,000, 5% on past-due balances of 470,000, and 30% on severely overdue balances of 168,000. Rates already include all required forward-looking and discounting effects. Find total loss allowance.
explanation: Apply each appropriate band rate and add: 1,680,000×1% + 470,000×5% + 168,000×30% = 90,700.00. Do not apply one blended band mechanically to all balances.

title: Equity FVOCI profit-or-loss dividend • case 34
prompt: An eligible equity investment has the irrevocable FVOCI election. During the year it gains LKR 188,000 in fair value and earns a dividend of 94,000. Dividend recognition criteria are met and the dividend clearly represents a return on investment, not recovery of cost. There are no other effects. Find income recognised in PROFIT OR LOSS.
explanation: The qualifying dividend of 94,000.00 is profit-or-loss income. The fair-value movement of 188,000 is OCI under this election and is not added to the profit-or-loss amount.

title: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset • case 34
prompt: A loan is sold with full derecognition. Immediately before sale, gross carrying amount is LKR 1,680,000, loss allowance 168,000, and cash proceeds 1,596,000. No accumulated OCI, sale fees or other adjustments exist. Find the derecognition GAIN relative to net carrying amount.
explanation: Net carrying amount = 1,680,000 − 168,000 = 1,512,000. Compare proceeds with that net amount: 1,596,000 − 1,512,000 = 84,000.00 gain. Derecognise both the gross asset and related allowance.
family: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset

title: Non-substantial liability modification gain • case 34
prompt: An amortised-cost liability is modified WITHOUT extinguishment, with no fees. Its carrying amount is LKR 1,340,000. The sole revised payment is 1,541,000 in two years. Original EIR is 10%; the modification is assessed as non-substantial. Find the immediate modification GAIN from recalculating amortised cost at the original EIR.
explanation: Revised amortised cost = 1,541,000/1.10² = 1,273,553.72. Gain = old liability 1,340,000 − revised PV = 66,446.28. The original EIR is retained for this non-extinguishing modification.

title: Credit-risk improvement allowance release • case 34
prompt: A debt asset under the GENERAL ECL model previously had significant credit-risk deterioration and lifetime allowance LKR 168,000. At reporting date the criteria for lifetime ECL are no longer met; required 12-month ECL is 27,000. No write-offs, new assets or other allowance movements occur. Find the impairment reversal in profit or loss.
explanation: When lifetime measurement is no longer required, the general model returns to 12-month ECL. Release the excess allowance: 168,000 − 27,000 = 141,000.00. This is not a receivable under mandatory simplified lifetime ECL.

title: Upstream inventory elimination with tax • case 34
prompt: P and S report profits AFTER their own tax of LKR 3,360,000 and 1,480,000. An upstream inventory sale leaves unrealised profit of 336,000 in group closing inventory. A recoverable DTA is recognised on the full elimination at 30%, with the tax effect in profit or loss. No other consolidation adjustments exist. Find TOTAL consolidated profit, before attribution to owners and NCI.
explanation: Combine separate after-tax profits, eliminate unrealised profit and recognise the recoverable tax benefit: 3,360,000 + 1,480,000 − 336,000 + 100,800.00 = 4,604,800.00. This question asks total group profit, not its attribution.

title: Full-goodwill impairment and owner profit • case 34
prompt: P owns 80% of S all year. Separate after-tax profits are P LKR 2,820,000 and S 1,040,000. Goodwill is recognised on the FULL-goodwill basis and an impairment of 370,000 is attributable to S’s CGU and allocated 80:20 between owners and NCI. No other adjustments or tax effects apply. Find consolidated profit attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Owners receive 80% of S’s profit and bear 80% of the full-goodwill loss: 2,820,000 + 80% × (1,040,000 − 370,000) = 3,356,000.00. Do not charge the owners with 100% of this full-goodwill loss.

title: Partial goodwill CGU gross-up • case 34
prompt: P owns 80% of S. Recognised PARTIAL goodwill is LKR 1,344,000; S’s other net assets in the tested CGU carry at 6,720,000. Recoverable amount of the WHOLE CGU is 7,560,000. Gross up goodwill for unrecognised NCI goodwill when testing; the whole impairment falls within grossed-up goodwill. No tax or other adjustments apply. Find impairment actually recognised on group goodwill.
explanation: Grossed-up goodwill = 1,344,000/80% = 1,680,000.00. Whole-CGU impairment = grossed goodwill + other net assets − recoverable amount = 840,000.00. Only the parent’s 80% goodwill portion is recognised, so recorded loss = 672,000.00.
reference: LKAS 36 Appendix C paras C4–C8; SLFRS 10 para B86

title: Consolidated retained earnings bridge • case 34
prompt: P owns 75% of S. At year end P retained earnings are LKR 4,700,000, and S retained earnings 3,020,000. S retained earnings at acquisition were 1,000,000. Cumulative post-acquisition extra FV depreciation is 168,000. A downstream sale by P leaves unrealised profit of 114,000. No tax, goodwill impairment, dividends recognised by P, OCI or other adjustments apply. Find consolidated retained earnings attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Group owners’ retained earnings = parent RE + 75% of adjusted post-acquisition S reserves − the parent’s downstream unrealised profit: 5,975,000.00. Pre-acquisition reserves do not enter post-acquisition group retained earnings.

title: Loss of control and translation reserve • case 34
prompt: P loses control of a foreign subsidiary. Proceeds are LKR 3,560,000; retained interest FV 840,000; NCI carrying amount 470,000; consolidated net assets INCLUDING goodwill 3,620,000. A cumulative translation GAIN of 168,000, entirely attributable to P, must be reclassified to profit or loss on loss of control. No other effects apply. Find total disposal gain including that reclassification.
explanation: Base gain = proceeds + retained FV + NCI − net assets = 1,250,000.00. Add the parent’s translation gain recycled on disposal: 168,000. Total = 1,418,000.00.
family: Loss of control and translation reserve

title: Residual guarantee expected payment • case 34
prompt: A lessee owes three year-end rentals of LKR 370,000. It guarantees residual value up to 200,000, but the amount EXPECTED to be payable under that guarantee is 64,000 at year three. Discount rate is 10%. No other liability payments exist. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the amount expected to be payable, not automatically the maximum guarantee. Liability = PV of three rentals + 64,000/1.10³ = 968,219.38.

title: Reasonably certain purchase option PV • case 34
prompt: A lease requires three year-end rentals of LKR 320,000, plus a purchase option price of 840,000 payable at year three. Exercise is reasonably certain. Discount rate is 10%. No incentives, other payments or initial prepayments apply. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the reasonably certain purchase price in the liability: PV of rentals + purchase price discounted for three years = 1,426,897.07. Do not omit or leave the future option payment undiscounted.

title: Lease and service component allocation • case 34
prompt: A two-year contract requires bundled payments of LKR 420,000 at each year end. Relative stand-alone prices are equipment lease 200,000 and distinct maintenance 50,000 per year. The lessee does NOT elect to combine components. Lease discount rate is 10%; no other payments exist. Find initial lease liability for the LEASE component only.
explanation: Allocate 200,000/250,000 = 80% of each bundled payment to the lease: 336,000.00. Discount those two lease payments, excluding maintenance, to obtain 583,140.50.

title: Exempt short-term lease rent-free start • case 34
prompt: A twelve-month lease with no purchase option qualifies for the elected short-term exemption. The first three months are rent free, then nine monthly payments of LKR 37,000 are due. The asset is available throughout and straight-line expense is appropriate. Find lease expense for the FIRST six months, ignoring accrual settlement timing.
explanation: Total fixed payments are nine rents. Spread evenly over all twelve months: 37,000 × 9/12 × 6 = 166,500.00. Rent-free months still receive an expense allocation.

title: Sale-and-leaseback rights transferred • case 34
prompt: A transfer qualifies as a sale under SLFRS 15 at fair value LKR 16,800,000; asset carrying amount is 9,400,000. Market-rate leaseback payments have PV 6,720,000. There are no off-market adjustments or variable-payment complications. At inception, what sale gain is recognised for rights TRANSFERRED to the buyer-lessor?
explanation: Total gain = 16,800,000 − 9,400,000 = 7,400,000. Retained-use proportion = lease PV / fair value = 40%. Recognise only the transferred-rights proportion of the gain: 4,440,000.00.

title: Reassessed bargain purchase gain • case 34
prompt: After the required reassessment, final acquisition-date consideration is LKR 3,360,000, NCI fair value is 400,000 and identifiable net assets are 5,040,000. There is no prior holding or other adjustment. Find the bargain purchase gain recognised in profit or loss.
explanation: Net identifiable assets exceed consideration plus NCI: 5,040,000 − 3,360,000 − 400,000 = 1,280,000.00. Reassessment has been completed before recognising the gain.

title: Acquired contingent liability in goodwill • case 34
prompt: Consideration is LKR 5,200,000; NCI FV is 500,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired contingent liability are 4,020,000. The acquired item is a present obligation with reliably measurable FV 370,000 and qualifies for recognition despite non-probable outflow. No tax or other adjustment applies. Find goodwill after recognising it.
explanation: Recognise the qualifying acquired liability: net identifiable assets become 4,020,000 − 370,000. Goodwill = consideration + NCI − adjusted net assets = 2,050,000.00.

title: Separate acquired brand from goodwill • case 34
prompt: Consideration is LKR 4,700,000; NCI FV 600,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired separable brand are 3,960,000. Brand FV is 740,000; tax base is zero and 30% DTL must be recognised. No other adjustments apply. Find goodwill after separate brand and tax recognition.
explanation: An identifiable acquired brand is separate from goodwill. Net addition to identifiable assets = brand FV − 30% DTL = 518,000.00. Goodwill = 4,700,000 + 600,000 − (3,960,000 + 518,000.00) = 822,000.00.

title: Acquisition costs versus issue costs • case 34
prompt: A business acquisition has consideration LKR 3,020,000. Additional costs are acquisition advisory 168,000, qualifying equity-issue costs 70,000 and qualifying debt-issue costs 40,000. The issue costs follow their relevant standards, and no immediate debt-cost amortisation or other expense arises this period. Find the immediate acquisition-related PROFIT-OR-LOSS expense from these costs.
explanation: Expense advisory acquisition costs of 168,000.00. Qualifying equity and debt issuance costs follow their respective standards and are not added to this immediate acquisition-service expense or goodwill.

title: Temporary difference and enacted rate change • case 34
prompt: A taxable temporary difference opens at LKR 200,000 with a DTL measured at 25%. At year end the difference is 470,000 and the enacted rate expected on reversal is 30%. Both the underlying movements and rate change belong in profit or loss. No other tax movements exist. Find deferred tax expense for the year.
explanation: Opening DTL = 200,000×25% = 50,000. Closing DTL = 470,000×30% = 141,000.00. Expense is the full increase, including rate remeasurement: 91,000.00. Rates are exercise assumptions.
family: Temporary difference and enacted rate change

title: Revalued non-depreciable land tax basis • case 34
prompt: Non-depreciable land is revalued from cost LKR 1,680,000 to fair value 2,520,000; tax base remains cost. The enacted rate for recovery through SALE is 20%, while a 30% use rate would otherwise apply. The revaluation and associated tax go to OCI. No other effects exist. Find the net OCI revaluation increase after deferred tax.
explanation: For this non-depreciable revalued asset, measure tax consequences on recovery through sale: DTL = (2,520,000 − 1,680,000)×20%. Net OCI increase = gross uplift less that DTL = 672,000.00.

title: Current tax reconciliation and prepayment • case 34
prompt: Accounting pretax profit is LKR 3,700,000. It includes a permanently non-deductible fine of 168,000, exempt income of 50,000, and warranty expense of 370,000 deductible only on payment. Current-year warranty payments of 80,000 are deductible and were charged against the provision, not current profit. Tax rate is 30%; tax prepayments are 300,000. No other tax adjustments exist. Find closing CURRENT tax payable, not total tax expense.
explanation: Taxable profit = 3,700,000 + fine 168,000 − exempt income 50,000 + provision expense 370,000 − deductible payments 80,000 = 4,108,000. Current tax less prepaid 300,000 = 932,400.00. Deferred tax is separate.

title: Consolidated inventory tax difference • case 34
prompt: After eliminating an intragroup profit, inventory carries in consolidated statements at LKR 1,008,000. Its tax base in the buyer’s tax jurisdiction is 1,512,000. The buyer’s enacted rate is 30%; sufficient taxable profit is probable. No offsetting, exception or other tax effects apply. Find the consolidated DTA on this inventory.
explanation: The consolidated carrying amount is below tax base, creating a deductible temporary difference of 504,000. Use the buyer’s relevant tax rate: difference ×30% = 151,200.00.

title: Depreciation after recognised impairment • case 34
prompt: Immediately before an impairment, equipment carries at LKR 1,680,000. Recoverable amount is 1,040,000 and impairment is recognised. After that date it has four years’ remaining useful life and residual value 100,000. Straight-line depreciation is appropriate; no further revaluation or impairment applies. Find depreciation for the next FULL year.
explanation: First reduce the asset to recoverable amount 1,040,000. Thereafter allocate revised depreciable amount over remaining life: (1,040,000 − 100,000)/4 = 235,000.00.

title: Allocated headquarters in CGU impairment • case 34
prompt: CGU A carries operating assets of LKR 940,000; CGU B carries 400,000. A headquarters asset of 200,000 can be allocated reasonably and consistently in proportion to those operating-asset amounts. A’s recoverable amount INCLUDING its headquarters share is 820,000. No goodwill or other assets exist. Find the impairment loss for A including its allocation.
explanation: Allocate headquarters to A: 200,000 × 940,000/(940,000+400,000) = 140,298.51. Tested A carrying amount is 1,080,298.51. Impairment versus recoverable amount 820,000 = 260,298.51.

title: Break-even value-in-use cash flow • case 34
prompt: An asset carries at LKR 1,680,000. Its fair value less costs of disposal is lower. A valid VIU model uses THREE equal year-end operating cash inflows, plus 100,000 net disposal proceeds at year three, discounted at 10%. What minimum equal ANNUAL operating cash inflow makes VIU exactly equal carrying amount? Ignore tax and other adjustments.
explanation: Let annual flow be X. X×(1/1.10 + 1/1.10² + 1/1.10³) + 100,000/1.10³ = 1,680,000. Solve for X = 645,341.39. This sensitivity calculation identifies the VIU break-even point.

title: Discounted warranty expected-value portfolio • case 34
prompt: A present warranty obligation covers 1,680 products. Per product, probabilities are 70% no defect, 25% a minor repair costing LKR 400, and 5% a major repair costing 2,000. All expected payments occur exactly in TWO years. Outflow for the portfolio is probable; appropriate discount rate is 10% with no risk double counting. Find the provision.
explanation: Expected cash payment = 1,680×(25%×400 + 5%×2,000) = 336,000.0. Discount two years at 10%: 336,000.0/1.10² = 277,685.95. The probability assessment applies to the portfolio.

title: Provision movement with revised estimate • case 34
prompt: A discounted provision opens at LKR 840,000. Unwinding for a full year is at 8%. A 100,000 settlement occurs at the year END, after unwinding. At that same reporting date, a new estimate increases the remaining provision by 118,000. No other changes occur. Find closing provision.
explanation: Closing = opening + 8% unwinding − year-end settlement + estimate increase: 840,000×1.08 −100,000 +118,000 = 925,200.00. Classification of the estimate change’s counterpart is assessed separately.

title: Revaluation increase after earlier loss • case 34
prompt: PPE carries at LKR 940,000 before revaluation and is revalued to 1,680,000. A prior revaluation decrease on THIS asset of 218,000 was recognised in profit or loss and has not been reversed. No tax effects apply. Find the current increase recognised in OCI after reversing the eligible prior loss in profit or loss.
explanation: Gross increase = 1,680,000 − 940,000 = 740,000. First recognise 218,000 in profit or loss to reverse the prior decrease. Remaining 522,000.00 is OCI revaluation surplus.

title: Nine-month depreciation and disposal gain • case 34
prompt: Equipment cost LKR 1,880,000, residual value 200,000 and useful life five years, straight-line. Two FULL years’ depreciation were recognised before this year. It is sold after nine months of the current year for 1,360,000. It was not previously held for sale and no impairment or revaluation applies. Find disposal GAIN after the required nine-month depreciation.
explanation: Annual depreciation = (1,880,000−200,000)/5. Deduct two full years and another 9/12 year from cost to obtain disposal-date carrying amount 956,000.00. Gain = proceeds − that amount = 404,000.00.

title: Customer collections with a write-off • case 34
prompt: All sales are on credit. Revenue is LKR 4,700,000; opening GROSS trade receivables are 600,000; closing GROSS receivables are 1,140,000. Receivables of 134,000 were written off during the year. There are no taxes, returns, contract balances, acquisitions or exchange changes. Find cash collected from customers.
explanation: Gross receivable roll-forward: opening + credit sales − cash receipts − write-offs = closing. Thus receipts = 4,700,000+600,000−1,140,000−134,000 = 4,026,000.00. Write-offs are not cash receipts.

title: Loan funding net cash effect • case 34
prompt: A company receives cash loan proceeds of LKR 1,680,000 and immediately pays a directly attributable lender issue fee of 37,000. Both payments are classified as financing cash flows in this case. No other cash movement occurs. Find the NET financing cash inflow from these two cash movements; this question does not require net line-item presentation.
explanation: Net financing cash effect = proceeds − cash fee = 1,680,000 − 37,000.00 = 1,643,000.00. Effective-interest amortisation later is not another inception cash payment.

title: Item-by-item NRV without offsetting headroom • case 34
prompt: Two unrelated inventory lines require separate NRV tests. A has 270 units, cost LKR 1,000 and NRV 900 each. B has 168 units, cost 1,000 and NRV 1,200 each. There is no basis to group them for the write-down test. Find TOTAL closing inventory carrying amount.
explanation: Carry A at 900 per unit and B at its lower cost of 1,000. Total = 270×900 + 168×1,000 = 411,000.00. B’s NRV headroom cannot offset A’s write-down.

title: Units-of-production intangible amortisation • case 34
prompt: A finite-life production licence costs LKR 1,580,000, has zero residual value, and is expected to support 150,000 units in total. Actual output this year is 47,000 units. A units-of-production method reliably reflects consumption and the asset was available throughout. No impairment or estimate change applies. Find annual amortisation.
explanation: Apply the supported consumption pattern: amortisation = 1,580,000 × 47,000/150,000 = 495,066.67. It is the share of expected lifetime production consumed, not an automatic straight-line charge.

title: Profit after suspended associate losses • case 34
prompt: An equity-method investment and relevant long-term interests were previously reduced to zero. Unrecognised share of prior losses totals LKR 148,000; the investor has no obligation and made no support payments. In the current year its share of associate profit is 222,000. No other adjustments or changes in interest apply. Find the share of profit that can now be RECOGNISED.
explanation: First absorb unrecognised prior losses before resuming recognised profit. Recognised amount = current profit share 222,000 − prior unrecognised losses 148,000 = 74,000.00.

title: Return recovery asset net of costs • case 35
prompt: A retailer has transferred 1,875 products. It expects 75 to be returned. Each returned product originally cost LKR 600; expected recovery handling is 20 per item and expected value deterioration is 30 per item. Estimates meet the relevant requirements. Find the separate asset for the right to recover returned products, excluding the refund liability.
explanation: Recovery asset = original carrying amount of expected returns less recovery costs and potential value decrease: 75 × (600 − 20 − 30) = 41,250.00. It is assessed separately from the customer refund liability.
family: Return recovery asset net of costs

title: Retrospective volume rebate true-up • case 35
prompt: A customer’s annual purchases reach 13,500 units at list price LKR 200. Crossing the threshold entitles it to a 5% retrospective rebate on ALL units. Cumulative revenue before this new supported estimate equals full list price; no rebate was previously accrued. The constraint permits the estimate. Find the reduction in cumulative revenue required now.
explanation: The revised transaction price reflects the retrospective rebate on all units. Revenue reduction = 13,500 × 200 × 5% = 135,000.00. Recognise the corresponding refund obligation as appropriate.

title: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation • case 35
prompt: A bundle has distinct goods A and B with stand-alone prices LKR 375,000 and 650,000. Total transaction price is 940,000. ALL paragraph 82 criteria demonstrate that the whole 85,000 discount relates only to A. A transfers now; B is not yet delivered. Find revenue recognised for A.
explanation: The specified discount-allocation exception applies. Allocate all 85,000 discount to A: 375,000 − 85,000 = 290,000.00. Do not default to relative allocation when the exception’s criteria are met.
family: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation

title: Three obligations and partial service • case 35
prompt: A contract price of LKR 2,250,000 covers goods A, goods B and twelve months of distinct support. Stand-alone prices are 600,000, 300,000 and 300,000 respectively. A is delivered, B is not, and six months of evenly provided support are complete. No allocation exception applies. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise allocation to A plus half of support: 2,250,000 × (600,000 + 150,000) / 1,200,000 = 1,406,250.00. B’s allocation remains unrecognised as revenue.

title: Progress excluding abnormal waste • case 35
prompt: An over-time contract has transaction price LKR 13,500,000. Costs incurred are 5,400,000, including abnormal waste of 270,000 that does not depict progress. Expected TOTAL productive costs excluding that waste are 10,800,000. Cost-to-cost is appropriate after excluding the waste; no other adjustment applies. Find cumulative revenue, not profit.
explanation: Exclude abnormal waste from the progress numerator. Productive progress = (5,400,000 − 270,000) / 10,800,000. Revenue = transaction price × that progress = 6,412,500.00. The wasted cost is not a revenue-producing input.

title: Uninstalled materials without margin • case 35
prompt: A single over-time construction obligation has price LKR 17,000,000. All B19(b) conditions justify recognising revenue equal to cost for significant uninstalled materials of 3,400,000 already controlled by the customer. Other productive costs incurred are 2,550,000; expected total OTHER costs are 10,200,000. No revenue was previously recognised. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise material revenue without margin: 3,400,000. Recognise the remaining price using other-cost progress: (17,000,000 − 3,400,000) × 2,550,000/10,200,000. Total revenue = 6,800,000.00.

title: Agent commission after collection • case 35
prompt: An intermediary is an AGENT and collects customer cash of LKR 2,750,000 for a completed supplier service. It must remit 88% to the supplier and is entitled to the remaining 12% commission. It controls neither the underlying service nor any distinct extra service, and there is no tax. Find its revenue.
explanation: An agent recognises its fee or commission, not the supplier’s gross billings: 2,750,000 × 12% = 330,000.00. The amount due to the supplier is separately accounted for.

title: Distinct remaining goods blended prospectively • case 35
prompt: At modification, 100 distinct goods remain under an existing contract at LKR 1,350 each. Another 50 distinct goods are added at 1,080 each. The modification is NOT a separate contract, but remaining goods are distinct from those already transferred, so paragraph 21(a) applies prospectively. Thirty of the remaining goods are then transferred. Find revenue for those thirty.
explanation: Prospective remaining consideration = 100 × 1,350 + 50 × 1,080. Divide by 150 remaining goods, then multiply by 30 = 37,800.00. Do not retrospectively revise revenue on goods already transferred.

title: FVTPL acquisition expense • case 35
prompt: A financial asset is acquired at fair value LKR 1,500,000 and is classified at FVTPL. Directly attributable broker costs are 37,500, paid separately. No fair-value change occurs immediately after purchase. Find the immediate profit-or-loss expense from acquiring this asset.
explanation: Transaction costs on an FVTPL asset are expensed. Initial asset carrying amount is fair value 1,500,000; immediate acquisition expense is 37,500.00.

title: Collateral cash-shortfall discounting • case 35
prompt: A credit loss scenario has a contractual receipt of LKR 1,875,000 due in one year. The ONLY expected recovery at that same date is collateral sale proceeds of 1,225,000, less sale costs of 85,000. Scenario probability is 100% and original EIR is 10%. Collateral is an integral contractual credit enhancement and not separately recognised. Find discounted ECL.
explanation: One-year shortfall = contractual receipt − net collateral recovery = 1,875,000 − (1,225,000 − 85,000). Discount that shortfall at 10%: 668,181.82. Do not ignore recovery costs or discount only one side of same-date cash flows.

title: Three-band provision matrix • case 35
prompt: Under the simplified lifetime-ECL approach, supported adjusted loss rates are 1% on current receivables of LKR 1,700,000, 5% on past-due balances of 475,000, and 30% on severely overdue balances of 170,000. Rates already include all required forward-looking and discounting effects. Find total loss allowance.
explanation: Apply each appropriate band rate and add: 1,700,000×1% + 475,000×5% + 170,000×30% = 91,750.00. Do not apply one blended band mechanically to all balances.

title: Equity FVOCI profit-or-loss dividend • case 35
prompt: An eligible equity investment has the irrevocable FVOCI election. During the year it gains LKR 190,000 in fair value and earns a dividend of 95,000. Dividend recognition criteria are met and the dividend clearly represents a return on investment, not recovery of cost. There are no other effects. Find income recognised in PROFIT OR LOSS.
explanation: The qualifying dividend of 95,000.00 is profit-or-loss income. The fair-value movement of 190,000 is OCI under this election and is not added to the profit-or-loss amount.

title: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset • case 35
prompt: A loan is sold with full derecognition. Immediately before sale, gross carrying amount is LKR 1,700,000, loss allowance 170,000, and cash proceeds 1,615,000. No accumulated OCI, sale fees or other adjustments exist. Find the derecognition GAIN relative to net carrying amount.
explanation: Net carrying amount = 1,700,000 − 170,000 = 1,530,000. Compare proceeds with that net amount: 1,615,000 − 1,530,000 = 85,000.00 gain. Derecognise both the gross asset and related allowance.
family: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset

title: Non-substantial liability modification gain • case 35
prompt: An amortised-cost liability is modified WITHOUT extinguishment, with no fees. Its carrying amount is LKR 1,350,000. The sole revised payment is 1,552,500 in two years. Original EIR is 10%; the modification is assessed as non-substantial. Find the immediate modification GAIN from recalculating amortised cost at the original EIR.
explanation: Revised amortised cost = 1,552,500/1.10² = 1,283,057.85. Gain = old liability 1,350,000 − revised PV = 66,942.15. The original EIR is retained for this non-extinguishing modification.

title: Credit-risk improvement allowance release • case 35
prompt: A debt asset under the GENERAL ECL model previously had significant credit-risk deterioration and lifetime allowance LKR 170,000. At reporting date the criteria for lifetime ECL are no longer met; required 12-month ECL is 27,500. No write-offs, new assets or other allowance movements occur. Find the impairment reversal in profit or loss.
explanation: When lifetime measurement is no longer required, the general model returns to 12-month ECL. Release the excess allowance: 170,000 − 27,500 = 142,500.00. This is not a receivable under mandatory simplified lifetime ECL.

title: Upstream inventory elimination with tax • case 35
prompt: P and S report profits AFTER their own tax of LKR 3,400,000 and 1,500,000. An upstream inventory sale leaves unrealised profit of 340,000 in group closing inventory. A recoverable DTA is recognised on the full elimination at 30%, with the tax effect in profit or loss. No other consolidation adjustments exist. Find TOTAL consolidated profit, before attribution to owners and NCI.
explanation: Combine separate after-tax profits, eliminate unrealised profit and recognise the recoverable tax benefit: 3,400,000 + 1,500,000 − 340,000 + 102,000.00 = 4,662,000.00. This question asks total group profit, not its attribution.

title: Full-goodwill impairment and owner profit • case 35
prompt: P owns 80% of S all year. Separate after-tax profits are P LKR 2,850,000 and S 1,050,000. Goodwill is recognised on the FULL-goodwill basis and an impairment of 375,000 is attributable to S’s CGU and allocated 80:20 between owners and NCI. No other adjustments or tax effects apply. Find consolidated profit attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Owners receive 80% of S’s profit and bear 80% of the full-goodwill loss: 2,850,000 + 80% × (1,050,000 − 375,000) = 3,390,000.00. Do not charge the owners with 100% of this full-goodwill loss.

title: Partial goodwill CGU gross-up • case 35
prompt: P owns 80% of S. Recognised PARTIAL goodwill is LKR 1,360,000; S’s other net assets in the tested CGU carry at 6,800,000. Recoverable amount of the WHOLE CGU is 7,650,000. Gross up goodwill for unrecognised NCI goodwill when testing; the whole impairment falls within grossed-up goodwill. No tax or other adjustments apply. Find impairment actually recognised on group goodwill.
explanation: Grossed-up goodwill = 1,360,000/80% = 1,700,000.00. Whole-CGU impairment = grossed goodwill + other net assets − recoverable amount = 850,000.00. Only the parent’s 80% goodwill portion is recognised, so recorded loss = 680,000.00.
reference: LKAS 36 Appendix C paras C4–C8; SLFRS 10 para B86

title: Consolidated retained earnings bridge • case 35
prompt: P owns 75% of S. At year end P retained earnings are LKR 4,750,000, and S retained earnings 3,050,000. S retained earnings at acquisition were 1,000,000. Cumulative post-acquisition extra FV depreciation is 170,000. A downstream sale by P leaves unrealised profit of 115,000. No tax, goodwill impairment, dividends recognised by P, OCI or other adjustments apply. Find consolidated retained earnings attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Group owners’ retained earnings = parent RE + 75% of adjusted post-acquisition S reserves − the parent’s downstream unrealised profit: 6,045,000.00. Pre-acquisition reserves do not enter post-acquisition group retained earnings.

title: Loss of control and translation reserve • case 35
prompt: P loses control of a foreign subsidiary. Proceeds are LKR 3,600,000; retained interest FV 850,000; NCI carrying amount 475,000; consolidated net assets INCLUDING goodwill 3,650,000. A cumulative translation GAIN of 170,000, entirely attributable to P, must be reclassified to profit or loss on loss of control. No other effects apply. Find total disposal gain including that reclassification.
explanation: Base gain = proceeds + retained FV + NCI − net assets = 1,275,000.00. Add the parent’s translation gain recycled on disposal: 170,000. Total = 1,445,000.00.
family: Loss of control and translation reserve

title: Residual guarantee expected payment • case 35
prompt: A lessee owes three year-end rentals of LKR 375,000. It guarantees residual value up to 200,000, but the amount EXPECTED to be payable under that guarantee is 65,000 at year three. Discount rate is 10%. No other liability payments exist. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the amount expected to be payable, not automatically the maximum guarantee. Liability = PV of three rentals + 65,000/1.10³ = 981,404.96.

title: Reasonably certain purchase option PV • case 35
prompt: A lease requires three year-end rentals of LKR 325,000, plus a purchase option price of 850,000 payable at year three. Exercise is reasonably certain. Discount rate is 10%. No incentives, other payments or initial prepayments apply. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the reasonably certain purchase price in the liability: PV of rentals + purchase price discounted for three years = 1,446,844.48. Do not omit or leave the future option payment undiscounted.

title: Lease and service component allocation • case 35
prompt: A two-year contract requires bundled payments of LKR 425,000 at each year end. Relative stand-alone prices are equipment lease 200,000 and distinct maintenance 50,000 per year. The lessee does NOT elect to combine components. Lease discount rate is 10%; no other payments exist. Find initial lease liability for the LEASE component only.
explanation: Allocate 200,000/250,000 = 80% of each bundled payment to the lease: 340,000.00. Discount those two lease payments, excluding maintenance, to obtain 590,082.64.

title: Exempt short-term lease rent-free start • case 35
prompt: A twelve-month lease with no purchase option qualifies for the elected short-term exemption. The first three months are rent free, then nine monthly payments of LKR 37,500 are due. The asset is available throughout and straight-line expense is appropriate. Find lease expense for the FIRST six months, ignoring accrual settlement timing.
explanation: Total fixed payments are nine rents. Spread evenly over all twelve months: 37,500 × 9/12 × 6 = 168,750.00. Rent-free months still receive an expense allocation.

title: Sale-and-leaseback rights transferred • case 35
prompt: A transfer qualifies as a sale under SLFRS 15 at fair value LKR 17,000,000; asset carrying amount is 9,500,000. Market-rate leaseback payments have PV 6,800,000. There are no off-market adjustments or variable-payment complications. At inception, what sale gain is recognised for rights TRANSFERRED to the buyer-lessor?
explanation: Total gain = 17,000,000 − 9,500,000 = 7,500,000. Retained-use proportion = lease PV / fair value = 40%. Recognise only the transferred-rights proportion of the gain: 4,500,000.00.

title: Reassessed bargain purchase gain • case 35
prompt: After the required reassessment, final acquisition-date consideration is LKR 3,400,000, NCI fair value is 400,000 and identifiable net assets are 5,100,000. There is no prior holding or other adjustment. Find the bargain purchase gain recognised in profit or loss.
explanation: Net identifiable assets exceed consideration plus NCI: 5,100,000 − 3,400,000 − 400,000 = 1,300,000.00. Reassessment has been completed before recognising the gain.

title: Acquired contingent liability in goodwill • case 35
prompt: Consideration is LKR 5,250,000; NCI FV is 500,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired contingent liability are 4,050,000. The acquired item is a present obligation with reliably measurable FV 375,000 and qualifies for recognition despite non-probable outflow. No tax or other adjustment applies. Find goodwill after recognising it.
explanation: Recognise the qualifying acquired liability: net identifiable assets become 4,050,000 − 375,000. Goodwill = consideration + NCI − adjusted net assets = 2,075,000.00.

title: Separate acquired brand from goodwill • case 35
prompt: Consideration is LKR 4,750,000; NCI FV 600,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired separable brand are 4,000,000. Brand FV is 750,000; tax base is zero and 30% DTL must be recognised. No other adjustments apply. Find goodwill after separate brand and tax recognition.
explanation: An identifiable acquired brand is separate from goodwill. Net addition to identifiable assets = brand FV − 30% DTL = 525,000.00. Goodwill = 4,750,000 + 600,000 − (4,000,000 + 525,000.00) = 825,000.00.

title: Acquisition costs versus issue costs • case 35
prompt: A business acquisition has consideration LKR 3,050,000. Additional costs are acquisition advisory 170,000, qualifying equity-issue costs 70,000 and qualifying debt-issue costs 40,000. The issue costs follow their relevant standards, and no immediate debt-cost amortisation or other expense arises this period. Find the immediate acquisition-related PROFIT-OR-LOSS expense from these costs.
explanation: Expense advisory acquisition costs of 170,000.00. Qualifying equity and debt issuance costs follow their respective standards and are not added to this immediate acquisition-service expense or goodwill.

title: Temporary difference and enacted rate change • case 35
prompt: A taxable temporary difference opens at LKR 200,000 with a DTL measured at 25%. At year end the difference is 475,000 and the enacted rate expected on reversal is 30%. Both the underlying movements and rate change belong in profit or loss. No other tax movements exist. Find deferred tax expense for the year.
explanation: Opening DTL = 200,000×25% = 50,000. Closing DTL = 475,000×30% = 142,500.00. Expense is the full increase, including rate remeasurement: 92,500.00. Rates are exercise assumptions.
family: Temporary difference and enacted rate change

title: Revalued non-depreciable land tax basis • case 35
prompt: Non-depreciable land is revalued from cost LKR 1,700,000 to fair value 2,550,000; tax base remains cost. The enacted rate for recovery through SALE is 20%, while a 30% use rate would otherwise apply. The revaluation and associated tax go to OCI. No other effects exist. Find the net OCI revaluation increase after deferred tax.
explanation: For this non-depreciable revalued asset, measure tax consequences on recovery through sale: DTL = (2,550,000 − 1,700,000)×20%. Net OCI increase = gross uplift less that DTL = 680,000.00.

title: Current tax reconciliation and prepayment • case 35
prompt: Accounting pretax profit is LKR 3,750,000. It includes a permanently non-deductible fine of 170,000, exempt income of 50,000, and warranty expense of 375,000 deductible only on payment. Current-year warranty payments of 80,000 are deductible and were charged against the provision, not current profit. Tax rate is 30%; tax prepayments are 300,000. No other tax adjustments exist. Find closing CURRENT tax payable, not total tax expense.
explanation: Taxable profit = 3,750,000 + fine 170,000 − exempt income 50,000 + provision expense 375,000 − deductible payments 80,000 = 4,165,000. Current tax less prepaid 300,000 = 949,500.00. Deferred tax is separate.

title: Consolidated inventory tax difference • case 35
prompt: After eliminating an intragroup profit, inventory carries in consolidated statements at LKR 1,020,000. Its tax base in the buyer’s tax jurisdiction is 1,530,000. The buyer’s enacted rate is 30%; sufficient taxable profit is probable. No offsetting, exception or other tax effects apply. Find the consolidated DTA on this inventory.
explanation: The consolidated carrying amount is below tax base, creating a deductible temporary difference of 510,000. Use the buyer’s relevant tax rate: difference ×30% = 153,000.00.

title: Depreciation after recognised impairment • case 35
prompt: Immediately before an impairment, equipment carries at LKR 1,700,000. Recoverable amount is 1,050,000 and impairment is recognised. After that date it has four years’ remaining useful life and residual value 100,000. Straight-line depreciation is appropriate; no further revaluation or impairment applies. Find depreciation for the next FULL year.
explanation: First reduce the asset to recoverable amount 1,050,000. Thereafter allocate revised depreciable amount over remaining life: (1,050,000 − 100,000)/4 = 237,500.00.

title: Allocated headquarters in CGU impairment • case 35
prompt: CGU A carries operating assets of LKR 950,000; CGU B carries 400,000. A headquarters asset of 200,000 can be allocated reasonably and consistently in proportion to those operating-asset amounts. A’s recoverable amount INCLUDING its headquarters share is 825,000. No goodwill or other assets exist. Find the impairment loss for A including its allocation.
explanation: Allocate headquarters to A: 200,000 × 950,000/(950,000+400,000) = 140,740.74. Tested A carrying amount is 1,090,740.74. Impairment versus recoverable amount 825,000 = 265,740.74.

title: Break-even value-in-use cash flow • case 35
prompt: An asset carries at LKR 1,700,000. Its fair value less costs of disposal is lower. A valid VIU model uses THREE equal year-end operating cash inflows, plus 100,000 net disposal proceeds at year three, discounted at 10%. What minimum equal ANNUAL operating cash inflow makes VIU exactly equal carrying amount? Ignore tax and other adjustments.
explanation: Let annual flow be X. X×(1/1.10 + 1/1.10² + 1/1.10³) + 100,000/1.10³ = 1,700,000. Solve for X = 653,383.69. This sensitivity calculation identifies the VIU break-even point.

title: Discounted warranty expected-value portfolio • case 35
prompt: A present warranty obligation covers 1,700 products. Per product, probabilities are 70% no defect, 25% a minor repair costing LKR 400, and 5% a major repair costing 2,000. All expected payments occur exactly in TWO years. Outflow for the portfolio is probable; appropriate discount rate is 10% with no risk double counting. Find the provision.
explanation: Expected cash payment = 1,700×(25%×400 + 5%×2,000) = 340,000.0. Discount two years at 10%: 340,000.0/1.10² = 280,991.74. The probability assessment applies to the portfolio.

title: Provision movement with revised estimate • case 35
prompt: A discounted provision opens at LKR 850,000. Unwinding for a full year is at 8%. A 100,000 settlement occurs at the year END, after unwinding. At that same reporting date, a new estimate increases the remaining provision by 120,000. No other changes occur. Find closing provision.
explanation: Closing = opening + 8% unwinding − year-end settlement + estimate increase: 850,000×1.08 −100,000 +120,000 = 938,000.00. Classification of the estimate change’s counterpart is assessed separately.

title: Revaluation increase after earlier loss • case 35
prompt: PPE carries at LKR 950,000 before revaluation and is revalued to 1,700,000. A prior revaluation decrease on THIS asset of 220,000 was recognised in profit or loss and has not been reversed. No tax effects apply. Find the current increase recognised in OCI after reversing the eligible prior loss in profit or loss.
explanation: Gross increase = 1,700,000 − 950,000 = 750,000. First recognise 220,000 in profit or loss to reverse the prior decrease. Remaining 530,000.00 is OCI revaluation surplus.

title: Nine-month depreciation and disposal gain • case 35
prompt: Equipment cost LKR 1,900,000, residual value 200,000 and useful life five years, straight-line. Two FULL years’ depreciation were recognised before this year. It is sold after nine months of the current year for 1,375,000. It was not previously held for sale and no impairment or revaluation applies. Find disposal GAIN after the required nine-month depreciation.
explanation: Annual depreciation = (1,900,000−200,000)/5. Deduct two full years and another 9/12 year from cost to obtain disposal-date carrying amount 965,000.00. Gain = proceeds − that amount = 410,000.00.

title: Customer collections with a write-off • case 35
prompt: All sales are on credit. Revenue is LKR 4,750,000; opening GROSS trade receivables are 600,000; closing GROSS receivables are 1,150,000. Receivables of 135,000 were written off during the year. There are no taxes, returns, contract balances, acquisitions or exchange changes. Find cash collected from customers.
explanation: Gross receivable roll-forward: opening + credit sales − cash receipts − write-offs = closing. Thus receipts = 4,750,000+600,000−1,150,000−135,000 = 4,065,000.00. Write-offs are not cash receipts.

title: Loan funding net cash effect • case 35
prompt: A company receives cash loan proceeds of LKR 1,700,000 and immediately pays a directly attributable lender issue fee of 37,500. Both payments are classified as financing cash flows in this case. No other cash movement occurs. Find the NET financing cash inflow from these two cash movements; this question does not require net line-item presentation.
explanation: Net financing cash effect = proceeds − cash fee = 1,700,000 − 37,500.00 = 1,662,500.00. Effective-interest amortisation later is not another inception cash payment.

title: Item-by-item NRV without offsetting headroom • case 35
prompt: Two unrelated inventory lines require separate NRV tests. A has 275 units, cost LKR 1,000 and NRV 900 each. B has 170 units, cost 1,000 and NRV 1,200 each. There is no basis to group them for the write-down test. Find TOTAL closing inventory carrying amount.
explanation: Carry A at 900 per unit and B at its lower cost of 1,000. Total = 275×900 + 170×1,000 = 417,500.00. B’s NRV headroom cannot offset A’s write-down.

title: Units-of-production intangible amortisation • case 35
prompt: A finite-life production licence costs LKR 1,600,000, has zero residual value, and is expected to support 150,000 units in total. Actual output this year is 47,500 units. A units-of-production method reliably reflects consumption and the asset was available throughout. No impairment or estimate change applies. Find annual amortisation.
explanation: Apply the supported consumption pattern: amortisation = 1,600,000 × 47,500/150,000 = 506,666.67. It is the share of expected lifetime production consumed, not an automatic straight-line charge.

title: Profit after suspended associate losses • case 35
prompt: An equity-method investment and relevant long-term interests were previously reduced to zero. Unrecognised share of prior losses totals LKR 150,000; the investor has no obligation and made no support payments. In the current year its share of associate profit is 225,000. No other adjustments or changes in interest apply. Find the share of profit that can now be RECOGNISED.
explanation: First absorb unrecognised prior losses before resuming recognised profit. Recognised amount = current profit share 225,000 − prior unrecognised losses 150,000 = 75,000.00.

title: Return recovery asset net of costs • case 36
prompt: A retailer has transferred 1,900 products. It expects 76 to be returned. Each returned product originally cost LKR 600; expected recovery handling is 20 per item and expected value deterioration is 30 per item. Estimates meet the relevant requirements. Find the separate asset for the right to recover returned products, excluding the refund liability.
explanation: Recovery asset = original carrying amount of expected returns less recovery costs and potential value decrease: 76 × (600 − 20 − 30) = 41,800.00. It is assessed separately from the customer refund liability.
family: Return recovery asset net of costs

title: Retrospective volume rebate true-up • case 36
prompt: A customer’s annual purchases reach 13,600 units at list price LKR 200. Crossing the threshold entitles it to a 5% retrospective rebate on ALL units. Cumulative revenue before this new supported estimate equals full list price; no rebate was previously accrued. The constraint permits the estimate. Find the reduction in cumulative revenue required now.
explanation: The revised transaction price reflects the retrospective rebate on all units. Revenue reduction = 13,600 × 200 × 5% = 136,000.00. Recognise the corresponding refund obligation as appropriate.

title: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation • case 36
prompt: A bundle has distinct goods A and B with stand-alone prices LKR 380,000 and 660,000. Total transaction price is 954,000. ALL paragraph 82 criteria demonstrate that the whole 86,000 discount relates only to A. A transfers now; B is not yet delivered. Find revenue recognised for A.
explanation: The specified discount-allocation exception applies. Allocate all 86,000 discount to A: 380,000 − 86,000 = 294,000.00. Do not default to relative allocation when the exception’s criteria are met.
family: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation

title: Three obligations and partial service • case 36
prompt: A contract price of LKR 2,280,000 covers goods A, goods B and twelve months of distinct support. Stand-alone prices are 600,000, 300,000 and 300,000 respectively. A is delivered, B is not, and six months of evenly provided support are complete. No allocation exception applies. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise allocation to A plus half of support: 2,280,000 × (600,000 + 150,000) / 1,200,000 = 1,425,000.00. B’s allocation remains unrecognised as revenue.

title: Progress excluding abnormal waste • case 36
prompt: An over-time contract has transaction price LKR 13,600,000. Costs incurred are 5,440,000, including abnormal waste of 272,000 that does not depict progress. Expected TOTAL productive costs excluding that waste are 10,880,000. Cost-to-cost is appropriate after excluding the waste; no other adjustment applies. Find cumulative revenue, not profit.
explanation: Exclude abnormal waste from the progress numerator. Productive progress = (5,440,000 − 272,000) / 10,880,000. Revenue = transaction price × that progress = 6,460,000.00. The wasted cost is not a revenue-producing input.

title: Uninstalled materials without margin • case 36
prompt: A single over-time construction obligation has price LKR 17,200,000. All B19(b) conditions justify recognising revenue equal to cost for significant uninstalled materials of 3,440,000 already controlled by the customer. Other productive costs incurred are 2,580,000; expected total OTHER costs are 10,320,000. No revenue was previously recognised. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise material revenue without margin: 3,440,000. Recognise the remaining price using other-cost progress: (17,200,000 − 3,440,000) × 2,580,000/10,320,000. Total revenue = 6,880,000.00.

title: Agent commission after collection • case 36
prompt: An intermediary is an AGENT and collects customer cash of LKR 2,800,000 for a completed supplier service. It must remit 88% to the supplier and is entitled to the remaining 12% commission. It controls neither the underlying service nor any distinct extra service, and there is no tax. Find its revenue.
explanation: An agent recognises its fee or commission, not the supplier’s gross billings: 2,800,000 × 12% = 336,000.00. The amount due to the supplier is separately accounted for.

title: Distinct remaining goods blended prospectively • case 36
prompt: At modification, 100 distinct goods remain under an existing contract at LKR 1,360 each. Another 50 distinct goods are added at 1,088 each. The modification is NOT a separate contract, but remaining goods are distinct from those already transferred, so paragraph 21(a) applies prospectively. Thirty of the remaining goods are then transferred. Find revenue for those thirty.
explanation: Prospective remaining consideration = 100 × 1,360 + 50 × 1,088. Divide by 150 remaining goods, then multiply by 30 = 38,080.00. Do not retrospectively revise revenue on goods already transferred.

title: FVTPL acquisition expense • case 36
prompt: A financial asset is acquired at fair value LKR 1,520,000 and is classified at FVTPL. Directly attributable broker costs are 38,000, paid separately. No fair-value change occurs immediately after purchase. Find the immediate profit-or-loss expense from acquiring this asset.
explanation: Transaction costs on an FVTPL asset are expensed. Initial asset carrying amount is fair value 1,520,000; immediate acquisition expense is 38,000.00.

title: Collateral cash-shortfall discounting • case 36
prompt: A credit loss scenario has a contractual receipt of LKR 1,900,000 due in one year. The ONLY expected recovery at that same date is collateral sale proceeds of 1,240,000, less sale costs of 86,000. Scenario probability is 100% and original EIR is 10%. Collateral is an integral contractual credit enhancement and not separately recognised. Find discounted ECL.
explanation: One-year shortfall = contractual receipt − net collateral recovery = 1,900,000 − (1,240,000 − 86,000). Discount that shortfall at 10%: 678,181.82. Do not ignore recovery costs or discount only one side of same-date cash flows.

title: Three-band provision matrix • case 36
prompt: Under the simplified lifetime-ECL approach, supported adjusted loss rates are 1% on current receivables of LKR 1,720,000, 5% on past-due balances of 480,000, and 30% on severely overdue balances of 172,000. Rates already include all required forward-looking and discounting effects. Find total loss allowance.
explanation: Apply each appropriate band rate and add: 1,720,000×1% + 480,000×5% + 172,000×30% = 92,800.00. Do not apply one blended band mechanically to all balances.

title: Equity FVOCI profit-or-loss dividend • case 36
prompt: An eligible equity investment has the irrevocable FVOCI election. During the year it gains LKR 192,000 in fair value and earns a dividend of 96,000. Dividend recognition criteria are met and the dividend clearly represents a return on investment, not recovery of cost. There are no other effects. Find income recognised in PROFIT OR LOSS.
explanation: The qualifying dividend of 96,000.00 is profit-or-loss income. The fair-value movement of 192,000 is OCI under this election and is not added to the profit-or-loss amount.

title: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset • case 36
prompt: A loan is sold with full derecognition. Immediately before sale, gross carrying amount is LKR 1,720,000, loss allowance 172,000, and cash proceeds 1,634,000. No accumulated OCI, sale fees or other adjustments exist. Find the derecognition GAIN relative to net carrying amount.
explanation: Net carrying amount = 1,720,000 − 172,000 = 1,548,000. Compare proceeds with that net amount: 1,634,000 − 1,548,000 = 86,000.00 gain. Derecognise both the gross asset and related allowance.
family: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset

title: Non-substantial liability modification gain • case 36
prompt: An amortised-cost liability is modified WITHOUT extinguishment, with no fees. Its carrying amount is LKR 1,360,000. The sole revised payment is 1,564,000 in two years. Original EIR is 10%; the modification is assessed as non-substantial. Find the immediate modification GAIN from recalculating amortised cost at the original EIR.
explanation: Revised amortised cost = 1,564,000/1.10² = 1,292,561.98. Gain = old liability 1,360,000 − revised PV = 67,438.02. The original EIR is retained for this non-extinguishing modification.

title: Credit-risk improvement allowance release • case 36
prompt: A debt asset under the GENERAL ECL model previously had significant credit-risk deterioration and lifetime allowance LKR 172,000. At reporting date the criteria for lifetime ECL are no longer met; required 12-month ECL is 28,000. No write-offs, new assets or other allowance movements occur. Find the impairment reversal in profit or loss.
