explanation: When lifetime measurement is no longer required, the general model returns to 12-month ECL. Release the excess allowance: 172,000 − 28,000 = 144,000.00. This is not a receivable under mandatory simplified lifetime ECL.

title: Upstream inventory elimination with tax • case 36
prompt: P and S report profits AFTER their own tax of LKR 3,440,000 and 1,520,000. An upstream inventory sale leaves unrealised profit of 344,000 in group closing inventory. A recoverable DTA is recognised on the full elimination at 30%, with the tax effect in profit or loss. No other consolidation adjustments exist. Find TOTAL consolidated profit, before attribution to owners and NCI.
explanation: Combine separate after-tax profits, eliminate unrealised profit and recognise the recoverable tax benefit: 3,440,000 + 1,520,000 − 344,000 + 103,200.00 = 4,719,200.00. This question asks total group profit, not its attribution.

title: Full-goodwill impairment and owner profit • case 36
prompt: P owns 80% of S all year. Separate after-tax profits are P LKR 2,880,000 and S 1,060,000. Goodwill is recognised on the FULL-goodwill basis and an impairment of 380,000 is attributable to S’s CGU and allocated 80:20 between owners and NCI. No other adjustments or tax effects apply. Find consolidated profit attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Owners receive 80% of S’s profit and bear 80% of the full-goodwill loss: 2,880,000 + 80% × (1,060,000 − 380,000) = 3,424,000.00. Do not charge the owners with 100% of this full-goodwill loss.

title: Partial goodwill CGU gross-up • case 36
prompt: P owns 80% of S. Recognised PARTIAL goodwill is LKR 1,376,000; S’s other net assets in the tested CGU carry at 6,880,000. Recoverable amount of the WHOLE CGU is 7,740,000. Gross up goodwill for unrecognised NCI goodwill when testing; the whole impairment falls within grossed-up goodwill. No tax or other adjustments apply. Find impairment actually recognised on group goodwill.
explanation: Grossed-up goodwill = 1,376,000/80% = 1,720,000.00. Whole-CGU impairment = grossed goodwill + other net assets − recoverable amount = 860,000.00. Only the parent’s 80% goodwill portion is recognised, so recorded loss = 688,000.00.
reference: LKAS 36 Appendix C paras C4–C8; SLFRS 10 para B86

title: Consolidated retained earnings bridge • case 36
prompt: P owns 75% of S. At year end P retained earnings are LKR 4,800,000, and S retained earnings 3,080,000. S retained earnings at acquisition were 1,000,000. Cumulative post-acquisition extra FV depreciation is 172,000. A downstream sale by P leaves unrealised profit of 116,000. No tax, goodwill impairment, dividends recognised by P, OCI or other adjustments apply. Find consolidated retained earnings attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Group owners’ retained earnings = parent RE + 75% of adjusted post-acquisition S reserves − the parent’s downstream unrealised profit: 6,115,000.00. Pre-acquisition reserves do not enter post-acquisition group retained earnings.

title: Loss of control and translation reserve • case 36
prompt: P loses control of a foreign subsidiary. Proceeds are LKR 3,640,000; retained interest FV 860,000; NCI carrying amount 480,000; consolidated net assets INCLUDING goodwill 3,680,000. A cumulative translation GAIN of 172,000, entirely attributable to P, must be reclassified to profit or loss on loss of control. No other effects apply. Find total disposal gain including that reclassification.
explanation: Base gain = proceeds + retained FV + NCI − net assets = 1,300,000.00. Add the parent’s translation gain recycled on disposal: 172,000. Total = 1,472,000.00.
family: Loss of control and translation reserve

title: Residual guarantee expected payment • case 36
prompt: A lessee owes three year-end rentals of LKR 380,000. It guarantees residual value up to 200,000, but the amount EXPECTED to be payable under that guarantee is 66,000 at year three. Discount rate is 10%. No other liability payments exist. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the amount expected to be payable, not automatically the maximum guarantee. Liability = PV of three rentals + 66,000/1.10³ = 994,590.53.

title: Reasonably certain purchase option PV • case 36
prompt: A lease requires three year-end rentals of LKR 330,000, plus a purchase option price of 860,000 payable at year three. Exercise is reasonably certain. Discount rate is 10%. No incentives, other payments or initial prepayments apply. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the reasonably certain purchase price in the liability: PV of rentals + purchase price discounted for three years = 1,466,791.89. Do not omit or leave the future option payment undiscounted.

title: Lease and service component allocation • case 36
prompt: A two-year contract requires bundled payments of LKR 430,000 at each year end. Relative stand-alone prices are equipment lease 200,000 and distinct maintenance 50,000 per year. The lessee does NOT elect to combine components. Lease discount rate is 10%; no other payments exist. Find initial lease liability for the LEASE component only.
explanation: Allocate 200,000/250,000 = 80% of each bundled payment to the lease: 344,000.00. Discount those two lease payments, excluding maintenance, to obtain 597,024.79.

title: Exempt short-term lease rent-free start • case 36
prompt: A twelve-month lease with no purchase option qualifies for the elected short-term exemption. The first three months are rent free, then nine monthly payments of LKR 38,000 are due. The asset is available throughout and straight-line expense is appropriate. Find lease expense for the FIRST six months, ignoring accrual settlement timing.
explanation: Total fixed payments are nine rents. Spread evenly over all twelve months: 38,000 × 9/12 × 6 = 171,000.00. Rent-free months still receive an expense allocation.

title: Sale-and-leaseback rights transferred • case 36
prompt: A transfer qualifies as a sale under SLFRS 15 at fair value LKR 17,200,000; asset carrying amount is 9,600,000. Market-rate leaseback payments have PV 6,880,000. There are no off-market adjustments or variable-payment complications. At inception, what sale gain is recognised for rights TRANSFERRED to the buyer-lessor?
explanation: Total gain = 17,200,000 − 9,600,000 = 7,600,000. Retained-use proportion = lease PV / fair value = 40%. Recognise only the transferred-rights proportion of the gain: 4,560,000.00.

title: Reassessed bargain purchase gain • case 36
prompt: After the required reassessment, final acquisition-date consideration is LKR 3,440,000, NCI fair value is 400,000 and identifiable net assets are 5,160,000. There is no prior holding or other adjustment. Find the bargain purchase gain recognised in profit or loss.
explanation: Net identifiable assets exceed consideration plus NCI: 5,160,000 − 3,440,000 − 400,000 = 1,320,000.00. Reassessment has been completed before recognising the gain.

title: Acquired contingent liability in goodwill • case 36
prompt: Consideration is LKR 5,300,000; NCI FV is 500,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired contingent liability are 4,080,000. The acquired item is a present obligation with reliably measurable FV 380,000 and qualifies for recognition despite non-probable outflow. No tax or other adjustment applies. Find goodwill after recognising it.
explanation: Recognise the qualifying acquired liability: net identifiable assets become 4,080,000 − 380,000. Goodwill = consideration + NCI − adjusted net assets = 2,100,000.00.

title: Separate acquired brand from goodwill • case 36
prompt: Consideration is LKR 4,800,000; NCI FV 600,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired separable brand are 4,040,000. Brand FV is 760,000; tax base is zero and 30% DTL must be recognised. No other adjustments apply. Find goodwill after separate brand and tax recognition.
explanation: An identifiable acquired brand is separate from goodwill. Net addition to identifiable assets = brand FV − 30% DTL = 532,000.00. Goodwill = 4,800,000 + 600,000 − (4,040,000 + 532,000.00) = 828,000.00.

title: Acquisition costs versus issue costs • case 36
prompt: A business acquisition has consideration LKR 3,080,000. Additional costs are acquisition advisory 172,000, qualifying equity-issue costs 70,000 and qualifying debt-issue costs 40,000. The issue costs follow their relevant standards, and no immediate debt-cost amortisation or other expense arises this period. Find the immediate acquisition-related PROFIT-OR-LOSS expense from these costs.
explanation: Expense advisory acquisition costs of 172,000.00. Qualifying equity and debt issuance costs follow their respective standards and are not added to this immediate acquisition-service expense or goodwill.

title: Temporary difference and enacted rate change • case 36
prompt: A taxable temporary difference opens at LKR 200,000 with a DTL measured at 25%. At year end the difference is 480,000 and the enacted rate expected on reversal is 30%. Both the underlying movements and rate change belong in profit or loss. No other tax movements exist. Find deferred tax expense for the year.
explanation: Opening DTL = 200,000×25% = 50,000. Closing DTL = 480,000×30% = 144,000.00. Expense is the full increase, including rate remeasurement: 94,000.00. Rates are exercise assumptions.
family: Temporary difference and enacted rate change

title: Revalued non-depreciable land tax basis • case 36
prompt: Non-depreciable land is revalued from cost LKR 1,720,000 to fair value 2,580,000; tax base remains cost. The enacted rate for recovery through SALE is 20%, while a 30% use rate would otherwise apply. The revaluation and associated tax go to OCI. No other effects exist. Find the net OCI revaluation increase after deferred tax.
explanation: For this non-depreciable revalued asset, measure tax consequences on recovery through sale: DTL = (2,580,000 − 1,720,000)×20%. Net OCI increase = gross uplift less that DTL = 688,000.00.

title: Current tax reconciliation and prepayment • case 36
prompt: Accounting pretax profit is LKR 3,800,000. It includes a permanently non-deductible fine of 172,000, exempt income of 50,000, and warranty expense of 380,000 deductible only on payment. Current-year warranty payments of 80,000 are deductible and were charged against the provision, not current profit. Tax rate is 30%; tax prepayments are 300,000. No other tax adjustments exist. Find closing CURRENT tax payable, not total tax expense.
explanation: Taxable profit = 3,800,000 + fine 172,000 − exempt income 50,000 + provision expense 380,000 − deductible payments 80,000 = 4,222,000. Current tax less prepaid 300,000 = 966,600.00. Deferred tax is separate.

title: Consolidated inventory tax difference • case 36
prompt: After eliminating an intragroup profit, inventory carries in consolidated statements at LKR 1,032,000. Its tax base in the buyer’s tax jurisdiction is 1,548,000. The buyer’s enacted rate is 30%; sufficient taxable profit is probable. No offsetting, exception or other tax effects apply. Find the consolidated DTA on this inventory.
explanation: The consolidated carrying amount is below tax base, creating a deductible temporary difference of 516,000. Use the buyer’s relevant tax rate: difference ×30% = 154,800.00.

title: Depreciation after recognised impairment • case 36
prompt: Immediately before an impairment, equipment carries at LKR 1,720,000. Recoverable amount is 1,060,000 and impairment is recognised. After that date it has four years’ remaining useful life and residual value 100,000. Straight-line depreciation is appropriate; no further revaluation or impairment applies. Find depreciation for the next FULL year.
explanation: First reduce the asset to recoverable amount 1,060,000. Thereafter allocate revised depreciable amount over remaining life: (1,060,000 − 100,000)/4 = 240,000.00.

title: Allocated headquarters in CGU impairment • case 36
prompt: CGU A carries operating assets of LKR 960,000; CGU B carries 400,000. A headquarters asset of 200,000 can be allocated reasonably and consistently in proportion to those operating-asset amounts. A’s recoverable amount INCLUDING its headquarters share is 830,000. No goodwill or other assets exist. Find the impairment loss for A including its allocation.
explanation: Allocate headquarters to A: 200,000 × 960,000/(960,000+400,000) = 141,176.47. Tested A carrying amount is 1,101,176.47. Impairment versus recoverable amount 830,000 = 271,176.47.

title: Break-even value-in-use cash flow • case 36
prompt: An asset carries at LKR 1,720,000. Its fair value less costs of disposal is lower. A valid VIU model uses THREE equal year-end operating cash inflows, plus 100,000 net disposal proceeds at year three, discounted at 10%. What minimum equal ANNUAL operating cash inflow makes VIU exactly equal carrying amount? Ignore tax and other adjustments.
explanation: Let annual flow be X. X×(1/1.10 + 1/1.10² + 1/1.10³) + 100,000/1.10³ = 1,720,000. Solve for X = 661,425.98. This sensitivity calculation identifies the VIU break-even point.

title: Discounted warranty expected-value portfolio • case 36
prompt: A present warranty obligation covers 1,720 products. Per product, probabilities are 70% no defect, 25% a minor repair costing LKR 400, and 5% a major repair costing 2,000. All expected payments occur exactly in TWO years. Outflow for the portfolio is probable; appropriate discount rate is 10% with no risk double counting. Find the provision.
explanation: Expected cash payment = 1,720×(25%×400 + 5%×2,000) = 344,000.0. Discount two years at 10%: 344,000.0/1.10² = 284,297.52. The probability assessment applies to the portfolio.

title: Provision movement with revised estimate • case 36
prompt: A discounted provision opens at LKR 860,000. Unwinding for a full year is at 8%. A 100,000 settlement occurs at the year END, after unwinding. At that same reporting date, a new estimate increases the remaining provision by 122,000. No other changes occur. Find closing provision.
explanation: Closing = opening + 8% unwinding − year-end settlement + estimate increase: 860,000×1.08 −100,000 +122,000 = 950,800.00. Classification of the estimate change’s counterpart is assessed separately.

title: Revaluation increase after earlier loss • case 36
prompt: PPE carries at LKR 960,000 before revaluation and is revalued to 1,720,000. A prior revaluation decrease on THIS asset of 222,000 was recognised in profit or loss and has not been reversed. No tax effects apply. Find the current increase recognised in OCI after reversing the eligible prior loss in profit or loss.
explanation: Gross increase = 1,720,000 − 960,000 = 760,000. First recognise 222,000 in profit or loss to reverse the prior decrease. Remaining 538,000.00 is OCI revaluation surplus.

title: Nine-month depreciation and disposal gain • case 36
prompt: Equipment cost LKR 1,920,000, residual value 200,000 and useful life five years, straight-line. Two FULL years’ depreciation were recognised before this year. It is sold after nine months of the current year for 1,390,000. It was not previously held for sale and no impairment or revaluation applies. Find disposal GAIN after the required nine-month depreciation.
explanation: Annual depreciation = (1,920,000−200,000)/5. Deduct two full years and another 9/12 year from cost to obtain disposal-date carrying amount 974,000.00. Gain = proceeds − that amount = 416,000.00.

title: Customer collections with a write-off • case 36
prompt: All sales are on credit. Revenue is LKR 4,800,000; opening GROSS trade receivables are 600,000; closing GROSS receivables are 1,160,000. Receivables of 136,000 were written off during the year. There are no taxes, returns, contract balances, acquisitions or exchange changes. Find cash collected from customers.
explanation: Gross receivable roll-forward: opening + credit sales − cash receipts − write-offs = closing. Thus receipts = 4,800,000+600,000−1,160,000−136,000 = 4,104,000.00. Write-offs are not cash receipts.

title: Loan funding net cash effect • case 36
prompt: A company receives cash loan proceeds of LKR 1,720,000 and immediately pays a directly attributable lender issue fee of 38,000. Both payments are classified as financing cash flows in this case. No other cash movement occurs. Find the NET financing cash inflow from these two cash movements; this question does not require net line-item presentation.
explanation: Net financing cash effect = proceeds − cash fee = 1,720,000 − 38,000.00 = 1,682,000.00. Effective-interest amortisation later is not another inception cash payment.

title: Item-by-item NRV without offsetting headroom • case 36
prompt: Two unrelated inventory lines require separate NRV tests. A has 280 units, cost LKR 1,000 and NRV 900 each. B has 172 units, cost 1,000 and NRV 1,200 each. There is no basis to group them for the write-down test. Find TOTAL closing inventory carrying amount.
explanation: Carry A at 900 per unit and B at its lower cost of 1,000. Total = 280×900 + 172×1,000 = 424,000.00. B’s NRV headroom cannot offset A’s write-down.

title: Units-of-production intangible amortisation • case 36
prompt: A finite-life production licence costs LKR 1,620,000, has zero residual value, and is expected to support 150,000 units in total. Actual output this year is 48,000 units. A units-of-production method reliably reflects consumption and the asset was available throughout. No impairment or estimate change applies. Find annual amortisation.
explanation: Apply the supported consumption pattern: amortisation = 1,620,000 × 48,000/150,000 = 518,400.00. It is the share of expected lifetime production consumed, not an automatic straight-line charge.

title: Profit after suspended associate losses • case 36
prompt: An equity-method investment and relevant long-term interests were previously reduced to zero. Unrecognised share of prior losses totals LKR 152,000; the investor has no obligation and made no support payments. In the current year its share of associate profit is 228,000. No other adjustments or changes in interest apply. Find the share of profit that can now be RECOGNISED.
explanation: First absorb unrecognised prior losses before resuming recognised profit. Recognised amount = current profit share 228,000 − prior unrecognised losses 152,000 = 76,000.00.

title: Return recovery asset net of costs • case 37
prompt: A retailer has transferred 1,925 products. It expects 77 to be returned. Each returned product originally cost LKR 600; expected recovery handling is 20 per item and expected value deterioration is 30 per item. Estimates meet the relevant requirements. Find the separate asset for the right to recover returned products, excluding the refund liability.
explanation: Recovery asset = original carrying amount of expected returns less recovery costs and potential value decrease: 77 × (600 − 20 − 30) = 42,350.00. It is assessed separately from the customer refund liability.
family: Return recovery asset net of costs

title: Retrospective volume rebate true-up • case 37
prompt: A customer’s annual purchases reach 13,700 units at list price LKR 200. Crossing the threshold entitles it to a 5% retrospective rebate on ALL units. Cumulative revenue before this new supported estimate equals full list price; no rebate was previously accrued. The constraint permits the estimate. Find the reduction in cumulative revenue required now.
explanation: The revised transaction price reflects the retrospective rebate on all units. Revenue reduction = 13,700 × 200 × 5% = 137,000.00. Recognise the corresponding refund obligation as appropriate.

title: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation • case 37
prompt: A bundle has distinct goods A and B with stand-alone prices LKR 385,000 and 670,000. Total transaction price is 968,000. ALL paragraph 82 criteria demonstrate that the whole 87,000 discount relates only to A. A transfers now; B is not yet delivered. Find revenue recognised for A.
explanation: The specified discount-allocation exception applies. Allocate all 87,000 discount to A: 385,000 − 87,000 = 298,000.00. Do not default to relative allocation when the exception’s criteria are met.
family: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation

title: Three obligations and partial service • case 37
prompt: A contract price of LKR 2,310,000 covers goods A, goods B and twelve months of distinct support. Stand-alone prices are 600,000, 300,000 and 300,000 respectively. A is delivered, B is not, and six months of evenly provided support are complete. No allocation exception applies. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise allocation to A plus half of support: 2,310,000 × (600,000 + 150,000) / 1,200,000 = 1,443,750.00. B’s allocation remains unrecognised as revenue.

title: Progress excluding abnormal waste • case 37
prompt: An over-time contract has transaction price LKR 13,700,000. Costs incurred are 5,480,000, including abnormal waste of 274,000 that does not depict progress. Expected TOTAL productive costs excluding that waste are 10,960,000. Cost-to-cost is appropriate after excluding the waste; no other adjustment applies. Find cumulative revenue, not profit.
explanation: Exclude abnormal waste from the progress numerator. Productive progress = (5,480,000 − 274,000) / 10,960,000. Revenue = transaction price × that progress = 6,507,500.00. The wasted cost is not a revenue-producing input.

title: Uninstalled materials without margin • case 37
prompt: A single over-time construction obligation has price LKR 17,400,000. All B19(b) conditions justify recognising revenue equal to cost for significant uninstalled materials of 3,480,000 already controlled by the customer. Other productive costs incurred are 2,610,000; expected total OTHER costs are 10,440,000. No revenue was previously recognised. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise material revenue without margin: 3,480,000. Recognise the remaining price using other-cost progress: (17,400,000 − 3,480,000) × 2,610,000/10,440,000. Total revenue = 6,960,000.00.

title: Agent commission after collection • case 37
prompt: An intermediary is an AGENT and collects customer cash of LKR 2,850,000 for a completed supplier service. It must remit 88% to the supplier and is entitled to the remaining 12% commission. It controls neither the underlying service nor any distinct extra service, and there is no tax. Find its revenue.
explanation: An agent recognises its fee or commission, not the supplier’s gross billings: 2,850,000 × 12% = 342,000.00. The amount due to the supplier is separately accounted for.

title: Distinct remaining goods blended prospectively • case 37
prompt: At modification, 100 distinct goods remain under an existing contract at LKR 1,370 each. Another 50 distinct goods are added at 1,096 each. The modification is NOT a separate contract, but remaining goods are distinct from those already transferred, so paragraph 21(a) applies prospectively. Thirty of the remaining goods are then transferred. Find revenue for those thirty.
explanation: Prospective remaining consideration = 100 × 1,370 + 50 × 1,096. Divide by 150 remaining goods, then multiply by 30 = 38,360.00. Do not retrospectively revise revenue on goods already transferred.

title: FVTPL acquisition expense • case 37
prompt: A financial asset is acquired at fair value LKR 1,540,000 and is classified at FVTPL. Directly attributable broker costs are 38,500, paid separately. No fair-value change occurs immediately after purchase. Find the immediate profit-or-loss expense from acquiring this asset.
explanation: Transaction costs on an FVTPL asset are expensed. Initial asset carrying amount is fair value 1,540,000; immediate acquisition expense is 38,500.00.

title: Collateral cash-shortfall discounting • case 37
prompt: A credit loss scenario has a contractual receipt of LKR 1,925,000 due in one year. The ONLY expected recovery at that same date is collateral sale proceeds of 1,255,000, less sale costs of 87,000. Scenario probability is 100% and original EIR is 10%. Collateral is an integral contractual credit enhancement and not separately recognised. Find discounted ECL.
explanation: One-year shortfall = contractual receipt − net collateral recovery = 1,925,000 − (1,255,000 − 87,000). Discount that shortfall at 10%: 688,181.82. Do not ignore recovery costs or discount only one side of same-date cash flows.

title: Three-band provision matrix • case 37
prompt: Under the simplified lifetime-ECL approach, supported adjusted loss rates are 1% on current receivables of LKR 1,740,000, 5% on past-due balances of 485,000, and 30% on severely overdue balances of 174,000. Rates already include all required forward-looking and discounting effects. Find total loss allowance.
explanation: Apply each appropriate band rate and add: 1,740,000×1% + 485,000×5% + 174,000×30% = 93,850.00. Do not apply one blended band mechanically to all balances.

title: Equity FVOCI profit-or-loss dividend • case 37
prompt: An eligible equity investment has the irrevocable FVOCI election. During the year it gains LKR 194,000 in fair value and earns a dividend of 97,000. Dividend recognition criteria are met and the dividend clearly represents a return on investment, not recovery of cost. There are no other effects. Find income recognised in PROFIT OR LOSS.
explanation: The qualifying dividend of 97,000.00 is profit-or-loss income. The fair-value movement of 194,000 is OCI under this election and is not added to the profit-or-loss amount.

title: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset • case 37
prompt: A loan is sold with full derecognition. Immediately before sale, gross carrying amount is LKR 1,740,000, loss allowance 174,000, and cash proceeds 1,653,000. No accumulated OCI, sale fees or other adjustments exist. Find the derecognition GAIN relative to net carrying amount.
explanation: Net carrying amount = 1,740,000 − 174,000 = 1,566,000. Compare proceeds with that net amount: 1,653,000 − 1,566,000 = 87,000.00 gain. Derecognise both the gross asset and related allowance.
family: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset

title: Non-substantial liability modification gain • case 37
prompt: An amortised-cost liability is modified WITHOUT extinguishment, with no fees. Its carrying amount is LKR 1,370,000. The sole revised payment is 1,575,500 in two years. Original EIR is 10%; the modification is assessed as non-substantial. Find the immediate modification GAIN from recalculating amortised cost at the original EIR.
explanation: Revised amortised cost = 1,575,500/1.10² = 1,302,066.12. Gain = old liability 1,370,000 − revised PV = 67,933.88. The original EIR is retained for this non-extinguishing modification.

title: Credit-risk improvement allowance release • case 37
prompt: A debt asset under the GENERAL ECL model previously had significant credit-risk deterioration and lifetime allowance LKR 174,000. At reporting date the criteria for lifetime ECL are no longer met; required 12-month ECL is 28,500. No write-offs, new assets or other allowance movements occur. Find the impairment reversal in profit or loss.
explanation: When lifetime measurement is no longer required, the general model returns to 12-month ECL. Release the excess allowance: 174,000 − 28,500 = 145,500.00. This is not a receivable under mandatory simplified lifetime ECL.

title: Upstream inventory elimination with tax • case 37
prompt: P and S report profits AFTER their own tax of LKR 3,480,000 and 1,540,000. An upstream inventory sale leaves unrealised profit of 348,000 in group closing inventory. A recoverable DTA is recognised on the full elimination at 30%, with the tax effect in profit or loss. No other consolidation adjustments exist. Find TOTAL consolidated profit, before attribution to owners and NCI.
explanation: Combine separate after-tax profits, eliminate unrealised profit and recognise the recoverable tax benefit: 3,480,000 + 1,540,000 − 348,000 + 104,400.00 = 4,776,400.00. This question asks total group profit, not its attribution.

title: Full-goodwill impairment and owner profit • case 37
prompt: P owns 80% of S all year. Separate after-tax profits are P LKR 2,910,000 and S 1,070,000. Goodwill is recognised on the FULL-goodwill basis and an impairment of 385,000 is attributable to S’s CGU and allocated 80:20 between owners and NCI. No other adjustments or tax effects apply. Find consolidated profit attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Owners receive 80% of S’s profit and bear 80% of the full-goodwill loss: 2,910,000 + 80% × (1,070,000 − 385,000) = 3,458,000.00. Do not charge the owners with 100% of this full-goodwill loss.

title: Partial goodwill CGU gross-up • case 37
prompt: P owns 80% of S. Recognised PARTIAL goodwill is LKR 1,392,000; S’s other net assets in the tested CGU carry at 6,960,000. Recoverable amount of the WHOLE CGU is 7,830,000. Gross up goodwill for unrecognised NCI goodwill when testing; the whole impairment falls within grossed-up goodwill. No tax or other adjustments apply. Find impairment actually recognised on group goodwill.
explanation: Grossed-up goodwill = 1,392,000/80% = 1,740,000.00. Whole-CGU impairment = grossed goodwill + other net assets − recoverable amount = 870,000.00. Only the parent’s 80% goodwill portion is recognised, so recorded loss = 696,000.00.
reference: LKAS 36 Appendix C paras C4–C8; SLFRS 10 para B86

title: Consolidated retained earnings bridge • case 37
prompt: P owns 75% of S. At year end P retained earnings are LKR 4,850,000, and S retained earnings 3,110,000. S retained earnings at acquisition were 1,000,000. Cumulative post-acquisition extra FV depreciation is 174,000. A downstream sale by P leaves unrealised profit of 117,000. No tax, goodwill impairment, dividends recognised by P, OCI or other adjustments apply. Find consolidated retained earnings attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Group owners’ retained earnings = parent RE + 75% of adjusted post-acquisition S reserves − the parent’s downstream unrealised profit: 6,185,000.00. Pre-acquisition reserves do not enter post-acquisition group retained earnings.

title: Loss of control and translation reserve • case 37
prompt: P loses control of a foreign subsidiary. Proceeds are LKR 3,680,000; retained interest FV 870,000; NCI carrying amount 485,000; consolidated net assets INCLUDING goodwill 3,710,000. A cumulative translation GAIN of 174,000, entirely attributable to P, must be reclassified to profit or loss on loss of control. No other effects apply. Find total disposal gain including that reclassification.
explanation: Base gain = proceeds + retained FV + NCI − net assets = 1,325,000.00. Add the parent’s translation gain recycled on disposal: 174,000. Total = 1,499,000.00.
family: Loss of control and translation reserve

title: Residual guarantee expected payment • case 37
prompt: A lessee owes three year-end rentals of LKR 385,000. It guarantees residual value up to 200,000, but the amount EXPECTED to be payable under that guarantee is 67,000 at year three. Discount rate is 10%. No other liability payments exist. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the amount expected to be payable, not automatically the maximum guarantee. Liability = PV of three rentals + 67,000/1.10³ = 1,007,776.11.

title: Reasonably certain purchase option PV • case 37
prompt: A lease requires three year-end rentals of LKR 335,000, plus a purchase option price of 870,000 payable at year three. Exercise is reasonably certain. Discount rate is 10%. No incentives, other payments or initial prepayments apply. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the reasonably certain purchase price in the liability: PV of rentals + purchase price discounted for three years = 1,486,739.29. Do not omit or leave the future option payment undiscounted.

title: Lease and service component allocation • case 37
prompt: A two-year contract requires bundled payments of LKR 435,000 at each year end. Relative stand-alone prices are equipment lease 200,000 and distinct maintenance 50,000 per year. The lessee does NOT elect to combine components. Lease discount rate is 10%; no other payments exist. Find initial lease liability for the LEASE component only.
explanation: Allocate 200,000/250,000 = 80% of each bundled payment to the lease: 348,000.00. Discount those two lease payments, excluding maintenance, to obtain 603,966.94.

title: Exempt short-term lease rent-free start • case 37
prompt: A twelve-month lease with no purchase option qualifies for the elected short-term exemption. The first three months are rent free, then nine monthly payments of LKR 38,500 are due. The asset is available throughout and straight-line expense is appropriate. Find lease expense for the FIRST six months, ignoring accrual settlement timing.
explanation: Total fixed payments are nine rents. Spread evenly over all twelve months: 38,500 × 9/12 × 6 = 173,250.00. Rent-free months still receive an expense allocation.

title: Sale-and-leaseback rights transferred • case 37
prompt: A transfer qualifies as a sale under SLFRS 15 at fair value LKR 17,400,000; asset carrying amount is 9,700,000. Market-rate leaseback payments have PV 6,960,000. There are no off-market adjustments or variable-payment complications. At inception, what sale gain is recognised for rights TRANSFERRED to the buyer-lessor?
explanation: Total gain = 17,400,000 − 9,700,000 = 7,700,000. Retained-use proportion = lease PV / fair value = 40%. Recognise only the transferred-rights proportion of the gain: 4,620,000.00.

title: Reassessed bargain purchase gain • case 37
prompt: After the required reassessment, final acquisition-date consideration is LKR 3,480,000, NCI fair value is 400,000 and identifiable net assets are 5,220,000. There is no prior holding or other adjustment. Find the bargain purchase gain recognised in profit or loss.
explanation: Net identifiable assets exceed consideration plus NCI: 5,220,000 − 3,480,000 − 400,000 = 1,340,000.00. Reassessment has been completed before recognising the gain.

title: Acquired contingent liability in goodwill • case 37
prompt: Consideration is LKR 5,350,000; NCI FV is 500,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired contingent liability are 4,110,000. The acquired item is a present obligation with reliably measurable FV 385,000 and qualifies for recognition despite non-probable outflow. No tax or other adjustment applies. Find goodwill after recognising it.
explanation: Recognise the qualifying acquired liability: net identifiable assets become 4,110,000 − 385,000. Goodwill = consideration + NCI − adjusted net assets = 2,125,000.00.

title: Separate acquired brand from goodwill • case 37
prompt: Consideration is LKR 4,850,000; NCI FV 600,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired separable brand are 4,080,000. Brand FV is 770,000; tax base is zero and 30% DTL must be recognised. No other adjustments apply. Find goodwill after separate brand and tax recognition.
explanation: An identifiable acquired brand is separate from goodwill. Net addition to identifiable assets = brand FV − 30% DTL = 539,000.00. Goodwill = 4,850,000 + 600,000 − (4,080,000 + 539,000.00) = 831,000.00.

title: Acquisition costs versus issue costs • case 37
prompt: A business acquisition has consideration LKR 3,110,000. Additional costs are acquisition advisory 174,000, qualifying equity-issue costs 70,000 and qualifying debt-issue costs 40,000. The issue costs follow their relevant standards, and no immediate debt-cost amortisation or other expense arises this period. Find the immediate acquisition-related PROFIT-OR-LOSS expense from these costs.
explanation: Expense advisory acquisition costs of 174,000.00. Qualifying equity and debt issuance costs follow their respective standards and are not added to this immediate acquisition-service expense or goodwill.

title: Temporary difference and enacted rate change • case 37
prompt: A taxable temporary difference opens at LKR 200,000 with a DTL measured at 25%. At year end the difference is 485,000 and the enacted rate expected on reversal is 30%. Both the underlying movements and rate change belong in profit or loss. No other tax movements exist. Find deferred tax expense for the year.
explanation: Opening DTL = 200,000×25% = 50,000. Closing DTL = 485,000×30% = 145,500.00. Expense is the full increase, including rate remeasurement: 95,500.00. Rates are exercise assumptions.
family: Temporary difference and enacted rate change

title: Revalued non-depreciable land tax basis • case 37
prompt: Non-depreciable land is revalued from cost LKR 1,740,000 to fair value 2,610,000; tax base remains cost. The enacted rate for recovery through SALE is 20%, while a 30% use rate would otherwise apply. The revaluation and associated tax go to OCI. No other effects exist. Find the net OCI revaluation increase after deferred tax.
explanation: For this non-depreciable revalued asset, measure tax consequences on recovery through sale: DTL = (2,610,000 − 1,740,000)×20%. Net OCI increase = gross uplift less that DTL = 696,000.00.

title: Current tax reconciliation and prepayment • case 37
prompt: Accounting pretax profit is LKR 3,850,000. It includes a permanently non-deductible fine of 174,000, exempt income of 50,000, and warranty expense of 385,000 deductible only on payment. Current-year warranty payments of 80,000 are deductible and were charged against the provision, not current profit. Tax rate is 30%; tax prepayments are 300,000. No other tax adjustments exist. Find closing CURRENT tax payable, not total tax expense.
explanation: Taxable profit = 3,850,000 + fine 174,000 − exempt income 50,000 + provision expense 385,000 − deductible payments 80,000 = 4,279,000. Current tax less prepaid 300,000 = 983,700.00. Deferred tax is separate.

title: Consolidated inventory tax difference • case 37
prompt: After eliminating an intragroup profit, inventory carries in consolidated statements at LKR 1,044,000. Its tax base in the buyer’s tax jurisdiction is 1,566,000. The buyer’s enacted rate is 30%; sufficient taxable profit is probable. No offsetting, exception or other tax effects apply. Find the consolidated DTA on this inventory.
explanation: The consolidated carrying amount is below tax base, creating a deductible temporary difference of 522,000. Use the buyer’s relevant tax rate: difference ×30% = 156,600.00.

title: Depreciation after recognised impairment • case 37
prompt: Immediately before an impairment, equipment carries at LKR 1,740,000. Recoverable amount is 1,070,000 and impairment is recognised. After that date it has four years’ remaining useful life and residual value 100,000. Straight-line depreciation is appropriate; no further revaluation or impairment applies. Find depreciation for the next FULL year.
explanation: First reduce the asset to recoverable amount 1,070,000. Thereafter allocate revised depreciable amount over remaining life: (1,070,000 − 100,000)/4 = 242,500.00.

title: Allocated headquarters in CGU impairment • case 37
prompt: CGU A carries operating assets of LKR 970,000; CGU B carries 400,000. A headquarters asset of 200,000 can be allocated reasonably and consistently in proportion to those operating-asset amounts. A’s recoverable amount INCLUDING its headquarters share is 835,000. No goodwill or other assets exist. Find the impairment loss for A including its allocation.
explanation: Allocate headquarters to A: 200,000 × 970,000/(970,000+400,000) = 141,605.84. Tested A carrying amount is 1,111,605.84. Impairment versus recoverable amount 835,000 = 276,605.84.

title: Break-even value-in-use cash flow • case 37
prompt: An asset carries at LKR 1,740,000. Its fair value less costs of disposal is lower. A valid VIU model uses THREE equal year-end operating cash inflows, plus 100,000 net disposal proceeds at year three, discounted at 10%. What minimum equal ANNUAL operating cash inflow makes VIU exactly equal carrying amount? Ignore tax and other adjustments.
explanation: Let annual flow be X. X×(1/1.10 + 1/1.10² + 1/1.10³) + 100,000/1.10³ = 1,740,000. Solve for X = 669,468.28. This sensitivity calculation identifies the VIU break-even point.

title: Discounted warranty expected-value portfolio • case 37
prompt: A present warranty obligation covers 1,740 products. Per product, probabilities are 70% no defect, 25% a minor repair costing LKR 400, and 5% a major repair costing 2,000. All expected payments occur exactly in TWO years. Outflow for the portfolio is probable; appropriate discount rate is 10% with no risk double counting. Find the provision.
explanation: Expected cash payment = 1,740×(25%×400 + 5%×2,000) = 348,000.0. Discount two years at 10%: 348,000.0/1.10² = 287,603.31. The probability assessment applies to the portfolio.

title: Provision movement with revised estimate • case 37
prompt: A discounted provision opens at LKR 870,000. Unwinding for a full year is at 8%. A 100,000 settlement occurs at the year END, after unwinding. At that same reporting date, a new estimate increases the remaining provision by 124,000. No other changes occur. Find closing provision.
explanation: Closing = opening + 8% unwinding − year-end settlement + estimate increase: 870,000×1.08 −100,000 +124,000 = 963,600.00. Classification of the estimate change’s counterpart is assessed separately.

title: Revaluation increase after earlier loss • case 37
prompt: PPE carries at LKR 970,000 before revaluation and is revalued to 1,740,000. A prior revaluation decrease on THIS asset of 224,000 was recognised in profit or loss and has not been reversed. No tax effects apply. Find the current increase recognised in OCI after reversing the eligible prior loss in profit or loss.
explanation: Gross increase = 1,740,000 − 970,000 = 770,000. First recognise 224,000 in profit or loss to reverse the prior decrease. Remaining 546,000.00 is OCI revaluation surplus.

title: Nine-month depreciation and disposal gain • case 37
prompt: Equipment cost LKR 1,940,000, residual value 200,000 and useful life five years, straight-line. Two FULL years’ depreciation were recognised before this year. It is sold after nine months of the current year for 1,405,000. It was not previously held for sale and no impairment or revaluation applies. Find disposal GAIN after the required nine-month depreciation.
explanation: Annual depreciation = (1,940,000−200,000)/5. Deduct two full years and another 9/12 year from cost to obtain disposal-date carrying amount 983,000.00. Gain = proceeds − that amount = 422,000.00.

prompt: All sales are on credit. Revenue is LKR 4,850,000; opening GROSS trade receivables are 600,000; closing GROSS receivables are 1,170,000. Receivables of 137,000 were written off during the year. There are no taxes, returns, contract balances, acquisitions or exchange changes. Find cash collected from customers.
explanation: Gross receivable roll-forward: opening + credit sales − cash receipts − write-offs = closing. Thus receipts = 4,850,000+600,000−1,170,000−137,000 = 4,143,000.00. Write-offs are not cash receipts.

title: Loan funding net cash effect • case 37
prompt: A company receives cash loan proceeds of LKR 1,740,000 and immediately pays a directly attributable lender issue fee of 38,500. Both payments are classified as financing cash flows in this case. No other cash movement occurs. Find the NET financing cash inflow from these two cash movements; this question does not require net line-item presentation.
explanation: Net financing cash effect = proceeds − cash fee = 1,740,000 − 38,500.00 = 1,701,500.00. Effective-interest amortisation later is not another inception cash payment.

title: Item-by-item NRV without offsetting headroom • case 37
prompt: Two unrelated inventory lines require separate NRV tests. A has 285 units, cost LKR 1,000 and NRV 900 each. B has 174 units, cost 1,000 and NRV 1,200 each. There is no basis to group them for the write-down test. Find TOTAL closing inventory carrying amount.
explanation: Carry A at 900 per unit and B at its lower cost of 1,000. Total = 285×900 + 174×1,000 = 430,500.00. B’s NRV headroom cannot offset A’s write-down.

title: Units-of-production intangible amortisation • case 37
prompt: A finite-life production licence costs LKR 1,640,000, has zero residual value, and is expected to support 150,000 units in total. Actual output this year is 48,500 units. title: Profit after suspended associate losses • case 37
prompt: An equity-method investment and relevant long-term interests were previously reduced to zero. Unrecognised share of prior losses totals LKR 154,000; the investor has no obligation and made no support payments. In the current year its share of associate profit is 231,000. No other adjustments or changes in interest apply. Find the share of profit that can now be RECOGNISED.
explanation: First absorb unrecognised prior losses before resuming recognised profit. Recognised amount = current profit share 231,000 − prior unrecognised losses 154,000 = 77,000.00.

title: Return recovery asset net of costs • case 38
prompt: A retailer has transferred 1,950 products. It expects 78 to be returned. Each returned product originally cost LKR 600; expected recovery handling is 20 per item and expected value deterioration is 30 per item. Estimates meet the relevant requirements. Find the separate asset for the right to recover returned products, excluding the refund liability.
explanation: Recovery asset = original carrying amount of expected returns less recovery costs and potential value decrease: 78 × (600 − 20 − 30) = 42,900.00. It is assessed separately from the customer refund liability.
family: Return recovery asset net of costs

title: Retrospective volume rebate true-up • case 38
prompt: A customer’s annual purchases reach 13,800 units at list price LKR 200. Crossing the threshold entitles it to a 5% retrospective rebate on ALL units. Cumulative revenue before this new supported estimate equals full list price; no rebate was previously accrued. The constraint permits the estimate. Find the reduction in cumulative revenue required now.
explanation: The revised transaction price reflects the retrospective rebate on all units. Revenue reduction = 13,800 × 200 × 5% = 138,000.00. Recognise the corresponding refund obligation as appropriate.

title: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation • case 38
prompt: A bundle has distinct goods A and B with stand-alone prices LKR 390,000 and 680,000. Total transaction price is 982,000. ALL paragraph 82 criteria demonstrate that the whole 88,000 discount relates only to A. A transfers now; B is not yet delivered. Find revenue recognised for A.
explanation: The specified discount-allocation exception applies. Allocate all 88,000 discount to A: 390,000 − 88,000 = 302,000.00. Do not default to relative allocation when the exception’s criteria are met.
family: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation

title: Three obligations and partial service • case 38
prompt: A contract price of LKR 2,340,000 covers goods A, goods B and twelve months of distinct support. Stand-alone prices are 600,000, 300,000 and 300,000 respectively. A is delivered, B is not, and six months of evenly provided support are complete. No allocation exception applies. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise allocation to A plus half of support: 2,340,000 × (600,000 + 150,000) / 1,200,000 = 1,462,500.00. B’s allocation remains unrecognised as revenue.

title: Progress excluding abnormal waste • case 38
prompt: An over-time contract has transaction price LKR 13,800,000. Costs incurred are 5,520,000, including abnormal waste of 276,000 that does not depict progress. Expected TOTAL productive costs excluding that waste are 11,040,000. Cost-to-cost is appropriate after excluding the waste; no other adjustment applies. Find cumulative revenue, not profit.
explanation: Exclude abnormal waste from the progress numerator. Productive progress = (5,520,000 − 276,000) / 11,040,000. Revenue = transaction price × that progress = 6,555,000.00. The wasted cost is not a revenue-producing input.

title: Uninstalled materials without margin • case 38
prompt: A single over-time construction obligation has price LKR 17,600,000. All B19(b) conditions justify recognising revenue equal to cost for significant uninstalled materials of 3,520,000 already controlled by the customer. Other productive costs incurred are 2,640,000; expected total OTHER costs are 10,560,000. No revenue was previously recognised. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise material revenue without margin: 3,520,000. Recognise the remaining price using other-cost progress: (17,600,000 − 3,520,000) × 2,640,000/10,560,000. Total revenue = 7,040,000.00.

title: Agent commission after collection • case 38
prompt: An intermediary is an AGENT and collects customer cash of LKR 2,900,000 for a completed supplier service. It must remit 88% to the supplier and is entitled to the remaining 12% commission. It controls neither the underlying service nor any distinct extra service, and there is no tax. Find its revenue.
explanation: An agent recognises its fee or commission, not the supplier’s gross billings: 2,900,000 × 12% = 348,000.00. The amount due to the supplier is separately accounted for.

title: Distinct remaining goods blended prospectively • case 38
prompt: At modification, 100 distinct goods remain under an existing contract at LKR 1,380 each. Another 50 distinct goods are added at 1,104 each. The modification is NOT a separate contract, but remaining goods are distinct from those already transferred, so paragraph 21(a) applies prospectively. Thirty of the remaining goods are then transferred. Find revenue for those thirty.
explanation: Prospective remaining consideration = 100 × 1,380 + 50 × 1,104. Divide by 150 remaining goods, then multiply by 30 = 38,640.00. Do not retrospectively revise revenue on goods already transferred.

title: FVTPL acquisition expense • case 38
prompt: A financial asset is acquired at fair value LKR 1,560,000 and is classified at FVTPL. Directly attributable broker costs are 39,000, paid separately. No fair-value change occurs immediately after purchase. Find the immediate profit-or-loss expense from acquiring this asset.
explanation: Transaction costs on an FVTPL asset are expensed. Initial asset carrying amount is fair value 1,560,000; immediate acquisition expense is 39,000.00.

title: Collateral cash-shortfall discounting • case 38
prompt: A credit loss scenario has a contractual receipt of LKR 1,950,000 due in one year. The ONLY expected recovery at that same date is collateral sale proceeds of 1,270,000, less sale costs of 88,000. Scenario probability is 100% and original EIR is 10%. Collateral is an integral contractual credit enhancement and not separately recognised. Find discounted ECL.
explanation: One-year shortfall = contractual receipt − net collateral recovery = 1,950,000 − (1,270,000 − 88,000). Discount that shortfall at 10%: 698,181.82. Do not ignore recovery costs or discount only one side of same-date cash flows.

title: Three-band provision matrix • case 38
prompt: Under the simplified lifetime-ECL approach, supported adjusted loss rates are 1% on current receivables of LKR 1,760,000, 5% on past-due balances of 490,000, and 30% on severely overdue balances of 176,000. Rates already include all required forward-looking and discounting effects. Find total loss allowance.
explanation: Apply each appropriate band rate and add: 1,760,000×1% + 490,000×5% + 176,000×30% = 94,900.00. Do not apply one blended band mechanically to all balances.

title: Equity FVOCI profit-or-loss dividend • case 38
prompt: An eligible equity investment has the irrevocable FVOCI election. During the year it gains LKR 196,000 in fair value and earns a dividend of 98,000. Dividend recognition criteria are met and the dividend clearly represents a return on investment, not recovery of cost. There are no other effects. Find income recognised in PROFIT OR LOSS.
explanation: The qualifying dividend of 98,000.00 is profit-or-loss income. The fair-value movement of 196,000 is OCI under this election and is not added to the profit-or-loss amount.

title: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset • case 38
prompt: A loan is sold with full derecognition. Immediately before sale, gross carrying amount is LKR 1,760,000, loss allowance 176,000, and cash proceeds 1,672,000. No accumulated OCI, sale fees or other adjustments exist. Find the derecognition GAIN relative to net carrying amount.
explanation: Net carrying amount = 1,760,000 − 176,000 = 1,584,000. Compare proceeds with that net amount: 1,672,000 − 1,584,000 = 88,000.00 gain. Derecognise both the gross asset and related allowance.
family: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset

title: Non-substantial liability modification gain • case 38
prompt: An amortised-cost liability is modified WITHOUT extinguishment, with no fees. Its carrying amount is LKR 1,380,000. The sole revised payment is 1,587,000 in two years. Original EIR is 10%; the modification is assessed as non-substantial. Find the immediate modification GAIN from recalculating amortised cost at the original EIR.
explanation: Revised amortised cost = 1,587,000/1.10² = 1,311,570.25. Gain = old liability 1,380,000 − revised PV = 68,429.75. The original EIR is retained for this non-extinguishing modification.

title: Credit-risk improvement allowance release • case 38
prompt: A debt asset under the GENERAL ECL model previously had significant credit-risk deterioration and lifetime allowance LKR 176,000. At reporting date the criteria for lifetime ECL are no longer met; required 12-month ECL is 29,000. No write-offs, new assets or other allowance movements occur. Find the impairment reversal in profit or loss.
explanation: When lifetime measurement is no longer required, the general model returns to 12-month ECL. Release the excess allowance: 176,000 − 29,000 = 147,000.00. This is not a receivable under mandatory simplified lifetime ECL.

title: Upstream inventory elimination with tax • case 38
prompt: P and S report profits AFTER their own tax of LKR 3,520,000 and 1,560,000. An upstream inventory sale leaves unrealised profit of 352,000 in group closing inventory. A recoverable DTA is recognised on the full elimination at 30%, with the tax effect in profit or loss. No other consolidation adjustments exist. Find TOTAL consolidated profit, before attribution to owners and NCI.
explanation: Combine separate after-tax profits, eliminate unrealised profit and recognise the recoverable tax benefit: 3,520,000 + 1,560,000 − 352,000 + 105,600.00 = 4,833,600.00. This question asks total group profit, not its attribution.

title: Full-goodwill impairment and owner profit • case 38
prompt: P owns 80% of S all year. Separate after-tax profits are P LKR 2,940,000 and S 1,080,000. Goodwill is recognised on the FULL-goodwill basis and an impairment of 390,000 is attributable to S’s CGU and allocated 80:20 between owners and NCI. No other adjustments or tax effects apply. Find consolidated profit attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Owners receive 80% of S’s profit and bear 80% of the full-goodwill loss: 2,940,000 + 80% × (1,080,000 − 390,000) = 3,492,000.00. Do not charge the owners with 100% of this full-goodwill loss.

title: Partial goodwill CGU gross-up • case 38
prompt: P owns 80% of S. Recognised PARTIAL goodwill is LKR 1,408,000; S’s other net assets in the tested CGU carry at 7,040,000. Recoverable amount of the WHOLE CGU is 7,920,000. Gross up goodwill for unrecognised NCI goodwill when testing; the whole impairment falls within grossed-up goodwill. No tax or other adjustments apply. Find impairment actually recognised on group goodwill.
explanation: Grossed-up goodwill = 1,408,000/80% = 1,760,000.00. Whole-CGU impairment = grossed goodwill + other net assets − recoverable amount = 880,000.00. Only the parent’s 80% goodwill portion is recognised, so recorded loss = 704,000.00.
reference: LKAS 36 Appendix C paras C4–C8; SLFRS 10 para B86

title: Consolidated retained earnings bridge • case 38
prompt: P owns 75% of S. At year end P retained earnings are LKR 4,900,000, and S retained earnings 3,140,000. S retained earnings at acquisition were 1,000,000. Cumulative post-acquisition extra FV depreciation is 176,000. A downstream sale by P leaves unrealised profit of 118,000. No tax, goodwill impairment, dividends recognised by P, OCI or other adjustments apply. Find consolidated retained earnings attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Group owners’ retained earnings = parent RE + 75% of adjusted post-acquisition S reserves − the parent’s downstream unrealised profit: 6,255,000.00. Pre-acquisition reserves do not enter post-acquisition group retained earnings.

title: Loss of control and translation reserve • case 38
prompt: P loses control of a foreign subsidiary. Proceeds are LKR 3,720,000; retained interest FV 880,000; NCI carrying amount 490,000; consolidated net assets INCLUDING goodwill 3,740,000. A cumulative translation GAIN of 176,000, entirely attributable to P, must be reclassified to profit or loss on loss of control. No other effects apply. Find total disposal gain including that reclassification.
explanation: Base gain = proceeds + retained FV + NCI − net assets = 1,350,000.00. Add the parent’s translation gain recycled on disposal: 176,000. Total = 1,526,000.00.
family: Loss of control and translation reserve

title: Residual guarantee expected payment • case 38
prompt: A lessee owes three year-end rentals of LKR 390,000. It guarantees residual value up to 200,000, but the amount EXPECTED to be payable under that guarantee is 68,000 at year three. Discount rate is 10%. No other liability payments exist. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the amount expected to be payable, not automatically the maximum guarantee. Liability = PV of three rentals + 68,000/1.10³ = 1,020,961.68.

title: Reasonably certain purchase option PV • case 38
prompt: A lease requires three year-end rentals of LKR 340,000, plus a purchase option price of 880,000 payable at year three. Exercise is reasonably certain. Discount rate is 10%. No incentives, other payments or initial prepayments apply. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the reasonably certain purchase price in the liability: PV of rentals + purchase price discounted for three years = 1,506,686.70. Do not omit or leave the future option payment undiscounted.

title: Lease and service component allocation • case 38
prompt: A two-year contract requires bundled payments of LKR 440,000 at each year end. Relative stand-alone prices are equipment lease 200,000 and distinct maintenance 50,000 per year. The lessee does NOT elect to combine components. Lease discount rate is 10%; no other payments exist. Find initial lease liability for the LEASE component only.
explanation: Allocate 200,000/250,000 = 80% of each bundled payment to the lease: 352,000.00. Discount those two lease payments, excluding maintenance, to obtain 610,909.09.

title: Exempt short-term lease rent-free start • case 38
prompt: A twelve-month lease with no purchase option qualifies for the elected short-term exemption. The first three months are rent free, then nine monthly payments of LKR 39,000 are due. The asset is available throughout and straight-line expense is appropriate. Find lease expense for the FIRST six months, ignoring accrual settlement timing.
explanation: Total fixed payments are nine rents. Spread evenly over all twelve months: 39,000 × 9/12 × 6 = 175,500.00. Rent-free months still receive an expense allocation.

title: Sale-and-leaseback rights transferred • case 38
prompt: A transfer qualifies as a sale under SLFRS 15 at fair value LKR 17,600,000; asset carrying amount is 9,800,000. Market-rate leaseback payments have PV 7,040,000. There are no off-market adjustments or variable-payment complications. At inception, what sale gain is recognised for rights TRANSFERRED to the buyer-lessor?
explanation: Total gain = 17,600,000 − 9,800,000 = 7,800,000. Retained-use proportion = lease PV / fair value = 40%. Recognise only the transferred-rights proportion of the gain: 4,680,000.00.

title: Reassessed bargain purchase gain • case 38
prompt: After the required reassessment, final acquisition-date consideration is LKR 3,520,000, NCI fair value is 400,000 and identifiable net assets are 5,280,000. There is no prior holding or other adjustment. Find the bargain purchase gain recognised in profit or loss.
explanation: Net identifiable assets exceed consideration plus NCI: 5,280,000 − 3,520,000 − 400,000 = 1,360,000.00. Reassessment has been completed before recognising the gain.

title: Acquired contingent liability in goodwill • case 38
prompt: Consideration is LKR 5,400,000; NCI FV is 500,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired contingent liability are 4,140,000. The acquired item is a present obligation with reliably measurable FV 390,000 and qualifies for recognition despite non-probable outflow. No tax or other adjustment applies. Find goodwill after recognising it.
explanation: Recognise the qualifying acquired liability: net identifiable assets become 4,140,000 − 390,000. Goodwill = consideration + NCI − adjusted net assets = 2,150,000.00.

title: Separate acquired brand from goodwill • case 38
prompt: Consideration is LKR 4,900,000; NCI FV 600,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired separable brand are 4,120,000. Brand FV is 780,000; tax base is zero and 30% DTL must be recognised. No other adjustments apply. Find goodwill after separate brand and tax recognition.
explanation: An identifiable acquired brand is separate from goodwill. Net addition to identifiable assets = brand FV − 30% DTL = 546,000.00. Goodwill = 4,900,000 + 600,000 − (4,120,000 + 546,000.00) = 834,000.00.

title: Acquisition costs versus issue costs • case 38
prompt: A business acquisition has consideration LKR 3,140,000. Additional costs are acquisition advisory 176,000, qualifying equity-issue costs 70,000 and qualifying debt-issue costs 40,000. The issue costs follow their relevant standards, and no immediate debt-cost amortisation or other expense arises this period. Find the immediate acquisition-related PROFIT-OR-LOSS expense from these costs.
explanation: Expense advisory acquisition costs of 176,000.00. Qualifying equity and debt issuance costs follow their respective standards and are not added to this immediate acquisition-service expense or goodwill.

title: Temporary difference and enacted rate change • case 38
prompt: A taxable temporary difference opens at LKR 200,000 with a DTL measured at 25%. At year end the difference is 490,000 and the enacted rate expected on reversal is 30%. Both the underlying movements and rate change belong in profit or loss. No other tax movements exist. Find deferred tax expense for the year.
explanation: Opening DTL = 200,000×25% = 50,000. Closing DTL = 490,000×30% = 147,000.00. Expense is the full increase, including rate remeasurement: 97,000.00. Rates are exercise assumptions.
family: Temporary difference and enacted rate change

title: Revalued non-depreciable land tax basis • case 38
prompt: Non-depreciable land is revalued from cost LKR 1,760,000 to fair value 2,640,000; tax base remains cost. The enacted rate for recovery through SALE is 20%, while a 30% use rate would otherwise apply. The revaluation and associated tax go to OCI. No other effects exist. Find the net OCI revaluation increase after deferred tax.
explanation: For this non-depreciable revalued asset, measure tax consequences on recovery through sale: DTL = (2,640,000 − 1,760,000)×20%. Net OCI increase = gross uplift less that DTL = 704,000.00.

title: Current tax reconciliation and prepayment • case 38
prompt: Accounting pretax profit is LKR 3,900,000. It includes a permanently non-deductible fine of 176,000, exempt income of 50,000, and warranty expense of 390,000 deductible only on payment. Current-year warranty payments of 80,000 are deductible and were charged against the provision, not current profit. Tax rate is 30%; tax prepayments are 300,000. No other tax adjustments exist. Find closing CURRENT tax payable, not total tax expense.
explanation: Taxable profit = 3,900,000 + fine 176,000 − exempt income 50,000 + provision expense 390,000 − deductible payments 80,000 = 4,336,000. Current tax less prepaid 300,000 = 1,000,800.00. Deferred tax is separate.

title: Consolidated inventory tax difference • case 38
prompt: After eliminating an intragroup profit, inventory carries in consolidated statements at LKR 1,056,000. Its tax base in the buyer’s tax jurisdiction is 1,584,000. The buyer’s enacted rate is 30%; sufficient taxable profit is probable. No offsetting, exception or other tax effects apply. Find the consolidated DTA on this inventory.
explanation: The consolidated carrying amount is below tax base, creating a deductible temporary difference of 528,000. Use the buyer’s relevant tax rate: difference ×30% = 158,400.00.

title: Depreciation after recognised impairment • case 38
prompt: Immediately before an impairment, equipment carries at LKR 1,760,000. Recoverable amount is 1,080,000 and impairment is recognised. After that date it has four years’ remaining useful life and residual value 100,000. Straight-line depreciation is appropriate; no further revaluation or impairment applies. Find depreciation for the next FULL year.
explanation: First reduce the asset to recoverable amount 1,080,000. Thereafter allocate revised depreciable amount over remaining life: (1,080,000 − 100,000)/4 = 245,000.00.

title: Allocated headquarters in CGU impairment • case 38
prompt: CGU A carries operating assets of LKR 980,000; CGU B carries 400,000. A headquarters asset of 200,000 can be allocated reasonably and consistently in proportion to those operating-asset amounts. A’s recoverable amount INCLUDING its headquarters share is 840,000. No goodwill or other assets exist. Find the impairment loss for A including its allocation.
explanation: Allocate headquarters to A: 200,000 × 980,000/(980,000+400,000) = 142,028.99. Tested A carrying amount is 1,122,028.99. Impairment versus recoverable amount 840,000 = 282,028.99.

title: Break-even value-in-use cash flow • case 38
prompt: An asset carries at LKR 1,760,000. Its fair value less costs of disposal is lower. A valid VIU model uses THREE equal year-end operating cash inflows, plus 100,000 net disposal proceeds at year three, discounted at 10%. What minimum equal ANNUAL operating cash inflow makes VIU exactly equal carrying amount? Ignore tax and other adjustments.
explanation: Let annual flow be X. X×(1/1.10 + 1/1.10² + 1/1.10³) + 100,000/1.10³ = 1,760,000. Solve for X = 677,510.57. This sensitivity calculation identifies the VIU break-even point.

title: Discounted warranty expected-value portfolio • case 38
prompt: A present warranty obligation covers 1,760 products. Per product, probabilities are 70% no defect, 25% a minor repair costing LKR 400, and 5% a major repair costing 2,000. All expected payments occur exactly in TWO years. Outflow for the portfolio is probable; appropriate discount rate is 10% with no risk double counting. Find the provision.
explanation: Expected cash payment = 1,760×(25%×400 + 5%×2,000) = 352,000.0. Discount two years at 10%: 352,000.0/1.10² = 290,909.09. The probability assessment applies to the portfolio.

title: Provision movement with revised estimate • case 38
prompt: A discounted provision opens at LKR 880,000. Unwinding for a full year is at 8%. A 100,000 settlement occurs at the year END, after unwinding. At that same reporting date, a new estimate increases the remaining provision by 126,000. No other changes occur. Find closing provision.
explanation: Closing = opening + 8% unwinding − year-end settlement + estimate increase: 880,000×1.08 −100,000 +126,000 = 976,400.00. Classification of the estimate change’s counterpart is assessed separately.

title: Revaluation increase after earlier loss • case 38
prompt: PPE carries at LKR 980,000 before revaluation and is revalued to 1,760,000. A prior revaluation decrease on THIS asset of 226,000 was recognised in profit or loss and has not been reversed. No tax effects apply. Find the current increase recognised in OCI after reversing the eligible prior loss in profit or loss.
explanation: Gross increase = 1,760,000 − 980,000 = 780,000. First recognise 226,000 in profit or loss to reverse the prior decrease. Remaining 554,000.00 is OCI revaluation surplus.

title: Nine-month depreciation and disposal gain • case 38
prompt: Equipment cost LKR 1,960,000, residual value 200,000 and useful life five years, straight-line. Two FULL years’ depreciation were recognised before this year. It is sold after nine months of the current year for 1,420,000. It was not previously held for sale and no impairment or revaluation applies. Find disposal GAIN after the required nine-month depreciation.
explanation: Annual depreciation = (1,960,000−200,000)/5. Deduct two full years and another 9/12 year from cost to obtain disposal-date carrying amount 992,000.00. Gain = proceeds − that amount = 428,000.00.

title: Customer collections with a write-off • case 38
prompt: All sales are on credit. Revenue is LKR 4,900,000; opening GROSS trade receivables are 600,000; closing GROSS receivables are 1,180,000. Receivables of 138,000 were written off during the year. There are no taxes, returns, contract balances, acquisitions or exchange changes. Find cash collected from customers.
explanation: Gross receivable roll-forward: opening + credit sales − cash receipts − write-offs = closing. Thus receipts = 4,900,000+600,000−1,180,000−138,000 = 4,182,000.00. Write-offs are not cash receipts.

title: Loan funding net cash effect • case 38
prompt: A company receives cash loan proceeds of LKR 1,760,000 and immediately pays a directly attributable lender issue fee of 39,000. Both payments are classified as financing cash flows in this case. No other cash movement occurs. Find the NET financing cash inflow from these two cash movements; this question does not require net line-item presentation.
explanation: Net financing cash effect = proceeds − cash fee = 1,760,000 − 39,000.00 = 1,721,000.00. Effective-interest amortisation later is not another inception cash payment.

title: Item-by-item NRV without offsetting headroom • case 38
prompt: Two unrelated inventory lines require separate NRV tests. A has 290 units, cost LKR 1,000 and NRV 900 each. B has 176 units, cost 1,000 and NRV 1,200 each. There is no basis to group them for the write-down test. Find TOTAL closing inventory carrying amount.
explanation: Carry A at 900 per unit and B at its lower cost of 1,000. Total = 290×900 + 176×1,000 = 437,000.00. B’s NRV headroom cannot offset A’s write-down.

title: Units-of-production intangible amortisation • case 38
prompt: A finite-life production licence costs LKR 1,660,000, has zero residual value, and is expected to support 150,000 units in total. Actual output this year is 49,000 units. A units-of-production method reliably reflects consumption and the asset was available throughout. No impairment or estimate change applies. Find annual amortisation.
explanation: Apply the supported consumption pattern: amortisation = 1,660,000 × 49,000/150,000 = 542,266.67. It is the share of expected lifetime production consumed, not an automatic straight-line charge.

title: Profit after suspended associate losses • case 38
prompt: An equity-method investment and relevant long-term interests were previously reduced to zero. Unrecognised share of prior losses totals LKR 156,000; the investor has no obligation and made no support payments. In the current year its share of associate profit is 234,000. No other adjustments or changes in interest apply. Find the share of profit that can now be RECOGNISED.
explanation: First absorb unrecognised prior losses before resuming recognised profit. Recognised amount = current profit share 234,000 − prior unrecognised losses 156,000 = 78,000.00.

title: Return recovery asset net of costs • case 39
prompt: A retailer has transferred 1,975 products. It expects 79 to be returned. Each returned product originally cost LKR 600; expected recovery handling is 20 per item and expected value deterioration is 30 per item. Estimates meet the relevant requirements. Find the separate asset for the right to recover returned products, excluding the refund liability.
explanation: Recovery asset = original carrying amount of expected returns less recovery costs and potential value decrease: 79 × (600 − 20 − 30) = 43,450.00. It is assessed separately from the customer refund liability.
family: Return recovery asset net of costs

title: Retrospective volume rebate true-up • case 39
prompt: A customer’s annual purchases reach 13,900 units at list price LKR 200. Crossing the threshold entitles it to a 5% retrospective rebate on ALL units. Cumulative revenue before this new supported estimate equals full list price; no rebate was previously accrued. The constraint permits the estimate. Find the reduction in cumulative revenue required now.
explanation: The revised transaction price reflects the retrospective rebate on all units. Revenue reduction = 13,900 × 200 × 5% = 139,000.00. Recognise the corresponding refund obligation as appropriate.

title: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation • case 39
prompt: A bundle has distinct goods A and B with stand-alone prices LKR 395,000 and 690,000. Total transaction price is 996,000. ALL paragraph 82 criteria demonstrate that the whole 89,000 discount relates only to A. A transfers now; B is not yet delivered. Find revenue recognised for A.
explanation: The specified discount-allocation exception applies. Allocate all 89,000 discount to A: 395,000 − 89,000 = 306,000.00. Do not default to relative allocation when the exception’s criteria are met.
family: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation

title: Three obligations and partial service • case 39
prompt: A contract price of LKR 2,370,000 covers goods A, goods B and twelve months of distinct support. Stand-alone prices are 600,000, 300,000 and 300,000 respectively. A is delivered, B is not, and six months of evenly provided support are complete. No allocation exception applies. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise allocation to A plus half of support: 2,370,000 × (600,000 + 150,000) / 1,200,000 = 1,481,250.00. B’s allocation remains unrecognised as revenue.

title: Progress excluding abnormal waste • case 39
prompt: An over-time contract has transaction price LKR 13,900,000. Costs incurred are 5,560,000, including abnormal waste of 278,000 that does not depict progress. Expected TOTAL productive costs excluding that waste are 11,120,000. Cost-to-cost is appropriate after excluding the waste; no other adjustment applies. Find cumulative revenue, not profit.
explanation: Exclude abnormal waste from the progress numerator. Productive progress = (5,560,000 − 278,000) / 11,120,000. Revenue = transaction price × that progress = 6,602,500.00. The wasted cost is not a revenue-producing input.

title: Uninstalled materials without margin • case 39
prompt: A single over-time construction obligation has price LKR 17,800,000. All B19(b) conditions justify recognising revenue equal to cost for significant uninstalled materials of 3,560,000 already controlled by the customer. Other productive costs incurred are 2,670,000; expected total OTHER costs are 10,680,000. No revenue was previously recognised. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise material revenue without margin: 3,560,000. Recognise the remaining price using other-cost progress: (17,800,000 − 3,560,000) × 2,670,000/10,680,000. Total revenue = 7,120,000.00.

title: Agent commission after collection • case 39
prompt: An intermediary is an AGENT and collects customer cash of LKR 2,950,000 for a completed supplier service. It must remit 88% to the supplier and is entitled to the remaining 12% commission. It controls neither the underlying service nor any distinct extra service, and there is no tax. Find its revenue.
explanation: An agent recognises its fee or commission, not the supplier’s gross billings: 2,950,000 × 12% = 354,000.00. The amount due to the supplier is separately accounted for.

title: Distinct remaining goods blended prospectively • case 39
prompt: At modification, 100 distinct goods remain under an existing contract at LKR 1,390 each. Another 50 distinct goods are added at 1,112 each. The modification is NOT a separate contract, but remaining goods are distinct from those already transferred, so paragraph 21(a) applies prospectively. Thirty of the remaining goods are then transferred. Find revenue for those thirty.
explanation: Prospective remaining consideration = 100 × 1,390 + 50 × 1,112. Divide by 150 remaining goods, then multiply by 30 = 38,920.00. Do not retrospectively revise revenue on goods already transferred.

title: FVTPL acquisition expense • case 39
prompt: A financial asset is acquired at fair value LKR 1,580,000 and is classified at FVTPL. Directly attributable broker costs are 39,500, paid separately. No fair-value change occurs immediately after purchase. Find the immediate profit-or-loss expense from acquiring this asset.
explanation: Transaction costs on an FVTPL asset are expensed. Initial asset carrying amount is fair value 1,580,000; immediate acquisition expense is 39,500.00.

title: Collateral cash-shortfall discounting • case 39
prompt: A credit loss scenario has a contractual receipt of LKR 1,975,000 due in one year. The ONLY expected recovery at that same date is collateral sale proceeds of 1,285,000, less sale costs of 89,000. Scenario probability is 100% and original EIR is 10%. Collateral is an integral contractual credit enhancement and not separately recognised. Find discounted ECL.
explanation: One-year shortfall = contractual receipt − net collateral recovery = 1,975,000 − (1,285,000 − 89,000). Discount that shortfall at 10%: 708,181.82. Do not ignore recovery costs or discount only one side of same-date cash flows.

title: Three-band provision matrix • case 39
prompt: Under the simplified lifetime-ECL approach, supported adjusted loss rates are 1% on current receivables of LKR 1,780,000, 5% on past-due balances of 495,000, and 30% on severely overdue balances of 178,000. Rates already include all required forward-looking and discounting effects. Find total loss allowance.
explanation: Apply each appropriate band rate and add: 1,780,000×1% + 495,000×5% + 178,000×30% = 95,950.00. Do not apply one blended band mechanically to all balances.

title: Equity FVOCI profit-or-loss dividend • case 39
prompt: An eligible equity investment has the irrevocable FVOCI election. During the year it gains LKR 198,000 in fair value and earns a dividend of 99,000. Dividend recognition criteria are met and the dividend clearly represents a return on investment, not recovery of cost. There are no other effects. Find income recognised in PROFIT OR LOSS.
explanation: The qualifying dividend of 99,000.00 is profit-or-loss income. The fair-value movement of 198,000 is OCI under this election and is not added to the profit-or-loss amount.

title: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset • case 39
prompt: A loan is sold with full derecognition. Immediately before sale, gross carrying amount is LKR 1,780,000, loss allowance 178,000, and cash proceeds 1,691,000. No accumulated OCI, sale fees or other adjustments exist. Find the derecognition GAIN relative to net carrying amount.
explanation: Net carrying amount = 1,780,000 − 178,000 = 1,602,000. Compare proceeds with that net amount: 1,691,000 − 1,602,000 = 89,000.00 gain. Derecognise both the gross asset and related allowance.
