prompt: Under the simplified lifetime-ECL approach, supported adjusted loss rates are 1% on current receivables of LKR 1,840,000, 5% on past-due balances of 510,000, and 30% on severely overdue balances of 184,000. Rates already include all required forward-looking and discounting effects. Find total loss allowance.
explanation: Apply each appropriate band rate and add: 1,840,000×1% + 510,000×5% + 184,000×30% = 99,100.00. Do not apply one blended band mechanically to all balances.

title: Equity FVOCI profit-or-loss dividend • case 42
prompt: An eligible equity investment has the irrevocable FVOCI election. During the year it gains LKR 204,000 in fair value and earns a dividend of 102,000. Dividend recognition criteria are met and the dividend clearly represents a return on investment, not recovery of cost. There are no other effects. Find income recognised in PROFIT OR LOSS.
explanation: The qualifying dividend of 102,000.00 is profit-or-loss income. The fair-value movement of 204,000 is OCI under this election and is not added to the profit-or-loss amount.

title: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset • case 42
prompt: A loan is sold with full derecognition. Immediately before sale, gross carrying amount is LKR 1,840,000, loss allowance 184,000, and cash proceeds 1,748,000. No accumulated OCI, sale fees or other adjustments exist. Find the derecognition GAIN relative to net carrying amount.
explanation: Net carrying amount = 1,840,000 − 184,000 = 1,656,000. Compare proceeds with that net amount: 1,748,000 − 1,656,000 = 92,000.00 gain. Derecognise both the gross asset and related allowance.
family: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset

title: Non-substantial liability modification gain • case 42
prompt: An amortised-cost liability is modified WITHOUT extinguishment, with no fees. Its carrying amount is LKR 1,420,000. The sole revised payment is 1,633,000 in two years. Original EIR is 10%; the modification is assessed as non-substantial. Find the immediate modification GAIN from recalculating amortised cost at the original EIR.
explanation: Revised amortised cost = 1,633,000/1.10² = 1,349,586.78. Gain = old liability 1,420,000 − revised PV = 70,413.22. The original EIR is retained for this non-extinguishing modification.

title: Credit-risk improvement allowance release • case 42
prompt: A debt asset under the GENERAL ECL model previously had significant credit-risk deterioration and lifetime allowance LKR 184,000. At reporting date the criteria for lifetime ECL are no longer met; required 12-month ECL is 31,000. No write-offs, new assets or other allowance movements occur. Find the impairment reversal in profit or loss.
explanation: When lifetime measurement is no longer required, the general model returns to 12-month ECL. Release the excess allowance: 184,000 − 31,000 = 153,000.00. This is not a receivable under mandatory simplified lifetime ECL.

title: Upstream inventory elimination with tax • case 42
prompt: P and S report profits AFTER their own tax of LKR 3,680,000 and 1,640,000. An upstream inventory sale leaves unrealised profit of 368,000 in group closing inventory. A recoverable DTA is recognised on the full elimination at 30%, with the tax effect in profit or loss. No other consolidation adjustments exist. Find TOTAL consolidated profit, before attribution to owners and NCI.
explanation: Combine separate after-tax profits, eliminate unrealised profit and recognise the recoverable tax benefit: 3,680,000 + 1,640,000 − 368,000 + 110,400.00 = 5,062,400.00. This question asks total group profit, not its attribution.

title: Full-goodwill impairment and owner profit • case 42
prompt: P owns 80% of S all year. Separate after-tax profits are P LKR 3,060,000 and S 1,120,000. Goodwill is recognised on the FULL-goodwill basis and an impairment of 410,000 is attributable to S’s CGU and allocated 80:20 between owners and NCI. No other adjustments or tax effects apply. Find consolidated profit attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Owners receive 80% of S’s profit and bear 80% of the full-goodwill loss: 3,060,000 + 80% × (1,120,000 − 410,000) = 3,628,000.00. Do not charge the owners with 100% of this full-goodwill loss.

title: Partial goodwill CGU gross-up • case 42
prompt: P owns 80% of S. Recognised PARTIAL goodwill is LKR 1,472,000; S’s other net assets in the tested CGU carry at 7,360,000. Recoverable amount of the WHOLE CGU is 8,280,000. Gross up goodwill for unrecognised NCI goodwill when testing; the whole impairment falls within grossed-up goodwill. No tax or other adjustments apply. Find impairment actually recognised on group goodwill.
explanation: Grossed-up goodwill = 1,472,000/80% = 1,840,000.00. Whole-CGU impairment = grossed goodwill + other net assets − recoverable amount = 920,000.00. Only the parent’s 80% goodwill portion is recognised, so recorded loss = 736,000.00.
reference: LKAS 36 Appendix C paras C4–C8; SLFRS 10 para B86

title: Consolidated retained earnings bridge • case 42
prompt: P owns 75% of S. At year end P retained earnings are LKR 5,100,000, and S retained earnings 3,260,000. S retained earnings at acquisition were 1,000,000. Cumulative post-acquisition extra FV depreciation is 184,000. A downstream sale by P leaves unrealised profit of 122,000. No tax, goodwill impairment, dividends recognised by P, OCI or other adjustments apply. Find consolidated retained earnings attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Group owners’ retained earnings = parent RE + 75% of adjusted post-acquisition S reserves − the parent’s downstream unrealised profit: 6,535,000.00. Pre-acquisition reserves do not enter post-acquisition group retained earnings.

title: Loss of control and translation reserve • case 42
prompt: P loses control of a foreign subsidiary. Proceeds are LKR 3,880,000; retained interest FV 920,000; NCI carrying amount 510,000; consolidated net assets INCLUDING goodwill 3,860,000. A cumulative translation GAIN of 184,000, entirely attributable to P, must be reclassified to profit or loss on loss of control. No other effects apply. Find total disposal gain including that reclassification.
explanation: Base gain = proceeds + retained FV + NCI − net assets = 1,450,000.00. Add the parent’s translation gain recycled on disposal: 184,000. Total = 1,634,000.00.
family: Loss of control and translation reserve

title: Residual guarantee expected payment • case 42
prompt: A lessee owes three year-end rentals of LKR 410,000. It guarantees residual value up to 200,000, but the amount EXPECTED to be payable under that guarantee is 72,000 at year three. Discount rate is 10%. No other liability payments exist. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the amount expected to be payable, not automatically the maximum guarantee. Liability = PV of three rentals + 72,000/1.10³ = 1,073,703.98.

title: Reasonably certain purchase option PV • case 42
prompt: A lease requires three year-end rentals of LKR 360,000, plus a purchase option price of 920,000 payable at year three. Exercise is reasonably certain. Discount rate is 10%. No incentives, other payments or initial prepayments apply. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the reasonably certain purchase price in the liability: PV of rentals + purchase price discounted for three years = 1,586,476.33. Do not omit or leave the future option payment undiscounted.

title: Lease and service component allocation • case 42
prompt: A two-year contract requires bundled payments of LKR 460,000 at each year end. Relative stand-alone prices are equipment lease 200,000 and distinct maintenance 50,000 per year. The lessee does NOT elect to combine components. Lease discount rate is 10%; no other payments exist. Find initial lease liability for the LEASE component only.
explanation: Allocate 200,000/250,000 = 80% of each bundled payment to the lease: 368,000.00. Discount those two lease payments, excluding maintenance, to obtain 638,677.69.

prompt: A twelve-month lease with no purchase option qualifies for the elected short-term exemption. The first three months are rent free, then nine monthly payments of LKR 41,000 are due. The asset is available throughout and straight-line expense is appropriate. Find lease expense for the FIRST six months, ignoring accrual settlement timing.
explanation: Total fixed payments are nine rents. Spread evenly over all twelve months: 41,000 × 9/12 × 6 = 184,500.00. Rent-free months still receive an expense allocation.

prompt: A transfer qualifies as a sale under SLFRS 15 at fair value LKR 18,400,000; asset carrying amount is 10,200,000. Market-rate leaseback payments have PV 7,360,000. There are no off-market adjustments or variable-payment complications. At inception, what sale gain is recognised for rights TRANSFERRED to the buyer-lessor?
explanation: Total gain = 18,400,000 − 10,200,000 = 8,200,000. Retained-use proportion = lease PV / fair value = 40%. Recognise only the transferred-rights proportion of the gain: 4,920,000.00.

title: Reassessed bargain purchase gain • case 42
prompt: After the required reassessment, final acquisition-date consideration is LKR 3,680,000, NCI fair value is 400,000 and identifiable net assets are 5,520,000. There is no prior holding or other adjustment. Find the bargain purchase gain recognised in profit or loss.
explanation: Net identifiable assets exceed consideration plus NCI: 5,520,000 − 3,680,000 − 400,000 = 1,440,000.00. Reassessment has been completed before recognising the gain.

title: Acquired contingent liability in goodwill • case 42
prompt: Consideration is LKR 5,600,000; NCI FV is 500,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired contingent liability are 4,260,000. The acquired item is a present obligation with reliably measurable FV 410,000 and qualifies for recognition despite non-probable outflow. No tax or other adjustment applies. Find goodwill after recognising it.
explanation: Recognise the qualifying acquired liability: net identifiable assets become 4,260,000 − 410,000. Goodwill = consideration + NCI − adjusted net assets = 2,250,000.00.

title: Separate acquired brand from goodwill • case 42
prompt: Consideration is LKR 5,100,000; NCI FV 600,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired separable brand are 4,280,000. Brand FV is 820,000; tax base is zero and 30% DTL must be recognised. No other adjustments apply. Find goodwill after separate brand and tax recognition.
explanation: An identifiable acquired brand is separate from goodwill. Net addition to identifiable assets = brand FV − 30% DTL = 574,000.00. Goodwill = 5,100,000 + 600,000 − (4,280,000 + 574,000.00) = 846,000.00.

prompt: A business acquisition has consideration LKR 3,260,000. Additional costs are acquisition advisory 184,000, qualifying equity-issue costs 70,000 and qualifying debt-issue costs 40,000. The issue costs follow their relevant standards, and no immediate debt-cost amortisation or other expense arises this period. Find the immediate acquisition-related PROFIT-OR-LOSS expense from these costs.
explanation: Expense advisory acquisition costs of 184,000.00. Qualifying equity and debt issuance costs follow their respective standards and are not added to this immediate acquisition-service expense or goodwill.

prompt: A taxable temporary difference opens at LKR 200,000 with a DTL measured at 25%. At year end the difference is 510,000 and the enacted rate expected on reversal is 30%. family: Temporary difference and enacted rate change

title: Revalued non-depreciable land tax basis • case 42
prompt: Non-depreciable land is revalued from cost LKR 1,840,000 to fair value 2,760,000; tax base remains cost. The enacted rate for recovery through SALE is 20%, while a 30% use rate would otherwise apply. The revaluation and associated tax go to OCI. No other effects exist. Find the net OCI revaluation increase after deferred tax.
explanation: For this non-depreciable revalued asset, measure tax consequences on recovery through sale: DTL = (2,760,000 − 1,840,000)×20%. Net OCI increase = gross uplift less that DTL = 736,000.00.

title: Current tax reconciliation and prepayment • case 42
prompt: Accounting pretax profit is LKR 4,100,000. It includes a permanently non-deductible fine of 184,000, exempt income of 50,000, and warranty expense of 410,000 deductible only on payment. Current-year warranty payments of 80,000 are deductible and were charged against the provision, not current profit. Tax rate is 30%; tax prepayments are 300,000. No other tax adjustments exist. Find closing CURRENT tax payable, not total tax expense.
explanation: Taxable profit = 4,100,000 + fine 184,000 − exempt income 50,000 + provision expense 410,000 − deductible payments 80,000 = 4,564,000. Current tax less prepaid 300,000 = 1,069,200.00. Deferred tax is separate.

title: Consolidated inventory tax difference • case 42
prompt: After eliminating an intragroup profit, inventory carries in consolidated statements at LKR 1,104,000. Its tax base in the buyer’s tax jurisdiction is 1,656,000. The buyer’s enacted rate is 30%; sufficient taxable profit is probable. No offsetting, exception or other tax effects apply. Find the consolidated DTA on this inventory.
explanation: The consolidated carrying amount is below tax base, creating a deductible temporary difference of 552,000. Use the buyer’s relevant tax rate: difference ×30% = 165,600.00.

title: Depreciation after recognised impairment • case 42
prompt: Immediately before an impairment, equipment carries at LKR 1,840,000. Recoverable amount is 1,120,000 and impairment is recognised. After that date it has four years’ remaining useful life and residual value 100,000. Straight-line depreciation is appropriate; no further revaluation or impairment applies. Find depreciation for the next FULL year.
explanation: First reduce the asset to recoverable amount 1,120,000. Thereafter allocate revised depreciable amount over remaining life: (1,120,000 − 100,000)/4 = 255,000.00.

title: Allocated headquarters in CGU impairment • case 42
prompt: CGU A carries operating assets of LKR 1,020,000; CGU B carries 400,000. A headquarters asset of 200,000 can be allocated reasonably and consistently in proportion to those operating-asset amounts. A’s recoverable amount INCLUDING its headquarters share is 860,000. No goodwill or other assets exist. Find the impairment loss for A including its allocation.
explanation: Allocate headquarters to A: 200,000 × 1,020,000/(1,020,000+400,000) = 143,661.97. Tested A carrying amount is 1,163,661.97. Impairment versus recoverable amount 860,000 = 303,661.97.

title: Break-even value-in-use cash flow • case 42
prompt: An asset carries at LKR 1,840,000. Its fair value less costs of disposal is lower. A valid VIU model uses THREE equal year-end operating cash inflows, plus 100,000 net disposal proceeds at year three, discounted at 10%. What minimum equal ANNUAL operating cash inflow makes VIU exactly equal carrying amount? Ignore tax and other adjustments.
explanation: Let annual flow be X. X×(1/1.10 + 1/1.10² + 1/1.10³) + 100,000/1.10³ = 1,840,000. Solve for X = 709,679.76. This sensitivity calculation identifies the VIU break-even point.

title: Discounted warranty expected-value portfolio • case 42
prompt: A present warranty obligation covers 1,840 products. Per product, probabilities are 70% no defect, 25% a minor repair costing LKR 400, and 5% a major repair costing 2,000. All expected payments occur exactly in TWO years. Outflow for the portfolio is probable; appropriate discount rate is 10% with no risk double counting. Find the provision.
explanation: Expected cash payment = 1,840×(25%×400 + 5%×2,000) = 368,000.0. Discount two years at 10%: 368,000.0/1.10² = 304,132.23. The probability assessment applies to the portfolio.

title: Provision movement with revised estimate • case 42
prompt: A discounted provision opens at LKR 920,000. Unwinding for a full year is at 8%. A 100,000 settlement occurs at the year END, after unwinding. At that same reporting date, a new estimate increases the remaining provision by 134,000. No other changes occur. Find closing provision.
explanation: Closing = opening + 8% unwinding − year-end settlement + estimate increase: 920,000×1.08 −100,000 +134,000 = 1,027,600.00. Classification of the estimate change’s counterpart is assessed separately.

title: Revaluation increase after earlier loss • case 42
prompt: PPE carries at LKR 1,020,000 before revaluation and is revalued to 1,840,000. A prior revaluation decrease on THIS asset of 234,000 was recognised in profit or loss and has not been reversed. No tax effects apply. Find the current increase recognised in OCI after reversing the eligible prior loss in profit or loss.
explanation: Gross increase = 1,840,000 − 1,020,000 = 820,000. First recognise 234,000 in profit or loss to reverse the prior decrease. Remaining 586,000.00 is OCI revaluation surplus.

title: Nine-month depreciation and disposal gain • case 42
prompt: Equipment cost LKR 2,040,000, residual value 200,000 and useful life five years, straight-line. Two FULL years’ depreciation were recognised before this year. It is sold after nine months of the current year for 1,480,000. It was not previously held for sale and no impairment or revaluation applies. Find disposal GAIN after the required nine-month depreciation.
explanation: Annual depreciation = (2,040,000−200,000)/5. Deduct two full years and another 9/12 year from cost to obtain disposal-date carrying amount 1,028,000.00. Gain = proceeds − that amount = 452,000.00.

title: Customer collections with a write-off • case 42
prompt: All sales are on credit. Revenue is LKR 5,100,000; opening GROSS trade receivables are 600,000; closing GROSS receivables are 1,220,000. Receivables of 142,000 were written off during the year. There are no taxes, returns, contract balances, acquisitions or exchange changes. Find cash collected from customers.
explanation: Gross receivable roll-forward: opening + credit sales − cash receipts − write-offs = closing. Thus receipts = 5,100,000+600,000−1,220,000−142,000 = 4,338,000.00. Write-offs are not cash receipts.

title: Loan funding net cash effect • case 42
prompt: A company receives cash loan proceeds of LKR 1,840,000 and immediately pays a directly attributable lender issue fee of 41,000. Both payments are classified as financing cash flows in this case. No other cash movement occurs. Find the NET financing cash inflow from these two cash movements; this question does not require net line-item presentation.
explanation: Net financing cash effect = proceeds − cash fee = 1,840,000 − 41,000.00 = 1,799,000.00. Effective-interest amortisation later is not another inception cash payment.

title: Item-by-item NRV without offsetting headroom • case 42
prompt: Two unrelated inventory lines require separate NRV tests. A has 310 units, cost LKR 1,000 and NRV 900 each. B has 184 units, cost 1,000 and NRV 1,200 each. There is no basis to group them for the write-down test. Find TOTAL closing inventory carrying amount.
explanation: Carry A at 900 per unit and B at its lower cost of 1,000. Total = 310×900 + 184×1,000 = 463,000.00. B’s NRV headroom cannot offset A’s write-down.

title: Units-of-production intangible amortisation • case 42
prompt: A finite-life production licence costs LKR 1,740,000, has zero residual value, and is expected to support 150,000 units in total. Actual output this year is 51,000 units. A units-of-production method reliably reflects consumption and the asset was available throughout. No impairment or estimate change applies. Find annual amortisation.
explanation: Apply the supported consumption pattern: amortisation = 1,740,000 × 51,000/150,000 = 591,600.00. It is the share of expected lifetime production consumed, not an automatic straight-line charge.

title: Profit after suspended associate losses • case 42
prompt: An equity-method investment and relevant long-term interests were previously reduced to zero. Unrecognised share of prior losses totals LKR 164,000; the investor has no obligation and made no support payments. In the current year its share of associate profit is 246,000. No other adjustments or changes in interest apply. Find the share of profit that can now be RECOGNISED.
explanation: First absorb unrecognised prior losses before resuming recognised profit. Recognised amount = current profit share 246,000 − prior unrecognised losses 164,000 = 82,000.00.

title: Return recovery asset net of costs • case 43
prompt: A retailer has transferred 2,075 products. It expects 83 to be returned. Each returned product originally cost LKR 600; expected recovery handling is 20 per item and expected value deterioration is 30 per item. Estimates meet the relevant requirements. Find the separate asset for the right to recover returned products, excluding the refund liability.
explanation: Recovery asset = original carrying amount of expected returns less recovery costs and potential value decrease: 83 × (600 − 20 − 30) = 45,650.00. It is assessed separately from the customer refund liability.
family: Return recovery asset net of costs

title: Retrospective volume rebate true-up • case 43
prompt: A customer’s annual purchases reach 14,300 units at list price LKR 200. Crossing the threshold entitles it to a 5% retrospective rebate on ALL units. Cumulative revenue before this new supported estimate equals full list price; no rebate was previously accrued. The constraint permits the estimate. Find the reduction in cumulative revenue required now.
explanation: The revised transaction price reflects the retrospective rebate on all units. Revenue reduction = 14,300 × 200 × 5% = 143,000.00. Recognise the corresponding refund obligation as appropriate.

title: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation • case 43
prompt: A bundle has distinct goods A and B with stand-alone prices LKR 415,000 and 730,000. Total transaction price is 1,052,000. ALL paragraph 82 criteria demonstrate that the whole 93,000 discount relates only to A. A transfers now; B is not yet delivered. Find revenue recognised for A.
explanation: The specified discount-allocation exception applies. Allocate all 93,000 discount to A: 415,000 − 93,000 = 322,000.00. Do not default to relative allocation when the exception’s criteria are met.
family: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation

title: Three obligations and partial service • case 43
prompt: A contract price of LKR 2,490,000 covers goods A, goods B and twelve months of distinct support. Stand-alone prices are 600,000, 300,000 and 300,000 respectively. A is delivered, B is not, and six months of evenly provided support are complete. No allocation exception applies. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise allocation to A plus half of support: 2,490,000 × (600,000 + 150,000) / 1,200,000 = 1,556,250.00. B’s allocation remains unrecognised as revenue.

title: Progress excluding abnormal waste • case 43
prompt: An over-time contract has transaction price LKR 14,300,000. Costs incurred are 5,720,000, including abnormal waste of 286,000 that does not depict progress. Expected TOTAL productive costs excluding that waste are 11,440,000. Cost-to-cost is appropriate after excluding the waste; no other adjustment applies. Find cumulative revenue, not profit.
explanation: Exclude abnormal waste from the progress numerator. Productive progress = (5,720,000 − 286,000) / 11,440,000. Revenue = transaction price × that progress = 6,792,500.00. The wasted cost is not a revenue-producing input.

title: Uninstalled materials without margin • case 43
prompt: A single over-time construction obligation has price LKR 18,600,000. All B19(b) conditions justify recognising revenue equal to cost for significant uninstalled materials of 3,720,000 already controlled by the customer. Other productive costs incurred are 2,790,000; expected total OTHER costs are 11,160,000. No revenue was previously recognised. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise material revenue without margin: 3,720,000. Recognise the remaining price using other-cost progress: (18,600,000 − 3,720,000) × 2,790,000/11,160,000. Total revenue = 7,440,000.00.

title: Agent commission after collection • case 43
prompt: An intermediary is an AGENT and collects customer cash of LKR 3,150,000 for a completed supplier service. It must remit 88% to the supplier and is entitled to the remaining 12% commission. It controls neither the underlying service nor any distinct extra service, and there is no tax. Find its revenue.
explanation: An agent recognises its fee or commission, not the supplier’s gross billings: 3,150,000 × 12% = 378,000.00. The amount due to the supplier is separately accounted for.

title: Distinct remaining goods blended prospectively • case 43
prompt: At modification, 100 distinct goods remain under an existing contract at LKR 1,430 each. Another 50 distinct goods are added at 1,144 each. The modification is NOT a separate contract, but remaining goods are distinct from those already transferred, so paragraph 21(a) applies prospectively. Thirty of the remaining goods are then transferred. Find revenue for those thirty.
explanation: Prospective remaining consideration = 100 × 1,430 + 50 × 1,144. Divide by 150 remaining goods, then multiply by 30 = 40,040.00. Do not retrospectively revise revenue on goods already transferred.

title: FVTPL acquisition expense • case 43
prompt: A financial asset is acquired at fair value LKR 1,660,000 and is classified at FVTPL. Directly attributable broker costs are 41,500, paid separately. No fair-value change occurs immediately after purchase. Find the immediate profit-or-loss expense from acquiring this asset.
explanation: Transaction costs on an FVTPL asset are expensed. Initial asset carrying amount is fair value 1,660,000; immediate acquisition expense is 41,500.00.

title: Collateral cash-shortfall discounting • case 43
prompt: A credit loss scenario has a contractual receipt of LKR 2,075,000 due in one year. The ONLY expected recovery at that same date is collateral sale proceeds of 1,345,000, less sale costs of 93,000. Scenario probability is 100% and original EIR is 10%. Collateral is an integral contractual credit enhancement and not separately recognised. Find discounted ECL.
explanation: One-year shortfall = contractual receipt − net collateral recovery = 2,075,000 − (1,345,000 − 93,000). Discount that shortfall at 10%: 748,181.82. Do not ignore recovery costs or discount only one side of same-date cash flows.

title: Three-band provision matrix • case 43
prompt: Under the simplified lifetime-ECL approach, supported adjusted loss rates are 1% on current receivables of LKR 1,860,000, 5% on past-due balances of 515,000, and 30% on severely overdue balances of 186,000. Rates already include all required forward-looking and discounting effects. Find total loss allowance.
explanation: Apply each appropriate band rate and add: 1,860,000×1% + 515,000×5% + 186,000×30% = 100,150.00. Do not apply one blended band mechanically to all balances.

title: Equity FVOCI profit-or-loss dividend • case 43
prompt: An eligible equity investment has the irrevocable FVOCI election. During the year it gains LKR 206,000 in fair value and earns a dividend of 103,000. Dividend recognition criteria are met and the dividend clearly represents a return on investment, not recovery of cost. There are no other effects. Find income recognised in PROFIT OR LOSS.
explanation: The qualifying dividend of 103,000.00 is profit-or-loss income. The fair-value movement of 206,000 is OCI under this election and is not added to the profit-or-loss amount.

title: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset • case 43
prompt: A loan is sold with full derecognition. Immediately before sale, gross carrying amount is LKR 1,860,000, loss allowance 186,000, and cash proceeds 1,767,000. No accumulated OCI, sale fees or other adjustments exist. Find the derecognition GAIN relative to net carrying amount.
explanation: Net carrying amount = 1,860,000 − 186,000 = 1,674,000. Compare proceeds with that net amount: 1,767,000 − 1,674,000 = 93,000.00 gain. Derecognise both the gross asset and related allowance.
family: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset

title: Non-substantial liability modification gain • case 43
prompt: An amortised-cost liability is modified WITHOUT extinguishment, with no fees. Its carrying amount is LKR 1,430,000. The sole revised payment is 1,644,500 in two years. Original EIR is 10%; the modification is assessed as non-substantial. Find the immediate modification GAIN from recalculating amortised cost at the original EIR.
explanation: Revised amortised cost = 1,644,500/1.10² = 1,359,090.91. Gain = old liability 1,430,000 − revised PV = 70,909.09. The original EIR is retained for this non-extinguishing modification.

title: Credit-risk improvement allowance release • case 43
prompt: A debt asset under the GENERAL ECL model previously had significant credit-risk deterioration and lifetime allowance LKR 186,000. At reporting date the criteria for lifetime ECL are no longer met; required 12-month ECL is 31,500. No write-offs, new assets or other allowance movements occur. Find the impairment reversal in profit or loss.
explanation: When lifetime measurement is no longer required, the general model returns to 12-month ECL. Release the excess allowance: 186,000 − 31,500 = 154,500.00. This is not a receivable under mandatory simplified lifetime ECL.

title: Upstream inventory elimination with tax • case 43
prompt: P and S report profits AFTER their own tax of LKR 3,720,000 and 1,660,000. An upstream inventory sale leaves unrealised profit of 372,000 in group closing inventory. A recoverable DTA is recognised on the full elimination at 30%, with the tax effect in profit or loss. No other consolidation adjustments exist. Find TOTAL consolidated profit, before attribution to owners and NCI.
explanation: Combine separate after-tax profits, eliminate unrealised profit and recognise the recoverable tax benefit: 3,720,000 + 1,660,000 − 372,000 + 111,600.00 = 5,119,600.00. This question asks total group profit, not its attribution.

title: Full-goodwill impairment and owner profit • case 43
prompt: P owns 80% of S all year. Separate after-tax profits are P LKR 3,090,000 and S 1,130,000. Goodwill is recognised on the FULL-goodwill basis and an impairment of 415,000 is attributable to S’s CGU and allocated 80:20 between owners and NCI. No other adjustments or tax effects apply. Find consolidated profit attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Owners receive 80% of S’s profit and bear 80% of the full-goodwill loss: 3,090,000 + 80% × (1,130,000 − 415,000) = 3,662,000.00. Do not charge the owners with 100% of this full-goodwill loss.

title: Partial goodwill CGU gross-up • case 43
prompt: P owns 80% of S. Recognised PARTIAL goodwill is LKR 1,488,000; S’s other net assets in the tested CGU carry at 7,440,000. Recoverable amount of the WHOLE CGU is 8,370,000. Gross up goodwill for unrecognised NCI goodwill when testing; the whole impairment falls within grossed-up goodwill. No tax or other adjustments apply. Find impairment actually recognised on group goodwill.
explanation: Grossed-up goodwill = 1,488,000/80% = 1,860,000.00. Whole-CGU impairment = grossed goodwill + other net assets − recoverable amount = 930,000.00. Only the parent’s 80% goodwill portion is recognised, so recorded loss = 744,000.00.
reference: LKAS 36 Appendix C paras C4–C8; SLFRS 10 para B86

title: Consolidated retained earnings bridge • case 43
prompt: P owns 75% of S. At year end P retained earnings are LKR 5,150,000, and S retained earnings 3,290,000. S retained earnings at acquisition were 1,000,000. Cumulative post-acquisition extra FV depreciation is 186,000. A downstream sale by P leaves unrealised profit of 123,000. No tax, goodwill impairment, dividends recognised by P, OCI or other adjustments apply. Find consolidated retained earnings attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Group owners’ retained earnings = parent RE + 75% of adjusted post-acquisition S reserves − the parent’s downstream unrealised profit: 6,605,000.00. Pre-acquisition reserves do not enter post-acquisition group retained earnings.

title: Loss of control and translation reserve • case 43
prompt: P loses control of a foreign subsidiary. Proceeds are LKR 3,920,000; retained interest FV 930,000; NCI carrying amount 515,000; consolidated net assets INCLUDING goodwill 3,890,000. A cumulative translation GAIN of 186,000, entirely attributable to P, must be reclassified to profit or loss on loss of control. No other effects apply. Find total disposal gain including that reclassification.
explanation: Base gain = proceeds + retained FV + NCI − net assets = 1,475,000.00. Add the parent’s translation gain recycled on disposal: 186,000. Total = 1,661,000.00.
family: Loss of control and translation reserve

title: Residual guarantee expected payment • case 43
prompt: A lessee owes three year-end rentals of LKR 415,000. It guarantees residual value up to 200,000, but the amount EXPECTED to be payable under that guarantee is 73,000 at year three. Discount rate is 10%. No other liability payments exist. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the amount expected to be payable, not automatically the maximum guarantee. Liability = PV of three rentals + 73,000/1.10³ = 1,086,889.56.

title: Reasonably certain purchase option PV • case 43
prompt: A lease requires three year-end rentals of LKR 365,000, plus a purchase option price of 930,000 payable at year three. Exercise is reasonably certain. Discount rate is 10%. No incentives, other payments or initial prepayments apply. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the reasonably certain purchase price in the liability: PV of rentals + purchase price discounted for three years = 1,606,423.74. Do not omit or leave the future option payment undiscounted.

title: Lease and service component allocation • case 43
prompt: A two-year contract requires bundled payments of LKR 465,000 at each year end. Relative stand-alone prices are equipment lease 200,000 and distinct maintenance 50,000 per year. The lessee does NOT elect to combine components. Lease discount rate is 10%; no other payments exist. Find initial lease liability for the LEASE component only.
explanation: Allocate 200,000/250,000 = 80% of each bundled payment to the lease: 372,000.00. Discount those two lease payments, excluding maintenance, to obtain 645,619.83.

title: Exempt short-term lease rent-free start • case 43
prompt: A twelve-month lease with no purchase option qualifies for the elected short-term exemption. The first three months are rent free, then nine monthly payments of LKR 41,500 are due. The asset is available throughout and straight-line expense is appropriate. Find lease expense for the FIRST six months, ignoring accrual settlement timing.
explanation: Total fixed payments are nine rents. Spread evenly over all twelve months: 41,500 × 9/12 × 6 = 186,750.00. Rent-free months still receive an expense allocation.

title: Sale-and-leaseback rights transferred • case 43
prompt: A transfer qualifies as a sale under SLFRS 15 at fair value LKR 18,600,000; asset carrying amount is 10,300,000. Market-rate leaseback payments have PV 7,440,000. There are no off-market adjustments or variable-payment complications. At inception, what sale gain is recognised for rights TRANSFERRED to the buyer-lessor?
explanation: Total gain = 18,600,000 − 10,300,000 = 8,300,000. Retained-use proportion = lease PV / fair value = 40%. Recognise only the transferred-rights proportion of the gain: 4,980,000.00.

title: Reassessed bargain purchase gain • case 43
prompt: After the required reassessment, final acquisition-date consideration is LKR 3,720,000, NCI fair value is 400,000 and identifiable net assets are 5,580,000. There is no prior holding or other adjustment. Find the bargain purchase gain recognised in profit or loss.
explanation: Net identifiable assets exceed consideration plus NCI: 5,580,000 − 3,720,000 − 400,000 = 1,460,000.00. Reassessment has been completed before recognising the gain.

title: Acquired contingent liability in goodwill • case 43
prompt: Consideration is LKR 5,650,000; NCI FV is 500,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired contingent liability are 4,290,000. The acquired item is a present obligation with reliably measurable FV 415,000 and qualifies for recognition despite non-probable outflow. No tax or other adjustment applies. Find goodwill after recognising it.
explanation: Recognise the qualifying acquired liability: net identifiable assets become 4,290,000 − 415,000. Goodwill = consideration + NCI − adjusted net assets = 2,275,000.00.

title: Separate acquired brand from goodwill • case 43
prompt: Consideration is LKR 5,150,000; NCI FV 600,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired separable brand are 4,320,000. Brand FV is 830,000; tax base is zero and 30% DTL must be recognised. No other adjustments apply. Find goodwill after separate brand and tax recognition.
explanation: An identifiable acquired brand is separate from goodwill. Net addition to identifiable assets = brand FV − 30% DTL = 581,000.00. Goodwill = 5,150,000 + 600,000 − (4,320,000 + 581,000.00) = 849,000.00.

title: Acquisition costs versus issue costs • case 43
prompt: A business acquisition has consideration LKR 3,290,000. Additional costs are acquisition advisory 186,000, qualifying equity-issue costs 70,000 and qualifying debt-issue costs 40,000. The issue costs follow their relevant standards, and no immediate debt-cost amortisation or other expense arises this period. Find the immediate acquisition-related PROFIT-OR-LOSS expense from these costs.
explanation: Expense advisory acquisition costs of 186,000.00. Qualifying equity and debt issuance costs follow their respective standards and are not added to this immediate acquisition-service expense or goodwill.

title: Temporary difference and enacted rate change • case 43
prompt: A taxable temporary difference opens at LKR 200,000 with a DTL measured at 25%. At year end the difference is 515,000 and the enacted rate expected on reversal is 30%. Both the underlying movements and rate change belong in profit or loss. No other tax movements exist. Find deferred tax expense for the year.
explanation: Opening DTL = 200,000×25% = 50,000. Closing DTL = 515,000×30% = 154,500.00. Expense is the full increase, including rate remeasurement: 104,500.00. Rates are exercise assumptions.
family: Temporary difference and enacted rate change

title: Revalued non-depreciable land tax basis • case 43
prompt: Non-depreciable land is revalued from cost LKR 1,860,000 to fair value 2,790,000; tax base remains cost. The enacted rate for recovery through SALE is 20%, while a 30% use rate would otherwise apply. The revaluation and associated tax go to OCI. No other effects exist. Find the net OCI revaluation increase after deferred tax.
explanation: For this non-depreciable revalued asset, measure tax consequences on recovery through sale: DTL = (2,790,000 − 1,860,000)×20%. Net OCI increase = gross uplift less that DTL = 744,000.00.

title: Current tax reconciliation and prepayment • case 43
prompt: Accounting pretax profit is LKR 4,150,000. It includes a permanently non-deductible fine of 186,000, exempt income of 50,000, and warranty expense of 415,000 deductible only on payment. Current-year warranty payments of 80,000 are deductible and were charged against the provision, not current profit. Tax rate is 30%; tax prepayments are 300,000. No other tax adjustments exist. Find closing CURRENT tax payable, not total tax expense.
explanation: Taxable profit = 4,150,000 + fine 186,000 − exempt income 50,000 + provision expense 415,000 − deductible payments 80,000 = 4,621,000. Current tax less prepaid 300,000 = 1,086,300.00. Deferred tax is separate.

title: Consolidated inventory tax difference • case 43
prompt: After eliminating an intragroup profit, inventory carries in consolidated statements at LKR 1,116,000. Its tax base in the buyer’s tax jurisdiction is 1,674,000. The buyer’s enacted rate is 30%; sufficient taxable profit is probable. No offsetting, exception or other tax effects apply. Find the consolidated DTA on this inventory.
explanation: The consolidated carrying amount is below tax base, creating a deductible temporary difference of 558,000. Use the buyer’s relevant tax rate: difference ×30% = 167,400.00.

title: Depreciation after recognised impairment • case 43
prompt: Immediately before an impairment, equipment carries at LKR 1,860,000. Recoverable amount is 1,130,000 and impairment is recognised. After that date it has four years’ remaining useful life and residual value 100,000. Straight-line depreciation is appropriate; no further revaluation or impairment applies. Find depreciation for the next FULL year.
explanation: First reduce the asset to recoverable amount 1,130,000. Thereafter allocate revised depreciable amount over remaining life: (1,130,000 − 100,000)/4 = 257,500.00.

title: Allocated headquarters in CGU impairment • case 43
prompt: CGU A carries operating assets of LKR 1,030,000; CGU B carries 400,000. A headquarters asset of 200,000 can be allocated reasonably and consistently in proportion to those operating-asset amounts. A’s recoverable amount INCLUDING its headquarters share is 865,000. No goodwill or other assets exist. Find the impairment loss for A including its allocation.
explanation: Allocate headquarters to A: 200,000 × 1,030,000/(1,030,000+400,000) = 144,055.94. Tested A carrying amount is 1,174,055.94. Impairment versus recoverable amount 865,000 = 309,055.94.

title: Break-even value-in-use cash flow • case 43
prompt: An asset carries at LKR 1,860,000. Its fair value less costs of disposal is lower. A valid VIU model uses THREE equal year-end operating cash inflows, plus 100,000 net disposal proceeds at year three, discounted at 10%. What minimum equal ANNUAL operating cash inflow makes VIU exactly equal carrying amount? Ignore tax and other adjustments.
explanation: Let annual flow be X. X×(1/1.10 + 1/1.10² + 1/1.10³) + 100,000/1.10³ = 1,860,000. Solve for X = 717,722.05. This sensitivity calculation identifies the VIU break-even point.

title: Discounted warranty expected-value portfolio • case 43
prompt: A present warranty obligation covers 1,860 products. Per product, probabilities are 70% no defect, 25% a minor repair costing LKR 400, and 5% a major repair costing 2,000. All expected payments occur exactly in TWO years. Outflow for the portfolio is probable; appropriate discount rate is 10% with no risk double counting. Find the provision.
explanation: Expected cash payment = 1,860×(25%×400 + 5%×2,000) = 372,000.0. Discount two years at 10%: 372,000.0/1.10² = 307,438.02. The probability assessment applies to the portfolio.

title: Provision movement with revised estimate • case 43
prompt: A discounted provision opens at LKR 930,000. Unwinding for a full year is at 8%. A 100,000 settlement occurs at the year END, after unwinding. At that same reporting date, a new estimate increases the remaining provision by 136,000. No other changes occur. Find closing provision.
explanation: Closing = opening + 8% unwinding − year-end settlement + estimate increase: 930,000×1.08 −100,000 +136,000 = 1,040,400.00. Classification of the estimate change’s counterpart is assessed separately.

title: Revaluation increase after earlier loss • case 43
prompt: PPE carries at LKR 1,030,000 before revaluation and is revalued to 1,860,000. A prior revaluation decrease on THIS asset of 236,000 was recognised in profit or loss and has not been reversed. No tax effects apply. Find the current increase recognised in OCI after reversing the eligible prior loss in profit or loss.
explanation: Gross increase = 1,860,000 − 1,030,000 = 830,000. First recognise 236,000 in profit or loss to reverse the prior decrease. Remaining 594,000.00 is OCI revaluation surplus.

title: Nine-month depreciation and disposal gain • case 43
prompt: Equipment cost LKR 2,060,000, residual value 200,000 and useful life five years, straight-line. Two FULL years’ depreciation were recognised before this year. It is sold after nine months of the current year for 1,495,000. It was not previously held for sale and no impairment or revaluation applies. Find disposal GAIN after the required nine-month depreciation.
explanation: Annual depreciation = (2,060,000−200,000)/5. Deduct two full years and another 9/12 year from cost to obtain disposal-date carrying amount 1,037,000.00. Gain = proceeds − that amount = 458,000.00.

title: Customer collections with a write-off • case 43
prompt: All sales are on credit. Revenue is LKR 5,150,000; opening GROSS trade receivables are 600,000; closing GROSS receivables are 1,230,000. Receivables of 143,000 were written off during the year. There are no taxes, returns, contract balances, acquisitions or exchange changes. Find cash collected from customers.
explanation: Gross receivable roll-forward: opening + credit sales − cash receipts − write-offs = closing. Thus receipts = 5,150,000+600,000−1,230,000−143,000 = 4,377,000.00. Write-offs are not cash receipts.

title: Loan funding net cash effect • case 43
prompt: A company receives cash loan proceeds of LKR 1,860,000 and immediately pays a directly attributable lender issue fee of 41,500. Both payments are classified as financing cash flows in this case. No other cash movement occurs. Find the NET financing cash inflow from these two cash movements; this question does not require net line-item presentation.
explanation: Net financing cash effect = proceeds − cash fee = 1,860,000 − 41,500.00 = 1,818,500.00. Effective-interest amortisation later is not another inception cash payment.

title: Item-by-item NRV without offsetting headroom • case 43
prompt: Two unrelated inventory lines require separate NRV tests. A has 315 units, cost LKR 1,000 and NRV 900 each. B has 186 units, cost 1,000 and NRV 1,200 each. There is no basis to group them for the write-down test. Find TOTAL closing inventory carrying amount.
explanation: Carry A at 900 per unit and B at its lower cost of 1,000. Total = 315×900 + 186×1,000 = 469,500.00. B’s NRV headroom cannot offset A’s write-down.

title: Units-of-production intangible amortisation • case 43
prompt: A finite-life production licence costs LKR 1,760,000, has zero residual value, and is expected to support 150,000 units in total. Actual output this year is 51,500 units. A units-of-production method reliably reflects consumption and the asset was available throughout. No impairment or estimate change applies. Find annual amortisation.
explanation: Apply the supported consumption pattern: amortisation = 1,760,000 × 51,500/150,000 = 604,266.67. It is the share of expected lifetime production consumed, not an automatic straight-line charge.

title: Profit after suspended associate losses • case 43
prompt: An equity-method investment and relevant long-term interests were previously reduced to zero. Unrecognised share of prior losses totals LKR 166,000; the investor has no obligation and made no support payments. In the current year its share of associate profit is 249,000. No other adjustments or changes in interest apply. Find the share of profit that can now be RECOGNISED.
explanation: First absorb unrecognised prior losses before resuming recognised profit. Recognised amount = current profit share 249,000 − prior unrecognised losses 166,000 = 83,000.00.

title: Return recovery asset net of costs • case 44
prompt: A retailer has transferred 2,100 products. It expects 84 to be returned. Each returned product originally cost LKR 600; expected recovery handling is 20 per item and expected value deterioration is 30 per item. Estimates meet the relevant requirements. Find the separate asset for the right to recover returned products, excluding the refund liability.
explanation: Recovery asset = original carrying amount of expected returns less recovery costs and potential value decrease: 84 × (600 − 20 − 30) = 46,200.00. It is assessed separately from the customer refund liability.
family: Return recovery asset net of costs

title: Retrospective volume rebate true-up • case 44
prompt: A customer’s annual purchases reach 14,400 units at list price LKR 200. Crossing the threshold entitles it to a 5% retrospective rebate on ALL units. Cumulative revenue before this new supported estimate equals full list price; no rebate was previously accrued. The constraint permits the estimate. Find the reduction in cumulative revenue required now.
explanation: The revised transaction price reflects the retrospective rebate on all units. Revenue reduction = 14,400 × 200 × 5% = 144,000.00. Recognise the corresponding refund obligation as appropriate.

title: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation • case 44
prompt: A bundle has distinct goods A and B with stand-alone prices LKR 420,000 and 740,000. Total transaction price is 1,066,000. ALL paragraph 82 criteria demonstrate that the whole 94,000 discount relates only to A. A transfers now; B is not yet delivered. Find revenue recognised for A.
explanation: The specified discount-allocation exception applies. Allocate all 94,000 discount to A: 420,000 − 94,000 = 326,000.00. Do not default to relative allocation when the exception’s criteria are met.
family: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation

title: Three obligations and partial service • case 44
prompt: A contract price of LKR 2,520,000 covers goods A, goods B and twelve months of distinct support. Stand-alone prices are 600,000, 300,000 and 300,000 respectively. A is delivered, B is not, and six months of evenly provided support are complete. No allocation exception applies. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise allocation to A plus half of support: 2,520,000 × (600,000 + 150,000) / 1,200,000 = 1,575,000.00. B’s allocation remains unrecognised as revenue.

title: Progress excluding abnormal waste • case 44
prompt: An over-time contract has transaction price LKR 14,400,000. Costs incurred are 5,760,000, including abnormal waste of 288,000 that does not depict progress. Expected TOTAL productive costs excluding that waste are 11,520,000. Cost-to-cost is appropriate after excluding the waste; no other adjustment applies. Find cumulative revenue, not profit.
explanation: Exclude abnormal waste from the progress numerator. Productive progress = (5,760,000 − 288,000) / 11,520,000. Revenue = transaction price × that progress = 6,840,000.00. The wasted cost is not a revenue-producing input.

title: Uninstalled materials without margin • case 44
prompt: A single over-time construction obligation has price LKR 18,800,000. All B19(b) conditions justify recognising revenue equal to cost for significant uninstalled materials of 3,760,000 already controlled by the customer. Other productive costs incurred are 2,820,000; expected total OTHER costs are 11,280,000. No revenue was previously recognised. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise material revenue without margin: 3,760,000. Recognise the remaining price using other-cost progress: (18,800,000 − 3,760,000) × 2,820,000/11,280,000. Total revenue = 7,520,000.00.

title: Agent commission after collection • case 44
prompt: An intermediary is an AGENT and collects customer cash of LKR 3,200,000 for a completed supplier service. It must remit 88% to the supplier and is entitled to the remaining 12% commission. It controls neither the underlying service nor any distinct extra service, and there is no tax. Find its revenue.
explanation: An agent recognises its fee or commission, not the supplier’s gross billings: 3,200,000 × 12% = 384,000.00. The amount due to the supplier is separately accounted for.

title: Distinct remaining goods blended prospectively • case 44
prompt: At modification, 100 distinct goods remain under an existing contract at LKR 1,440 each. Another 50 distinct goods are added at 1,152 each. The modification is NOT a separate contract, but remaining goods are distinct from those already transferred, so paragraph 21(a) applies prospectively. Thirty of the remaining goods are then transferred. Find revenue for those thirty.
explanation: Prospective remaining consideration = 100 × 1,440 + 50 × 1,152. Divide by 150 remaining goods, then multiply by 30 = 40,320.00. Do not retrospectively revise revenue on goods already transferred.

title: FVTPL acquisition expense • case 44
prompt: A financial asset is acquired at fair value LKR 1,680,000 and is classified at FVTPL. Directly attributable broker costs are 42,000, paid separately. No fair-value change occurs immediately after purchase. Find the immediate profit-or-loss expense from acquiring this asset.
explanation: Transaction costs on an FVTPL asset are expensed. Initial asset carrying amount is fair value 1,680,000; immediate acquisition expense is 42,000.00.

title: Collateral cash-shortfall discounting • case 44
prompt: A credit loss scenario has a contractual receipt of LKR 2,100,000 due in one year. The ONLY expected recovery at that same date is collateral sale proceeds of 1,360,000, less sale costs of 94,000. Scenario probability is 100% and original EIR is 10%. Collateral is an integral contractual credit enhancement and not separately recognised. Find discounted ECL.
explanation: One-year shortfall = contractual receipt − net collateral recovery = 2,100,000 − (1,360,000 − 94,000). Discount that shortfall at 10%: 758,181.82. Do not ignore recovery costs or discount only one side of same-date cash flows.

title: Three-band provision matrix • case 44
prompt: Under the simplified lifetime-ECL approach, supported adjusted loss rates are 1% on current receivables of LKR 1,880,000, 5% on past-due balances of 520,000, and 30% on severely overdue balances of 188,000. Rates already include all required forward-looking and discounting effects. Find total loss allowance.
explanation: Apply each appropriate band rate and add: 1,880,000×1% + 520,000×5% + 188,000×30% = 101,200.00. Do not apply one blended band mechanically to all balances.

title: Equity FVOCI profit-or-loss dividend • case 44
prompt: An eligible equity investment has the irrevocable FVOCI election. During the year it gains LKR 208,000 in fair value and earns a dividend of 104,000. Dividend recognition criteria are met and the dividend clearly represents a return on investment, not recovery of cost. There are no other effects. Find income recognised in PROFIT OR LOSS.
explanation: The qualifying dividend of 104,000.00 is profit-or-loss income. The fair-value movement of 208,000 is OCI under this election and is not added to the profit-or-loss amount.

title: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset • case 44
prompt: A loan is sold with full derecognition. Immediately before sale, gross carrying amount is LKR 1,880,000, loss allowance 188,000, and cash proceeds 1,786,000. No accumulated OCI, sale fees or other adjustments exist. Find the derecognition GAIN relative to net carrying amount.
explanation: Net carrying amount = 1,880,000 − 188,000 = 1,692,000. Compare proceeds with that net amount: 1,786,000 − 1,692,000 = 94,000.00 gain. Derecognise both the gross asset and related allowance.
family: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset

title: Non-substantial liability modification gain • case 44
prompt: An amortised-cost liability is modified WITHOUT extinguishment, with no fees. Its carrying amount is LKR 1,440,000. The sole revised payment is 1,656,000 in two years. Original EIR is 10%; the modification is assessed as non-substantial. Find the immediate modification GAIN from recalculating amortised cost at the original EIR.
explanation: Revised amortised cost = 1,656,000/1.10² = 1,368,595.04. Gain = old liability 1,440,000 − revised PV = 71,404.96. The original EIR is retained for this non-extinguishing modification.

title: Credit-risk improvement allowance release • case 44
prompt: A debt asset under the GENERAL ECL model previously had significant credit-risk deterioration and lifetime allowance LKR 188,000. At reporting date the criteria for lifetime ECL are no longer met; required 12-month ECL is 32,000. No write-offs, new assets or other allowance movements occur. Find the impairment reversal in profit or loss.
explanation: When lifetime measurement is no longer required, the general model returns to 12-month ECL. Release the excess allowance: 188,000 − 32,000 = 156,000.00. This is not a receivable under mandatory simplified lifetime ECL.

title: Upstream inventory elimination with tax • case 44
prompt: P and S report profits AFTER their own tax of LKR 3,760,000 and 1,680,000. An upstream inventory sale leaves unrealised profit of 376,000 in group closing inventory. A recoverable DTA is recognised on the full elimination at 30%, with the tax effect in profit or loss. No other consolidation adjustments exist. Find TOTAL consolidated profit, before attribution to owners and NCI.
explanation: Combine separate after-tax profits, eliminate unrealised profit and recognise the recoverable tax benefit: 3,760,000 + 1,680,000 − 376,000 + 112,800.00 = 5,176,800.00. This question asks total group profit, not its attribution.

title: Full-goodwill impairment and owner profit • case 44
prompt: P owns 80% of S all year. Separate after-tax profits are P LKR 3,120,000 and S 1,140,000. Goodwill is recognised on the FULL-goodwill basis and an impairment of 420,000 is attributable to S’s CGU and allocated 80:20 between owners and NCI. No other adjustments or tax effects apply. Find consolidated profit attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Owners receive 80% of S’s profit and bear 80% of the full-goodwill loss: 3,120,000 + 80% × (1,140,000 − 420,000) = 3,696,000.00. Do not charge the owners with 100% of this full-goodwill loss.

title: Partial goodwill CGU gross-up • case 44
prompt: P owns 80% of S. Recognised PARTIAL goodwill is LKR 1,504,000; S’s other net assets in the tested CGU carry at 7,520,000. Recoverable amount of the WHOLE CGU is 8,460,000. Gross up goodwill for unrecognised NCI goodwill when testing; the whole impairment falls within grossed-up goodwill. No tax or other adjustments apply. Find impairment actually recognised on group goodwill.
explanation: Grossed-up goodwill = 1,504,000/80% = 1,880,000.00. Whole-CGU impairment = grossed goodwill + other net assets − recoverable amount = 940,000.00. Only the parent’s 80% goodwill portion is recognised, so recorded loss = 752,000.00.
reference: LKAS 36 Appendix C paras C4–C8; SLFRS 10 para B86

title: Consolidated retained earnings bridge • case 44
prompt: P owns 75% of S. At year end P retained earnings are LKR 5,200,000, and S retained earnings 3,320,000. S retained earnings at acquisition were 1,000,000. Cumulative post-acquisition extra FV depreciation is 188,000. A downstream sale by P leaves unrealised profit of 124,000. No tax, goodwill impairment, dividends recognised by P, OCI or other adjustments apply. Find consolidated retained earnings attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Group owners’ retained earnings = parent RE + 75% of adjusted post-acquisition S reserves − the parent’s downstream unrealised profit: 6,675,000.00. Pre-acquisition reserves do not enter post-acquisition group retained earnings.

title: Loss of control and translation reserve • case 44
prompt: P loses control of a foreign subsidiary. Proceeds are LKR 3,960,000; retained interest FV 940,000; NCI carrying amount 520,000; consolidated net assets INCLUDING goodwill 3,920,000. A cumulative translation GAIN of 188,000, entirely attributable to P, must be reclassified to profit or loss on loss of control. No other effects apply. Find total disposal gain including that reclassification.
explanation: Base gain = proceeds + retained FV + NCI − net assets = 1,500,000.00. Add the parent’s translation gain recycled on disposal: 188,000. Total = 1,688,000.00.
family: Loss of control and translation reserve

title: Residual guarantee expected payment • case 44
prompt: A lessee owes three year-end rentals of LKR 420,000. It guarantees residual value up to 200,000, but the amount EXPECTED to be payable under that guarantee is 74,000 at year three. Discount rate is 10%. No other liability payments exist. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the amount expected to be payable, not automatically the maximum guarantee. Liability = PV of three rentals + 74,000/1.10³ = 1,100,075.13.

title: Reasonably certain purchase option PV • case 44
prompt: A lease requires three year-end rentals of LKR 370,000, plus a purchase option price of 940,000 payable at year three. Exercise is reasonably certain. Discount rate is 10%. No incentives, other payments or initial prepayments apply. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the reasonably certain purchase price in the liability: PV of rentals + purchase price discounted for three years = 1,626,371.15. Do not omit or leave the future option payment undiscounted.

title: Lease and service component allocation • case 44
prompt: A two-year contract requires bundled payments of LKR 470,000 at each year end. Relative stand-alone prices are equipment lease 200,000 and distinct maintenance 50,000 per year. The lessee does NOT elect to combine components. Lease discount rate is 10%; no other payments exist. Find initial lease liability for the LEASE component only.
explanation: Allocate 200,000/250,000 = 80% of each bundled payment to the lease: 376,000.00. Discount those two lease payments, excluding maintenance, to obtain 652,561.98.

title: Exempt short-term lease rent-free start • case 44
prompt: A twelve-month lease with no purchase option qualifies for the elected short-term exemption. The first three months are rent free, then nine monthly payments of LKR 42,000 are due. The asset is available throughout and straight-line expense is appropriate. Find lease expense for the FIRST six months, ignoring accrual settlement timing.
explanation: Total fixed payments are nine rents. Spread evenly over all twelve months: 42,000 × 9/12 × 6 = 189,000.00. Rent-free months still receive an expense allocation.

title: Sale-and-leaseback rights transferred • case 44
prompt: A transfer qualifies as a sale under SLFRS 15 at fair value LKR 18,800,000; asset carrying amount is 10,400,000. Market-rate leaseback payments have PV 7,520,000. There are no off-market adjustments or variable-payment complications. At inception, what sale gain is recognised for rights TRANSFERRED to the buyer-lessor?
explanation: Total gain = 18,800,000 − 10,400,000 = 8,400,000. Retained-use proportion = lease PV / fair value = 40%. Recognise only the transferred-rights proportion of the gain: 5,040,000.00.

title: Reassessed bargain purchase gain • case 44
prompt: After the required reassessment, final acquisition-date consideration is LKR 3,760,000, NCI fair value is 400,000 and identifiable net assets are 5,640,000. There is no prior holding or other adjustment. Find the bargain purchase gain recognised in profit or loss.
explanation: Net identifiable assets exceed consideration plus NCI: 5,640,000 − 3,760,000 − 400,000 = 1,480,000.00. Reassessment has been completed before recognising the gain.

title: Acquired contingent liability in goodwill • case 44
prompt: Consideration is LKR 5,700,000; NCI FV is 500,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired contingent liability are 4,320,000. The acquired item is a present obligation with reliably measurable FV 420,000 and qualifies for recognition despite non-probable outflow. No tax or other adjustment applies. Find goodwill after recognising it.
explanation: Recognise the qualifying acquired liability: net identifiable assets become 4,320,000 − 420,000. Goodwill = consideration + NCI − adjusted net assets = 2,300,000.00.

title: Separate acquired brand from goodwill • case 44
prompt: Consideration is LKR 5,200,000; NCI FV 600,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired separable brand are 4,360,000. Brand FV is 840,000; tax base is zero and 30% DTL must be recognised. No other adjustments apply. Find goodwill after separate brand and tax recognition.
explanation: An identifiable acquired brand is separate from goodwill. Net addition to identifiable assets = brand FV − 30% DTL = 588,000.00. Goodwill = 5,200,000 + 600,000 − (4,360,000 + 588,000.00) = 852,000.00.

title: Acquisition costs versus issue costs • case 44
prompt: A business acquisition has consideration LKR 3,320,000. Additional costs are acquisition advisory 188,000, qualifying equity-issue costs 70,000 and qualifying debt-issue costs 40,000. The issue costs follow their relevant standards, and no immediate debt-cost amortisation or other expense arises this period. Find the immediate acquisition-related PROFIT-OR-LOSS expense from these costs.
explanation: Expense advisory acquisition costs of 188,000.00. Qualifying equity and debt issuance costs follow their respective standards and are not added to this immediate acquisition-service expense or goodwill.

title: Temporary difference and enacted rate change • case 44
prompt: A taxable temporary difference opens at LKR 200,000 with a DTL measured at 25%. At year end the difference is 520,000 and the enacted rate expected on reversal is 30%. Both the underlying movements and rate change belong in profit or loss. No other tax movements exist. Find deferred tax expense for the year.
explanation: Opening DTL = 200,000×25% = 50,000. Closing DTL = 520,000×30% = 156,000.00. Expense is the full increase, including rate remeasurement: 106,000.00. Rates are exercise assumptions.
family: Temporary difference and enacted rate change

title: Revalued non-depreciable land tax basis • case 44
prompt: Non-depreciable land is revalued from cost LKR 1,880,000 to fair value 2,820,000; tax base remains cost. The enacted rate for recovery through SALE is 20%, while a 30% use rate would otherwise apply. The revaluation and associated tax go to OCI. No other effects exist. Find the net OCI revaluation increase after deferred tax.
explanation: For this non-depreciable revalued asset, measure tax consequences on recovery through sale: DTL = (2,820,000 − 1,880,000)×20%. Net OCI increase = gross uplift less that DTL = 752,000.00.

title: Current tax reconciliation and prepayment • case 44
prompt: Accounting pretax profit is LKR 4,200,000. It includes a permanently non-deductible fine of 188,000, exempt income of 50,000, and warranty expense of 420,000 deductible only on payment. Current-year warranty payments of 80,000 are deductible and were charged against the provision, not current profit. Tax rate is 30%; tax prepayments are 300,000. No other tax adjustments exist. Find closing CURRENT tax payable, not total tax expense.
explanation: Taxable profit = 4,200,000 + fine 188,000 − exempt income 50,000 + provision expense 420,000 − deductible payments 80,000 = 4,678,000. Current tax less prepaid 300,000 = 1,103,400.00. Deferred tax is separate.

title: Consolidated inventory tax difference • case 44
prompt: After eliminating an intragroup profit, inventory carries in consolidated statements at LKR 1,128,000. Its tax base in the buyer’s tax jurisdiction is 1,692,000. The buyer’s enacted rate is 30%; sufficient taxable profit is probable. No offsetting, exception or other tax effects apply. Find the consolidated DTA on this inventory.
explanation: The consolidated carrying amount is below tax base, creating a deductible temporary difference of 564,000. Use the buyer’s relevant tax rate: difference ×30% = 169,200.00.

title: Depreciation after recognised impairment • case 44
prompt: Immediately before an impairment, equipment carries at LKR 1,880,000. Recoverable amount is 1,140,000 and impairment is recognised. After that date it has four years’ remaining useful life and residual value 100,000. Straight-line depreciation is appropriate; no further revaluation or impairment applies. Find depreciation for the next FULL year.
explanation: First reduce the asset to recoverable amount 1,140,000. Thereafter allocate revised depreciable amount over remaining life: (1,140,000 − 100,000)/4 = 260,000.00.

title: Allocated headquarters in CGU impairment • case 44
prompt: CGU A carries operating assets of LKR 1,040,000; CGU B carries 400,000. A headquarters asset of 200,000 can be allocated reasonably and consistently in proportion to those operating-asset amounts. A’s recoverable amount INCLUDING its headquarters share is 870,000. No goodwill or other assets exist. Find the impairment loss for A including its allocation.
explanation: Allocate headquarters to A: 200,000 × 1,040,000/(1,040,000+400,000) = 144,444.44. Tested A carrying amount is 1,184,444.44. Impairment versus recoverable amount 870,000 = 314,444.44.

title: Break-even value-in-use cash flow • case 44
prompt: An asset carries at LKR 1,880,000. Its fair value less costs of disposal is lower. A valid VIU model uses THREE equal year-end operating cash inflows, plus 100,000 net disposal proceeds at year three, discounted at 10%. What minimum equal ANNUAL operating cash inflow makes VIU exactly equal carrying amount? Ignore tax and other adjustments.
explanation: Let annual flow be X. X×(1/1.10 + 1/1.10² + 1/1.10³) + 100,000/1.10³ = 1,880,000. Solve for X = 725,764.35. This sensitivity calculation identifies the VIU break-even point.

title: Discounted warranty expected-value portfolio • case 44
prompt: A present warranty obligation covers 1,880 products. Per product, probabilities are 70% no defect, 25% a minor repair costing LKR 400, and 5% a major repair costing 2,000. All expected payments occur exactly in TWO years. Outflow for the portfolio is probable; appropriate discount rate is 10% with no risk double counting. Find the provision.
explanation: Expected cash payment = 1,880×(25%×400 + 5%×2,000) = 376,000.0. Discount two years at 10%: 376,000.0/1.10² = 310,743.80. The probability assessment applies to the portfolio.

title: Provision movement with revised estimate • case 44
prompt: A discounted provision opens at LKR 940,000. Unwinding for a full year is at 8%. A 100,000 settlement occurs at the year END, after unwinding. At that same reporting date, a new estimate increases the remaining provision by 138,000. No other changes occur. Find closing provision.
explanation: Closing = opening + 8% unwinding − year-end settlement + estimate increase: 940,000×1.08 −100,000 +138,000 = 1,053,200.00. Classification of the estimate change’s counterpart is assessed separately.

title: Revaluation increase after earlier loss • case 44
prompt: PPE carries at LKR 1,040,000 before revaluation and is revalued to 1,880,000. A prior revaluation decrease on THIS asset of 238,000 was recognised in profit or loss and has not been reversed. No tax effects apply. Find the current increase recognised in OCI after reversing the eligible prior loss in profit or loss.
explanation: Gross increase = 1,880,000 − 1,040,000 = 840,000. First recognise 238,000 in profit or loss to reverse the prior decrease. Remaining 602,000.00 is OCI revaluation surplus.

title: Nine-month depreciation and disposal gain • case 44
prompt: Equipment cost LKR 2,080,000, residual value 200,000 and useful life five years, straight-line. Two FULL years’ depreciation were recognised before this year. It is sold after nine months of the current year for 1,510,000. It was not previously held for sale and no impairment or revaluation applies. Find disposal GAIN after the required nine-month depreciation.
explanation: Annual depreciation = (2,080,000−200,000)/5. Deduct two full years and another 9/12 year from cost to obtain disposal-date carrying amount 1,046,000.00. Gain = proceeds − that amount = 464,000.00.

title: Customer collections with a write-off • case 44
prompt: All sales are on credit. Revenue is LKR 5,200,000; opening GROSS trade receivables are 600,000; closing GROSS receivables are 1,240,000. Receivables of 144,000 were written off during the year. There are no taxes, returns, contract balances, acquisitions or exchange changes. Find cash collected from customers.
explanation: Gross receivable roll-forward: opening + credit sales − cash receipts − write-offs = closing. Thus receipts = 5,200,000+600,000−1,240,000−144,000 = 4,416,000.00. Write-offs are not cash receipts.

title: Loan funding net cash effect • case 44
prompt: A company receives cash loan proceeds of LKR 1,880,000 and immediately pays a directly attributable lender issue fee of 42,000. Both payments are classified as financing cash flows in this case. No other cash movement occurs. Find the NET financing cash inflow from these two cash movements; this question does not require net line-item presentation.
explanation: Net financing cash effect = proceeds − cash fee = 1,880,000 − 42,000.00 = 1,838,000.00. Effective-interest amortisation later is not another inception cash payment.

title: Item-by-item NRV without offsetting headroom • case 44
prompt: Two unrelated inventory lines require separate NRV tests. A has 320 units, cost LKR 1,000 and NRV 900 each. B has 188 units, cost 1,000 and NRV 1,200 each. There is no basis to group them for the write-down test. Find TOTAL closing inventory carrying amount.
explanation: Carry A at 900 per unit and B at its lower cost of 1,000. Total = 320×900 + 188×1,000 = 476,000.00. B’s NRV headroom cannot offset A’s write-down.

title: Units-of-production intangible amortisation • case 44
prompt: A finite-life production licence costs LKR 1,780,000, has zero residual value, and is expected to support 150,000 units in total. Actual output this year is 52,000 units. A units-of-production method reliably reflects consumption and the asset was available throughout. No impairment or estimate change applies. Find annual amortisation.
explanation: Apply the supported consumption pattern: amortisation = 1,780,000 × 52,000/150,000 = 617,066.67. It is the share of expected lifetime production consumed, not an automatic straight-line charge.

title: Profit after suspended associate losses • case 44
prompt: An equity-method investment and relevant long-term interests were previously reduced to zero. Unrecognised share of prior losses totals LKR 168,000; the investor has no obligation and made no support payments. In the current year its share of associate profit is 252,000. No other adjustments or changes in interest apply. Find the share of profit that can now be RECOGNISED.
explanation: First absorb unrecognised prior losses before resuming recognised profit. Recognised amount = current profit share 252,000 − prior unrecognised losses 168,000 = 84,000.00.

title: Return recovery asset net of costs • case 45
prompt: A retailer has transferred 2,125 products. It expects 85 to be returned. Each returned product originally cost LKR 600; expected recovery handling is 20 per item and expected value deterioration is 30 per item. Estimates meet the relevant requirements. Find the separate asset for the right to recover returned products, excluding the refund liability.
explanation: Recovery asset = original carrying amount of expected returns less recovery costs and potential value decrease: 85 × (600 − 20 − 30) = 46,750.00. It is assessed separately from the customer refund liability.
family: Return recovery asset net of costs

title: Retrospective volume rebate true-up • case 45
prompt: A customer’s annual purchases reach 14,500 units at list price LKR 200. Crossing the threshold entitles it to a 5% retrospective rebate on ALL units. Cumulative revenue before this new supported estimate equals full list price; no rebate was previously accrued. The constraint permits the estimate. Find the reduction in cumulative revenue required now.
explanation: The revised transaction price reflects the retrospective rebate on all units. Revenue reduction = 14,500 × 200 × 5% = 145,000.00. Recognise the corresponding refund obligation as appropriate.

title: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation • case 45
prompt: A bundle has distinct goods A and B with stand-alone prices LKR 425,000 and 750,000. Total transaction price is 1,080,000. ALL paragraph 82 criteria demonstrate that the whole 95,000 discount relates only to A. A transfers now; B is not yet delivered. Find revenue recognised for A.
explanation: The specified discount-allocation exception applies. Allocate all 95,000 discount to A: 425,000 − 95,000 = 330,000.00. Do not default to relative allocation when the exception’s criteria are met.
family: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation

title: Three obligations and partial service • case 45
prompt: A contract price of LKR 2,550,000 covers goods A, goods B and twelve months of distinct support. Stand-alone prices are 600,000, 300,000 and 300,000 respectively. A is delivered, B is not, and six months of evenly provided support are complete. No allocation exception applies. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise allocation to A plus half of support: 2,550,000 × (600,000 + 150,000) / 1,200,000 = 1,593,750.00. B’s allocation remains unrecognised as revenue.

title: Progress excluding abnormal waste • case 45
prompt: An over-time contract has transaction price LKR 14,500,000. Costs incurred are 5,800,000, including abnormal waste of 290,000 that does not depict progress. Expected TOTAL productive costs excluding that waste are 11,600,000. Cost-to-cost is appropriate after excluding the waste; no other adjustment applies. Find cumulative revenue, not profit.
explanation: Exclude abnormal waste from the progress numerator. Productive progress = (5,800,000 − 290,000) / 11,600,000. Revenue = transaction price × that progress = 6,887,500.00. The wasted cost is not a revenue-producing input.

title: Uninstalled materials without margin • case 45
prompt: A single over-time construction obligation has price LKR 19,000,000. All B19(b) conditions justify recognising revenue equal to cost for significant uninstalled materials of 3,800,000 already controlled by the customer. Other productive costs incurred are 2,850,000; expected total OTHER costs are 11,400,000. No revenue was previously recognised. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise material revenue without margin: 3,800,000. Recognise the remaining price using other-cost progress: (19,000,000 − 3,800,000) × 2,850,000/11,400,000. Total revenue = 7,600,000.00.

title: Agent commission after collection • case 45
prompt: An intermediary is an AGENT and collects customer cash of LKR 3,250,000 for a completed supplier service. It must remit 88% to the supplier and is entitled to the remaining 12% commission. It controls neither the underlying service nor any distinct extra service, and there is no tax. Find its revenue.
explanation: An agent recognises its fee or commission, not the supplier’s gross billings: 3,250,000 × 12% = 390,000.00. The amount due to the supplier is separately accounted for.

title: Distinct remaining goods blended prospectively • case 45
prompt: At modification, 100 distinct goods remain under an existing contract at LKR 1,450 each. Another 50 distinct goods are added at 1,160 each. The modification is NOT a separate contract, but remaining goods are distinct from those already transferred, so paragraph 21(a) applies prospectively. Thirty of the remaining goods are then transferred. Find revenue for those thirty.
explanation: Prospective remaining consideration = 100 × 1,450 + 50 × 1,160. Divide by 150 remaining goods, then multiply by 30 = 40,600.00. Do not retrospectively revise revenue on goods already transferred.

title: FVTPL acquisition expense • case 45
