explanation: Carry A at 900 per unit and B at its lower cost of 1,000. Total = 380×900 + 212×1,000 = 554,000.00. B’s NRV headroom cannot offset A’s write-down.

title: Units-of-production intangible amortisation • case 56
prompt: A finite-life production licence costs LKR 2,020,000, has zero residual value, and is expected to support 150,000 units in total. Actual output this year is 58,000 units. A units-of-production method reliably reflects consumption and the asset was available throughout. No impairment or estimate change applies. Find annual amortisation.
explanation: Apply the supported consumption pattern: amortisation = 2,020,000 × 58,000/150,000 = 781,066.67. It is the share of expected lifetime production consumed, not an automatic straight-line charge.

title: Profit after suspended associate losses • case 56
prompt: An equity-method investment and relevant long-term interests were previously reduced to zero. Unrecognised share of prior losses totals LKR 192,000; the investor has no obligation and made no support payments. In the current year its share of associate profit is 288,000. No other adjustments or changes in interest apply. Find the share of profit that can now be RECOGNISED.
explanation: First absorb unrecognised prior losses before resuming recognised profit. Recognised amount = current profit share 288,000 − prior unrecognised losses 192,000 = 96,000.00.

title: Return recovery asset net of costs • case 57
prompt: A retailer has transferred 2,425 products. It expects 97 to be returned. Each returned product originally cost LKR 600; expected recovery handling is 20 per item and expected value deterioration is 30 per item. Estimates meet the relevant requirements. Find the separate asset for the right to recover returned products, excluding the refund liability.
explanation: Recovery asset = original carrying amount of expected returns less recovery costs and potential value decrease: 97 × (600 − 20 − 30) = 53,350.00. It is assessed separately from the customer refund liability.
family: Return recovery asset net of costs

title: Retrospective volume rebate true-up • case 57
prompt: A customer’s annual purchases reach 15,700 units at list price LKR 200. Crossing the threshold entitles it to a 5% retrospective rebate on ALL units. Cumulative revenue before this new supported estimate equals full list price; no rebate was previously accrued. The constraint permits the estimate. Find the reduction in cumulative revenue required now.
explanation: The revised transaction price reflects the retrospective rebate on all units. Revenue reduction = 15,700 × 200 × 5% = 157,000.00. Recognise the corresponding refund obligation as appropriate.

title: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation • case 57
prompt: A bundle has distinct goods A and B with stand-alone prices LKR 485,000 and 870,000. Total transaction price is 1,248,000. ALL paragraph 82 criteria demonstrate that the whole 107,000 discount relates only to A. A transfers now; B is not yet delivered. Find revenue recognised for A.
explanation: The specified discount-allocation exception applies. Allocate all 107,000 discount to A: 485,000 − 107,000 = 378,000.00. Do not default to relative allocation when the exception’s criteria are met.
family: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation

title: Three obligations and partial service • case 57
prompt: A contract price of LKR 2,910,000 covers goods A, goods B and twelve months of distinct support. Stand-alone prices are 600,000, 300,000 and 300,000 respectively. A is delivered, B is not, and six months of evenly provided support are complete. No allocation exception applies. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise allocation to A plus half of support: 2,910,000 × (600,000 + 150,000) / 1,200,000 = 1,818,750.00. B’s allocation remains unrecognised as revenue.

title: Progress excluding abnormal waste • case 57
prompt: An over-time contract has transaction price LKR 15,700,000. Costs incurred are 6,280,000, including abnormal waste of 314,000 that does not depict progress. Expected TOTAL productive costs excluding that waste are 12,560,000. Cost-to-cost is appropriate after excluding the waste; no other adjustment applies. Find cumulative revenue, not profit.
explanation: Exclude abnormal waste from the progress numerator. Productive progress = (6,280,000 − 314,000) / 12,560,000. Revenue = transaction price × that progress = 7,457,500.00. The wasted cost is not a revenue-producing input.

title: Uninstalled materials without margin • case 57
prompt: A single over-time construction obligation has price LKR 21,400,000. All B19(b) conditions justify recognising revenue equal to cost for significant uninstalled materials of 4,280,000 already controlled by the customer. Other productive costs incurred are 3,210,000; expected total OTHER costs are 12,840,000. No revenue was previously recognised. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise material revenue without margin: 4,280,000. Recognise the remaining price using other-cost progress: (21,400,000 − 4,280,000) × 3,210,000/12,840,000. Total revenue = 8,560,000.00.

title: Agent commission after collection • case 57
prompt: An intermediary is an AGENT and collects customer cash of LKR 3,850,000 for a completed supplier service. It must remit 88% to the supplier and is entitled to the remaining 12% commission. It controls neither the underlying service nor any distinct extra service, and there is no tax. Find its revenue.
explanation: An agent recognises its fee or commission, not the supplier’s gross billings: 3,850,000 × 12% = 462,000.00. The amount due to the supplier is separately accounted for.

title: Distinct remaining goods blended prospectively • case 57
prompt: At modification, 100 distinct goods remain under an existing contract at LKR 1,570 each. Another 50 distinct goods are added at 1,256 each. The modification is NOT a separate contract, but remaining goods are distinct from those already transferred, so paragraph 21(a) applies prospectively. Thirty of the remaining goods are then transferred. Find revenue for those thirty.
explanation: Prospective remaining consideration = 100 × 1,570 + 50 × 1,256. Divide by 150 remaining goods, then multiply by 30 = 43,960.00. Do not retrospectively revise revenue on goods already transferred.

title: FVTPL acquisition expense • case 57
prompt: A financial asset is acquired at fair value LKR 1,940,000 and is classified at FVTPL. Directly attributable broker costs are 48,500, paid separately. No fair-value change occurs immediately after purchase. Find the immediate profit-or-loss expense from acquiring this asset.
explanation: Transaction costs on an FVTPL asset are expensed. Initial asset carrying amount is fair value 1,940,000; immediate acquisition expense is 48,500.00.

title: Collateral cash-shortfall discounting • case 57
prompt: A credit loss scenario has a contractual receipt of LKR 2,425,000 due in one year. The ONLY expected recovery at that same date is collateral sale proceeds of 1,555,000, less sale costs of 107,000. Scenario probability is 100% and original EIR is 10%. Collateral is an integral contractual credit enhancement and not separately recognised. Find discounted ECL.
explanation: One-year shortfall = contractual receipt − net collateral recovery = 2,425,000 − (1,555,000 − 107,000). Discount that shortfall at 10%: 888,181.82. Do not ignore recovery costs or discount only one side of same-date cash flows.

title: Three-band provision matrix • case 57
prompt: Under the simplified lifetime-ECL approach, supported adjusted loss rates are 1% on current receivables of LKR 2,140,000, 5% on past-due balances of 585,000, and 30% on severely overdue balances of 214,000. Rates already include all required forward-looking and discounting effects. Find total loss allowance.
explanation: Apply each appropriate band rate and add: 2,140,000×1% + 585,000×5% + 214,000×30% = 114,850.00. Do not apply one blended band mechanically to all balances.

title: Equity FVOCI profit-or-loss dividend • case 57
prompt: An eligible equity investment has the irrevocable FVOCI election. During the year it gains LKR 234,000 in fair value and earns a dividend of 117,000. Dividend recognition criteria are met and the dividend clearly represents a return on investment, not recovery of cost. There are no other effects. Find income recognised in PROFIT OR LOSS.
explanation: The qualifying dividend of 117,000.00 is profit-or-loss income. The fair-value movement of 234,000 is OCI under this election and is not added to the profit-or-loss amount.

title: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset • case 57
prompt: A loan is sold with full derecognition. Immediately before sale, gross carrying amount is LKR 2,140,000, loss allowance 214,000, and cash proceeds 2,033,000. No accumulated OCI, sale fees or other adjustments exist. Find the derecognition GAIN relative to net carrying amount.
explanation: Net carrying amount = 2,140,000 − 214,000 = 1,926,000. Compare proceeds with that net amount: 2,033,000 − 1,926,000 = 107,000.00 gain. Derecognise both the gross asset and related allowance.
family: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset

title: Non-substantial liability modification gain • case 57
prompt: An amortised-cost liability is modified WITHOUT extinguishment, with no fees. Its carrying amount is LKR 1,570,000. The sole revised payment is 1,805,500 in two years. Original EIR is 10%; the modification is assessed as non-substantial. Find the immediate modification GAIN from recalculating amortised cost at the original EIR.
explanation: Revised amortised cost = 1,805,500/1.10² = 1,492,148.76. Gain = old liability 1,570,000 − revised PV = 77,851.24. The original EIR is retained for this non-extinguishing modification.

title: Credit-risk improvement allowance release • case 57
prompt: A debt asset under the GENERAL ECL model previously had significant credit-risk deterioration and lifetime allowance LKR 214,000. At reporting date the criteria for lifetime ECL are no longer met; required 12-month ECL is 38,500. No write-offs, new assets or other allowance movements occur. Find the impairment reversal in profit or loss.
explanation: When lifetime measurement is no longer required, the general model returns to 12-month ECL. Release the excess allowance: 214,000 − 38,500 = 175,500.00. This is not a receivable under mandatory simplified lifetime ECL.

title: Upstream inventory elimination with tax • case 57
prompt: P and S report profits AFTER their own tax of LKR 4,280,000 and 1,940,000. An upstream inventory sale leaves unrealised profit of 428,000 in group closing inventory. A recoverable DTA is recognised on the full elimination at 30%, with the tax effect in profit or loss. No other consolidation adjustments exist. Find TOTAL consolidated profit, before attribution to owners and NCI.
explanation: Combine separate after-tax profits, eliminate unrealised profit and recognise the recoverable tax benefit: 4,280,000 + 1,940,000 − 428,000 + 128,400.00 = 5,920,400.00. This question asks total group profit, not its attribution.

title: Full-goodwill impairment and owner profit • case 57
prompt: P owns 80% of S all year. Separate after-tax profits are P LKR 3,510,000 and S 1,270,000. Goodwill is recognised on the FULL-goodwill basis and an impairment of 485,000 is attributable to S’s CGU and allocated 80:20 between owners and NCI. No other adjustments or tax effects apply. Find consolidated profit attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Owners receive 80% of S’s profit and bear 80% of the full-goodwill loss: 3,510,000 + 80% × (1,270,000 − 485,000) = 4,138,000.00. Do not charge the owners with 100% of this full-goodwill loss.

title: Partial goodwill CGU gross-up • case 57
prompt: P owns 80% of S. Recognised PARTIAL goodwill is LKR 1,712,000; S’s other net assets in the tested CGU carry at 8,560,000. Recoverable amount of the WHOLE CGU is 9,630,000. Gross up goodwill for unrecognised NCI goodwill when testing; the whole impairment falls within grossed-up goodwill. No tax or other adjustments apply. Find impairment actually recognised on group goodwill.
explanation: Grossed-up goodwill = 1,712,000/80% = 2,140,000.00. Whole-CGU impairment = grossed goodwill + other net assets − recoverable amount = 1,070,000.00. Only the parent’s 80% goodwill portion is recognised, so recorded loss = 856,000.00.
reference: LKAS 36 Appendix C paras C4–C8; SLFRS 10 para B86

title: Consolidated retained earnings bridge • case 57
prompt: P owns 75% of S. At year end P retained earnings are LKR 5,850,000, and S retained earnings 3,710,000. S retained earnings at acquisition were 1,000,000. Cumulative post-acquisition extra FV depreciation is 214,000. A downstream sale by P leaves unrealised profit of 137,000. No tax, goodwill impairment, dividends recognised by P, OCI or other adjustments apply. Find consolidated retained earnings attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Group owners’ retained earnings = parent RE + 75% of adjusted post-acquisition S reserves − the parent’s downstream unrealised profit: 7,585,000.00. Pre-acquisition reserves do not enter post-acquisition group retained earnings.

title: Loss of control and translation reserve • case 57
prompt: P loses control of a foreign subsidiary. Proceeds are LKR 4,480,000; retained interest FV 1,070,000; NCI carrying amount 585,000; consolidated net assets INCLUDING goodwill 4,310,000. A cumulative translation GAIN of 214,000, entirely attributable to P, must be reclassified to profit or loss on loss of control. No other effects apply. Find total disposal gain including that reclassification.
explanation: Base gain = proceeds + retained FV + NCI − net assets = 1,825,000.00. Add the parent’s translation gain recycled on disposal: 214,000. Total = 2,039,000.00.
family: Loss of control and translation reserve

title: Residual guarantee expected payment • case 57
prompt: A lessee owes three year-end rentals of LKR 485,000. It guarantees residual value up to 200,000, but the amount EXPECTED to be payable under that guarantee is 87,000 at year three. Discount rate is 10%. No other liability payments exist. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the amount expected to be payable, not automatically the maximum guarantee. Liability = PV of three rentals + 87,000/1.10³ = 1,271,487.60.

title: Reasonably certain purchase option PV • case 57
prompt: A lease requires three year-end rentals of LKR 435,000, plus a purchase option price of 1,070,000 payable at year three. Exercise is reasonably certain. Discount rate is 10%. No incentives, other payments or initial prepayments apply. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the reasonably certain purchase price in the liability: PV of rentals + purchase price discounted for three years = 1,885,687.45. Do not omit or leave the future option payment undiscounted.

title: Lease and service component allocation • case 57
prompt: A two-year contract requires bundled payments of LKR 535,000 at each year end. Relative stand-alone prices are equipment lease 200,000 and distinct maintenance 50,000 per year. The lessee does NOT elect to combine components. Lease discount rate is 10%; no other payments exist. Find initial lease liability for the LEASE component only.
explanation: Allocate 200,000/250,000 = 80% of each bundled payment to the lease: 428,000.00. Discount those two lease payments, excluding maintenance, to obtain 742,809.92.

title: Exempt short-term lease rent-free start • case 57
prompt: A twelve-month lease with no purchase option qualifies for the elected short-term exemption. The first three months are rent free, then nine monthly payments of LKR 48,500 are due. The asset is available throughout and straight-line expense is appropriate. Find lease expense for the FIRST six months, ignoring accrual settlement timing.
explanation: Total fixed payments are nine rents. Spread evenly over all twelve months: 48,500 × 9/12 × 6 = 218,250.00. Rent-free months still receive an expense allocation.

title: Sale-and-leaseback rights transferred • case 57
prompt: A transfer qualifies as a sale under SLFRS 15 at fair value LKR 21,400,000; asset carrying amount is 11,700,000. Market-rate leaseback payments have PV 8,560,000. There are no off-market adjustments or variable-payment complications. At inception, what sale gain is recognised for rights TRANSFERRED to the buyer-lessor?
explanation: Total gain = 21,400,000 − 11,700,000 = 9,700,000. Retained-use proportion = lease PV / fair value = 40%. Recognise only the transferred-rights proportion of the gain: 5,820,000.00.

title: Reassessed bargain purchase gain • case 57
prompt: After the required reassessment, final acquisition-date consideration is LKR 4,280,000, NCI fair value is 400,000 and identifiable net assets are 6,420,000. There is no prior holding or other adjustment. Find the bargain purchase gain recognised in profit or loss.
explanation: Net identifiable assets exceed consideration plus NCI: 6,420,000 − 4,280,000 − 400,000 = 1,740,000.00. Reassessment has been completed before recognising the gain.

title: Acquired contingent liability in goodwill • case 57
prompt: Consideration is LKR 6,350,000; NCI FV is 500,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired contingent liability are 4,710,000. The acquired item is a present obligation with reliably measurable FV 485,000 and qualifies for recognition despite non-probable outflow. No tax or other adjustment applies. Find goodwill after recognising it.
explanation: Recognise the qualifying acquired liability: net identifiable assets become 4,710,000 − 485,000. Goodwill = consideration + NCI − adjusted net assets = 2,625,000.00.

title: Separate acquired brand from goodwill • case 57
prompt: Consideration is LKR 5,850,000; NCI FV 600,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired separable brand are 4,880,000. Brand FV is 970,000; tax base is zero and 30% DTL must be recognised. No other adjustments apply. Find goodwill after separate brand and tax recognition.
explanation: An identifiable acquired brand is separate from goodwill. Net addition to identifiable assets = brand FV − 30% DTL = 679,000.00. Goodwill = 5,850,000 + 600,000 − (4,880,000 + 679,000.00) = 891,000.00.

title: Acquisition costs versus issue costs • case 57
prompt: A business acquisition has consideration LKR 3,710,000. Additional costs are acquisition advisory 214,000, qualifying equity-issue costs 70,000 and qualifying debt-issue costs 40,000. The issue costs follow their relevant standards, and no immediate debt-cost amortisation or other expense arises this period. Find the immediate acquisition-related PROFIT-OR-LOSS expense from these costs.
explanation: Expense advisory acquisition costs of 214,000.00. Qualifying equity and debt issuance costs follow their respective standards and are not added to this immediate acquisition-service expense or goodwill.

title: Temporary difference and enacted rate change • case 57
prompt: A taxable temporary difference opens at LKR 200,000 with a DTL measured at 25%. At year end the difference is 585,000 and the enacted rate expected on reversal is 30%. Both the underlying movements and rate change belong in profit or loss. No other tax movements exist. Find deferred tax expense for the year.
explanation: Opening DTL = 200,000×25% = 50,000. Closing DTL = 585,000×30% = 175,500.00. Expense is the full increase, including rate remeasurement: 125,500.00. Rates are exercise assumptions.
family: Temporary difference and enacted rate change

title: Revalued non-depreciable land tax basis • case 57
prompt: Non-depreciable land is revalued from cost LKR 2,140,000 to fair value 3,210,000; tax base remains cost. The enacted rate for recovery through SALE is 20%, while a 30% use rate would otherwise apply. The revaluation and associated tax go to OCI. No other effects exist. Find the net OCI revaluation increase after deferred tax.
explanation: For this non-depreciable revalued asset, measure tax consequences on recovery through sale: DTL = (3,210,000 − 2,140,000)×20%. Net OCI increase = gross uplift less that DTL = 856,000.00.

title: Current tax reconciliation and prepayment • case 57
prompt: Accounting pretax profit is LKR 4,850,000. It includes a permanently non-deductible fine of 214,000, exempt income of 50,000, and warranty expense of 485,000 deductible only on payment. Current-year warranty payments of 80,000 are deductible and were charged against the provision, not current profit. Tax rate is 30%; tax prepayments are 300,000. No other tax adjustments exist. Find closing CURRENT tax payable, not total tax expense.
explanation: Taxable profit = 4,850,000 + fine 214,000 − exempt income 50,000 + provision expense 485,000 − deductible payments 80,000 = 5,419,000. Current tax less prepaid 300,000 = 1,325,700.00. Deferred tax is separate.

title: Consolidated inventory tax difference • case 57
prompt: After eliminating an intragroup profit, inventory carries in consolidated statements at LKR 1,284,000. Its tax base in the buyer’s tax jurisdiction is 1,926,000. The buyer’s enacted rate is 30%; sufficient taxable profit is probable. No offsetting, exception or other tax effects apply. Find the consolidated DTA on this inventory.
explanation: The consolidated carrying amount is below tax base, creating a deductible temporary difference of 642,000. Use the buyer’s relevant tax rate: difference ×30% = 192,600.00.

title: Depreciation after recognised impairment • case 57
prompt: Immediately before an impairment, equipment carries at LKR 2,140,000. Recoverable amount is 1,270,000 and impairment is recognised. After that date it has four years’ remaining useful life and residual value 100,000. Straight-line depreciation is appropriate; no further revaluation or impairment applies. Find depreciation for the next FULL year.
explanation: First reduce the asset to recoverable amount 1,270,000. Thereafter allocate revised depreciable amount over remaining life: (1,270,000 − 100,000)/4 = 292,500.00.

title: Allocated headquarters in CGU impairment • case 57
prompt: CGU A carries operating assets of LKR 1,170,000; CGU B carries 400,000. A headquarters asset of 200,000 can be allocated reasonably and consistently in proportion to those operating-asset amounts. A’s recoverable amount INCLUDING its headquarters share is 935,000. No goodwill or other assets exist. Find the impairment loss for A including its allocation.
explanation: Allocate headquarters to A: 200,000 × 1,170,000/(1,170,000+400,000) = 149,044.59. Tested A carrying amount is 1,319,044.59. Impairment versus recoverable amount 935,000 = 384,044.59.

title: Break-even value-in-use cash flow • case 57
prompt: An asset carries at LKR 2,140,000. Its fair value less costs of disposal is lower. A valid VIU model uses THREE equal year-end operating cash inflows, plus 100,000 net disposal proceeds at year three, discounted at 10%. What minimum equal ANNUAL operating cash inflow makes VIU exactly equal carrying amount? Ignore tax and other adjustments.
explanation: Let annual flow be X. X×(1/1.10 + 1/1.10² + 1/1.10³) + 100,000/1.10³ = 2,140,000. Solve for X = 830,314.20. This sensitivity calculation identifies the VIU break-even point.

title: Discounted warranty expected-value portfolio • case 57
prompt: A present warranty obligation covers 2,140 products. Per product, probabilities are 70% no defect, 25% a minor repair costing LKR 400, and 5% a major repair costing 2,000. All expected payments occur exactly in TWO years. Outflow for the portfolio is probable; appropriate discount rate is 10% with no risk double counting. Find the provision.
explanation: Expected cash payment = 2,140×(25%×400 + 5%×2,000) = 428,000.0. Discount two years at 10%: 428,000.0/1.10² = 353,719.01. The probability assessment applies to the portfolio.

title: Provision movement with revised estimate • case 57
prompt: A discounted provision opens at LKR 1,070,000. Unwinding for a full year is at 8%. A 100,000 settlement occurs at the year END, after unwinding. At that same reporting date, a new estimate increases the remaining provision by 164,000. No other changes occur. Find closing provision.
explanation: Closing = opening + 8% unwinding − year-end settlement + estimate increase: 1,070,000×1.08 −100,000 +164,000 = 1,219,600.00. Classification of the estimate change’s counterpart is assessed separately.

title: Revaluation increase after earlier loss • case 57
prompt: PPE carries at LKR 1,170,000 before revaluation and is revalued to 2,140,000. A prior revaluation decrease on THIS asset of 264,000 was recognised in profit or loss and has not been reversed. No tax effects apply. Find the current increase recognised in OCI after reversing the eligible prior loss in profit or loss.
explanation: Gross increase = 2,140,000 − 1,170,000 = 970,000. First recognise 264,000 in profit or loss to reverse the prior decrease. Remaining 706,000.00 is OCI revaluation surplus.

title: Nine-month depreciation and disposal gain • case 57
prompt: Equipment cost LKR 2,340,000, residual value 200,000 and useful life five years, straight-line. Two FULL years’ depreciation were recognised before this year. It is sold after nine months of the current year for 1,705,000. It was not previously held for sale and no impairment or revaluation applies. Find disposal GAIN after the required nine-month depreciation.
explanation: Annual depreciation = (2,340,000−200,000)/5. Deduct two full years and another 9/12 year from cost to obtain disposal-date carrying amount 1,163,000.00. Gain = proceeds − that amount = 542,000.00.

title: Customer collections with a write-off • case 57
prompt: All sales are on credit. Revenue is LKR 5,850,000; opening GROSS trade receivables are 600,000; closing GROSS receivables are 1,370,000. Receivables of 157,000 were written off during the year. There are no taxes, returns, contract balances, acquisitions or exchange changes. Find cash collected from customers.
explanation: Gross receivable roll-forward: opening + credit sales − cash receipts − write-offs = closing. Thus receipts = 5,850,000+600,000−1,370,000−157,000 = 4,923,000.00. Write-offs are not cash receipts.

title: Loan funding net cash effect • case 57
prompt: A company receives cash loan proceeds of LKR 2,140,000 and immediately pays a directly attributable lender issue fee of 48,500. Both payments are classified as financing cash flows in this case. No other cash movement occurs. Find the NET financing cash inflow from these two cash movements; this question does not require net line-item presentation.
explanation: Net financing cash effect = proceeds − cash fee = 2,140,000 − 48,500.00 = 2,091,500.00. Effective-interest amortisation later is not another inception cash payment.

title: Item-by-item NRV without offsetting headroom • case 57
prompt: Two unrelated inventory lines require separate NRV tests. A has 385 units, cost LKR 1,000 and NRV 900 each. B has 214 units, cost 1,000 and NRV 1,200 each. There is no basis to group them for the write-down test. Find TOTAL closing inventory carrying amount.
explanation: Carry A at 900 per unit and B at its lower cost of 1,000. Total = 385×900 + 214×1,000 = 560,500.00. B’s NRV headroom cannot offset A’s write-down.

title: Units-of-production intangible amortisation • case 57
prompt: A finite-life production licence costs LKR 2,040,000, has zero residual value, and is expected to support 150,000 units in total. Actual output this year is 58,500 units. A units-of-production method reliably reflects consumption and the asset was available throughout. No impairment or estimate change applies. Find annual amortisation.
explanation: Apply the supported consumption pattern: amortisation = 2,040,000 × 58,500/150,000 = 795,600.00. It is the share of expected lifetime production consumed, not an automatic straight-line charge.

title: Profit after suspended associate losses • case 57
prompt: An equity-method investment and relevant long-term interests were previously reduced to zero. Unrecognised share of prior losses totals LKR 194,000; the investor has no obligation and made no support payments. In the current year its share of associate profit is 291,000. No other adjustments or changes in interest apply. Find the share of profit that can now be RECOGNISED.
explanation: First absorb unrecognised prior losses before resuming recognised profit. Recognised amount = current profit share 291,000 − prior unrecognised losses 194,000 = 97,000.00.

title: Return recovery asset net of costs • case 58
prompt: A retailer has transferred 2,450 products. It expects 98 to be returned. Each returned product originally cost LKR 600; expected recovery handling is 20 per item and expected value deterioration is 30 per item. Estimates meet the relevant requirements. Find the separate asset for the right to recover returned products, excluding the refund liability.
explanation: Recovery asset = original carrying amount of expected returns less recovery costs and potential value decrease: 98 × (600 − 20 − 30) = 53,900.00. It is assessed separately from the customer refund liability.
family: Return recovery asset net of costs

title: Retrospective volume rebate true-up • case 58
prompt: A customer’s annual purchases reach 15,800 units at list price LKR 200. Crossing the threshold entitles it to a 5% retrospective rebate on ALL units. Cumulative revenue before this new supported estimate equals full list price; no rebate was previously accrued. The constraint permits the estimate. Find the reduction in cumulative revenue required now.
explanation: The revised transaction price reflects the retrospective rebate on all units. Revenue reduction = 15,800 × 200 × 5% = 158,000.00. Recognise the corresponding refund obligation as appropriate.

title: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation • case 58
prompt: A bundle has distinct goods A and B with stand-alone prices LKR 490,000 and 880,000. Total transaction price is 1,262,000. ALL paragraph 82 criteria demonstrate that the whole 108,000 discount relates only to A. A transfers now; B is not yet delivered. Find revenue recognised for A.
explanation: The specified discount-allocation exception applies. Allocate all 108,000 discount to A: 490,000 − 108,000 = 382,000.00. Do not default to relative allocation when the exception’s criteria are met.
family: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation

title: Three obligations and partial service • case 58
prompt: A contract price of LKR 2,940,000 covers goods A, goods B and twelve months of distinct support. Stand-alone prices are 600,000, 300,000 and 300,000 respectively. A is delivered, B is not, and six months of evenly provided support are complete. No allocation exception applies. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise allocation to A plus half of support: 2,940,000 × (600,000 + 150,000) / 1,200,000 = 1,837,500.00. B’s allocation remains unrecognised as revenue.

title: Progress excluding abnormal waste • case 58
prompt: An over-time contract has transaction price LKR 15,800,000. Costs incurred are 6,320,000, including abnormal waste of 316,000 that does not depict progress. Expected TOTAL productive costs excluding that waste are 12,640,000. Cost-to-cost is appropriate after excluding the waste; no other adjustment applies. Find cumulative revenue, not profit.
explanation: Exclude abnormal waste from the progress numerator. Productive progress = (6,320,000 − 316,000) / 12,640,000. Revenue = transaction price × that progress = 7,505,000.00. The wasted cost is not a revenue-producing input.

title: Uninstalled materials without margin • case 58
prompt: A single over-time construction obligation has price LKR 21,600,000. All B19(b) conditions justify recognising revenue equal to cost for significant uninstalled materials of 4,320,000 already controlled by the customer. Other productive costs incurred are 3,240,000; expected total OTHER costs are 12,960,000. No revenue was previously recognised. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise material revenue without margin: 4,320,000. Recognise the remaining price using other-cost progress: (21,600,000 − 4,320,000) × 3,240,000/12,960,000. Total revenue = 8,640,000.00.

title: Agent commission after collection • case 58
prompt: An intermediary is an AGENT and collects customer cash of LKR 3,900,000 for a completed supplier service. It must remit 88% to the supplier and is entitled to the remaining 12% commission. It controls neither the underlying service nor any distinct extra service, and there is no tax. Find its revenue.
explanation: An agent recognises its fee or commission, not the supplier’s gross billings: 3,900,000 × 12% = 468,000.00. The amount due to the supplier is separately accounted for.

title: Distinct remaining goods blended prospectively • case 58
prompt: At modification, 100 distinct goods remain under an existing contract at LKR 1,580 each. Another 50 distinct goods are added at 1,264 each. The modification is NOT a separate contract, but remaining goods are distinct from those already transferred, so paragraph 21(a) applies prospectively. Thirty of the remaining goods are then transferred. Find revenue for those thirty.
explanation: Prospective remaining consideration = 100 × 1,580 + 50 × 1,264. Divide by 150 remaining goods, then multiply by 30 = 44,240.00. Do not retrospectively revise revenue on goods already transferred.

title: FVTPL acquisition expense • case 58
prompt: A financial asset is acquired at fair value LKR 1,960,000 and is classified at FVTPL. Directly attributable broker costs are 49,000, paid separately. No fair-value change occurs immediately after purchase. Find the immediate profit-or-loss expense from acquiring this asset.
explanation: Transaction costs on an FVTPL asset are expensed. Initial asset carrying amount is fair value 1,960,000; immediate acquisition expense is 49,000.00.

title: Collateral cash-shortfall discounting • case 58
prompt: A credit loss scenario has a contractual receipt of LKR 2,450,000 due in one year. The ONLY expected recovery at that same date is collateral sale proceeds of 1,570,000, less sale costs of 108,000. Scenario probability is 100% and original EIR is 10%. Collateral is an integral contractual credit enhancement and not separately recognised. Find discounted ECL.
explanation: One-year shortfall = contractual receipt − net collateral recovery = 2,450,000 − (1,570,000 − 108,000). Discount that shortfall at 10%: 898,181.82. Do not ignore recovery costs or discount only one side of same-date cash flows.

title: Three-band provision matrix • case 58
prompt: Under the simplified lifetime-ECL approach, supported adjusted loss rates are 1% on current receivables of LKR 2,160,000, 5% on past-due balances of 590,000, and 30% on severely overdue balances of 216,000. Rates already include all required forward-looking and discounting effects. Find total loss allowance.
explanation: Apply each appropriate band rate and add: 2,160,000×1% + 590,000×5% + 216,000×30% = 115,900.00. Do not apply one blended band mechanically to all balances.

title: Equity FVOCI profit-or-loss dividend • case 58
prompt: An eligible equity investment has the irrevocable FVOCI election. During the year it gains LKR 236,000 in fair value and earns a dividend of 118,000. Dividend recognition criteria are met and the dividend clearly represents a return on investment, not recovery of cost. There are no other effects. Find income recognised in PROFIT OR LOSS.
explanation: The qualifying dividend of 118,000.00 is profit-or-loss income. The fair-value movement of 236,000 is OCI under this election and is not added to the profit-or-loss amount.

title: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset • case 58
prompt: A loan is sold with full derecognition. Immediately before sale, gross carrying amount is LKR 2,160,000, loss allowance 216,000, and cash proceeds 2,052,000. No accumulated OCI, sale fees or other adjustments exist. Find the derecognition GAIN relative to net carrying amount.
explanation: Net carrying amount = 2,160,000 − 216,000 = 1,944,000. Compare proceeds with that net amount: 2,052,000 − 1,944,000 = 108,000.00 gain. Derecognise both the gross asset and related allowance.
family: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset

title: Non-substantial liability modification gain • case 58
prompt: An amortised-cost liability is modified WITHOUT extinguishment, with no fees. Its carrying amount is LKR 1,580,000. The sole revised payment is 1,817,000 in two years. Original EIR is 10%; the modification is assessed as non-substantial. Find the immediate modification GAIN from recalculating amortised cost at the original EIR.
explanation: Revised amortised cost = 1,817,000/1.10² = 1,501,652.89. Gain = old liability 1,580,000 − revised PV = 78,347.11. The original EIR is retained for this non-extinguishing modification.

title: Credit-risk improvement allowance release • case 58
prompt: A debt asset under the GENERAL ECL model previously had significant credit-risk deterioration and lifetime allowance LKR 216,000. At reporting date the criteria for lifetime ECL are no longer met; required 12-month ECL is 39,000. No write-offs, new assets or other allowance movements occur. Find the impairment reversal in profit or loss.
explanation: When lifetime measurement is no longer required, the general model returns to 12-month ECL. Release the excess allowance: 216,000 − 39,000 = 177,000.00. This is not a receivable under mandatory simplified lifetime ECL.

title: Upstream inventory elimination with tax • case 58
prompt: P and S report profits AFTER their own tax of LKR 4,320,000 and 1,960,000. An upstream inventory sale leaves unrealised profit of 432,000 in group closing inventory. A recoverable DTA is recognised on the full elimination at 30%, with the tax effect in profit or loss. No other consolidation adjustments exist. Find TOTAL consolidated profit, before attribution to owners and NCI.
explanation: Combine separate after-tax profits, eliminate unrealised profit and recognise the recoverable tax benefit: 4,320,000 + 1,960,000 − 432,000 + 129,600.00 = 5,977,600.00. This question asks total group profit, not its attribution.

title: Full-goodwill impairment and owner profit • case 58
prompt: P owns 80% of S all year. Separate after-tax profits are P LKR 3,540,000 and S 1,280,000. Goodwill is recognised on the FULL-goodwill basis and an impairment of 490,000 is attributable to S’s CGU and allocated 80:20 between owners and NCI. No other adjustments or tax effects apply. Find consolidated profit attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Owners receive 80% of S’s profit and bear 80% of the full-goodwill loss: 3,540,000 + 80% × (1,280,000 − 490,000) = 4,172,000.00. Do not charge the owners with 100% of this full-goodwill loss.

title: Partial goodwill CGU gross-up • case 58
prompt: P owns 80% of S. Recognised PARTIAL goodwill is LKR 1,728,000; S’s other net assets in the tested CGU carry at 8,640,000. Recoverable amount of the WHOLE CGU is 9,720,000. Gross up goodwill for unrecognised NCI goodwill when testing; the whole impairment falls within grossed-up goodwill. No tax or other adjustments apply. Find impairment actually recognised on group goodwill.
explanation: Grossed-up goodwill = 1,728,000/80% = 2,160,000.00. Whole-CGU impairment = grossed goodwill + other net assets − recoverable amount = 1,080,000.00. Only the parent’s 80% goodwill portion is recognised, so recorded loss = 864,000.00.
reference: LKAS 36 Appendix C paras C4–C8; SLFRS 10 para B86

title: Consolidated retained earnings bridge • case 58
prompt: P owns 75% of S. At year end P retained earnings are LKR 5,900,000, and S retained earnings 3,740,000. S retained earnings at acquisition were 1,000,000. Cumulative post-acquisition extra FV depreciation is 216,000. A downstream sale by P leaves unrealised profit of 138,000. No tax, goodwill impairment, dividends recognised by P, OCI or other adjustments apply. Find consolidated retained earnings attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Group owners’ retained earnings = parent RE + 75% of adjusted post-acquisition S reserves − the parent’s downstream unrealised profit: 7,655,000.00. Pre-acquisition reserves do not enter post-acquisition group retained earnings.

title: Loss of control and translation reserve • case 58
prompt: P loses control of a foreign subsidiary. Proceeds are LKR 4,520,000; retained interest FV 1,080,000; NCI carrying amount 590,000; consolidated net assets INCLUDING goodwill 4,340,000. A cumulative translation GAIN of 216,000, entirely attributable to P, must be reclassified to profit or loss on loss of control. No other effects apply. Find total disposal gain including that reclassification.
explanation: Base gain = proceeds + retained FV + NCI − net assets = 1,850,000.00. Add the parent’s translation gain recycled on disposal: 216,000. Total = 2,066,000.00.
family: Loss of control and translation reserve

title: Residual guarantee expected payment • case 58
prompt: A lessee owes three year-end rentals of LKR 490,000. It guarantees residual value up to 200,000, but the amount EXPECTED to be payable under that guarantee is 88,000 at year three. Discount rate is 10%. No other liability payments exist. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the amount expected to be payable, not automatically the maximum guarantee. Liability = PV of three rentals + 88,000/1.10³ = 1,284,673.18.

title: Reasonably certain purchase option PV • case 58
prompt: A lease requires three year-end rentals of LKR 440,000, plus a purchase option price of 1,080,000 payable at year three. Exercise is reasonably certain. Discount rate is 10%. No incentives, other payments or initial prepayments apply. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the reasonably certain purchase price in the liability: PV of rentals + purchase price discounted for three years = 1,905,634.86. Do not omit or leave the future option payment undiscounted.

title: Lease and service component allocation • case 58
prompt: A two-year contract requires bundled payments of LKR 540,000 at each year end. Relative stand-alone prices are equipment lease 200,000 and distinct maintenance 50,000 per year. The lessee does NOT elect to combine components. Lease discount rate is 10%; no other payments exist. Find initial lease liability for the LEASE component only.
explanation: Allocate 200,000/250,000 = 80% of each bundled payment to the lease: 432,000.00. Discount those two lease payments, excluding maintenance, to obtain 749,752.07.

title: Exempt short-term lease rent-free start • case 58
prompt: A twelve-month lease with no purchase option qualifies for the elected short-term exemption. The first three months are rent free, then nine monthly payments of LKR 49,000 are due. The asset is available throughout and straight-line expense is appropriate. Find lease expense for the FIRST six months, ignoring accrual settlement timing.
explanation: Total fixed payments are nine rents. Spread evenly over all twelve months: 49,000 × 9/12 × 6 = 220,500.00. Rent-free months still receive an expense allocation.

title: Sale-and-leaseback rights transferred • case 58
prompt: A transfer qualifies as a sale under SLFRS 15 at fair value LKR 21,600,000; asset carrying amount is 11,800,000. Market-rate leaseback payments have PV 8,640,000. There are no off-market adjustments or variable-payment complications. At inception, what sale gain is recognised for rights TRANSFERRED to the buyer-lessor?
explanation: Total gain = 21,600,000 − 11,800,000 = 9,800,000. Retained-use proportion = lease PV / fair value = 40%. Recognise only the transferred-rights proportion of the gain: 5,880,000.00.

title: Reassessed bargain purchase gain • case 58
prompt: After the required reassessment, final acquisition-date consideration is LKR 4,320,000, NCI fair value is 400,000 and identifiable net assets are 6,480,000. There is no prior holding or other adjustment. Find the bargain purchase gain recognised in profit or loss.
explanation: Net identifiable assets exceed consideration plus NCI: 6,480,000 − 4,320,000 − 400,000 = 1,760,000.00. Reassessment has been completed before recognising the gain.

title: Acquired contingent liability in goodwill • case 58
prompt: Consideration is LKR 6,400,000; NCI FV is 500,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired contingent liability are 4,740,000. The acquired item is a present obligation with reliably measurable FV 490,000 and qualifies for recognition despite non-probable outflow. No tax or other adjustment applies. Find goodwill after recognising it.
explanation: Recognise the qualifying acquired liability: net identifiable assets become 4,740,000 − 490,000. Goodwill = consideration + NCI − adjusted net assets = 2,650,000.00.

title: Separate acquired brand from goodwill • case 58
prompt: Consideration is LKR 5,900,000; NCI FV 600,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired separable brand are 4,920,000. Brand FV is 980,000; tax base is zero and 30% DTL must be recognised. No other adjustments apply. Find goodwill after separate brand and tax recognition.
explanation: An identifiable acquired brand is separate from goodwill. Net addition to identifiable assets = brand FV − 30% DTL = 686,000.00. Goodwill = 5,900,000 + 600,000 − (4,920,000 + 686,000.00) = 894,000.00.

title: Acquisition costs versus issue costs • case 58
prompt: A business acquisition has consideration LKR 3,740,000. Additional costs are acquisition advisory 216,000, qualifying equity-issue costs 70,000 and qualifying debt-issue costs 40,000. The issue costs follow their relevant standards, and no immediate debt-cost amortisation or other expense arises this period. Find the immediate acquisition-related PROFIT-OR-LOSS expense from these costs.
explanation: Expense advisory acquisition costs of 216,000.00. Qualifying equity and debt issuance costs follow their respective standards and are not added to this immediate acquisition-service expense or goodwill.

title: Temporary difference and enacted rate change • case 58
prompt: A taxable temporary difference opens at LKR 200,000 with a DTL measured at 25%. At year end the difference is 590,000 and the enacted rate expected on reversal is 30%. Both the underlying movements and rate change belong in profit or loss. No other tax movements exist. Find deferred tax expense for the year.
explanation: Opening DTL = 200,000×25% = 50,000. Closing DTL = 590,000×30% = 177,000.00. Expense is the full increase, including rate remeasurement: 127,000.00. Rates are exercise assumptions.
family: Temporary difference and enacted rate change

title: Revalued non-depreciable land tax basis • case 58
prompt: Non-depreciable land is revalued from cost LKR 2,160,000 to fair value 3,240,000; tax base remains cost. The enacted rate for recovery through SALE is 20%, while a 30% use rate would otherwise apply. The revaluation and associated tax go to OCI. No other effects exist. Find the net OCI revaluation increase after deferred tax.
explanation: For this non-depreciable revalued asset, measure tax consequences on recovery through sale: DTL = (3,240,000 − 2,160,000)×20%. Net OCI increase = gross uplift less that DTL = 864,000.00.

title: Current tax reconciliation and prepayment • case 58
prompt: Accounting pretax profit is LKR 4,900,000. It includes a permanently non-deductible fine of 216,000, exempt income of 50,000, and warranty expense of 490,000 deductible only on payment. Current-year warranty payments of 80,000 are deductible and were charged against the provision, not current profit. Tax rate is 30%; tax prepayments are 300,000. No other tax adjustments exist. Find closing CURRENT tax payable, not total tax expense.
explanation: Taxable profit = 4,900,000 + fine 216,000 − exempt income 50,000 + provision expense 490,000 − deductible payments 80,000 = 5,476,000. Current tax less prepaid 300,000 = 1,342,800.00. Deferred tax is separate.

title: Consolidated inventory tax difference • case 58
prompt: After eliminating an intragroup profit, inventory carries in consolidated statements at LKR 1,296,000. Its tax base in the buyer’s tax jurisdiction is 1,944,000. The buyer’s enacted rate is 30%; sufficient taxable profit is probable. No offsetting, exception or other tax effects apply. Find the consolidated DTA on this inventory.
explanation: The consolidated carrying amount is below tax base, creating a deductible temporary difference of 648,000. Use the buyer’s relevant tax rate: difference ×30% = 194,400.00.

title: Depreciation after recognised impairment • case 58
prompt: Immediately before an impairment, equipment carries at LKR 2,160,000. Recoverable amount is 1,280,000 and impairment is recognised. After that date it has four years’ remaining useful life and residual value 100,000. Straight-line depreciation is appropriate; no further revaluation or impairment applies. Find depreciation for the next FULL year.
explanation: First reduce the asset to recoverable amount 1,280,000. Thereafter allocate revised depreciable amount over remaining life: (1,280,000 − 100,000)/4 = 295,000.00.

title: Allocated headquarters in CGU impairment • case 58
prompt: CGU A carries operating assets of LKR 1,180,000; CGU B carries 400,000. A headquarters asset of 200,000 can be allocated reasonably and consistently in proportion to those operating-asset amounts. A’s recoverable amount INCLUDING its headquarters share is 940,000. No goodwill or other assets exist. Find the impairment loss for A including its allocation.
explanation: Allocate headquarters to A: 200,000 × 1,180,000/(1,180,000+400,000) = 149,367.09. Tested A carrying amount is 1,329,367.09. Impairment versus recoverable amount 940,000 = 389,367.09.

title: Break-even value-in-use cash flow • case 58
prompt: An asset carries at LKR 2,160,000. Its fair value less costs of disposal is lower. A valid VIU model uses THREE equal year-end operating cash inflows, plus 100,000 net disposal proceeds at year three, discounted at 10%. explanation: Let annual flow be X. X×(1/1.10 + 1/1.10² + 1/1.10³) + 100,000/1.10³ = 2,160,000. Solve for X = 838,356.50. This sensitivity calculation identifies the VIU break-even point.

title: Discounted warranty expected-value portfolio • case 58
prompt: A present warranty obligation covers 2,160 products. Per product, probabilities are 70% no defect, 25% a minor repair costing LKR 400, and 5% a major repair costing 2,000. All expected payments occur exactly in TWO years. Outflow for the portfolio is probable; appropriate discount rate is 10% with no risk double counting. Find the provision.
explanation: Expected cash payment = 2,160×(25%×400 + 5%×2,000) = 432,000.0. Discount two years at 10%: 432,000.0/1.10² = 357,024.79. The probability assessment applies to the portfolio.

title: Provision movement with revised estimate • case 58
prompt: A discounted provision opens at LKR 1,080,000. Unwinding for a full year is at 8%. A 100,000 settlement occurs at the year END, after unwinding. At that same reporting date, a new estimate increases the remaining provision by 166,000. No other changes occur. Find closing provision.
explanation: Closing = opening + 8% unwinding − year-end settlement + estimate increase: 1,080,000×1.08 −100,000 +166,000 = 1,232,400.00. Classification of the estimate change’s counterpart is assessed separately.

title: Revaluation increase after earlier loss • case 58
prompt: PPE carries at LKR 1,180,000 before revaluation and is revalued to 2,160,000. A prior revaluation decrease on THIS asset of 266,000 was recognised in profit or loss and has not been reversed. No tax effects apply. Find the current increase recognised in OCI after reversing the eligible prior loss in profit or loss.
explanation: Gross increase = 2,160,000 − 1,180,000 = 980,000. First recognise 266,000 in profit or loss to reverse the prior decrease. Remaining 714,000.00 is OCI revaluation surplus.

title: Nine-month depreciation and disposal gain • case 58
prompt: Equipment cost LKR 2,360,000, residual value 200,000 and useful life five years, straight-line. Two FULL years’ depreciation were recognised before this year. It is sold after nine months of the current year for 1,720,000. It was not previously held for sale and no impairment or revaluation applies. Find disposal GAIN after the required nine-month depreciation.
