prompt: A finite-life production licence costs LKR 2,120,000, has zero residual value, and is expected to support 150,000 units in total. Actual output this year is 60,500 units. A units-of-production method reliably reflects consumption and the asset was available throughout. No impairment or estimate change applies. Find annual amortisation.
explanation: Apply the supported consumption pattern: amortisation = 2,120,000 × 60,500/150,000 = 855,066.67. It is the share of expected lifetime production consumed, not an automatic straight-line charge.

title: Profit after suspended associate losses • case 61
prompt: An equity-method investment and relevant long-term interests were previously reduced to zero. Unrecognised share of prior losses totals LKR 202,000; the investor has no obligation and made no support payments. In the current year its share of associate profit is 303,000. No other adjustments or changes in interest apply. Find the share of profit that can now be RECOGNISED.
explanation: First absorb unrecognised prior losses before resuming recognised profit. Recognised amount = current profit share 303,000 − prior unrecognised losses 202,000 = 101,000.00.

title: Return recovery asset net of costs • case 62
prompt: A retailer has transferred 2,550 products. It expects 102 to be returned. Each returned product originally cost LKR 600; expected recovery handling is 20 per item and expected value deterioration is 30 per item. Estimates meet the relevant requirements. Find the separate asset for the right to recover returned products, excluding the refund liability.
explanation: Recovery asset = original carrying amount of expected returns less recovery costs and potential value decrease: 102 × (600 − 20 − 30) = 56,100.00. It is assessed separately from the customer refund liability.
family: Return recovery asset net of costs

title: Retrospective volume rebate true-up • case 62
prompt: A customer’s annual purchases reach 16,200 units at list price LKR 200. Crossing the threshold entitles it to a 5% retrospective rebate on ALL units. Cumulative revenue before this new supported estimate equals full list price; no rebate was previously accrued. The constraint permits the estimate. Find the reduction in cumulative revenue required now.
explanation: The revised transaction price reflects the retrospective rebate on all units. Revenue reduction = 16,200 × 200 × 5% = 162,000.00. Recognise the corresponding refund obligation as appropriate.

title: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation • case 62
prompt: A bundle has distinct goods A and B with stand-alone prices LKR 510,000 and 920,000. Total transaction price is 1,318,000. ALL paragraph 82 criteria demonstrate that the whole 112,000 discount relates only to A. A transfers now; B is not yet delivered. Find revenue recognised for A.
explanation: The specified discount-allocation exception applies. Allocate all 112,000 discount to A: 510,000 − 112,000 = 398,000.00. Do not default to relative allocation when the exception’s criteria are met.
family: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation

title: Three obligations and partial service • case 62
prompt: A contract price of LKR 3,060,000 covers goods A, goods B and twelve months of distinct support. Stand-alone prices are 600,000, 300,000 and 300,000 respectively. A is delivered, B is not, and six months of evenly provided support are complete. No allocation exception applies. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise allocation to A plus half of support: 3,060,000 × (600,000 + 150,000) / 1,200,000 = 1,912,500.00. B’s allocation remains unrecognised as revenue.

title: Progress excluding abnormal waste • case 62
prompt: An over-time contract has transaction price LKR 16,200,000. Costs incurred are 6,480,000, including abnormal waste of 324,000 that does not depict progress. Expected TOTAL productive costs excluding that waste are 12,960,000. Cost-to-cost is appropriate after excluding the waste; no other adjustment applies. Find cumulative revenue, not profit.
explanation: Exclude abnormal waste from the progress numerator. Productive progress = (6,480,000 − 324,000) / 12,960,000. Revenue = transaction price × that progress = 7,695,000.00. The wasted cost is not a revenue-producing input.

title: Uninstalled materials without margin • case 62
prompt: A single over-time construction obligation has price LKR 22,400,000. All B19(b) conditions justify recognising revenue equal to cost for significant uninstalled materials of 4,480,000 already controlled by the customer. Other productive costs incurred are 3,360,000; expected total OTHER costs are 13,440,000. No revenue was previously recognised. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise material revenue without margin: 4,480,000. Recognise the remaining price using other-cost progress: (22,400,000 − 4,480,000) × 3,360,000/13,440,000. Total revenue = 8,960,000.00.

title: Agent commission after collection • case 62
prompt: An intermediary is an AGENT and collects customer cash of LKR 4,100,000 for a completed supplier service. It must remit 88% to the supplier and is entitled to the remaining 12% commission. It controls neither the underlying service nor any distinct extra service, and there is no tax. Find its revenue.
explanation: An agent recognises its fee or commission, not the supplier’s gross billings: 4,100,000 × 12% = 492,000.00. The amount due to the supplier is separately accounted for.

title: Distinct remaining goods blended prospectively • case 62
prompt: At modification, 100 distinct goods remain under an existing contract at LKR 1,620 each. Another 50 distinct goods are added at 1,296 each. The modification is NOT a separate contract, but remaining goods are distinct from those already transferred, so paragraph 21(a) applies prospectively. Thirty of the remaining goods are then transferred. Find revenue for those thirty.
explanation: Prospective remaining consideration = 100 × 1,620 + 50 × 1,296. Divide by 150 remaining goods, then multiply by 30 = 45,360.00. Do not retrospectively revise revenue on goods already transferred.

title: FVTPL acquisition expense • case 62
prompt: A financial asset is acquired at fair value LKR 2,040,000 and is classified at FVTPL. Directly attributable broker costs are 51,000, paid separately. No fair-value change occurs immediately after purchase. Find the immediate profit-or-loss expense from acquiring this asset.
explanation: Transaction costs on an FVTPL asset are expensed. Initial asset carrying amount is fair value 2,040,000; immediate acquisition expense is 51,000.00.

title: Collateral cash-shortfall discounting • case 62
prompt: A credit loss scenario has a contractual receipt of LKR 2,550,000 due in one year. The ONLY expected recovery at that same date is collateral sale proceeds of 1,630,000, less sale costs of 112,000. Scenario probability is 100% and original EIR is 10%. Collateral is an integral contractual credit enhancement and not separately recognised. Find discounted ECL.
explanation: One-year shortfall = contractual receipt − net collateral recovery = 2,550,000 − (1,630,000 − 112,000). Discount that shortfall at 10%: 938,181.82. Do not ignore recovery costs or discount only one side of same-date cash flows.

title: Three-band provision matrix • case 62
prompt: Under the simplified lifetime-ECL approach, supported adjusted loss rates are 1% on current receivables of LKR 2,240,000, 5% on past-due balances of 610,000, and 30% on severely overdue balances of 224,000. Rates already include all required forward-looking and discounting effects. Find total loss allowance.
explanation: Apply each appropriate band rate and add: 2,240,000×1% + 610,000×5% + 224,000×30% = 120,100.00. Do not apply one blended band mechanically to all balances.

title: Equity FVOCI profit-or-loss dividend • case 62
prompt: An eligible equity investment has the irrevocable FVOCI election. During the year it gains LKR 244,000 in fair value and earns a dividend of 122,000. Dividend recognition criteria are met and the dividend clearly represents a return on investment, not recovery of cost. There are no other effects. Find income recognised in PROFIT OR LOSS.
explanation: The qualifying dividend of 122,000.00 is profit-or-loss income. The fair-value movement of 244,000 is OCI under this election and is not added to the profit-or-loss amount.

title: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset • case 62
prompt: A loan is sold with full derecognition. Immediately before sale, gross carrying amount is LKR 2,240,000, loss allowance 224,000, and cash proceeds 2,128,000. No accumulated OCI, sale fees or other adjustments exist. Find the derecognition GAIN relative to net carrying amount.
explanation: Net carrying amount = 2,240,000 − 224,000 = 2,016,000. Compare proceeds with that net amount: 2,128,000 − 2,016,000 = 112,000.00 gain. Derecognise both the gross asset and related allowance.
family: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset

title: Non-substantial liability modification gain • case 62
prompt: An amortised-cost liability is modified WITHOUT extinguishment, with no fees. Its carrying amount is LKR 1,620,000. The sole revised payment is 1,863,000 in two years. Original EIR is 10%; the modification is assessed as non-substantial. Find the immediate modification GAIN from recalculating amortised cost at the original EIR.
explanation: Revised amortised cost = 1,863,000/1.10² = 1,539,669.42. Gain = old liability 1,620,000 − revised PV = 80,330.58. The original EIR is retained for this non-extinguishing modification.

title: Credit-risk improvement allowance release • case 62
prompt: A debt asset under the GENERAL ECL model previously had significant credit-risk deterioration and lifetime allowance LKR 224,000. At reporting date the criteria for lifetime ECL are no longer met; required 12-month ECL is 41,000. No write-offs, new assets or other allowance movements occur. Find the impairment reversal in profit or loss.
explanation: When lifetime measurement is no longer required, the general model returns to 12-month ECL. Release the excess allowance: 224,000 − 41,000 = 183,000.00. This is not a receivable under mandatory simplified lifetime ECL.

title: Upstream inventory elimination with tax • case 62
prompt: P and S report profits AFTER their own tax of LKR 4,480,000 and 2,040,000. An upstream inventory sale leaves unrealised profit of 448,000 in group closing inventory. A recoverable DTA is recognised on the full elimination at 30%, with the tax effect in profit or loss. No other consolidation adjustments exist. Find TOTAL consolidated profit, before attribution to owners and NCI.
explanation: Combine separate after-tax profits, eliminate unrealised profit and recognise the recoverable tax benefit: 4,480,000 + 2,040,000 − 448,000 + 134,400.00 = 6,206,400.00. This question asks total group profit, not its attribution.

title: Full-goodwill impairment and owner profit • case 62
prompt: P owns 80% of S all year. Separate after-tax profits are P LKR 3,660,000 and S 1,320,000. Goodwill is recognised on the FULL-goodwill basis and an impairment of 510,000 is attributable to S’s CGU and allocated 80:20 between owners and NCI. No other adjustments or tax effects apply. Find consolidated profit attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Owners receive 80% of S’s profit and bear 80% of the full-goodwill loss: 3,660,000 + 80% × (1,320,000 − 510,000) = 4,308,000.00. Do not charge the owners with 100% of this full-goodwill loss.

title: Partial goodwill CGU gross-up • case 62
prompt: P owns 80% of S. Recognised PARTIAL goodwill is LKR 1,792,000; S’s other net assets in the tested CGU carry at 8,960,000. Recoverable amount of the WHOLE CGU is 10,080,000. Gross up goodwill for unrecognised NCI goodwill when testing; the whole impairment falls within grossed-up goodwill. No tax or other adjustments apply. Find impairment actually recognised on group goodwill.
explanation: Grossed-up goodwill = 1,792,000/80% = 2,240,000.00. Whole-CGU impairment = grossed goodwill + other net assets − recoverable amount = 1,120,000.00. Only the parent’s 80% goodwill portion is recognised, so recorded loss = 896,000.00.
reference: LKAS 36 Appendix C paras C4–C8; SLFRS 10 para B86

title: Consolidated retained earnings bridge • case 62
prompt: P owns 75% of S. At year end P retained earnings are LKR 6,100,000, and S retained earnings 3,860,000. S retained earnings at acquisition were 1,000,000. Cumulative post-acquisition extra FV depreciation is 224,000. A downstream sale by P leaves unrealised profit of 142,000. No tax, goodwill impairment, dividends recognised by P, OCI or other adjustments apply. Find consolidated retained earnings attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Group owners’ retained earnings = parent RE + 75% of adjusted post-acquisition S reserves − the parent’s downstream unrealised profit: 7,935,000.00. Pre-acquisition reserves do not enter post-acquisition group retained earnings.

title: Loss of control and translation reserve • case 62
prompt: P loses control of a foreign subsidiary. Proceeds are LKR 4,680,000; retained interest FV 1,120,000; NCI carrying amount 610,000; consolidated net assets INCLUDING goodwill 4,460,000. A cumulative translation GAIN of 224,000, entirely attributable to P, must be reclassified to profit or loss on loss of control. No other effects apply. Find total disposal gain including that reclassification.
explanation: Base gain = proceeds + retained FV + NCI − net assets = 1,950,000.00. Add the parent’s translation gain recycled on disposal: 224,000. Total = 2,174,000.00.
family: Loss of control and translation reserve

title: Residual guarantee expected payment • case 62
prompt: A lessee owes three year-end rentals of LKR 510,000. It guarantees residual value up to 200,000, but the amount EXPECTED to be payable under that guarantee is 92,000 at year three. Discount rate is 10%. No other liability payments exist. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the amount expected to be payable, not automatically the maximum guarantee. Liability = PV of three rentals + 92,000/1.10³ = 1,337,415.48.

title: Reasonably certain purchase option PV • case 62
prompt: A lease requires three year-end rentals of LKR 460,000, plus a purchase option price of 1,120,000 payable at year three. Exercise is reasonably certain. Discount rate is 10%. No incentives, other payments or initial prepayments apply. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the reasonably certain purchase price in the liability: PV of rentals + purchase price discounted for three years = 1,985,424.49. Do not omit or leave the future option payment undiscounted.

title: Lease and service component allocation • case 62
prompt: A two-year contract requires bundled payments of LKR 560,000 at each year end. Relative stand-alone prices are equipment lease 200,000 and distinct maintenance 50,000 per year. The lessee does NOT elect to combine components. Lease discount rate is 10%; no other payments exist. Find initial lease liability for the LEASE component only.
explanation: Allocate 200,000/250,000 = 80% of each bundled payment to the lease: 448,000.00. Discount those two lease payments, excluding maintenance, to obtain 777,520.66.

title: Exempt short-term lease rent-free start • case 62
prompt: A twelve-month lease with no purchase option qualifies for the elected short-term exemption. The first three months are rent free, then nine monthly payments of LKR 51,000 are due. The asset is available throughout and straight-line expense is appropriate. Find lease expense for the FIRST six months, ignoring accrual settlement timing.
explanation: Total fixed payments are nine rents. Spread evenly over all twelve months: 51,000 × 9/12 × 6 = 229,500.00. Rent-free months still receive an expense allocation.

title: Sale-and-leaseback rights transferred • case 62
prompt: A transfer qualifies as a sale under SLFRS 15 at fair value LKR 22,400,000; asset carrying amount is 12,200,000. Market-rate leaseback payments have PV 8,960,000. There are no off-market adjustments or variable-payment complications. At inception, what sale gain is recognised for rights TRANSFERRED to the buyer-lessor?
explanation: Total gain = 22,400,000 − 12,200,000 = 10,200,000. Retained-use proportion = lease PV / fair value = 40%. Recognise only the transferred-rights proportion of the gain: 6,120,000.00.

title: Reassessed bargain purchase gain • case 62
prompt: After the required reassessment, final acquisition-date consideration is LKR 4,480,000, NCI fair value is 400,000 and identifiable net assets are 6,720,000. There is no prior holding or other adjustment. Find the bargain purchase gain recognised in profit or loss.
explanation: Net identifiable assets exceed consideration plus NCI: 6,720,000 − 4,480,000 − 400,000 = 1,840,000.00. Reassessment has been completed before recognising the gain.

title: Acquired contingent liability in goodwill • case 62
prompt: Consideration is LKR 6,600,000; NCI FV is 500,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired contingent liability are 4,860,000. The acquired item is a present obligation with reliably measurable FV 510,000 and qualifies for recognition despite non-probable outflow. No tax or other adjustment applies. Find goodwill after recognising it.
explanation: Recognise the qualifying acquired liability: net identifiable assets become 4,860,000 − 510,000. Goodwill = consideration + NCI − adjusted net assets = 2,750,000.00.

title: Separate acquired brand from goodwill • case 62
prompt: Consideration is LKR 6,100,000; NCI FV 600,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired separable brand are 5,080,000. Brand FV is 1,020,000; tax base is zero and 30% DTL must be recognised. No other adjustments apply. Find goodwill after separate brand and tax recognition.
explanation: An identifiable acquired brand is separate from goodwill. Net addition to identifiable assets = brand FV − 30% DTL = 714,000.00. Goodwill = 6,100,000 + 600,000 − (5,080,000 + 714,000.00) = 906,000.00.

title: Acquisition costs versus issue costs • case 62
prompt: A business acquisition has consideration LKR 3,860,000. Additional costs are acquisition advisory 224,000, qualifying equity-issue costs 70,000 and qualifying debt-issue costs 40,000. The issue costs follow their relevant standards, and no immediate debt-cost amortisation or other expense arises this period. Find the immediate acquisition-related PROFIT-OR-LOSS expense from these costs.
explanation: Expense advisory acquisition costs of 224,000.00. Qualifying equity and debt issuance costs follow their respective standards and are not added to this immediate acquisition-service expense or goodwill.

title: Temporary difference and enacted rate change • case 62
prompt: A taxable temporary difference opens at LKR 200,000 with a DTL measured at 25%. At year end the difference is 610,000 and the enacted rate expected on reversal is 30%. Both the underlying movements and rate change belong in profit or loss. No other tax movements exist. Find deferred tax expense for the year.
explanation: Opening DTL = 200,000×25% = 50,000. Closing DTL = 610,000×30% = 183,000.00. Expense is the full increase, including rate remeasurement: 133,000.00. Rates are exercise assumptions.
family: Temporary difference and enacted rate change

title: Revalued non-depreciable land tax basis • case 62
prompt: Non-depreciable land is revalued from cost LKR 2,240,000 to fair value 3,360,000; tax base remains cost. The enacted rate for recovery through SALE is 20%, while a 30% use rate would otherwise apply. The revaluation and associated tax go to OCI. No other effects exist. Find the net OCI revaluation increase after deferred tax.
explanation: For this non-depreciable revalued asset, measure tax consequences on recovery through sale: DTL = (3,360,000 − 2,240,000)×20%. Net OCI increase = gross uplift less that DTL = 896,000.00.

title: Current tax reconciliation and prepayment • case 62
prompt: Accounting pretax profit is LKR 5,100,000. It includes a permanently non-deductible fine of 224,000, exempt income of 50,000, and warranty expense of 510,000 deductible only on payment. Current-year warranty payments of 80,000 are deductible and were charged against the provision, not current profit. Tax rate is 30%; tax prepayments are 300,000. No other tax adjustments exist. Find closing CURRENT tax payable, not total tax expense.
explanation: Taxable profit = 5,100,000 + fine 224,000 − exempt income 50,000 + provision expense 510,000 − deductible payments 80,000 = 5,704,000. Current tax less prepaid 300,000 = 1,411,200.00. Deferred tax is separate.

title: Consolidated inventory tax difference • case 62
prompt: After eliminating an intragroup profit, inventory carries in consolidated statements at LKR 1,344,000. Its tax base in the buyer’s tax jurisdiction is 2,016,000. The buyer’s enacted rate is 30%; sufficient taxable profit is probable. No offsetting, exception or other tax effects apply. Find the consolidated DTA on this inventory.
explanation: The consolidated carrying amount is below tax base, creating a deductible temporary difference of 672,000. Use the buyer’s relevant tax rate: difference ×30% = 201,600.00.

title: Depreciation after recognised impairment • case 62
prompt: Immediately before an impairment, equipment carries at LKR 2,240,000. Recoverable amount is 1,320,000 and impairment is recognised. After that date it has four years’ remaining useful life and residual value 100,000. Straight-line depreciation is appropriate; no further revaluation or impairment applies. Find depreciation for the next FULL year.
explanation: First reduce the asset to recoverable amount 1,320,000. Thereafter allocate revised depreciable amount over remaining life: (1,320,000 − 100,000)/4 = 305,000.00.

title: Allocated headquarters in CGU impairment • case 62
prompt: CGU A carries operating assets of LKR 1,220,000; CGU B carries 400,000. A headquarters asset of 200,000 can be allocated reasonably and consistently in proportion to those operating-asset amounts. A’s recoverable amount INCLUDING its headquarters share is 960,000. No goodwill or other assets exist. Find the impairment loss for A including its allocation.
explanation: Allocate headquarters to A: 200,000 × 1,220,000/(1,220,000+400,000) = 150,617.28. Tested A carrying amount is 1,370,617.28. Impairment versus recoverable amount 960,000 = 410,617.28.

title: Break-even value-in-use cash flow • case 62
prompt: An asset carries at LKR 2,240,000. Its fair value less costs of disposal is lower. A valid VIU model uses THREE equal year-end operating cash inflows, plus 100,000 net disposal proceeds at year three, discounted at 10%. What minimum equal ANNUAL operating cash inflow makes VIU exactly equal carrying amount? Ignore tax and other adjustments.
explanation: Let annual flow be X. X×(1/1.10 + 1/1.10² + 1/1.10³) + 100,000/1.10³ = 2,240,000. Solve for X = 870,525.68. This sensitivity calculation identifies the VIU break-even point.

title: Discounted warranty expected-value portfolio • case 62
prompt: A present warranty obligation covers 2,240 products. Per product, probabilities are 70% no defect, 25% a minor repair costing LKR 400, and 5% a major repair costing 2,000. All expected payments occur exactly in TWO years. Outflow for the portfolio is probable; appropriate discount rate is 10% with no risk double counting. Find the provision.
explanation: Expected cash payment = 2,240×(25%×400 + 5%×2,000) = 448,000.0. Discount two years at 10%: 448,000.0/1.10² = 370,247.93. The probability assessment applies to the portfolio.

title: Provision movement with revised estimate • case 62
prompt: A discounted provision opens at LKR 1,120,000. Unwinding for a full year is at 8%. A 100,000 settlement occurs at the year END, after unwinding. At that same reporting date, a new estimate increases the remaining provision by 174,000. No other changes occur. Find closing provision.
explanation: Closing = opening + 8% unwinding − year-end settlement + estimate increase: 1,120,000×1.08 −100,000 +174,000 = 1,283,600.00. Classification of the estimate change’s counterpart is assessed separately.

title: Revaluation increase after earlier loss • case 62
prompt: PPE carries at LKR 1,220,000 before revaluation and is revalued to 2,240,000. A prior revaluation decrease on THIS asset of 274,000 was recognised in profit or loss and has not been reversed. No tax effects apply. Find the current increase recognised in OCI after reversing the eligible prior loss in profit or loss.
explanation: Gross increase = 2,240,000 − 1,220,000 = 1,020,000. First recognise 274,000 in profit or loss to reverse the prior decrease. Remaining 746,000.00 is OCI revaluation surplus.

title: Nine-month depreciation and disposal gain • case 62
prompt: Equipment cost LKR 2,440,000, residual value 200,000 and useful life five years, straight-line. Two FULL years’ depreciation were recognised before this year. It is sold after nine months of the current year for 1,780,000. It was not previously held for sale and no impairment or revaluation applies. Find disposal GAIN after the required nine-month depreciation.
explanation: Annual depreciation = (2,440,000−200,000)/5. Deduct two full years and another 9/12 year from cost to obtain disposal-date carrying amount 1,208,000.00. Gain = proceeds − that amount = 572,000.00.

title: Customer collections with a write-off • case 62
prompt: All sales are on credit. Revenue is LKR 6,100,000; opening GROSS trade receivables are 600,000; closing GROSS receivables are 1,420,000. Receivables of 162,000 were written off during the year. There are no taxes, returns, contract balances, acquisitions or exchange changes. Find cash collected from customers.
explanation: Gross receivable roll-forward: opening + credit sales − cash receipts − write-offs = closing. Thus receipts = 6,100,000+600,000−1,420,000−162,000 = 5,118,000.00. Write-offs are not cash receipts.

title: Loan funding net cash effect • case 62
prompt: A company receives cash loan proceeds of LKR 2,240,000 and immediately pays a directly attributable lender issue fee of 51,000. Both payments are classified as financing cash flows in this case. No other cash movement occurs. Find the NET financing cash inflow from these two cash movements; this question does not require net line-item presentation.
explanation: Net financing cash effect = proceeds − cash fee = 2,240,000 − 51,000.00 = 2,189,000.00. Effective-interest amortisation later is not another inception cash payment.

title: Item-by-item NRV without offsetting headroom • case 62
prompt: Two unrelated inventory lines require separate NRV tests. A has 410 units, cost LKR 1,000 and NRV 900 each. B has 224 units, cost 1,000 and NRV 1,200 each. There is no basis to group them for the write-down test. Find TOTAL closing inventory carrying amount.
explanation: Carry A at 900 per unit and B at its lower cost of 1,000. Total = 410×900 + 224×1,000 = 593,000.00. B’s NRV headroom cannot offset A’s write-down.

title: Units-of-production intangible amortisation • case 62
prompt: A finite-life production licence costs LKR 2,140,000, has zero residual value, and is expected to support 150,000 units in total. Actual output this year is 61,000 units. A units-of-production method reliably reflects consumption and the asset was available throughout. No impairment or estimate change applies. Find annual amortisation.
explanation: Apply the supported consumption pattern: amortisation = 2,140,000 × 61,000/150,000 = 870,266.67. It is the share of expected lifetime production consumed, not an automatic straight-line charge.

title: Profit after suspended associate losses • case 62
prompt: An equity-method investment and relevant long-term interests were previously reduced to zero. Unrecognised share of prior losses totals LKR 204,000; the investor has no obligation and made no support payments. In the current year its share of associate profit is 306,000. No other adjustments or changes in interest apply. Find the share of profit that can now be RECOGNISED.
explanation: First absorb unrecognised prior losses before resuming recognised profit. Recognised amount = current profit share 306,000 − prior unrecognised losses 204,000 = 102,000.00.

title: Return recovery asset net of costs • case 63
prompt: A retailer has transferred 2,575 products. It expects 103 to be returned. Each returned product originally cost LKR 600; expected recovery handling is 20 per item and expected value deterioration is 30 per item. Estimates meet the relevant requirements. Find the separate asset for the right to recover returned products, excluding the refund liability.
explanation: Recovery asset = original carrying amount of expected returns less recovery costs and potential value decrease: 103 × (600 − 20 − 30) = 56,650.00. It is assessed separately from the customer refund liability.
family: Return recovery asset net of costs

title: Retrospective volume rebate true-up • case 63
prompt: A customer’s annual purchases reach 16,300 units at list price LKR 200. Crossing the threshold entitles it to a 5% retrospective rebate on ALL units. Cumulative revenue before this new supported estimate equals full list price; no rebate was previously accrued. The constraint permits the estimate. Find the reduction in cumulative revenue required now.
explanation: The revised transaction price reflects the retrospective rebate on all units. Revenue reduction = 16,300 × 200 × 5% = 163,000.00. Recognise the corresponding refund obligation as appropriate.

title: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation • case 63
prompt: A bundle has distinct goods A and B with stand-alone prices LKR 515,000 and 930,000. Total transaction price is 1,332,000. ALL paragraph 82 criteria demonstrate that the whole 113,000 discount relates only to A. A transfers now; B is not yet delivered. Find revenue recognised for A.
explanation: The specified discount-allocation exception applies. Allocate all 113,000 discount to A: 515,000 − 113,000 = 402,000.00. Do not default to relative allocation when the exception’s criteria are met.
family: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation

title: Three obligations and partial service • case 63
prompt: A contract price of LKR 3,090,000 covers goods A, goods B and twelve months of distinct support. Stand-alone prices are 600,000, 300,000 and 300,000 respectively. A is delivered, B is not, and six months of evenly provided support are complete. No allocation exception applies. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise allocation to A plus half of support: 3,090,000 × (600,000 + 150,000) / 1,200,000 = 1,931,250.00. B’s allocation remains unrecognised as revenue.

title: Progress excluding abnormal waste • case 63
prompt: An over-time contract has transaction price LKR 16,300,000. Costs incurred are 6,520,000, including abnormal waste of 326,000 that does not depict progress. Expected TOTAL productive costs excluding that waste are 13,040,000. Cost-to-cost is appropriate after excluding the waste; no other adjustment applies. Find cumulative revenue, not profit.
explanation: Exclude abnormal waste from the progress numerator. Productive progress = (6,520,000 − 326,000) / 13,040,000. Revenue = transaction price × that progress = 7,742,500.00. The wasted cost is not a revenue-producing input.

title: Uninstalled materials without margin • case 63
prompt: A single over-time construction obligation has price LKR 22,600,000. All B19(b) conditions justify recognising revenue equal to cost for significant uninstalled materials of 4,520,000 already controlled by the customer. Other productive costs incurred are 3,390,000; expected total OTHER costs are 13,560,000. No revenue was previously recognised. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise material revenue without margin: 4,520,000. Recognise the remaining price using other-cost progress: (22,600,000 − 4,520,000) × 3,390,000/13,560,000. Total revenue = 9,040,000.00.

title: Agent commission after collection • case 63
prompt: An intermediary is an AGENT and collects customer cash of LKR 4,150,000 for a completed supplier service. It must remit 88% to the supplier and is entitled to the remaining 12% commission. It controls neither the underlying service nor any distinct extra service, and there is no tax. Find its revenue.
explanation: An agent recognises its fee or commission, not the supplier’s gross billings: 4,150,000 × 12% = 498,000.00. The amount due to the supplier is separately accounted for.

title: Distinct remaining goods blended prospectively • case 63
prompt: At modification, 100 distinct goods remain under an existing contract at LKR 1,630 each. Another 50 distinct goods are added at 1,304 each. The modification is NOT a separate contract, but remaining goods are distinct from those already transferred, so paragraph 21(a) applies prospectively. Thirty of the remaining goods are then transferred. Find revenue for those thirty.
explanation: Prospective remaining consideration = 100 × 1,630 + 50 × 1,304. Divide by 150 remaining goods, then multiply by 30 = 45,640.00. Do not retrospectively revise revenue on goods already transferred.

title: FVTPL acquisition expense • case 63
prompt: A financial asset is acquired at fair value LKR 2,060,000 and is classified at FVTPL. Directly attributable broker costs are 51,500, paid separately. No fair-value change occurs immediately after purchase. Find the immediate profit-or-loss expense from acquiring this asset.
explanation: Transaction costs on an FVTPL asset are expensed. Initial asset carrying amount is fair value 2,060,000; immediate acquisition expense is 51,500.00.

title: Collateral cash-shortfall discounting • case 63
prompt: A credit loss scenario has a contractual receipt of LKR 2,575,000 due in one year. The ONLY expected recovery at that same date is collateral sale proceeds of 1,645,000, less sale costs of 113,000. Scenario probability is 100% and original EIR is 10%. Collateral is an integral contractual credit enhancement and not separately recognised. Find discounted ECL.
explanation: One-year shortfall = contractual receipt − net collateral recovery = 2,575,000 − (1,645,000 − 113,000). Discount that shortfall at 10%: 948,181.82. Do not ignore recovery costs or discount only one side of same-date cash flows.

title: Three-band provision matrix • case 63
prompt: Under the simplified lifetime-ECL approach, supported adjusted loss rates are 1% on current receivables of LKR 2,260,000, 5% on past-due balances of 615,000, and 30% on severely overdue balances of 226,000. Rates already include all required forward-looking and discounting effects. Find total loss allowance.
explanation: Apply each appropriate band rate and add: 2,260,000×1% + 615,000×5% + 226,000×30% = 121,150.00. Do not apply one blended band mechanically to all balances.

title: Equity FVOCI profit-or-loss dividend • case 63
prompt: An eligible equity investment has the irrevocable FVOCI election. During the year it gains LKR 246,000 in fair value and earns a dividend of 123,000. Dividend recognition criteria are met and the dividend clearly represents a return on investment, not recovery of cost. There are no other effects. Find income recognised in PROFIT OR LOSS.
explanation: The qualifying dividend of 123,000.00 is profit-or-loss income. The fair-value movement of 246,000 is OCI under this election and is not added to the profit-or-loss amount.

title: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset • case 63
prompt: A loan is sold with full derecognition. Immediately before sale, gross carrying amount is LKR 2,260,000, loss allowance 226,000, and cash proceeds 2,147,000. No accumulated OCI, sale fees or other adjustments exist. Find the derecognition GAIN relative to net carrying amount.
explanation: Net carrying amount = 2,260,000 − 226,000 = 2,034,000. Compare proceeds with that net amount: 2,147,000 − 2,034,000 = 113,000.00 gain. Derecognise both the gross asset and related allowance.
family: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset

title: Non-substantial liability modification gain • case 63
prompt: An amortised-cost liability is modified WITHOUT extinguishment, with no fees. Its carrying amount is LKR 1,630,000. The sole revised payment is 1,874,500 in two years. Original EIR is 10%; the modification is assessed as non-substantial. Find the immediate modification GAIN from recalculating amortised cost at the original EIR.
explanation: Revised amortised cost = 1,874,500/1.10² = 1,549,173.55. Gain = old liability 1,630,000 − revised PV = 80,826.45. The original EIR is retained for this non-extinguishing modification.

title: Credit-risk improvement allowance release • case 63
prompt: A debt asset under the GENERAL ECL model previously had significant credit-risk deterioration and lifetime allowance LKR 226,000. At reporting date the criteria for lifetime ECL are no longer met; required 12-month ECL is 41,500. No write-offs, new assets or other allowance movements occur. Find the impairment reversal in profit or loss.
explanation: When lifetime measurement is no longer required, the general model returns to 12-month ECL. Release the excess allowance: 226,000 − 41,500 = 184,500.00. This is not a receivable under mandatory simplified lifetime ECL.

title: Upstream inventory elimination with tax • case 63
prompt: P and S report profits AFTER their own tax of LKR 4,520,000 and 2,060,000. An upstream inventory sale leaves unrealised profit of 452,000 in group closing inventory. A recoverable DTA is recognised on the full elimination at 30%, with the tax effect in profit or loss. No other consolidation adjustments exist. Find TOTAL consolidated profit, before attribution to owners and NCI.
explanation: Combine separate after-tax profits, eliminate unrealised profit and recognise the recoverable tax benefit: 4,520,000 + 2,060,000 − 452,000 + 135,600.00 = 6,263,600.00. This question asks total group profit, not its attribution.

title: Full-goodwill impairment and owner profit • case 63
prompt: P owns 80% of S all year. Separate after-tax profits are P LKR 3,690,000 and S 1,330,000. Goodwill is recognised on the FULL-goodwill basis and an impairment of 515,000 is attributable to S’s CGU and allocated 80:20 between owners and NCI. No other adjustments or tax effects apply. Find consolidated profit attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Owners receive 80% of S’s profit and bear 80% of the full-goodwill loss: 3,690,000 + 80% × (1,330,000 − 515,000) = 4,342,000.00. Do not charge the owners with 100% of this full-goodwill loss.

title: Partial goodwill CGU gross-up • case 63
prompt: P owns 80% of S. Recognised PARTIAL goodwill is LKR 1,808,000; S’s other net assets in the tested CGU carry at 9,040,000. Recoverable amount of the WHOLE CGU is 10,170,000. Gross up goodwill for unrecognised NCI goodwill when testing; the whole impairment falls within grossed-up goodwill. No tax or other adjustments apply. Find impairment actually recognised on group goodwill.
explanation: Grossed-up goodwill = 1,808,000/80% = 2,260,000.00. Whole-CGU impairment = grossed goodwill + other net assets − recoverable amount = 1,130,000.00. Only the parent’s 80% goodwill portion is recognised, so recorded loss = 904,000.00.
reference: LKAS 36 Appendix C paras C4–C8; SLFRS 10 para B86

title: Consolidated retained earnings bridge • case 63
prompt: P owns 75% of S. At year end P retained earnings are LKR 6,150,000, and S retained earnings 3,890,000. S retained earnings at acquisition were 1,000,000. Cumulative post-acquisition extra FV depreciation is 226,000. A downstream sale by P leaves unrealised profit of 143,000. No tax, goodwill impairment, dividends recognised by P, OCI or other adjustments apply. Find consolidated retained earnings attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Group owners’ retained earnings = parent RE + 75% of adjusted post-acquisition S reserves − the parent’s downstream unrealised profit: 8,005,000.00. Pre-acquisition reserves do not enter post-acquisition group retained earnings.

title: Loss of control and translation reserve • case 63
prompt: P loses control of a foreign subsidiary. Proceeds are LKR 4,720,000; retained interest FV 1,130,000; NCI carrying amount 615,000; consolidated net assets INCLUDING goodwill 4,490,000. A cumulative translation GAIN of 226,000, entirely attributable to P, must be reclassified to profit or loss on loss of control. No other effects apply. Find total disposal gain including that reclassification.
explanation: Base gain = proceeds + retained FV + NCI − net assets = 1,975,000.00. Add the parent’s translation gain recycled on disposal: 226,000. Total = 2,201,000.00.
family: Loss of control and translation reserve

title: Residual guarantee expected payment • case 63
prompt: A lessee owes three year-end rentals of LKR 515,000. It guarantees residual value up to 200,000, but the amount EXPECTED to be payable under that guarantee is 93,000 at year three. Discount rate is 10%. No other liability payments exist. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the amount expected to be payable, not automatically the maximum guarantee. Liability = PV of three rentals + 93,000/1.10³ = 1,350,601.05.

title: Reasonably certain purchase option PV • case 63
prompt: A lease requires three year-end rentals of LKR 465,000, plus a purchase option price of 1,130,000 payable at year three. Exercise is reasonably certain. Discount rate is 10%. No incentives, other payments or initial prepayments apply. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the reasonably certain purchase price in the liability: PV of rentals + purchase price discounted for three years = 2,005,371.90. Do not omit or leave the future option payment undiscounted.

title: Lease and service component allocation • case 63
prompt: A two-year contract requires bundled payments of LKR 565,000 at each year end. Relative stand-alone prices are equipment lease 200,000 and distinct maintenance 50,000 per year. The lessee does NOT elect to combine components. Lease discount rate is 10%; no other payments exist. Find initial lease liability for the LEASE component only.
explanation: Allocate 200,000/250,000 = 80% of each bundled payment to the lease: 452,000.00. Discount those two lease payments, excluding maintenance, to obtain 784,462.81.

title: Exempt short-term lease rent-free start • case 63
prompt: A twelve-month lease with no purchase option qualifies for the elected short-term exemption. The first three months are rent free, then nine monthly payments of LKR 51,500 are due. The asset is available throughout and straight-line expense is appropriate. Find lease expense for the FIRST six months, ignoring accrual settlement timing.
explanation: Total fixed payments are nine rents. Spread evenly over all twelve months: 51,500 × 9/12 × 6 = 231,750.00. Rent-free months still receive an expense allocation.

title: Sale-and-leaseback rights transferred • case 63
prompt: A transfer qualifies as a sale under SLFRS 15 at fair value LKR 22,600,000; asset carrying amount is 12,300,000. Market-rate leaseback payments have PV 9,040,000. There are no off-market adjustments or variable-payment complications. At inception, what sale gain is recognised for rights TRANSFERRED to the buyer-lessor?
explanation: Total gain = 22,600,000 − 12,300,000 = 10,300,000. Retained-use proportion = lease PV / fair value = 40%. Recognise only the transferred-rights proportion of the gain: 6,180,000.00.

title: Reassessed bargain purchase gain • case 63
prompt: After the required reassessment, final acquisition-date consideration is LKR 4,520,000, NCI fair value is 400,000 and identifiable net assets are 6,780,000. There is no prior holding or other adjustment. Find the bargain purchase gain recognised in profit or loss.
explanation: Net identifiable assets exceed consideration plus NCI: 6,780,000 − 4,520,000 − 400,000 = 1,860,000.00. Reassessment has been completed before recognising the gain.

title: Acquired contingent liability in goodwill • case 63
prompt: Consideration is LKR 6,650,000; NCI FV is 500,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired contingent liability are 4,890,000. The acquired item is a present obligation with reliably measurable FV 515,000 and qualifies for recognition despite non-probable outflow. No tax or other adjustment applies. Find goodwill after recognising it.
explanation: Recognise the qualifying acquired liability: net identifiable assets become 4,890,000 − 515,000. Goodwill = consideration + NCI − adjusted net assets = 2,775,000.00.

title: Separate acquired brand from goodwill • case 63
prompt: Consideration is LKR 6,150,000; NCI FV 600,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired separable brand are 5,120,000. Brand FV is 1,030,000; tax base is zero and 30% DTL must be recognised. No other adjustments apply. Find goodwill after separate brand and tax recognition.
explanation: An identifiable acquired brand is separate from goodwill. Net addition to identifiable assets = brand FV − 30% DTL = 721,000.00. Goodwill = 6,150,000 + 600,000 − (5,120,000 + 721,000.00) = 909,000.00.

title: Acquisition costs versus issue costs • case 63
prompt: A business acquisition has consideration LKR 3,890,000. Additional costs are acquisition advisory 226,000, qualifying equity-issue costs 70,000 and qualifying debt-issue costs 40,000. The issue costs follow their relevant standards, and no immediate debt-cost amortisation or other expense arises this period. Find the immediate acquisition-related PROFIT-OR-LOSS expense from these costs.
explanation: Expense advisory acquisition costs of 226,000.00. Qualifying equity and debt issuance costs follow their respective standards and are not added to this immediate acquisition-service expense or goodwill.

title: Temporary difference and enacted rate change • case 63
prompt: A taxable temporary difference opens at LKR 200,000 with a DTL measured at 25%. At year end the difference is 615,000 and the enacted rate expected on reversal is 30%. Both the underlying movements and rate change belong in profit or loss. No other tax movements exist. Find deferred tax expense for the year.
explanation: Opening DTL = 200,000×25% = 50,000. Closing DTL = 615,000×30% = 184,500.00. Expense is the full increase, including rate remeasurement: 134,500.00. Rates are exercise assumptions.
family: Temporary difference and enacted rate change

title: Revalued non-depreciable land tax basis • case 63
prompt: Non-depreciable land is revalued from cost LKR 2,260,000 to fair value 3,390,000; tax base remains cost. The enacted rate for recovery through SALE is 20%, while a 30% use rate would otherwise apply. The revaluation and associated tax go to OCI. No other effects exist. Find the net OCI revaluation increase after deferred tax.
explanation: For this non-depreciable revalued asset, measure tax consequences on recovery through sale: DTL = (3,390,000 − 2,260,000)×20%. Net OCI increase = gross uplift less that DTL = 904,000.00.

title: Current tax reconciliation and prepayment • case 63
prompt: Accounting pretax profit is LKR 5,150,000. It includes a permanently non-deductible fine of 226,000, exempt income of 50,000, and warranty expense of 515,000 deductible only on payment. Current-year warranty payments of 80,000 are deductible and were charged against the provision, not current profit. Tax rate is 30%; tax prepayments are 300,000. No other tax adjustments exist. Find closing CURRENT tax payable, not total tax expense.
explanation: Taxable profit = 5,150,000 + fine 226,000 − exempt income 50,000 + provision expense 515,000 − deductible payments 80,000 = 5,761,000. Current tax less prepaid 300,000 = 1,428,300.00. Deferred tax is separate.

title: Consolidated inventory tax difference • case 63
prompt: After eliminating an intragroup profit, inventory carries in consolidated statements at LKR 1,356,000. Its tax base in the buyer’s tax jurisdiction is 2,034,000. The buyer’s enacted rate is 30%; sufficient taxable profit is probable. No offsetting, exception or other tax effects apply. Find the consolidated DTA on this inventory.
explanation: The consolidated carrying amount is below tax base, creating a deductible temporary difference of 678,000. Use the buyer’s relevant tax rate: difference ×30% = 203,400.00.

title: Depreciation after recognised impairment • case 63
prompt: Immediately before an impairment, equipment carries at LKR 2,260,000. Recoverable amount is 1,330,000 and impairment is recognised. After that date it has four years’ remaining useful life and residual value 100,000. Straight-line depreciation is appropriate; no further revaluation or impairment applies. Find depreciation for the next FULL year.
explanation: First reduce the asset to recoverable amount 1,330,000. Thereafter allocate revised depreciable amount over remaining life: (1,330,000 − 100,000)/4 = 307,500.00.

title: Allocated headquarters in CGU impairment • case 63
prompt: CGU A carries operating assets of LKR 1,230,000; CGU B carries 400,000. A headquarters asset of 200,000 can be allocated reasonably and consistently in proportion to those operating-asset amounts. A’s recoverable amount INCLUDING its headquarters share is 965,000. No goodwill or other assets exist. Find the impairment loss for A including its allocation.
explanation: Allocate headquarters to A: 200,000 × 1,230,000/(1,230,000+400,000) = 150,920.25. Tested A carrying amount is 1,380,920.25. Impairment versus recoverable amount 965,000 = 415,920.25.

title: Break-even value-in-use cash flow • case 63
prompt: An asset carries at LKR 2,260,000. Its fair value less costs of disposal is lower. A valid VIU model uses THREE equal year-end operating cash inflows, plus 100,000 net disposal proceeds at year three, discounted at 10%. What minimum equal ANNUAL operating cash inflow makes VIU exactly equal carrying amount? Ignore tax and other adjustments.
explanation: Let annual flow be X. X×(1/1.10 + 1/1.10² + 1/1.10³) + 100,000/1.10³ = 2,260,000. Solve for X = 878,567.98. This sensitivity calculation identifies the VIU break-even point.

title: Discounted warranty expected-value portfolio • case 63
prompt: A present warranty obligation covers 2,260 products. Per product, probabilities are 70% no defect, 25% a minor repair costing LKR 400, and 5% a major repair costing 2,000. All expected payments occur exactly in TWO years. Outflow for the portfolio is probable; appropriate discount rate is 10% with no risk double counting. Find the provision.
explanation: Expected cash payment = 2,260×(25%×400 + 5%×2,000) = 452,000.0. Discount two years at 10%: 452,000.0/1.10² = 373,553.72. The probability assessment applies to the portfolio.

title: Provision movement with revised estimate • case 63
prompt: A discounted provision opens at LKR 1,130,000. Unwinding for a full year is at 8%. A 100,000 settlement occurs at the year END, after unwinding. At that same reporting date, a new estimate increases the remaining provision by 176,000. No other changes occur. Find closing provision.
explanation: Closing = opening + 8% unwinding − year-end settlement + estimate increase: 1,130,000×1.08 −100,000 +176,000 = 1,296,400.00. Classification of the estimate change’s counterpart is assessed separately.

title: Revaluation increase after earlier loss • case 63
prompt: PPE carries at LKR 1,230,000 before revaluation and is revalued to 2,260,000. A prior revaluation decrease on THIS asset of 276,000 was recognised in profit or loss and has not been reversed. No tax effects apply. Find the current increase recognised in OCI after reversing the eligible prior loss in profit or loss.
explanation: Gross increase = 2,260,000 − 1,230,000 = 1,030,000. First recognise 276,000 in profit or loss to reverse the prior decrease. Remaining 754,000.00 is OCI revaluation surplus.

title: Nine-month depreciation and disposal gain • case 63
prompt: Equipment cost LKR 2,460,000, residual value 200,000 and useful life five years, straight-line. Two FULL years’ depreciation were recognised before this year. It is sold after nine months of the current year for 1,795,000. It was not previously held for sale and no impairment or revaluation applies. Find disposal GAIN after the required nine-month depreciation.
explanation: Annual depreciation = (2,460,000−200,000)/5. Deduct two full years and another 9/12 year from cost to obtain disposal-date carrying amount 1,217,000.00. Gain = proceeds − that amount = 578,000.00.

title: Customer collections with a write-off • case 63
prompt: All sales are on credit. Revenue is LKR 6,150,000; opening GROSS trade receivables are 600,000; closing GROSS receivables are 1,430,000. Receivables of 163,000 were written off during the year. There are no taxes, returns, contract balances, acquisitions or exchange changes. Find cash collected from customers.
explanation: Gross receivable roll-forward: opening + credit sales − cash receipts − write-offs = closing. Thus receipts = 6,150,000+600,000−1,430,000−163,000 = 5,157,000.00. Write-offs are not cash receipts.

title: Loan funding net cash effect • case 63
prompt: A company receives cash loan proceeds of LKR 2,260,000 and immediately pays a directly attributable lender issue fee of 51,500. Both payments are classified as financing cash flows in this case. No other cash movement occurs. Find the NET financing cash inflow from these two cash movements; this question does not require net line-item presentation.
explanation: Net financing cash effect = proceeds − cash fee = 2,260,000 − 51,500.00 = 2,208,500.00. Effective-interest amortisation later is not another inception cash payment.

title: Item-by-item NRV without offsetting headroom • case 63
prompt: Two unrelated inventory lines require separate NRV tests. A has 415 units, cost LKR 1,000 and NRV 900 each. B has 226 units, cost 1,000 and NRV 1,200 each. There is no basis to group them for the write-down test. Find TOTAL closing inventory carrying amount.
explanation: Carry A at 900 per unit and B at its lower cost of 1,000. Total = 415×900 + 226×1,000 = 599,500.00. B’s NRV headroom cannot offset A’s write-down.

title: Units-of-production intangible amortisation • case 63
prompt: A finite-life production licence costs LKR 2,160,000, has zero residual value, and is expected to support 150,000 units in total. Actual output this year is 61,500 units. A units-of-production method reliably reflects consumption and the asset was available throughout. No impairment or estimate change applies. Find annual amortisation.
explanation: Apply the supported consumption pattern: amortisation = 2,160,000 × 61,500/150,000 = 885,600.00. It is the share of expected lifetime production consumed, not an automatic straight-line charge.

title: Profit after suspended associate losses • case 63
prompt: An equity-method investment and relevant long-term interests were previously reduced to zero. Unrecognised share of prior losses totals LKR 206,000; the investor has no obligation and made no support payments. In the current year its share of associate profit is 309,000. No other adjustments or changes in interest apply. Find the share of profit that can now be RECOGNISED.
explanation: First absorb unrecognised prior losses before resuming recognised profit. Recognised amount = current profit share 309,000 − prior unrecognised losses 206,000 = 103,000.00.

title: Return recovery asset net of costs • case 64
prompt: A retailer has transferred 2,600 products. It expects 104 to be returned. Each returned product originally cost LKR 600; expected recovery handling is 20 per item and expected value deterioration is 30 per item. Estimates meet the relevant requirements. Find the separate asset for the right to recover returned products, excluding the refund liability.
explanation: Recovery asset = original carrying amount of expected returns less recovery costs and potential value decrease: 104 × (600 − 20 − 30) = 57,200.00. It is assessed separately from the customer refund liability.
family: Return recovery asset net of costs

title: Retrospective volume rebate true-up • case 64
prompt: A customer’s annual purchases reach 16,400 units at list price LKR 200. Crossing the threshold entitles it to a 5% retrospective rebate on ALL units. Cumulative revenue before this new supported estimate equals full list price; no rebate was previously accrued. The constraint permits the estimate. Find the reduction in cumulative revenue required now.
explanation: The revised transaction price reflects the retrospective rebate on all units. Revenue reduction = 16,400 × 200 × 5% = 164,000.00. Recognise the corresponding refund obligation as appropriate.

title: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation • case 64
prompt: A bundle has distinct goods A and B with stand-alone prices LKR 520,000 and 940,000. Total transaction price is 1,346,000. ALL paragraph 82 criteria demonstrate that the whole 114,000 discount relates only to A. A transfers now; B is not yet delivered. Find revenue recognised for A.
explanation: The specified discount-allocation exception applies. Allocate all 114,000 discount to A: 520,000 − 114,000 = 406,000.00. Do not default to relative allocation when the exception’s criteria are met.
family: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation

title: Three obligations and partial service • case 64
prompt: A contract price of LKR 3,120,000 covers goods A, goods B and twelve months of distinct support. Stand-alone prices are 600,000, 300,000 and 300,000 respectively. A is delivered, B is not, and six months of evenly provided support are complete. No allocation exception applies. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise allocation to A plus half of support: 3,120,000 × (600,000 + 150,000) / 1,200,000 = 1,950,000.00. B’s allocation remains unrecognised as revenue.

title: Progress excluding abnormal waste • case 64
prompt: An over-time contract has transaction price LKR 16,400,000. Costs incurred are 6,560,000, including abnormal waste of 328,000 that does not depict progress. Expected TOTAL productive costs excluding that waste are 13,120,000. Cost-to-cost is appropriate after excluding the waste; no other adjustment applies. Find cumulative revenue, not profit.
explanation: Exclude abnormal waste from the progress numerator. Productive progress = (6,560,000 − 328,000) / 13,120,000. Revenue = transaction price × that progress = 7,790,000.00. The wasted cost is not a revenue-producing input.

title: Uninstalled materials without margin • case 64
prompt: A single over-time construction obligation has price LKR 22,800,000. All B19(b) conditions justify recognising revenue equal to cost for significant uninstalled materials of 4,560,000 already controlled by the customer. Other productive costs incurred are 3,420,000; expected total OTHER costs are 13,680,000. No revenue was previously recognised. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise material revenue without margin: 4,560,000. Recognise the remaining price using other-cost progress: (22,800,000 − 4,560,000) × 3,420,000/13,680,000. Total revenue = 9,120,000.00.

title: Agent commission after collection • case 64
prompt: An intermediary is an AGENT and collects customer cash of LKR 4,200,000 for a completed supplier service. It must remit 88% to the supplier and is entitled to the remaining 12% commission. It controls neither the underlying service nor any distinct extra service, and there is no tax. Find its revenue.
explanation: An agent recognises its fee or commission, not the supplier’s gross billings: 4,200,000 × 12% = 504,000.00. The amount due to the supplier is separately accounted for.

title: Distinct remaining goods blended prospectively • case 64
prompt: At modification, 100 distinct goods remain under an existing contract at LKR 1,640 each. Another 50 distinct goods are added at 1,312 each. The modification is NOT a separate contract, but remaining goods are distinct from those already transferred, so paragraph 21(a) applies prospectively. Thirty of the remaining goods are then transferred. Find revenue for those thirty.
explanation: Prospective remaining consideration = 100 × 1,640 + 50 × 1,312. Divide by 150 remaining goods, then multiply by 30 = 45,920.00. Do not retrospectively revise revenue on goods already transferred.

title: FVTPL acquisition expense • case 64
prompt: A financial asset is acquired at fair value LKR 2,080,000 and is classified at FVTPL. Directly attributable broker costs are 52,000, paid separately. No fair-value change occurs immediately after purchase. Find the immediate profit-or-loss expense from acquiring this asset.
explanation: Transaction costs on an FVTPL asset are expensed. Initial asset carrying amount is fair value 2,080,000; immediate acquisition expense is 52,000.00.

title: Collateral cash-shortfall discounting • case 64
prompt: A credit loss scenario has a contractual receipt of LKR 2,600,000 due in one year. The ONLY expected recovery at that same date is collateral sale proceeds of 1,660,000, less sale costs of 114,000. Scenario probability is 100% and original EIR is 10%. Collateral is an integral contractual credit enhancement and not separately recognised. Find discounted ECL.
explanation: One-year shortfall = contractual receipt − net collateral recovery = 2,600,000 − (1,660,000 − 114,000). Discount that shortfall at 10%: 958,181.82. Do not ignore recovery costs or discount only one side of same-date cash flows.

title: Three-band provision matrix • case 64
prompt: Under the simplified lifetime-ECL approach, supported adjusted loss rates are 1% on current receivables of LKR 2,280,000, 5% on past-due balances of 620,000, and 30% on severely overdue balances of 228,000. Rates already include all required forward-looking and discounting effects. Find total loss allowance.
explanation: Apply each appropriate band rate and add: 2,280,000×1% + 620,000×5% + 228,000×30% = 122,200.00. Do not apply one blended band mechanically to all balances.

title: Equity FVOCI profit-or-loss dividend • case 64
prompt: An eligible equity investment has the irrevocable FVOCI election. During the year it gains LKR 248,000 in fair value and earns a dividend of 124,000. Dividend recognition criteria are met and the dividend clearly represents a return on investment, not recovery of cost. There are no other effects. Find income recognised in PROFIT OR LOSS.
explanation: The qualifying dividend of 124,000.00 is profit-or-loss income. The fair-value movement of 248,000 is OCI under this election and is not added to the profit-or-loss amount.

title: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset • case 64
prompt: A loan is sold with full derecognition. Immediately before sale, gross carrying amount is LKR 2,280,000, loss allowance 228,000, and cash proceeds 2,166,000. No accumulated OCI, sale fees or other adjustments exist. Find the derecognition GAIN relative to net carrying amount.
explanation: Net carrying amount = 2,280,000 − 228,000 = 2,052,000. Compare proceeds with that net amount: 2,166,000 − 2,052,000 = 114,000.00 gain. Derecognise both the gross asset and related allowance.
family: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset

title: Non-substantial liability modification gain • case 64
prompt: An amortised-cost liability is modified WITHOUT extinguishment, with no fees. Its carrying amount is LKR 1,640,000. The sole revised payment is 1,886,000 in two years. Original EIR is 10%; the modification is assessed as non-substantial. Find the immediate modification GAIN from recalculating amortised cost at the original EIR.
explanation: Revised amortised cost = 1,886,000/1.10² = 1,558,677.69. Gain = old liability 1,640,000 − revised PV = 81,322.31. The original EIR is retained for this non-extinguishing modification.

title: Credit-risk improvement allowance release • case 64
prompt: A debt asset under the GENERAL ECL model previously had significant credit-risk deterioration and lifetime allowance LKR 228,000. At reporting date the criteria for lifetime ECL are no longer met; required 12-month ECL is 42,000. No write-offs, new assets or other allowance movements occur. Find the impairment reversal in profit or loss.
explanation: When lifetime measurement is no longer required, the general model returns to 12-month ECL. Release the excess allowance: 228,000 − 42,000 = 186,000.00. This is not a receivable under mandatory simplified lifetime ECL.

title: Upstream inventory elimination with tax • case 64
prompt: P and S report profits AFTER their own tax of LKR 4,560,000 and 2,080,000. An upstream inventory sale leaves unrealised profit of 456,000 in group closing inventory. A recoverable DTA is recognised on the full elimination at 30%, with the tax effect in profit or loss. No other consolidation adjustments exist. Find TOTAL consolidated profit, before attribution to owners and NCI.
explanation: Combine separate after-tax profits, eliminate unrealised profit and recognise the recoverable tax benefit: 4,560,000 + 2,080,000 − 456,000 + 136,800.00 = 6,320,800.00. This question asks total group profit, not its attribution.

title: Full-goodwill impairment and owner profit • case 64
prompt: P owns 80% of S all year. Separate after-tax profits are P LKR 3,720,000 and S 1,340,000. Goodwill is recognised on the FULL-goodwill basis and an impairment of 520,000 is attributable to S’s CGU and allocated 80:20 between owners and NCI. No other adjustments or tax effects apply. Find consolidated profit attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Owners receive 80% of S’s profit and bear 80% of the full-goodwill loss: 3,720,000 + 80% × (1,340,000 − 520,000) = 4,376,000.00. Do not charge the owners with 100% of this full-goodwill loss.

title: Partial goodwill CGU gross-up • case 64
prompt: P owns 80% of S. Recognised PARTIAL goodwill is LKR 1,824,000; S’s other net assets in the tested CGU carry at 9,120,000. Recoverable amount of the WHOLE CGU is 10,260,000. Gross up goodwill for unrecognised NCI goodwill when testing; the whole impairment falls within grossed-up goodwill. No tax or other adjustments apply. Find impairment actually recognised on group goodwill.
explanation: Grossed-up goodwill = 1,824,000/80% = 2,280,000.00. Whole-CGU impairment = grossed goodwill + other net assets − recoverable amount = 1,140,000.00. Only the parent’s 80% goodwill portion is recognised, so recorded loss = 912,000.00.
reference: LKAS 36 Appendix C paras C4–C8; SLFRS 10 para B86

title: Consolidated retained earnings bridge • case 64
prompt: P owns 75% of S. At year end P retained earnings are LKR 6,200,000, and S retained earnings 3,920,000. S retained earnings at acquisition were 1,000,000. Cumulative post-acquisition extra FV depreciation is 228,000. A downstream sale by P leaves unrealised profit of 144,000. No tax, goodwill impairment, dividends recognised by P, OCI or other adjustments apply. Find consolidated retained earnings attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Group owners’ retained earnings = parent RE + 75% of adjusted post-acquisition S reserves − the parent’s downstream unrealised profit: 8,075,000.00. Pre-acquisition reserves do not enter post-acquisition group retained earnings.

title: Loss of control and translation reserve • case 64
prompt: P loses control of a foreign subsidiary. Proceeds are LKR 4,760,000; retained interest FV 1,140,000; NCI carrying amount 620,000; consolidated net assets INCLUDING goodwill 4,520,000. A cumulative translation GAIN of 228,000, entirely attributable to P, must be reclassified to profit or loss on loss of control. No other effects apply. Find total disposal gain including that reclassification.
explanation: Base gain = proceeds + retained FV + NCI − net assets = 2,000,000.00. Add the parent’s translation gain recycled on disposal: 228,000. Total = 2,228,000.00.
family: Loss of control and translation reserve

title: Residual guarantee expected payment • case 64
prompt: A lessee owes three year-end rentals of LKR 520,000. It guarantees residual value up to 200,000, but the amount EXPECTED to be payable under that guarantee is 94,000 at year three. Discount rate is 10%. No other liability payments exist. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the amount expected to be payable, not automatically the maximum guarantee. Liability = PV of three rentals + 94,000/1.10³ = 1,363,786.63.

title: Reasonably certain purchase option PV • case 64
prompt: A lease requires three year-end rentals of LKR 470,000, plus a purchase option price of 1,140,000 payable at year three. Exercise is reasonably certain. Discount rate is 10%. No incentives, other payments or initial prepayments apply. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the reasonably certain purchase price in the liability: PV of rentals + purchase price discounted for three years = 2,025,319.31. Do not omit or leave the future option payment undiscounted.

title: Lease and service component allocation • case 64
prompt: A two-year contract requires bundled payments of LKR 570,000 at each year end. Relative stand-alone prices are equipment lease 200,000 and distinct maintenance 50,000 per year. The lessee does NOT elect to combine components. Lease discount rate is 10%; no other payments exist. Find initial lease liability for the LEASE component only.
explanation: Allocate 200,000/250,000 = 80% of each bundled payment to the lease: 456,000.00. Discount those two lease payments, excluding maintenance, to obtain 791,404.96.

title: Exempt short-term lease rent-free start • case 64
prompt: A twelve-month lease with no purchase option qualifies for the elected short-term exemption. The first three months are rent free, then nine monthly payments of LKR 52,000 are due. The asset is available throughout and straight-line expense is appropriate. Find lease expense for the FIRST six months, ignoring accrual settlement timing.
explanation: Total fixed payments are nine rents. Spread evenly over all twelve months: 52,000 × 9/12 × 6 = 234,000.00. Rent-free months still receive an expense allocation.

title: Sale-and-leaseback rights transferred • case 64
prompt: A transfer qualifies as a sale under SLFRS 15 at fair value LKR 22,800,000; asset carrying amount is 12,400,000. Market-rate leaseback payments have PV 9,120,000. There are no off-market adjustments or variable-payment complications. At inception, what sale gain is recognised for rights TRANSFERRED to the buyer-lessor?
explanation: Total gain = 22,800,000 − 12,400,000 = 10,400,000. Retained-use proportion = lease PV / fair value = 40%. Recognise only the transferred-rights proportion of the gain: 6,240,000.00.

title: Reassessed bargain purchase gain • case 64
prompt: After the required reassessment, final acquisition-date consideration is LKR 4,560,000, NCI fair value is 400,000 and identifiable net assets are 6,840,000. There is no prior holding or other adjustment. Find the bargain purchase gain recognised in profit or loss.
explanation: Net identifiable assets exceed consideration plus NCI: 6,840,000 − 4,560,000 − 400,000 = 1,880,000.00. Reassessment has been completed before recognising the gain.

title: Acquired contingent liability in goodwill • case 64
prompt: Consideration is LKR 6,700,000; NCI FV is 500,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired contingent liability are 4,920,000. The acquired item is a present obligation with reliably measurable FV 520,000 and qualifies for recognition despite non-probable outflow. No tax or other adjustment applies. Find goodwill after recognising it.
explanation: Recognise the qualifying acquired liability: net identifiable assets become 4,920,000 − 520,000. Goodwill = consideration + NCI − adjusted net assets = 2,800,000.00.

title: Separate acquired brand from goodwill • case 64
prompt: Consideration is LKR 6,200,000; NCI FV 600,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired separable brand are 5,160,000. Brand FV is 1,040,000; tax base is zero and 30% DTL must be recognised. No other adjustments apply. Find goodwill after separate brand and tax recognition.
explanation: An identifiable acquired brand is separate from goodwill. Net addition to identifiable assets = brand FV − 30% DTL = 728,000.00. Goodwill = 6,200,000 + 600,000 − (5,160,000 + 728,000.00) = 912,000.00.

title: Acquisition costs versus issue costs • case 64
prompt: A business acquisition has consideration LKR 3,920,000. Additional costs are acquisition advisory 228,000, qualifying equity-issue costs 70,000 and qualifying debt-issue costs 40,000. The issue costs follow their relevant standards, and no immediate debt-cost amortisation or other expense arises this period. Find the immediate acquisition-related PROFIT-OR-LOSS expense from these costs.
explanation: Expense advisory acquisition costs of 228,000.00. Qualifying equity and debt issuance costs follow their respective standards and are not added to this immediate acquisition-service expense or goodwill.

title: Temporary difference and enacted rate change • case 64
prompt: A taxable temporary difference opens at LKR 200,000 with a DTL measured at 25%. At year end the difference is 620,000 and the enacted rate expected on reversal is 30%. Both the underlying movements and rate change belong in profit or loss. No other tax movements exist. Find deferred tax expense for the year.
explanation: Opening DTL = 200,000×25% = 50,000. Closing DTL = 620,000×30% = 186,000.00. Expense is the full increase, including rate remeasurement: 136,000.00. Rates are exercise assumptions.
family: Temporary difference and enacted rate change

title: Revalued non-depreciable land tax basis • case 64
prompt: Non-depreciable land is revalued from cost LKR 2,280,000 to fair value 3,420,000; tax base remains cost. The enacted rate for recovery through SALE is 20%, while a 30% use rate would otherwise apply. The revaluation and associated tax go to OCI. No other effects exist. Find the net OCI revaluation increase after deferred tax.
explanation: For this non-depreciable revalued asset, measure tax consequences on recovery through sale: DTL = (3,420,000 − 2,280,000)×20%. Net OCI increase = gross uplift less that DTL = 912,000.00.

title: Current tax reconciliation and prepayment • case 64
prompt: Accounting pretax profit is LKR 5,200,000. It includes a permanently non-deductible fine of 228,000, exempt income of 50,000, and warranty expense of 520,000 deductible only on payment. Current-year warranty payments of 80,000 are deductible and were charged against the provision, not current profit. Tax rate is 30%; tax prepayments are 300,000. No other tax adjustments exist. Find closing CURRENT tax payable, not total tax expense.
explanation: Taxable profit = 5,200,000 + fine 228,000 − exempt income 50,000 + provision expense 520,000 − deductible payments 80,000 = 5,818,000. Current tax less prepaid 300,000 = 1,445,400.00. Deferred tax is separate.

title: Consolidated inventory tax difference • case 64
prompt: After eliminating an intragroup profit, inventory carries in consolidated statements at LKR 1,368,000. Its tax base in the buyer’s tax jurisdiction is 2,052,000. The buyer’s enacted rate is 30%; sufficient taxable profit is probable. No offsetting, exception or other tax effects apply. Find the consolidated DTA on this inventory.
explanation: The consolidated carrying amount is below tax base, creating a deductible temporary difference of 684,000. Use the buyer’s relevant tax rate: difference ×30% = 205,200.00.

title: Depreciation after recognised impairment • case 64
prompt: Immediately before an impairment, equipment carries at LKR 2,280,000. Recoverable amount is 1,340,000 and impairment is recognised. After that date it has four years’ remaining useful life and residual value 100,000. Straight-line depreciation is appropriate; no further revaluation or impairment applies. Find depreciation for the next FULL year.
explanation: First reduce the asset to recoverable amount 1,340,000. Thereafter allocate revised depreciable amount over remaining life: (1,340,000 − 100,000)/4 = 310,000.00.

title: Allocated headquarters in CGU impairment • case 64
prompt: CGU A carries operating assets of LKR 1,240,000; CGU B carries 400,000. A headquarters asset of 200,000 can be allocated reasonably and consistently in proportion to those operating-asset amounts. A’s recoverable amount INCLUDING its headquarters share is 970,000. No goodwill or other assets exist. Find the impairment loss for A including its allocation.
explanation: Allocate headquarters to A: 200,000 × 1,240,000/(1,240,000+400,000) = 151,219.51. Tested A carrying amount is 1,391,219.51. Impairment versus recoverable amount 970,000 = 421,219.51.

title: Break-even value-in-use cash flow • case 64
prompt: An asset carries at LKR 2,280,000. Its fair value less costs of disposal is lower. A valid VIU model uses THREE equal year-end operating cash inflows, plus 100,000 net disposal proceeds at year three, discounted at 10%. What minimum equal ANNUAL operating cash inflow makes VIU exactly equal carrying amount? Ignore tax and other adjustments.
explanation: Let annual flow be X. X×(1/1.10 + 1/1.10² + 1/1.10³) + 100,000/1.10³ = 2,280,000. Solve for X = 886,610.27. This sensitivity calculation identifies the VIU break-even point.

title: Discounted warranty expected-value portfolio • case 64
prompt: A present warranty obligation covers 2,280 products. Per product, probabilities are 70% no defect, 25% a minor repair costing LKR 400, and 5% a major repair costing 2,000. All expected payments occur exactly in TWO years. Outflow for the portfolio is probable; appropriate discount rate is 10% with no risk double counting. Find the provision.
explanation: Expected cash payment = 2,280×(25%×400 + 5%×2,000) = 456,000.0. Discount two years at 10%: 456,000.0/1.10² = 376,859.50. The probability assessment applies to the portfolio.

title: Provision movement with revised estimate • case 64
prompt: A discounted provision opens at LKR 1,140,000. Unwinding for a full year is at 8%. A 100,000 settlement occurs at the year END, after unwinding. At that same reporting date, a new estimate increases the remaining provision by 178,000. No other changes occur. Find closing provision.
explanation: Closing = opening + 8% unwinding − year-end settlement + estimate increase: 1,140,000×1.08 −100,000 +178,000 = 1,309,200.00. Classification of the estimate change’s counterpart is assessed separately.

title: Revaluation increase after earlier loss • case 64
prompt: PPE carries at LKR 1,240,000 before revaluation and is revalued to 2,280,000. A prior revaluation decrease on THIS asset of 278,000 was recognised in profit or loss and has not been reversed. No tax effects apply. Find the current increase recognised in OCI after reversing the eligible prior loss in profit or loss.
explanation: Gross increase = 2,280,000 − 1,240,000 = 1,040,000. First recognise 278,000 in profit or loss to reverse the prior decrease. Remaining 762,000.00 is OCI revaluation surplus.

title: Nine-month depreciation and disposal gain • case 64
prompt: Equipment cost LKR 2,480,000, residual value 200,000 and useful life five years, straight-line. Two FULL years’ depreciation were recognised before this year. It is sold after nine months of the current year for 1,810,000. It was not previously held for sale and no impairment or revaluation applies. Find disposal GAIN after the required nine-month depreciation.
explanation: Annual depreciation = (2,480,000−200,000)/5. Deduct two full years and another 9/12 year from cost to obtain disposal-date carrying amount 1,226,000.00. Gain = proceeds − that amount = 584,000.00.

title: Customer collections with a write-off • case 64
