explanation: The revised transaction price reflects the retrospective rebate on all units. Revenue reduction = 16,700 × 200 × 5% = 167,000.00. Recognise the corresponding refund obligation as appropriate.

title: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation • case 67
prompt: A bundle has distinct goods A and B with stand-alone prices LKR 535,000 and 970,000. Total transaction price is 1,388,000. ALL paragraph 82 criteria demonstrate that the whole 117,000 discount relates only to A. A transfers now; B is not yet delivered. Find revenue recognised for A.
explanation: The specified discount-allocation exception applies. Allocate all 117,000 discount to A: 535,000 − 117,000 = 418,000.00. Do not default to relative allocation when the exception’s criteria are met.
family: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation

title: Three obligations and partial service • case 67
prompt: A contract price of LKR 3,210,000 covers goods A, goods B and twelve months of distinct support. Stand-alone prices are 600,000, 300,000 and 300,000 respectively. A is delivered, B is not, and six months of evenly provided support are complete. No allocation exception applies. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise allocation to A plus half of support: 3,210,000 × (600,000 + 150,000) / 1,200,000 = 2,006,250.00. B’s allocation remains unrecognised as revenue.

title: Progress excluding abnormal waste • case 67
prompt: An over-time contract has transaction price LKR 16,700,000. Costs incurred are 6,680,000, including abnormal waste of 334,000 that does not depict progress. Expected TOTAL productive costs excluding that waste are 13,360,000. Cost-to-cost is appropriate after excluding the waste; no other adjustment applies. Find cumulative revenue, not profit.
explanation: Exclude abnormal waste from the progress numerator. Productive progress = (6,680,000 − 334,000) / 13,360,000. Revenue = transaction price × that progress = 7,932,500.00. The wasted cost is not a revenue-producing input.

title: Uninstalled materials without margin • case 67
prompt: A single over-time construction obligation has price LKR 23,400,000. All B19(b) conditions justify recognising revenue equal to cost for significant uninstalled materials of 4,680,000 already controlled by the customer. Other productive costs incurred are 3,510,000; expected total OTHER costs are 14,040,000. No revenue was previously recognised. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise material revenue without margin: 4,680,000. Recognise the remaining price using other-cost progress: (23,400,000 − 4,680,000) × 3,510,000/14,040,000. Total revenue = 9,360,000.00.

title: Agent commission after collection • case 67
prompt: An intermediary is an AGENT and collects customer cash of LKR 4,350,000 for a completed supplier service. It must remit 88% to the supplier and is entitled to the remaining 12% commission. It controls neither the underlying service nor any distinct extra service, and there is no tax. Find its revenue.
explanation: An agent recognises its fee or commission, not the supplier’s gross billings: 4,350,000 × 12% = 522,000.00. The amount due to the supplier is separately accounted for.

title: Distinct remaining goods blended prospectively • case 67
prompt: At modification, 100 distinct goods remain under an existing contract at LKR 1,670 each. Another 50 distinct goods are added at 1,336 each. The modification is NOT a separate contract, but remaining goods are distinct from those already transferred, so paragraph 21(a) applies prospectively. Thirty of the remaining goods are then transferred. Find revenue for those thirty.
explanation: Prospective remaining consideration = 100 × 1,670 + 50 × 1,336. Divide by 150 remaining goods, then multiply by 30 = 46,760.00. Do not retrospectively revise revenue on goods already transferred.

title: FVTPL acquisition expense • case 67
prompt: A financial asset is acquired at fair value LKR 2,140,000 and is classified at FVTPL. Directly attributable broker costs are 53,500, paid separately. No fair-value change occurs immediately after purchase. Find the immediate profit-or-loss expense from acquiring this asset.
explanation: Transaction costs on an FVTPL asset are expensed. Initial asset carrying amount is fair value 2,140,000; immediate acquisition expense is 53,500.00.

title: Collateral cash-shortfall discounting • case 67
prompt: A credit loss scenario has a contractual receipt of LKR 2,675,000 due in one year. The ONLY expected recovery at that same date is collateral sale proceeds of 1,705,000, less sale costs of 117,000. Scenario probability is 100% and original EIR is 10%. Collateral is an integral contractual credit enhancement and not separately recognised. Find discounted ECL.
explanation: One-year shortfall = contractual receipt − net collateral recovery = 2,675,000 − (1,705,000 − 117,000). Discount that shortfall at 10%: 988,181.82. Do not ignore recovery costs or discount only one side of same-date cash flows.

title: Three-band provision matrix • case 67
prompt: Under the simplified lifetime-ECL approach, supported adjusted loss rates are 1% on current receivables of LKR 2,340,000, 5% on past-due balances of 635,000, and 30% on severely overdue balances of 234,000. Rates already include all required forward-looking and discounting effects. Find total loss allowance.
explanation: Apply each appropriate band rate and add: 2,340,000×1% + 635,000×5% + 234,000×30% = 125,350.00. Do not apply one blended band mechanically to all balances.

title: Equity FVOCI profit-or-loss dividend • case 67
prompt: An eligible equity investment has the irrevocable FVOCI election. During the year it gains LKR 254,000 in fair value and earns a dividend of 127,000. Dividend recognition criteria are met and the dividend clearly represents a return on investment, not recovery of cost. There are no other effects. Find income recognised in PROFIT OR LOSS.
explanation: The qualifying dividend of 127,000.00 is profit-or-loss income. The fair-value movement of 254,000 is OCI under this election and is not added to the profit-or-loss amount.

title: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset • case 67
prompt: A loan is sold with full derecognition. Immediately before sale, gross carrying amount is LKR 2,340,000, loss allowance 234,000, and cash proceeds 2,223,000. No accumulated OCI, sale fees or other adjustments exist. Find the derecognition GAIN relative to net carrying amount.
explanation: Net carrying amount = 2,340,000 − 234,000 = 2,106,000. Compare proceeds with that net amount: 2,223,000 − 2,106,000 = 117,000.00 gain. Derecognise both the gross asset and related allowance.
family: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset

title: Non-substantial liability modification gain • case 67
prompt: An amortised-cost liability is modified WITHOUT extinguishment, with no fees. Its carrying amount is LKR 1,670,000. The sole revised payment is 1,920,500 in two years. Original EIR is 10%; the modification is assessed as non-substantial. Find the immediate modification GAIN from recalculating amortised cost at the original EIR.
explanation: Revised amortised cost = 1,920,500/1.10² = 1,587,190.08. Gain = old liability 1,670,000 − revised PV = 82,809.92. The original EIR is retained for this non-extinguishing modification.

title: Credit-risk improvement allowance release • case 67
prompt: A debt asset under the GENERAL ECL model previously had significant credit-risk deterioration and lifetime allowance LKR 234,000. At reporting date the criteria for lifetime ECL are no longer met; required 12-month ECL is 43,500. No write-offs, new assets or other allowance movements occur. Find the impairment reversal in profit or loss.
explanation: When lifetime measurement is no longer required, the general model returns to 12-month ECL. Release the excess allowance: 234,000 − 43,500 = 190,500.00. This is not a receivable under mandatory simplified lifetime ECL.

title: Upstream inventory elimination with tax • case 67
prompt: P and S report profits AFTER their own tax of LKR 4,680,000 and 2,140,000. An upstream inventory sale leaves unrealised profit of 468,000 in group closing inventory. A recoverable DTA is recognised on the full elimination at 30%, with the tax effect in profit or loss. No other consolidation adjustments exist. Find TOTAL consolidated profit, before attribution to owners and NCI.
explanation: Combine separate after-tax profits, eliminate unrealised profit and recognise the recoverable tax benefit: 4,680,000 + 2,140,000 − 468,000 + 140,400.00 = 6,492,400.00. This question asks total group profit, not its attribution.

title: Full-goodwill impairment and owner profit • case 67
prompt: P owns 80% of S all year. Separate after-tax profits are P LKR 3,810,000 and S 1,370,000. Goodwill is recognised on the FULL-goodwill basis and an impairment of 535,000 is attributable to S’s CGU and allocated 80:20 between owners and NCI. No other adjustments or tax effects apply. Find consolidated profit attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Owners receive 80% of S’s profit and bear 80% of the full-goodwill loss: 3,810,000 + 80% × (1,370,000 − 535,000) = 4,478,000.00. Do not charge the owners with 100% of this full-goodwill loss.

title: Partial goodwill CGU gross-up • case 67
prompt: P owns 80% of S. Recognised PARTIAL goodwill is LKR 1,872,000; S’s other net assets in the tested CGU carry at 9,360,000. Recoverable amount of the WHOLE CGU is 10,530,000. Gross up goodwill for unrecognised NCI goodwill when testing; the whole impairment falls within grossed-up goodwill. No tax or other adjustments apply. Find impairment actually recognised on group goodwill.
explanation: Grossed-up goodwill = 1,872,000/80% = 2,340,000.00. Whole-CGU impairment = grossed goodwill + other net assets − recoverable amount = 1,170,000.00. Only the parent’s 80% goodwill portion is recognised, so recorded loss = 936,000.00.
reference: LKAS 36 Appendix C paras C4–C8; SLFRS 10 para B86

title: Consolidated retained earnings bridge • case 67
prompt: P owns 75% of S. At year end P retained earnings are LKR 6,350,000, and S retained earnings 4,010,000. S retained earnings at acquisition were 1,000,000. Cumulative post-acquisition extra FV depreciation is 234,000. A downstream sale by P leaves unrealised profit of 147,000. No tax, goodwill impairment, dividends recognised by P, OCI or other adjustments apply. Find consolidated retained earnings attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Group owners’ retained earnings = parent RE + 75% of adjusted post-acquisition S reserves − the parent’s downstream unrealised profit: 8,285,000.00. Pre-acquisition reserves do not enter post-acquisition group retained earnings.

title: Loss of control and translation reserve • case 67
prompt: P loses control of a foreign subsidiary. Proceeds are LKR 4,880,000; retained interest FV 1,170,000; NCI carrying amount 635,000; consolidated net assets INCLUDING goodwill 4,610,000. A cumulative translation GAIN of 234,000, entirely attributable to P, must be reclassified to profit or loss on loss of control. No other effects apply. Find total disposal gain including that reclassification.
explanation: Base gain = proceeds + retained FV + NCI − net assets = 2,075,000.00. Add the parent’s translation gain recycled on disposal: 234,000. Total = 2,309,000.00.
family: Loss of control and translation reserve

title: Residual guarantee expected payment • case 67
prompt: A lessee owes three year-end rentals of LKR 535,000. It guarantees residual value up to 200,000, but the amount EXPECTED to be payable under that guarantee is 97,000 at year three. Discount rate is 10%. No other liability payments exist. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the amount expected to be payable, not automatically the maximum guarantee. Liability = PV of three rentals + 97,000/1.10³ = 1,403,343.35.

title: Reasonably certain purchase option PV • case 67
prompt: A lease requires three year-end rentals of LKR 485,000, plus a purchase option price of 1,170,000 payable at year three. Exercise is reasonably certain. Discount rate is 10%. No incentives, other payments or initial prepayments apply. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the reasonably certain purchase price in the liability: PV of rentals + purchase price discounted for three years = 2,085,161.53. Do not omit or leave the future option payment undiscounted.

title: Lease and service component allocation • case 67
prompt: A two-year contract requires bundled payments of LKR 585,000 at each year end. Relative stand-alone prices are equipment lease 200,000 and distinct maintenance 50,000 per year. The lessee does NOT elect to combine components. Lease discount rate is 10%; no other payments exist. Find initial lease liability for the LEASE component only.
explanation: Allocate 200,000/250,000 = 80% of each bundled payment to the lease: 468,000.00. Discount those two lease payments, excluding maintenance, to obtain 812,231.40.

title: Exempt short-term lease rent-free start • case 67
prompt: A twelve-month lease with no purchase option qualifies for the elected short-term exemption. The first three months are rent free, then nine monthly payments of LKR 53,500 are due. The asset is available throughout and straight-line expense is appropriate. Find lease expense for the FIRST six months, ignoring accrual settlement timing.
explanation: Total fixed payments are nine rents. Spread evenly over all twelve months: 53,500 × 9/12 × 6 = 240,750.00. Rent-free months still receive an expense allocation.

title: Sale-and-leaseback rights transferred • case 67
prompt: A transfer qualifies as a sale under SLFRS 15 at fair value LKR 23,400,000; asset carrying amount is 12,700,000. Market-rate leaseback payments have PV 9,360,000. There are no off-market adjustments or variable-payment complications. At inception, what sale gain is recognised for rights TRANSFERRED to the buyer-lessor?
explanation: Total gain = 23,400,000 − 12,700,000 = 10,700,000. Retained-use proportion = lease PV / fair value = 40%. Recognise only the transferred-rights proportion of the gain: 6,420,000.00.

title: Reassessed bargain purchase gain • case 67
prompt: After the required reassessment, final acquisition-date consideration is LKR 4,680,000, NCI fair value is 400,000 and identifiable net assets are 7,020,000. There is no prior holding or other adjustment. Find the bargain purchase gain recognised in profit or loss.
explanation: Net identifiable assets exceed consideration plus NCI: 7,020,000 − 4,680,000 − 400,000 = 1,940,000.00. Reassessment has been completed before recognising the gain.

title: Acquired contingent liability in goodwill • case 67
prompt: Consideration is LKR 6,850,000; NCI FV is 500,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired contingent liability are 5,010,000. The acquired item is a present obligation with reliably measurable FV 535,000 and qualifies for recognition despite non-probable outflow. No tax or other adjustment applies. Find goodwill after recognising it.
explanation: Recognise the qualifying acquired liability: net identifiable assets become 5,010,000 − 535,000. Goodwill = consideration + NCI − adjusted net assets = 2,875,000.00.

title: Separate acquired brand from goodwill • case 67
prompt: Consideration is LKR 6,350,000; NCI FV 600,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired separable brand are 5,280,000. Brand FV is 1,070,000; tax base is zero and 30% DTL must be recognised. No other adjustments apply. Find goodwill after separate brand and tax recognition.
explanation: An identifiable acquired brand is separate from goodwill. Net addition to identifiable assets = brand FV − 30% DTL = 749,000.00. Goodwill = 6,350,000 + 600,000 − (5,280,000 + 749,000.00) = 921,000.00.

title: Acquisition costs versus issue costs • case 67
prompt: A business acquisition has consideration LKR 4,010,000. Additional costs are acquisition advisory 234,000, qualifying equity-issue costs 70,000 and qualifying debt-issue costs 40,000. The issue costs follow their relevant standards, and no immediate debt-cost amortisation or other expense arises this period. Find the immediate acquisition-related PROFIT-OR-LOSS expense from these costs.
explanation: Expense advisory acquisition costs of 234,000.00. Qualifying equity and debt issuance costs follow their respective standards and are not added to this immediate acquisition-service expense or goodwill.

title: Temporary difference and enacted rate change • case 67
prompt: A taxable temporary difference opens at LKR 200,000 with a DTL measured at 25%. At year end the difference is 635,000 and the enacted rate expected on reversal is 30%. Both the underlying movements and rate change belong in profit or loss. No other tax movements exist. Find deferred tax expense for the year.
explanation: Opening DTL = 200,000×25% = 50,000. Closing DTL = 635,000×30% = 190,500.00. Expense is the full increase, including rate remeasurement: 140,500.00. Rates are exercise assumptions.
family: Temporary difference and enacted rate change

title: Revalued non-depreciable land tax basis • case 67
prompt: Non-depreciable land is revalued from cost LKR 2,340,000 to fair value 3,510,000; tax base remains cost. The enacted rate for recovery through SALE is 20%, while a 30% use rate would otherwise apply. The revaluation and associated tax go to OCI. No other effects exist. Find the net OCI revaluation increase after deferred tax.
explanation: For this non-depreciable revalued asset, measure tax consequences on recovery through sale: DTL = (3,510,000 − 2,340,000)×20%. Net OCI increase = gross uplift less that DTL = 936,000.00.

title: Current tax reconciliation and prepayment • case 67
prompt: Accounting pretax profit is LKR 5,350,000. It includes a permanently non-deductible fine of 234,000, exempt income of 50,000, and warranty expense of 535,000 deductible only on payment. Current-year warranty payments of 80,000 are deductible and were charged against the provision, not current profit. Tax rate is 30%; tax prepayments are 300,000. No other tax adjustments exist. Find closing CURRENT tax payable, not total tax expense.
explanation: Taxable profit = 5,350,000 + fine 234,000 − exempt income 50,000 + provision expense 535,000 − deductible payments 80,000 = 5,989,000. Current tax less prepaid 300,000 = 1,496,700.00. Deferred tax is separate.

title: Consolidated inventory tax difference • case 67
prompt: After eliminating an intragroup profit, inventory carries in consolidated statements at LKR 1,404,000. Its tax base in the buyer’s tax jurisdiction is 2,106,000. The buyer’s enacted rate is 30%; sufficient taxable profit is probable. No offsetting, exception or other tax effects apply. Find the consolidated DTA on this inventory.
explanation: The consolidated carrying amount is below tax base, creating a deductible temporary difference of 702,000. Use the buyer’s relevant tax rate: difference ×30% = 210,600.00.

title: Depreciation after recognised impairment • case 67
prompt: Immediately before an impairment, equipment carries at LKR 2,340,000. Recoverable amount is 1,370,000 and impairment is recognised. After that date it has four years’ remaining useful life and residual value 100,000. Straight-line depreciation is appropriate; no further revaluation or impairment applies. Find depreciation for the next FULL year.
explanation: First reduce the asset to recoverable amount 1,370,000. Thereafter allocate revised depreciable amount over remaining life: (1,370,000 − 100,000)/4 = 317,500.00.

title: Allocated headquarters in CGU impairment • case 67
prompt: CGU A carries operating assets of LKR 1,270,000; CGU B carries 400,000. A headquarters asset of 200,000 can be allocated reasonably and consistently in proportion to those operating-asset amounts. A’s recoverable amount INCLUDING its headquarters share is 985,000. No goodwill or other assets exist. Find the impairment loss for A including its allocation.
explanation: Allocate headquarters to A: 200,000 × 1,270,000/(1,270,000+400,000) = 152,095.81. Tested A carrying amount is 1,422,095.81. Impairment versus recoverable amount 985,000 = 437,095.81.

title: Break-even value-in-use cash flow • case 67
prompt: An asset carries at LKR 2,340,000. Its fair value less costs of disposal is lower. A valid VIU model uses THREE equal year-end operating cash inflows, plus 100,000 net disposal proceeds at year three, discounted at 10%. What minimum equal ANNUAL operating cash inflow makes VIU exactly equal carrying amount? Ignore tax and other adjustments.
explanation: Let annual flow be X. X×(1/1.10 + 1/1.10² + 1/1.10³) + 100,000/1.10³ = 2,340,000. Solve for X = 910,737.16. This sensitivity calculation identifies the VIU break-even point.

title: Discounted warranty expected-value portfolio • case 67
prompt: A present warranty obligation covers 2,340 products. Per product, probabilities are 70% no defect, 25% a minor repair costing LKR 400, and 5% a major repair costing 2,000. All expected payments occur exactly in TWO years. Outflow for the portfolio is probable; appropriate discount rate is 10% with no risk double counting. Find the provision.
explanation: Expected cash payment = 2,340×(25%×400 + 5%×2,000) = 468,000.0. Discount two years at 10%: 468,000.0/1.10² = 386,776.86. The probability assessment applies to the portfolio.

title: Provision movement with revised estimate • case 67
prompt: A discounted provision opens at LKR 1,170,000. Unwinding for a full year is at 8%. A 100,000 settlement occurs at the year END, after unwinding. At that same reporting date, a new estimate increases the remaining provision by 184,000. No other changes occur. Find closing provision.
explanation: Closing = opening + 8% unwinding − year-end settlement + estimate increase: 1,170,000×1.08 −100,000 +184,000 = 1,347,600.00. Classification of the estimate change’s counterpart is assessed separately.

title: Revaluation increase after earlier loss • case 67
prompt: PPE carries at LKR 1,270,000 before revaluation and is revalued to 2,340,000. A prior revaluation decrease on THIS asset of 284,000 was recognised in profit or loss and has not been reversed. No tax effects apply. Find the current increase recognised in OCI after reversing the eligible prior loss in profit or loss.
explanation: Gross increase = 2,340,000 − 1,270,000 = 1,070,000. First recognise 284,000 in profit or loss to reverse the prior decrease. Remaining 786,000.00 is OCI revaluation surplus.

title: Nine-month depreciation and disposal gain • case 67
prompt: Equipment cost LKR 2,540,000, residual value 200,000 and useful life five years, straight-line. Two FULL years’ depreciation were recognised before this year. It is sold after nine months of the current year for 1,855,000. It was not previously held for sale and no impairment or revaluation applies. Find disposal GAIN after the required nine-month depreciation.
explanation: Annual depreciation = (2,540,000−200,000)/5. Deduct two full years and another 9/12 year from cost to obtain disposal-date carrying amount 1,253,000.00. Gain = proceeds − that amount = 602,000.00.

title: Customer collections with a write-off • case 67
prompt: All sales are on credit. Revenue is LKR 6,350,000; opening GROSS trade receivables are 600,000; closing GROSS receivables are 1,470,000. Receivables of 167,000 were written off during the year. There are no taxes, returns, contract balances, acquisitions or exchange changes. Find cash collected from customers.
explanation: Gross receivable roll-forward: opening + credit sales − cash receipts − write-offs = closing. Thus receipts = 6,350,000+600,000−1,470,000−167,000 = 5,313,000.00. Write-offs are not cash receipts.

title: Loan funding net cash effect • case 67
prompt: A company receives cash loan proceeds of LKR 2,340,000 and immediately pays a directly attributable lender issue fee of 53,500. Both payments are classified as financing cash flows in this case. No other cash movement occurs. Find the NET financing cash inflow from these two cash movements; this question does not require net line-item presentation.
explanation: Net financing cash effect = proceeds − cash fee = 2,340,000 − 53,500.00 = 2,286,500.00. Effective-interest amortisation later is not another inception cash payment.

title: Item-by-item NRV without offsetting headroom • case 67
prompt: Two unrelated inventory lines require separate NRV tests. A has 435 units, cost LKR 1,000 and NRV 900 each. B has 234 units, cost 1,000 and NRV 1,200 each. There is no basis to group them for the write-down test. Find TOTAL closing inventory carrying amount.
explanation: Carry A at 900 per unit and B at its lower cost of 1,000. Total = 435×900 + 234×1,000 = 625,500.00. B’s NRV headroom cannot offset A’s write-down.

title: Units-of-production intangible amortisation • case 67
prompt: A finite-life production licence costs LKR 2,240,000, has zero residual value, and is expected to support 150,000 units in total. Actual output this year is 63,500 units. A units-of-production method reliably reflects consumption and the asset was available throughout. No impairment or estimate change applies. Find annual amortisation.
explanation: Apply the supported consumption pattern: amortisation = 2,240,000 × 63,500/150,000 = 948,266.67. It is the share of expected lifetime production consumed, not an automatic straight-line charge.

title: Profit after suspended associate losses • case 67
prompt: An equity-method investment and relevant long-term interests were previously reduced to zero. Unrecognised share of prior losses totals LKR 214,000; the investor has no obligation and made no support payments. In the current year its share of associate profit is 321,000. No other adjustments or changes in interest apply. Find the share of profit that can now be RECOGNISED.
explanation: First absorb unrecognised prior losses before resuming recognised profit. Recognised amount = current profit share 321,000 − prior unrecognised losses 214,000 = 107,000.00.

title: Return recovery asset net of costs • case 68
prompt: A retailer has transferred 2,700 products. It expects 108 to be returned. Each returned product originally cost LKR 600; expected recovery handling is 20 per item and expected value deterioration is 30 per item. Estimates meet the relevant requirements. Find the separate asset for the right to recover returned products, excluding the refund liability.
explanation: Recovery asset = original carrying amount of expected returns less recovery costs and potential value decrease: 108 × (600 − 20 − 30) = 59,400.00. It is assessed separately from the customer refund liability.
family: Return recovery asset net of costs

title: Retrospective volume rebate true-up • case 68
prompt: A customer’s annual purchases reach 16,800 units at list price LKR 200. Crossing the threshold entitles it to a 5% retrospective rebate on ALL units. Cumulative revenue before this new supported estimate equals full list price; no rebate was previously accrued. The constraint permits the estimate. Find the reduction in cumulative revenue required now.
explanation: The revised transaction price reflects the retrospective rebate on all units. Revenue reduction = 16,800 × 200 × 5% = 168,000.00. Recognise the corresponding refund obligation as appropriate.

prompt: A bundle has distinct goods A and B with stand-alone prices LKR 540,000 and 980,000. Total transaction price is 1,402,000. ALL paragraph 82 criteria demonstrate that the whole 118,000 discount relates only to A. A transfers now; B is not yet delivered. Find revenue recognised for A.
explanation: The specified discount-allocation exception applies. Allocate all 118,000 discount to A: 540,000 − 118,000 = 422,000.00. Do not default to relative allocation when the exception’s criteria are met.
family: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation

prompt: A single over-time construction obligation has price LKR 23,600,000. explanation: Recognise material revenue without margin: 4,720,000. Recognise the remaining price using other-cost progress: (23,600,000 − 4,720,000) × 3,540,000/14,160,000. Total revenue = 9,440,000.00.

prompt: An intermediary is an AGENT and collects customer cash of LKR 4,400,000 for a completed supplier service. It must remit 88% to the supplier and is entitled to the remaining 12% commission. explanation: Prospective remaining consideration = 100 × 1,680 + 50 × 1,344. Divide by 150 remaining goods, then multiply by 30 = 47,040.00. Do not retrospectively revise revenue on goods already transferred.

title: FVTPL acquisition expense • case 68
prompt: A financial asset is acquired at fair value LKR 2,160,000 and is classified at FVTPL. Directly attributable broker costs are 54,000, paid separately. No fair-value change occurs immediately after purchase. Find the immediate profit-or-loss expense from acquiring this asset.
explanation: Transaction costs on an FVTPL asset are expensed. Initial asset carrying amount is fair value 2,160,000; immediate acquisition expense is 54,000.00.

prompt: A credit loss scenario has a contractual receipt of LKR 2,700,000 due in one year. Collateral is an integral contractual credit enhancement and not separately recognised. Find discounted ECL.
explanation: One-year shortfall = contractual receipt − net collateral recovery = 2,700,000 − (1,720,000 − 118,000). Discount that shortfall at 10%: 998,181.82. Do not ignore recovery costs or discount only one side of same-date cash flows.

title: Three-band provision matrix • case 68
prompt: Under the simplified lifetime-ECL approach, supported adjusted loss rates are 1% on current receivables of LKR 2,360,000, 5% on past-due balances of 640,000, and 30% on severely overdue balances of 236,000. Rates already include all required forward-looking and discounting effects. Find total loss allowance.
explanation: Apply each appropriate band rate and add: 2,360,000×1% + 640,000×5% + 236,000×30% = 126,400.00. Do not apply one blended band mechanically to all balances.

title: Equity FVOCI profit-or-loss dividend • case 68
prompt: An eligible equity investment has the irrevocable FVOCI election. During the year it gains LKR 256,000 in fair value and earns a dividend of 128,000. Dividend recognition criteria are met and the dividend clearly represents a return on investment, not recovery of cost. There are no other effects. Find income recognised in PROFIT OR LOSS.
explanation: The qualifying dividend of 128,000.00 is profit-or-loss income. The fair-value movement of 256,000 is OCI under this election and is not added to the profit-or-loss amount.

title: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset • case 68
prompt: A loan is sold with full derecognition. Immediately before sale, gross carrying amount is LKR 2,360,000, loss allowance 236,000, and cash proceeds 2,242,000. No accumulated OCI, sale fees or other adjustments exist. Find the derecognition GAIN relative to net carrying amount.
explanation: Net carrying amount = 2,360,000 − 236,000 = 2,124,000. Compare proceeds with that net amount: 2,242,000 − 2,124,000 = 118,000.00 gain. Derecognise both the gross asset and related allowance.
family: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset

title: Non-substantial liability modification gain • case 68
prompt: An amortised-cost liability is modified WITHOUT extinguishment, with no fees. Its carrying amount is LKR 1,680,000. The sole revised payment is 1,932,000 in two years. Original EIR is 10%; the modification is assessed as non-substantial. Find the immediate modification GAIN from recalculating amortised cost at the original EIR.
explanation: Revised amortised cost = 1,932,000/1.10² = 1,596,694.21. Gain = old liability 1,680,000 − revised PV = 83,305.79. The original EIR is retained for this non-extinguishing modification.

title: Credit-risk improvement allowance release • case 68
prompt: A debt asset under the GENERAL ECL model previously had significant credit-risk deterioration and lifetime allowance LKR 236,000. At reporting date the criteria for lifetime ECL are no longer met; required 12-month ECL is 44,000. No write-offs, new assets or other allowance movements occur. Find the impairment reversal in profit or loss.
explanation: When lifetime measurement is no longer required, the general model returns to 12-month ECL. Release the excess allowance: 236,000 − 44,000 = 192,000.00. This is not a receivable under mandatory simplified lifetime ECL.

title: Upstream inventory elimination with tax • case 68
prompt: P and S report profits AFTER their own tax of LKR 4,720,000 and 2,160,000. An upstream inventory sale leaves unrealised profit of 472,000 in group closing inventory. A recoverable DTA is recognised on the full elimination at 30%, with the tax effect in profit or loss. No other consolidation adjustments exist. Find TOTAL consolidated profit, before attribution to owners and NCI.
explanation: Combine separate after-tax profits, eliminate unrealised profit and recognise the recoverable tax benefit: 4,720,000 + 2,160,000 − 472,000 + 141,600.00 = 6,549,600.00. This question asks total group profit, not its attribution.

title: Full-goodwill impairment and owner profit • case 68
prompt: P owns 80% of S all year. Separate after-tax profits are P LKR 3,840,000 and S 1,380,000. Goodwill is recognised on the FULL-goodwill basis and an impairment of 540,000 is attributable to S’s CGU and allocated 80:20 between owners and NCI. No other adjustments or tax effects apply. Find consolidated profit attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Owners receive 80% of S’s profit and bear 80% of the full-goodwill loss: 3,840,000 + 80% × (1,380,000 − 540,000) = 4,512,000.00. Do not charge the owners with 100% of this full-goodwill loss.

title: Partial goodwill CGU gross-up • case 68
prompt: P owns 80% of S. Recognised PARTIAL goodwill is LKR 1,888,000; S’s other net assets in the tested CGU carry at 9,440,000. Recoverable amount of the WHOLE CGU is 10,620,000. Gross up goodwill for unrecognised NCI goodwill when testing; the whole impairment falls within grossed-up goodwill. No tax or other adjustments apply. Find impairment actually recognised on group goodwill.
explanation: Grossed-up goodwill = 1,888,000/80% = 2,360,000.00. Whole-CGU impairment = grossed goodwill + other net assets − recoverable amount = 1,180,000.00. Only the parent’s 80% goodwill portion is recognised, so recorded loss = 944,000.00.
reference: LKAS 36 Appendix C paras C4–C8; SLFRS 10 para B86

title: Consolidated retained earnings bridge • case 68
prompt: P owns 75% of S. At year end P retained earnings are LKR 6,400,000, and S retained earnings 4,040,000. S retained earnings at acquisition were 1,000,000. Cumulative post-acquisition extra FV depreciation is 236,000. A downstream sale by P leaves unrealised profit of 148,000. No tax, goodwill impairment, dividends recognised by P, OCI or other adjustments apply. Find consolidated retained earnings attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Group owners’ retained earnings = parent RE + 75% of adjusted post-acquisition S reserves − the parent’s downstream unrealised profit: 8,355,000.00. Pre-acquisition reserves do not enter post-acquisition group retained earnings.

title: Loss of control and translation reserve • case 68
prompt: P loses control of a foreign subsidiary. Proceeds are LKR 4,920,000; retained interest FV 1,180,000; NCI carrying amount 640,000; consolidated net assets INCLUDING goodwill 4,640,000. A cumulative translation GAIN of 236,000, entirely attributable to P, must be reclassified to profit or loss on loss of control. No other effects apply. Find total disposal gain including that reclassification.
explanation: Base gain = proceeds + retained FV + NCI − net assets = 2,100,000.00. Add the parent’s translation gain recycled on disposal: 236,000. Total = 2,336,000.00.
family: Loss of control and translation reserve

title: Residual guarantee expected payment • case 68
prompt: A lessee owes three year-end rentals of LKR 540,000. It guarantees residual value up to 200,000, but the amount EXPECTED to be payable under that guarantee is 98,000 at year three. Discount rate is 10%. No other liability payments exist. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the amount expected to be payable, not automatically the maximum guarantee. Liability = PV of three rentals + 98,000/1.10³ = 1,416,528.93.

title: Reasonably certain purchase option PV • case 68
prompt: A lease requires three year-end rentals of LKR 490,000, plus a purchase option price of 1,180,000 payable at year three. Exercise is reasonably certain. Discount rate is 10%. No incentives, other payments or initial prepayments apply. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the reasonably certain purchase price in the liability: PV of rentals + purchase price discounted for three years = 2,105,108.94. Do not omit or leave the future option payment undiscounted.

title: Lease and service component allocation • case 68
prompt: A two-year contract requires bundled payments of LKR 590,000 at each year end. Relative stand-alone prices are equipment lease 200,000 and distinct maintenance 50,000 per year. The lessee does NOT elect to combine components. Lease discount rate is 10%; no other payments exist. Find initial lease liability for the LEASE component only.
explanation: Allocate 200,000/250,000 = 80% of each bundled payment to the lease: 472,000.00. Discount those two lease payments, excluding maintenance, to obtain 819,173.55.

title: Exempt short-term lease rent-free start • case 68
prompt: A twelve-month lease with no purchase option qualifies for the elected short-term exemption. The first three months are rent free, then nine monthly payments of LKR 54,000 are due. The asset is available throughout and straight-line expense is appropriate. Find lease expense for the FIRST six months, ignoring accrual settlement timing.
explanation: Total fixed payments are nine rents. Spread evenly over all twelve months: 54,000 × 9/12 × 6 = 243,000.00. Rent-free months still receive an expense allocation.

title: Sale-and-leaseback rights transferred • case 68
prompt: A transfer qualifies as a sale under SLFRS 15 at fair value LKR 23,600,000; asset carrying amount is 12,800,000. Market-rate leaseback payments have PV 9,440,000. There are no off-market adjustments or variable-payment complications. At inception, what sale gain is recognised for rights TRANSFERRED to the buyer-lessor?
explanation: Total gain = 23,600,000 − 12,800,000 = 10,800,000. Retained-use proportion = lease PV / fair value = 40%. Recognise only the transferred-rights proportion of the gain: 6,480,000.00.

title: Reassessed bargain purchase gain • case 68
prompt: After the required reassessment, final acquisition-date consideration is LKR 4,720,000, NCI fair value is 400,000 and identifiable net assets are 7,080,000. There is no prior holding or other adjustment. Find the bargain purchase gain recognised in profit or loss.
explanation: Net identifiable assets exceed consideration plus NCI: 7,080,000 − 4,720,000 − 400,000 = 1,960,000.00. Reassessment has been completed before recognising the gain.

title: Acquired contingent liability in goodwill • case 68
prompt: Consideration is LKR 6,900,000; NCI FV is 500,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired contingent liability are 5,040,000. The acquired item is a present obligation with reliably measurable FV 540,000 and qualifies for recognition despite non-probable outflow. No tax or other adjustment applies. Find goodwill after recognising it.
explanation: Recognise the qualifying acquired liability: net identifiable assets become 5,040,000 − 540,000. Goodwill = consideration + NCI − adjusted net assets = 2,900,000.00.

title: Separate acquired brand from goodwill • case 68
prompt: Consideration is LKR 6,400,000; NCI FV 600,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired separable brand are 5,320,000. Brand FV is 1,080,000; tax base is zero and 30% DTL must be recognised. No other adjustments apply. Find goodwill after separate brand and tax recognition.
explanation: An identifiable acquired brand is separate from goodwill. Net addition to identifiable assets = brand FV − 30% DTL = 756,000.00. Goodwill = 6,400,000 + 600,000 − (5,320,000 + 756,000.00) = 924,000.00.

title: Acquisition costs versus issue costs • case 68
prompt: A business acquisition has consideration LKR 4,040,000. Additional costs are acquisition advisory 236,000, qualifying equity-issue costs 70,000 and qualifying debt-issue costs 40,000. The issue costs follow their relevant standards, and no immediate debt-cost amortisation or other expense arises this period. Find the immediate acquisition-related PROFIT-OR-LOSS expense from these costs.
explanation: Expense advisory acquisition costs of 236,000.00. Qualifying equity and debt issuance costs follow their respective standards and are not added to this immediate acquisition-service expense or goodwill.

title: Temporary difference and enacted rate change • case 68
prompt: A taxable temporary difference opens at LKR 200,000 with a DTL measured at 25%. At year end the difference is 640,000 and the enacted rate expected on reversal is 30%. Both the underlying movements and rate change belong in profit or loss. No other tax movements exist. Find deferred tax expense for the year.
explanation: Opening DTL = 200,000×25% = 50,000. Closing DTL = 640,000×30% = 192,000.00. Expense is the full increase, including rate remeasurement: 142,000.00. Rates are exercise assumptions.
family: Temporary difference and enacted rate change

title: Revalued non-depreciable land tax basis • case 68
prompt: Non-depreciable land is revalued from cost LKR 2,360,000 to fair value 3,540,000; tax base remains cost. The enacted rate for recovery through SALE is 20%, while a 30% use rate would otherwise apply. The revaluation and associated tax go to OCI. No other effects exist. Find the net OCI revaluation increase after deferred tax.
explanation: For this non-depreciable revalued asset, measure tax consequences on recovery through sale: DTL = (3,540,000 − 2,360,000)×20%. Net OCI increase = gross uplift less that DTL = 944,000.00.

title: Current tax reconciliation and prepayment • case 68
prompt: Accounting pretax profit is LKR 5,400,000. It includes a permanently non-deductible fine of 236,000, exempt income of 50,000, and warranty expense of 540,000 deductible only on payment. Current-year warranty payments of 80,000 are deductible and were charged against the provision, not current profit. Tax rate is 30%; tax prepayments are 300,000. No other tax adjustments exist. Find closing CURRENT tax payable, not total tax expense.
explanation: Taxable profit = 5,400,000 + fine 236,000 − exempt income 50,000 + provision expense 540,000 − deductible payments 80,000 = 6,046,000. Current tax less prepaid 300,000 = 1,513,800.00. Deferred tax is separate.

title: Consolidated inventory tax difference • case 68
prompt: After eliminating an intragroup profit, inventory carries in consolidated statements at LKR 1,416,000. Its tax base in the buyer’s tax jurisdiction is 2,124,000. The buyer’s enacted rate is 30%; sufficient taxable profit is probable. No offsetting, exception or other tax effects apply. Find the consolidated DTA on this inventory.
explanation: The consolidated carrying amount is below tax base, creating a deductible temporary difference of 708,000. Use the buyer’s relevant tax rate: difference ×30% = 212,400.00.

title: Depreciation after recognised impairment • case 68
prompt: Immediately before an impairment, equipment carries at LKR 2,360,000. Recoverable amount is 1,380,000 and impairment is recognised. After that date it has four years’ remaining useful life and residual value 100,000. Straight-line depreciation is appropriate; no further revaluation or impairment applies. Find depreciation for the next FULL year.
explanation: First reduce the asset to recoverable amount 1,380,000. Thereafter allocate revised depreciable amount over remaining life: (1,380,000 − 100,000)/4 = 320,000.00.

title: Allocated headquarters in CGU impairment • case 68
prompt: CGU A carries operating assets of LKR 1,280,000; CGU B carries 400,000. A headquarters asset of 200,000 can be allocated reasonably and consistently in proportion to those operating-asset amounts. A’s recoverable amount INCLUDING its headquarters share is 990,000. No goodwill or other assets exist. Find the impairment loss for A including its allocation.
explanation: Allocate headquarters to A: 200,000 × 1,280,000/(1,280,000+400,000) = 152,380.95. Tested A carrying amount is 1,432,380.95. Impairment versus recoverable amount 990,000 = 442,380.95.

title: Break-even value-in-use cash flow • case 68
prompt: An asset carries at LKR 2,360,000. Its fair value less costs of disposal is lower. A valid VIU model uses THREE equal year-end operating cash inflows, plus 100,000 net disposal proceeds at year three, discounted at 10%. What minimum equal ANNUAL operating cash inflow makes VIU exactly equal carrying amount? Ignore tax and other adjustments.
explanation: Let annual flow be X. X×(1/1.10 + 1/1.10² + 1/1.10³) + 100,000/1.10³ = 2,360,000. Solve for X = 918,779.46. This sensitivity calculation identifies the VIU break-even point.

title: Discounted warranty expected-value portfolio • case 68
prompt: A present warranty obligation covers 2,360 products. Per product, probabilities are 70% no defect, 25% a minor repair costing LKR 400, and 5% a major repair costing 2,000. All expected payments occur exactly in TWO years. Outflow for the portfolio is probable; appropriate discount rate is 10% with no risk double counting. Find the provision.
explanation: Expected cash payment = 2,360×(25%×400 + 5%×2,000) = 472,000.0. Discount two years at 10%: 472,000.0/1.10² = 390,082.64. The probability assessment applies to the portfolio.

title: Provision movement with revised estimate • case 68
prompt: A discounted provision opens at LKR 1,180,000. Unwinding for a full year is at 8%. A 100,000 settlement occurs at the year END, after unwinding. At that same reporting date, a new estimate increases the remaining provision by 186,000. No other changes occur. Find closing provision.
explanation: Closing = opening + 8% unwinding − year-end settlement + estimate increase: 1,180,000×1.08 −100,000 +186,000 = 1,360,400.00. Classification of the estimate change’s counterpart is assessed separately.

title: Revaluation increase after earlier loss • case 68
prompt: PPE carries at LKR 1,280,000 before revaluation and is revalued to 2,360,000. A prior revaluation decrease on THIS asset of 286,000 was recognised in profit or loss and has not been reversed. No tax effects apply. Find the current increase recognised in OCI after reversing the eligible prior loss in profit or loss.
explanation: Gross increase = 2,360,000 − 1,280,000 = 1,080,000. First recognise 286,000 in profit or loss to reverse the prior decrease. Remaining 794,000.00 is OCI revaluation surplus.

title: Nine-month depreciation and disposal gain • case 68
prompt: Equipment cost LKR 2,560,000, residual value 200,000 and useful life five years, straight-line. Two FULL years’ depreciation were recognised before this year. It is sold after nine months of the current year for 1,870,000. It was not previously held for sale and no impairment or revaluation applies. Find disposal GAIN after the required nine-month depreciation.
explanation: Annual depreciation = (2,560,000−200,000)/5. Deduct two full years and another 9/12 year from cost to obtain disposal-date carrying amount 1,262,000.00. Gain = proceeds − that amount = 608,000.00.

title: Customer collections with a write-off • case 68
prompt: All sales are on credit. Revenue is LKR 6,400,000; opening GROSS trade receivables are 600,000; closing GROSS receivables are 1,480,000. Receivables of 168,000 were written off during the year. There are no taxes, returns, contract balances, acquisitions or exchange changes. Find cash collected from customers.
explanation: Gross receivable roll-forward: opening + credit sales − cash receipts − write-offs = closing. Thus receipts = 6,400,000+600,000−1,480,000−168,000 = 5,352,000.00. Write-offs are not cash receipts.

title: Loan funding net cash effect • case 68
prompt: A company receives cash loan proceeds of LKR 2,360,000 and immediately pays a directly attributable lender issue fee of 54,000. Both payments are classified as financing cash flows in this case. No other cash movement occurs. Find the NET financing cash inflow from these two cash movements; this question does not require net line-item presentation.
explanation: Net financing cash effect = proceeds − cash fee = 2,360,000 − 54,000.00 = 2,306,000.00. Effective-interest amortisation later is not another inception cash payment.

title: Item-by-item NRV without offsetting headroom • case 68
prompt: Two unrelated inventory lines require separate NRV tests. A has 440 units, cost LKR 1,000 and NRV 900 each. B has 236 units, cost 1,000 and NRV 1,200 each. There is no basis to group them for the write-down test. Find TOTAL closing inventory carrying amount.
explanation: Carry A at 900 per unit and B at its lower cost of 1,000. Total = 440×900 + 236×1,000 = 632,000.00. B’s NRV headroom cannot offset A’s write-down.

title: Units-of-production intangible amortisation • case 68
prompt: A finite-life production licence costs LKR 2,260,000, has zero residual value, and is expected to support 150,000 units in total. Actual output this year is 64,000 units. A units-of-production method reliably reflects consumption and the asset was available throughout. No impairment or estimate change applies. Find annual amortisation.
explanation: Apply the supported consumption pattern: amortisation = 2,260,000 × 64,000/150,000 = 964,266.67. It is the share of expected lifetime production consumed, not an automatic straight-line charge.

title: Profit after suspended associate losses • case 68
prompt: An equity-method investment and relevant long-term interests were previously reduced to zero. Unrecognised share of prior losses totals LKR 216,000; the investor has no obligation and made no support payments. In the current year its share of associate profit is 324,000. No other adjustments or changes in interest apply. Find the share of profit that can now be RECOGNISED.
explanation: First absorb unrecognised prior losses before resuming recognised profit. Recognised amount = current profit share 324,000 − prior unrecognised losses 216,000 = 108,000.00.

title: Return recovery asset net of costs • case 69
prompt: A retailer has transferred 2,725 products. It expects 109 to be returned. Each returned product originally cost LKR 600; expected recovery handling is 20 per item and expected value deterioration is 30 per item. Estimates meet the relevant requirements. Find the separate asset for the right to recover returned products, excluding the refund liability.
explanation: Recovery asset = original carrying amount of expected returns less recovery costs and potential value decrease: 109 × (600 − 20 − 30) = 59,950.00. It is assessed separately from the customer refund liability.
family: Return recovery asset net of costs

title: Retrospective volume rebate true-up • case 69
prompt: A customer’s annual purchases reach 16,900 units at list price LKR 200. Crossing the threshold entitles it to a 5% retrospective rebate on ALL units. Cumulative revenue before this new supported estimate equals full list price; no rebate was previously accrued. The constraint permits the estimate. Find the reduction in cumulative revenue required now.
explanation: The revised transaction price reflects the retrospective rebate on all units. Revenue reduction = 16,900 × 200 × 5% = 169,000.00. Recognise the corresponding refund obligation as appropriate.

title: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation • case 69
prompt: A bundle has distinct goods A and B with stand-alone prices LKR 545,000 and 990,000. Total transaction price is 1,416,000. ALL paragraph 82 criteria demonstrate that the whole 119,000 discount relates only to A. A transfers now; B is not yet delivered. Find revenue recognised for A.
explanation: The specified discount-allocation exception applies. Allocate all 119,000 discount to A: 545,000 − 119,000 = 426,000.00. Do not default to relative allocation when the exception’s criteria are met.
family: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation

title: Three obligations and partial service • case 69
prompt: A contract price of LKR 3,270,000 covers goods A, goods B and twelve months of distinct support. Stand-alone prices are 600,000, 300,000 and 300,000 respectively. A is delivered, B is not, and six months of evenly provided support are complete. No allocation exception applies. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise allocation to A plus half of support: 3,270,000 × (600,000 + 150,000) / 1,200,000 = 2,043,750.00. B’s allocation remains unrecognised as revenue.

title: Progress excluding abnormal waste • case 69
prompt: An over-time contract has transaction price LKR 16,900,000. Costs incurred are 6,760,000, including abnormal waste of 338,000 that does not depict progress. Expected TOTAL productive costs excluding that waste are 13,520,000. Cost-to-cost is appropriate after excluding the waste; no other adjustment applies. Find cumulative revenue, not profit.
explanation: Exclude abnormal waste from the progress numerator. Productive progress = (6,760,000 − 338,000) / 13,520,000. Revenue = transaction price × that progress = 8,027,500.00. The wasted cost is not a revenue-producing input.

title: Uninstalled materials without margin • case 69
prompt: A single over-time construction obligation has price LKR 23,800,000. All B19(b) conditions justify recognising revenue equal to cost for significant uninstalled materials of 4,760,000 already controlled by the customer. Other productive costs incurred are 3,570,000; expected total OTHER costs are 14,280,000. No revenue was previously recognised. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise material revenue without margin: 4,760,000. Recognise the remaining price using other-cost progress: (23,800,000 − 4,760,000) × 3,570,000/14,280,000. Total revenue = 9,520,000.00.

title: Agent commission after collection • case 69
prompt: An intermediary is an AGENT and collects customer cash of LKR 4,450,000 for a completed supplier service. It must remit 88% to the supplier and is entitled to the remaining 12% commission. It controls neither the underlying service nor any distinct extra service, and there is no tax. Find its revenue.
explanation: An agent recognises its fee or commission, not the supplier’s gross billings: 4,450,000 × 12% = 534,000.00. The amount due to the supplier is separately accounted for.

title: Distinct remaining goods blended prospectively • case 69
prompt: At modification, 100 distinct goods remain under an existing contract at LKR 1,690 each. Another 50 distinct goods are added at 1,352 each. The modification is NOT a separate contract, but remaining goods are distinct from those already transferred, so paragraph 21(a) applies prospectively. Thirty of the remaining goods are then transferred. Find revenue for those thirty.
explanation: Prospective remaining consideration = 100 × 1,690 + 50 × 1,352. Divide by 150 remaining goods, then multiply by 30 = 47,320.00. Do not retrospectively revise revenue on goods already transferred.

title: FVTPL acquisition expense • case 69
prompt: A financial asset is acquired at fair value LKR 2,180,000 and is classified at FVTPL. Directly attributable broker costs are 54,500, paid separately. No fair-value change occurs immediately after purchase. Find the immediate profit-or-loss expense from acquiring this asset.
explanation: Transaction costs on an FVTPL asset are expensed. Initial asset carrying amount is fair value 2,180,000; immediate acquisition expense is 54,500.00.

title: Collateral cash-shortfall discounting • case 69
prompt: A credit loss scenario has a contractual receipt of LKR 2,725,000 due in one year. The ONLY expected recovery at that same date is collateral sale proceeds of 1,735,000, less sale costs of 119,000. Scenario probability is 100% and original EIR is 10%. Collateral is an integral contractual credit enhancement and not separately recognised. Find discounted ECL.
explanation: One-year shortfall = contractual receipt − net collateral recovery = 2,725,000 − (1,735,000 − 119,000). Discount that shortfall at 10%: 1,008,181.82. Do not ignore recovery costs or discount only one side of same-date cash flows.

title: Three-band provision matrix • case 69
prompt: Under the simplified lifetime-ECL approach, supported adjusted loss rates are 1% on current receivables of LKR 2,380,000, 5% on past-due balances of 645,000, and 30% on severely overdue balances of 238,000. Rates already include all required forward-looking and discounting effects. Find total loss allowance.
explanation: Apply each appropriate band rate and add: 2,380,000×1% + 645,000×5% + 238,000×30% = 127,450.00. Do not apply one blended band mechanically to all balances.

title: Equity FVOCI profit-or-loss dividend • case 69
prompt: An eligible equity investment has the irrevocable FVOCI election. During the year it gains LKR 258,000 in fair value and earns a dividend of 129,000. Dividend recognition criteria are met and the dividend clearly represents a return on investment, not recovery of cost. There are no other effects. Find income recognised in PROFIT OR LOSS.
explanation: The qualifying dividend of 129,000.00 is profit-or-loss income. The fair-value movement of 258,000 is OCI under this election and is not added to the profit-or-loss amount.

title: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset • case 69
prompt: A loan is sold with full derecognition. Immediately before sale, gross carrying amount is LKR 2,380,000, loss allowance 238,000, and cash proceeds 2,261,000. No accumulated OCI, sale fees or other adjustments exist. Find the derecognition GAIN relative to net carrying amount.
explanation: Net carrying amount = 2,380,000 − 238,000 = 2,142,000. Compare proceeds with that net amount: 2,261,000 − 2,142,000 = 119,000.00 gain. Derecognise both the gross asset and related allowance.
family: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset

title: Non-substantial liability modification gain • case 69
prompt: An amortised-cost liability is modified WITHOUT extinguishment, with no fees. Its carrying amount is LKR 1,690,000. The sole revised payment is 1,943,500 in two years. Original EIR is 10%; the modification is assessed as non-substantial. Find the immediate modification GAIN from recalculating amortised cost at the original EIR.
explanation: Revised amortised cost = 1,943,500/1.10² = 1,606,198.35. Gain = old liability 1,690,000 − revised PV = 83,801.65. The original EIR is retained for this non-extinguishing modification.

title: Credit-risk improvement allowance release • case 69
prompt: A debt asset under the GENERAL ECL model previously had significant credit-risk deterioration and lifetime allowance LKR 238,000. At reporting date the criteria for lifetime ECL are no longer met; required 12-month ECL is 44,500. No write-offs, new assets or other allowance movements occur. Find the impairment reversal in profit or loss.
explanation: When lifetime measurement is no longer required, the general model returns to 12-month ECL. Release the excess allowance: 238,000 − 44,500 = 193,500.00. This is not a receivable under mandatory simplified lifetime ECL.

title: Upstream inventory elimination with tax • case 69
prompt: P and S report profits AFTER their own tax of LKR 4,760,000 and 2,180,000. An upstream inventory sale leaves unrealised profit of 476,000 in group closing inventory. A recoverable DTA is recognised on the full elimination at 30%, with the tax effect in profit or loss. No other consolidation adjustments exist. Find TOTAL consolidated profit, before attribution to owners and NCI.
explanation: Combine separate after-tax profits, eliminate unrealised profit and recognise the recoverable tax benefit: 4,760,000 + 2,180,000 − 476,000 + 142,800.00 = 6,606,800.00. This question asks total group profit, not its attribution.

title: Full-goodwill impairment and owner profit • case 69
prompt: P owns 80% of S all year. Separate after-tax profits are P LKR 3,870,000 and S 1,390,000. Goodwill is recognised on the FULL-goodwill basis and an impairment of 545,000 is attributable to S’s CGU and allocated 80:20 between owners and NCI. No other adjustments or tax effects apply. Find consolidated profit attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Owners receive 80% of S’s profit and bear 80% of the full-goodwill loss: 3,870,000 + 80% × (1,390,000 − 545,000) = 4,546,000.00. Do not charge the owners with 100% of this full-goodwill loss.

title: Partial goodwill CGU gross-up • case 69
prompt: P owns 80% of S. Recognised PARTIAL goodwill is LKR 1,904,000; S’s other net assets in the tested CGU carry at 9,520,000. Recoverable amount of the WHOLE CGU is 10,710,000. Gross up goodwill for unrecognised NCI goodwill when testing; the whole impairment falls within grossed-up goodwill. No tax or other adjustments apply. Find impairment actually recognised on group goodwill.
explanation: Grossed-up goodwill = 1,904,000/80% = 2,380,000.00. Whole-CGU impairment = grossed goodwill + other net assets − recoverable amount = 1,190,000.00. Only the parent’s 80% goodwill portion is recognised, so recorded loss = 952,000.00.
reference: LKAS 36 Appendix C paras C4–C8; SLFRS 10 para B86

title: Consolidated retained earnings bridge • case 69
prompt: P owns 75% of S. At year end P retained earnings are LKR 6,450,000, and S retained earnings 4,070,000. S retained earnings at acquisition were 1,000,000. Cumulative post-acquisition extra FV depreciation is 238,000. A downstream sale by P leaves unrealised profit of 149,000. No tax, goodwill impairment, dividends recognised by P, OCI or other adjustments apply. Find consolidated retained earnings attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Group owners’ retained earnings = parent RE + 75% of adjusted post-acquisition S reserves − the parent’s downstream unrealised profit: 8,425,000.00. Pre-acquisition reserves do not enter post-acquisition group retained earnings.

title: Loss of control and translation reserve • case 69
prompt: P loses control of a foreign subsidiary. Proceeds are LKR 4,960,000; retained interest FV 1,190,000; NCI carrying amount 645,000; consolidated net assets INCLUDING goodwill 4,670,000. A cumulative translation GAIN of 238,000, entirely attributable to P, must be reclassified to profit or loss on loss of control. No other effects apply. Find total disposal gain including that reclassification.
explanation: Base gain = proceeds + retained FV + NCI − net assets = 2,125,000.00. Add the parent’s translation gain recycled on disposal: 238,000. Total = 2,363,000.00.
family: Loss of control and translation reserve

title: Residual guarantee expected payment • case 69
prompt: A lessee owes three year-end rentals of LKR 545,000. It guarantees residual value up to 200,000, but the amount EXPECTED to be payable under that guarantee is 99,000 at year three. Discount rate is 10%. No other liability payments exist. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the amount expected to be payable, not automatically the maximum guarantee. Liability = PV of three rentals + 99,000/1.10³ = 1,429,714.50.

title: Reasonably certain purchase option PV • case 69
prompt: A lease requires three year-end rentals of LKR 495,000, plus a purchase option price of 1,190,000 payable at year three. Exercise is reasonably certain. Discount rate is 10%. No incentives, other payments or initial prepayments apply. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the reasonably certain purchase price in the liability: PV of rentals + purchase price discounted for three years = 2,125,056.35. Do not omit or leave the future option payment undiscounted.

title: Lease and service component allocation • case 69
prompt: A two-year contract requires bundled payments of LKR 595,000 at each year end. Relative stand-alone prices are equipment lease 200,000 and distinct maintenance 50,000 per year. The lessee does NOT elect to combine components. Lease discount rate is 10%; no other payments exist. Find initial lease liability for the LEASE component only.
explanation: Allocate 200,000/250,000 = 80% of each bundled payment to the lease: 476,000.00. Discount those two lease payments, excluding maintenance, to obtain 826,115.70.

title: Exempt short-term lease rent-free start • case 69
prompt: A twelve-month lease with no purchase option qualifies for the elected short-term exemption. The first three months are rent free, then nine monthly payments of LKR 54,500 are due. The asset is available throughout and straight-line expense is appropriate. Find lease expense for the FIRST six months, ignoring accrual settlement timing.
explanation: Total fixed payments are nine rents. Spread evenly over all twelve months: 54,500 × 9/12 × 6 = 245,250.00. Rent-free months still receive an expense allocation.

title: Sale-and-leaseback rights transferred • case 69
prompt: A transfer qualifies as a sale under SLFRS 15 at fair value LKR 23,800,000; asset carrying amount is 12,900,000. Market-rate leaseback payments have PV 9,520,000. There are no off-market adjustments or variable-payment complications. At inception, what sale gain is recognised for rights TRANSFERRED to the buyer-lessor?
explanation: Total gain = 23,800,000 − 12,900,000 = 10,900,000. Retained-use proportion = lease PV / fair value = 40%. Recognise only the transferred-rights proportion of the gain: 6,540,000.00.

title: Reassessed bargain purchase gain • case 69
prompt: After the required reassessment, final acquisition-date consideration is LKR 4,760,000, NCI fair value is 400,000 and identifiable net assets are 7,140,000. There is no prior holding or other adjustment. Find the bargain purchase gain recognised in profit or loss.
explanation: Net identifiable assets exceed consideration plus NCI: 7,140,000 − 4,760,000 − 400,000 = 1,980,000.00. Reassessment has been completed before recognising the gain.

title: Acquired contingent liability in goodwill • case 69
prompt: Consideration is LKR 6,950,000; NCI FV is 500,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired contingent liability are 5,070,000. The acquired item is a present obligation with reliably measurable FV 545,000 and qualifies for recognition despite non-probable outflow. No tax or other adjustment applies. Find goodwill after recognising it.
explanation: Recognise the qualifying acquired liability: net identifiable assets become 5,070,000 − 545,000. Goodwill = consideration + NCI − adjusted net assets = 2,925,000.00.

title: Separate acquired brand from goodwill • case 69
prompt: Consideration is LKR 6,450,000; NCI FV 600,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired separable brand are 5,360,000. Brand FV is 1,090,000; tax base is zero and 30% DTL must be recognised. No other adjustments apply. Find goodwill after separate brand and tax recognition.
explanation: An identifiable acquired brand is separate from goodwill. Net addition to identifiable assets = brand FV − 30% DTL = 763,000.00. Goodwill = 6,450,000 + 600,000 − (5,360,000 + 763,000.00) = 927,000.00.

title: Acquisition costs versus issue costs • case 69
prompt: A business acquisition has consideration LKR 4,070,000. Additional costs are acquisition advisory 238,000, qualifying equity-issue costs 70,000 and qualifying debt-issue costs 40,000. The issue costs follow their relevant standards, and no immediate debt-cost amortisation or other expense arises this period. Find the immediate acquisition-related PROFIT-OR-LOSS expense from these costs.
explanation: Expense advisory acquisition costs of 238,000.00. Qualifying equity and debt issuance costs follow their respective standards and are not added to this immediate acquisition-service expense or goodwill.

title: Temporary difference and enacted rate change • case 69
prompt: A taxable temporary difference opens at LKR 200,000 with a DTL measured at 25%. At year end the difference is 645,000 and the enacted rate expected on reversal is 30%. Both the underlying movements and rate change belong in profit or loss. No other tax movements exist. Find deferred tax expense for the year.
explanation: Opening DTL = 200,000×25% = 50,000. Closing DTL = 645,000×30% = 193,500.00. Expense is the full increase, including rate remeasurement: 143,500.00. Rates are exercise assumptions.
family: Temporary difference and enacted rate change

title: Revalued non-depreciable land tax basis • case 69
prompt: Non-depreciable land is revalued from cost LKR 2,380,000 to fair value 3,570,000; tax base remains cost. The enacted rate for recovery through SALE is 20%, while a 30% use rate would otherwise apply. The revaluation and associated tax go to OCI. No other effects exist. Find the net OCI revaluation increase after deferred tax.
explanation: For this non-depreciable revalued asset, measure tax consequences on recovery through sale: DTL = (3,570,000 − 2,380,000)×20%. Net OCI increase = gross uplift less that DTL = 952,000.00.

title: Current tax reconciliation and prepayment • case 69
prompt: Accounting pretax profit is LKR 5,450,000. It includes a permanently non-deductible fine of 238,000, exempt income of 50,000, and warranty expense of 545,000 deductible only on payment. Current-year warranty payments of 80,000 are deductible and were charged against the provision, not current profit. Tax rate is 30%; tax prepayments are 300,000. No other tax adjustments exist. Find closing CURRENT tax payable, not total tax expense.
explanation: Taxable profit = 5,450,000 + fine 238,000 − exempt income 50,000 + provision expense 545,000 − deductible payments 80,000 = 6,103,000. Current tax less prepaid 300,000 = 1,530,900.00. Deferred tax is separate.

title: Consolidated inventory tax difference • case 69
prompt: After eliminating an intragroup profit, inventory carries in consolidated statements at LKR 1,428,000. Its tax base in the buyer’s tax jurisdiction is 2,142,000. The buyer’s enacted rate is 30%; sufficient taxable profit is probable. No offsetting, exception or other tax effects apply. Find the consolidated DTA on this inventory.
explanation: The consolidated carrying amount is below tax base, creating a deductible temporary difference of 714,000. Use the buyer’s relevant tax rate: difference ×30% = 214,200.00.

title: Depreciation after recognised impairment • case 69
prompt: Immediately before an impairment, equipment carries at LKR 2,380,000. Recoverable amount is 1,390,000 and impairment is recognised. After that date it has four years’ remaining useful life and residual value 100,000. Straight-line depreciation is appropriate; no further revaluation or impairment applies. Find depreciation for the next FULL year.
explanation: First reduce the asset to recoverable amount 1,390,000. Thereafter allocate revised depreciable amount over remaining life: (1,390,000 − 100,000)/4 = 322,500.00.

title: Allocated headquarters in CGU impairment • case 69
prompt: CGU A carries operating assets of LKR 1,290,000; CGU B carries 400,000. A headquarters asset of 200,000 can be allocated reasonably and consistently in proportion to those operating-asset amounts. A’s recoverable amount INCLUDING its headquarters share is 995,000. No goodwill or other assets exist. Find the impairment loss for A including its allocation.
explanation: Allocate headquarters to A: 200,000 × 1,290,000/(1,290,000+400,000) = 152,662.72. Tested A carrying amount is 1,442,662.72. Impairment versus recoverable amount 995,000 = 447,662.72.

title: Break-even value-in-use cash flow • case 69
prompt: An asset carries at LKR 2,380,000. Its fair value less costs of disposal is lower. A valid VIU model uses THREE equal year-end operating cash inflows, plus 100,000 net disposal proceeds at year three, discounted at 10%. What minimum equal ANNUAL operating cash inflow makes VIU exactly equal carrying amount? Ignore tax and other adjustments.
explanation: Let annual flow be X. X×(1/1.10 + 1/1.10² + 1/1.10³) + 100,000/1.10³ = 2,380,000. Solve for X = 926,821.75. This sensitivity calculation identifies the VIU break-even point.

title: Discounted warranty expected-value portfolio • case 69
prompt: A present warranty obligation covers 2,380 products. Per product, probabilities are 70% no defect, 25% a minor repair costing LKR 400, and 5% a major repair costing 2,000. All expected payments occur exactly in TWO years. Outflow for the portfolio is probable; appropriate discount rate is 10% with no risk double counting. Find the provision.
explanation: Expected cash payment = 2,380×(25%×400 + 5%×2,000) = 476,000.0. Discount two years at 10%: 476,000.0/1.10² = 393,388.43. The probability assessment applies to the portfolio.

title: Provision movement with revised estimate • case 69
prompt: A discounted provision opens at LKR 1,190,000. Unwinding for a full year is at 8%. A 100,000 settlement occurs at the year END, after unwinding. At that same reporting date, a new estimate increases the remaining provision by 188,000. No other changes occur. Find closing provision.
explanation: Closing = opening + 8% unwinding − year-end settlement + estimate increase: 1,190,000×1.08 −100,000 +188,000 = 1,373,200.00. Classification of the estimate change’s counterpart is assessed separately.

title: Revaluation increase after earlier loss • case 69
prompt: PPE carries at LKR 1,290,000 before revaluation and is revalued to 2,380,000. A prior revaluation decrease on THIS asset of 288,000 was recognised in profit or loss and has not been reversed. No tax effects apply. Find the current increase recognised in OCI after reversing the eligible prior loss in profit or loss.
explanation: Gross increase = 2,380,000 − 1,290,000 = 1,090,000. First recognise 288,000 in profit or loss to reverse the prior decrease. Remaining 802,000.00 is OCI revaluation surplus.

title: Nine-month depreciation and disposal gain • case 69
prompt: Equipment cost LKR 2,580,000, residual value 200,000 and useful life five years, straight-line. Two FULL years’ depreciation were recognised before this year. It is sold after nine months of the current year for 1,885,000. It was not previously held for sale and no impairment or revaluation applies. Find disposal GAIN after the required nine-month depreciation.
explanation: Annual depreciation = (2,580,000−200,000)/5. Deduct two full years and another 9/12 year from cost to obtain disposal-date carrying amount 1,271,000.00. Gain = proceeds − that amount = 614,000.00.

title: Customer collections with a write-off • case 69
prompt: All sales are on credit. Revenue is LKR 6,450,000; opening GROSS trade receivables are 600,000; closing GROSS receivables are 1,490,000. Receivables of 169,000 were written off during the year. There are no taxes, returns, contract balances, acquisitions or exchange changes. Find cash collected from customers.
explanation: Gross receivable roll-forward: opening + credit sales − cash receipts − write-offs = closing. Thus receipts = 6,450,000+600,000−1,490,000−169,000 = 5,391,000.00. Write-offs are not cash receipts.

title: Loan funding net cash effect • case 69
prompt: A company receives cash loan proceeds of LKR 2,380,000 and immediately pays a directly attributable lender issue fee of 54,500. Both payments are classified as financing cash flows in this case. No other cash movement occurs. Find the NET financing cash inflow from these two cash movements; this question does not require net line-item presentation.
explanation: Net financing cash effect = proceeds − cash fee = 2,380,000 − 54,500.00 = 2,325,500.00. Effective-interest amortisation later is not another inception cash payment.

title: Item-by-item NRV without offsetting headroom • case 69
prompt: Two unrelated inventory lines require separate NRV tests. A has 445 units, cost LKR 1,000 and NRV 900 each. B has 238 units, cost 1,000 and NRV 1,200 each. There is no basis to group them for the write-down test. Find TOTAL closing inventory carrying amount.
explanation: Carry A at 900 per unit and B at its lower cost of 1,000. Total = 445×900 + 238×1,000 = 638,500.00. B’s NRV headroom cannot offset A’s write-down.

title: Units-of-production intangible amortisation • case 69
prompt: A finite-life production licence costs LKR 2,280,000, has zero residual value, and is expected to support 150,000 units in total. Actual output this year is 64,500 units. A units-of-production method reliably reflects consumption and the asset was available throughout. No impairment or estimate change applies. Find annual amortisation.
explanation: Apply the supported consumption pattern: amortisation = 2,280,000 × 64,500/150,000 = 980,400.00. It is the share of expected lifetime production consumed, not an automatic straight-line charge.

title: Profit after suspended associate losses • case 69
prompt: An equity-method investment and relevant long-term interests were previously reduced to zero. Unrecognised share of prior losses totals LKR 218,000; the investor has no obligation and made no support payments. In the current year its share of associate profit is 327,000. No other adjustments or changes in interest apply. Find the share of profit that can now be RECOGNISED.
explanation: First absorb unrecognised prior losses before resuming recognised profit. Recognised amount = current profit share 327,000 − prior unrecognised losses 218,000 = 109,000.00.

title: Return recovery asset net of costs • case 70
prompt: A retailer has transferred 2,750 products. It expects 110 to be returned. Each returned product originally cost LKR 600; expected recovery handling is 20 per item and expected value deterioration is 30 per item. Estimates meet the relevant requirements. Find the separate asset for the right to recover returned products, excluding the refund liability.
explanation: Recovery asset = original carrying amount of expected returns less recovery costs and potential value decrease: 110 × (600 − 20 − 30) = 60,500.00. It is assessed separately from the customer refund liability.
family: Return recovery asset net of costs

title: Retrospective volume rebate true-up • case 70
prompt: A customer’s annual purchases reach 17,000 units at list price LKR 200. Crossing the threshold entitles it to a 5% retrospective rebate on ALL units. Cumulative revenue before this new supported estimate equals full list price; no rebate was previously accrued. The constraint permits the estimate. Find the reduction in cumulative revenue required now.
explanation: The revised transaction price reflects the retrospective rebate on all units. Revenue reduction = 17,000 × 200 × 5% = 170,000.00. Recognise the corresponding refund obligation as appropriate.

title: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation • case 70
prompt: A bundle has distinct goods A and B with stand-alone prices LKR 550,000 and 1,000,000. Total transaction price is 1,430,000. ALL paragraph 82 criteria demonstrate that the whole 120,000 discount relates only to A. A transfers now; B is not yet delivered. Find revenue recognised for A.
explanation: The specified discount-allocation exception applies. Allocate all 120,000 discount to A: 550,000 − 120,000 = 430,000.00. Do not default to relative allocation when the exception’s criteria are met.
family: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation

title: Three obligations and partial service • case 70
