explanation: Carry A at 900 per unit and B at its lower cost of 1,000. Total = 475×900 + 250×1,000 = 677,500.00. B’s NRV headroom cannot offset A’s write-down.

title: Units-of-production intangible amortisation • case 75
prompt: A finite-life production licence costs LKR 2,400,000, has zero residual value, and is expected to support 150,000 units in total. Actual output this year is 67,500 units. A units-of-production method reliably reflects consumption and the asset was available throughout. No impairment or estimate change applies. Find annual amortisation.
explanation: Apply the supported consumption pattern: amortisation = 2,400,000 × 67,500/150,000 = 1,080,000.00. It is the share of expected lifetime production consumed, not an automatic straight-line charge.

title: Profit after suspended associate losses • case 75
prompt: An equity-method investment and relevant long-term interests were previously reduced to zero. Unrecognised share of prior losses totals LKR 230,000; the investor has no obligation and made no support payments. In the current year its share of associate profit is 345,000. No other adjustments or changes in interest apply. Find the share of profit that can now be RECOGNISED.
explanation: First absorb unrecognised prior losses before resuming recognised profit. Recognised amount = current profit share 345,000 − prior unrecognised losses 230,000 = 115,000.00.

title: Return recovery asset net of costs • case 76
prompt: A retailer has transferred 2,900 products. It expects 116 to be returned. Each returned product originally cost LKR 600; expected recovery handling is 20 per item and expected value deterioration is 30 per item. Estimates meet the relevant requirements. Find the separate asset for the right to recover returned products, excluding the refund liability.
explanation: Recovery asset = original carrying amount of expected returns less recovery costs and potential value decrease: 116 × (600 − 20 − 30) = 63,800.00. It is assessed separately from the customer refund liability.
family: Return recovery asset net of costs

title: Retrospective volume rebate true-up • case 76
prompt: A customer’s annual purchases reach 17,600 units at list price LKR 200. Crossing the threshold entitles it to a 5% retrospective rebate on ALL units. Cumulative revenue before this new supported estimate equals full list price; no rebate was previously accrued. The constraint permits the estimate. Find the reduction in cumulative revenue required now.
explanation: The revised transaction price reflects the retrospective rebate on all units. Revenue reduction = 17,600 × 200 × 5% = 176,000.00. Recognise the corresponding refund obligation as appropriate.

title: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation • case 76
prompt: A bundle has distinct goods A and B with stand-alone prices LKR 580,000 and 1,060,000. Total transaction price is 1,514,000. ALL paragraph 82 criteria demonstrate that the whole 126,000 discount relates only to A. A transfers now; B is not yet delivered. Find revenue recognised for A.
explanation: The specified discount-allocation exception applies. Allocate all 126,000 discount to A: 580,000 − 126,000 = 454,000.00. Do not default to relative allocation when the exception’s criteria are met.
family: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation

title: Three obligations and partial service • case 76
prompt: A contract price of LKR 3,480,000 covers goods A, goods B and twelve months of distinct support. Stand-alone prices are 600,000, 300,000 and 300,000 respectively. A is delivered, B is not, and six months of evenly provided support are complete. No allocation exception applies. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise allocation to A plus half of support: 3,480,000 × (600,000 + 150,000) / 1,200,000 = 2,175,000.00. B’s allocation remains unrecognised as revenue.

title: Progress excluding abnormal waste • case 76
prompt: An over-time contract has transaction price LKR 17,600,000. Costs incurred are 7,040,000, including abnormal waste of 352,000 that does not depict progress. Expected TOTAL productive costs excluding that waste are 14,080,000. Cost-to-cost is appropriate after excluding the waste; no other adjustment applies. Find cumulative revenue, not profit.
explanation: Exclude abnormal waste from the progress numerator. Productive progress = (7,040,000 − 352,000) / 14,080,000. Revenue = transaction price × that progress = 8,360,000.00. The wasted cost is not a revenue-producing input.

title: Uninstalled materials without margin • case 76
prompt: A single over-time construction obligation has price LKR 25,200,000. All B19(b) conditions justify recognising revenue equal to cost for significant uninstalled materials of 5,040,000 already controlled by the customer. Other productive costs incurred are 3,780,000; expected total OTHER costs are 15,120,000. No revenue was previously recognised. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise material revenue without margin: 5,040,000. Recognise the remaining price using other-cost progress: (25,200,000 − 5,040,000) × 3,780,000/15,120,000. Total revenue = 10,080,000.00.

title: Agent commission after collection • case 76
prompt: An intermediary is an AGENT and collects customer cash of LKR 4,800,000 for a completed supplier service. It must remit 88% to the supplier and is entitled to the remaining 12% commission. It controls neither the underlying service nor any distinct extra service, and there is no tax. Find its revenue.
explanation: An agent recognises its fee or commission, not the supplier’s gross billings: 4,800,000 × 12% = 576,000.00. The amount due to the supplier is separately accounted for.

title: Distinct remaining goods blended prospectively • case 76
prompt: At modification, 100 distinct goods remain under an existing contract at LKR 1,760 each. Another 50 distinct goods are added at 1,408 each. The modification is NOT a separate contract, but remaining goods are distinct from those already transferred, so paragraph 21(a) applies prospectively. Thirty of the remaining goods are then transferred. Find revenue for those thirty.
explanation: Prospective remaining consideration = 100 × 1,760 + 50 × 1,408. Divide by 150 remaining goods, then multiply by 30 = 49,280.00. Do not retrospectively revise revenue on goods already transferred.

title: FVTPL acquisition expense • case 76
prompt: A financial asset is acquired at fair value LKR 2,320,000 and is classified at FVTPL. Directly attributable broker costs are 58,000, paid separately. No fair-value change occurs immediately after purchase. Find the immediate profit-or-loss expense from acquiring this asset.
explanation: Transaction costs on an FVTPL asset are expensed. Initial asset carrying amount is fair value 2,320,000; immediate acquisition expense is 58,000.00.

title: Collateral cash-shortfall discounting • case 76
prompt: A credit loss scenario has a contractual receipt of LKR 2,900,000 due in one year. The ONLY expected recovery at that same date is collateral sale proceeds of 1,840,000, less sale costs of 126,000. Scenario probability is 100% and original EIR is 10%. Collateral is an integral contractual credit enhancement and not separately recognised. Find discounted ECL.
explanation: One-year shortfall = contractual receipt − net collateral recovery = 2,900,000 − (1,840,000 − 126,000). Discount that shortfall at 10%: 1,078,181.82. Do not ignore recovery costs or discount only one side of same-date cash flows.

title: Three-band provision matrix • case 76
prompt: Under the simplified lifetime-ECL approach, supported adjusted loss rates are 1% on current receivables of LKR 2,520,000, 5% on past-due balances of 680,000, and 30% on severely overdue balances of 252,000. Rates already include all required forward-looking and discounting effects. Find total loss allowance.
explanation: Apply each appropriate band rate and add: 2,520,000×1% + 680,000×5% + 252,000×30% = 134,800.00. Do not apply one blended band mechanically to all balances.

title: Equity FVOCI profit-or-loss dividend • case 76
prompt: An eligible equity investment has the irrevocable FVOCI election. During the year it gains LKR 272,000 in fair value and earns a dividend of 136,000. Dividend recognition criteria are met and the dividend clearly represents a return on investment, not recovery of cost. There are no other effects. Find income recognised in PROFIT OR LOSS.
explanation: The qualifying dividend of 136,000.00 is profit-or-loss income. The fair-value movement of 272,000 is OCI under this election and is not added to the profit-or-loss amount.

title: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset • case 76
prompt: A loan is sold with full derecognition. Immediately before sale, gross carrying amount is LKR 2,520,000, loss allowance 252,000, and cash proceeds 2,394,000. No accumulated OCI, sale fees or other adjustments exist. Find the derecognition GAIN relative to net carrying amount.
explanation: Net carrying amount = 2,520,000 − 252,000 = 2,268,000. Compare proceeds with that net amount: 2,394,000 − 2,268,000 = 126,000.00 gain. Derecognise both the gross asset and related allowance.
family: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset

title: Non-substantial liability modification gain • case 76
prompt: An amortised-cost liability is modified WITHOUT extinguishment, with no fees. Its carrying amount is LKR 1,760,000. The sole revised payment is 2,024,000 in two years. Original EIR is 10%; the modification is assessed as non-substantial. Find the immediate modification GAIN from recalculating amortised cost at the original EIR.
explanation: Revised amortised cost = 2,024,000/1.10² = 1,672,727.27. Gain = old liability 1,760,000 − revised PV = 87,272.73. The original EIR is retained for this non-extinguishing modification.

title: Credit-risk improvement allowance release • case 76
prompt: A debt asset under the GENERAL ECL model previously had significant credit-risk deterioration and lifetime allowance LKR 252,000. At reporting date the criteria for lifetime ECL are no longer met; required 12-month ECL is 48,000. No write-offs, new assets or other allowance movements occur. Find the impairment reversal in profit or loss.
explanation: When lifetime measurement is no longer required, the general model returns to 12-month ECL. Release the excess allowance: 252,000 − 48,000 = 204,000.00. This is not a receivable under mandatory simplified lifetime ECL.

title: Upstream inventory elimination with tax • case 76
prompt: P and S report profits AFTER their own tax of LKR 5,040,000 and 2,320,000. An upstream inventory sale leaves unrealised profit of 504,000 in group closing inventory. A recoverable DTA is recognised on the full elimination at 30%, with the tax effect in profit or loss. No other consolidation adjustments exist. Find TOTAL consolidated profit, before attribution to owners and NCI.
explanation: Combine separate after-tax profits, eliminate unrealised profit and recognise the recoverable tax benefit: 5,040,000 + 2,320,000 − 504,000 + 151,200.00 = 7,007,200.00. This question asks total group profit, not its attribution.

title: Full-goodwill impairment and owner profit • case 76
prompt: P owns 80% of S all year. Separate after-tax profits are P LKR 4,080,000 and S 1,460,000. Goodwill is recognised on the FULL-goodwill basis and an impairment of 580,000 is attributable to S’s CGU and allocated 80:20 between owners and NCI. No other adjustments or tax effects apply. Find consolidated profit attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Owners receive 80% of S’s profit and bear 80% of the full-goodwill loss: 4,080,000 + 80% × (1,460,000 − 580,000) = 4,784,000.00. Do not charge the owners with 100% of this full-goodwill loss.

title: Partial goodwill CGU gross-up • case 76
prompt: P owns 80% of S. Recognised PARTIAL goodwill is LKR 2,016,000; S’s other net assets in the tested CGU carry at 10,080,000. Recoverable amount of the WHOLE CGU is 11,340,000. Gross up goodwill for unrecognised NCI goodwill when testing; the whole impairment falls within grossed-up goodwill. No tax or other adjustments apply. Find impairment actually recognised on group goodwill.
explanation: Grossed-up goodwill = 2,016,000/80% = 2,520,000.00. Whole-CGU impairment = grossed goodwill + other net assets − recoverable amount = 1,260,000.00. Only the parent’s 80% goodwill portion is recognised, so recorded loss = 1,008,000.00.
reference: LKAS 36 Appendix C paras C4–C8; SLFRS 10 para B86

title: Consolidated retained earnings bridge • case 76
prompt: P owns 75% of S. At year end P retained earnings are LKR 6,800,000, and S retained earnings 4,280,000. S retained earnings at acquisition were 1,000,000. Cumulative post-acquisition extra FV depreciation is 252,000. A downstream sale by P leaves unrealised profit of 156,000. No tax, goodwill impairment, dividends recognised by P, OCI or other adjustments apply. Find consolidated retained earnings attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Group owners’ retained earnings = parent RE + 75% of adjusted post-acquisition S reserves − the parent’s downstream unrealised profit: 8,915,000.00. Pre-acquisition reserves do not enter post-acquisition group retained earnings.

title: Loss of control and translation reserve • case 76
prompt: P loses control of a foreign subsidiary. Proceeds are LKR 5,240,000; retained interest FV 1,260,000; NCI carrying amount 680,000; consolidated net assets INCLUDING goodwill 4,880,000. A cumulative translation GAIN of 252,000, entirely attributable to P, must be reclassified to profit or loss on loss of control. No other effects apply. Find total disposal gain including that reclassification.
explanation: Base gain = proceeds + retained FV + NCI − net assets = 2,300,000.00. Add the parent’s translation gain recycled on disposal: 252,000. Total = 2,552,000.00.
family: Loss of control and translation reserve

title: Residual guarantee expected payment • case 76
prompt: A lessee owes three year-end rentals of LKR 580,000. It guarantees residual value up to 200,000, but the amount EXPECTED to be payable under that guarantee is 106,000 at year three. Discount rate is 10%. No other liability payments exist. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the amount expected to be payable, not automatically the maximum guarantee. Liability = PV of three rentals + 106,000/1.10³ = 1,522,013.52.

title: Reasonably certain purchase option PV • case 76
prompt: A lease requires three year-end rentals of LKR 530,000, plus a purchase option price of 1,260,000 payable at year three. Exercise is reasonably certain. Discount rate is 10%. No incentives, other payments or initial prepayments apply. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the reasonably certain purchase price in the liability: PV of rentals + purchase price discounted for three years = 2,264,688.20. Do not omit or leave the future option payment undiscounted.

title: Lease and service component allocation • case 76
prompt: A two-year contract requires bundled payments of LKR 630,000 at each year end. Relative stand-alone prices are equipment lease 200,000 and distinct maintenance 50,000 per year. The lessee does NOT elect to combine components. Lease discount rate is 10%; no other payments exist. Find initial lease liability for the LEASE component only.
explanation: Allocate 200,000/250,000 = 80% of each bundled payment to the lease: 504,000.00. Discount those two lease payments, excluding maintenance, to obtain 874,710.74.

title: Exempt short-term lease rent-free start • case 76
prompt: A twelve-month lease with no purchase option qualifies for the elected short-term exemption. The first three months are rent free, then nine monthly payments of LKR 58,000 are due. The asset is available throughout and straight-line expense is appropriate. Find lease expense for the FIRST six months, ignoring accrual settlement timing.
explanation: Total fixed payments are nine rents. Spread evenly over all twelve months: 58,000 × 9/12 × 6 = 261,000.00. Rent-free months still receive an expense allocation.

title: Sale-and-leaseback rights transferred • case 76
prompt: A transfer qualifies as a sale under SLFRS 15 at fair value LKR 25,200,000; asset carrying amount is 13,600,000. Market-rate leaseback payments have PV 10,080,000. There are no off-market adjustments or variable-payment complications. At inception, what sale gain is recognised for rights TRANSFERRED to the buyer-lessor?
explanation: Total gain = 25,200,000 − 13,600,000 = 11,600,000. Retained-use proportion = lease PV / fair value = 40%. Recognise only the transferred-rights proportion of the gain: 6,960,000.00.

title: Reassessed bargain purchase gain • case 76
prompt: After the required reassessment, final acquisition-date consideration is LKR 5,040,000, NCI fair value is 400,000 and identifiable net assets are 7,560,000. There is no prior holding or other adjustment. Find the bargain purchase gain recognised in profit or loss.
explanation: Net identifiable assets exceed consideration plus NCI: 7,560,000 − 5,040,000 − 400,000 = 2,120,000.00. Reassessment has been completed before recognising the gain.

title: Acquired contingent liability in goodwill • case 76
prompt: Consideration is LKR 7,300,000; NCI FV is 500,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired contingent liability are 5,280,000. The acquired item is a present obligation with reliably measurable FV 580,000 and qualifies for recognition despite non-probable outflow. No tax or other adjustment applies. Find goodwill after recognising it.
explanation: Recognise the qualifying acquired liability: net identifiable assets become 5,280,000 − 580,000. Goodwill = consideration + NCI − adjusted net assets = 3,100,000.00.

title: Separate acquired brand from goodwill • case 76
prompt: Consideration is LKR 6,800,000; NCI FV 600,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired separable brand are 5,640,000. Brand FV is 1,160,000; tax base is zero and 30% DTL must be recognised. No other adjustments apply. Find goodwill after separate brand and tax recognition.
explanation: An identifiable acquired brand is separate from goodwill. Net addition to identifiable assets = brand FV − 30% DTL = 812,000.00. Goodwill = 6,800,000 + 600,000 − (5,640,000 + 812,000.00) = 948,000.00.

title: Acquisition costs versus issue costs • case 76
prompt: A business acquisition has consideration LKR 4,280,000. Additional costs are acquisition advisory 252,000, qualifying equity-issue costs 70,000 and qualifying debt-issue costs 40,000. The issue costs follow their relevant standards, and no immediate debt-cost amortisation or other expense arises this period. Find the immediate acquisition-related PROFIT-OR-LOSS expense from these costs.
explanation: Expense advisory acquisition costs of 252,000.00. Qualifying equity and debt issuance costs follow their respective standards and are not added to this immediate acquisition-service expense or goodwill.

title: Temporary difference and enacted rate change • case 76
prompt: A taxable temporary difference opens at LKR 200,000 with a DTL measured at 25%. At year end the difference is 680,000 and the enacted rate expected on reversal is 30%. Both the underlying movements and rate change belong in profit or loss. No other tax movements exist. Find deferred tax expense for the year.
explanation: Opening DTL = 200,000×25% = 50,000. Closing DTL = 680,000×30% = 204,000.00. Expense is the full increase, including rate remeasurement: 154,000.00. Rates are exercise assumptions.
family: Temporary difference and enacted rate change

title: Revalued non-depreciable land tax basis • case 76
prompt: Non-depreciable land is revalued from cost LKR 2,520,000 to fair value 3,780,000; tax base remains cost. The enacted rate for recovery through SALE is 20%, while a 30% use rate would otherwise apply. The revaluation and associated tax go to OCI. No other effects exist. Find the net OCI revaluation increase after deferred tax.
explanation: For this non-depreciable revalued asset, measure tax consequences on recovery through sale: DTL = (3,780,000 − 2,520,000)×20%. Net OCI increase = gross uplift less that DTL = 1,008,000.00.

title: Current tax reconciliation and prepayment • case 76
prompt: Accounting pretax profit is LKR 5,800,000. It includes a permanently non-deductible fine of 252,000, exempt income of 50,000, and warranty expense of 580,000 deductible only on payment. Current-year warranty payments of 80,000 are deductible and were charged against the provision, not current profit. Tax rate is 30%; tax prepayments are 300,000. No other tax adjustments exist. Find closing CURRENT tax payable, not total tax expense.
explanation: Taxable profit = 5,800,000 + fine 252,000 − exempt income 50,000 + provision expense 580,000 − deductible payments 80,000 = 6,502,000. Current tax less prepaid 300,000 = 1,650,600.00. Deferred tax is separate.

title: Consolidated inventory tax difference • case 76
prompt: After eliminating an intragroup profit, inventory carries in consolidated statements at LKR 1,512,000. Its tax base in the buyer’s tax jurisdiction is 2,268,000. The buyer’s enacted rate is 30%; sufficient taxable profit is probable. No offsetting, exception or other tax effects apply. Find the consolidated DTA on this inventory.
explanation: The consolidated carrying amount is below tax base, creating a deductible temporary difference of 756,000. Use the buyer’s relevant tax rate: difference ×30% = 226,800.00.

title: Depreciation after recognised impairment • case 76
prompt: Immediately before an impairment, equipment carries at LKR 2,520,000. Recoverable amount is 1,460,000 and impairment is recognised. After that date it has four years’ remaining useful life and residual value 100,000. Straight-line depreciation is appropriate; no further revaluation or impairment applies. Find depreciation for the next FULL year.
explanation: First reduce the asset to recoverable amount 1,460,000. Thereafter allocate revised depreciable amount over remaining life: (1,460,000 − 100,000)/4 = 340,000.00.

title: Allocated headquarters in CGU impairment • case 76
prompt: CGU A carries operating assets of LKR 1,360,000; CGU B carries 400,000. A headquarters asset of 200,000 can be allocated reasonably and consistently in proportion to those operating-asset amounts. A’s recoverable amount INCLUDING its headquarters share is 1,030,000. No goodwill or other assets exist. Find the impairment loss for A including its allocation.
explanation: Allocate headquarters to A: 200,000 × 1,360,000/(1,360,000+400,000) = 154,545.45. Tested A carrying amount is 1,514,545.45. Impairment versus recoverable amount 1,030,000 = 484,545.45.

title: Break-even value-in-use cash flow • case 76
prompt: An asset carries at LKR 2,520,000. Its fair value less costs of disposal is lower. A valid VIU model uses THREE equal year-end operating cash inflows, plus 100,000 net disposal proceeds at year three, discounted at 10%. What minimum equal ANNUAL operating cash inflow makes VIU exactly equal carrying amount? Ignore tax and other adjustments.
explanation: Let annual flow be X. X×(1/1.10 + 1/1.10² + 1/1.10³) + 100,000/1.10³ = 2,520,000. Solve for X = 983,117.82. This sensitivity calculation identifies the VIU break-even point.

title: Discounted warranty expected-value portfolio • case 76
prompt: A present warranty obligation covers 2,520 products. Per product, probabilities are 70% no defect, 25% a minor repair costing LKR 400, and 5% a major repair costing 2,000. All expected payments occur exactly in TWO years. Outflow for the portfolio is probable; appropriate discount rate is 10% with no risk double counting. Find the provision.
explanation: Expected cash payment = 2,520×(25%×400 + 5%×2,000) = 504,000.0. Discount two years at 10%: 504,000.0/1.10² = 416,528.93. The probability assessment applies to the portfolio.

title: Provision movement with revised estimate • case 76
prompt: A discounted provision opens at LKR 1,260,000. Unwinding for a full year is at 8%. A 100,000 settlement occurs at the year END, after unwinding. At that same reporting date, a new estimate increases the remaining provision by 202,000. No other changes occur. Find closing provision.
explanation: Closing = opening + 8% unwinding − year-end settlement + estimate increase: 1,260,000×1.08 −100,000 +202,000 = 1,462,800.00. Classification of the estimate change’s counterpart is assessed separately.

title: Revaluation increase after earlier loss • case 76
prompt: PPE carries at LKR 1,360,000 before revaluation and is revalued to 2,520,000. A prior revaluation decrease on THIS asset of 302,000 was recognised in profit or loss and has not been reversed. No tax effects apply. Find the current increase recognised in OCI after reversing the eligible prior loss in profit or loss.
explanation: Gross increase = 2,520,000 − 1,360,000 = 1,160,000. First recognise 302,000 in profit or loss to reverse the prior decrease. Remaining 858,000.00 is OCI revaluation surplus.

title: Nine-month depreciation and disposal gain • case 76
prompt: Equipment cost LKR 2,720,000, residual value 200,000 and useful life five years, straight-line. Two FULL years’ depreciation were recognised before this year. It is sold after nine months of the current year for 1,990,000. It was not previously held for sale and no impairment or revaluation applies. Find disposal GAIN after the required nine-month depreciation.
explanation: Annual depreciation = (2,720,000−200,000)/5. Deduct two full years and another 9/12 year from cost to obtain disposal-date carrying amount 1,334,000.00. Gain = proceeds − that amount = 656,000.00.

title: Customer collections with a write-off • case 76
prompt: All sales are on credit. Revenue is LKR 6,800,000; opening GROSS trade receivables are 600,000; closing GROSS receivables are 1,560,000. Receivables of 176,000 were written off during the year. There are no taxes, returns, contract balances, acquisitions or exchange changes. Find cash collected from customers.
explanation: Gross receivable roll-forward: opening + credit sales − cash receipts − write-offs = closing. Thus receipts = 6,800,000+600,000−1,560,000−176,000 = 5,664,000.00. Write-offs are not cash receipts.

title: Loan funding net cash effect • case 76
prompt: A company receives cash loan proceeds of LKR 2,520,000 and immediately pays a directly attributable lender issue fee of 58,000. Both payments are classified as financing cash flows in this case. No other cash movement occurs. Find the NET financing cash inflow from these two cash movements; this question does not require net line-item presentation.
explanation: Net financing cash effect = proceeds − cash fee = 2,520,000 − 58,000.00 = 2,462,000.00. Effective-interest amortisation later is not another inception cash payment.

title: Item-by-item NRV without offsetting headroom • case 76
prompt: Two unrelated inventory lines require separate NRV tests. A has 480 units, cost LKR 1,000 and NRV 900 each. B has 252 units, cost 1,000 and NRV 1,200 each. There is no basis to group them for the write-down test. Find TOTAL closing inventory carrying amount.
explanation: Carry A at 900 per unit and B at its lower cost of 1,000. Total = 480×900 + 252×1,000 = 684,000.00. B’s NRV headroom cannot offset A’s write-down.

title: Units-of-production intangible amortisation • case 76
prompt: A finite-life production licence costs LKR 2,420,000, has zero residual value, and is expected to support 150,000 units in total. Actual output this year is 68,000 units. A units-of-production method reliably reflects consumption and the asset was available throughout. No impairment or estimate change applies. Find annual amortisation.
explanation: Apply the supported consumption pattern: amortisation = 2,420,000 × 68,000/150,000 = 1,097,066.67. It is the share of expected lifetime production consumed, not an automatic straight-line charge.

title: Profit after suspended associate losses • case 76
prompt: An equity-method investment and relevant long-term interests were previously reduced to zero. Unrecognised share of prior losses totals LKR 232,000; the investor has no obligation and made no support payments. In the current year its share of associate profit is 348,000. No other adjustments or changes in interest apply. Find the share of profit that can now be RECOGNISED.
explanation: First absorb unrecognised prior losses before resuming recognised profit. Recognised amount = current profit share 348,000 − prior unrecognised losses 232,000 = 116,000.00.

title: Return recovery asset net of costs • case 77
prompt: A retailer has transferred 2,925 products. It expects 117 to be returned. Each returned product originally cost LKR 600; expected recovery handling is 20 per item and expected value deterioration is 30 per item. Estimates meet the relevant requirements. Find the separate asset for the right to recover returned products, excluding the refund liability.
explanation: Recovery asset = original carrying amount of expected returns less recovery costs and potential value decrease: 117 × (600 − 20 − 30) = 64,350.00. It is assessed separately from the customer refund liability.
family: Return recovery asset net of costs

title: Retrospective volume rebate true-up • case 77
prompt: A customer’s annual purchases reach 17,700 units at list price LKR 200. Crossing the threshold entitles it to a 5% retrospective rebate on ALL units. Cumulative revenue before this new supported estimate equals full list price; no rebate was previously accrued. The constraint permits the estimate. Find the reduction in cumulative revenue required now.
explanation: The revised transaction price reflects the retrospective rebate on all units. Revenue reduction = 17,700 × 200 × 5% = 177,000.00. Recognise the corresponding refund obligation as appropriate.

title: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation • case 77
prompt: A bundle has distinct goods A and B with stand-alone prices LKR 585,000 and 1,070,000. Total transaction price is 1,528,000. ALL paragraph 82 criteria demonstrate that the whole 127,000 discount relates only to A. A transfers now; B is not yet delivered. Find revenue recognised for A.
explanation: The specified discount-allocation exception applies. Allocate all 127,000 discount to A: 585,000 − 127,000 = 458,000.00. Do not default to relative allocation when the exception’s criteria are met.
family: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation

title: Three obligations and partial service • case 77
prompt: A contract price of LKR 3,510,000 covers goods A, goods B and twelve months of distinct support. Stand-alone prices are 600,000, 300,000 and 300,000 respectively. A is delivered, B is not, and six months of evenly provided support are complete. No allocation exception applies. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise allocation to A plus half of support: 3,510,000 × (600,000 + 150,000) / 1,200,000 = 2,193,750.00. B’s allocation remains unrecognised as revenue.

title: Progress excluding abnormal waste • case 77
prompt: An over-time contract has transaction price LKR 17,700,000. Costs incurred are 7,080,000, including abnormal waste of 354,000 that does not depict progress. Expected TOTAL productive costs excluding that waste are 14,160,000. Cost-to-cost is appropriate after excluding the waste; no other adjustment applies. Find cumulative revenue, not profit.
explanation: Exclude abnormal waste from the progress numerator. Productive progress = (7,080,000 − 354,000) / 14,160,000. Revenue = transaction price × that progress = 8,407,500.00. The wasted cost is not a revenue-producing input.

title: Uninstalled materials without margin • case 77
prompt: A single over-time construction obligation has price LKR 25,400,000. All B19(b) conditions justify recognising revenue equal to cost for significant uninstalled materials of 5,080,000 already controlled by the customer. Other productive costs incurred are 3,810,000; expected total OTHER costs are 15,240,000. No revenue was previously recognised. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise material revenue without margin: 5,080,000. Recognise the remaining price using other-cost progress: (25,400,000 − 5,080,000) × 3,810,000/15,240,000. Total revenue = 10,160,000.00.

title: Agent commission after collection • case 77
prompt: An intermediary is an AGENT and collects customer cash of LKR 4,850,000 for a completed supplier service. It must remit 88% to the supplier and is entitled to the remaining 12% commission. It controls neither the underlying service nor any distinct extra service, and there is no tax. Find its revenue.
explanation: An agent recognises its fee or commission, not the supplier’s gross billings: 4,850,000 × 12% = 582,000.00. The amount due to the supplier is separately accounted for.

title: Distinct remaining goods blended prospectively • case 77
prompt: At modification, 100 distinct goods remain under an existing contract at LKR 1,770 each. Another 50 distinct goods are added at 1,416 each. The modification is NOT a separate contract, but remaining goods are distinct from those already transferred, so paragraph 21(a) applies prospectively. Thirty of the remaining goods are then transferred. Find revenue for those thirty.
explanation: Prospective remaining consideration = 100 × 1,770 + 50 × 1,416. Divide by 150 remaining goods, then multiply by 30 = 49,560.00. Do not retrospectively revise revenue on goods already transferred.

title: FVTPL acquisition expense • case 77
prompt: A financial asset is acquired at fair value LKR 2,340,000 and is classified at FVTPL. Directly attributable broker costs are 58,500, paid separately. No fair-value change occurs immediately after purchase. Find the immediate profit-or-loss expense from acquiring this asset.
explanation: Transaction costs on an FVTPL asset are expensed. Initial asset carrying amount is fair value 2,340,000; immediate acquisition expense is 58,500.00.

title: Collateral cash-shortfall discounting • case 77
prompt: A credit loss scenario has a contractual receipt of LKR 2,925,000 due in one year. The ONLY expected recovery at that same date is collateral sale proceeds of 1,855,000, less sale costs of 127,000. Scenario probability is 100% and original EIR is 10%. Collateral is an integral contractual credit enhancement and not separately recognised. Find discounted ECL.
explanation: One-year shortfall = contractual receipt − net collateral recovery = 2,925,000 − (1,855,000 − 127,000). Discount that shortfall at 10%: 1,088,181.82. Do not ignore recovery costs or discount only one side of same-date cash flows.

title: Three-band provision matrix • case 77
prompt: Under the simplified lifetime-ECL approach, supported adjusted loss rates are 1% on current receivables of LKR 2,540,000, 5% on past-due balances of 685,000, and 30% on severely overdue balances of 254,000. Rates already include all required forward-looking and discounting effects. Find total loss allowance.
explanation: Apply each appropriate band rate and add: 2,540,000×1% + 685,000×5% + 254,000×30% = 135,850.00. Do not apply one blended band mechanically to all balances.

title: Equity FVOCI profit-or-loss dividend • case 77
prompt: An eligible equity investment has the irrevocable FVOCI election. During the year it gains LKR 274,000 in fair value and earns a dividend of 137,000. Dividend recognition criteria are met and the dividend clearly represents a return on investment, not recovery of cost. There are no other effects. Find income recognised in PROFIT OR LOSS.
explanation: The qualifying dividend of 137,000.00 is profit-or-loss income. The fair-value movement of 274,000 is OCI under this election and is not added to the profit-or-loss amount.

title: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset • case 77
prompt: A loan is sold with full derecognition. Immediately before sale, gross carrying amount is LKR 2,540,000, loss allowance 254,000, and cash proceeds 2,413,000. No accumulated OCI, sale fees or other adjustments exist. Find the derecognition GAIN relative to net carrying amount.
explanation: Net carrying amount = 2,540,000 − 254,000 = 2,286,000. Compare proceeds with that net amount: 2,413,000 − 2,286,000 = 127,000.00 gain. Derecognise both the gross asset and related allowance.
family: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset

title: Non-substantial liability modification gain • case 77
prompt: An amortised-cost liability is modified WITHOUT extinguishment, with no fees. Its carrying amount is LKR 1,770,000. The sole revised payment is 2,035,500 in two years. Original EIR is 10%; the modification is assessed as non-substantial. Find the immediate modification GAIN from recalculating amortised cost at the original EIR.
explanation: Revised amortised cost = 2,035,500/1.10² = 1,682,231.40. Gain = old liability 1,770,000 − revised PV = 87,768.60. The original EIR is retained for this non-extinguishing modification.

title: Credit-risk improvement allowance release • case 77
prompt: A debt asset under the GENERAL ECL model previously had significant credit-risk deterioration and lifetime allowance LKR 254,000. At reporting date the criteria for lifetime ECL are no longer met; required 12-month ECL is 48,500. No write-offs, new assets or other allowance movements occur. Find the impairment reversal in profit or loss.
explanation: When lifetime measurement is no longer required, the general model returns to 12-month ECL. Release the excess allowance: 254,000 − 48,500 = 205,500.00. This is not a receivable under mandatory simplified lifetime ECL.

title: Upstream inventory elimination with tax • case 77
prompt: P and S report profits AFTER their own tax of LKR 5,080,000 and 2,340,000. An upstream inventory sale leaves unrealised profit of 508,000 in group closing inventory. A recoverable DTA is recognised on the full elimination at 30%, with the tax effect in profit or loss. No other consolidation adjustments exist. Find TOTAL consolidated profit, before attribution to owners and NCI.
explanation: Combine separate after-tax profits, eliminate unrealised profit and recognise the recoverable tax benefit: 5,080,000 + 2,340,000 − 508,000 + 152,400.00 = 7,064,400.00. This question asks total group profit, not its attribution.

title: Full-goodwill impairment and owner profit • case 77
prompt: P owns 80% of S all year. Separate after-tax profits are P LKR 4,110,000 and S 1,470,000. Goodwill is recognised on the FULL-goodwill basis and an impairment of 585,000 is attributable to S’s CGU and allocated 80:20 between owners and NCI. No other adjustments or tax effects apply. Find consolidated profit attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Owners receive 80% of S’s profit and bear 80% of the full-goodwill loss: 4,110,000 + 80% × (1,470,000 − 585,000) = 4,818,000.00. Do not charge the owners with 100% of this full-goodwill loss.

title: Partial goodwill CGU gross-up • case 77
prompt: P owns 80% of S. Recognised PARTIAL goodwill is LKR 2,032,000; S’s other net assets in the tested CGU carry at 10,160,000. Recoverable amount of the WHOLE CGU is 11,430,000. Gross up goodwill for unrecognised NCI goodwill when testing; the whole impairment falls within grossed-up goodwill. No tax or other adjustments apply. Find impairment actually recognised on group goodwill.
explanation: Grossed-up goodwill = 2,032,000/80% = 2,540,000.00. Whole-CGU impairment = grossed goodwill + other net assets − recoverable amount = 1,270,000.00. Only the parent’s 80% goodwill portion is recognised, so recorded loss = 1,016,000.00.
reference: LKAS 36 Appendix C paras C4–C8; SLFRS 10 para B86

title: Consolidated retained earnings bridge • case 77
prompt: P owns 75% of S. At year end P retained earnings are LKR 6,850,000, and S retained earnings 4,310,000. S retained earnings at acquisition were 1,000,000. Cumulative post-acquisition extra FV depreciation is 254,000. A downstream sale by P leaves unrealised profit of 157,000. No tax, goodwill impairment, dividends recognised by P, OCI or other adjustments apply. Find consolidated retained earnings attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Group owners’ retained earnings = parent RE + 75% of adjusted post-acquisition S reserves − the parent’s downstream unrealised profit: 8,985,000.00. Pre-acquisition reserves do not enter post-acquisition group retained earnings.

title: Loss of control and translation reserve • case 77
prompt: P loses control of a foreign subsidiary. Proceeds are LKR 5,280,000; retained interest FV 1,270,000; NCI carrying amount 685,000; consolidated net assets INCLUDING goodwill 4,910,000. A cumulative translation GAIN of 254,000, entirely attributable to P, must be reclassified to profit or loss on loss of control. No other effects apply. Find total disposal gain including that reclassification.
explanation: Base gain = proceeds + retained FV + NCI − net assets = 2,325,000.00. Add the parent’s translation gain recycled on disposal: 254,000. Total = 2,579,000.00.
family: Loss of control and translation reserve

title: Residual guarantee expected payment • case 77
prompt: A lessee owes three year-end rentals of LKR 585,000. It guarantees residual value up to 200,000, but the amount EXPECTED to be payable under that guarantee is 107,000 at year three. Discount rate is 10%. No other liability payments exist. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the amount expected to be payable, not automatically the maximum guarantee. Liability = PV of three rentals + 107,000/1.10³ = 1,535,199.10.

title: Reasonably certain purchase option PV • case 77
prompt: A lease requires three year-end rentals of LKR 535,000, plus a purchase option price of 1,270,000 payable at year three. Exercise is reasonably certain. Discount rate is 10%. No incentives, other payments or initial prepayments apply. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the reasonably certain purchase price in the liability: PV of rentals + purchase price discounted for three years = 2,284,635.61. Do not omit or leave the future option payment undiscounted.

title: Lease and service component allocation • case 77
prompt: A two-year contract requires bundled payments of LKR 635,000 at each year end. Relative stand-alone prices are equipment lease 200,000 and distinct maintenance 50,000 per year. The lessee does NOT elect to combine components. Lease discount rate is 10%; no other payments exist. Find initial lease liability for the LEASE component only.
explanation: Allocate 200,000/250,000 = 80% of each bundled payment to the lease: 508,000.00. Discount those two lease payments, excluding maintenance, to obtain 881,652.89.

title: Exempt short-term lease rent-free start • case 77
prompt: A twelve-month lease with no purchase option qualifies for the elected short-term exemption. The first three months are rent free, then nine monthly payments of LKR 58,500 are due. The asset is available throughout and straight-line expense is appropriate. Find lease expense for the FIRST six months, ignoring accrual settlement timing.
explanation: Total fixed payments are nine rents. Spread evenly over all twelve months: 58,500 × 9/12 × 6 = 263,250.00. Rent-free months still receive an expense allocation.

title: Sale-and-leaseback rights transferred • case 77
prompt: A transfer qualifies as a sale under SLFRS 15 at fair value LKR 25,400,000; asset carrying amount is 13,700,000. Market-rate leaseback payments have PV 10,160,000. There are no off-market adjustments or variable-payment complications. At inception, what sale gain is recognised for rights TRANSFERRED to the buyer-lessor?
explanation: Total gain = 25,400,000 − 13,700,000 = 11,700,000. Retained-use proportion = lease PV / fair value = 40%. Recognise only the transferred-rights proportion of the gain: 7,020,000.00.

title: Reassessed bargain purchase gain • case 77
prompt: After the required reassessment, final acquisition-date consideration is LKR 5,080,000, NCI fair value is 400,000 and identifiable net assets are 7,620,000. There is no prior holding or other adjustment. Find the bargain purchase gain recognised in profit or loss.
explanation: Net identifiable assets exceed consideration plus NCI: 7,620,000 − 5,080,000 − 400,000 = 2,140,000.00. Reassessment has been completed before recognising the gain.

title: Acquired contingent liability in goodwill • case 77
prompt: Consideration is LKR 7,350,000; NCI FV is 500,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired contingent liability are 5,310,000. The acquired item is a present obligation with reliably measurable FV 585,000 and qualifies for recognition despite non-probable outflow. No tax or other adjustment applies. Find goodwill after recognising it.
explanation: Recognise the qualifying acquired liability: net identifiable assets become 5,310,000 − 585,000. Goodwill = consideration + NCI − adjusted net assets = 3,125,000.00.

title: Separate acquired brand from goodwill • case 77
prompt: Consideration is LKR 6,850,000; NCI FV 600,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired separable brand are 5,680,000. Brand FV is 1,170,000; tax base is zero and 30% DTL must be recognised. No other adjustments apply. Find goodwill after separate brand and tax recognition.
explanation: An identifiable acquired brand is separate from goodwill. Net addition to identifiable assets = brand FV − 30% DTL = 819,000.00. Goodwill = 6,850,000 + 600,000 − (5,680,000 + 819,000.00) = 951,000.00.

title: Acquisition costs versus issue costs • case 77
prompt: A business acquisition has consideration LKR 4,310,000. Additional costs are acquisition advisory 254,000, qualifying equity-issue costs 70,000 and qualifying debt-issue costs 40,000. The issue costs follow their relevant standards, and no immediate debt-cost amortisation or other expense arises this period. Find the immediate acquisition-related PROFIT-OR-LOSS expense from these costs.
explanation: Expense advisory acquisition costs of 254,000.00. Qualifying equity and debt issuance costs follow their respective standards and are not added to this immediate acquisition-service expense or goodwill.

title: Temporary difference and enacted rate change • case 77
prompt: A taxable temporary difference opens at LKR 200,000 with a DTL measured at 25%. At year end the difference is 685,000 and the enacted rate expected on reversal is 30%. Both the underlying movements and rate change belong in profit or loss. No other tax movements exist. Find deferred tax expense for the year.
explanation: Opening DTL = 200,000×25% = 50,000. Closing DTL = 685,000×30% = 205,500.00. Expense is the full increase, including rate remeasurement: 155,500.00. Rates are exercise assumptions.
family: Temporary difference and enacted rate change

title: Revalued non-depreciable land tax basis • case 77
prompt: Non-depreciable land is revalued from cost LKR 2,540,000 to fair value 3,810,000; tax base remains cost. The enacted rate for recovery through SALE is 20%, while a 30% use rate would otherwise apply. The revaluation and associated tax go to OCI. No other effects exist. Find the net OCI revaluation increase after deferred tax.
explanation: For this non-depreciable revalued asset, measure tax consequences on recovery through sale: DTL = (3,810,000 − 2,540,000)×20%. Net OCI increase = gross uplift less that DTL = 1,016,000.00.

title: Current tax reconciliation and prepayment • case 77
prompt: Accounting pretax profit is LKR 5,850,000. It includes a permanently non-deductible fine of 254,000, exempt income of 50,000, and warranty expense of 585,000 deductible only on payment. Current-year warranty payments of 80,000 are deductible and were charged against the provision, not current profit. Tax rate is 30%; tax prepayments are 300,000. No other tax adjustments exist. Find closing CURRENT tax payable, not total tax expense.
explanation: Taxable profit = 5,850,000 + fine 254,000 − exempt income 50,000 + provision expense 585,000 − deductible payments 80,000 = 6,559,000. Current tax less prepaid 300,000 = 1,667,700.00. Deferred tax is separate.

title: Consolidated inventory tax difference • case 77
prompt: After eliminating an intragroup profit, inventory carries in consolidated statements at LKR 1,524,000. Its tax base in the buyer’s tax jurisdiction is 2,286,000. The buyer’s enacted rate is 30%; sufficient taxable profit is probable. No offsetting, exception or other tax effects apply. Find the consolidated DTA on this inventory.
explanation: The consolidated carrying amount is below tax base, creating a deductible temporary difference of 762,000. Use the buyer’s relevant tax rate: difference ×30% = 228,600.00.

title: Depreciation after recognised impairment • case 77
prompt: Immediately before an impairment, equipment carries at LKR 2,540,000. Recoverable amount is 1,470,000 and impairment is recognised. After that date it has four years’ remaining useful life and residual value 100,000. Straight-line depreciation is appropriate; no further revaluation or impairment applies. Find depreciation for the next FULL year.
explanation: First reduce the asset to recoverable amount 1,470,000. Thereafter allocate revised depreciable amount over remaining life: (1,470,000 − 100,000)/4 = 342,500.00.

title: Allocated headquarters in CGU impairment • case 77
prompt: CGU A carries operating assets of LKR 1,370,000; CGU B carries 400,000. A headquarters asset of 200,000 can be allocated reasonably and consistently in proportion to those operating-asset amounts. A’s recoverable amount INCLUDING its headquarters share is 1,035,000. No goodwill or other assets exist. Find the impairment loss for A including its allocation.
explanation: Allocate headquarters to A: 200,000 × 1,370,000/(1,370,000+400,000) = 154,802.26. Tested A carrying amount is 1,524,802.26. Impairment versus recoverable amount 1,035,000 = 489,802.26.

title: Break-even value-in-use cash flow • case 77
prompt: An asset carries at LKR 2,540,000. Its fair value less costs of disposal is lower. A valid VIU model uses THREE equal year-end operating cash inflows, plus 100,000 net disposal proceeds at year three, discounted at 10%. What minimum equal ANNUAL operating cash inflow makes VIU exactly equal carrying amount? Ignore tax and other adjustments.
explanation: Let annual flow be X. X×(1/1.10 + 1/1.10² + 1/1.10³) + 100,000/1.10³ = 2,540,000. Solve for X = 991,160.12. This sensitivity calculation identifies the VIU break-even point.

title: Discounted warranty expected-value portfolio • case 77
prompt: A present warranty obligation covers 2,540 products. Per product, probabilities are 70% no defect, 25% a minor repair costing LKR 400, and 5% a major repair costing 2,000. All expected payments occur exactly in TWO years. Outflow for the portfolio is probable; appropriate discount rate is 10% with no risk double counting. Find the provision.
explanation: Expected cash payment = 2,540×(25%×400 + 5%×2,000) = 508,000.0. Discount two years at 10%: 508,000.0/1.10² = 419,834.71. The probability assessment applies to the portfolio.

title: Provision movement with revised estimate • case 77
prompt: A discounted provision opens at LKR 1,270,000. Unwinding for a full year is at 8%. A 100,000 settlement occurs at the year END, after unwinding. At that same reporting date, a new estimate increases the remaining provision by 204,000. No other changes occur. Find closing provision.
explanation: Closing = opening + 8% unwinding − year-end settlement + estimate increase: 1,270,000×1.08 −100,000 +204,000 = 1,475,600.00. Classification of the estimate change’s counterpart is assessed separately.

title: Revaluation increase after earlier loss • case 77
prompt: PPE carries at LKR 1,370,000 before revaluation and is revalued to 2,540,000. A prior revaluation decrease on THIS asset of 304,000 was recognised in profit or loss and has not been reversed. No tax effects apply. Find the current increase recognised in OCI after reversing the eligible prior loss in profit or loss.
explanation: Gross increase = 2,540,000 − 1,370,000 = 1,170,000. First recognise 304,000 in profit or loss to reverse the prior decrease. Remaining 866,000.00 is OCI revaluation surplus.

title: Nine-month depreciation and disposal gain • case 77
prompt: Equipment cost LKR 2,740,000, residual value 200,000 and useful life five years, straight-line. Two FULL years’ depreciation were recognised before this year. It is sold after nine months of the current year for 2,005,000. It was not previously held for sale and no impairment or revaluation applies. Find disposal GAIN after the required nine-month depreciation.
explanation: Annual depreciation = (2,740,000−200,000)/5. Deduct two full years and another 9/12 year from cost to obtain disposal-date carrying amount 1,343,000.00. Gain = proceeds − that amount = 662,000.00.

title: Customer collections with a write-off • case 77
prompt: All sales are on credit. Revenue is LKR 6,850,000; opening GROSS trade receivables are 600,000; closing GROSS receivables are 1,570,000. Receivables of 177,000 were written off during the year. There are no taxes, returns, contract balances, acquisitions or exchange changes. Find cash collected from customers.
explanation: Gross receivable roll-forward: opening + credit sales − cash receipts − write-offs = closing. Thus receipts = 6,850,000+600,000−1,570,000−177,000 = 5,703,000.00. Write-offs are not cash receipts.

title: Loan funding net cash effect • case 77
prompt: A company receives cash loan proceeds of LKR 2,540,000 and immediately pays a directly attributable lender issue fee of 58,500. Both payments are classified as financing cash flows in this case. No other cash movement occurs. Find the NET financing cash inflow from these two cash movements; this question does not require net line-item presentation.
explanation: Net financing cash effect = proceeds − cash fee = 2,540,000 − 58,500.00 = 2,481,500.00. Effective-interest amortisation later is not another inception cash payment.

title: Item-by-item NRV without offsetting headroom • case 77
prompt: Two unrelated inventory lines require separate NRV tests. A has 485 units, cost LKR 1,000 and NRV 900 each. B has 254 units, cost 1,000 and NRV 1,200 each. There is no basis to group them for the write-down test. Find TOTAL closing inventory carrying amount.
explanation: Carry A at 900 per unit and B at its lower cost of 1,000. Total = 485×900 + 254×1,000 = 690,500.00. B’s NRV headroom cannot offset A’s write-down.

title: Units-of-production intangible amortisation • case 77
prompt: A finite-life production licence costs LKR 2,440,000, has zero residual value, and is expected to support 150,000 units in total. Actual output this year is 68,500 units. A units-of-production method reliably reflects consumption and the asset was available throughout. No impairment or estimate change applies. Find annual amortisation.
explanation: Apply the supported consumption pattern: amortisation = 2,440,000 × 68,500/150,000 = 1,114,266.67. It is the share of expected lifetime production consumed, not an automatic straight-line charge.

title: Profit after suspended associate losses • case 77
prompt: An equity-method investment and relevant long-term interests were previously reduced to zero. Unrecognised share of prior losses totals LKR 234,000; the investor has no obligation and made no support payments. In the current year its share of associate profit is 351,000. No other adjustments or changes in interest apply. Find the share of profit that can now be RECOGNISED.
explanation: First absorb unrecognised prior losses before resuming recognised profit. Recognised amount = current profit share 351,000 − prior unrecognised losses 234,000 = 117,000.00.

title: Return recovery asset net of costs • case 78
prompt: A retailer has transferred 2,950 products. It expects 118 to be returned. Each returned product originally cost LKR 600; expected recovery handling is 20 per item and expected value deterioration is 30 per item. Estimates meet the relevant requirements. Find the separate asset for the right to recover returned products, excluding the refund liability.
explanation: Recovery asset = original carrying amount of expected returns less recovery costs and potential value decrease: 118 × (600 − 20 − 30) = 64,900.00. It is assessed separately from the customer refund liability.
family: Return recovery asset net of costs

title: Retrospective volume rebate true-up • case 78
prompt: A customer’s annual purchases reach 17,800 units at list price LKR 200. Crossing the threshold entitles it to a 5% retrospective rebate on ALL units. Cumulative revenue before this new supported estimate equals full list price; no rebate was previously accrued. The constraint permits the estimate. Find the reduction in cumulative revenue required now.
explanation: The revised transaction price reflects the retrospective rebate on all units. Revenue reduction = 17,800 × 200 × 5% = 178,000.00. Recognise the corresponding refund obligation as appropriate.

title: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation • case 78
prompt: A bundle has distinct goods A and B with stand-alone prices LKR 590,000 and 1,080,000. Total transaction price is 1,542,000. ALL paragraph 82 criteria demonstrate that the whole 128,000 discount relates only to A. A transfers now; B is not yet delivered. Find revenue recognised for A.
explanation: The specified discount-allocation exception applies. Allocate all 128,000 discount to A: 590,000 − 128,000 = 462,000.00. Do not default to relative allocation when the exception’s criteria are met.
family: Discount specifically allocated to one obligation

title: Three obligations and partial service • case 78
prompt: A contract price of LKR 3,540,000 covers goods A, goods B and twelve months of distinct support. Stand-alone prices are 600,000, 300,000 and 300,000 respectively. A is delivered, B is not, and six months of evenly provided support are complete. No allocation exception applies. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise allocation to A plus half of support: 3,540,000 × (600,000 + 150,000) / 1,200,000 = 2,212,500.00. B’s allocation remains unrecognised as revenue.

title: Progress excluding abnormal waste • case 78
prompt: An over-time contract has transaction price LKR 17,800,000. Costs incurred are 7,120,000, including abnormal waste of 356,000 that does not depict progress. Expected TOTAL productive costs excluding that waste are 14,240,000. Cost-to-cost is appropriate after excluding the waste; no other adjustment applies. Find cumulative revenue, not profit.
explanation: Exclude abnormal waste from the progress numerator. Productive progress = (7,120,000 − 356,000) / 14,240,000. Revenue = transaction price × that progress = 8,455,000.00. The wasted cost is not a revenue-producing input.

title: Uninstalled materials without margin • case 78
prompt: A single over-time construction obligation has price LKR 25,600,000. All B19(b) conditions justify recognising revenue equal to cost for significant uninstalled materials of 5,120,000 already controlled by the customer. Other productive costs incurred are 3,840,000; expected total OTHER costs are 15,360,000. No revenue was previously recognised. Find cumulative revenue.
explanation: Recognise material revenue without margin: 5,120,000. Recognise the remaining price using other-cost progress: (25,600,000 − 5,120,000) × 3,840,000/15,360,000. Total revenue = 10,240,000.00.

title: Agent commission after collection • case 78
prompt: An intermediary is an AGENT and collects customer cash of LKR 4,900,000 for a completed supplier service. It must remit 88% to the supplier and is entitled to the remaining 12% commission. It controls neither the underlying service nor any distinct extra service, and there is no tax. Find its revenue.
explanation: An agent recognises its fee or commission, not the supplier’s gross billings: 4,900,000 × 12% = 588,000.00. The amount due to the supplier is separately accounted for.

title: Distinct remaining goods blended prospectively • case 78
prompt: At modification, 100 distinct goods remain under an existing contract at LKR 1,780 each. Another 50 distinct goods are added at 1,424 each. The modification is NOT a separate contract, but remaining goods are distinct from those already transferred, so paragraph 21(a) applies prospectively. Thirty of the remaining goods are then transferred. Find revenue for those thirty.
explanation: Prospective remaining consideration = 100 × 1,780 + 50 × 1,424. Divide by 150 remaining goods, then multiply by 30 = 49,840.00. Do not retrospectively revise revenue on goods already transferred.

title: FVTPL acquisition expense • case 78
prompt: A financial asset is acquired at fair value LKR 2,360,000 and is classified at FVTPL. Directly attributable broker costs are 59,000, paid separately. No fair-value change occurs immediately after purchase. Find the immediate profit-or-loss expense from acquiring this asset.
explanation: Transaction costs on an FVTPL asset are expensed. Initial asset carrying amount is fair value 2,360,000; immediate acquisition expense is 59,000.00.

title: Collateral cash-shortfall discounting • case 78
prompt: A credit loss scenario has a contractual receipt of LKR 2,950,000 due in one year. The ONLY expected recovery at that same date is collateral sale proceeds of 1,870,000, less sale costs of 128,000. Scenario probability is 100% and original EIR is 10%. Collateral is an integral contractual credit enhancement and not separately recognised. Find discounted ECL.
explanation: One-year shortfall = contractual receipt − net collateral recovery = 2,950,000 − (1,870,000 − 128,000). Discount that shortfall at 10%: 1,098,181.82. Do not ignore recovery costs or discount only one side of same-date cash flows.

title: Three-band provision matrix • case 78
prompt: Under the simplified lifetime-ECL approach, supported adjusted loss rates are 1% on current receivables of LKR 2,560,000, 5% on past-due balances of 690,000, and 30% on severely overdue balances of 256,000. Rates already include all required forward-looking and discounting effects. Find total loss allowance.
explanation: Apply each appropriate band rate and add: 2,560,000×1% + 690,000×5% + 256,000×30% = 136,900.00. Do not apply one blended band mechanically to all balances.

title: Equity FVOCI profit-or-loss dividend • case 78
prompt: An eligible equity investment has the irrevocable FVOCI election. During the year it gains LKR 276,000 in fair value and earns a dividend of 138,000. Dividend recognition criteria are met and the dividend clearly represents a return on investment, not recovery of cost. There are no other effects. Find income recognised in PROFIT OR LOSS.
explanation: The qualifying dividend of 138,000.00 is profit-or-loss income. The fair-value movement of 276,000 is OCI under this election and is not added to the profit-or-loss amount.

title: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset • case 78
prompt: A loan is sold with full derecognition. Immediately before sale, gross carrying amount is LKR 2,560,000, loss allowance 256,000, and cash proceeds 2,432,000. No accumulated OCI, sale fees or other adjustments exist. Find the derecognition GAIN relative to net carrying amount.
explanation: Net carrying amount = 2,560,000 − 256,000 = 2,304,000. Compare proceeds with that net amount: 2,432,000 − 2,304,000 = 128,000.00 gain. Derecognise both the gross asset and related allowance.
family: Disposal of an impaired amortised-cost asset

title: Non-substantial liability modification gain • case 78
prompt: An amortised-cost liability is modified WITHOUT extinguishment, with no fees. Its carrying amount is LKR 1,780,000. The sole revised payment is 2,047,000 in two years. Original EIR is 10%; the modification is assessed as non-substantial. Find the immediate modification GAIN from recalculating amortised cost at the original EIR.
explanation: Revised amortised cost = 2,047,000/1.10² = 1,691,735.54. Gain = old liability 1,780,000 − revised PV = 88,264.46. The original EIR is retained for this non-extinguishing modification.

title: Credit-risk improvement allowance release • case 78
prompt: A debt asset under the GENERAL ECL model previously had significant credit-risk deterioration and lifetime allowance LKR 256,000. At reporting date the criteria for lifetime ECL are no longer met; required 12-month ECL is 49,000. No write-offs, new assets or other allowance movements occur. Find the impairment reversal in profit or loss.
explanation: When lifetime measurement is no longer required, the general model returns to 12-month ECL. Release the excess allowance: 256,000 − 49,000 = 207,000.00. This is not a receivable under mandatory simplified lifetime ECL.

title: Upstream inventory elimination with tax • case 78
prompt: P and S report profits AFTER their own tax of LKR 5,120,000 and 2,360,000. An upstream inventory sale leaves unrealised profit of 512,000 in group closing inventory. A recoverable DTA is recognised on the full elimination at 30%, with the tax effect in profit or loss. No other consolidation adjustments exist. Find TOTAL consolidated profit, before attribution to owners and NCI.
explanation: Combine separate after-tax profits, eliminate unrealised profit and recognise the recoverable tax benefit: 5,120,000 + 2,360,000 − 512,000 + 153,600.00 = 7,121,600.00. This question asks total group profit, not its attribution.

title: Full-goodwill impairment and owner profit • case 78
prompt: P owns 80% of S all year. Separate after-tax profits are P LKR 4,140,000 and S 1,480,000. Goodwill is recognised on the FULL-goodwill basis and an impairment of 590,000 is attributable to S’s CGU and allocated 80:20 between owners and NCI. No other adjustments or tax effects apply. Find consolidated profit attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Owners receive 80% of S’s profit and bear 80% of the full-goodwill loss: 4,140,000 + 80% × (1,480,000 − 590,000) = 4,852,000.00. Do not charge the owners with 100% of this full-goodwill loss.

title: Partial goodwill CGU gross-up • case 78
prompt: P owns 80% of S. Recognised PARTIAL goodwill is LKR 2,048,000; S’s other net assets in the tested CGU carry at 10,240,000. Recoverable amount of the WHOLE CGU is 11,520,000. Gross up goodwill for unrecognised NCI goodwill when testing; the whole impairment falls within grossed-up goodwill. No tax or other adjustments apply. Find impairment actually recognised on group goodwill.
explanation: Grossed-up goodwill = 2,048,000/80% = 2,560,000.00. Whole-CGU impairment = grossed goodwill + other net assets − recoverable amount = 1,280,000.00. Only the parent’s 80% goodwill portion is recognised, so recorded loss = 1,024,000.00.
reference: LKAS 36 Appendix C paras C4–C8; SLFRS 10 para B86

title: Consolidated retained earnings bridge • case 78
prompt: P owns 75% of S. At year end P retained earnings are LKR 6,900,000, and S retained earnings 4,340,000. S retained earnings at acquisition were 1,000,000. Cumulative post-acquisition extra FV depreciation is 256,000. A downstream sale by P leaves unrealised profit of 158,000. No tax, goodwill impairment, dividends recognised by P, OCI or other adjustments apply. Find consolidated retained earnings attributable to P’s owners.
explanation: Group owners’ retained earnings = parent RE + 75% of adjusted post-acquisition S reserves − the parent’s downstream unrealised profit: 9,055,000.00. Pre-acquisition reserves do not enter post-acquisition group retained earnings.

title: Loss of control and translation reserve • case 78
prompt: P loses control of a foreign subsidiary. Proceeds are LKR 5,320,000; retained interest FV 1,280,000; NCI carrying amount 690,000; consolidated net assets INCLUDING goodwill 4,940,000. A cumulative translation GAIN of 256,000, entirely attributable to P, must be reclassified to profit or loss on loss of control. No other effects apply. Find total disposal gain including that reclassification.
explanation: Base gain = proceeds + retained FV + NCI − net assets = 2,350,000.00. Add the parent’s translation gain recycled on disposal: 256,000. Total = 2,606,000.00.
family: Loss of control and translation reserve

title: Residual guarantee expected payment • case 78
prompt: A lessee owes three year-end rentals of LKR 590,000. It guarantees residual value up to 200,000, but the amount EXPECTED to be payable under that guarantee is 108,000 at year three. Discount rate is 10%. No other liability payments exist. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the amount expected to be payable, not automatically the maximum guarantee. Liability = PV of three rentals + 108,000/1.10³ = 1,548,384.67.

title: Reasonably certain purchase option PV • case 78
prompt: A lease requires three year-end rentals of LKR 540,000, plus a purchase option price of 1,280,000 payable at year three. Exercise is reasonably certain. Discount rate is 10%. No incentives, other payments or initial prepayments apply. Find initial lease liability.
explanation: Include the reasonably certain purchase price in the liability: PV of rentals + purchase price discounted for three years = 2,304,583.02. Do not omit or leave the future option payment undiscounted.

title: Lease and service component allocation • case 78
prompt: A two-year contract requires bundled payments of LKR 640,000 at each year end. Relative stand-alone prices are equipment lease 200,000 and distinct maintenance 50,000 per year. The lessee does NOT elect to combine components. Lease discount rate is 10%; no other payments exist. Find initial lease liability for the LEASE component only.
explanation: Allocate 200,000/250,000 = 80% of each bundled payment to the lease: 512,000.00. Discount those two lease payments, excluding maintenance, to obtain 888,595.04.

title: Exempt short-term lease rent-free start • case 78
prompt: A twelve-month lease with no purchase option qualifies for the elected short-term exemption. The first three months are rent free, then nine monthly payments of LKR 59,000 are due. The asset is available throughout and straight-line expense is appropriate. Find lease expense for the FIRST six months, ignoring accrual settlement timing.
explanation: Total fixed payments are nine rents. Spread evenly over all twelve months: 59,000 × 9/12 × 6 = 265,500.00. Rent-free months still receive an expense allocation.

title: Sale-and-leaseback rights transferred • case 78
prompt: A transfer qualifies as a sale under SLFRS 15 at fair value LKR 25,600,000; asset carrying amount is 13,800,000. Market-rate leaseback payments have PV 10,240,000. There are no off-market adjustments or variable-payment complications. At inception, what sale gain is recognised for rights TRANSFERRED to the buyer-lessor?
explanation: Total gain = 25,600,000 − 13,800,000 = 11,800,000. Retained-use proportion = lease PV / fair value = 40%. Recognise only the transferred-rights proportion of the gain: 7,080,000.00.

title: Reassessed bargain purchase gain • case 78
prompt: After the required reassessment, final acquisition-date consideration is LKR 5,120,000, NCI fair value is 400,000 and identifiable net assets are 7,680,000. There is no prior holding or other adjustment. Find the bargain purchase gain recognised in profit or loss.
explanation: Net identifiable assets exceed consideration plus NCI: 7,680,000 − 5,120,000 − 400,000 = 2,160,000.00. Reassessment has been completed before recognising the gain.

title: Acquired contingent liability in goodwill • case 78
prompt: Consideration is LKR 7,400,000; NCI FV is 500,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired contingent liability are 5,340,000. The acquired item is a present obligation with reliably measurable FV 590,000 and qualifies for recognition despite non-probable outflow. No tax or other adjustment applies. Find goodwill after recognising it.
explanation: Recognise the qualifying acquired liability: net identifiable assets become 5,340,000 − 590,000. Goodwill = consideration + NCI − adjusted net assets = 3,150,000.00.

title: Separate acquired brand from goodwill • case 78
prompt: Consideration is LKR 6,900,000; NCI FV 600,000; identifiable net assets BEFORE an acquired separable brand are 5,720,000. Brand FV is 1,180,000; tax base is zero and 30% DTL must be recognised. No other adjustments apply. Find goodwill after separate brand and tax recognition.
explanation: An identifiable acquired brand is separate from goodwill. Net addition to identifiable assets = brand FV − 30% DTL = 826,000.00. Goodwill = 6,900,000 + 600,000 − (5,720,000 + 826,000.00) = 954,000.00.

title: Acquisition costs versus issue costs • case 78
prompt: A business acquisition has consideration LKR 4,340,000. Additional costs are acquisition advisory 256,000, qualifying equity-issue costs 70,000 and qualifying debt-issue costs 40,000. The issue costs follow their relevant standards, and no immediate debt-cost amortisation or other expense arises this period. Find the immediate acquisition-related PROFIT-OR-LOSS expense from these costs.
explanation: Expense advisory acquisition costs of 256,000.00. Qualifying equity and debt issuance costs follow their respective standards and are not added to this immediate acquisition-service expense or goodwill.

title: Temporary difference and enacted rate change • case 78
prompt: A taxable temporary difference opens at LKR 200,000 with a DTL measured at 25%. At year end the difference is 690,000 and the enacted rate expected on reversal is 30%. Both the underlying movements and rate change belong in profit or loss. No other tax movements exist. Find deferred tax expense for the year.
explanation: Opening DTL = 200,000×25% = 50,000. Closing DTL = 690,000×30% = 207,000.00. Expense is the full increase, including rate remeasurement: 157,000.00. Rates are exercise assumptions.
family: Temporary difference and enacted rate change

title: Revalued non-depreciable land tax basis • case 78
prompt: Non-depreciable land is revalued from cost LKR 2,560,000 to fair value 3,840,000; tax base remains cost. The enacted rate for recovery through SALE is 20%, while a 30% use rate would otherwise apply. The revaluation and associated tax go to OCI. No other effects exist. Find the net OCI revaluation increase after deferred tax.
explanation: For this non-depreciable revalued asset, measure tax consequences on recovery through sale: DTL = (3,840,000 − 2,560,000)×20%. Net OCI increase = gross uplift less that DTL = 1,024,000.00.

title: Current tax reconciliation and prepayment • case 78
prompt: Accounting pretax profit is LKR 5,900,000. It includes a permanently non-deductible fine of 256,000, exempt income of 50,000, and warranty expense of 590,000 deductible only on payment. Current-year warranty payments of 80,000 are deductible and were charged against the provision, not current profit. Tax rate is 30%; tax prepayments are 300,000. No other tax adjustments exist. Find closing CURRENT tax payable, not total tax expense.
explanation: Taxable profit = 5,900,000 + fine 256,000 − exempt income 50,000 + provision expense 590,000 − deductible payments 80,000 = 6,616,000. Current tax less prepaid 300,000 = 1,684,800.00. Deferred tax is separate.

title: Consolidated inventory tax difference • case 78
prompt: After eliminating an intragroup profit, inventory carries in consolidated statements at LKR 1,536,000. Its tax base in the buyer’s tax jurisdiction is 2,304,000. The buyer’s enacted rate is 30%; sufficient taxable profit is probable. No offsetting, exception or other tax effects apply. Find the consolidated DTA on this inventory.
explanation: The consolidated carrying amount is below tax base, creating a deductible temporary difference of 768,000. Use the buyer’s relevant tax rate: difference ×30% = 230,400.00.

title: Depreciation after recognised impairment • case 78
prompt: Immediately before an impairment, equipment carries at LKR 2,560,000. Recoverable amount is 1,480,000 and impairment is recognised. After that date it has four years’ remaining useful life and residual value 100,000. Straight-line depreciation is appropriate; no further revaluation or impairment applies. Find depreciation for the next FULL year.
explanation: First reduce the asset to recoverable amount 1,480,000. Thereafter allocate revised depreciable amount over remaining life: (1,480,000 − 100,000)/4 = 345,000.00.

title: Allocated headquarters in CGU impairment • case 78
prompt: CGU A carries operating assets of LKR 1,380,000; CGU B carries 400,000. A headquarters asset of 200,000 can be allocated reasonably and consistently in proportion to those operating-asset amounts. A’s recoverable amount INCLUDING its headquarters share is 1,040,000. No goodwill or other assets exist. Find the impairment loss for A including its allocation.
explanation: Allocate headquarters to A: 200,000 × 1,380,000/(1,380,000+400,000) = 155,056.18. Tested A carrying amount is 1,535,056.18. Impairment versus recoverable amount 1,040,000 = 495,056.18.

title: Break-even value-in-use cash flow • case 78
prompt: An asset carries at LKR 2,560,000. Its fair value less costs of disposal is lower. A valid VIU model uses THREE equal year-end operating cash inflows, plus 100,000 net disposal proceeds at year three, discounted at 10%. What minimum equal ANNUAL operating cash inflow makes VIU exactly equal carrying amount? Ignore tax and other adjustments.
explanation: Let annual flow be X. X×(1/1.10 + 1/1.10² + 1/1.10³) + 100,000/1.10³ = 2,560,000. Solve for X = 999,202.42. This sensitivity calculation identifies the VIU break-even point.

title: Discounted warranty expected-value portfolio • case 78
prompt: A present warranty obligation covers 2,560 products. Per product, probabilities are 70% no defect, 25% a minor repair costing LKR 400, and 5% a major repair costing 2,000. All expected payments occur exactly in TWO years. Outflow for the portfolio is probable; appropriate discount rate is 10% with no risk double counting. Find the provision.
explanation: Expected cash payment = 2,560×(25%×400 + 5%×2,000) = 512,000.0. Discount two years at 10%: 512,000.0/1.10² = 423,140.50. The probability assessment applies to the portfolio.

title: Provision movement with revised estimate • case 78
prompt: A discounted provision opens at LKR 1,280,000. Unwinding for a full year is at 8%. A 100,000 settlement occurs at the year END, after unwinding. At that same reporting date, a new estimate increases the remaining provision by 206,000. No other changes occur. Find closing provision.
explanation: Closing = opening + 8% unwinding − year-end settlement + estimate increase: 1,280,000×1.08 −100,000 +206,000 = 1,488,400.00. Classification of the estimate change’s counterpart is assessed separately.

title: Revaluation increase after earlier loss • case 78
prompt: PPE carries at LKR 1,380,000 before revaluation and is revalued to 2,560,000. A prior revaluation decrease on THIS asset of 306,000 was recognised in profit or loss and has not been reversed. No tax effects apply. Find the current increase recognised in OCI after reversing the eligible prior loss in profit or loss.
explanation: Gross increase = 2,560,000 − 1,380,000 = 1,180,000. First recognise 306,000 in profit or loss to reverse the prior decrease. Remaining 874,000.00 is OCI revaluation surplus.

title: Nine-month depreciation and disposal gain • case 78
prompt: Equipment cost LKR 2,760,000, residual value 200,000 and useful life five years, straight-line. Two FULL years’ depreciation were recognised before this year. It is sold after nine months of the current year for 2,020,000. It was not previously held for sale and no impairment or revaluation applies. Find disposal GAIN after the required nine-month depreciation.
