prompt: A service portfolio appropriately uses the EXPECTED VALUE method for variable consideration. Fixed consideration is LKR 1,290,000. Possible additional bonuses are zero with 20% probability, 129,000 with 50%, and 387,000 with 30%. The revenue constraint permits the whole supported estimate and there are no other pricing adjustments. Find the estimated transaction price, not merely the bonus.
explanation: Expected bonus = 20%×0 + 50%×129,000 + 30%×387,000 = 180,600.00. Add fixed consideration 1,290,000 for transaction price 1,470,600.00. The method choice and constraint are explicit assumptions.

title: Gross profit with return recovery adjustment • case 29
prompt: A retailer transfers 1,580 products at LKR 1,500 each; each cost 600. It expects 79 products to be returned for full refund. Recovery handling is 20 and expected deterioration 30 per returned product. Estimates meet all requirements. No other costs or taxes exist. Find gross profit after recognising revenue net of expected refunds and the separate right-to-recover asset.
family: Gross profit with return recovery adjustment

title: Debt FVOCI sale and OCI recycling • case 29
prompt: A debt asset at FVOCI is sold with full derecognition. Immediately before sale its fair-value carrying amount is LKR 1,680,000; proceeds are 1,845,000. Its accumulated OCI gain is 138,000. There is no impairment, sale cost, current interest or foreign-exchange adjustment. Find the TOTAL profit-or-loss gain at sale, including the debt OCI reclassification.
explanation: Gain against current carrying amount = 1,845,000−1,680,000 = 165,000. Reclassify the accumulated debt FVOCI gain of 138,000 to profit or loss. Total sale-related gain = 303,000.00. Equity FVOCI uses different recycling rules.
family: Debt FVOCI sale and OCI recycling

title: Allowance bridge including recovered write-offs • case 29
prompt: A receivables loss allowance opens at LKR 129,000. Write-offs of 44,500 use that allowance. Required closing allowance is 178,000. Separately, cash recovery of a previously written-off receivable of 15,800 is recognised as an impairment recovery in profit or loss and does not change the allowance. No other movements exist. Find NET impairment expense in profit or loss after that recovery.
explanation: Allowance charge before recovery = closing required 178,000 − opening 129,000 + allowance used on write-offs 44,500 = 93,500. Deduct the separately recognised recovery 15,800: net expense 77,700.00.

title: Closing NCI with full-goodwill impairment • case 29
prompt: P owns 80% of S all year. Opening NCI is LKR 545,000. S’s adjusted post-acquisition annual profit is 1,090,000, OCI gain is 129,000, and total dividend to all shareholders is 200,000. Full-goodwill impairment of 158,000 is allocated 80:20 to owners and NCI. There are no other changes or tax effects. Find closing NCI.
explanation: Closing NCI = opening +20%×profit +20%×OCI −20%×dividend −20%×full-goodwill impairment = 717,200.00. The dividend amount stated is for all shareholders, not only NCI.

title: Remeasurement reduction beyond the ROU asset • case 29
prompt: A qualifying lease-liability remeasurement reduces the liability from LKR 790,000 to a revised present value of 495,000. The related ROU asset carries at 158,000 immediately before adjustment. Apply the ordinary paragraph 39 adjustment rule, not partial-termination accounting. No other asset is available to absorb the reduction. Find the excess reduction recognised as a GAIN in profit or loss after reducing ROU to zero.
explanation: Liability reduction = 790,000−495,000 = 295,000. Reduce ROU by its carrying amount 158,000 to zero. Recognise the remaining reduction 295,000−158,000 = 137,000.00 in profit or loss.
family: Remeasurement reduction beyond the ROU asset

title: Tax expense separating OCI and profit • case 29
prompt: Current tax expense for profit or loss is LKR 295,000. Total DTL increases by 138,000; of this, 59,000 relates to a revaluation recognised in OCI. A DTA decreases by 34,500, entirely through profit or loss. No other tax changes exist. Find TOTAL income tax expense recognised in PROFIT OR LOSS.
explanation: P&L deferred tax expense = DTL increase excluding OCI + DTA decrease = 138,000−59,000+34,500. Add current tax 295,000; total P&L tax expense = 408,500.00. Do not charge OCI tax to profit again.
family: Tax expense separating OCI and profit

title: Reversal redistribution with an asset ceiling • case 29
prompt: A previously impaired CGU, containing no goodwill, has asset A at LKR 890,000 and B at 545,000. Updated recoverable amount supports a TOTAL reversal of 178,000. Allocation starts pro rata, but A’s permitted increase is capped at 44,500 by its no-impairment ceiling. B can absorb the balance without any limit binding. No other assets or changes exist. Find B’s carrying amount AFTER reversal.
explanation: Initial pro-rata allocation to A exceeds its stated cap, so A receives only 44,500. Allocate the remaining total reversal 178,000−44,500 = 133,500 to B. Closing B = 545,000+133,500 = 678,500.00.
family: Reversal redistribution with an asset ceiling

title: SLFRS 18 profit before financing and tax • case 29
prompt: Apply the SLFRS 18. An ordinary manufacturer without a specified main investing or customer-financing activity has operating profit LKR 4,450,000, cash interest income 69,000, an equity-method associate LOSS of 178,000, and a gain of 143,500 on an independent investment. Financing expense is 100,000 and income tax expense 500,000. No paragraph 73 exception applies. Find profit BEFORE financing and income taxes.
explanation: This subtotal = operating profit + all investing-category income and expenses. Add cash interest and independent investment gain; subtract equity-method loss: 4,450,000+69,000−178,000+143,500 = 4,484,500.00. Financing and tax stay below it.
family: SLFRS 18 profit before financing and tax

title: SLFRS 18 reverse an adjusted-profit bridge • case 29
prompt: Apply the SLFRS 18. A qualifying adjusted operating-profit MPM is LKR 5,450,000. It adds back a restructuring expense of 445,000 and impairment expense of 258,000, and excludes an operating disposal GAIN of 129,000. No other adjustments exist. Find the most directly comparable SLFRS OPERATING profit before those management adjustments. Ignore tax and NCI for this pre-tax subtotal.
explanation: Adjusted measure = SLFRS operating profit + expenses added back − gain excluded. Therefore operating profit = 5,450,000−445,000−258,000+129,000 = 4,876,000.00. This is a disclosure bridge, not a change to underlying recognition.

title: Expected-value transaction price • case 30
prompt: A service portfolio appropriately uses the EXPECTED VALUE method for variable consideration. Fixed consideration is LKR 1,300,000. Possible additional bonuses are zero with 20% probability, 130,000 with 50%, and 390,000 with 30%. The revenue constraint permits the whole supported estimate and there are no other pricing adjustments. Find the estimated transaction price, not merely the bonus.
explanation: Expected bonus = 20%×0 + 50%×130,000 + 30%×390,000 = 182,000.00. Add fixed consideration 1,300,000 for transaction price 1,482,000.00. The method choice and constraint are explicit assumptions.

title: Gross profit with return recovery adjustment • case 30
prompt: A retailer transfers 1,600 products at LKR 1,500 each; each cost 600. It expects 80 products to be returned for full refund. Recovery handling is 20 and expected deterioration 30 per returned product. Estimates meet all requirements. No other costs or taxes exist. Find gross profit after recognising revenue net of expected refunds and the separate right-to-recover asset.
family: Gross profit with return recovery adjustment

title: Debt FVOCI sale and OCI recycling • case 30
prompt: A debt asset at FVOCI is sold with full derecognition. Immediately before sale its fair-value carrying amount is LKR 1,700,000; proceeds are 1,870,000. Its accumulated OCI gain is 140,000. There is no impairment, sale cost, current interest or foreign-exchange adjustment. Find the TOTAL profit-or-loss gain at sale, including the debt OCI reclassification.
explanation: Gain against current carrying amount = 1,870,000−1,700,000 = 170,000. Reclassify the accumulated debt FVOCI gain of 140,000 to profit or loss. Total sale-related gain = 310,000.00. Equity FVOCI uses different recycling rules.
family: Debt FVOCI sale and OCI recycling

title: Allowance bridge including recovered write-offs • case 30
prompt: A receivables loss allowance opens at LKR 130,000. Write-offs of 45,000 use that allowance. Required closing allowance is 180,000. Separately, cash recovery of a previously written-off receivable of 16,000 is recognised as an impairment recovery in profit or loss and does not change the allowance. No other movements exist. Find NET impairment expense in profit or loss after that recovery.
explanation: Allowance charge before recovery = closing required 180,000 − opening 130,000 + allowance used on write-offs 45,000 = 95,000. Deduct the separately recognised recovery 16,000: net expense 79,000.00.

title: Closing NCI with full-goodwill impairment • case 30
prompt: P owns 80% of S all year. Opening NCI is LKR 550,000. S’s adjusted post-acquisition annual profit is 1,100,000, OCI gain is 130,000, and total dividend to all shareholders is 200,000. Full-goodwill impairment of 160,000 is allocated 80:20 to owners and NCI. There are no other changes or tax effects. Find closing NCI.
explanation: Closing NCI = opening +20%×profit +20%×OCI −20%×dividend −20%×full-goodwill impairment = 724,000.00. The dividend amount stated is for all shareholders, not only NCI.

title: Remeasurement reduction beyond the ROU asset • case 30
prompt: A qualifying lease-liability remeasurement reduces the liability from LKR 800,000 to a revised present value of 500,000. The related ROU asset carries at 160,000 immediately before adjustment. Apply the ordinary paragraph 39 adjustment rule, not partial-termination accounting. No other asset is available to absorb the reduction. Find the excess reduction recognised as a GAIN in profit or loss after reducing ROU to zero.
explanation: Liability reduction = 800,000−500,000 = 300,000. Reduce ROU by its carrying amount 160,000 to zero. Recognise the remaining reduction 300,000−160,000 = 140,000.00 in profit or loss.
family: Remeasurement reduction beyond the ROU asset

title: Tax expense separating OCI and profit • case 30
prompt: Current tax expense for profit or loss is LKR 300,000. Total DTL increases by 140,000; of this, 60,000 relates to a revaluation recognised in OCI. A DTA decreases by 35,000, entirely through profit or loss. No other tax changes exist. Find TOTAL income tax expense recognised in PROFIT OR LOSS.
explanation: P&L deferred tax expense = DTL increase excluding OCI + DTA decrease = 140,000−60,000+35,000. Add current tax 300,000; total P&L tax expense = 415,000.00. Do not charge OCI tax to profit again.
family: Tax expense separating OCI and profit

title: Reversal redistribution with an asset ceiling • case 30
prompt: A previously impaired CGU, containing no goodwill, has asset A at LKR 900,000 and B at 550,000. Updated recoverable amount supports a TOTAL reversal of 180,000. Allocation starts pro rata, but A’s permitted increase is capped at 45,000 by its no-impairment ceiling. B can absorb the balance without any limit binding. No other assets or changes exist. Find B’s carrying amount AFTER reversal.
explanation: Initial pro-rata allocation to A exceeds its stated cap, so A receives only 45,000. Allocate the remaining total reversal 180,000−45,000 = 135,000 to B. Closing B = 550,000+135,000 = 685,000.00.
family: Reversal redistribution with an asset ceiling

title: SLFRS 18 profit before financing and tax • case 30
prompt: Apply the SLFRS 18. An ordinary manufacturer without a specified main investing or customer-financing activity has operating profit LKR 4,500,000, cash interest income 70,000, an equity-method associate LOSS of 180,000, and a gain of 145,000 on an independent investment. Financing expense is 100,000 and income tax expense 500,000. No paragraph 73 exception applies. Find profit BEFORE financing and income taxes.
explanation: This subtotal = operating profit + all investing-category income and expenses. Add cash interest and independent investment gain; subtract equity-method loss: 4,500,000+70,000−180,000+145,000 = 4,535,000.00. Financing and tax stay below it.
family: SLFRS 18 profit before financing and tax

title: SLFRS 18 reverse an adjusted-profit bridge • case 30
prompt: Apply the SLFRS 18. A qualifying adjusted operating-profit MPM is LKR 5,500,000. It adds back a restructuring expense of 450,000 and impairment expense of 260,000, and excludes an operating disposal GAIN of 130,000. No other adjustments exist. Find the most directly comparable SLFRS OPERATING profit before those management adjustments. Ignore tax and NCI for this pre-tax subtotal.
explanation: Adjusted measure = SLFRS operating profit + expenses added back − gain excluded. Therefore operating profit = 5,500,000−450,000−260,000+130,000 = 4,920,000.00. This is a disclosure bridge, not a change to underlying recognition.

title: SME incidental fiduciary holdings
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. A travel agency holds customer deposits incidentally to arranging travel; holding assets for outsiders is not its primary business. Does this incidental fact alone automatically create public accountability?
options: No; distinguish incidental fiduciary holdings from holding them as a primary business
Yes; any customer deposit makes every entity publicly accountable
Yes; every travel agency is a listed bank
No; public accountability is determined only by employee count
explanation: Some entities hold assets for outsiders incidentally to their primary business. Section 1 distinguishes those facts from the primary-business fiduciary criterion; other public-accountability conditions must still be assessed.

title: SME subsidiary of a full-SLFRS parent
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. A subsidiary has no public accountability and otherwise meets SME eligibility. Its parent prepares full-SLFRS consolidated statements. Is that parent framework alone a barrier to SME statements by the subsidiary?
options: No; the eligible subsidiary can apply the SME framework in its own statements
Yes; every subsidiary must use its parent’s framework for its own published statements
Yes; SME eligibility requires having no parent
No; the subsidiary may freely mix unrelated framework rules
explanation: A subsidiary is not prohibited from using this Standard in its own statements if it has no public accountability, even if its parent uses full SLFRSs. Group consolidation adjustments are a separate matter.

title: SME undue cost is entity-specific
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. A permitted undue-cost-or-effort exemption is being considered. Management relies only on another company’s conclusion without assessing its own circumstances. What is needed?
options: An assessment of the entity’s circumstances, considering costs and benefits to users
A blanket exemption for every SME in the industry
A rule that low profit always excuses compliance
An assumption that all fair values are impossible
explanation: Undue cost or effort is assessed in the entity’s specific circumstances under the relevant permitted exemption; it is not a general choice to ignore requirements.

title: SME specific rule overrides general concepts
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. A specific SME section has a requirement that differs from management’s reading of general concepts. Which normally applies?
options: The full-SLFRS rule regardless of this framework
No accounting is required when concepts differ
explanation: The concepts support application but do not override a specific requirement in another section of the Standard.

title: SME materiality includes nature
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. A small transaction reveals a significant director conflict. Management calls it immaterial solely because of its amount. What should be considered?
options: Nature, magnitude and the reporting context in assessing influence on users
Only a fixed universal percentage of profit
Only whether cash has been paid
Only the amount used by a larger listed company
explanation: Information is material if omission, misstatement or obscuring could influence users. Nature and magnitude are assessed in context, not solely by a numerical threshold.

title: SME compliance statement
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. An entity follows most SME sections but knowingly omits a material required treatment without an applicable exception. May it make an unreserved SME compliance statement?
options: No; compliance requires all requirements of this Standard to be met
Yes; a small entity can omit any difficult rule
explanation: Financial statements are not described as complying with this Standard unless they comply with all its requirements.

title: SME going-concern assessment
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. Management intends to liquidate the entity and has no realistic alternative to liquidation. Is going concern automatically appropriate because last year’s accounts used it?
options: No; assess the basis using the current facts and required disclosures
Yes; the previous basis can never change
Yes; profitability is the only consideration
Only cash flow statement presentation changes
explanation: Going concern is assessed in preparing statements. Intention to liquidate or cease trading, or no realistic alternative, affects the appropriate basis.

title: SME comparative amounts
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. There is no specific exception requiring a different treatment. What is generally required for amounts in the current financial statements?
options: Comparative information for the previous comparable period
Only the previous period’s cash balance
explanation: Comparative information is generally presented for the previous comparable period, including narrative and descriptive information when relevant.

title: SME normal operating cycle
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. Inventory will be sold in the normal operating cycle, which is longer than twelve months. How is the current/non-current distinction generally applied to it?
options: It can be current because it is realised in the normal operating cycle
It must always be non-current beyond twelve months
It is excluded from the statement of financial position
explanation: The current-asset criteria include expected realisation, sale or consumption in the normal operating cycle. Twelve months is not the sole criterion.

title: SME deferred tax classification
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. An entity presents current and non-current classifications. Where are deferred tax assets and liabilities classified?
options: Always as current because tax is paid annually
explanation: When current and non-current classifications are presented, deferred tax assets and liabilities are not classified as current.

title: SME combined retained-earnings statement
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. The only equity changes in all periods presented arise from profit or loss, dividends, prior-period error corrections and accounting-policy changes. What simplification may be available?
options: A statement of income and retained earnings under the specified conditions
A cash-only balance sheet replacing all statements
Mandatory separate OCI even if there are no OCI items
explanation: The specified limited equity changes permit a statement of income and retained earnings in place of the statements identified by the Standard.

title: SME cash-equivalent maturity
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. An investment had a six-month maturity when acquired and has two months left at reporting date. Does remaining year-end maturity alone make it a cash equivalent?
options: No; short maturity is normally assessed from acquisition and all other criteria matter
Yes; any two-month remaining maturity automatically qualifies
Yes; all debt investments are cash equivalents
No; cash equivalents are prohibited for SMEs
explanation: Cash equivalents meet the liquidity and risk conditions and normally have a maturity of three months or less from acquisition.

title: SME notes are part of reporting
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. All primary statement totals are correct, but material accounting-policy information and required explanatory notes are omitted. Is mathematical correctness alone sufficient?
options: No; the required notes and policy information are part of compliant reporting
Yes; notes are optional for every SME
Yes; only lenders may ask for notes
explanation: Notes provide required explanations and additional material information, including material accounting-policy information under the relevant requirements.

title: SME consolidation follows control
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. An eligible SME parent controls another entity and no consolidation exemption applies. What is generally required?
options: Consolidated statements including the subsidiaries under Section 9
Always cost-only investments instead of consolidation
Never consolidate because the parent is small
Consolidate only subsidiaries that pay dividends
explanation: The SME framework contains its own consolidation requirements and exemptions. Small size alone does not eliminate consolidation when the conditions require it.

title: SME voluntary policy change
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. A voluntary policy change is proposed. No new requirement mandates it. What condition must justify the change?
options: Reliable and more relevant information under the SME requirement
A higher profit figure by itself
A different accountant’s personal preference alone
Any change in the company’s logo
explanation: A voluntary policy change is permitted when it results in reliable and more relevant financial information, with the applicable transition treatment.

title: SME correcting a material error
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. A material prior-period error is discovered and retrospective correction is practicable. What is the general response?
options: Restate affected comparatives or relevant opening balances retrospectively
Treat every prior error as a new estimate prospectively
Ignore it because cash has not changed
explanation: Material prior-period errors are corrected retrospectively to the extent practicable under the specified requirements.

title: SME impairment is not automatic ECL
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. A financial asset is measured at amortised cost under Section 11. Which impairment trigger belongs to this SME edition?
options: Assess objective evidence of impairment and recognise an indicated loss
Automatically import full SLFRS 9 lifetime ECL for every such asset
Use the PPE revaluation surplus as the allowance
explanation: Section 11.21 requires assessment of objective evidence of impairment for assets at cost or amortised cost. The SME model must not be replaced silently by full SLFRS 9 ECL.

title: SME derivative fair-value movement
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. A derivative is within Part II of Section 11, measured at fair value, and no hedge-accounting exception applies. How are its fair-value changes generally recognised?
explanation: Part II generally requires fair-value measurement with changes in profit or loss, subject to its specified exceptions.

title: SME transaction costs on an FVTPL instrument
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. An instrument is measured at fair value through profit or loss. How are its directly attributable acquisition transaction costs generally treated?
options: Exclude them from initial FVTPL measurement and expense them
Always add them to every instrument’s carrying amount
explanation: The initial-measurement requirement includes transaction costs except for instruments measured at FVTPL; the exception is important.

title: SME accessible principal market
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. An accessible principal market exists for an asset. Another market has higher net proceeds but is not the principal market. Which market generally anchors fair value?
options: Always the market with the highest gross price
An inaccessible market with a quoted price
The entity’s preferred budget selling price
explanation: Fair value uses the principal market or, in its absence, the most advantageous market, with required market access.

title: SME transaction versus transport cost
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. When location is an asset characteristic, how does fair-value measurement generally distinguish transaction and transport costs?
options: Ignore transaction costs in fair value but adjust for relevant transport to market
Deduct both automatically as transaction costs
Add all selling commissions to the exit price
explanation: Transaction costs are transaction-specific rather than an asset characteristic. Location-related transport costs can adjust the market price.

title: SME abnormal production waste
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. An entity incurs abnormal wasted materials and proposes adding them to inventory to prevent a loss. What is appropriate?
options: Expense abnormal waste rather than include it in inventory cost
Capitalise all waste because production occurred
Add it only to unsold units regardless of normal capacity
explanation: Abnormal wasted materials, labour and other production costs are excluded from inventory cost and expensed.

title: SME interchangeable inventory formulas
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. A retailer wants to use LIFO for ordinarily interchangeable goods. Which formulas does this SME section permit?
options: FIFO or weighted average; LIFO is not permitted
Any formula chosen each year for profit smoothing
Only selling price with no cost test
explanation: The Standard specifies FIFO or weighted average for the relevant inventories and expressly prohibits LIFO.

title: SME associate measurement choices
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. An entity holds investments in associates. Does this framework require the equity method for all associates in every case?
options: No; Section 14 specifies cost, equity or fair-value models subject to its rules
Yes; full SLFRS associate accounting must always be copied unchanged
Yes; every associate must be fully consolidated
explanation: Section 14.4 provides policy models for all investments in associates, with detailed requirements including published-price rules.

title: SME jointly controlled entity models
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. A party has joint control over a jointly controlled entity. Which framework-specific point matters?
options: Section 15 provides cost, equity or fair-value model choices under its requirements
Every such interest must be treated as an ordinary customer receivable
Full SLFRS 11 accounting replaces Section 15 automatically
Only proportionate consolidation is ever permitted
explanation: The SME framework has its own measurement choices for investments in jointly controlled entities.

title: SME investment-property fair value
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. Investment-property fair value can be measured reliably without undue cost or effort. Which subsequent model does Section 16 require?
options: Fair value through profit or loss
An unrestricted choice to use PPE revaluation OCI for that property
explanation: Investment property meeting the reliability and undue-cost-or-effort condition is measured at fair value each reporting date with changes in profit or loss.

title: SME investment-property fallback
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. Investment-property fair value cannot be measured reliably without undue cost or effort. Which specified fallback applies?
options: A fabricated fair value chosen by management
The full-SLFRS choice automatically without considering Section 16
explanation: Other investment property is accounted for under Section 17’s cost model as required by this framework.

title: SME PPE revaluation class
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. An entity elects the permitted PPE revaluation model. Can it selectively revalue one favourable asset while ignoring the rest of the same class?
options: No; apply the model to the entire class with required regularity
Yes; selective gains are the purpose of the model
No; PPE revaluation is never permitted under this edition
Yes; only the largest asset needs revaluation
explanation: The SME edition permits cost or revaluation for a PPE class. Selective revaluation within the class is not permitted.

title: SME replacing a major inspection
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. A new major inspection qualifies for recognition and replaces an identifiable old inspection component with remaining carrying amount. What is appropriate?
options: Recognise qualifying new inspection cost and derecognise the old component
Recognise the old amount as revenue
Always capitalise the old component again
explanation: The Standard addresses replacement and major-inspection components, including derecognition of the remaining carrying amount of the previous inspection.

title: SME internal development is not full LKAS 38
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. Internally incurred development expenditure would meet full LKAS 38 capitalisation criteria. It does not form part of another asset under the SME framework. What does this SME edition require?
options: Expense the internal research and development expenditure
Capitalise it automatically by importing full LKAS 38
Recognise it in OCI without an asset
explanation: Section 18.14 expenses internally incurred intangible expenditure, including research and development, unless it forms part of another qualifying asset under this Standard.

title: SME every intangible has a finite life
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. Management proposes an indefinite useful life for an acquired intangible under this SME framework. What is the framework-specific requirement?
options: All intangible assets are treated as having finite useful lives
All acquired intangibles are automatically indefinite
Only purchased software has a life
An indefinite label removes all impairment testing
explanation: This Standard considers all intangible assets finite-life; legal rights and expected use inform the assessment.

title: SME unreliable intangible life estimate
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. An intangible’s useful life cannot be established reliably. What is required?
options: Use management’s best estimate, not exceeding ten years
Always assume an infinite useful life
explanation: The ten-year maximum applies when useful life cannot be established reliably. It is not a universal ten-year cap when a longer life is reliably established.

title: SME intangible subsequent measurement
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. Management wants to use an active-market revaluation model for a recognised intangible. What model does Section 18 specify?
options: Cost less accumulated amortisation and impairment
An unrestricted choice between cost and revaluation
Fair value with all changes in equity
explanation: The SME intangible section specifies the cost-based subsequent measurement model; the full-framework revaluation option is not imported.

title: SME goodwill is amortised
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. A business combination produces recognised goodwill. What subsequent treatment belongs to this SME edition?
options: Cost less accumulated amortisation and impairment
No amortisation under the full-SLFRS goodwill model
explanation: Section 19.34 requires goodwill amortisation and impairment. If useful life cannot be reliably established, the best estimate cannot exceed ten years.

title: SME acquisition advisory costs in 2025
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. A business acquisition incurs advisory service fees that are not debt or equity issue costs. What does this 2025 edition require?
options: Expense acquisition-related services when incurred and received
Always add advisory fees to goodwill
Defer every advisory fee until sale of the subsidiary
explanation: The edition separates acquisition-related costs from the combination and expenses them, with exceptions for debt/equity issue costs under their sections.

title: SME measurement-period evidence
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. New information within twelve months of acquisition concerns a condition that already existed at acquisition and changes a provisional acquired-asset value. What is relevant?
options: Retrospective adjustment of provisional acquisition amounts under the specified rules
Every event after acquisition is automatically current revenue
Goodwill can never change for provisional measurements
All later events adjust goodwill regardless of what they concern
explanation: The measurement-period rule concerns acquisition-date facts and circumstances, within the twelve-month limit; new post-acquisition events are different.

title: SME finance versus operating lessee leases
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. A lessee is applying Section 20. Must it automatically apply full SLFRS 16’s single lessee ROU model to every lease?
options: No; this SME section retains finance and operating lease accounting
Yes; all SME leases are automatically finance leases
Yes; Section 20 has no classification requirements
No; SMEs never recognise leased assets
explanation: The SME framework retains lease classification based on transfer of risks and rewards and different finance/operating lessee treatments.

title: SME operating lease expense pattern
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. An operating lease has uneven fixed payments. Neither the alternative-consumption-pattern nor inflation exception applies. Which expense pattern generally applies?
options: Only cash payments as expense each period
Capitalise every operating lease payment as goodwill
explanation: Section 20.15 normally recognises operating lease expense straight-line, with specified exceptions that are excluded by the facts.

title: SME forecast operating loss
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. A budget forecasts future operating losses but there is no present obligation from a past event. What is appropriate?
options: Do not recognise a provision solely for the forecast losses
Recognise the full budget as a provision
Recognise a deferred asset equal to the loss
Always credit revenue to avoid the forecast loss
explanation: A provision requires the specified present-obligation and recognition conditions; future operating losses do not themselves create an obligation.

title: SME probable contingent asset
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. A possible asset from litigation has a probable but not virtually certain inflow. What is the general treatment?
options: Do not recognise the contingent asset; provide required disclosure
Recognise it whenever management hopes to win
Recognise the maximum claim as revenue
explanation: Contingent assets are not recognised until the inflow becomes virtually certain; probable inflows require the specified disclosure.

title: SME compound financial instrument
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. A convertible debt instrument has both a contractual liability and an equity conversion component under this framework. How is initial allocation generally performed?
options: Measure the liability component first; allocate the residual to equity
Classify the entire instrument as equity solely because it is convertible
Recognise the whole issue as sales revenue
explanation: The liability is measured first, and the residual proceeds are allocated to equity, with no subsequent remeasurement of that equity component.

title: SME 2025 revenue model
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. A learner uses an older risks-and-rewards-only summary as a substitute for reading the 2025 revenue section. Which model does this edition explicitly set out?
options: Five steps from identifying the contract and promises to recognising revenue as promises are fulfilled
A model that recognises every signed quotation immediately
A rule that all revenue is recognised on invoice date
explanation: The Section 23 sets out a five-step contract revenue model. Its current wording must be used rather than assuming an older edition’s requirements.

title: SME non-refundable set-up fee
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. A joining activity transfers no distinct good or service to the customer. The fee is non-refundable. What is the general consequence?
options: Include it in transaction price and allocate it to the contract’s promises
Recognise all fee revenue immediately solely because it is non-refundable
Omit it from the transaction price permanently
explanation: An activity required to fulfil a contract is not itself a promise unless it transfers a good or service. Upfront fees without a separate promise are allocated to the actual promises.

title: SME right of return
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. A sale has a supported estimate of customer returns under the revenue model. Which liability concept is relevant?
options: Recognise the required refund liability for consideration expected to be repaid
Ignore every return until physical receipt
Recognise all expected refunds as equity
Treat every return right as a finance lease
explanation: The transaction-price and sales-with-return requirements address consideration not expected to be retained, including a refund liability and the related recovery right where required.

title: SME grant performance conditions
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. A government grant is received before its specified future performance conditions are met. What is the general treatment?

Recognise all income solely on receipt
Automatically amortise every grant over a PPE life regardless of conditions
Credit all grants directly to equity
explanation: Section 24 bases income recognition on its specified performance-condition rules. Receipt before the criteria are satisfied is a liability.

title: SME equity-settled employee award
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. An employee equity-settled award has reliably measurable grant-date fair value and a service vesting period. What measurement basis is generally relevant?

Always the year-end share price for an equity-settled award
Only the cash paid on eventual exercise
Nominal share capital with no service expense
explanation: Employee equity-settled awards use grant-date measurement, with expense recognition over the service conditions as required.

title: SME goodwill impairment reversal

Only if management changes the company name
explanation: The SME impairment section prohibits reversal of a goodwill impairment loss. This is distinct from potential reversal for other assets.

title: SME actuarial gain presentation election

Defer them permanently outside recognised amounts
explanation: Section 28.24 allows the specified profit-or-loss or OCI policy election, applied consistently to all defined benefit plans and all actuarial gains and losses.

title: SME deferred tax discounting
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. A recognised deferred tax balance will reverse far in the future. Is it discounted under this SME section?

title: SME foreign monetary payable at year end

title: SME 2025 finance-lease initial asset • case 8
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. A lease is classified as a FINANCE lease under Section 20. Two payments of LKR 380,000 occur at the ends of years one and two; the appropriate rate is 10%. Fair value of leased property is 1,000,000, and qualifying initial direct costs are 20,000. No other payments apply. Find the asset initially recognised by the lessee.
explanation: Initial asset before direct costs = lower of fair value and PV of minimum payments. PV=380,000/1.10+380,000/1.10²=659,504.13. Add 20,000 direct costs: 679,504.13.

title: SME 2025 finance-lease liability bridge • case 8
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. A finance-lease liability opens at LKR 760,000. Its effective annual rate is 8% and a minimum lease payment of 200,000 occurs at year end. There are no modifications, contingent rents or other cash flows. Find closing liability.
explanation: Finance charge=760,000×8%=60,800.00. Closing liability=opening+finance charge−payment=620,800.00. The payment includes interest and principal, rather than being wholly principal.

title: SME 2025 operating-lease rent-free start • case 8
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. A twelve-month lease is classified as OPERATING under Section 20. The first three months are rent free, followed by nine monthly rentals of LKR 28,000. The asset is used evenly throughout. Neither the alternative-pattern nor inflation exception applies. Find expense for the first six months.
explanation: Total fixed payments=9×28,000. Spread across twelve months and charge six months: 9×28,000/12×6=126,000.00. This is operating-lease expense under the SME model.

title: SME 2025 grant condition income • case 8
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. Grant A of LKR 280,000 is receivable with NO specified future performance condition. Grant B of 340,000 has been received but its specified future condition is not met. Grant C of 190,000 has been received and its specified condition is fully met this year. No other restrictions or recognition issues apply. Find grant income this year.
explanation: Recognise A when receivable and C when its condition is met. Keep B as a liability. Income=280,000+190,000=470,000.00. Do not automatically apply an asset-life grant-release model from full LKAS 20.

title: SME 2025 construction borrowing expense • case 8
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. A qualifying long construction project has equipment and construction expenditure of LKR 2,400,000 plus installation of 100,000. Borrowing costs incurred this year are 320,000. They meet full LKAS 23 capitalisation conditions, but the entity is applying THIS SME framework. No other financing costs exist. What borrowing-cost expense is recognised?
explanation: Section 25.2 requires ALL borrowing costs to be expensed when incurred. The full-framework qualifying-asset treatment does not override it. Borrowing-cost expense = 320,000.00.

title: SME 2025 basic-debt effective interest • case 8
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. A basic debt asset is appropriately measured at amortised cost under Section 11. Its opening carrying amount is LKR 1,200,000; effective annual rate is 8%; coupon received at year end is 68,000. No impairment, fees beyond those already in EIR or other movements apply. Find closing amortised cost.
explanation: Effective interest=1,200,000×8%. Closing amortised cost=opening+effective interest−coupon=1,228,000.00. The coupon is not necessarily the effective interest amount.

title: SME 2025 objectively evidenced impairment • case 8
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. A fixed-rate financial asset at amortised cost has OBJECTIVE evidence of impairment under Section 11. Its carrying amount before impairment is LKR 1,200,000. The only estimated future receipt is 920,000 in one year; original EIR is 10%. No collateral or other cash flows apply. Find impairment loss.
explanation: Under the SME objective-evidence model, compare carrying amount with PV of estimated future cash flows at original EIR: 1,200,000−920,000/1.10=363,636.36. Do not substitute full SLFRS 9 ECL terminology or measurement.

title: SME 2025 deferred-tax expense bridge • case 8
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. Opening DTL is LKR 50,000 and closing DTL 106,000. Opening DTA is 30,000 and closing DTA 24,000. All balances meet recognition conditions; all movements relate to profit or loss. No acquisition, foreign-exchange, OCI or equity effects exist. Find deferred-tax expense for the year.
explanation: Deferred expense=increase in DTL+decrease in DTA=(106,000−50,000)+(30,000−24,000.00)=62,000.00. Closing net tax balance is not the same as period expense.

title: SME 2025 non-financial asset impairment • case 8
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. An asset within Section 27 carries at LKR 1,060,000; value in use is 780,000; fair value less costs to sell is 790,000. Both measures are valid and no revaluation surplus exists. Find the impairment loss.
explanation: Recoverable amount is the HIGHER of value in use and fair value less costs to sell: 790,000. Loss=carrying amount less recoverable amount=270,000.00.

title: SME 2025 discounted warranty portfolio • case 8
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. A present warranty obligation covers 1,400 products. Each has a 70% chance of no defect, 25% chance of a repair costing LKR 400 and 5% chance of a repair costing 2,000. Portfolio outflow is probable. All payments occur in two years; appropriate discount rate is 10%, with risks not double counted. Find the provision.
explanation: Expected portfolio cash payment=1,400×(25%×400+5%×2,000)=280,000.0. Discount two years at 10%: 231,404.96. The large-population probability-weighted measure differs from simply using one possible repair cost.

title: SME 2025 allocated goods and service revenue • case 8
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. A contract begins on 1 October year one and reporting date is 31 December. Price LKR 1,440,000 covers distinct goods delivered immediately and a twelve-month evenly provided service ending NEXT year. Stand-alone prices are goods 600,000 and service 400,000. Step 4 applies; there is no allocation exception. Three service months are complete. Find cumulative revenue at year one end.
explanation: Allocate by relative stand-alone prices. Recognise all goods allocation plus 3/12 of service allocation: 1,440,000×(600,000+100,000)/1,000,000=1,008,000.00. The promises are not all completed in the starting reporting period, so the stated allocation requirement is relevant.
family: SME 2025 allocated goods and service revenue

title: SME 2025 over-time cumulative catch-up • case 8
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. A Section 23 contract meets the over-time recognition criteria and an input cost method appropriately depicts progress. Transaction price is LKR 10,800,000; cumulative eligible costs are 4,400,000; revised TOTAL expected eligible costs are 8,800,000. Revenue previously recognised is 3,000,000. No waste, uninstalled materials or price constraints complicate measurement. Find revenue for the CURRENT period.
explanation: Updated cumulative progress=4,400,000/8,800,000. Cumulative revenue=price×progress. Deduct prior revenue 3,000,000 to obtain the current-period catch-up of 2,400,000.00.

title: SME 2025 monetary payable exchange loss • case 8
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. A USD 14,000 trade payable was initially translated at LKR 300/USD and remains unpaid. Closing rate is LKR 318/USD. No hedge, net-investment or other exception applies. Find the exchange LOSS recognised on reporting-date retranslation.
explanation: The payable is monetary and uses the closing rate. Liability increase and exchange loss=USD 14,000×(318−300)=252,000.00. Historical-cost non-monetary items have a different translation rule.

title: SME 2025 elected equity-method associate • case 8
prompt: Apply SLFRS for SMEs 2025. The investor has elected Section 14’s EQUITY method for its associates and owns 30%. Opening investment is LKR 1,160,000; associate profit is 580,000; total associate dividends are 100,000. Extra depreciation on acquisition-date fair-value differences is 50,000. No tax, OCI, unrealised transactions or impairment applies. Find closing investment.
explanation: Under the explicitly selected equity method, adjust associate profit for extra depreciation, take the 30% share and deduct the 30% dividend: 1,160,000+30%×(580,000−50,000−100,000)=1,289,000.00. Other Section 14 policy models are not being used here.
